reviews.comment: He's clearly passionate about the area but the classes weren't as intellectually engaging as I would have liked them to be. I sometimes felt the materials were just glossed over superficially and the feedback wasn't great. The project was fun to work on! It's an easy A for those looking.

This was a relatively easy class. I expected it to provide a strong foundation in understanding global development and the role of technology within it. Instead, it felt more like a collection of various technological solutions, focused on adoption rather than deeper analysis. Many readings were his own research which was weird too.
This was one of the best courses I have attended. The course opened up completely new perspectives on me and the learning will help me regardless of what I do next.

An excellent exploration of global perspectives in computing. Challenges technological saviorism attitudes. Prof. Vashistha is incredibly engaging, passionate, and knowledgeable. There is a significant group project due at the end and reading quizzes before classes, but it was a reasonable class with reasonable expectations. Very worthwhile.

Great professor, he is very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. He clearly cares about the content and has a great, engaging lecture style that makes it easy to be interested in the subject. Reading heavy and attendance required, though.
One of the best course that I took at Cornell. Great way to learn how to design and build technology for underserved communities in different parts of the world. Strongly recommended.
Great professor with reading heavy coursework. Be ready to explore outside of the American ecosystem and learn more about global development in all his classes.

Professor Vashistha is nice and really cares about the content of this class. There's a lot of reading but nothing that's too much to handle. The only hard part of this class is the final project where you have to start super early and show that you put a lot of thought and work into it to do well. Other than the final project, super manageable.

Adalja is a great professor, unfortunately the lectures can be quite boring, and the hw seems a bit like busy work. the case studies and prelims werent difficult as long as u study enough for them. the labs were ok, fun sometimes, but the final project was a lot of work and pretty difficult as well.
Good lectures and Good office hours. I just hate the labs. No finals and the prelims are pretty easy if you study (I got an average of high 80s just by studying 2 days prior with chatgpt)
Fantastic professor. Two prelims, gave review sessions for both. While lab grade primarily depends on chefs, Professor Adalja is very understanding and helps in giving proper feedback.

super awesome and sweet guy. lectures can be a little boring but you can tell he's really interested in the topic. if you pay attention in class, prelims are super straightforward. super helpful and understanding.

Nicest person. Prelims are easy if you pay attention at all. The final project was work though so make sure you have a good group. He genuinely cares and wants you to do well and understand the material (which he teaches quite straightforwardly).
Mr. Adalja creates a very nice learning environment and makes his class very manageable.

The content of this class isn't the most interesting; however, Professor Adalja does a good job of making it engaging. Grading criteria is very clear. Exams were easy and straightforward if you studied. There are lots of ways you can cusion your grade (reading quizzes, hw, projects, etc.) if you are worried about not doing well on the prelims.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. If you are interested in restaurants, he is great. Exams can be a bit tough, but if you study and know the material, it shouldn't be too bad.

This course is required for freshmen. With a 3 hour lab and two 75-minute lectures a week, this course is time-consuming, but Professor Alja wants to help you succeed so it isn't too hard. Most of the content is on the slides for the exam so easy A if you study and do well in lab.

Professor Adalja's lectures are very boring and long, but he is very helpful outside the classroom. Quizzes due before every class which is tedious, but they are easy points to get. Prelims are very straightforward and not that tough. I would recommend to take him.

Awesome professor. Had him in 1360 and took 3310 because I loved the freshman class so much. Super chill too, he gets were all college students. You can only miss 3 classes, but its a class you look forward to going to.

Adalja is a solid prof. Honestly I didn't find his lectures to be that interesting, but I'm not interested in f&b so that's expected. Test questions are hella specific, so study the slides he gives out well. I will say, he's super likable as a person and is definitely understanding when it comes to issues.

Pretty good professor, very chill and down to earth. His slides tend to have a lot of information and the test questions tend to be very specific, so taking good notes and studying throughout the class will help you a lot.

Professor Adalja was my most caring and friendly professor this semester. He grades very fairly and is always approachable. His TA's are very helpful and he frequently holds office hours. There are many grades in the class but as long as you stay ahead and pay attention you will do fine. I liked that he lets you see what you missed on exams too.

Great Professor. I think a lot of the reviews here was when he was new to teaching, and the course was fluid. Now that he has experience teaching, the course is awesome. Learned a lot and actually enjoyed showing up to class, even though I am not interested in F&B as a career. Lectures were interesting and lively, and the coursework/exams were easy
Great Lecturer. Understanding. Very Reasonable work. Exams are easy if you studied the slides. Got Drip too.

The workload and difficulty of the class are reasonable and he is very approachable outside of class. I'm not interested in F&B, but this was a good intro class to complement my hotel education. Read through his lecture slides and do the practice problems and you'll do fine.

Prof. Adalja is genuinely one of the nicest people I've met at Cornell-- and is insanely intelligent with really cool experience to share. I don't know a single person last year who didn't enjoy his class and get something out of it. If Food Ops was put in the hands of the wrong person it could easily be boring, but Adalja makes sure that it isn't.
Adalja is a great prof. He is accessible outside of class and so on top of his game.
The information is not very useful

The exams were more challenging in comparison to other Hotel classes, but was definitely manageable if you paid attention in class and read through his notes. He makes time for his students and answers any questions and is very accommodating. There were lots of extra credit opportunities to boost the final grade and exams were generously curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: It was hard but he tried his best. Nice hairstyle. Accessible. Nice outside of the class. Lots of extra credit. Let's go to Per Seeeee
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ok, I'll admit, Adalja is not the best professor in the world, but clearly a lot of people want to be handed an A on a silver spoon. This was Adalja's first semester teaching so, yes, we were guinea pigs. But whenever the class got upset about something, he tried to fix it. Yes, he made some mistakes in the beginning, but he got better with time.

He is the worst professor/teacher I have ever had. He has no regard for his students and his tests include topics we have never learned. He does not even know the material himself. He is pretentious, dry, and he contradicts his own material. This course is mandatory but I'd rather not graduate than take this class. He should be fired immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class is not enjoyable at all. He does not care about his students. All he does is give incredibly hard quizzes that ask you very specific questions. His exams are also unnecessarily hard. He is also very uptight during exams and won't let you ask any questions at all even if they are just clarifying questions. I miss the old professor.

He gives out almost weekly reading quizzes online to do. He told us they would be simple if you done the reading but they are very specific with a bunch of numbers and thus it's quite complicated even as someone who did all the reading. His exams are crazy as well. They are so heavy in material and nothing like past professors of Food Ops. BAD PROF
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I thought this was a very accessible class for those trying to get an overview of environmental law. I had no issue with the Exams, there were cheat sheets available, and the questions were relatively straightforward. Attendance is mandatory, as it is with all law classes, but I didn't mind that. The professor is very amicable and experienced.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Chatrchyan is not a law professor, but she taught a course heavily reliant on understanding of American law. She was often unprepared for lectures, redirecting questions to undergraduate TAs or back to the student who asked for clarification. The grading rubrics for exams were unclear, leading to confusion from students and TAs.

Slides were poorly made and presented, exams were made the night before being given and contained frequent mistakes, grading was unfair and TAs could often not explain the rationale of their peers or the instructor. Readings are heavy and interesting, completely necessary to pass. Would only recommend this class if you LOVE environmental law.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: To be honest this class wasn't that hard. At all. I'm not sure what these other students are seeing, because Prof. Drake's bio class was pretty lightweight.

Added her class post add/drop and was told my missed assignments prior to joining would be dropped. When my letter grade came out at end of semester, I received below what I expected and sent her an email making sure these grades were dropped. 5 days later I got a reply saying they were, but after asking my TA, I found out they weren't dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly the rudest professor I've had so far at cornell . Pretends like she wants her students to laugh and foster and comfortable environment for learning but does the opposite. Would not take a class with her again.

This professor is very sarcastic. She makes the lecture environment very uncomfortable with shady remarks towards people's questions, for example. To put it quite bluntly, she's rude to students. She acts like she has a surperiority complex about her teaching style. I am sure many of the reviews would agree with this.

She seems convinced her teaching method is inherently superior and beyond criticism. Team-Based Learning is treated more like a belief system than a tool, despite working poorly for many students. The focus feels ego-driven rather than student-centered, with too much time wasted on forced group work.

most of her bad reviews are from the class itself. Abby's a pretty nice prof, and offers to go over missed problems from the prelim + lots of extra cred. that said, BIOEE1780 has an excessive amount of work. lots of memorization, field trips, and pre-lecture assignments. tip: vodcasts and lectures are a MUST, but dont waste your time on the reading

I wrote a bad review of Prof. Drake, and felt bad so had it removed. Retrospectively, I wish I kept it up. She is the single worst professor I've had at Cornell who will literally laugh in your face and make you feel small. The subject matter of her course was interesting, but the course structure itself was painstakingly boring. I warn everyone!!
Repetitive lectures, but overall interesting course
If you take the time to complete all the lectures and assignments, the class is extremely easy

If this class isn't required, I strongly recommend not taking it. It's mostly mindless memorization with 2-3 hours of online lectures before class. The class is poorly structured, time-consuming, and boring, with lectures filled with quiz questions worth 30% of your grade. Prelims were easy but included trick questions meant to lower your score.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Boring class. Wouldn't recommend it unless it's required for your major. Had to memorize the Tree of Life, which required a lot of work while also seeming completely useless. Exams were fair as long as you study.
I knew I should have avoided this professor. Avoid her at all costs!

Attendance is 100% mandatory because of clicker questions during each lecture and 5 question quizzes to start to see if you did the homework. Yes, it is annoying, but if you do the work (which there's a lot of), you'll be fine. Material isn't necessarily difficult, just a lot of memorization. If you put time and effort in, you will get an A or A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was an incredibly boring class. Took it as a non-stem kid for my bio credit, and it was torturous. The kids in your group make a huge difference, and the effort was low all around. Constant tedious work so it's easy to fall behind. Had a bad interaction with a TA who refused to let me make up an assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The amount of grunt work this class gives (for no reason) is absolutely appalling. The only thing the flipped classroom structure does is waste your time outside of class. Not happy at all with how the course is taught. The professors claim that research on flipped classrooms is more beneficial but research findings change all the time...

Flipped classroom style - lots of repetitive busy work and in-class sessions were mostly sitting around. Frustrating miscommunications (TA told me exam was open note, announcement days before exam that it wasn't). BUT they changed stuff after mid-semester evals, so she does care about students. Not a hard class, but requires time and memorization

A hybrid class where you watch hours videos each week, spending class doing quizzes. A class Discord, no Ed, where you must post with your real name if you want help. A course email where you will be ignored. A lack of TAs leading to rushed discussions. A condescending professor. All this plus more make for the worst class I have ever taken here.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had the privilege of taking a class with. Listening to her feels like bad chalk on a blackboard. I don't encourage anyone to take a class with her.

Disclaimer: I took 1781 asynchronously, which isn't an option here so I picked 1780, which has the same content but diff structure.
Excellent lectures that force you to learn, as well as helpful assignments. Very time-consuming course. Tests are open book. Prof is not very responsive to questions.
I recommend this course only if you have time.

Took BIOEE4940 Biostats w her over summer. Inconsistent in responding to questions emailed in abt material (she'll answer some questions in an email but not others??), tested on material that was never taught (as in "oops-here's the R code for that"), sent out an exam for material that hadn't been covered yet (granted, this was quickly fixed).

1780 is heavy on memorization but offers lots of room to succeed (total exams make up 1/3 of grade, the rest is essentially participation). Compared to bioee 1610, 1780 requires more studying and outside work but has a higher median in the end fwiw. Abby clearly cares about her students' learning and is enthusiastic about he material.

My main complaint about Abby's teaching is that recorded lectures were long and repetitive (2x speed is a must). In-person "lectures" were annoying and not very helpful review sessions. She can come across as a bit condescending, but she's at least enthusiastic about the material. I don't think anyone needs to dread her class.
Lectures were meh, lots of work and lectures, wasn't a huge fan of flipped classroom model, but at least the course was easy.

Class is easy but 100% memorization based. You have to learn the entire tree of life, which is rly hard. My semester was online, which made it slightly easier. The profs and TAs are very accessible. Grading is split up into a lot of small things, which means you have to try hard on everything to do well, which is annoying but overall good class.

Passive aggressive for no reason, as someone else mentioned in their rating. We understood the assignment without writing down anything (it was not required, we just had to get the answers), and she tells us as a group “if you guys are guessing I wonder how you’ll guess through the exam”. We weren’t guessing. Be cautious. Simple class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Drake is unnecessarily passive aggressive. We were completing a team assignment in lecture (we did it very quickly without actually doing the assignment), and she came up to us and talked to us for 5 minutes about how we didn't do the assignment (even though we got all the questions right). Beware. Otherwise, the class is really easy.

She's kind of crazy but in a good way. This class uses flipped classroom/active learning, which worked really well for me as a more independent learner -- it's just a heavy workload. They do a great job of teaching the material, rotating lecturers. Abby is very caring and a good communicator. Also interesting material!

This class is essentially entirely online. There are weekly pre-lecture modules containing video lectures and quizzes. Unfortunately, that doesn't mean you can skip the in-person lectures as there are iClicker questions. The content is simple and the prelims were straightforward. Study the learning objectives and memorize the TOL and you're set.

As others said, 1780 has many in-class quizzes. If you do take it, take good notes on the pre-lecture videos, as that's what the exams will actually cover. The material is interesting, and Professor Drake is very nice, but the teaching style didn't work for me. Take BIOEE 1610 if you just want to fulfill the A&S biology distribution requirement.

I'm pretty sure if I took this class in-person it would be a nightmare. She may take things slow during lectures, but the material was fascinating. You can tell that she loves teaching the class. The class was straightforward enough to allow for a strong understanding of material. It did help that I was online and exams were open-note, otherwise...

Dr. Drake seems to have good intentions and did want us to learn. Otherwise, I disliked her as a professor. The class was nothing but painful memorization. The tests were written very unclearly, and the lectures were pointless. I learned more about evolution in the short time we spent on it in my AP bio class in HS.

I don't usually review literally anything, but I loved this course, so I had to. It's an active learning class, with heavy emphasis on class participation through small group activities and iClicker questions. A lot of people don't like this, but I have ADHD and it was beyond perfect. Dr. Drake is great, attentive, and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Drake is the real mastermind behind 1780. She is nice and well meaning, but her voice can be annoying as it constantly sounds on the edge of a nervous breakdown. She is a huge fan of "Active Learning", which basically means tons of in class clicker quizzes. Lectures are pointless otherwise - all the actual teaching is done via videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Awful course. She's the worst lecturer and she runs the course. Prepare to drown in iclicker questions, section assignments, and readings that are really nothing but busywork.

As mentioned previously, not the biggest fan of the structure of the class (way too participation-heavy, interactive, and elementary), but the material itself was very interesting and at times relevant. Exams are easy. Take good notes on/study from vodcasts, show up to lecture and section, and keep up with the material and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is very memorization heavy and the "flipped classroom" can be highly frustrating. A lot of the learning is done through homework, while the actual lecture is a lot of quizzing. However, Abby is very caring and seems to really want her students to do well. Your grade in this class is based on more than just a couple of tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: dull class, lots of pointless memorization.

Makes many mistakes. Not organized at all. Class is all over the place. The interactive classroom thing is not effective. Class is essentially useless if you're not going into evolutionary science. All memorization. Wish I never took it.
Dr. Drake is on the teaching team for an intro bio course (1780) that is heavy on memorization of taxa and phylogenies. If you can memorize you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Took 1780 class can really drag and is a lot of brute memorization of phylogeny and taxa no one would ever need to know unless a researcher in the field nor will remember after the test. Also not the biggest fan of flipped classroom, very little actual material presented about half of class is spent solely on testing

Dr. Abby Drake was one of the professors in the teaching team when I took 1780. She was definitely into the subject she was teaching, but in all honesty, memorization of phylogenetic trees is dull at best. I didn't like her "flipped classroom" method, but that being said, she is a really caring professor who wants to help her students succeed

Hopeless! I feel unfortunate to have chosen this course where she literally relates everything in her life as well as every single thing around her with whi-tie-s for absolutely no reason!!!! This course is at the peak of its negativity and can get no better if she continues teaching it!
Just don't!!!!!
Weird readings, dis cri miN tory articles and a ha. tred filled mind.
The course description is different compares to what actually is taught in the course. A lot of discrepancy exists and this course needs to be STOPPED for God's Sakes!!
Is she mentally stable? Maybe she needs some help. This program needs to conduct a health check-up for their faculty.
If there was a tag for differentiation, I'd add that. She spreads negativity against certain people in her weird course.

What's the ATTITUDE about? Has a major support from the program but lacks respect. She assumes she is EXCLUSIVE and has been mean to students this year. She told me you will be graduating with lesser skills. So basically she is proving that she is NOT a great instructor.
She is the first hire at this program but the worst hire. Racist mentality. Too young to be a professor, she herself is a student and needs some training.
I felt uncomfortable during office hours due to rude comments. I also did not receive support with internship recommendations, which was disappointing.

Dr. Allen is truly a great professor. He is unapologetically himself, and it is so refreshing. It is not often that I come across a challenging class that I look forward to attending. I would highly recommend Dr. Allen to anyone interested in learning about biology, physiology, or life in general.

Amazing professor, made a pretty difficult class bearable. My grade was not because of the professor but my own fault, and if you put more time into learning the material than I did, you can get an A.
Don't be fooled by his jokes, toughest tests ever. You can study for a week straight and still fail, test format just doesn't work for me.

Dr. Allen is an amazing professor. He takes the time to learn everyone's name and really cares about his students. The class had an annoying amount of work (especially in lab) but I learned a lot. I would say the class is mostly busywork and memorization more than anything. Also lots of opportunities to earn points outside of prelims

Dr. Allen is awesome. His class is certaintly difficult, but he is super open to working one on one with you if you are struggling. 100% recommend this professor - he is truly hilarious and one of a kind.
yes yes yes yes Yes yes

Dr. Allen is one of the best professors I have ever had. Not only is he passionate about the subjects he teaches, he is always trying to make sure his students understand the material and is more than happy to answer questions. His lectures are hilarious and he really cares about his students.

It is impossible to have an adult conversation with this professor. If you are looking for any guidance from Dr. Allen, I wouldn't. If you want to get on his good side, just laugh at his jokes (regardless if they're rude or inappropriate)  BUT don't laugh too hard or he might talk about you behind your back. Good luck.

very understanding and funny prof. his jokes in the class are to die for and actually helps rmbr info to study for for exams. exams are reflective of lecture slides (memorize slides to get a good grade). he is a very understanding and kind person and provides so many resources to do well in the class :)

Great teacher and very funny, the perfect person to teach this class. Everything you need for the tests are on the slides, and there are so many TA office hours as well as his own that you can go to if you need help. If you do poorly on tests there are plenty of other assignments that can boost your grade. Study the slides and you'll be fine.

It is impressive that Professor Allen makes everyone feel comfortable talking about reproductive biology. His lectures are fast paced but very entertaining. All the information is on the slides (no readings, hardly any homework). If you study hard for tests you'll get an A.

He is one of the kindest people on campus. He is the perfect person to teach the intro course and makes you feel like you belong immediately on campus. The course is a lot of material, but he gives enough bonus and other non-test opportunities. He makes an effort to know everyone in the class, and with a class of that size, it's amazing.

Class covers a lot of material, but everything is explained so clearly that I always felt prepared before exams. He creates in class activities that are direct reflections of exam material, very helpful for review. Very explicit course expectations, grading is very fair. He is very knowledgeable of the material, and I am glad I took this course.

You need to work hard in this class. Attend lecture + study weekly and you will do well in this class. Dr. Allen puts in 110% to every one of his classes and makes sure that every format is available to his students; lectures, lab, hands on learning, recordings, etc. etc. The TAs also try really hard too and their office hours are very helpful!

He's a “if I tell you the answer you're never going to learn” type of professor (if you get something wrong on an exam you're never going to know why unless a nice TA decides to tell you. He often says something rude and excuses it by saying it's just his humor.

He's a good teacher if you're naturally smart, and he masks his rudeness with being funny. His jokes can be funny, it does make class more interesting. If you're not naturally smart you can study for a rest for two weeks straight and answer all the questions, but still get points taken off for not being specific enough, even if you got most of it.

His teaching style definitely didn't match my learning style and there was a lot of fast paced read off the slides type lectures. That being said, his TAs were super helpful, his slides are detailed, and the lab was well paired with the lectures. If you're confused, just ask your questions and you'll be fine
Dr. Allen is a gem to behold. He is hilarious and engaging. He cares deeply about all of his students and helps them succeed, even with things that do not relate to his class.

Dr. Allen is a great lecturer and makes class interesting even when the topic is boring. the class is very difficult in my opinion but the exams reflect the class material and the grade you receive is very representative how much effort you put into the class. there is a textbook that is provided for extra help but it was not used in class.

Dr. Allen is awesome. Explains all the material well and lets you know exactly what he's looking for on tests. This class has A LOT of content, but is completely doable. Don't need the textbook at all and TAs are a great resource. The total course grade it made up of a lot of smaller things, so a bad grade on a test isn't the end of the world.
By far my favorite professor at Cornell. This class was much easier than domestic but still a challenge. Would recommend him to anyone!!!!

Dr. Allen is awesome! He loves his students and works to see you succeed. Its a very big course with lots of content. Sometimes content is skimmed and prelims can be very difficult, but he makes the class fun

Super funny and great professor, really understanding and loves to get to know his students. This is a super hard class because of how much content there is, but it is doable. Stay on top of studying and go to TA's if you need help with figuring out how to study for this class. I didn't like TA exam grading and how lab was run though.
just take him. Literally my favorite, ever.

Dr. Allen is one of the best professors in the Animal Science department. His classes are difficult but not impossible - you just need to be able to put the work in. He is super personable and really cares for his students. I cannot recommend him enough!

Yes, the course is hard. But Dr. Allen makes it 100x better and much more manageable. If you try your best, he will work with you to help your succeed. He does do random attendance checks, so just beware of that. But overall, this is one of my most favorite classes I have ever taken and most of the reason why is because of Dr. Allen

Avian Management is an easy class compared to 1100 and 2400. He makes the prelims difficult but only because he wants you to study and learn the material instead of brushing the class aside. It was a fun class, and I learned a lot. There's no final but instead a group final project that makes the last month of the semester a little easier on you.

Cornell should pay him triple his salary. His back must hurt from carrying animal science. He's the Michael Jordan of talking about reproduction. If you didn't take BIOAP1100 this class will be really hard, but if you did it will be challenging but easier than domestic. People bring friends not in the class to lecture cause he's that good.

Dr. Allen is a great professor. He is very personable and is always there as someone to talk to if times get tough. Funny guy too; he makes a lot of inappropriate jokes but makes sure to not cross lines and will apologize if he does. Overall, tough course but I learned a lot. He makes sure your education at Cornell is rigorous. Prelims suck though.

Jeremy is the goat. If you disagree you are wrong. He genuinely cares about his students more than any other teacher I've ever had. The class is difficult, but he structures it so that everybody can succeed and offers so much support. He can offer you so much help inside and outside of the class; my Cornell experience is 10x better because of him.

Best professor at Cornell hands down. Hilarious guy, makes you feel so welcome your first year. I suggest any freshman taking Domestic their first semester to get to know him. He helps you so unbelievably much. Get as close as you can to him. Fantastic guy.
Dr.Allen was a top tier professor, I literally take any class I can with him.

It's not a difficult class if you keep up with it, and he's more than fair on every assignment. His exams are extensive, but he will prepare you for every single question. He's funny, but often toes the line. If you put in a little bit of effort to build a rapport with him, you'll find he's very helpful. A mainstay in the animal science department.

Dr. Allen is understanding and caring. You can talk to him about anything. Tests are reasonable for ansc2400 and bioap1100. He is also inspirational and hilarious, incorporating memes into lectures. His lectures are clear and his mode of instruction is among the best professor I've had in cornell. Fantastic professor!

Dr. Allen is a really wonderful professor. He is there to help students who are struggling whether it be with the class itself or with problems outside of class. In both the lecture and the lab he creates an environment conducive to learning and also makes an inclusive space, in and outside of the classroom. Expect to put work into the class.

Dr. Allen is very charismatic and a favorite in the animal science department, evidently. His lectures are engaging and he makes a real effort to foster a comfortable and relaxed classroom environment. His grading is a bit questionable, as he inflates individual assignments but then deflates the class as a whole. Otherwise he is highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man was by far the BEST professor I have ever had. His lighthearted attitude and amazing teaching abilities have allowed me to thrive in his class. He is always SO supportive and such an amazing person to talk to

Dr. Allen is one of the best professors I had in Animal Science. He is compassionate, enthusiastic and extremely reasonable. He wants to make class accessible to everyone and is truly enthusiastic about teaching and the subject matter. He is very open to communication and has a great sense of humor, but that doesn't make his class an easy A.
Dr. Allen is an incredible professor. His classes are engaging and entertaining, and you will learn a lot, however this isn't necessarily an easy class. You have to pay attention and stay engaged.

Absolutely the best professor at Cornell hands down. Cares about his students so much but won't just give you the credit, work hard and you will be rewarded. Most respectable and down to Earth guy you'll find teaching any class. Lectures are interesting and funny. Even people that never had him know of him and think he is amazing.
Hands down my favorite professor. He makes everything fun and engaging and will do his best to make sure that you do yours. The class is not easy, but the content is very clear.

Dr. Allen is by far my favorite professor at Cornell so far. Besides his evident knowledge and passion for the material he teaches, he has a remarkable sense of humor that makes his class extremely engaging and fun. The nature of the course certainly requires lots of memorization so be ready to grind. On the bright side, Dr. A is extremely helpful

Dr. Allen is one of the nicest professors I have ever met. He truly cares about every one of his students. He makes lectures fun with jokes, memes, and stories. You definitely have to study hard to get a good grade, but he also gives out extra credit. He picks really good TAs that are also extremely helpful. I wish all my professors were like Dr. A

Dr. Allen is genuinely kind and understanding. In lectures, he takes time to thoroughly explain concepts while keeping students' attention during longer and complicated topics. He has a fantastic sense of humor but maintains respect. During office hours, he is receptive to all questions and willing to meet additionally for any reason if needed.
Dr. A is probably one of the nicest profs you'll have the luck to learn under at Cornell. He will listen to you, help whenever he can and honestly, do his darndest to make sure you don't flunk.

He's a nice guy with a great sense of humor, but don't let that fool you into believing that you can get away without studying. Prelims and quizzes require a huge amount of memorization to do well on, so try to avoid this class if you aren't ready to grind.

Dr. Allen is an amazing person who can teach very well, but expect to study very hard for this class -- lots of memorization needed. Really unavoidable as it is an ANSC requirement, if you are having trouble start meeting with him when the semester begins. He lets you retake your lowest test, and the final is usually multiple choice.

Dr. Allen is a great professor. Lectures are always organized and clear, and he is always very transparent about what material you need to know. Gives plenty of extra credit and is flexible with deadlines. He is very understanding of his students and just overall a very genuine person. Best ansci course I've taken at Cornell.
a jocular and knowledgeable professor. Never stop thinking for the students, exams are very fair as long as you study.

Hand down, this was the best class I have taken so far. He is hilarious and makes sure as long you do what you need to do he will help you pass. He cares about his students and offers many resources to make sure you understand the material before the test.

Professor Allen is the best professor I've had at Cornell thus far. He genuinely cares about his students, and it is clear that he truly wants us to learn and understand the material. His tests are never designed to be unfair or unnecessarily fastidious, but rather to fairly judge what we have learned so far. He is enthusiastic and compassionate.

Dr. Allen is by far my favorite professor at Cornell. Absolutely hilarious, makes learning really fun and easy. Course content is very manageable and exams are fair. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit. I'm going to miss this class a lot and wish I could take it again with him.
Dr. Allen is one of the best professors and individuals I've had the pleasure of receiving. He is absolutely hilarious and cares a lot about his students. I wish I could take his class over again!
Wonderful, informative class

Dr. Allen is a great person and professor. He cares about his students and gives engaging lectures. One of the best professors I've had, and repro is not my thing. He doesn't grade on a curve, but he's willing to give extra credit. If you go to class, he makes it pretty clear what kind of stuff will be on the exam, but he's a good lecturer anyway.

Dr. Allen is the best!! If you are a dairy student struggling through the ANSC required classes, don't worry he does a lot of lectures that tie into basic dairy knowledge with regard to repro. It is challenging, but only if you make it that way. Attend lecture, take notes by hand, go to review sessions, and ask questions!

I loved Dr. Allen!! He really cares about his students doing well. While he doesn't believe in curving, he gives many free points and always offers extra credit opportunities. He will always tell you exactly the topics you should study before prelims. He's hilarious and his stories related to the topic he's lecturing about are always so funny! :)
Dr. Allen is truly the best professor I've had at Cornell. The class isn't easy but the lectures are understandable and enjoyable. He's a wonderful person.
Hard class, grade teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is very well organized, with plenty of help available when needed. Office hours are especially useful for clarifying material. The professor lectures clearly, though the course can be challenging without prior experience in proofs. Homework and exams are demanding but help reinforce key concepts and prepare you well.

The lectures are good, but the textbook is infinitely better (note: there's a slight difference between the lectures and the textbook with NFAs and Thompson's construction, because the textbook doesn't allow NFAs to have lambda transitions but the lectures do). The grading is also very pedantic.

anke is a fantastic cs2800 professor, definitely take it with her. lectures were extremely well prepared and interesting. the hw and prelims are definitely challenging, but they help you understand material at a deeper level and are still fairly manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: ANKE MY GOAT!! Discrete math isn't easy but her lectures were very good at explaining difficult concepts -- I even ended up enjoying the subject! Tests are very fair/doable and we got a lot of good resources to prepare. The hw she writes also significantly improved my understanding. If you must take CS2800 take it with Anke.

Yes the class it hard but Anke makes it bearable. Nobody wants to take 2800 but she genuinely cares for her students and made the lectures very informative. I will say that the final was very hard. Honestly, if I had to take the class again, I would take it with Anke.

I have taken two classes with her and have not enjoyed either of them. She has an incredible ability to make content more confusing and boring at the same time. Her exams and homework are moderately difficult, but combined with the complete lack of support and poor lectures they become very hard. I would stay away from any of her future classes.
My favorite professor at Cornell, if you have the chance to take her courses, you should

Anke is an incredible lecturer who has an excellent grasp of the material and really challenges you to think during her lectures. I would definitely recommend going to class as much as possible if you have her.

This class was fairly difficult but Anke was a great professor and really helped to explain the material. Her lectures were very engaging and clear. The homework and tests were a bit hard but the class as a whole was a very positive experience largely due to Anke.

My advice, use the textbook, lecture slides were made off the textbook. Anke was enthusiastic and caring, but sometimes skimmed through topics. The key is to visit office hours, as long as you do HW well, you are set for the exam. Discrete math may require some creativity but once you notice the patterns its manageable. Poll for attendance.

Class is so hard but it's one of the hardest CS classes notoriously so I don't know what else you'd expect there. As a person, she's wonderful. Amazing lecturer and explains well. She cares deeply about her students as well and is absolutely lovely. You may not get an amazing grade in this class but it is a fair class overall.

Retaliates if a student knows more than her.
She is not as savvy as they portray her.

I took Algo with Professor Anke in FA23. Her lectures were easy to understand yet fascinating, delivered with humor, and provoked further exploration of topics through the textbook and other sources. The homework was hard, but really grinding it ensured success on exams. Her teaching has inspired me to continue studying algorithms more in-depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class cause I had to. I was lowkey depressed juggling the workload of this class and other classes. Word of advice, find a really good TA and religiously go to their OH for the PSETs. She is a good lecturer, but the tests are extremely hard. Think around 55% on each test. Also, don't cheat for any hw, she puts up fake answers online.

This class is the definition of artificial difficulty. PSET problems are intentionally detached from the actual material we learn in class solely to make them more difficult. I would learn far more with completion-based PSET grading rather than flushing my time down the toilet. Camping office hours should never be required to do well on homework.

Anke van Zuylen is a passionate lecture who makes discrete much more interesting than daunting. Psets are typically very doable, and are graded rather fairly. Office hours are super extensive, and certain TAs are just as passionate and good at explaining the material as Anke is. Office hours are incredibly well structured, class is interesting.

Anke van Zuylen is a passionate lecturer who makes a daunting subject interesting. Problem Sets can be difficult, but are intellectually stimulating. Office Hours are hosted by TAs who are just as passionate as Anke about the subject, so they are a great source of additional help, and are very structured.

Lectures are generally done well and the material is presented in an engaging way, but the material does not always carry over to the assignments. It is very possible to attend all the lectures, understand the material, and still pull C's on exams because of harsh grading.
Was incredibly misled by past reviews. In class lectures are superficial and do not carry over well to HWs and exams.
Good prof, but I am straight up not having a good time.
Wouldnt take unless absolutely necessary or have a background in PROOF BASED math. Dont be fooled by the high ratings, not a bad professor but incredibly overhyped. Exams and psets are challenging.
The psets and exams were so difficult I considered dropping out multiple times.
I highly recommend if you can wait a semester to take it with a different professor if they have easier hws/prelims her prelims and hws were both really hard

One of the best professors I have ever encountered. I love how she is open to hearing any of the ideas we have and truly cares about each of the students.
Suggestions for taking Anke's course: listen carefully and follow tight in lecture, clear up questions right after the lecture. And you are in good shape!
good

Anke's lectures were probably the best I've ever attended at Cornell. She wrote them out on blank slides every class, allowing us to go through content at a reasonable pace. Also very willing to discuss questions. The textbook, although not strictly necessary, was highly useful in doing well. Definitely recommend!!!

Anke's lectures were incredibly well put together and went through every detail of course content in excellent detail. Homework was sometimes lengthy, but definitely worth it in improving understanding.

Anke was one of the best professors I've had. She was proficient at teaching the course material and consistently motivated ideas. She also clearly cares about the mental health of her students, as she decreased the difficulty of the class halfway through. That said, this was also one of the hardest courses I've taken, which is normal for algo.

Anke is very sympathetic and cares about her students. She is an engaging professor and conveys the information well. It is difficult to find good STEM professors, but she is one of them. I have heard amazing things from other classes she teaches as well. Highly recommend taking a course taught by her.

This FWS is 2x the work of others, but you emerge with a very solid grasp on expository writing and maybe even a new worldview. You also get helpful advice from your TA--most FWS's lack one. Dr. G himself is an acquired taste. To some, he is refreshingly blunt; to others, he seems self-important. To the former camp (me), he's pretty fun to talk to.

This class gives you what you put in.. or so I thought. Take this class if you need to fulfill FWS and don't mind getting a high B or low A. Professor is caring and the class lectures are extremely surface-level. The real education is when you do the readings and write on your own. I recommend just reading John Berger's "Ways of Seeing" instead.

Awesome Professor! His class improved my writing significantly. He was especially helpful in individual meetings and always gave insightful feedback on my work. I believe, however, that this class grades harsher relative to other FWS. If you want an easy A, this is not the class for you. If you want to improve your writing, then I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Fun and Engaging! Great Professor if your main goal is to improve your writing capabilities, Otherwise it isn't worth it to take the class as a freshman, grading is comparatively harsh compared to other offerings, with courses offering B's just by showing up to class, choose those if you are just trying to fulfill your FWS requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Mostly lectures and tended to go over the time of the class by like 10 minutes consistently. Somewhat easy but lowkey didn't complete the amount we were supposed to finish the semester so the next semester we had to do more to make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very enjoyable professor, very knowledgeable and open to questions. All material is on printed notes handed out each class, but not much of it will make sense if you don't go to lecture. I did have his class in the late afternoon and his voice put me to sleep several times, but not for lack of interesting content.

Great professor. Really laid back, doesn't give many homework assignments or tests. Essentially, he'll teach the amount you're willing to learn. We read Ovid--about as interesting as Nussbaum himself, but it's not like classes are dreadfully boring.Very nice, funny man. Looks like he's headed towards retirement, take a class of his while you can.
It was a fantastic class.
It was an amazing class!

Engaging content in the lectures. Overall a fun course. Was pretty chill, we were allowed cheat sheets for exams. People in previous years seemed to give negative reviews, but they likely did not go to class/did not pay attention. Asking questions during lectures will help you understand a lot, and the professor gives pretty detailed responses.

He really stepped it up since last spring because most (all?) of the issues are irrelevant now. Clear grading, fair exams, strong support system in OH and after lectures, assignments are well spread out throughout the semester. The syllabus is also refreshed now to include more recent topics like NeRFs, transformers, semantic segmentation, etc.

This isn't the worst course I've ever taken, but it's definitely up there. The material is interesting, but the course is so disorganized that it makes it hard to care about the material. Almost all of our assignments were shoved into the last month of the course. Lectures are boring, slide decks are not organized, and staff support is non-existent
boring lecture. I feel like I barely learned from this course, even though I did well

Seriously disorganized class. Gives us about 2 assignments in the first 90% of the semester and then drops 4 towards the last 2 weeks of class. Review material has no answers, frequently canceled office hours, and no help on ed discussion.  Terrible grading scale as well which was final despite half the class doing not as well as he expected.

This may have been one of the most disorganized classes I have taken. The TAs in this course were useless and assignments were graded extremely late. It feels like the relaxed grading scale was used to make up for the faults of the course. Luckily Bharath is a somewhat decent lecturer.
Get ready for a few out of syllabus questions.

Very hard prelim and final exams with unfair marking scheme (no partial marks, though assignments and prelim had). Did not look at my regrade requests or provide finals solution sheet. Almost 300 students per class with high level of cheating on untimed take home exam. Very bad student support almost nil interaction with professor in crucial times.
Great professor, knows the content super well. Very nice and approachable after class. Gives good suggestions on research/professional-related questions.
Great professor, the course covers a good amount. Explained things really well. Projects were fun to do.
Excellent professor and can explain topics very clearly. Could answer any question any student has instantly, and explain the answer very well.

The class wasn't much work, and the written homeworks and exams were very relevant. However, the projects were more programming-focused, so many hours were spent debugging code that I would rather have spent learning new concepts. Most of the class is dedicated to classical computer vision, and the last few weeks are spent on ML topics.
What kind of professor leaves most of the work ungraded, provides little to no lecture notes, and drops us in the deep end for exams? A very bad one.
A very very bad class.
Lectures were messy, half of the assignments were not graded, little to no feedback or prep. Avoid.
Ive never taken such a disorganized course.
Good teacher and explains material well. Decent slides and tests are pretty fair. However, assignments can be pretty confusing.

Unclear and sparse slides, virtually no exam preparation materials, unresponsive course staff, messy handwriting, unclear and bug -ridden programming assignments, changing syllabus, unfair grading guidelines, dry material.

Despite what the comments below say, Bharath cares a lot about all his students and tries to make the content as understandable as possible. This semester new projects were tried out and though the documentation was bad, he cleared up any misconceptions about the projects. Great to talk to and very approachable
Terribly managed course.
Projects and assignments widely out of sync with lectures. Incomprehensible lectures. Terse slides.

Lectures are well planned, and most of the learning is visual. Lecture notes are enough for a good understanding of the material and, most of the homework can be solved by just relying on it. Since the course projects are research-oriented, he grades them by looking at the amount of effort you put in and what you have learned from it.

Ms. Happiness is genuinely one of the greatest teachers that i have ever had. She is very understanding and cares very much about building a community with the students of her classes, makes class feel like a family.

Bi Happiness is one of the best professors out there! She is so nice and caring! I took this class as a language requirement, but it ended up being my favorite class of the semester. For learning a new language, Bi Happiness makes it super enjoyable and easy. Weekly assignments help you improve both speaking and writing. 10/10 would recommend
Most of the submitted class work is online and 4 days a week short lectures mainly focus on reviewing homework and in class discussions

Happiness is the best language professor/teacher I have ever had. She is unbelievably caring and genuinely interested in her students. Swahili is a fun language to learn and Happiness creates a low-stress environment to do so. I look forward to her class every day and no Friday classes are a perk :) I highly, highly recommend!!

I love Happiness so much. I've learned a lot of Swahili from her and would encourage anyone to take her class. If you want to skim by and get an A, it's totally doable. If you really wanted to learn Swahili that's doable too. What you put into this course is what you get out of it. I love starting my day with Happiness and my Swahili class

Bulugu is, simply put, a great professor. Swahili with her is always fun and is an easy course so long as you put in just a little time going over vocab/grammar each week. Because of the small class size, you'll definitely bond with your classmates. Only good things to say.

not the nicest, expects everyone to know things from courses that are not pre-reqs. Does the socratic style of teaching but the questions he will prompt you with are not helpful and condescending. gives no examples. Rarely grades on time.

Very knowledgeable, the course definitely provides a good preview for prospective matscis. Baker has this idea that the ideal test mean is a 50, so the tests are correspondingly difficult, but the class is curved so don't be scared. Labs and homework were pretty substantial, but they did help me learn the material better.

Fantastic teacher!! Very nice and reasonable to talk to, and motivated to teach students!! A bit of memorization, but also has conceptual stuff.. i agree with the other person, the grading is definitely pretty weird. Like my friends who are smarter than me did worse than me but I'm also really organized, so being organized is key!!

Interesting class, great professor, but designed like a highschool class. Your grade has little to do with how much you know the material and can figure out, but lots to do with how well your work is organized, and how you show it. You'll get little credit if a careless arithmetic error is made. Put stuff that wasn't asked for or you lose points!

He's a great person, always friendly, and not unreasonable when his grading or teaching is questioned. He is also very thorough (but sometimes not very clear) in lecture. However, he does have some irritating habits which hurt my ability to learn in the class like starting a new topic in lecture with 2 or 3 minutes left of class.

His teaching style is absolutely dreadful. He does not explain to help you visualize the concept, his most used phrase is "it turns out that, this is equal to..." To make it more confusing, there are course notes online, textbook, and his lectures, all cover different things. He is very friendly, but going to lecture is a pain. I dropped the class.

Professor Baker is the friendliest professor I've ever had. MSE 2610 is  the hardest class I've taken thus far, but it also has taught me a lot. I would definitely recommend taking a class with Baker, but if you're not a material science major or minor, it might be too time consuming.
pretty hard class, dun take it unless it's necessary.

Teaches quickly and covers a lot. Deluge of information, only half the equations are tested (the major ones). Occasional in-class demonstrations. Group labs (3) are harder than necessary and an exercise in lab write-ups and delegation (little learned from them). Homeworks and tests are hard (but at least can make a cheat sheet). Friendly in person.

good class. His exams are open book. Most of the problems are similar to the homeworks. He is approachable and friendly. Only problem is that he teaches a bit too slowly at the semester beginning and rushes through at the end with a lot of homeworks and quizzes.
Extraordinarily well-organized, very clear notes and lecture.  Hard work, but do-able.  Baker is approachable and very good at conveying information and comprehension.  Excellent professor!
No Comments

Worst professor I've ever had. Extremely unclear notes. Randomly introduces things without much explanation. A very very terrible teacher. Especially, his notes are extremely unclear and hard to understand. Nice guy, but very bad professor. Sorry guys, but try to avoid him if you can.
Terrible notes (bad handwriting and lots of errors). Good guy though. Only assigns 1 hw half the semester and all of a sudden assigns more hw and quizzes during the exam week. Poor lecturing style.
He showed a great interest in making sure you understood material.  Went out of his way to explain things on his own time past office hours.
Taught straight from notes without explaining much. Confused the hell out of me sometimes. Can tell that he knows his stuff though. Pretty boring too.
Despised us all for our ignorance but good natured about it. Okay class

Lectures interesting but office hours w/ him were useless- he once spent 1hr teaching a group of us the WRONG way to solve a problem. Homeworks constantly being revised b/c of mistakes- tests are extremely hard! Labs/assignments disorganized
He makes you work hard, but you learn *alot*!  Easy to talk to and all around nice guy.
i loved the class, though it was hard...
One of the best classes I've taken :) Not easy, but worth it.
great lectures
Excellent Prof! Great course

Do not take this class if you don't like scientific writing. All he grades you on is the accuracy of your thoughts and not your writing. Class is also boring and he overcomplicates ideas for no reason. Grade is made up of 5 essays with no homework but you have 20+ page readings before class. If you want a fun and easy FWS, this is not for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take his class.
Great professor. Some of the topics can be confusing at times. He is super helpful outside of class. The only thing is that the subject was too philosophical for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Gives a lot of useful comments. Don't be scared by the philosophical words! Flexible deadlines.

Take his FWS. Interesting, sometimes confusing concepts, but he cares a lot about his students and will review drafts and devote many hours to helping his students. Compared to other FWS, this class is not a lot of work.

Professor Bush is deeply committed to ensuring his students enjoy the learning process. He is very accommodating and often shares stories about his home life and family, which shows that he genuinely values building meaningful connections with his students. While the material can be complex at times, just continue to ask questions and participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor. Makes the content very interesting and gives a lot of useful feedback.
You can tell he really cares about his students and is very passionate about the content he teaches.

Professor Bush is a great person; he is super kind and clearly cares about his students. From providing feedback and his fair grading, Bush wants his students to succeed. He brings a joyous and fun class environment. Take his FWS classes

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. Super super chill and, especially for an FWS, there is not a lot of work and there is no attendance. Four three-page papers throughout the semester and then quite a long paper at the end but he guides you through most of the writing. Wants students to succeed and it super into the class he teaches.
Clearly has passion for propulsion, very kind person and intelligent also
Fisher is the goat, love her. I think I may become a professional thermophysicist or thermomatician or whatever you call it because of her. Shout out to Sadi Carnot

One of my favorite lecturers at Cornell. Clearly very passionate about her work and her students. Takes time to thoroughly address questions during lecture. Her teaching style is extremely engaging and she makes the material fun to learn!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a great lecturer!! I am not a fan of thermodynamics, but she makes it way easier to understand and talks her way slowly through material that makes it easier to understand.

She's a great professor! The grading for homework assignments and exams is very fair. Most of the assignments were done in groups; lecture attendence is vital. The textbook is needed for the assignments, but not so much for learning the content.

By far the best professor Ive had at Cornell. Besides being an amazing lecturer, she really cares about her students and their well-being. This was clearly evident through the rocky semester we had this fall. Shes extremely fair with her homework assignments and tests. Would definitely take a class with her again.

Hands down best professor I've had at Cornell. Didn't know what a meaningful lecture was until I had her as a lecturer. I only used the textbook as a supplement to study, but it wasn't really necessary. VERY fair exams, not easy, just fair given what we cover in class and on the HW. Actually cares about students & our wellbeing!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, kept people engaged. Homeworks and tests were very fair. Always willing to help/

While the course was not too difficult, I found many things very frustrating. She frequently had to repost homeworks and grades (even edit questions during tests) due to mistakes. I found the homeworks time consuming but not unnecessary. The lectures were sometimes disorganized and the notes (posted afterward) were difficult to read

Her lectures are very clear, the material is engaging but not too difficult. The homeworks and exams are very fair. She clearly cares about her students. She sometimes comes to the next lecture with slides prepared to better answer student questions from the lecture before.
Such a great professor who really cares about people learning!

Lectures were very well organized and easy to follow. Covered a wide range of propulsion topics and went appropriately in-depth with most of them. Weekly homeworks that weren't too difficult, were usually engaging and applicable. Office hours were always very helpful.
Homeworks are done in groups, which in my experience is a great way to learn. Professor Fisher definitely cares about her students and makes every effort to help them out.
Great professor--her lectures were pretty clear, and the exams were fair.

Class can be boring sometimes. However, she is very clear and organized. Tests/homework are very fair, and her lecture notes are thorough and clear. Not the most enjoyable class (distribution requirement), but Prof. Fisher overall does a great job of conveying the material.
Professor Canuedo is very cobfusing and the TAs are not very competent too. Hard and confusing tests, I really dislike the way that this class is run

This course is not particularly difficult, but there are many issues with the way it's run and taught. It's clear that the course is lazily-structured: the homeworks and exams are written badly and are very unclear with what they're asking, and the professor lacks the ability to explain topics. From my experience, I would not recommend.

She is not a great lecturer. She goes really fast during lectures and jumps from topic to topic so be ready to take notes and lock in the whole time, or just self study. She also has an accent which can be hard to pick up sometimes. The workload was alright with group problem sets and mostly just exams.
The teaching was bad. I wouldn't recommend it.
CURVED DOWN EVERYONE'S GRADES BY A HALF-LETTER. Does not follow her own grading rubric. Reads directly off of slides in thick accent. Homeworks not related to lecture material. Do not recommend.
rushes through slides in class despite TAs asking her to slow down and struggles to answer questions clearly, leaving the TAs to carry the class.
This course gave me foundational knowledge about markets, inflation, unemployment, interest rates. Very applicable things that have a lot of value. A must to understand the real world
Professor Caunedo is inspirational. She is teaching tough material and I liked her style of bringing it down to real world examples.

I have learnt a ton for this course. The professor was available to answer questions outside class and always clear when asked for clarification. My letter grade was wrong and was freaking out because of internship applications but she fixed it by the morning after.

Enraged by Econ 3040. Lectures are unclear, and grading is arbitrary and inconsistent between exams. Content unclear throughout. The stats are concerning, but prof said it's normal. Unresponsive before final. Got sick (102° fever), but makeup would mean "I" on the transcript. Never been so frustrated with a course.
Terrible clarity in class and absolutely did not follow syllabus grading. Never take a class with her.
Terrible professor. Doesn't know what she's teaching. Grading couldn't be more random. Doesn't stick to her own syllabus. Managed to curve grades down. Never take her class.

Professor Caunedo disregarded syllabus grading and gave much lower grades for many students than was outlined in the provided syllabus. The lectures were difficult to follow, yet the content was easy to digest once reviewed outside of class. Highly recommend taking a different professor for 3040 if possible
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor really funny. She let you to drop a prelim and replaced by a higher final score, deeply cares about the growth of students. I would definitely recommend this. One of the most caring professors I have at Cornell so far

Professor and nice and really funny, keeps lectures lighthearted. Homeworks and exams start hard, but it seems to all click around the final few weeks. 

Attendance not mandatory, but save yourself confusion and extra hours studying by going.

Highly enjoyed 3040 with Caunedo! Learning curve was tough, but she lets you replace prelims with your final if it's higher, so there's chance for a comeback. Cracks jokes in class and asks questions during lecture - I struggle with focus but she was able to keep me engaged. I liked her "MBA-flavor" (as she put it) - would recommend her for 3040.

her class is a learning curve. I started out doing so bad but ended up with good grade once I got used to her exam style and her lecture style. Homework is graded sorta harshly but seems like she curved the class generously
She cares about the students. Lectures are dense, but I feel I learnt a bunch.
Don't recommand. Most boring class ever. She reads through the slide. Heavy accent. Exams aren't really hard though. She's not awful, she just can't catch anybody's attention.

Macroeconomics is very dry material but was delivered very-well in an MBA setting, I really liked that the material was tied to the current economy. Her lectures are intense, maybe the models could be simplified a little so things are better understood, but I like that she facilitated discussions that came up in class instead of shutting them down.

Professor Julieta, while bright, doesn't seem to understand that many MBA students do not have a background in economics. She never manages to finish what she planned for a lecture in just ONE lecture, and crams an absurd amount of information in every sentence she says. With her heavy accent as well, classes become impossible to understand.
Really bad class organization Never able to finish class material as planned Discussion always went out of the way Speak too fast mostly mumbling with heavy accent

Caunedo is knowledgeable but really bad at teaching. Struggles to explain basic concepts, skips important points and rambles a lot. Has a heavy accent, if you are not good at deciphering accents, go with another professor.

Nice but relatively new -- slides still had some errors, but she corrected them in class. Does a pretty good job explaining in lecture. Discussion helps too.   Practice prelim/finals from previous semesters weren't very exemplary of the actual prelims/final, especially the 2014 ones.   HW was easy (1-2 hrs/pset). Tests were easy, uncurved.
very nice

She sometimes made mistakes on the slides, but was quick to clarify. This might be because it was her first year teaching though. She's generally very helpful and as long as you understood the lecture slide deck, the problem sets were not too challenging.
New professor. Not super comfortable in front of the class. Would constantly change her mind on statements of theorems when questioned. Extremely nice and willing to help if asked though.

Nice teacher, but first year teaching. Understands concepts, but can't really teach students. She doesn't follow a book, so you have to go to lecture. A lot of students have trouble understanding. Would recommend taking other ECON3040.   Bottom line: she can't teach, but her tests are fair.
good teacher, prelims are exactly what is on the lecture. Nothing surprising about this class. Be prepared to spend your entire sundays before prelims studying.

such a sweet prof and seems passionate ab what he does. the exams were very reflective of lecture slides and the lectures were basically just the profs reading off the slides which was great imo since it was relatively easy to study for. (just memorize all the slides fully).

Just a chill guy who loves cells. His lectures are kinda boring but they get to the point. Hardly any homework for this class and you do not need to read the textbook. 2-3 days prior to exams study super hard and you should be fine, for the rest just do the 1 weekly homework. If you do well enough on the 4 prelims, you can skip the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fromme is very knowledgable, passionate about biology, and enjoys teaching and coming to class each day. He's easy going and very accessible either after class or during his office hours. He explains concepts well and calculates your class grade 1 of 3 ways in order to give you the best score possible.

Fromme's lectures were extremely boring and consisted of him reading from the slides; what made this class hard was the exams bc there is so much info and the tests are literally designed to trick you and make you not do well; don't need to attend lecture, but you should read the textbook and go to office hours; pick a diff. bio class if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: first off you don't need to read the textbook even if he heavily encourages it. He's a cool guy who just wants everybody to learn about cells. It's structured in a very understandable way that builds in a way where the pieces fit together. Lots of options for grading so don't worry about failing a prelim. Exams just memorize big ideas from slides.

Fromme is a fantastic person and professor. He genuinely cares about the course and students and is clearly very passionate about the subject matter. Do at least some of the readings and study and you will do well in this course.

Such a great lecturer although he speaks fast at times. Content is very manageable. 1350 as a class overall is hard but he made it super enjoyable. He is one of the lecturers in combination with Kelly Liu, and he was definitively missed once his part of the course was over.

I already miss Fromme. Probably my favorite professor at Cornell. Prof. Fromme cares about his students and tests us on what we know instead of what we don't know like some other classes at Cornell. He genuinely cares about our learning and engages with us, even if it's nerdy/cheesy jokes (my favorite). The class is test heavy but if very do-able!
understandable lectures, but can't always help when the material is tough. he clearly enjoys teaching tho and is pretty helpful and engaging

I think he's a great lecturer, really clear on his explanations. However, he was not helpful in person sometimes. He did not have office hours and was inaccessible many times. Tests are becoming harder every year, but still pretty manageable. But overall nice guy. (Second part of the class makes me miss him)
Very funny and moves quickly through the material. He's very energetic and genuinely interested in your learning. One of my favorite professors.

He's really straightforward and funny in lectures, makes it very engaging. He also had more in-lecture polling questions than Dr.Helmann and Dr.Pesciotta, and that helped me understand and engage with the topic more. Generally a really fun bio class, especially if you have a bit of background (e.g. IB HL Biology). Loved his martial art shirts.
1440 made bio feel like one big, weirdly logical story, and Buchon explains it super clearly (with just enough humor) that I actually looked forward to lecture.

Professor Buchon is excellent! BIOG 1440 was challenging, but it's remarkable how far we dove into physiology for an intro class. His clear explanations and enthusiasm made the complexity fascinating and rewarding.

I thought he was a pretty good prof, but his lectures were the most difficult for me to understand out of the 3 profs. His were so extremely content-dense that it was nearly impossible to actually memorize everything. Though the material was extremely interesting, and I thoroughly enjoyed learning it all, even though it took a lot of work to do so.

I had the pleasure of being in Professor Buchon's class this semester, and I must say it was an absolutely enriching experience. I highly recommend their class for anyone interested in physiology, especially if you plan on taking the MCAT
I really liked his style of teaching. He mixes clear explanations, with physiological problem sets and I really got a sense I learned a lot. A must have for premeds

Taking Professor Buchon's physiology class was super cool! He made it easy for us to get what he wwas talking about. He really cared about us doing well and was always there to help out, whether it's explaining stuff after class or using fun ways to teach. I'd totally recommend his class to anyone who wants to learn about how their body works!

Great professor who cracks a lot of jokes. he deals with the most complicated lectures in class but make them very accessible. Follow in class. This helps a lot! Accessible professor outside of class.
Very good professor that made complicated concepts pretty clear. Very accessible outside of class, supportive and quite funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really nice professor

Really funny professor, wrote the easiest out of the four prelims. I thought his lectures were the most entertaining and very clear. Very heavy french accent but still not hard to understand. His prelim was not too detailed oriented. Loml

Dr. Buchon is, in my opinion, the best 1440 instructor! His slides are very clear. His lecture was thorough and his explanations was extremely clear. He takes hard physiology concepts and explains it in a way that's really easy to understand. He's very accessible outside of class and holds extra office hours before exams so we get the help we need.

His videos were helpful, but it is a little hard to understand his French accent. His lectures were pretty engaging and thorough. The class is moderately difficult. There's lecture videos, readings, and mandatory quizzes twice a week, 4 prelims, optional final, and attendance is not mandatory. Prelims are tricky. Don't take if not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: best 1440 lecturer, with very clear presentations, slides, and grading criteria. organizes and explains things very well and grades super fairly. the only problem I've ever heard from people about him is his accent, but I never had any issue (it's french, if anyone is wondering) wish he taught the entire semester!

From the three instructors in BioG1440, Pr. Buchon was the most interesting and clear.
Easy to talk to and mentions in class what the test will be on.
Lectures are content heavy, but complex concepts are well explained.
