Prof Buchon's slides and lectures were by far the most clear and easy to understand. I felt like the topics he taught were some of the more difficult ones, but his explanations and heavy use of in-class practice questions helped a lot. He also pushed back a prelim when he knew the students were stressed about other emergency matters.

The ability to watch the recorded lectures is what carries this class. All the information you need for the exams are in the recorded lectures, and the three professors that teach this class have plenty of office hour times to help with understanding the lectures. The discussion sections are great fun, with great experiments. JOIN BIOG1044! GL

An interesting class where you will learn a lot about physiology. Contrary to what is said in the syllabus, it is heavy in human physiology and not so much focused on other organisms. Pr. Buchon really explained well complicated concepts.
Intelligent and thoughtful professor with interactive lectures. Explains topics well. The way the class is curved is annoying.

I really loved the lectures of Pr. Buchon, they were very structured and the problems were well explained. I took AP biology so have seen some of that content before, but this was way more structured.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved the lecture of Professor Buchon on how microbes influence physiology. Coolest lecture ever. It made me think a lot.

I actually loved BioG1440 and especially the section taught by Buchon. The exams were very fair, you really just have to listen to what he says in class. The other instructors were a bit less clear, but overall a good class. Exams come one day apart from chem, this was tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took BIOG1440 with Buchon, Shapleigh, and Selveraj in FA 2020. Class had both synchronous and asynchronous lecture components. Buchon's slides and lectures were by far the most comprehensive and he emphasized topics that were likely to be tested. Compared to the other two professors Buchon was by far the best.
The course itself is difficult but Buchon explains things in a very clear and understandable way. He does have an accent that can be heavy at times, but his way of teaching is great
There were 3 instructors for this class and they were really uneven. The body physiology is really the coolest part. Advice: go to office hours!
I am very thankful for this professor's time. He hold something like 10 extra office hours sessions before prelim and these really help.

Professor Buchon had very good powerpoints, but his thick French accent sometimes made it difficult to understand him. BIOG 1440 itself is difficult and very memorization heavy, but I think he explained concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. He made some complicated subjects feel quite simple!

Dr Buchon was very helpful during the semester. I started with a bad score during my first prelim, but thanks to TAs and Professors' office hours, I kept increasing my score. Dr Buchon advices were really helpful
Dr Buchon explained everything we needed to know very clearly and plainly. I was glad to get to study from him

Dr. Buchon is a great professor and really cares about his students and the subject material. Very easy to understand and available for extra help during office hours. I went every week. He is passionate about physiology and you will learn a lot from him. I wish I could take more courses with him!
Great teacher. Loved it!

Great introduction to physiology. Has been recommended to me by my academic mentor as a premed. This course is very time-consuming course but also very rewarding and practical to understand human physiology.

The material is difficult but presented very clearly. Exams are fair; but you better go to review sessions. This professor is very accessible, he will spend time with you until you understand things. There is a lot of information so better study from the start. Thankfully the final is not cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This professor really helped me organize to study for my exams. In addition, he took ample time to explain the material even after exams, or to explain what I was missing in my exam. This class is my last requirement and this helped a lot!

He's amazing! If you put your all into his classes you will be rewarded. Yes it will be the hardest class of your life but you will not regret a single moment- be sure to take advantage of office hours and ask questions!
The lectures are amazing. I consider changing major and taking more biology because of this class.
He was sooo helpful during review sessions!!!
Fantastic professor. He makes everything clear !
I loved that class. But it was clearly the toughest since I started at Cornell !
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took that class as an external student. The content was very interesting, and challenging. I really appreciated the feedback from the Professor, who answered all my questions quickly.
Great class. But the curving really makes it difficult to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is quite interesting but tough on non bio majors. The course goes quite in depth which requires a lot of memorization. Overall a very interesting class for premeds.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A very solid class for physiology
This class was terrible- so disorganized, the material was not presented in a clear way and it was very unclear what we were meant to learn. Class objectives were not meant

she is thorough, smart, and caring. i wish they had her teach the entire program, she is genuine and very encouraging professionally. please bring her back and make her a full time professor for cybersecurity and contract law

Dr. Nateram was in a roundtable and development chat, and she went the extra mile to show everyone principles of a good contract and also talked about cybersecurity how important it is to review data we put into AI models and how we store information. She is so sweet and smart, if you get a chance to take her class, do it!

It's an ivy league school, so expect it to be challenging and difficult. Not sure about the other ratings but i learned alot from her and the course. I really like cornell's professional development classes and all the professors they have. Celina always took the time to have a coffee chat with students after going through the materials. 10/10

I really loved her instruction on my courses at Cornell and despite my challenges between being a busy mom and having a career, she made the time to respond to all my questions and genuinely felt she cared about the well being of students. I love Cornell and having professors like her.

Celina was an OUTSTANDING instructor for the Power and Ethics in Negotiation class.Her energy, intelligence and teaching style made the live sessions both fun and informative. She provided meticulous feedback, showing genuine care for students' growth.Cornell's cert programs are pricey but worth the investment, I'd love to take more of her courses.

One of the few classes I've felt fully immersed into when going to class. Participation is a large part of class which became very productive over time helping me learn how to look at material differently. Grading based on criteria and improving, so it becomes a class you can enjoy material for instead of stressing your grade. Great teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is very nice, who encourages you to answer questions and participate in class discussions. The class atmosphere is chill and respectful. She grades you based on completion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She's really nice and grades based on personal improvement and completion. Classes include a lot of close reading, working with peers, and discussion.

COGST1101 was a mixed bag. There were times when it was very interesting and thought-provoking, and other times when there were no thoughts to be had. The format of the class is not great, as most of the time, students are giving presentations on the content and not Casasanto. If she taught more, I think her class would be more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes. A good amount of reading but no homework, I enjoyed her lectures. I didn't like having to listen to students' presentations because most were not very good. Her tests were so easy, two short-answer exams (mostly had to argue well) and 1 MCQ. You can do a group presentation in place of an exam. Easiest A+ for me.

Professor was okay, but did not actually teach most of the class. She would only give 1 of the 5 presentations each class, with a majority of time spent listening to other students' group presentations. Her lectures were solid and covered the reading well, but beware of the class format. Exams were a bit tough, but doable if you did the readings.

She's a great professor. This class is all group projects and Socratic seminar. If you like talking about current events and are very opinionated, you'll love it. DO NOT take this class if you have a fear of public speaking. This is the kind of class where 1 super liberal & 1 super conservative kid fight the whole time. Lot of fun.
Great teacher, but doesn't like it when you yawn. He has a pleasant side and a dark side. Proceed with caution especially if you have to yawn during a lecture
Great interesting Prof
This guy is a literal Nazi who thinks Hitler was great and the Holocaust was mostly made up. Puts his Nazi attitudes and racist comments in his class repeatedly.
David seems to know at least a little of chemistry, but spends most of the class arguing that the Holocaust was the fault of America and the Soviet Union.
He was professional and funny making difficult scientific analogies to simple life lessons. It made material more understandable.
Amazing Prof. Most honest and knowledgeable Prof or person I've ever known. If your willing to learn and have an open mind, no one will teach you more. Wish he was my Prof for every class.

The class itself isn't bad, but mostly depends on your TA. I hope I never have to take a class taught by Dave again though - offensive guy but tries to be funny. Makes students uncomfortable (check his twitter). Lectures are a mess and he goes off on tangents constantly. Not sure I learned a single thing from him. Bad at technology & no canvas.
He's a king and a bright man all around. keep on rockin Dr. C!
A complete nutjob. Check out his twitter feed. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just dont like him or the class

Hilarious guy and the most awesome stories you'll ever hear in your entire life. Wish he spent time in class clarifying the material better than just telling stories. Exams are tough, but fair. Overall good professor.
Fun class.  Dave is hilarious and very opinionated.  Tests are tough as hell but don't count for anything.
Best lab course. Looked forward to lectures and labs. Lectures, especially. I was actually sad when he started cancelling lectures second half of the semester.
This was the first lab I ever looked forward to coming to. The work is interesting and Dave is a great lecturer, on topic or not.
Dave is so inappropriate and hilarious!  He is so hott and the class is awesome.  I'll really miss going to lecture!
No Comments
Dave is so funny!  He tells the best stories and the labs are really fun too.  Everyone should take this class.

chemistry is hard whether you have a good or bad prof. kinsland is a good one imo she gives you all the material you need to do well but organic chemistry will just always be hard. her lectures have all the information, and the tests are heavy but fair.
I've never learned so little in a course. I had to use Khan academy to teach myself all the material.

She gets a bad rap but I really do think she cares about her students. Yes, this class sucks and her rubrics are often very annoying (ie 19/20 on labs is “perfect” and 20/20 is just a bonus) but she is a gifted lecturer and will tend to your issues if you make the time and show that you care. Grading often dependent on what TA you get which sucks.

really cares abt teaching + students. outlines all content + objectives needed to know throughout the course. hard to pass LO on prelim/final if you didn't pass on the 1st quiz (questions get much harder). orgo II is really hard, and she is a great and caring professor, but just a tough class + grader.

Clearly outlines everything you need to know for the course and adheres to this for exams. She is always accessible outside of class and really cares about how all of her students are doing. 
I learned so much over the course of this class.
Cynthia is a great professor. She really cares and wants everyone to do well. Yes, her class is hard, but its Orgo, I don't know what else to expect.

graded on a "learning objective" (LO) basis this semester, meaning you took weekly LO quizzes outside of class hours. if you passed ALL 20 LO's -> it only translates to a B- in the class. i also scored 15% more than a friend on a prelim, but her scuffed grading system we received same # of points. gets worked up easily & sends pretty nasty emails.

Cynthia is the most caring professor you'll meet at Cornell. You didn't put in any effort if you have a problem with her. She went above and beyond to ensure everyone had a chance to pass this class (or, for most, get an A). Her lectures weren't my favorite, but her office hours were insightful, and the textbook was helpful. Love her
So awful. Unnecessarily tricky and terrible sense of humor. Enjoys sending condescending emails on weekends. Such a dreadful experience.
Don't worry if you understand organic chem - this class will grade you like you don't. Loves to put her students down and seeing people fail makes her happy. Cynthia is the worst.

I would have to say that she is a fantastic lecturer and she enjoys teaching her students the material in regards to organic chemistry. She's passionate about her teaching methods, and she clearly knows what she teaches, based on well her lectures flow. I would say that her exams are fair, but don't be fooled you need to put in the time to study.

Dr. Kinsland is an extremely gifted lecturer and is fantastic at teaching complicated material. Orgo lab is a lot of work - too much for 2 credits - but that is up to the university and the department, not her. Also, she does care about her students - you just need to try! She is direct and sometimes curt, but soley because she gets 200 emails/day.
Orgo lab is is supposed to be hard yet it's made harder. Prelims are outrageously overweighted and test very little of what you do in lab. Grading criteria was strictest of all stem classes

worst professor ever! past prelim questions are so different from lecture content. more work than 3 credit class. very very unclear test questions that u have to guess what the questions are asking for.
I cannot tell whether she is genuinely care or a sociopath hiding behind a charming mask.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Kinsland has such a bad reputation, but she is genuinely one of my favorite profs ever. Her lectures were whatever (they were pretty slow paced), but her office hours are where I got the most out of the course. She gets off track very easily (beware), but she explains things in simple terms and genuinely wants to see us succeed.
Not a great lecturer but cares about students, will tell you the truth if you will pass or fail her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Kinsland as a person - she is very easy to talk to, and I recommend communicating with her if you're concerned about your grade. However, I did not enjoy her prelims. A lot of questions came down to not whether you knew the material, but rather how well you can guess what she wants. Old prelims are super helpful, use them well.

I was scared of her based on what I heard about her class. I am convinced those people did not work for this class. Orgo is hard regardless of who teaches, but Dr. Kinsland is an excellent lecturer who supports her students; Open to questions and gave great analogies to help with understanding. I found her exams fair based on what she provided us.

Ya gotta go to lecture, but I wish there was more textbook/online info to learn from bc she goes on tangents and rushes through material. If you do bad on prelim one you are screwed bc its the easiest of the four exams and worth just as much
Apparently Kinsland in 1570 is totally different than Kinsland in 2510. She's honestly a great lecturer and makes learning orgo somewhat fun. However the class is curved to a B which is pretty harsh

if ur taking this its a requirement. Doesnt matter how good u do in labs tests determine most of grade. 1 test is easier one is incredibly hard. had 100s on all labs and practicals and bombed one prelim and it brought my grade down!! dont be stressed by labs u can make up most data if u dont get it/collaborate w other kids in OH
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People with negative reviews haven't gotten to know her. Kinsland is one of the most considerate and approachable professors at Cornell and truly cares about student success. Her prelims are difficult but if you actually make an effort to understand her lectures you'll do well. She holds tons of office hours so take advantage of them!

Orgo lab is set up poorly, and the prof makes it harder than it needs to be. This 2-credit class will ruin your week, only take this if you ABSOLUTELY have to. The prelims are NOT representative of the material learned in lecture and lab. Unclear grading criteria for lab reports, and the TAs usually do not know what is going on either :(

This professor is incredibly passive aggressive. While she attempts to maintain an air of professionalism, it's clear she believes herself to be above her students. She adds extra exams just for the sake of it and is a perfect example of the shallow instructor who teaches only to keep a research position. Community college professors are better.

It's the worst class I've ever taken at here. I heard that a few years ago, there wasn't even any exam. And now there's 2 prelims and 1 practical exam which all combine make up about 53% of your grade. The professor is also so passive aggressive and just so inconsiderate compare to the other professors in chem department. Too much work for 2 credit

Not sure why there are so many negative reviews but I haven't interacted w/ her 1 on 1. Class is boring and monotonous and there's quite a bit of workload for 2 credits (including prelims) but I've treated it as a regular 3 cr. chem course and done well. Really its just a requirement you have to get through...not a particularly interesting class.

Kinsland is awfully inconsiderate, and the lab experience was dreadful. Additionally, it's baffling that this is only a 2-credit lab class yet exams are given and weighed more than the labs themselves. Compare to a 2-credit bio lab class I took a few semesters ago, the difference in expectations is simply unreasonable.

She is a horrible teacher, does not provide adequate practice for exams, which I don't even know why we have in a 2 credit lab class; terrible grading, does not provide us guidance as to how to actually write our reports, its just guess and get your grade back to see, and by then we have already done 3 or 4 lab reports so its pointless.
terrible
Absolutely awful. Grading designed to fail students not teach them. Horrible experience.

For all of the hate Dr. Kinsland gets here, she can actually be very considerate. She let me schedule a makeup prelim at quite short notice due to a debilitating sickness. Not only that, but she expressed great concern for my health. I was able to take the prelim a few days later and did decently well.

She is an awful professor and very snarky. She treats the students in this course as numbers rather than the humans we are. I asked for an opportunity to redo an assignment because I recently had a loss in my family. She told me tough luck and that I am not able to redo assignments even though I was still mourning the loss of my uncle.
Quite literally cried every single day because of this class. Almost transferred out of Cornell because of it too. Traumatized. Felt so hurt and disrespected for an entire semester.

Cynthia Kinsland wants her students to fail. She has zero respect for any student and projects all of her personal issues onto the difficulty of the class. Overall worst class I've taken at Cornell. Far worse than chem 2070 with Dr. Lee. Even if you've learned everything she wants you to know, she'll make sure you do poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cynthia is the most degrading teacher at Cornell. I had the exact error as the girl next to me in lab. She wrote me an incredibly hurtful email and regraded my whole lab whereas she kindly told my lab friend she was right and could give her the points back. If you get a bad TA w/ bad grading, not worth asking for help. The student is always wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The 2080 lab is horribly run, and is genuinely a mess.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lab reports are complete luck. There is no "set" rubric and truly depends on whether you have a nice TA grader or not. The tests are in no way representative of previous exams and are very unfair. Through several interactions with her, she has given rude, snarky comments that are meant to be "funny". Would not recommend her class unless required.

Completely unfair tests that don't resemble practice at all. Once walked by me in lab and said "your product looks wrong" when I had water in my beaker since I was cleaning it. Lectures are a waste of time. Don't take this unless u need it to graduate.

The way the lab reports are graded is horrendous and completely dependent on whether you get a nice TA or not. I have never had a professor spend half a lecture explaining to the class how to "respectfully email professors", but cannot even provide a grading rubric other than a link to a website for our lab reports whose format she didn't explain.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Way too much work for 2 credit class. Doesn't post guidelines for lab reports so you have guess what you need to include and is not receptive to grade change requests. Only lab prof that assigns problem sets and prelims. Labs are time consuming and tedious. Avoid this course if you can, not worth the 2 credits. Everyone's least favorite professor.
Cynthia Kinsland is actually very considerate of student needs, especially one on one.

Dr. Kinsland is a passionate professor who cares about her students. Orgo is naturally hard, but Dr. Kinsland does her best to provide a ton of resources, so there is no lack of material to study with. Office hours were so helpful! The only thing was that she would occasionally go on stage tangents or put barely covered details on prelims.

Orgo is tough, put simply. Dr. Kinsland makes this class fun and interesting even for those who struggle with it. Her passion for the subject comes across. She also clearly loves teaching (rare in a Cornell STEM professor). She often goes into more detail in her lectures than you'll actually need for the exams, so don't get overwhelmed.

Her class was challenging for me, but she was incredibly fair and accessible. She truly cared about her studetns and was always very happy in lecture. She was a great lecturer and always posted her lectures as well. She honestly made orgo as enjoyable as possible. Very intelligent, kind lady. Cannot say a bad thing about her.

A lot of work for 2 credits. Practical is 20% of grade % graded on purity, ability to identity unknown comps, and report. Barely give feedback on reports so if u do bad, ur gonna keep doing bad. Weekly psets but if you go to OH, they give u the answers. Lectures are recorded on zoom - I never went to class and did fine. Final is easy if u study.

I took CHEM 1570 with Dr. Kinsland and I really enjoyed it. Her TAs are also great. The prelims would sometimes have errors in grading, but they would be resolved within a day or two. Her office hours were very helpful and she is more than willing to chat with you and give you advice.

extremely difficult, nit-picky grader. more focused on having the assignments be completed "her way" rather than the students learning. quick response on emails and willing to physically communicate with you but not willing to actually hear students, accommodate them, or understand their perspective in any kind of meaningful way

I really liked her when I took chem 2080 over the summer but when i took 2510, she was the most unapproachable, obnoxious professor. I received a C in the class even though when calculated my raw score was around a C/C+. I emailed her about it three times and after reaching out to the department, i learned she ignored me and wouldnt do a grade fix

Took it last sem, in the midst of covid. She is so accommodating and communicative. If you just talk to her, she will understand and is willing to make changes to ease up your stress. Yea the lecture itself is fast paced and the class is pretty test heavy, but she really made me enjoy the class.

Professor Kinsland is the most accommodating professor I've had during the Covid-19 situation in Sp2020. She was extremely understanding and changed the course to help us as much as possible given the circumstances. While I do agree that her class is difficult, she made it abundantly clear the amount of work you would expect at the start of the sem
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Cynthia took over orgo lab last semester after Prof Ruttledge had to take a leave of absence and she was amazing. Her lectures were very entertaining and her sense of humor was on point. She taught everything that we needed to know for the final during lectures and was very fair when writing the final. Its sad that others wont have her for lab.

Dr. Kinsland is amazing! She is so friendly and really invests time in students who invest time in the class by going to office hours and by seeking help outside of class. It is crucial that you go to lectures and take good notes because the lecture notes are what the prelims are based off of. I highly recommend doing the homework every week too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class is hard but easy to pass. She promised a C- or more if you got 300/500 points available in the class (including 50 participation points.) Class is test heavy, if you are not a good test taker, you are not going to do well. Check your exams after she gives them back, TAs made a lot of mistakes in grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Totally fine and what's expected. Slightly difficult, but difficult subject matter. Kinsland kept it interesting and kinda fun.

Lectures don't help, she goes by everything too fast, your entire grades are based on 3 prelims and 1 final, and to top the cake the materials gone through in class are "orgo 2 level", according to my friend in a biochemistry major. If you are going to take this class, know that it will likely be the hardest intro class you will ever take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wow I've taken numerous "Intro to" courses during college but Cynthia's "Intro Organic Chemistry" is anything but an intro class. Hardest class I've taken at Cornell, lectures are so fast you don't have time to comprehend the material, and there's practically no help available out of class (nearly 400 students and only 2 TAs?).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: All of the grades were from the three prelims and the final exam. There was homework but it was not graded or turned in. Not doing the homework will make the exams very hard. You have to do the readings. She does not explain what she is doing in lecture.

If you want to do well on the exams, do the homework (similar questions). I found Kinsland to be quite bland and too "try hard" when it came to humor. Did not get a lot out of class. I knew a lot of friends who just did the work outside of class and never went to lecture and still did well on prelims.  However, the curve is huge.

Homework was optional, meaning it didn't have to be turned in. However, not doing the homework meant not being able to do anything on the exam, so you always have to do it anyway- it should be graded. Lectures were amusing, but not helpful in the learning process. I learned almost nothing from any lecture because she never explained what she did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Cynthia has an amazing sense of humor. Her deadpan make me enjoy going to lectures. She always slips in some interesting facts and uses real life examples. She uploads annotated lecture notes which is nice but lecture are no substitute for the textbook (which is very good). Expect to memorize.
A little condescending at times during instruction for sure. Wouldn't take again.

Useful class, but can be rude and aggressive. This instructor is retiring anyway, but just putting it out there as a warning. Def agrees with the comments earlier down here that she can be condescending and unreasonable.
LOVE her. And learned great skills
She is the moment
best teacher ever
AVOID.

Christina is the best and her classes are the ones alumni rave about as a must-take. Took two classes with her already and would take her again if possible. The most useful class for internships and beyond, you think you know Excel until you take her class and realize how little you actually know. And you get a certification in the process.

one of my favorite classes taken. great teacher and lecturer, I HIGHLY recommend taking this class. you learn so much so quickly that is so applicable, and you get a nice certification on top of it all. she is very nice and personable.
Super caring professor, explains things clearly. She takes the time to make sure you understand material. Just a long class, but she gives a break in the middle.

For HADM1740, your professor doesn't matter all that much. For her part, Christina was very meh. She isn't always super helpful and can be pretty condescending at times, although she is nice enough. I liked my TAs much better. Overall, the class is not difficult but the grading rubrics are pretty harsh. Little mistakes will cost a lot of points.
Really great class. If you liked EDA, it is more of the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: EDA is an essential class for any Cornell student, and Christina is an excellent professor. That is all that needs to be said.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Christina is amazing! She's funny, helpful, and cares about her students. I took business computing with her and mark and I did well because she provided us everything we needed for exercises. Attendance is mandatory. I'd love to take another course with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super helpful class that can be an easy class, but don't underestimate it. Make sure you are well prepared for the two in class excel quizzes and you should be fine.
I highly recommend taking EDA with Christina. The content is really useful and she makes the lectures interesting. She's also super nice and approachable. 10/10.

Christina is one of the best professors at Cornell, she puts a lot of work into making lectures applicable to the real world while maintaining a great attitude. Always makes expectations clear, connects with students, and is careful to explain things in a very clear manner to reduce potential for confusion. Take her lab for Business Computing!
Amazing class do not regret it at all, have learned a lot of useful things in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: EDA is by far the most applicable course offered at Cornell. Christina teaches skills that are necessary for most jobs that ILR students have. She makes class really fun and rewarding. Easy A if you practice the techniques. This class is a must-take for all ILR students.

She's a great lecturer. I enjoyed her. Some didn't but I guess it's just about how you mesh with a professor sometimes. The structure of the class was terrible but there were four professors responsible for it so can't put it all on her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: So blessed to have taken all three of her classes: EDA, ADA and XDA. The Expert Certification in Microsoft Excel is a nice resume booster, but even more valuable are the actual skills she teaches so well. I now use Excel for everything from tracking income/expenses to creating charts and graphs for various purposes. Couldn't recommend enough

I am so thankful that I had a Christina as a teacher for EDA. I now graduated and she is even willing to help with a excel-based work assignment that I have been struggling with. She genuinely cares about her students and this class is the most useful class that I have taken throughout my time at Cornell.
She does a good job with this course that ends up being very valuable. Would definitely recommend.

Undoubtedly one of the best professors at Cornell. ADA was a little harder than EDA, and the skills that she teaches you are prob the most applicable. She is a little frank, but far from rude. The comment about her being rude is absurd; she treats you like you treat her. If you disrespect her, she'll give you no respect back. Try a little, easy A
Easy class and useful but was taken back by her rudeness... would recommend taking another desktop/excel/ microsoft class if you do not want to be hurt.

Her class is not difficult and if your willing to work hard then an A is easily obtainable, but this is not a course you can blow off and do well. She also is not as reasonable as others have suggested, she is down to earth, but there are no second chances in her course if you make one mistake on a test you put yourself out of the A range.

Christina Homrighouse is one of the most entertaining lecturers I've had to date. You literally cannot fail if you just show up, listen, and follow instructions. I had experience in Excel/Powerpoint before the class and that only made it easier.
Christina is the best business computing professor you can have. She cares about her students, 100%.

Christina is a phenomenal teacher. She knows her stuff and she is willing to work with students who may be struggling. Christina cares about her students and wants them all to succeed if they put in the required amount of effort. I recommend going to every class and taking notes. Excel will help you not only at Cornell but well afterwards.

One of the most understanding professors I have ever had. She is straightforward and truly cares about helping you succeed. She is also HILARIOUS and makes class fun. If you miss lecture make sure to attend one of the other lectures that week or else you will fall behind very quickly. Tests are easy if you pay attention in class.
Great class, great professor.

There is absolutely no excuse not to take her class if you are in ILR. Not only is the subject matter essential to your future success, but the course itself is very well instructed by a professor who genuinely cares for her students.
Awesome professor, great and USEFUL class.

Christina is literally the best and most genuine person on campus. She is so invested in each student and she develops their technical, professional, and personal skills. The topics she teaches are taught with ingenuity and are the most practical and important skills any student can ask for. She is a FANTASTIC educator and friend. Thank you Mrs. H!

Christina is one of more friendly and easy-going teachers at Cornell. The class is invaluable in terms of the excel and powerpoint skills is gives you, which are all highly looked upon by employers. It's an "easy A" kind of class, but requires a little extra effort if you really want the A+.

The nicest professor I will ever have. I'm a total techie and I actually learned really cool tips and tricks I use all the time for Windows and Office 07 which comes in real use for corporate jobs. Homrighouse is amazing. Take her. Now.

Extremely easy. there is no way you can not get an A+. I think I did a total of four hours of work for the entire semester. The only complaint was that attendence was mandatory and the class was at 8:00AM on Fridays.

If you don't get an A+, you should probably drop out of school. Let's just say the class average on one project was a 112. That is no typo. She's very cool though, and you really learn some good stuff in the class. And she's a Yankees fan to boot!!

Easy A+ class.  Cant really skip class that often, but Homrighouse tells you exactly what you have to do on the projects and what will be on the quizzes.  GO TO OFFICE HOURS, she shows you how to do everything so that you really learn it.  The material is easy. Take this class!

Prof H. was so interested in getting everyone onboard and learning that it was refreshing to wake up that early and go to class! She really has an interest in students learning material...other professors could learn alot from her! If I weren't graduationg I would take all of her classes...

She's the best! Veeeery easy A, but you will learn a lot, too. If you're interested in sharpening your computer skills, with almost no work, just REAL learning, this is it. Highly recommended course for anyone (not only ILR)!

She's the coolest ILR professor.  She's always willing to help...in fact, she forced students to do the extra credit...and going to her for help isn't intimidating...she understands some peeps may be a bit tech stupid.  Overall, she rocks! Definitely take her!
Yeah, the grades are high. But hey--it's truly a good class to take, even if you feel very comfortable with Office.
Should be a required class for college students. Learn real world skills such as powerpoint, access and excel. Teacher very nice and wants everyone to do well.
good class - easy A+
Fun class that you will actually learn something in, even though it is a very easy class.  Always has a positive attitude.
Great class!
Take this class for a positive classroom environment in the morning!
Greatest class i've taken
No Comments
The mean grade in this course in a A+, that's sexy!
No Comments

If you just show up and follow along on the spreadsheet during class, you'll understand how to do the homework and prelims. Willing to answer questions during class. If she says class isn't mandatory, I'd recommend going.

Mrs. Haegar was dedicated to ensuring her students not only learned Excel but also enjoyed the process. This year placed a strong emphasis on AI, and her enthusiasm for what the technology is capable of made it clear how passionate she is about teaching. I recommend introducing yourself to her and the TAs who help make this course such a success.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Originally, I was nervous about this class after reading the reviews. However, she is very kind, caring, and willing to explain any questions you have about the course. Her prelims were fair and a clear representation of what was taught in class. As long as you respect class time and are on top of your work, you will do fine.
Grade is based off whether or not you have a good TA. Some are stricter than others. Prelims are unorganized, but manageable if you watch her videos.

She is nice to students during lectures, and also like to help students on their HW. The HWs can be a little hard since they aren't always exactly the same as in the demos, and the HW instructions can be unclear. The beginning of the semester was a bit confusing, and the prelims are a little hard and very time consuming. She teaches very fast.
Great class for folks trying to explore the waters of excel. Assignment are easy to complete as long as you just follow along with the videos and understand how and when to use what functions.

Does the bare minimum for her students, will not accommodate for anything (I'm not talking about late submissions) unless "required by the university". Disrespectful to students and clearly does not enjoy teaching. Beware.
Forcing students to watch those low-quality videos is torturous. Plus the class policy is so weird. Not a fan.

The class is very accuracy-based. The prelims are a lot like the practice ones, and she does not necessarily make anything confusing; everything is stuff we have seen in the past. She is very kind and genuinely seems to want to help her students.
While the class is easy, Haeger is often rude to students unnecessarily.

As was mentioned before by some other rating, she is notorious at Cornell for being by far the most disrespectful towards students. Constant patronizing and passive aggression towards students and an extremely tough grader when it comes to the most minute details. All incoming Dyson students should be aware of this.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would argue that this is the worst professor at Cornell. The teacher puts on the facade of a supposedly nice person, but during one-to-one interactions, she completely changes. Whoever is applying or attending Cornell should think twice about the school because of this class. Notorious at Cornell for her disrespect towards students!!

Lectures and videos provide precisely what you need to know to complete the assignment. TAs were also nice with helping during class and office hours. I would say that grading could be harsh at times, and the cutoff for an A in this class was surprisingly high (95%). Someone that pays a little bit of attention to detail will have no problem.

Great professor, very clear, easy-to-follow lectures with helpful videos. 2 hw assignments/week align very closely w/ lectures. Prelims are almost exactly like the homework, so you'll know exactly what to prepare for. No final exam, just a final group project which isn't too much work. Just note that cutoff for A this sem was 95%

Course content is really useful. Nice prof but she is strict with deadlines. As long as you watch her video tutorials, attend her lectures, and do your homework, you should have the prelim part completely covered. Make use of Thursday lab sessions and OHs to get full credit for assignments (if not you will always lose a point here and there).

The class is pretty easy and it was primarily asynchronous this past semester. Professor Haeger was always attentive and accommodating to students, but she was often not present on Thursday classes with the TAs to take questions. Prelims are a large portion of the grade, so review the activities and cases before taking these exams.
Not a hard class, but I've never seen a professor be so rude to her students. Especially for one that just teaches excel at an ivy league.

I oved Professor Haeger's class and as an instructor, she did a good job. What I vehemently disliked was the disrespect towards students. I had her for an early class period, so students often would arrive a little late. Each time she would stop the whole class to essentially berate the student in front of their peers. It was absolutely unnecessary
One of the most useful classes in the major. Learned a lot without the class being overly difficult. Probably could add some concepts but overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easy class, but not a great professor. She's super disrespectful to her students and very arrogant.

Can be nit picky and corky, but overall if you come to class youll be fine. Videos of the lecture are online. The TAs are easily accessible. The first class will be a demo of what youre doing, next class you will do it yourself, then a case due outside of class. Demos can be different from your other activity. Study activities for tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: VERY easy course. Assignments and tests are easy, and you learn a lot. She is nice but she seemed unnecessarily harsh about academic integrity. There were several kids who had hearings but nothing ever came from it. The course is set up well, but a lot of learning is TA dependent. The final project is long but good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is not a great professor, but if you watch the video tutorial on blackboard you will do well. Pick a good group for final project because it is a lot of work. Average grade in class is A+
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: It was my first time learning Excel, and all the assignments and prelims were very easy. However, the month-long final group project was extremely hard. Be sure to have someone who really understands Excel in your group, then you'll be fine. And do NOT procrastinate on the project.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The first half of the term was difficult to follow, with lectures relying heavily on slides and moving quickly. The second half improved, with more engaging lectures and clearer explanations. Since it was his first time teaching, I expect the course will improve.
Made analogy that when you go to the gym you need to push yourself and used that as justification for making his class the way that it is.
Avoid if you can.
so bad. avoid dorn if you can and take it with someone else

Very caring and passionate professor and is willing to answer any questions and help out when available. Sometimes lectures got off-track, and exams tend to be partially different than the content in the lectures and problem sets. But, I'm sure the class and his lectures will be far more cohesive as he teaches more.

His lectures are fast and not always organized. However, he always tries to improve because he is new.
There are a total of 6 problem sets, 2 prelims (20% for the higher and 10% for the lower) and 1 final. 
Exams practice are hard unless you do a lot of practice from psets. I recommend must go to TA sections!
Beware of homework, but great class overall. Easy to ask questions to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's an intense class you will need to study hard and go to office hours. He's clearly a kind person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed the content but definitely need to put time into the class. Loved how passionate the professor was!
Prof. Dorn was an incredible professor. Definitely challenged me to think outside the box. It's a class worth taking
Professor Dorn was extremely passionate and easy to access outside of class. Material was challenging but Professor Dorn was able to explain everything very clearly.
Great professor, would take again.

Pretty nice guy who knows his stuff, but many basic concepts were explained in really long-winded ways that made it hard to follow. The material isn't extremely hard and you can def study it in your own time, and the grade cutoffs were pretty generous. TA slides were a godsend, it was just his first sem teaching so I think the quality will improve

Professor Dorn may be a nice guy but he is fresh out of graduate school and should not be teaching this level of class. His lectures are confusing and exams very difficult. I found the TA discussion section to give me better teaching than what he could give in class. I wish I had taken this class with a different professor.

Professor Dorn really grew on me throughout the semester. I am grateful to have taken his class and really learned a lot. I feel like I have a strong foundation in supply and demand side analysis in microeconomic theory, and I would recommend that everyone take his intermediate microeconomics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: RUN!!! You can tell that Jacob wants to make a great class, but his lectures are confusing, his slides have errors, and he will contradict what he has said. DON'T take it unless no other alternatives at all.

Super nice guy and eager to teach, but he's a recent PhD grad and it shows. Often makes mistakes in class and walks back on what he says. Combined with overexplaining simple concepts, his lectures are often confusing. Going to OH may be helpful and exams are managable. Eager to improve course.
First time teaching. Fresh phd grad. Does not know how to teach. Lectures are extremely confusing and tests don't look anything like problem sets or practice tests. He tries though.

Lectures are overcomplicated and confusing, problem sets and the minimal practice problems given for each exam weren't reflective of tested content. He is a nice guy and the curve is projected to be generous, but I'd rather be taught well than rely on a subjective curve and feel impending doom going into every exam. I hope this course will improve.

Avoid if possible. Over-explains simple concepts with heaps of unnecessary mathematical notation. Doesn't communicate well with TAs and regularly struggles to keep a class running effectively. Problem sets are incoherent and messy. However, he's a nice guy and obviously eager to improve, so you can expect his class to be better-run in the future.
Freund is a great professor, he made us muffins. The class sucks tho. LOTS of hw, and an emphasis on group work, which isnt my preferred way of learning. prelims and final were difficult too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Really liked the learning objectives system. Rewarded staying on top of content and kept stress low throughout the semester. Freund has very nice lecture notes and quite good lectures. Much better experience for Diff-Eq than Lin-Alg in my opinion. Very kind and cares about students, personally helped with logistics issue.

I have heard varying things by section, but my non-mandatory section consisted of being handed a worksheet and getting no guidance. We had long problem sets due weekly that did not line up with our in-class work.The tests were 5x harder then any other work we had seen; if you had not previously done well in this course, I would not recommend.

freund was a great prof! accessible outside of class, and taught the information well. 

that said, CALC 1110 as a class was a nightmare. HW is graded on ACCURACY, textbook is useless, and prelims are 5x harder than what's taught in class. might be easier if you have taken calc before, but if you havent (like me), dont take this class

Aside from the weird grading system of 2930 that starts out great but then hits you like a truck in the last 3 weeks, Freund's lectures towards students are outstanding. His lectures are fun and engaging, but sometimes can be hard to follow. You can tell he tries to take students' thoughts into account. Sad to find out he got demoted to calc 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Freund's lecture are extremely clear, fun, and well-organized. He is also very helpful at office hour and never make you feel stupid. Stay on track with the LOs and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear and funny lecturer, but dont fall behind on your LOs. His office hours are helpful
Great prof. Sad that he's getting demoted.
I like his funny hair
Amazing lecturer who makes great math jokes to keep the class interested. Moves in a clear logical way and also answers questions well.

lectures are very good, make sure to attend. homework ramps up in time and difficulty significantly towards the end (as does the rest of the class). very strange grading scheme that makes it easy to breeze through the course if you stay on top of things, but is very punishing if you fall behind at any point.
Amazing professor. Super kind and teaches very well. Go to lecture and you'll be fine!

Fruend was good at explaining but I found it kind of slow at times. He has many in class "discussions" where you talk with other students, but I feel like it would have been so much better if he just spent more time explained concepts instead of making the learning interactive.

Terrible lecturer, always saw people nodding off during lecture because he is just bad at teaching. The class itself is prepared fine and the materials like notes and study guides are well made. He is a very bad professor though.

Literally maybe the most KINDEST professor I've had here. Imo course was hard, esp comp to prev years, but it was DEFINETLYY doable (i'm just especially bad at math) so idk what the other reviewers were on lmaoo. Do practice and ur fine, its all textbook based.
Grade cutoffs were fair too, and grades are mainly tests/quiz, but thats normal for math

The quizzes in this class were generally quite rough (and 20% of grade all together). Tests were pretty fair, lecture notes were not always super helpful, homework was fair. I had a technical issue and Professor Freund personally fixed it, he's nice and super helpful. I've heard MATH 2930 is better with him so looking forward to that in the Spring.

David Freund is a nice guy but a bad professor for Linear Algebra. I had him for Diff Eq and he was great because there was a clear rubric and clear expectations. The curriculum for Linear Algebra was all over the place and had few concrete conceptual examples. We kept on revisiting past topics as it became apparent the class failed the T/F probs.

He's a really kind and supportive professor, and his office hours are extremely helpful. The tests were fair, but the True/False questions were quite challenging, being more conceptual and theoretical than I expected.

He's a caring and funny guy. I didn't find his lectures particularly helpful due to a lack of examples and structure, but the course has a lot of resources to help you succeed. The tests were fair, but I think the quizzes were a bit too difficult.
Just lock in and study hard. Linear might be 'considered' easy and you might want to slack off, BUT don't.
He is so nice and you can tell that he truly wants his students to succeed. However, the T/F questions were highly conceptual and difficult for most students. I had an extremely hard time with them.

Every positive review this sem must either have previous experience or is super talented. It's a rigorous version of Lin Alg and is transformed from its “reasonable” reputation it had. True-False questions conceptually are more theoretical and harder than the CAS lin alg (I compared). Conceptual rigor is extremely high- beware of the work.

David is a super nice and kind proffesor! 2940 is very exam heavy 90% of the grade comes from exams/quizzes. The discussion section + textbook readings are very helpful. Lectures are concept based, and include short applications. If you really understand major concepts and the HW then the exams are very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Better for 2930 than 2940. Test heavy like every other math class. Very nice and accessible. Quizzes are pretty easy; exams are harder but more than reasonable. Goes a little too slow for me; he should focus going thru more practice problems in lecture. Lecture style not for everyone. Keep in mind, people often come here to rant; you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very difficult professor for LinAlg. Extremely heavy on conceptual understanding. Quizzes and exams are worth 90% of the class! Unforgiving class and punishes those who struggle with exams. The positive ratings on this professor are either extremely gifted test takers or have some sort of linear algebra experience coming into the class.

This class is awful! The professor is absolutely terrible! His lectures are run like a circus. Impossible to pay attention and jumping between random topics, the prelims are impossible with topics that have never been taught or seen on homework. Please spare yourself and do not take 2940 with this professor, absolutely terrible!
Light class, cool professor.

People in these reviews saying he is the worst lecturer they have had are actually delusional. David is an amazing professor. He is by far the kindest professor I have had at Cornell. Quizzes are not bad. Prelims are harder but still reasonable. 10/10 recommend. Great guy. Objectively (3+)/5 professor. I'm saying 5 because he is the goat.

Lectures for this class were basically useless and barely went over any example questions. Homework was long and hard and not similar to what was done in class. Tests are relatively fair. This class is not curved, which sucks. There are four hour-long "quizzes" you need to take, which are often unfairly hard. This class was fair before he taught it

save yourself and do not take Lin Alg with him. most miserable class of my entire college career and he references random Harvard problems all the time and has topics on exams that arent even in the textbook. problems are terribly hard and are heinous. I would rather take a class called how to poke your eye out with a spork than take this one

Heard this class wasn't too hard before he taught it. Lectures and notes give very little information and you have to read the textbook in order to do even remotely well. Tests are much more difficult than the content taught.

Spring 2024: He was a solid lecturer. The grading structure keeps this class rather lowkey if you're on top of it since it isn't really cumulative. I wish less time was spent on the easier topics and more on the last few topics (e.g. PDEs) but the grading system doesn't really allow that to be so. Easy class relative to the other eng. math classes.
Great lecturer

Implemented the mastery system very well, and his lectures were easy to understand. As the course progresses you get less attempts on the harder topics such as PDEs, but that's an issue that can't really be solved given the format of the course. Overall great experience.

He made the learning outcome thing much better this sem. I liked it a lot personally. His lectures were pretty solid. Kinda rushed at the end a little since content was harder. Course is generally smooth sailing until u hit Fourier Series/PDEs. Just practice PDEs a lot b4 the final and use the inner product shortcut when u can, it makes life easier

The Mastery system was a complete trainwreck last fall, and I was scared when I learned Freund would be implementing it as well. However, his version of the system was far superior to Ritz's and as long as you stay on top of things, it's honestly a nice system. Quizzes were fair, prelims were a little harder. Lectures were not great, not terrible.
Amazing lecturer!!! This class was much easier than I was led to believe

Very nice guy and seems like he is a good professor, but the way he teaches makes no sense. Students have to teach themselves new concepts, and get thrown hard questions about what we taught ourselves the next day in class. Might just be Calc 1 in general, not sure
Great professor with amazing lectures.
Not only the best math teacher I have ever had, but one of the kindest people out there. Lecturing is his second nature; participate in class and you'll get so much out of it.
Good prof. You can tell he's taught before. Not sure if he or delp made the tests this year but they were fairer than most past years.
He does aerial silks and bakes cookies for his class. 10/10 would recommend
Every single class has 100 pages of slides, every page full of theorems to be tested with no explanation in class.

1. the lecture covers a wide range of topics but does not go quite deeper, and some of the slides are not well-structured, making it hard to follow.
2. prelims are challenging and goes much deeper than both the lectures and the homework, it is difficult to review every topic while also preparing for the level of depth.
The course covers important materials in financial statistics, which is very useful for interviews. Professor Ruppert definitely knows a lot, but his lectures are quite dry.

Lectures are boring and I feel like sometimes the Prof. only reads the lecture to finish tasks given by the school but doesn't care about teach us anything at all. Disorganized lecture notes. The Prof. cannot even explain his own notes clearly. Financial background is not required but if you don't have any financial knowledge, you will SUFFER a lot

4 prelims but u can drop one. Attend lectures at all costs. The homeworks are hard but office hour and collaboration between classmates help. As for the exam, you have to find resources to help you ace(doing past prelims help). Financial Engineering is a very useful class and it will benefit you outside Cornell

Homeworks are especially hard. However, the prelims that count much are extremely easy to score A. Overall lecture was instructive and helpful. Very kind and moderate. Patient for any follow up questions. Highly recommend.
Very boring and uninspiring. Lecture content is disorganized. Difficult to learn. Coursework poorly prepared.

Rupper's lectures are quite monotonous and boring.  They are poorly worded and very disorganized.  The material he teaches during his portion of the course is difficult to learn and he does not make it any easier by providing a textbook, only his lecture slides.  The final is a huge surprise because it is nothing like the homework.
As others have noted, his lectures were good, but I found him to be highly inflexible and condescending when approached after class or during office hours.
He treats you like you are 4 years old in office hours. Grading critera seemed to change like the wind. Would not reccomend taking the course
This testing brought benefit to me. Examinations were of the easiest, require no study.

Dr. Kowal was a nice prof, and I believe he made BTRY 4030 as interesting as he could. It's not a very applied course by nature, but he tried hard to give us homework and exam problems which were applied  to the real world, which I enjoyed. The work load in this class was manageable, but exams were hard in my opinion.
Good personality, good lecture style! The exams are pretty easy and his notes are good for reviewing. Asking questions after class is always welcome.

Basically no curve. Which he said he would. Like my raw grade was a B+ and I end with a B+. IDK maybe I was not scoring meaningfully more to get a A-. But he is so unbelievably rude. Like his lectures are good and easy to follow but he is insanely rude. Like talking to him feels insulting at times and he grades really hard.

Yes, he can be boring with dry lectures. BUT, incredibly approachable, very helpful when asking questions, gives few homeworks and they're easy, gives easy exams, and will often take your side when you have regrade requests. Exams are basically the same as practice exams and there are no trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is incredibly confident (to put it nicely). He believes it is the world's greatest inconvenience when you have to ask him a question. He is a decent lecturer but completely unreasonable to work with as an instructor. Fair exams. Would recommend waiting to take it with another professor.

He was very dry and seemed pretty unapproachable and uninterested in the class. He was EXTREMELY unclear about grading policies (although i will recognize it was his first time teaching the course) and just overall vague and uncommunicative. The class is a major requirement but didn't even feel useful. Don't really recommend

He was not communicative at all, rude and dismissive to those who wanted to talk about grades, and was not transparent about grading (no curve). TAs graded your assignments twice, often resulting in lower grades. Cheating on exams was rampant. If he teaches this again, don't take it. For the stats major, you are probably better off in ECON 3140.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His slides seem very low-effort. Content is not too bad, and sometimes can be interesting. Overall, not a bad person, though.

He never seems very prepared for class, saying that many of his lecture ideas came the morning of. And although ethics is never cut and dry, the lectures are often unsatisfying and lack takeaways because Doris often avoids picking sides or tries too hard be contrarian. He also says he encourages free thought, but sometimes shoots valid ideas down.
just awful. so difficult. useless boring class. exams suck and so harshly graded.

Prof Doris' class was enjoyable mainly due to the discussions he had in class with students. One of the few classes I've taken where opposing views are respected. The class is very easy and you don't need to go to lecture to do well, but I found the lectures enjoyable and learned a decent amount
Dude blows, does not respond to emails and teaches a terrible course, get a grip.

Interesting lecturer (a bit fast) and the content is interesting, exams are straight memorization focused on very specific information in the slides. Cheat all you want I guess - he doesn't care. Wow, I hated this class.

The class is interesting but really easy to get an A in if you go, take notes. I never study for the exams and I get As because its really straight forward. Dont need to read/textbook stuff but I would go to class. Extra credit if you do business simulation. Also really easy homeworks every week. Participation pollevs and stuff so go to class.

Eddy is the clearest and most articulate lecturer I've ever had. He never stutters, never goes overboard, but every explanation has a lot of value and is very understandable for students, almost like he's reading off a script. Upperclassmen say he used to be strict, but I guess that's a thing of the past, because he is honestly very accomodating.

The class teaches a variety of media, and as long as you follow the rubric and attend class, earning an A is very achievable. The emphasis on technique reduced the pressure to be creative while still leaving plenty of room for creative exploration. Professor Kim also deserves five stars—he is kind, supportive, open-minded, and very professional.

Professor Kim is a serious but fair and considerate professor. He is well respected in the field of design and architecture and is a valuable resource for students like me who want to become better designers/creatives. His Principles of Design Computing class helped me develop my technical toolbelt and my professional/academic portfolio.

Professor Kim is a passionate professor and designer, but he doesn't tolerate slow students or "bad" questions. Make sure to pay attention in lecture. There's no wiggle room for mistakes, so read the guidelines. The lecture recordings are a lifesaver. He is very passionate and constructive for people who both pay attention and are open to learning.

This class is ver manageable, that being said it really depend on how tech savvy you are. Additionally this class is very important to pay attention to. Instructions are vital for all assignments, if the basic criteria isn't followed its an automatic fail. Sit in the front or a spot where you can see the board. Eddy is nice though and funny.

professor kim cares about his students in that he is mostly nice in class and one time even brought snacks, but when you mess up he is very passive aggressive which i found unsettling. you can bounce back from mistakes grade wise but i thought his passive aggressiveness was really rude and unnecessary and the environment wasnt welcoming

professor kim was passive aggressive and rude when students had difficulty keeping up or felt confused about the classwork, which felt especially unwarranted since it was an introductory level course. he also discouraged creative takes on the assignments, and instead emphasized simply following directions, which was upsetting in a design class.

You definitely have to ask the TAs questions to succeed - however, they are super accessible during class and there are a lot of office hours so it's easy to get them to help you. Projects are designed to help you learn useful, practical software applications. Professor Kim cares about his students and gives 1-on-1 help when possible.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is a highly respectable professor who is very knowledgable on the information he presents. If you pay close attention to his expectations and the rubric then grading should not be too stressful, and instead the projects allow you to creatively express what you learn during his lectures.

Professor Kim is incredibly caring and thoughtful. He often brings snacks to class, which is especially appreciated since it's a night class and many of us are tired. The snacks help keep us energized and focused. On the last day, he even bought us pizza, showing how much he values his students. It's such a kind gesture!

The techniques I learned here have been so helpful for both current projects and future professional goals. I gained valuable skills in Adobe software, Revit, and Rhino, which I've applied to other courses. My professors even complimented the quality of my work, which wouldn't have been possible without Professor Kim's detailed and expert teaching.

Professor Kim goes above and beyond for his students, recording hour-long tutorials to guide us through software so we never feel stuck. He's considerate, respecting our time and well-being—like holding Zoom sessions during Thanksgiving break for those who left early. He also shares internships— he truly cares about his students and their success!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: If you want to learn how to use Adobe and useful FSAD modeling technology - this is not the course for you. There are only a few major assignments and your grade hinges entirely on what TAs you get and what mood they're in that day. Be prepared to get blindsided by a B- or lower if you make a single mistake on an assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would rather fall into the needle pit from Saw II than take this class again. Grading is heavily determined by who is assigned to grade your work and how they are feeling that day. Very few graded assignments were given and if you mess one up..... well too bad I guess. It seems like nobody knows what this course is actually supposed to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wow, what an interesting man. I'm pretty sure he is a robot, but really enjoyed his class. He teaches really fast so be warned, but everything he does he does for a reason. J pay attention during lecture and you will be fine.

Elke's lectures are quite fluid and free-form, but she is one of the most caring and genuine professors at this school. She encourages participation through engagement and creates an environment where students feel comfortable sharing their ideas. Do the readings — if you stay on track, you'll do great. I'd highly encourage ANY course of hers.

She was filling in for a colleague on sabbatical so IDK if she'll teach the course again. Made me fall in love with humanities. Obvious she cared about all her students in and out of class, was willing to talk about anything. Clear grader...and everyone got an A+

She is interested in the topics she covered, but there wasn't much of a connection between all of them. She does give great insight into learning German better, and her feedback on papers is also great.

Elke Siegel is hands down my favorite professor at Cornell. I've taken three German classes with her and it is very apparent that she is there to teach you German - she doesn't give busy work and she doesn't grade unfairly. If anything she is a too nice a grader. If you have any interest in taking a GERST classs, take Siegel's!!!

My hatred for poetry is long and enduring; I was in the class to improve my German. I agree with the previous reviewer, that anyone who speaks German should take a class with Professor Siegel.   If you only have time in your schedule to fit in one German class, take whatever class Siegel is offering. You won't regret it.

I took Frau Siegel's class Lyric Poetry, which I never thought I would take because I hate poetry. But she made it super interesting and I would definitely recommend this course if she teaches it again! If you're into German whatsoever you absolutely have to take a class with her. And on top of that she's a really nice grader.

GREAT TEACHER!! So passionate and knows so much about Dante's inferno. This is not an easy class, but great for improving writing and analysis. is based off of effort/improvement and you can get an A (not based off of individual grades)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Grading are based on your commitment.Homeworks are basically journals (200 words ish) and Assignments (1000 words ish). The professor is quite flexibile on ddls. Assignments are not graded, but instead you have to sign up individual meetings with her, and she gives really helpful feedback.

IEA very clearly cares a lot about her class and her role as a teacher. She is there to help you improve in your writing and will NOT give an easy A for FWS. She will give a lot of feedback and help you get better. If you put in the work and clearly try to improve, you'll get good grade and you'll learn a fair amount. Def more work than other FWS.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of, if not the, best first-year writing seminar professors. Her feedback is incredibly detailed. Instead of simply giving out letter grades and due dates, she expects you to improve your essays as much as possible through office hours. All grades in her course are based on the final drafts at the end of the semester: she focuses on improvement!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love this prof, the topics were so interesting and we read/watching things about love so most of our assignments were a response to them. The final project was ab a topic of your choosing, it was so helpful to have meetings with her ab the essays and she's super understanding. My new fws doesn't compare-also the community in the class was on top

ROMS 1108: Took her FWS and almost everybody got a B+. AVOID THIS CLASS. If you turn in assignments on time and do work well the default is a B+, which is lower than other writing seminars, which usually give As.

Alvisi was great and taught me a lot about Italian literature. I really enjoyed her classes, and I definitely would have enjoyed them more if they were in person. Just be sure to participate a ton and always come prepared, she respects that a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Definitely gives extremely harsh feedback on essays but is a lovely break from high school English classes. She managed to make learning about Dante's Inferno fun, with a superb mastery of the text and frequent humor. Does not grade individual essays, but requires multiple meetings for feedback.

She's a great lecturer and is very knowledgeable about the text. Also, I learned how to organize my thoughts in writing properly thanks to her. At first, I thought she gave me excessively harsh feedback on my papers, but her concete and thoughtful criticism ultimately improved my writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Funny in class. Get ready to do a lot of assignments.
killed my love for architecture

This instructor yells at students in public, dismisses questions, and undermines the co-instructor. Reacts emotionally and grades vindictively, giving abnormally low marks that even other faculty noted. Lacks the ability to teach, making the studio toxic, demoralizing, and a total waste of time.
Killed my love for learning
Great professor would definitely recommend!

An amazing professor who deeply cares about his students, if you went to his office hours he would walk through the problems, would also crack jokes in lecture as well. I hope his retirement treats him with nothing but kindness.
Prof Diciccio is very thorough, forgiving, and light-hearted. Homeworks are due at the end of the semester, if you pace yourself there will be no problem. Exams were open note, attendance optional.

Diciccio clearly actually cares about his students and reducing stress. Our exams were all online and they give half of the homework answers in section. However, he seems to be a little tired of Ithaca and teaching in general, and most people I know didn't learn anything in the class.

ABSOLUTELY GOAT. Always recommend his classes. You can learn a lot if you put in effort, but you will also be fine if you just follow the slides and assignments. Tests are not hard, and the pressure of ddl is low.
I love him. He's actually the best and deserves the world

Professor DiCiccio was definitely one of the best teachers I've had so far. He is very chill and genuinely cares about his students. We often talked with him after class since I had questions about university applications and course material
He is very interesting. Classes are honestly very clear. Really recommend you to take his class.

Homeworks are kind of difficult and really really long, but they are all due by the end of the semester. There are no practice exams provided, so taking notes on the slides will be the best bet.
