I went to almost every office hour, gave it my all, and still somehow got wrecked. 10/10 for vibes, 2/10 for my GPA.

Has the greatest slides to help study-- literally just read them through and review and you will do fine on exams. He also provides great practice materials before exams they are pretty much exactly like the real thing.

Orlov gets a lot of unjustified hate. As long as you actually go to class, the material is super understandable. He genuinely cares about making sure students know the content and his slides are very thorough. He also provides plenty of extra resources and ample help hours for extra practice. The tests are exactly like the practice exams.

Orlov is a good lecturer and has very clear slides. If you go to lecture and pay attention, you'll know the material. He provides practice exams that are basically exactly what's on the actual exam and are super helpful for studying. The median grades on exams tend to be pretty high as well.

Professor Orlov's class is slightly difficult and does require some level of attention. If you actually read the textbook and read the slides, you should not have much of an issue with this class. Additionally Professor Orlov, is always willing to answer questions if any confusion arises.

Professor Orlov's class is honestly not very difficult if you go to the lectures, or even if you just look at the notes. He also makes himself very available and wants to help you learn. I took AP Macro in high school and found that the class was very similar to that, and I honestly just studied the slides and did well on the exams

Bro's slides might be the best slides I've ever seen in my life. His lectures are pretty good, but if you're still confused by something his slides literally go over everything step by step. Even though the upper level Econs get way harder, this class made me want to be an Econ major and I don't regret it.

Professor Orlov is one of two microeconomics professors in the semester I took this class. After hearing about the other class (which was primarily online), I feel as though my foundation in microeconomics is a lot stronger than my peers who took the other professor. He also curves each exam to make the median a B. Extra credit at end.

Professor Orlov is an amazing educator as long as you attend lectures/discussions and study for the prelims using his practice exams (they are very similar to the real prelims). Also, he takes attendance using pollev for every class so be aware (but he allows 6 absences).

His lectures are extremely organized and concise. His lecture slides contain everything he discusses almost for verbatim. As long as you go to class or read through the slides before the prelims you are going to do well. People who say he is a bad Prof or the class is hard probably put in almost zero effort because I did basically the bare minimum.
Very disorganized class, difficult to understand, test-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good slides that are easy to learn from outside of class, and so helpful for studying for exams so you don't have to take notes. His prelims were fair and representative of the practice prelims. Only issue is that in my experience Ed Stem is not a good way to reach him, if you have questions go to office hours or ask right after lecture.
Good lecturer and engaging. I left with a good understanding of microeconomics and helpful slides to look back on. I also really liked the textbook he used.

He is definitely a very nice/caring person, but the exams (which makes up a large percentage of your grade) can be tough if you don't study the right things. Textbook was sort of helpful, but I would say the practice exams were the best way to learn.

Pros: caring/respectful, wants students to succeed + gain a thorough understanding, extra credit, several top-notch TAs, useful/challenging practice prelims

Cons: HWs r good GPA boosters but long/not super useful 4 prelims, provides confusing/long-winded explanations in OH, can't go into the class w/out knowing Econ, some terrible TAs

Orlov is actually very nice AND I do think I have an extremely thorough knowledge of micro econ after taking the class. So if learning is important to you, then you'll like this class. But it's graded off of very few things and prelims took an extremely long amount of time to grade. Ur gonna be stressed about the final regardless of current grade
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Can definitely do well in this class if you have a baseline knowledge of microeconomics and study the lectures/practice tests very well. I would say it was one of the harder classes, but it is very doable. He's an extremely nice person and very excited about what he teaches, but maybe look elsewhere if you are focused on getting a good grade.

You'll have to study and know his materials well. he offers tons of out of class opportunities for you to study though. Literally every day of the week before the final there was office hours. hard class but afterwards I really feel like I understand the material significantly better, and he did a great job. for an easy A, take a different prof.

Receives more hate than necessary. Prelims and Finals were very similar to practice tests, and everyone could definitely get an A if they prepared well for them. Annoying amount of homework and required participation, but really not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Orlov is amazing!!! I don't know why people have so many complaints. He provides accessible resources to succeed on the prelim and finals. He doesn't do open note exams so students are forced to learn the material. Thank god professors like him still exist. 100% recommend this class if you want a solid foundation in Microeconomics.

Professor Orlov is okay. If you have to take him, take him. But beware of a stringent attendance policy and lectures that can be likened most closely to sonic Xanax. He is not too strict gradewise, but his sections are led by soulless PhD candidates and he can never seem to settle on OH timing, making accessing help harder. Overall, not worth $44k

Orlov is nice, but that's it. For 1 thing, the other micro class has all online exams which makes Orlov's class so frustrating. 2 prelim + 1 finals = 80% of grade, course assistants are clueless, and the prelims take MONTHS to grade. Writing this on Christmas Eve and still don't know my final grade! Orlov is ok but get Thomas if possible

He is not as bad a lot of ppl say he is. He's a nice guy, very accessible and he explains stuff ok; he could be a little more clear sometimes. The class is not that hard; the exams are pretty similar to the practice ones. His voice did make me want to fall asleep sometimes since it was a 9am. This is coming from an engineer.

Orlov is a great guy, and very willing to answer questions if you approach him after lecture. Class is very organized/slides are posted regularly. Little HW, so 80% of the grade is based on exams, which were moderately challenging but similar to the practice ones. Class size is ~600, so if you want support you have to go out of your way to get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Graded based off lecture participation because he knew that if he didn't, nobody would show up to those crappy lectures. Spoke as if it's middle school, would get super pissed at people for getting up and leaving the lecture hall early. "The bell doesn't dismiss you, I do" type of guy.
Nice professor with extremely clear slides. Didn't like how attendance was mandatory, enjoyed the pop cultures references on exams.

This man's lectures make 0 sense but are mandatory to attend. You have to teach yourself the entire course and there's always something on the tests he only went over one time or not at all. Never take this class.
Lectures don't help and the whole grade is based on exams and final. Hard exams and hard final because he struggles to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Orlov has incredibly clear lecture slides and seems to generally be a nice person. However, he is not great at teaching the material and he assigns a ridiculous amount of homework. The homework is also very different to what is tested on the prelim. Avoid taking him as an instructor if at all possible.

Little homework, 6 absences allowed before your grade drops- but even then it barely takes any percentage off. Exams are exactly like practice prelim and are not that hard. Lecture slides are clear. Passionate lecturer too

Orlov is a nice guy who cares about his students. The only complaint I have for his class is that attendance is tracked and pre lim two was so hard. Considering Thomas has open note exams I would take her

Take with caution. Prof. is nice but he doesn't teach the material well. His slides are long & not everything is on the exams. He doesn't take extra time to teach the most important problems. He should show us how to construct the graphs step-by-step, but he doesn't, and instead just shows pictures on slides. Students need guidance- he lacks this.

No cheat sheet on exam is really really really annoying............
Mandatory attendance is also really really really annoying........
One practice prelim is not enough as well

Take Sanders or Thomas-- I've heard from other students that they allow cheat sheets and you can take exams online. We had no cheat sheets and IRL exams. 

He was enthusiastic and knowledgeable but could not convey information well. Lovely guy, terrible lecturer.

He was fine. Not the best lecturer but not bad. Exams were a little harder than I thought they should be but not terrible. Homeworks were fine. Attendance policy was annoying. He's really nice and enthusiastic about the content just not the best at explaining things sometimes.

Pretty clear in his lectures, only 2 prelims & 1 final so exams are 85% of your grade but he gives 2 options. Class avg is a B+ I think, he gives practice final pdfs, & lots of office hours. Lowest 3 hws are dropped, pollev for participation each class. Exams are fair but can be tricky so study the slides. At the end, he offers extra credit

bro is kinda the goat, go to office hours if you're struggling since the class does move fast. offers extra credit questions on every test that're easy if you go to lecture as well as a 5% ish curve, class median was a B+ I think
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
I've loved Orlov as a professor.
I've taken his micro & macro intro classes, and I loved the way he structured the course. He always gave a review class day and a class off before a prelim, which I appreciated. Tbh his lectures were not super helpful for me, especially at 9am, but the HW helped reinforce the topics I'd need for the prelims.

By far, the most difficult economics course I have taken this far. The content itself is not terribly difficult, but he moves through it at a rapid pace. He does have an accent which makes certain things difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Okay so Professor Orlov is a really nice guy who is clearly trying his best to provide a good experience for his students. Despite this effort, he teaches introductory macroeconomics like it's a 6000 level graduate course. Difficult subject matter that goes beyond basic Econ, tests are ridiculous, homework is overwhelming, and the list goes on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The prelims are horrendous; 20 questions valued at 5 points each. You miss two and that is a whole letter grade down. He is a nice person but terrible professor. He goes through 10 slides in a matter of seconds. Worst professor I have had, not even Stephanie Thomas was this bad. His class will make you wish you never enrolled.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Orlov is a great human being, and he is one of the kindest Professors I have ever had. With that being said, the prelims were ridiculous. The median is far below other macro professors, and the lectures can be quite hard to follow. I never left class understanding what I was doing. Best of luck.

Orlov is a great lecturer. While many say otherwise, the way he treats lectures is more of a supplement to the textbook. Light workload and a lot of practice tests. Orlov even cares about keeping the same grade distribution from previous years. Man is trying his best.

Unstructured and not engaging. extremely low median exam score for prelims (which make up most of your grade in the class). I did better on the exams when I read the textbook on my own and stopped caring for the lecture. Discouraging class to take, but it's an intro class and requirement for so many people so you just have to bear with it.
If you want to take a class where you are given absolutely no guidance and have to teach all of the material to yourself, Orlov is the professor for you to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the class doesn't have a ridiculous workload, he's a terrible professor and his lectures are painful to sit through. Theres weekly hw with large textbook readings, and I'd be ok with this if I felt it prepared me for the prelims, yet the class average on our first prelim was a 71, a ridiculous grade for an introduction class with 400 people.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Smart guy who was super nice. If you struggle in Econ I suggest you take this class because he is always willing to help. Also gives out chips and snacks during the late night class. Graded on attendance so super easy A

I'd definitely recommend taking Prof. Orlov's class. Be aware that ECON 1120 is lecture heavy and there will be mandatory attendance as well as hefty homeworks 1x week. 

That being said, it's pretty obvious he wants his students to succeed. He makes himself extremely available and will go over material in class to ensure a thorough understanding.
Iago is a great professor all around. Super accommodating of students. Taught largely from his own experience in Iran, which made the course feel very real.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: THE BEST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL. PERIOD!!!!
best teacher ever at cornell he is so nice and caring

super kind and helpful professor despite my lack of knowledge in Persian. Really patient in teaching and never shames anyone for their less-than-perfect participation or attentiveness. Strives to create an equal learning opportunity and doesn't exclusively pick up good students.

Such an amazing instructor and just simply a wonderful human being. His attentiveness and thoughtfulness towards the students was inspiring, his kindness and humbleness was heartwarming and provided such a unique and comfortable learning environment. Witnessing his knowledge and how easily he talked about such complex topics was really impressive.

Iago was one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. He cares so much about his students and shows genuine passion and interest for the subject he's teaching. Be wary of the TA because he was an extremely harsh grader at times. However, if you participate and keep up with the material you should be fine in the end.
if you speak persian this class is easy, if you dont it is hard but manageable. absolutely love him!! not too much homework and a flexible grader, super kind

He is such a sweetheart! He made sure his class was a comfortable space for everyone. I loved coming to class everyday. His lectures are fun and engaging. Farsi was so easy to learn with him because he adds fun activities to make you more interested. He doesnt fault you if you have absolutely no experience in the language.

Extremely nice professor. Lectures are some of the most interesting and well taught Ive had at Cornell. TA was a very harsh grader, but extra credit makes it so that you do better than you thought in the end.
Iago is superb! One of the nicest, kindest, most caring instructors at Cornell. You will not regret taking his class.

Iago was by far the best professor I had at Cornell. He is kind, understanding, and truly wants his students to enjoy his class and learn a ton. I took three classes with him and loved every single one. Would recommend 100% to anyone even vaguely interested in the language - his classes will inspire you to keep learning!!
By far one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. I've taken three classes with him and he teaches them all incredibly well. My Farsi has greatly improved thanks to him. Can't recommend enough

Great teacher! Amazing lecturer, teaches fast though, so you have to keep up and do your homework every day. If you do that, you'll learn farsi very quickly! He is always willing to help as well, whether it be outside of class, or in the middle of class!

Best professor I've had at Cornell. Not only is he extremely willing to help whenever you need, he's so knowledgable and interesting. If you put in the work, you will learn Persian very well, in just one semester.

Definitely one of the best professors I have ever had. Classes are interesting, thought provoking, and well-conceptualized. His class inspired me to learn Persian.  Take his classes if you get a chance--by far the best decision I made this semester!
One of the best teachers at Cornell.  Exceptionally kind, passionate about NES and has lived all over the middle east.  Take the time to ask him about his life, he has an amazing background.

Unbelievably gifted professor.  Not only is his class easy, but also effective.  I feel quite confident in my Persian abilities after only one year of studying with him.  On top of that, he's nice, smart, engaging, and willing to help.  Basically everything one could possibly want in a professor.

His are the only lectures which have never bored me out of any class I've ever taken. His energy, clarity, and knowledge make the material very interesting and I managed to learn a lot. In his own words the texts are unnecessary and I did almost no reading, but the course is extremely easy. Trivial A+ and absolutely worth it for the enjoyment.

I took this course in fall and loved it. It was never boring. I liked that material was planed the way that it wasn't overwhelming but I learned a lot. Professor is knowledgeable about the topic and teahcing. He is very donw to earth, approachable and helpful. Awsome course.I recommend it.

I took this course in fall and loved it. It was never boring. I liked that material was planed the way that it wasn't overwhelming but I learned a lot. Professor is knowledgeable about the topic and teahcing. He is very donw to earth, approachable and helpful. Awsome course.I recommend it.

i took the course for distribution requirements and loved the course. it became one of my favorites at cornell. lectures were interesting and involving. because it was about one specific country it wasn't overwhelming, but because professor put everything in broader context you learn about the region and world history. highly recommend.
incredibly knowledgeable and helpful.  cares about his students and wants you to learn. i loved his lectures. overall a very nice person person.
He's very knowledgeable, not only about the material, but also about how to teach. He makes the class fun and knows how to involve students. He's also a very nice and cool person. Highly recommended.

great course. phenomenal professor,  extremely knowledgeable and great at explaining material. very passionate about his field, enthusiastic and helpful,  approachable.lectures were great-helpful slides and videos, interacrtiveness.probably most interetsing lectures i've attended.  make sure to ask for help if you need-you'll get.

one of my favorite courses at cornell. wasn't overwhelming and learned a ton.Professor is approachable, gives extra office hrs if you ask. it helps to speak up in class. we had a quiz,  2  take-home exams with essay questions, a paper.   The lecture slides and videos were fun+ very helpful for exams. i looked forward to every class. take it!
great course

History of iran course, very interesting material. Kinda boring powerpoints, almost no work required. Just a couple quizzes, 2 tests, 1 paper, and an easy final test before exam week. Honestly, if you don't get an A, it's your fault. The tests involve no essay writing, just fact memorization, it was like I was back in high school. Take this class!

Professor Vidan is one of the most thoughtful and engaging professors I have across. The lecture materials are super well curated and she puts in a lot of work tying threads together during the lectures. Her office hours are amazing! If one's attentive and puts in the work, it will give you a great footing in tech policy and science studies.

Lectures are dry, but content is super interesting. 

READING QUIZZES every lecture, 1 question based on reading assigned. This is a huge part of your grade but very easy and straightforward.

Prelim format is outlined very clearly and it is easy to study. Structured exactly like an AP test, in a good way. Discussion sections are so helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Okay class but you genuinely can't reason with her.

The class is pretty interesting and I like how it evolves each year with current events. Most of it was busy work but definitely easy, and they told us the exact format to expect for the prelims. There are two policy memos which also weren't too bad. They have a clear grading point standard which is nice.

She is clearly very passionate, however not the most interesting professor I've had. The subject material is usually really interesting though, including up-to-date assignments that require actual creative thought to try to pose solutions to modern day policy problems. Overall I'd say the class and material was more interesting than the lectures.

She is very knowledgeable and eager to help students. Her lecture slides are well-organized, but her lectures themselves often didn't add to the slides that much. Highly recommend going to office hours - she is happy to talk about the subjects, and much more helpful one-on-one! Also - strict about talking in class, don't try and get away with it.

The lectures are easy to follow and exams are quite straightforward. Weekly write-ups are not bad and help guide the main points of the upcoming lectures. My only gripe is that the grades on the two policy memos (a huge part of your final grade!) heavily depend on who your TA is; some TAs seem to grade way tougher than others.

Michael Gold is a great professor that really gets one interested in ethics. The class is graded by few things but it is not hard if you actually do the readings, which he gives you multiple classes to finish. Would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great prof, very informative. Very tough grader, I hate his quizzes. Grades them right-wrong/total so an 8/10 gets you a 60%. Leave the answers you do not know blank, don't try and guess you'll just get it wrong. read the "common ways to lose points" for the research paper, be very conservative w/ word count. Its stressful but grades get curved.

I avoided this class because of the reviews, but it turned out to be one of the most informative classes I have taken in college. Gold knows his tough, and his toughness while grading pushes you to put the effort needed. Your grade will suck, but his curve makes it all worth it. Had a 76 curve to an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gold has been my favorite professor at Cornell. This class taught me how to read dense information critically to create a case brief, which is an invaluable skill for law school. The course might've been changed to make grading more lenient, since my 82 curved to an A+. If you're considering law school (and even if you're not) take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: YOU WILL BE OK and ask the TA Lisa for help, she's amazing! There is weekly group work, but I never did an assigned reading and ended up ok. I had a 10% raw score my first essay and got a 90% on the revised version. The curve is insanely good at the end, I went from a 75% to an A-, so there is hope. Go to every class cause those points add up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: ILRGL 4820 He's a nice professor, but he grades extremely harshly and uses archaic methods to teach his students. Extremely difficult to understand what you're being graded on, as the questions for the exams and papers are vague and there is no real rubric. Grades are based on whim. Do not expect feedback on exams or ways to improve for next time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very hard class. First paper had a median of around a 25%. If you want to do well on the two papers, you basically have to spend two straight weeks in the library before you submit them. If you don't want to do that, and you care a lot about your grades, try to avoid this class. Curve saves you; upper 80s turns into A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had Professor Gold for Labor Law many years ago and, because the class was so exceptional, I then selected him to be my advisor for my ILR honors thesis. Professor Gold was excellent as a thesis advisor and helped me develop much better writing and analytical skills. I have always been grateful for his wisdom and patience. He will make you think!

Gold is a class act and a wonderful professor. I was definitely apprehensive coming into this class, considering all of the folklore surrounding both him and the course, but he is a brilliant teacher who really pushes for you to actually learn. I would genuinely take any class he taught.
This dude is terrible do not take this professor he will make you want to go to Cornells bridge

Gold randomly assigns you two partners to always work with for exercises. Pray you have some good partners who do the reading. I got a 27% on the 1st writing assignment that I worked my butt off on. I dedicated an entire week to the final essay and got a 92%. I averaged 56% throughout the semester and got a 69% total after the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great class to get exposure to law school, but I learned nothing in this class. However, Gold is a great professor nonetheless who will call you out on your bs in class and in papers. also is just a nice and respectable dude overall. I was way below the medians on all the papers (50% weight) and still got a b+.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The pop quizzes are graded right minus wrong answers. Annoying, especially when it is later in the semester and you feel pressured to earn more points to improve your grade. The final paper is incredibly hard, so start early. You can do ok in this class. Participate and you will learn a lot. More than labor law, you are taught critical thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: okay so basically class grade is based off homeworks/pop quizzes abt homework and TWO big papers (+ a rewrite of the paper for final essay.) You can do well in this class but you have to go to office hours with prof and start papers weeks in advance (to have enough time to change it). not very accessible + super unclear criteria for essays.

Gold's instructions for assignment seem clear at first. Ultimately, you realize you did not and he pulls a "gotcha" and you fail the exam. Ex: I spent 20+ hours first assignment, I got a 50%. I spent another 20+ on another assignment and worked with 5 other people, I got the highest grade and it was still below average. Avoid him.

Very knowledgeable, but extremely tough course. If you are going into law, take this class. If not, you will learn a lot but put in an insane amount of time and effort. If I had the option to take a different professor, I would've because I don't want to go into law, but still glad I had this experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easy to relate with and very understanding
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yeah, Gold is the hardest professor in ILR for the most difficult course; however, he is one of the most knowledgable professors in the school. This class will not be easy, and will require a lot of work. If you take this class, I promise you will leave it a better student. Gold is unique!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gold is a gem. You will truly learn and get your money's worth. Everyone exaggerates over how hard this class is. If you put in the work, you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have taken so much at ILR. The material was very dry and the pop quizzes are really difficult. Don't plan on sleeping because there are often 3+ readings due every class plus homework. Papers are graded very harshly. Gold starts every class off with a joke, but someone needs to tell him that he isn't funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Most difficult class I've ever taken in the ILR School. Labor Law took up at least 70% of my time this semester, with my other classes crammed into the other 30%. Because most of the cases are antiquated, they're a pain to read and understand. He distances himself from students and I felt intimidated to talk to him most of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you value sleep, I wouldn't recommend this prof, but if you have any interest in law you have to take it with him.  Unbelievable amount of hard work, but it pays off in the end.

Professor Gold's class was not easy. But it was my favorite class at Cornell. You learn  a TON. He is inspiring and really dedicated to his students; I was assigned a group and we got along super well so it took some of the pressure off. He wrote my recommendation for law school and now I'm a labor and employment lawyer, if that tells you anything.

worst professor in ILR. Least clear assignments, but has very specific expectations. He doesn't realize that students have other classes besides his, and you will leave each class with no idea of what to do/how to apply the information from class.  Very smart man but awful instructor. Avoid his class at all costs.

if you want to go to law school this is life affirming. otherwise, get a different professor for labor law.  I spent all my time on this class and got an 80% which curved  to an A. Lots of group work but you can't choose your group which sucks sometimes. The Law school TA is SUPER HELPFUL, you'll learn a ton about labor law/your writing. MeanB+

Prof. Gold is great. His class had  a reputation for being hard as hell, but it really isn't all that bad. There is a lot of required reading and pop quizzes just about every class. Most of the homework is group work. Don't worry about his tough grading;  I had a 45% raw score at the end of the semester that got curved to a B. Learned a TON.

For Ethics at Work (sophomore writing seminar), he values more quality than quantity. You don't write that much, but you need to summarize complicated philosophical concepts and theories in 2 pages. Take notes; they help a little. Reading helps a little. Office hours help more.

If you take this class, make sure your footnotes are on the correct side of the period at the end of the sentence--I had 1% taken of my final paper for each incorrectly placed footnote (about 34 in all). If thats the kind of class you like, then go for it. If its not, then you will regret taking it and you probably wont get above a B-.

Professor Gold is the professor who lets you challenge him and doesn't dismiss your ideas when they're different.  My class with Professor Gold is the highlight of my semester. His comments on your papers are longer than the papers themselves; I learn so much about my writing style, my strengths, and my weaknesses. It's  such a pleasure.

His Labor Law course is by far my favorite class. While the work is extensive it is all extremely relevant to the lectures. He starts off each class with a joke or a funny story. He also asks if there are any questions from the previous lecture. In the end, the curve will help you a ton so don't freak about the low grades throughout the semester.

Gold is incredibly intense and intimidating & labor law is undeniably demanding. But he is a fascinating lecturer, a fair teacher, and incredibly knowledgeable. The workload is very heavy but classmates bond over essays & seemingly impossible assignments. The difficulty is worth it; I learned so much in this class. Attendance- basically mandatory.

Probably the most demanding professor at Cornell and the teacher of ILR's most demanding class. He's incredibly smart and experienced.  You will learn TONS about labor law (and time management). Workload is insane, but his lectures and your knowledge at the end of the course make up for it. 2010 is great for bonding with others over lack of sleep.

Professor Gold's course has been by far the best course I have ever taken at Cornell University.  He is a very fair professor which views students as equals, no matter their backgrounds, and challenges every student in the same manner.  I highly recommend this course.
he is a great guy and amazing teacher. don't be scared to take his class. there's work, but it's definitely worth it in the end.
The material is not easy for sure. Luckily, Professor Gold makes it interesting and he is fair.

Probably the best class I've taken at Cornell.  I dreaded the course and Professor Gold before taking his class, and ended up loving them both.  Plan your other classes around this one though -- incredible amount of nightly work.  Gold stimulates creative thinking unlike any professor I've had, and in the end, I view the world differently.

So I figured I would kick off 2009 by reiterating that Professor Gold still is, in fact, moderately deranged. With that said, he is a brilliant professor and a leader in his field. I would not discourage any ILRee from taking his class. His work is tough and time consuming, but I can not criticize Gold for demanding a lot from his students.
Amazing teacher. If you get a chance, chat with him outside of class about something besides class, you'll be suprised.

As a current law school student and former labor relations specialist, I can fully appreciate Gold's teaching style.  I'm sure that I learned more in his class than the other CB201 professors taught their students.  Do not shy away from this class if you really want to learn labor law.

Not to belabor the point, but Prof. Gold definitely is intelligent, knows labor law well, and teaches the topic well. However, unless you have a major interest in (labor) law, it is truly senseless to work exponentially harder in this class than in the other labor law classes. The grading is fair, it's just that the amount of work is excessive.

While he might be a good professor, there is way too much work compared to the other labor law class, and the grades end up being the same.  If you want to learn and dont care about grades, then take him, if however care about your gpa and or time, think twice before signing up

What can you say about Gold? Yes, it's a very demanding & grueling class & you will learn a lot. And yes, nothing that you could ever read or say will prepare you for the amount of work required for this class. He can be insensitive & a harsh grader, but you will walk away w/more knowledge than you ever thought possible. Take him & enjoy the ride.
If you want to go to Law School...take GOLD! He is one of ILR's most knowledgable professors and you are truly missing out if you choose not to take him at least once.

This class is worth at least 6 credits and not the 3 they claim, you WILL be doing hmwk for this class EVERY night and it WILL keep you up to the early hours in the morning for research papers and homework alike- Gold isn't a bad guy, but he doesn't seem to understand that students are taking more than just his class- that or he doesn't care
Gold is pretty interesting in lecture, but this class has waaaaaaaaaay to much work invovled for a mere 3 credits.... avoid if possible

Take Intro Labor Law with Gold if you actually want an introduction to labor law. Yeah this class is hard but if you put in effort you do well, and thats how a class should be taught. You'll learn more here than in any other class I've taken at the ILR school. If you can afford to, do it.
Great Professor, but this class is not for the faint of heart...

most of the positive comments that i've seen and heard about him have been about his wardrobe; i think that should say enough, shouldnt it? this class is very very very hard. there is  online homework every day, and he gives pop quizzes in class. avoid gold if you can.
No Comments

A dapper gentleman indeed, finer cloths could not be weaved by angels.  A symphony of colors await the eyes as he bedazzles the room with his latest vest's of splendor.  Oh what a sight it is to glare upon Michael Evan Gold in all of his splendor, yes a class worth taking if only for the aesthetics

Prof. Gold is one of the most handsomely dressed men at Cornell.  A throwback to a gone era when professors never wore jeans and and always wore a tie.  He classes it up with an array of argiles, sweater vests, and bow ties.  He also has the academic prowess of no one i've had at Cornell

Surviving this class is quite an accomplishment.  A typical week consisted on 3-4 homework assignments and 2-3 quizzes.  Plus, he is also the type of professor who takes advantage of the fact that Cornell schedules breaks to start at 1 in the afternoon.  Also, don't plan on sleeping come paper time.

He requires a lot of work, if you stay on top of it you should be fine.  No final or midterm, but you will take 50-60 online quizes throughout the semester.  He also requires a three part final paper, talk to someone who took the class before to find out how to do well on the paper.

Not that bad of a class.  A lot of work, but when it's over and you don't have to take a final it feels worth it.  You learn a lot, but work hard to learn it.  Prof Gold is intimidating at first, but if you ask him for help he's very receptive and willing.

Somewhat helpful in OH; extreeeeemley hard class, take it only if you really want to go to law school of like the law.  Sometimes can be a real jerk, but sometimes can be nice.  Not a very interesting person
Tons of work. But overall, well worth it. You will get the most out of his classes than you would anywhere else. If you are considering law school, you must take him.
He is one of the smartest profs in cornell, but the class requires a lot of work. He'll "force" you to learn stuff
The mean on a paper was a 30%, enough said. So difficult, you feel so stupid in the class.
tons of work. very difficult. stay away.
Lots of work, but if you do it and do it well, you will be fine
Impossible assignments, but great class. He is a genius and is good at providing help to those who seek it. A must for anyone considering law school, ILR or otherwise.
Tough, but if you stick with Gold's classes you will learn a ton.  He's a great guy if you prove to him that you want to succeed.  Not a professor to take if you are lazy.
You will learn more about the law than you would ever imagine.  He's extremely smart.  He talks down to you.  The assignments are impossible.  Amazing class!
No Comments
You Learn So Much...He will help you if you ask!
Had this guy as professor-- get ready to work hard and fail!
Avoid!
impossible
Demanding, but a great guy if you know him
The worst--degrading to students.
She gives more than two job positions to only one student, which looks fishy! No talent, no caliber seen in the student, so what is actually the criterion for hiring?

She has her own favorites and favors them more than anybody else. Gives TA jobs to some 2025 alumni who don't even know how to write grants or explain them. Neither the TA nor the class was helpful. Waste of money, time, and energy!

Instructions are extremely unclear, nothing important is taught in class. 82% of the class fail on the first homework, that's an instructions PROBLEM. Student went to her, brought up the problems and then never acknowledge the problem, kept emphasizing that her intentions were to "help" us, "setting us up for success"?

Jealous of students who work hard and acheive this by themselves. She is less of a teacher more of a competitor! Highly racist. Not sure who has given the good review about her saying she is easy to reach, but you have to email her a lot to get in touch with her or reach out to a staff member in the MPH suite. She and Audrey Baker are the worst.

When she sits in a group, her problem is she will entertain potty mouth students who will bully asian students. Instead of neutralizing the situation and creating a friendly environment, she will laugh and make jokes out of them. She leaves her professionalism at home and comes to work. She is a big bully!
Love Gen! She's super supportive and is easy to get into contact with. Offers great feedback and makes the grading criteria very clear on the rubric.

Horrible! Very egotistic about her experiences, flaunts it everywhere. Very biased. Rubrics -unclear! She never responds to emails. Has zero knowledge. Doesn't teach at all, and will just make students sit in teams and work on the rubric. Very insecure and jealous of ambitious students. Misleads students in career opportunities and is unsupportive.
She's very caring, explains systems very clearly, easy to understand, good class structure, has dogs :)
good class
great class
Great class!

Guidi is a great lecturer. She occasionally stumbles or makes slight mistakes, but she's also a pretty new lecturer and those really don't get in the way. When there rare mistakes, she fixes them. Course organization was excellent, even considering the course had just been redesigned. Grading was fair as well. Definitely recommend!
The class is very applied, covers a wide range of topics, and introduces you to numerous tools. The homework can be long but is always rewarding. The lectures are good.
I would not recommend this professor due to their teaching style.
Not good, stay away
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor

if you're confused by the variance in ratings, he writes the good ones himself. he is notoriously bad, and I recommend you don't take his class unless you need to for graduating/going abroad. otherwise wait.
Unreasonable, abrupt bursts and Unnecessary strict approach made it a stressful learning environment.

Prof. Jakubson's teaching style is certainly unique, but overall, his lectures, which were often at a slowed-down pace, made the material digestible. His cold-calling was intimidating, but you should be fine as long as you're clearly paying attention in class. Expectations for exams are clear, and he's a fair grader. But review slides thoroughly.

Professor Jakubson has a tough teaching style, but engaging with it can pay off. Lectures may be confusing at first, but office hours help clarify things. For study prep, try using unstuck study alongside the free textbook - it's a game-changer.
very disrespectful

He's an extremely nice guy. From the first classes, he clearly clarifies what bothers him and what doesn't. Make sure you are on his side: don't take out your cell phone in class, participate, etc. Basically, be engaged with the class and you will do well. He knows a lot about econometrics and tries to make it easy for students to understand.

To pass GJ's class go to lectures &review the problem sets, modules, &sample test materials. If you don't attend lectures you won't understand how to apply his notes to answer problems on prelims. Mostly he spoke of his EMT experiences & cautioned us to be safe during cold winters, covid, & slope day season. Put in some effort you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. He teaches a difficult subject very well. He does get irked when students ask basic questions he's already gone over, which is why he gets a bad rap. But if you try, getting an A is very doable. His office hours help a lot. Don't let these lousy reviews scare you, they are likely from students who put in little effort

A friendly guy with a hard shell. You will do well if you go to office hours. His lectures can be confusing but once you get it, you get it. The other reviews are misleading-- no one goes to class and no one goes to office hours. It is hard work, but I enjoyed my class with him.

i'm sure he is a very smart economist but he simply should not be a professor. lectures are genuinely useless but attendance counts. acts personally offended if you have a question that is "too simple." extremely condescending. exams are evil (q's are purposely misleading, include "optional" content, avg in 50s vs 90s in other classes). avoid.

By far the worst Cornell professor I've ever had and I've taken every ILR core class. Jakubson genuinely ruined my semester. It's genuinely impossible to follow the lectures/slides, and there is no textbook. He complains every class about how no one comes to class as though it's anyone but his fault.

The other reviews say it all. Professor Jakubson as Economics DUS has been very rude in his communication with students. I don't understand where all this anger comes from when all a student does was asking simple questions.

So rude that I don't understand how he's still allowed to teach. It shocks me that a professor can speak to a student like this. Watching him speak to people like that made me shocked that an institution like Cornell could ever hire him. This man should not be an educator, nor exposed to most decent humans because of his unprofessionalism.
This is one of the rudest most unprofessional professors who will come across on this campus. This man should not be allowed to interact with students.

I only took Jakubson's class to avoid having an 8AM and that was the biggest mistake I've made in my entire Cornell career. If you can avoid Jakubson's class AVOID IT LIKE THE PLAGUE!!!!! He is truly a terrible teacher, if you take his class prepare to not understand anything despite studying for prelims 2 weeks in advance and attending lecture.

Lectures are very hard to follow. material unclear. The only actually helpful days are workdays. I was excited about this class but as time went on, the material taught didn't translate in PS. TA was amazing. I was able to learn the very basic stuff from them. Take it with someone else,
Super lost in this class. Could have been a cool/enjoyable subject, but every lecture makes things more unclear. Wish I had taken it in a different semester.

Professor Jakubson gets a bad rep. He teaches a technical course to students who normally hate anything quantitative, but he really does care about his students. If you do the work and consistently practice on your own outside of class, you'll be fine in this course. This is not a spectator's course - don't try to cram the material.

Professor Jakubson has some harsh reviews, and I knew that going into his class it would be tricky. However, the people writing reviews are likely the ones who didn't put in the effort. He was extremely accessible outside of class and willing to answer any questions! GO TO OFFICE HOURS and you will be fine in this course. Cannot stress it enough
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Went from live to online. Likes to waste time telling stories in class. Lecture barely makes any sense and neither do the psets or tests. He doesn't use a textbook or slides and writes messy stuff on a chalkboard. Study his pset answers hard and you'll do okay on tests thanks to the massive curve. Tests avgs are like a 50. AVOID this class.

One of the worst professors at Cornell, certainly worst in ILR. Incredibly rude to students, expects everyone to know as much as him. Gets distracted during lectures telling pointless stories and being passive aggressive - this class is the biggest waste of time. Also extremely disorganized, prelims are not easy. Avoid this class at all costs.

Jakubson is by far the least caring professor I have ever/will ever interact with at Cornell. He is extremely passive aggressive to students for no reason. I have reached out to him a few times with professional emails asking simple questions about the course of study for econ, and each time he has responded extremely rudely. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!

Completely mishandled online classes. Expects students to attend online lectures but spends the first 20 minutes nagging and down-talking to students. He has a large temper and has a habit of getting upset with students during lecture. Lectures are rambly and unfocused, may be due to unfamiliarity with online format, but still bad for the student.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at Cornell. The topic was difficult, but Professor Jakubson is incredibly willing to help outside of class. The TA was great. He really wants you to succeed, but you have to put in work. Lectures could be a little slow and tests are hard but everything is curved up.

AVOID this class. He's a nice guy, but not meant for teaching. No one knows what he talks about in class, and he doesn't use slides or a textbook. Says attendance doesn't matter but passes around a sign-in sheet every class. Psets and tests also make no sense, and means fall below 50. Don't worry, the massive curve will save you. Utilize the TA.

One of the best professors I have ever had. If you show up with respect and determination George will show you mutual respect and dedication. He makes sure that everybody in class knows what is going on and is extremely personable. Makes waking up for an early class not just worth it but ENJOYABLE! I absolutely recommend taking his class.

This class is a straight up disaster. Tests are much harder than the hw. I think I finished 2/3 of the final. He is difficult to deal with in class or in OH and gets mad when the prelim average is a 50. I would recommend avoiding him at all costs and take 3120 w/ someone else

Worst class I've taken. Condescending and very disrespectful. He literally makes students chant after him and says things like "good job, you guys finally reached grade school" He says he makes us do this to engage in "educational scaffolding" but anyone with a brain will know that he's just doing it for the sense of control. tldr:Napoleon Complex
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AVOID him at all costs. He gave the "option" of starting the final an hour earlier with a super long exam that you would't even be able to finish in 4 hours, not to mention that it was not fair for those who chose to show up on time. Questions were tricky and LONG. He didn't provide practice exams and lectures were pointless.
It depends. If you are a normal human, avoid him.

This was the worst class I've taken at Cornell by far. The material is inherently more difficult and mathematical than any course in the Econ major but Professor Jacobson makes life harder than it needs to be. He flips if you whisper to a friend next to you or fall asleep for a second. Very demanding and has absurdly high expectations for students.

I would not recommend taking Labor Econ with Professor Jakubson. He is a nice enough guy, but he takes the structure out of the material and tries to explain it all like one big story. Grading is very arbitrary as students who got 40s and 50s on prelims ended up getting Bs in the class. Take Labor Econ with Hutchens instead.

Amazing professor, I honestly learned so much even though I basically failed every exam, and it ended up being my highest grade in the semester. Visit office hours, study the practice exams, and attend lecture. If you have an option to take him then I highly recommend it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: AVOID Prof Jakubson at ALL costs. He is the WORST. He is nice if you approach him correctly. But, his class is SO hard. The lectures and textbooks are pretty much useless. Go to office hours and take the practice prelims until you memorize the answers (exactly what he doesn't want you to do) the class is impossible if you don't. Disrespectful Prof.

All test questions are based on practice prelims and problems sets.  There are 2 problems sets about 6 questions each throughout the course. He doesn't grade them he just checks for completion. At the end he curves generously so people who got 40 and 60ish on prelims end up getting Bs for final grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His class is difficult, but it is fair. His lectures are really helpful and cannot be substituted by the textbook. He really gives a good understanding of basic labor economic thought and theory. I highly recommend taking his class!

Professor George was clear, engaging, and most of all cared about actually teaching econometrics to us in practical terms. He made himself available every day after class if you had any extra question. As long as you went to class, did the homework, and participated you should have no trouble getting an A. Great guy- really glad i look this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE labor economics with Jakubson. For someone who has taken Intermediate level economics courses at Cornell, Jakubson's Labor Economics course was a nightmare. He is disorganized, lectures are like story times, and the more he tries to take the "math" out of his material, more he makes the course pointless. Grading is also very arbitrary.
no, just no

Jakubson just wants his students to learn and if you put in the effort, you will absolutely get a great grade. I understood more about economics in 1 week of his class than I did from an entire semester of micro or macro econ. Do the problem sets, go to office hours, show you're making an effort, and an A+ is very possible.

Professor Jakubson was an amazing professor, definitely one of my favorites. I took the course during the summer and learned so much! I recommend going to office hours. Jakubson really cares about his students and wants them to learn the material, if you show progression throughout the course you will be fine! Thanks George!

Amazing Professor... I entered his class having failed Labor Econ already and ended with a B+.. pretty good considering I failed the first two tests. More importantly, I'm now an econ minor. Thanks Prof. Jakubson!
Great professor. Don't rely on the book. Go to lecture and you'll be fine. Expect to put in some work but he's very approachable in office hours.

Jakubson is a phenomenal lecturer. Prior to the course I had little to no understanding of the material, but he is incredibly good at simply explaining complex topics and I left the class feeling like I finally "got" it. He makes himself very available for office hours. He can be condescending, but he's a very patient teacher for those who struggle

Professor Jakubson made econometrics as painless as possible. He posts solid practice prelims and made himself available every morning for office hours to help struggling students. He grades based on improvement so he won't kill your grade if you bomb one of the exams. His exams are typically very long though.

George's class is intimidating. Prelims are hard. However, if you go to office hours and show progression throughout the course its an easy A-. I almost dropped the class, but decided to stay and I couldn't be happier with the decision. Hes a great guy, quirky but runs a great class. PS  no need to buy the book, just use his hand outs

During office hours, Jakubson is very helpful. During class, however, it seems as if he doesn't care at all. You either know it or you don't, and too bad for you if you don't. Additionally, his exams are ridiculously hard, and we are expected to know the material as well as he does. If you are able to, take ILRLE 2400 with a different professor.

Class is absolutely boring! He uses the same sayings and "explanations" constantly.  Answers questions with questions and useless tangents that have no relation to what the student wanted to figure out. Miserable excuse for a teacher, since he does not like to teach. Talked badly about TA too. Perfect example of the cons of tenure.

This man helped me so much, beyond the classroom included. He is a genuinely caring person who wants to help his students if they come to him for help. As  teacher, he is a little loopy and can be a little frazzled-seeming, but he makes his points relatively clear. Of course, I had him over the summer so I don't know what he's like usually.

Lectures arent exactly clear but they are fairly interesting. He gives out solid practice prelims for the test and curves it generously if need be. Take ILRLE 2400 with Jakubson if you actually want to learn something. The class is curved to a B+/A-.

He really wants to be the professor who gets you into statistics, but his glaring mental instability prevents him from achieving this.  His class is like a gauntlet, be ready to be verbally taunted and treated with zero tolerance if you make the slightly faux pas. Take at own risk

Had him for summer. His notes in his lectures make you wonder why you copied them down in the first place when you review them, but then the magic appears when you go to his office hours because he does a WAY better job explaining than during class. Btw, do NOT do anything distracting such as and even asking your TA a question, or you'll regret it.

Liked the graphs and comparisons and approach of prof. Not a bad guy. Needs to get over his Napoleon complex. He's too much about power and control. Gets in the way of enjoyment of class and the material. Needs to take some vicodin and chill out. Has too much tendency towards anger.
Great professor! Super helpful, one of the nicest I've had at Cornell. Makes econometrics as clear as possible!
Worst professor I've ever had. Avoid this guy if at all possible. He is the devil's reincarnate. You have been warned. That is all.

Is not easy, although, if you do all the homeworks and keep notes in class it is totally do-able! Sessions are extremely important in order to pass the exams and completely understand. The material is great since all are real life/applied cases and that gives the class a great point of view.

Man, everyone's being so mean about this guy. He was really nice to me. Admittedly, he doesn't dress for class and he does kind of swagger, but he's still a great prof. Haters hate because they didn't get a good grade!

Took the course over the Summer.  Definitely a great professor.  Knew what he was teaching and used real world data for the course.  Just go to class, do what Jakubson tells you to do for hw, etc, and there should be no reason why any student cannot ace this course.

Jakubson's an excellent professor with a sense of humor and a passion for economics. Admittedly, he hates it when students don't show up to class or treat him as a joke -- understandably. If you do the work (don't bother with the textbook), go to class, and go to office hours, you'll get an A.

Jakubson is one of the LE department's worst (has been there for 30 years and still has very little recognition). His lectures are terrible--he spends many of them shaming his students after a poor test, then does little to prepare students for the next one. Simply inept at explaining econ concepts and stifles classroom discussion Faculty hates him

If the Devil had a name it would be Jakubson. If you are looking for the worst professor in the world... congratulations you have found him. This guy is worse than death. I generally do well in all my courses but this class i blame it 130% on this guy's mediocre teaching skills. If you are taking this class prepare your souls.

Horrible.  Lectures are incomprehensible. Related everything to "the moon is made of cream cheese." Tested and assigned homework on SAS programming without a single mention or guide. Tests are wayyyyy too long for alloted time. Without exaggeration, the worst professor ever.

He always made himself appear to be very helpful, but I'm not sure how helpful he really was. He has catchphrases which get old fast. He said he would make it a 2 1/2 hour open note final but give us 3 1/2 hours to do it. By the end of the 2 1/2 hours, I had finally arrived at the last 17-part question. Despite this, still not a bad class.

Teacher was very helpful, very approachable. Material was not easy, but he welcome you to his office hours and helped there. He gave out practice prelims and a practice final which all were very useful. His exams reflected what he taught in class. Class attendance is a must to do well!

I second the comments made by the previous commenter. The midterm was hard and the final was god-awful. The lectures were hard to follow and there was very little continuity from lecture to lecture. Not recommended.

Basically taught as an applied course.  Disorganized lectures and a lot of jumping around in the textbook.  Still, Jakubson is a really nice guy and very smart; he always makes an effort to accommodate students.  Few homeworks; tests were really long.  Wish we had gone into the more technical side of concepts.  He doesn't like math.
Publicly humiliates students in a semi-joking manner, causes permanent trauma and fear of the professor.
Totally awesome.

Rudest guy ever. He explains things to you like you're an idiot. Even more unhelpful in office hours. Definitely does NOT stick to the syllabus, he changes what you'll be graded on after every prelim. Overall, is very knowledgeable but CANNOT teach to save his life.
Garbage.  Straight garbage.  Good luck.
No outline of what is expected in class or on tests
Econometics is hard, but if you go to class and pay attention you can get a good grade.  Jakubson is tough, but his office hours are very helpful and the material is interesting.  Great class!
cares about our learning, funny guy
Avoid! Avoid! Spends the majority of the class period making students feel stupid...Does not use the text...This class has given me a huge headache. It is not worth your time.

this man called some poor kid stupid in front of the whole class. i find the way he swaggers and sways about to be greatly offensive. he also needs to stop saying "so far so good" bc its not so good, ITS NOT SO GOOD. finally, he needs to stop talking about his children, as they probably hate him just as much as the rest of the world.
AVOID. Spends the whole class time trying to find different ways to call you an idiot. Doesn't seem like he is teaching economics at all.
No Comments

Terrible teacher.  For one he dresses like a construction worker.  He is unclear and all over the place.  Seems to lecture from the top of his head.  Don't buy the book, he doesn't test from it at all.  He makes fun of ILR students to his higher level econ classes.  My suggestion is to go to the TA's office hours early on.  stay on top of it.

Oki...econometrics is a hard subject to study..there will be people who wont understand it at all...and professor's teaching style can be arguable..BUT he George is very nice person, if you use his office hours, and he is THE easiest grader in economics department. And if metics make sense to you,...you will easily get A+ on this class..

He is actually really nice and only rude when someone deserves it.  HOWEVER, I agree that the question of what to study is extremely unclear:  you don't want to waste your time druding through that boring textbook, but at the same time his class lectures are scattered in their material and it's impossible to to tell which concepts are important.

Office Hours: Gets annoyed when visited, actually called one girl an "idiot" for coming to office hours. She cried. Classes: Also says things like "shut up" and "sick of you" to a certain person in front of the whole class without reservation. Book: totally irrelevant and he just teaches whatever the heck he wants, not necessarily following the boo

He is very knowledgable and a very engagin lecturer. Give him a chance and ignore the silly ratings left by the few unfortunates who are too retarded to understanted basic economic concepts. He gives you solid practice exams and throws a nice curve on the grades if need be. Utilyze office hours if you are confused...he likes explaining things

Jakubson is an outstanding professor and knows his economics.  You must utilize your time well and actually put some effort into this class in order to do well.  The concepts aren't too hard to grasp and he is always willing to help you out if you don't understand the content.  I recommend taking Jakubson although you must know your basic algebra.

I dont know what these negative comments are about. He is amazing. So smart, Jakubson, teaches to the common person. His analogy of picking up chicks in the bar and applying economic theory to it made my semester complete. TAKE LE WITH HIM!

uggggghhhh what a HARD class.  he somehow managed to inject soooo much math into a class that really didn't require it.  Spent much of the class talking about the theories but would expect students to magically know how to do the math on the test. Avoid if at all possible.
Jakubson = Satan. Anyone who says otherwise is an engineer crying tears of joy to have a break from their miserable engineering curriculum.

What a pompous prick. His lectures are jumbled, he removes the projector sheets after 30 seconds, and the textbook is completely useless. His tests are marathons that are challenges to complete. It doesn’t reward knowledge, but how fast you can work. In office hours he says u r either stupid or lazy
worst professor, worst class, avoid at all costs

The worst Econ professor I have ever had. He is arrogant, has an annoying lecture format, and makes his exams unreasonably long. He seems to know his stuff, but he has a really hard time passing any knowledge on to his students.
I thought his class was very fair.  He is very approchable if you give him a chance.  Also he is hot. With that beautiful facial hair.
No Comments
very unhelpful
He is a great teacher and always helpful during office hours.  You just have to go to lecture and take advantage of office hours. Not easy, but you learn a lot.

DON'T BELIEVE THE LIES! Excellent, challenging Economics course - you learn a LOT. Professor Jakubson is super nice and super helpful, and rewards students for exceptional progress. Our TA, Jing Liu was absolutely awesome! HIGHLY RECOMMENDENDED COURSE!
I agree with someone down there. This man is Satan. Every rumor you have heard is absolutely true. This man and this class are two of the WORST things about this school.
His lectures are clear, but the problem sets basically REQUIRE you to show up to every office hours for help.  Tests are exactly like the practice exam.
Straight up awful.
The hardest class I ever took in Cornell...I can still remember the pain of the problem sets after 3+ years...
not a bad lecturer, but unhelpful and arrogant.  thinks he's god's gift to statistics.  smirks a lot and is very short.

Jakubson actually isn't a bad lecturer. Unfortunately, he doesn't convey the material particularly well and his tests are unreasonably difficult. He also was not particularly helpful and when I voiced a concern about the class he kind of blew up.
He thinks that he is an amazing teacher and that his methods will help everybody see the light.  This couldn't be further from the truth.
Yuck.

This man is the devil. He will do whatever he can to make your experience as harsh and terrible as possible. Do not take 321. It is worth it to take 319 and 320 just to not have to deal with Jakubson.
Very interesting lecturer and class. Exams tended to be specific, but graded fairly. Lab portion is a lot of work with making the collection
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
very kind and funny, flexible about deadlines, and reasonable grading.

That said, this class is extremely hard if you don't already have a very strong understanding of insect bio it will take up a lot of time to memorize and learn everything.

I love this guy, but I don't love the way he teaches. Super cool guy, but his lectures are unclear and he includes material that is neither in the textbook nor lectures in his prelim. I thought BIOG 1440 was easy, but he was by far the hardest out of the four professors. Still love him though.

He's interesting and engaging, but his slides are mostly pics so you need to pay good attention. A lot of times he talks about unrelated things. The class is moderately difficult. There's videos, readings, and mandatory quizzes twice a week, 4 prelims, optional final, and attendance is not mandatory. Prelims are tricky. Don't take if not required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite lecturers from this class.

Lecture notes are unclear and difficult to understand. Supplemental material don't pertain to lecture. Lecture topics random and disorganized. Lectures are repetitive and boring. Tests are on hyper-specific topics sometimes missing from lectures entirely. no curve

His lectures are a bit boring and each of his slides are just crammed with info. Pretty friendly guy tho. He makes an effort to teach but sometimes he explains concepts in a way that is more confusing than it should be. I also feel like the content on the exams are deeper than what he discusses in lecture.

He didn't get everyone falling asleep in class, but that DOESN'T MEAN he was a good professor. Lecture content was VERY different from test material, and the class WAS NOT curved. The average was supposed to be a C, but he widened the bins so everyone got a B-. Then the very last day of grading, he changed half the grades due to math error. RUN.

Dr Gilbert is by far the funniest and coolest lecturer of 1780. He teaches Animal evolutionary history and is hilarious and one of the few professors for the class that is actually engaging. Very down to earth, very meme worthy. Favorite professor of the semester by far, if only for the pure sass and sarcasm emanating from this man.
The insect collection is tough, but that's mandatory for the course and good planning will make it work. Cole is hilarious and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This professor is boring and disorganized. I have not gotten lower than an "A" until this 1440 Biology class. If you think looking at slides all course and cracking silly jokes is fun great. Exams had no continuity with lectures! Should have gotten out of his course. Then half the final grades posted were wrong and the final grades reposted - WOW!

Cole is a great lecturer and cracks a lot of dumb jokes. Definitely a steep learning curve in the lab and obviously geared towards people with some background knowledge already. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on the insect collection.

The fun does not balance out the work. The first half of the semester is unreasonably hard. Lecture is interesting even though it is early in the morning. Lab and the practicals are harder than class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Terrible Class. Will never take again. Must have entire bug collection in addition to lab tests AND prelims in class. Tons of work. No reward.

He is definitely a nice guy, but I don't see how the lab and lecture correlate. In lab, you get thrown right in without any explanation. Lectures, he talks about basic, cool things, but you have to know a lot of details which he doesn't make you aware of. This should be an intro course, but I feel like I should have had a lot of prior knowledge.
Cole is an amazing lecturer and incredibly funny. He's super helpful and really does his best to make the class as informative and fun as possible.
So much better than Booker! And he's funny. He's very clear and keeps students engaged. Great professor!

Prof. Gilbert was great! He tried to be as interesting as you can with this material. His lectures were clear and simple, and he showed genuine interest in our understanding the subject and being prepared for the exams. Oh, and sometimes he'd randomly run around to make a point. Cool guy!

Cole is one of the best professors at Cornell that I've encountered. His lectures are interesting, and doesn't just lecture the reading; he goes above and beyond the reading. He is an incredibly nice guy, and extremely knowledgeable about entomology. I loved this course with him. A+

Hilarious.  The powerpoint slides he makes are very entertaining.  His material in 1780 can be hard because it's all memorization but he gives lots of interesting examples.  Possibly my favorite of the five 1780 lecturers.

Cole Gilbert is awesome.  Coming from an engineering and pre-med background, its really refreshing to have a teacher that is enthralled with what he teaches and can talk to students in a relaxed atmosphere.  As for the class, study his lectures and ask questions during lab and you'll do fine.  I just wish he'd teach more classes!
It was clear that he wanted us to do well, but he was not effective at teaching and I found the tests to be unfair compared to the material taught.

Fun class, Professor Gilbert made what would have been rather dry and straight from the text much more interesting with his anecdotes and examples but did not get sidetracked by them - lecture focused on major concepts not detail.
Great, interesting professor.
No Comments
Okay class, not a great teacher. Make sure you stay on schedule with the readings.

Dr. Gilbert is really, REALLY good. One of the best lecturers I could wish for. I wish all teachers could be so amiable yet knowledgeable. There are some profs you can't hear bc they mumble- Dr. Gilbert will never subject you to that. Crystal clear! Makes Bio accessible!!!
nice guy, sort of interesting sometimes, class needs a lot of reading and lectures can get pretty boring

Dr. Gilbert is an amazing teacher. Unlike other profs, he genuinely wants you to succeed and isn't out to get you. Tests are fair, but be prepared to put in a lot of effort. Goes through ppts and lectures very quickly, but they're all online afterwards. He also has pre lecture questions to help with the reading. Overall, an amazing teacher.

Fun lecturer.  Goes through slides a little too fast, but posts powerpoints and audio recording of lectures online, so you can catch up later and study easily.  Tests aren't easy, but they won't contain that many inordinately difficult questions.
Kool dude. Go through the powerpoint and lecture audio before the exam and ur golden.

Dr. Gilbert is not a good professor...he flies through his powerpoints without taking a breath...it's impossible to catch hardly any of what he is saying...his tests are unbearably difficult b/c of the large amount of material he inadequately covers..if you want to pass his class, be prepared to put in lot of extra work teaching yourself everything

Cole Gilbert is one of the most helpful professors at Cornell just go to his office hours. Though he zips through lecture and it can be difficult to keep up at first, as long as you actually put some effort its managable. He has a sence of humor too and truly tries to make class entertaining. Great professor to have.
Though he zipps through his lecture he tries to keep it interesting and is extremely accessable and helpfull during his office hours
No Comments

His lectures were informative but boring, he chose some really random and irrelevant things to go in depth with. Otherwise really helpful though. Good use of powerpoints and the clicker questions were actually helpful. For prelims though, your best bet is to just memorize the book. It's a challenging class, but not impossible.

His teaching style doesn't make or break the class - he's just aite. Ideally, you could look at the ppt slides (& listen to audio if you want to) & skip class & do just fine, but you gotta go for the clicker q's. Study really hard, you know the rep of intro bio...
He's very enthusiatic and willing to help anybody
I liked how he taught the class with funny jokes and whatnot

Dynamic and exciting lectures. He sometimes goes into certain topics too deep, but that's fine. Prelims can be harder than you think so be prepared. I personally didn't like his prelims because some questions seemed irrelevant. Yet, overall, Prof.Gilbert is a great guy.
I like his lectures. The diagrams are great !!

Gilbert is AMAZING!!!  I absolutely love this class.  He's a really dynamic lecturer, and he knows his stuff.  I'm pretty sad that he won't be teaching 2nd semester intro bio.  The best way I've found to study for this class is to take my textbook and highlight/take notes in it as he lectures...he tends to follow it pretty closely.  He's great!

As an intro level bio class for majors, the class is meant to be difficult and lives up to its reputation. However Cole does a great job in teaching the class. By going to lecutres, keeping up on the readings, and studying difficult material extra the class in manageable. Cole does excellent lectures, has great powerpoints, and is so knowledgeable.
No Comments

Ent 212 was the best class I have ever taken!  Dr Gilbert teaches in a fun, involved manner; he takes a deep interest in each student's progress.  Classes are interesting, field trips are fun, and the lab-work actually holds purpose!!!!!!

Harms is an incredible professor who cares deeply about students' learning. He explains things in a way that anybody can understand how websites are designed and built. His grading criteria are extremely clear — you can get an A+ if you do what's expected. If you use Gen AI and miss the req that's on you. Genuinely the best coding prof at Cornell
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He manages to make simple things so convoluted with all of his extra steps and procedures. He also is just a very unforgiving and genuinely does not seem to care about his students.
