reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is not honestly as bad as most people claim -- the course has improved. The lectures were somewhat confusing and were paced oddly, so I often used the published notes. Professor was quite nice and helpful during office hours for revisions. Preparing for later LOs (Heat etc.) was annoying as pset problems did not align with exam problems.
I don't know what the hate for Ritz is. She gives amazing lectures, and really cares about her students. Sure the tests are hard; just study well.

Do not understand the hate towards this professor. The LO grading system is okay if you put in consistent effort across the entire semester and all quizzes and exams. This professor was wonderful in her office hours and her lectures were quite informative even if you don't read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Ritz is able to teach course content with clarity, providing students with plenty of opportunities to ask questions in lecture and review material. She uses interesting demonstrations during lecture (i.e., MATLAB scripts) to describe the physical behavior of differential equations. Overall, I really enjoyed this class with Prof. Ritz.

Ritz isn't the worst, but her grading with Learning Objectives (LO) is. You could be doing good all year, getting 3/3s on LOs on all 4 graded quizzes, and going into the final with 14/21 graded LOs as 3/3s and then bam. If you don't get the answer almost perfectly right you get a 1/3 and your grade is ruined. It's perfection or nothing with grades.

I think her teaching is fine, but most of her responses to questions on Ed Discussion are snarky and unfriendly. She will refuse to give actual answers to genuine questions and respond with things along the lines of "I will not entertain this" or "Why are you asking this?". It just makes me lose respect for her as a person.

For statics ritz has always been very transparent about all of the resources and the criteria to do well in her class. She is more than willing to help you in any way you need to succeed, if only you reach out to her. It's a hard class so make use of the resources.

I will not understand the hate against Ritz, she is mega caring and extremely accessible outside of class. You can tell she cares a lot about her students. For context, her canvas home page has a pep talk for the students. I truly enjoy the grading for this class and it is not as terrible as everyone says: just make sure to not fall behind.

Ritz is the best lecturer I have had at Cornell, for both ENGRD 2020 and MATH 2930. Her classes are definitely tough, but she is always there to support her students and wants to see them all succeed.
This is the worst grading system of any class I've ever had the misfortune of taking. You could do the entire course perfectly up to the final, miss two questions, and get an A-.
What can I say that hasn't already been said? Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Atrocious grading rubrics with no thought behind them. Consistently took off 20-40% from total homework grades for tiny errors like not writing dimensions on a Free Body Diagram or not writing "Given: Find: Plan" above the solution to a problem, even when all final answers were correct. Partial credit wasn't given on prelims, which weren't curved.

Says we get multiple attempts-not true. Gave no advice about approach to prelim 1, making prelim 2 a sprint through 9 questions. 2 problems drop a whole letter grade, we got 1 try for them, how this even makes sense when the whole point of this grading system is to have multiple chances. Class material is not bad but just ridiculous grading.
Some people have good karma coming their way. This is not one of those people

Not one to ever use this site, but wanted to publish a review for Professor Ritz.

I truly enjoyed my time in MATH2930 with Hadas Ritz, and I truly believe that this is the most that I have ever learned from a math class. Her lectures are incredibly understandable, and while the grading system may seem odd, she is very fair and it helped me learn.

Disrespectful/snarky on Ed, restricts posting to reduce criticism, doesn't respond to complaints, changes the rules every single day based on mood swings, revokes opportunities, contradicts her syllabus, imposes a draconian grading scheme no one asked for to try to prove research paper she wrote, targeted student who called her out

The new grading system is... interesting. I (and many others) did not like Ritz's course (the lectures move painfully slow), and it covers shockingly little material (no transforms??). The grading scheme doesn't aid with "learn at your own pace" and instead obfuscates what should be a pretty simple class. The material's easy, but grading isn't.

Ritz's grading system where your final grade is determined by mastery is awful. While her lectures were ok, she's got an attitude outside of class and on Ed discussion. Students tried to address some of these concerns and her solution was to set all threads to approval only and tries to silence students in class.

This class was awful; wouldn't recommend it. Uncertain grading scheme caused stress, with assignments delayed throughout the semester. She changed syllabus multiple times, leading to excessive work over holidays. Office hours were chaotic, and criticisms were dismissed as disrespectful. Students unfairly faced consequences due to her shortcomings.
Hadas Ritz is the GOAT when it comes to teaching Differential Equations! She's super chill and makes complex topics feel like a breeze. Love her teaching style!

Ritz is a great lecturer, but the grading scheme she tried to implement this semester was poorly organized and incredibly ineffective. Some things on the syllabus were changed in the last week of class, and there is little/no partial credit.

The class is graded by mastery which is an interesting adjustment to make. However, I enjoyed this grading style. While some of the assignments were very difficult the overall stress around exams was lessened and I believe I performed better on them because of this. Dr.Ritz is also very kind and super willing to help in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really easy class, easy grading scheme
grading system makes no sense

I have never learned as much as I did in this class. The homework and material IS very difficult. Ritz asked for feedback multiple times throughout the class and actually applied what she received; it's obvious she cares about students' learning. She is amazing at summarizing the material in approachable ways. Does a good job mixing in examples.

The material itself is not that difficult; she is.
A group of my friends went to find her for help because the exam average was a 70 (and we knew she was not going to give a good curve) -> professor said our year is just dumb. She doesn't understand how COVID exams are easier.

The class was curved to a low B- (she called it a generous curve).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ritz tried a new grading scheme that was too good to be true. While it intended to give us lots of opportunities to succeed, it ended up doing the opposite. There was a lack of transparency with the grading scheme, and students were left confused for the majority of the semester, with a huge workload at the end of the semester.

Took ENGRD 2020 in FA 22. Prof. Ritz tries her best to lecture well and convey the necessary material; however the homework sets were pretty long/convoluted and exams usually had a fair share of curveballs. Class was curved to low B- (super annoying) ... be ready for a lot of work for this class with her.

dumb grading system dumb; there were so many important quizzes due during the study period that it was hard to do work for other courses. Missing a single quiz can knock you down a +/- for the overall grade.

The psets are tough but doable for the most part. The content starts out alright but suddenly gets difficult toward the end. There's a harsh curve (median B-) for the overall course grade, and I literally did one std above the mean for prelim 2 and the final and still got a B+. There is "online homework" in addition to the pset, which are annoying.

Grading scheme had a cool concept but basically made all assignments either not worth the time or worth the same as an exam. Every assessment demands perfection or you won't get any credit at all, which makes it way harder to prove understanding than it needs to be. Make sure your TA likes you & be persistent with regrade requests.

The grading was inconsistent/inaccurate. Grading was either full points or no points: no partial credit. There were many times when I got full points on an assignment, and someone with the same answer and work got no points. Or I got no points, put in a regrade request, and then was told my answer was perfectly correct. Disappointing class.

Worst grading system of all time. Does not to partial credit at all. I did not receive credit for several things that I know how to do, because any small algebra mistake means you get no credit for an entire problem. That policy applies to exams, homework, quizes, and everything we do. It is the most awful system I have ever seen
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very stupid and unclear grading system that requires perfection. First two months we didn't know exactly how grading worked. It caused so much unnecessary stress and anxiety because they didn't communicate with students and assignments were graded very late. There were 6 assignments during study week and some of them were due after the final exam.

Very tough grader. She claimed that the course is graded on a curve and in the end, she said it is not exactly curved which doesn't make sense since the medians for all exams were in the mid 60s. They only slightly adjusted grade boundaries and still, the median grade was low B-. Don't take this course if you don't have to or you will only suffer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely confusing grading scheme. Good idea but poor implementation. Students were not informed enough until the end of semester where every assignment piles up and become very stressful.
Her courses traumatize me to the fullest

Avoid at all costs. horrible woman with zero empathy for students. Had her for both ENGRD2020 and MATH2930 in the same semester, would strongly advise against taking either course from her, but especially recommend not taking both from her at the same time unless you're willing to sacrifice both your gpa and many nights of sleep.

Assignments are graded late, no partial credit or mercy. Even going to office hours and getting your work personally checked is not enough, staff might still say it is wrong. Grading scheme felt unfair and does not reflect students mastery of concepts. Is a good lecturer when compared to the rest of the math department.

The grading system seemed appealing at first but it was not executed well at all. Students got drastically different levels of difficulty for the questions. The course was not planned well in that we had 2 checkpoints before prelim 2 and there were 8 due during the study period before finals. Does not address student concerns very well.

I took diff. eq. with Ritz under her new grading system, and unlike the majority of the class thought it was awesome! The grading scheme not only made it extremely easy to do well in the class, it also helped with learning and retaining the material. Ritz is a great lecturer who explains concepts well and addresses any and all question in lecture.

horrible new grading scheme that left students scrambling during finals week. students have no idea how they are doing in the course due to grades not being returned in a timely manner. she assigned ridiculous amounts of work during finals, doubt it'll be graded on time. she's causing stress to students already under lots of stress as engineers

Literally the worst Cornell class I have ever taken. I did well in this class and it still has inspired me to never take a class with professor Ritz ever again. If you see that Ritz is teaching a class that you need to graduate, you're better off taking a 5th year to get there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was a completely awful experience. I still have no clue what my grade is going to be and she owes me like ten grades. A total failure on her part. I do not know how a mandatory course can be taught this badly.

Professor Ritz fails to organize a half-decent, organized class. Students have little clue how well they are performing in the class until they recieve their final exam. The grading is lazy, as partial credit is simply not awarded, including for computation and algebra-heavy problems. 
Lectures are dull. Online course components are buggy. bad.

Bruuuuuuhhhhhh. Staff cannot keep up with new grading scheme. This has lead to a disorganized mess with feedback coming weeks after its relevant. We also have multiple assignments due 4 days after the last class - which the results of dictate what we need to study for on the final. Absolutey embarassing, and ridiculously stressful on students.

Her new grading scheme is too idealistic and disorganized. Her vision was good (student assessed based on general performance instead of test grades) , but as one of the guinea pig students I can say the disorganization of it all makes it only counterproductive. Turns out we are even more harshly penalized by any mistakes. Run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Remarkably and unacceptably poor at explaining concepts. Learned through textbook/other resources for the whole semester. Frequently makes errors in lecture, and often changes course structure in detrimental ways. If you can, try not to take this class with Prof. Ritz.
Worst professor I have ever had.

extremely disappointed with this classes policies, especially regarding the hw. Problem sets are excessively long + assigned every week, even on weeks with an exam/break. She also refuses to grade the 10+ page assignments unless they follow her insane formatting to a T. otherwise decent lecturer, just wish staff was even remotely empathetic.

Lectures were fine, not too hard to follow but some rough days on harder concepts. Homework was atrociously hard and took a whole day per assignment, covering more than what was on the prelims or in class. Prelims were terrible for covid semester as they were open book/entirely conceptual, with little actual math done on the exam. Discussions suck.
I was often confused during the semester because the material was difficult, but the lectures were so organized and help was so available that it was not difficult to catch up when I fell behind.
Moves too slowly through material in an uninteresting manner.

She is terrifying. But go to office hours for the homework (it's basically impossible without OH or some other kind of help). She has very high but clear expectations and posts good videos to help with difficult concepts. The exams are hard but straightforward so do the practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Ritz was the best engineering professor I had at Cornell. She is VERY knowledgeable, very organized, and was using digital resources effectively even before the pandemic. She doesn't take nonsense from students, but is also not abrasive or hostile to students. She will simply teach you the subject matter clearly and effectively.
Great professor
Just not a good lecturer. Spends lots of time in silence just writing stuff, which makes it very hard to focus. Doesn't help that her handwriting is really hard to read either.

One of my favorites at Cornell! She really cares about teaching, and is great at explaining things, both in lecture at office hours. She was very approachable and made lectures interesting. The class is undoubtedly hard, and you'll have to work for your grade, but there's a high level of support, and expectations are clear. Highly recommend!
Doesn't understand that there's a pandemic going on. Literally so frustrated and office hours were not helpful for this course at all. worst engineering class i've ever taken.

Incredibly off-putting personality, made me hate the subject from the very start of class. On top of this seems to assign work with some sort of vendetta in mind, intentionally confusing students with the mere selection of problems (not to mention the ridiculous format in which homework must be submitted) and then penalizing the confused class.

She doesn't understand that a lot of people do not care about mechanical engineering and how diff eq applies mostly to physics/mechE stuff. We just need the math requirement and will never use that material again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Assigns huge amounts of work even during weeks with exams
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Online homeworks are very difficult. Homeworks are usually manageable. Exams are hard, but fair
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class seems to be going well at the start then all of the sudden she throws a bunch of material and assignment at us at a time that we were supposed to be on break. The material that she threw at us was not easy and was not explained at all in lecture, she simply just clicked through the slides without a care in the world for her students.

Great lectures, definitely worth getting up before 8am for. Could actually do the hw on my own. Unfortunately, the exams were written by a different professor so that wasn't too great. Very good at explaining complicated topics in an understandable way and very patient.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I was wary of Statics, but Ritz was a fantastic professor who really made me interested in the material. The class is hard but not unmanageable if you put in the work - OH are very helpful! Lectures were above average and the exams were fair (although difficult). Homework sometimes seemed like a lot but the problems were worthwhile.

She is a great professor for freshman intro classes, but for junior/senior standing courses she expects more from her students to the point where it's almost too demanding. She gives a lot of difficult work across multiple categories (iClickers, lab quizzes and reports, hws, hit-or-miss exams) which makes it hard to maintain a consistent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lots of good reviews for 1000 level classes, but MAE3260 (Systems)  is a totally different animal. She got criticism last year for the sheer length of problem sets, cut them down for this year, and they are still three times longer than those in any other class. The class material is hard, yes, but her grading policies make it brutal. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. Lecture included participation which is unusual and helpful. She would give example problems in class and have you solve them, and give you time to work as she walked around the room to make sure people understood on an individual basis. Was glad to go over things that students didn't understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She cares  about her students but often struggles to get a hold of their attention. Not a lot of work with the exception of the final project which takes way too much time for the course's level.

Class super easy except the final design project takes up way too much time fore a 1000 level engineering course. Doesn't really lecture and just goes over problems in class, which is really a better class structure.

Really enjoyed this class. Lectures were usually enjoyable and the material was interesting but not too difficult. Labs can be very frustrating but the final project is a lot of fun. Good overview of mechanical engineering.

She likes doing examples on the board,  always pay attention to it. Doing them yourself helps you really learn the material. Also, don't be scared to ask questions in class, she'll answer and help you learn. Especially if you sit in the front like me. 1910 isn't always easy, going to her lectures will help. So please, don't skip, even if an 8 am!
Prof Ritz is an excellent lecturer - very clear and concise. She moves a bit quickly sometimes, and can seem intimidating, but overall a great professor. The tests for 1910 are very difficult.

Amazing teacher with a genuine concern for her students. She Encourages participation in class, is open to many different views, and facilitates engaging discussions in her classes. Count getting her as a professor as a christmas present.

She is an amazing teacher! Humorous and also absolutely nice! Her lectures are very organized and clear. Although sometimes the materials are difficult, if you go to lectures and study hard, you will be fine! Prelims are fair (although prelims are not written by her). She gives me a good start in engineering math in college!

I would say that Ritz is a great math professor. She is very helpful and open in office hours. However, the class is definitely a challenge... as are many of the first engineering math classes. Tests were written by the other professor, who was definitely a lot worse than Ritz. She also coined the term "Math Happens"!

Ritz is a pretty decent teacher. She's really helpful. She'll answer anything you have trouble with and she loves it when students come to her office hours. She's a really fair teacher. She tests her students on their knowledge, doesn't really seem to try to trick us. I really liked her! Take this class!

Ritz is a great math teacher! She is really clear and helpful when explaining topics and is really funny too! Great teacher, and from what I've heard, the best professor if you are taking 1910. The prelims are fair (I don't think she makes them though..) and the content is about what you would expect from an engineering calc class.
AMAZING!! Funny, clear, helpful!!! Great class, great professor!
A bit strict for a freshman class, but overall very straightforward and helpful.  A good lecturer, plus has very generous "quizzes instead of prelims" policy.

Overall, Ritz is a clear, her class difficulty is fair, and she is a pretty good lecturer.  Instead of giving prelims, she gives ~10 (relatively easy) pop quizzes over the semester (I liked this policy).  She does give a final.  The final project was a lot of fun. My TA (Anoop) was the best TA I have ever had.  Labs were fun.
great class

He might be good at researching, but he is absolutely not good at lecturing and breaking things down. If you take his class, be ready to learn on your own for more than 80% of the time. Even many CS lovers on YouTube outperform him in terms of teaching DB stuff.

This class is relatively interesting, but takes SO MUCH time. Only take it if you have a significant interest in getting started with DB design. You will need equally committed partners.
If you choose to take it take advantage of opportunities to fix and ask for regrades. Additionally, make sure to rigorously test.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class is eh. People are right that it is 'easy', the hard part is parsing the content out of the lecture material. Slides are very long, while what is important is not always evident. Exams have a strong emphasis on SQL which for a DB class I think is good, but I found them difficult. SQL is covered but not enforced to the degree which is tested.

He's lowkey just a chill guy, he is def passionate about the material and it shows when you ask him questions. This is the easiest CS class you can take at this school, like, its easier then 1110. The material is also pretty useful for industry, though I don't think ill ever use a where not where not exist sql negation irl.

Loved his lectures. He answers questions if you have any (even though only few people asked). Homeworks are very representative of the exams and also gives enough practice exams. Not hard to get a good grade in this class. Office hours are also good.
Great Prof, great content

Might as well not even be there. Course staff never answers Ed posts. There's no syllabus, and he would flip flop on the late policy to whatever he feels like. Normal DB is just boring, but the practicum is an unreal amount of work. Infuriating how absent he would be from what should be easy questions on Ed.

Despite his looks and how he speaks, Dr. Trummer is actually a very smart guy. Otherwise, our department wouldn't hire him as a new faculty member.

His lectures are very difficult to understand, and the TA I interacted with is not helpful at all. I dropped the course during the first month. I ain't wasting my time here.

Good luck.

This class was terrible. Legit could win an award for how badly he teaches. The content isn't necessarily hard, but his extreme lack of explanation and his terribly worded problem sets make it unnecessarily difficult. To top it off, the course staff he hires for this class have absolutely no idea what they are doing and mess up when they help.

This is a very demanding class. It felt more like a 4 credit class than a 2 credit one. The 5 projects were difficult and built off of each other, so if you implemented something wrong it has to be resolved before your next project (and you do not get access to solutions or the test cases that TAs run). You have to be a strong Java developer.

Because of COVID this class was graded only on 6 homeworks (no exams) and it ended up being very easy. Trummer is a clear & effective lecturer and made concepts easy to understand with examples and visualizations in his slides. Homeworks were straightforward and followed directly from the lectures. There was a textbook but I did not use it.
The content of the course is really useful. However, his lecture is hard to understand even with the video recordings from past semester.
His lecture was somewhat hard to follow!

Lectures were super dry, but they were posted online so you could work through them at your own pace. Made the requirements clear and assignments+exams were manageable. Grading was very slow. Material somewhat interesting.
Ambiguous Assignment with unrefined score judgement. Accent is 'tuple' or 'Lets get started!"
Learning from Trummer was the highlight of my college career.
Very good course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Extremely good professor. Enjoyed the lectures. Highly recommend the course.
Trummer was a below average professor. His lectures were tough to understand. MANY people dropped.

The course content is not for the weak, but Dr. Lorey explains it in a way that makes it easy to understand. I dreaded missing his class because one lecture could mean missing important details not explained deeply in the textbook. The exams reflected the prelim reviews, and his lectures really helped make sense of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class for the CALS requirement, as did most students likely. It was not a class to sleep on (lots of memorization required) but material is just above that of an advanced high school class. Prof. Lorey has thorough slides and breaks down concepts in class with on-the-fly notes. Attendance optional, but I'd go. Class is curved at the end
THE MOST BORING LECTURES EVER YOU WILL FALL ASLEEP,  The way he teaches is so boring and make you go to sleep. Every time I'm there I fall asleep, not only me but many students
Profesor Dan Lorey is a bit boring, but the class itself is easy.
His lectures are decently engaging and he thoroughly covers the material students are tested on.
Dry lectures but his videos are fun. Topics are broken down to be understandable.
Great lecturer. Posted slides, homework on achieve were very helpful and fair. Chemistry is hard, and that's not his fault.
Chemistry was hard, but an amazing lecturer, super nice, funny, and wrote fair exams.

Don't fall into the habit of skipping class - if you go and pay attention, you'll be much more prepared. Go to office hours!! He is really nice and wants to help you understand; if you ask for help, he will help until you actually get it. Read the lab report guidelines. He provides prelims from previous year. Class is curved at end. He's also funny

I love this man. Lectures are fast but slideshows are posted. This class built a community. Labs tend to be dull but thats only because they are taught by random TA's not King Dan. 1560 is challenging but VERY FAIR. I go to Dan's office hours twice a week and he is incredibly helpful with HW Labs and explanations. If you study a lot you can do well

Dr. Dan is the best! Super nice and fun lecturer. Although the class is really boring and difficult at points, Dr. Dan keeps it light with his humor and general caring personality. I would definitely recommend 1560 as an alternative to 2070 if its not a requirement.
Loved prof. Lorey. Never a dull moment in his class.

Dr. Lorey is a great professor. This is one of the most challenging courses I had to take but he makes sure that there are lots of opportunities to get help and he is accessible outside/after class. I have almost no chem background and was still able to understand his lectures, he does a great job at making them engaging.

Dr. Lorey is an amazing teacher as well as an amazing person. Although I did terribly in this class, it was in no way his fault. His office hours are inviting, and he provides lots of resources for people like me who struggle with this kind of class to at least have a halfway decent chance at passing.

Truly amazing dude, and that means a lot considering I despise chemistry. Get help after hours from Prof! Didnt get an A because didnt have time to devote to this one class. Labs are crucial; pre-lab quiz irrelevant for finals; practice exams almost exactly like real exam!! Dont take too many STEM classes in one semester and youll be g:)

Lab reports are super important! You don't have a ton of grades in this class so make sure your reports are good! Dr. Lorey is great and loves talking to his students but make sure you keep up with the work. The exams are pretty difficult so make sure you study a lot and apply problems from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I am so bad at chemistry but Dr. Lorey really helped me grasp the concepts that were challenging. The class requires work to be put in but if you complete the assignments and come to lecture, youll do just fine. 2090 in the summer is a great class to take for those struggling with gen chem in the fall or spring
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Experiments were pretty interesting and not too difficult. The lab practical at the end of the semester was challenging, but Dr. Lorey doesn't make it worth too much. Weekly lab reports were laborious, but easy to do well on as long as you were thorough. Overall, very fair class that was a very appropriate difficulty.

The class starts out pretty easy, but after the first prelim, picks up speed pretty quickly. Dr. Lorey is a great professor, if something isn't clear to you during class, hes good for in class questions and provides plenty of office hours for you to get help.
Clear, consistent, and actually cares for his students. Dr. Lorey will get you through Chem1560 as long as you are willing to put in the work.

He's super knowledgable and a good guy to talk to but his content in WLC tends to be all over the place without as much cohesiveness as other lecturers. In regards to the exam def the toughest to prepare for b/c you have to cite readings in a closed-book exam. Exam Qs were rough but grading seemed more lenient relative to other profs

Had him as the second professor for Work Labor Capital. He mixed lectures with documentaries which I enjoyed. Provided a list of all of the readings on the final which was useful as we were required to quote from them during the short answer section. Final was much harder than Boyer's so beware of the difficulty spike. A decent prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He mixed lectures with documentaries which was interesting but the test was hard. Short essay and short answers, a couple people weren't able to finish. DO THE READINGS and take notes.

Great professor. Readings were insightful and informative. He expertly covers a plethora of interesting topics, including workplace cultures and discrimination. Papers are really easy (just have to reflect on the readings), and tests were graded fairly. I enjoyed the lectures, but if you aren't interested in the topics they may be boring. Gives EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The entire class is based off of readings, most of which I found interesting, but long. The class has no clear theme and is very disjointed. Lectures are useless, but mandatory. The actual grading is entirely done by your TA and it matters which one. I like the content and idea of the class but it was poorly executed.

Class itself was not that difficult just incredibly boring and required you to do an obnoxious amount of reading which was NEVER talked about in class so you had to infer meanings on the tests. Tests are mostly short answers and discussions were useless. He seemed like he did not want to teach the class and word-for-word read off the slides.

God, he is the absolute worst. He literally just chats, like no content comes out of his mouth, he just says words. I personally think his class is the biggest waste of time, but attendance is mandatory!!!

For a 1.5 credit class, the amount of readings and work given seemed unnecessary. Professor Ivory used an index card system that made lecture attendance mandatory. They improved after the first prelim, but the lectures were generally pretty useless and did little to help me understand the incredibly dense and long readings for the week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: unnecessarily strict with his attendance/deadline policies and is unsympathetic to needing flexibility. he basically reads off of his slides, so going to lecture feels pointless, and rather than discussing the incredibly dense readings, he just puts "discussion questions" up on the board and reads them to the class. he doesn't even answer them.
Seems like a nice guy, but I couldn't hear a single thing. Talks into his neck. Tests were dumb. Like high school. Did not enjoy. Some readings were interesting though. Lectures were just not good.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is based on readings which are never discussed meaningfully in class, useless lectures, attendance is mandatory with mini flashcard assignments about readings, he doesn't seem like he wants to be there, must study hard, some TAs make class much easier than others, overall would not recommend class unless you have to take it as an ILRie
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very boring and useless lectures. He just reads off from the slides every day. And attendance is mandatory. Extremely heavy readings with few explanations in class lectures. Would not take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor DeVault is one of my favorite professors in ILR. She is extremely knowledgeable and cares a lot about your learning. The readings were worth it and she always has her door open to students if you ever want to discuss essays, ideas or topics covered in class. Attend lecture for good grades!

Devault was the most biased Prof I had at Cornell. Teaches 'historical facts' but implies clear political ideology. Grading scheme (letter grade averaged out at the end based on the lowest range of that letter) doesn't make sense. Lectures dull, didn't encourage diverse discussion. Decently easy class though.

No clear grading criteria. Essay grade ranges were insane and many students had conflicting thoughts. Slides have pictures not actual content. Of you don't go to lecture, you're done for. We also had a final which is unnecessary. Also, did I mention the class was electronic free?  If I had to do it again, I probably wouldn't take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Devault is very knowledgeable and has her Labor History lectures memorized. They can be dull, but class discussions were interesting at times. Weekly quizzes depend on your TA; sometimes notes are allowed. Essays are manageable, no rubric. The final is in person, focus on 2–3 books to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Devault is very knowledgeable and has her Labor History lectures memorized. They can be dull, but class discussions were interesting at times. Weekly quizzes depend on your TA; sometimes notes are allowed. Essays are manageable, no rubric. The final is in person, focus on 2–3 books to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Said in class that slavery “wasn't that bad” and enslaved black people had it easier than white apprentices because at least they were provided food and shelter. Completely racist and unacceptable coming from a Cornell professor. Was not really apologetic at all after. Seems like ILR has removed the class due to this incident.

Not super difficult at all but said in online class that black people were better off during. Slavery than white apprentices because at least they were provided food and shelter. Seemed combative when receiving pushback on this statement. That was a completely unacceptable and racist statement and I wouldn't feel comfortable in class as a POC.

Not the worst professor but definitely misinformed. In her unfree labor class, she suggested that Black people were better off as slaves than free since they were “taken” care of which is shocking, racist and deeply disrespectful coming from a Cornell professor. 
The ILR department has since cancelled this class apparently.

There are better profs for this class. Prof DeVault's grading depends heavily (85% of grade) on 2 essay with virtually no directions and no rubric and an in-class final writing exam (only teacher that does this). She gives weekly quizzes on readings and attendance is taken based on participation. If you don't participate, you're not marked present.
plz avoid this class its so unclear
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DeVault is one of my favorite professors at ILR. Super knowledgeable, engaging and interesting lectures, very helpful during office hours, fair grader. If you do the readings you'll do well in the class and leave knowing so much about labor history. She also answers to emails quite well and writes good comments on essays so you can improve

She assigns 100-250 pages of reading per week with weekly quizzes in discussion. Slides are pictures with a title and she just speaks about it. Attendance not mandatory but she tracks engagement and office hour attendance, and slides not helpful. Harsh grader on essays and final. OH not rlly helpful she laughs at questions (me and others)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Devault is very passionate about labor history and it shows. She assigns a TON of reading, but you should just skim.

DeVault  gives us pop quizzes every week on the reading which is usually over 200 pages. I had pneumonia for two weeks and she wouldn't give me her notes from lecture. If you miss class you cannot make it up because she slides she post just include images and no information. Final exam where we wrote two essays in a hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Devault assigns a ton of reading and you don't need to do all of it (though she does have weekly quizzes that typically test one aspect of the reading, so at least skimming is a good idea to not lose points there). Somewhat tough essay grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Highly recommend taking this seminar if you have an interest in history and need to knock out the ILR advanced writing requirement. Genuinely a caring professor, and super great to chat with during OH. Reads your journal entries in full, and writes thoughtful comments in the entries.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A very caring and passionate professor. A lot of readings but the work is manageable. Clear grading based on a mix of attendance and participation, journal entries, and essays. She is very understanding so would recommend going to office hours and communicating if you have any questions with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Shes super kind and caring, you can tell shes very passionate about her work. Homework is mostly reading assignments up to 150+ pages a week and general quizzes during discussion. 2 papers and a take-home final that makes the majority of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DeVault clearly cares about the subject and the class. Go to office hours for help on the essays and you will do well.

Professor DeVault is clearly passionate about her subject matter. However, her class had excess work as well as a final exam that other labor history classes did not have. She graded harshly and the clear expectations were not laid out prior to paper assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Grade based on: Critical book report, Primary source project, Research paper proposal, Final exam, and participation. Some assignment due dates vary by topic, allowing you to pick what weeks you want to work for the class. Thursday classes are all discussion so make sure to read what is assigned for the week (200-ish pages).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weekly "quiz" on readings in discussion. Read lots of short books over the semester
Professor Devault is very kind! Although there is a large amount of reading every week, it helps acclimate you with the college course load
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lot of reading as it is a history class. Paper heavy. But she is a great professor and she is a very nice person very understanding great professor to get you into college
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Devault is a great professor. Labor History can be a dry topic but she is very good at trying to make it as easy as possible. 3 papers one of which is the final paper, and weekly quizzes in discussion which are not that bad. Take her if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Interesting professor who presents interesting material, but lectures had the tendency to be very dry. I appreciated that she made an effort to learn students' names and was accessible for questions. There were about 2 extra credit opportunities. A lot of reading, but skimming is ok. Weekly reading quizzes during discussion section, not so bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: DeVault is one of the nicest people I have ever met. She genuinely cares about her students. I had a class during her office hours, so she regularly scheduled other times to meet. I struggled a lot with the first essay assignment, but DeVault helped me and taught me what I did wrong. Her lectures can be dry, but the information is interesting.

Awesome professor, super passionate and nice.  Lots of weekly reading with reading quizzes in discussion, but you can definitely "skim" main concepts and do extremely well. Two papers, go to TA office hours and you will do well on them. Extremely fair final. Some find the subject boring overall but DeVault makes it as painless as possible.
Excellent professor! Clear and learned a lot, definitely not an easy grader but she is very helpful and sweet and a fair grader. Love her!
Nice and helpful.

Not a bad course..very dry though. make sure you suck up in section to your TA and dont worry about the weekly quizzes too much. most imporant thing about this class would be to meet with both the TA and DeVault before both of the papers to talk about your thesis and make sure youre on the right track... they will tell you what to write basically

Unfree Labor: Slaves, Servants, Wives.  Great Teacher, learned alot, ALOT of reading, one book per week, sometimes half a book, seminar style, classes tend to be very large.  Attendance is not required but necessary for class participation points.  She really knows her stuff and goes a long way to ensure your understanding.

Comparative History of Women at Work.  Best seminar class I've ever been in, attendance is not mandatory, but necessary to get class participation points.  Reading is tough, one book per week+short paper, but well worth the effort, learned alot, seminar style allowed for greater understanding of others opinions on women's issues

Intro to Labor History, lots of reading, but if you keep  up your set, class participation counts for alot, you'll definitely learn something.  I liked her so much, I've taken 2 more of her classes. (IC636 and CB388)

DeVault is very passionate about labor history and is a good lecturer; she gave us weekly ‘reading quizzes’ which were annoying but I guess it made us read the many books we were assigned...  A pretty interesting class if you’re into the subject. 2 papers, final exam was 2 essay questions; DeVault is a tough grader but a good teacher overall.

Wonderful teacher.  She is very interested in the subject and conveys it.  She is also very helpful, friendly, and pleasant to talk to if you see her in office hours.  Probably my favorite teacher this semester.

Excellent professor. I have heard that other CB100 profs are more dynamic lecturers, but I never had a problem staying engaged or awake in her class. She's definitely a professional, and I respect her tremendously. She has very high standards for your work, but that definitely motivates you to do well.
Boring and dry, but very clear and organized.  Go to lecture and get the gist of the readings, and you'll be fine.  Was also very understanding and accommodating when I had a conflict.

I have taken three classes with her,and I would take more if they were offered! Show up to class and you're set. Being interested in history helps a lot, but overall she is extremely nice and cares about how you do.

Good lectures, make the material as interesting as it can be. Ton of reading, nobody expects you to do it all though. For papers, make sure you hav a good thesis and you will do fine. She is very interested in women's issues, clearly. Overall, great prof.

An excellent professor and lecturer.  She made a very dry topic into something interesting. She assigns a lot of reading, however she doesn't intend for you to do it all, but rather gather general concepts.  Overall it was a pretty easy course if you went to lectures.
Incredibly boring.  Her many random examples are irrelevant and a waste of time.  She also refuses to change a grade no matter how unfair it may be.

One of the best professors you will have.  Lectures were clear, easy to follow and interesting.  Take good notes in lecture and you're guarenteed good grades.  Papers are a decent amount of work but very fairly graded.  The best prof. for the class by far.

Great professor- very clear and helpful. There is a lot of reading which is useful when it comes to doing papers. Papers can be tough...it helps to run your ideas by her first. Very nice and approachable and her lectures are very clear. No complaints here!
very clear and informative lectures, requires work (esp for the reading) but you'll learn a lot about US labor history

My favorite prof so far. I wasn't expecting labor history to be fun, but it's the only class I'm never inclined to skip. She's a really nice lady, very knowledgable, makes the class interesting w/o compromising depth or clarity of material. Papers aren't bad; reading can be a bit much, but doable.
Ileen is a goddess
Excellent professor; Papers require work, but if you try you can do well; Very clear lectures

This is a very interesting course on immigration. Devault does a great job at putting the history of immigration into context with work related stuff.  She is a very nice person who is very honest and fair.
very nice and helpful if you ask.  papers aren't that bad.  very good lectures and decent amount of reading for a cb class.
Tons of respect for this professor. DeVault is organized, clear, and strives to be as accessible to her students as time allows. No complaints!
very knowledgeable, great lectures. Papers requre some work though.
No Comments
am a senior and this is one of the best classes i have taken because it intersects microbiology, marine biology, and eeb. very very interesting course

Prof. Hewson is amazing! I was nervous going into this class because I have no background in oceanography, but it's been super interesting and not stressful. Learn a lot of content but no tests/quizzes. He often ties his own research/field work into class content and you can tell he just wants to get students excited to learn!

This class was really interesting. The prof went above and beyond to make the class accessible and flexible in the online learning environment. While the lectures were dense, learning goals were clearly identified and the assessments were firmly focused around these. Also assessment was flexible and tailored to each student's preferred method.

Prof. Hewson is clearly very knowledgeable&passionate about his field, but the lectures are very dense and got to be a bit monotonous at the end of the semester Luckily there was no exams on the detailed lecture content, rather theres weekly literature/writing HW, group proj, and final proj. This was nice but made it too easy to tune out lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hewson is a fantastic individual who really knows his stuff! Such a pleasure to have him as a teacher.
This was a great introduction to marine biology. Some of the labs were a little disorganized but at least there were labs!

Dr. Ian's Hewson class is more suited for people with no familiarity with biology than anyone who has even taken intro biology.  It is overall disorganized and presented in a distinctly anthropocentric and unscientific manner

As a tenured professor, it is clear that she no longer enjoys teaching. No devices in class, frequent reprimanding of the entire class for individual's mistakes. Her lectures are extremely boring and slow-paced. Do not take this class if you do not have to. It may be easy, but it comes at the cost of extreme disrespect to your time.

Professor Rickard tends to go on lecture tangents that are unrelated to class and not particularly interesting. All presented ideas seem partially unfinished or unclear. The prompts for papers and vague and the grading criteria similarly vague.

The professor was very knowledgeable and the lectures were generally interesting. However, the course structure could sometimes be disorganized and instructions for assignments were unclear. What you get out of the course is what you put in.
The content was interesting and discussions definitely helped make the ideas cohesive.  Pretty straightforward to get a good grade.

As someone who was not really interested in visual studies, this course helped me to gain a true appreciation for things that I otherwise take for granted. I'm not sure if any of my other classes have influenced me in this way yet. Overall, I learned a lot!!

The class was disorganized and the professor would ramble about unrelated topics during lectures. The readings and content were fascinating, but never related to what we discussed in the lecture. Very easy A, though.

This is one of the best classes that I've taken thus far! My eyes were opened in lecture. Usually profs just make us learn on our own, but prof. Rickard actually teaches the content. I would enroll in another class taught by her in a heartbeat!
The class felt unorganized. She rambled on during lecture about nothing specific, and gave vague assignments. Disappointing class.
Life-changing course! If you put the work into the course, you will reap the benefits.

This class really opened my eyes to an amazing area of art. Professor Rickard is very knowledgable about so many issues outside of art that entered cultural studies because of her. You would be lucky to take a class with her!

I found the class to be very informative even though it was a lot of work. Professor Rickard is very knowledgable on the theory behind Native issues, but students without any background knowledge (attended American schools) may have found the class difficult to grasp. And in reality she was a fair grader, hard word was rewarded.

Jolene took time out of her insanely busy schedule as interim director of the Arts dept to work with me on an independent study project on settler colonialism, imaging & resistance. I found her to be, in contrast with most of these comments, a dynamic & challenging teacher who genuinely cares for students-their development but also well-being.

I learned absolutely nothing in this class and feel asleep everyday for at least 30 mins. Prof. Rickard is REALLY boring and talks in the most uncomprehensible roundabout way. Also, she is a harsh grader for no reason. The assignments were stupid, not hard.

This class was horrible!! She didn't follow the syllabus at all and assigned random papers with no prompts. It took her several weeks to return anything graded, and her grading system was very ambiguous. Impossible for her to stay on topic and lectures felt like they lasted foreverrr. DO NOT take this class if you can avoid it!!
So sassy and unforgiving. If this isnt requirement, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. Lab reports were the worst part of my days, weeks, months, and overall life. You have been warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: makes the chem lab rubrics and makes sure TAs don't give student points or any leeway. lab grade is dragging down my grade.

Currently taking 3570. She doesn't go by the textbook order unlike every other professor and just jumps around, so the support class is unhelpful. She denies every regrade request and doesn't post any notes. How is it possible that the prelim 1 avg is a 67% when the past semesters the averages have been around 90.
actually insane. There's no way

Hardest part about 2070. No rubrics provided, so students are left guessing about what info they need to include in lab reports. Harsh grading and regrade requests are often denied without proper reasoning. Grading is inconsistent between TAs, so just hope you get lucky. Instructions are not explicit and even one bad lab is hard to recover from.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There is no rubric for lab reports and they are graded strictly. The regrade system has many holes that bar students from receiving the points they actually made on assignments. The lab section is the hardest part of the class, and the one you're least able to progress in due to the set up of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Impossible to do well

She makes the lab reports difficult because we are not allowed to see a rubric, and her grading is very inconsistent. She grades super strictly and somehow expects you to read her mind. Also, if too many students submit regrade requests, she will go into lecture and yells at everyone. She genuinely prays on every student's downfall.
Don't take a class with her

She is the lab director for General Chemistry. The TAs for CHEM 2071 are expected to deduct a set number of points (with quotas), and students have been discouraged from requesting regrades. Rubrics are not provided before lab reports are due and are instead created afterward, with TAs instructed to grade very harshly. Nice person, however.

She makes it unnecessarily difficult to do well on labs by changing the grading rubric each time and taking off points for the smallest things. She expects students to read her mind and know exactly what to include in lab reports (e.g. which outside sources to cite in the introduction). This course was honestly more difficult than CHEM 2070 lecture

Does not provide rubric for labs to students or TAs, so there is no way to improve performance. Grades on things never mentioned before, then tells students not to submit regrades. Leaves comments on reports that is not constructive, but critical and unsupportive.

Does not respond to emails and will not release rubrics so students are left guessing what they did right and what they should keep on doing for following labs. Lab TA's are don't have them either and are left confused with grading as they also don't know rubrics till after we submit. Graded on things that were never asked of us in instructions.
lab instructor who did anything to ensure you didn't succeed.

great guy. ok professor. very disorganized, went overtime on a couple of labs. and not labs that are on campus. labs in the middle of the woods... overtime. lectures disorganized. and flipped class where you watch hours of video lectures every week and he js talks scattered-mindedly in class. he is rly great person and knowledgeable tho

He's a really sweet guy, but is super disorganized with the way he runs things. His directions are never very clear, but he is a pretty fair/easy grader. He is also super passionate about this class and is overall, a great guy.
Amazing lectures, caring and respected instructor

Flipped class- lectures were online (1-3 hr per week) but they didn't always make sense. Class was meant to be used for homework, but half the time it was more lecturing. Bad class to take if you don't have friends taking it. Everything turned in on paper and he lost our first prelims. Goes over time on labs. However, really cares about students.

He is an incredibly unorganized professor that teaches a flipped class. On the first day of the year he said, "the biggest complaint about this class is that its a flipped class, but I'm gonna try it again." It did not work this year either, and overall he is a very unorganized and dysfunctional professor as well as grader.

The man is awesome and passionate about what he teaches. However, not posting ANY grades on Canvas even after final grades are released put me off a bit altho we received our grades back from every assignment and tests. Also, beware that all assignments/reports are expected to be turned in in-person on PAPER. Instructions were often unclear.

Was taught as a "flipped class," meaning the lectures would be watched at home and activities in class. Instead, we ended up watching 3 recorded lectures a week (from 2012, public on YouTube) AND each class was a lecture, aka 6+ lectures a week. The labs were pretty cool but the lab reports were difficult and the exams were overly complicated.

He has passion but seems like he doesn't want to teach. He attempts to radiate positivity ("Go be awesome!") yet comes across as irritated. Class was flipped with about 3-6 hours/week of videos. Monday is a lecture on lab, and the other two days are either a sloppy representation of the videos or busywork. Lots of extra effort with little return.

Such a great professor- makes sure you understand (doesn't mind re-explaining concepts) and has a sense of humor. He's the perfect guy to teach an intro soil class since he's so enthusiastic. The lab reports were sometimes a pain to write but they were graded easily (might depend on the TA, though). I highly recommend taking a class with him!

Jonathan LOVES soil. I mean he LOVES it. Super passionate about what he does and really wants students to understand the material. Tests are simple if you attend the lectures and do the reading. Labs every week are straight forward. A B is pretty easy to get in the class, but an A would require some serious effort and/or a hard science background.

He is very helpful and nice.  The subject (soil science) is a very complex one and he did a good job of teaching this intro class.  My only complaint would probably be a slight lack of explanation on what he wanted lab reports to contain.  However, I'm sure he'd elaborate if one were to just ask him.  Great teacher!
very unclear with what was expected for lab reports
Very good professor, tries hard to make sure students understand and is willing to work with them to make things clear.  This class was challenging but fascinating!
This class is just us teaching our peers the whole semester
lot of group projects with vague instructions that she then harshly critiques when giving feedback. 50% of this class is just listening to classmates present their work
Interesting content; manageable assignments

Look, boys, this was a great class. The professor is really really smart, but you WILL BE CHALLENGED. the quizzes aren't too bad if you do the homework on your own. My favorite part was how INTERACTIVE the professor was, specifically the October 31st class where we learned and saw SPOOKY experiments! This was an amazing course, glad I took it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Course is very disorganized, discussion quizzes were very inconsistent (some graded for correctness while others completion based on TA), no practice prelim answers given, no responses on ed, somewhat condescending in lecture, able to get a good grade but not very enjoyable
UNC IS SO CHOPPED!!!!!!!!!!!!

Though this class was not perfect, with several areas for improvement, Prof. Cohen is a perfectly fine professor. Heavy workload and dry lecture slides are there, but there is A LOT of content. It doesn't seem like he enjoys teaching 2214, but despite an occasional condescending edge in lecture (accidental?), if you pay attention you will be fine.

Prof. Cohen and his course staff have made PHYS 2214 by far the worst class I have taken at Cornell. I recommend strongly to avoid his offering of the course. Multiple times this semester, the professors on the course staff failed to show up for their scheduled office hours without notice to the students. They also do not respond on Ed.

At very few times he actually seemed to care for people in the class, but instead of answering anyone's questions on Ed he would only be available in the case that someone was answering polling outside of lecture. Class was very disorganized, and he didn't even hold his own office hours, which made it really hard to grasp the material intuitively.

This might be the worst class I have taken at Cornell. The class is disorganised, nobody responds on the ed, he takes a month to respond to emails, and nobody (students or TAs) has the answer key to practice prelims. It genuinely feels like he doesn't want his students to succeed in this class. Lectures are confusing and hard to follow along with.

I have no idea why this man teaches because he has no interest in talking to students or coming up with course content. All of his materials are from 2018. He doesn't give solutions on any practice tests so it's like you try and you hope you are right but there's no way to find out. I don't think I have ever seen him respond on Ed.

Horrible organization of this class. First class in all of my engineering career that does not provide answer key to the practice prelims so you don't even know if what you are doing is wrong. Not enough TAs to help you. No one answers to my ED discussion posts other than other students who are trying to also understand what's going on.

It was the most disorganized class ever. The course with over 100 students only has one TA, with office hours once a week. Post no review for prelim, and never respond on ed discussion. Poorly organized class and professor can't teach.

Terrible lecturer. Writes chicken scratch on the board during his lectures and in general they are extremely confusing and really hard to follow because it's not pre planned slides its just random things he jots down projected onto the screen. Then the homework is nothing like what he mentions in class.
If you dont have to take a class with him don't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: WHAT DO YOU MEAN YOU DIDN'T READ YOUR OWN SYLLABUS AND CHANGE IT HALFWAY THROUGH???
Most disorganized class I have ever taken.
Rough
Godawful professor. Even my friends who are cracked at physics cannot stand his teaching. He could not teach a fish to swim.
Don't bother taking this class if you want to learn anything. The prelims are far too difficult for how terribly the professor teaches us the content.
The class is so catastrophically taught that I wanted to drop out of physics altogether. Honestly so sad that we get terrible professors even though we pay so much in tuition
The content itself is honestly manageable. The problem is that the professor can't teach, which makes learning it so difficult

For the love of your GPA don't take class with this professor. The complete lack of teaching knowledge this prof has is embarrassing. You would learn just as much from a robo voice speaking the lecture slides out loud,
Trying take any class with this professor feels like a chore. Hes a nice person but can't teach
The class feels like just the prof regurgitating lecture slides. Completely useless in helping you prep for prelims
Incredibly unclear in lecture and explaining content in general, might as well learn the content on your own.
A nice person but an absolutely terrible professor. Often useless on ED and the lectures are incredibly dry. Don't take any class with this professor.
This professor cannot explain anything, the whole class just feels like plug and chug.
worst prof i have had at cornell

Prof Cohen is a nice person but he is a terrible professor. I don't have a bad grade (currently A/B+) but his course is designed EXTREMELY poorly and unfairly. The lectures do not help with the homework at all. The midterm is impossible because the questions are just too complex for beginner physics students. Worst Cornell course I have taken.

It is not recommended to do research under this professor. Very unclear in communicating objectives and willing to take credit for other people's ideas to get onto papers where his lab did very little work. Overall a poor/borderline unethical manager of his undergraduate and graduate researchers.
will not take class with this professor again.
Terrible experience

The professor is very tricky. For the class he required using iclicker. Many people did not show up and then in one of the last lectures he told people not to click on one of the questions and used this way to catch people who clicked the iclicker remotely. This is a lie and a terrible way to catch student.

Itai is an amazing professor. He's incredibly passionate about physics and students remain engaged during his lectures because of his energetic composition. I am not a physics major but he made physics probably the most interesting and amazing class I'd taken my 2nd to last semester at Cornell. I definitely recommend taking a class with him.
Serious professor
Very knowledgable and insightful. Lots of background info that was helpful.
Avoid.

His explanation is definitely clear. However, I sometimes doubts that he understands the material exactly. He just writes things in his notes, and he doesn't answer the questions students ask properly. If you take this class, you have to take some to study your book.
No Comments

His lectures were often unclear and difficult to follow, leaving many students disengaged. Attendance expectations felt random and inconsistent, adding to the lack of structure. I frequently relied on outside resources to learn material that should have been covered in the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor West is a only a decent lecturer, but he is VERY good at explaining things when you ASK QUESTIONS. To succeed, sit at the front, ask questions, and attend office hours! Professor West is available very often, so take advantage! He loves to get to know students during his office hours, and is more than willing to accommodate your schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jim West is very kind and intelligent, but I fear that since he was been an expert in "Geometric topology and infinite-dimensional topology" for so long, he no longer really is able to teach undergraduate classes. That means he usually is unable to explain the material in a way that someone new to the material can really understand it.

Every kid in his class deserves a refund on their semester's tuition. His lectures were so useless that maybe a fifth of the class attended. On the upside he knew his lectures were bad, so the tests were easy. Also the homework solutions are online. Using the MIT lectures on YouTube gives an easy A.
Lectures boring and not very well attended. Good textbook though and he let us know which sections each lecture/homework covered. No website and unclear grading guidelines. Not great not horrible.

People hate on Tarantino too much. Yeah, the flipped classroom style of the class sucks, and the homework is lots of work and the grading is nitpicky, but if you ask the TAs or Tarantino for help in class, they'll pretty much give you the answers. Beware of the prelims, my grade never recovered after the first prelim, final is cake compared to them

This was my least favourite class of the semester. Most of the content is taught by videos, and we weren't even taught everything for the final MOS Excel exam. Attendance is mandatory despite the lecture having negligible content and consisting solely of completing an assignment. I would not recommend this class in any circumstance.

Tarantino barely teaches with the excuse of using a "flipped style" and relies on videos she made so many years ago. She doesn't prepare you well for prelims and instructions are very unclear. She's also extremely strict about attendance, and after you miss 3 classes every absence after that your grade drops half a letter.

Kasey is hands-down, the most unsympathetic professor I have ever had. She enforces mandatory attendance, even if you have interviews or have to go to a funeral. Also doesn't teach in-class; instead, she has videos from 5 years ago and have students watch before class. If you have to go to the bathroom, she would give you an absence.
Make sure u study really well for prelims. She is the most unforgiving teacher

Ppl are rlly overdramatic about this class. The flipped style isn't fun & watching the vids def takes time, but if you actually take notes you will understand and it won't be hard. MOS final is super easy in comparison to the prelims. Def a lot of assignments and the project mid-way thru was stressful, but not at all as bad as people make it out.

work in this class was doable -- directions were super unclear and even when asking her/TAs, would be no help. OH did not help at all. You really have to rely on yourself for this class. Flipped style is super annoying.

Mrs Tarantino is super kind, smart, and overall a lovely person! The class, however, is disastrous. Since it's "flipped" every class is anxiety-inducing. Each class you, work on the assignment of the day. Prelims are hard, but the MOS exam at the end of the semester is easy.

For this class, she had a teaching style where she gave videos to learn the material, and then she did a short lecture in class on new (sometimes more challenging) material and then gave the rest of the time to work on the homework assignment. I enjoyed the class because it was professionally applicable and easy to handle. Grading very harshly tho.

The class isn't the most engaging, but you learn a lot of valuable skills. Most people are happy they took it. The flipped classroom isn't ideal, but you have to learn how to live with it. Exams aren't difficult if you practice. MAKE SURE YOU GO TO OFFICE HOURS FOR EXCEL! Doing well on the homework assignments is a great way to cushion your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The videos assigned are extremely boring and redundant which makes the mandatory aspect of the class very irritating. However, she cares about her students and their well being. Watch the videos and ask questions and you should be fine.

Content is valuable, but the structure could be a lot more student-friendly. Grading is petty and inconsistent, with hidden criteria. "Nothing a TA or professor tells you is guaranteed correct". Relies heavily on pre-recorded videos, actual class time is redundant. Weird 9 P.M. deadlines. Prof's lack of enthusiasm affects learning atmosphere.

I would reccomend taking this class with Professor Whitmore. Tarantino makes her prelims very tough and provides no review or resources for her prelims. The average was below a 70% and she blamed the class on not studying hard enough. All the assignments are graded by the TAs and the rubric is always so vague and unclear. Good luck if you have her.

Not a fan of the inverse course structure HADM1740 (we learn 95% through pre-recorded videos, and in-class is just basically study hall and asking questions to TAs). Professor Tarantino barely teaches anything in person, yet attendance is mandatory. Class average for the excel midterm was lower than 60%, and instructions on prelim are unclear

Terrible prof. Doesn't teach, just has you watch her videos which are hard to listen to because she ends every sentence like it was a question. She isn't very knowledgeable in her field either. She has a hard time answering questions she doesn't expect. I could have learned more by watching somebody else's YouTube videos. Take someone else.

I took CS 6820 with Professor Kleinberg (graduate version of CS 4820), and it has been my favorite course at Cornell thus far. Bobby is an amazing lecturer and answers questions very clearly and concisely. I would take every class at Cornell with him if I could. He is very fun, and even outside of the classroom, is always full of great advice.
Super engaging lectures, explains complex topics well. Makes proofs a conversation and motivates each step

Really good class but super challenging, def got a lot out of the class. In class quizzes were fairly easy as long as you paid attention in class, and the final was fair. Would recommend starting HWs later as he often makes edits because he realized problems are way too hard.

Professor is amazing, and the workload is light with only 6 homework and 4 small quizzes. Homeworks sometimes require a bit of thinking. Overall, although not too hard, this is a decent course to take if you want to satisfy the probability requirement but don't want to waste credits on trivialities like MATH 4710.

Kleinberg's are amazing and funny. He is extremely good at explaining complex subjects, and will let you see ideas in a new light. The price you pay is that the course is quite difficult and time-consuming. It is definitely worth it though.

Really nice, kind of funny, uber nerdy guy. I find him charming and easy to talk to. Also have him as my faculty advisor. But, hardest class I've ever taken. Could put hours and hours into HW and OH and still get <20% on it, HW/exam medians were about 50%. Maybe worse because it was online. Also I just suck at algo, which is not his fault.

Prof. Kleinberg is one of those professors that, the more complicated the concept, the better he is at explaining it. His lectures on max flow, NP-Completeness, and Turing Machines were very helpful, while I mostly learned about greedy algorithms and DP from the book. His homeworks are definitely very challenging, with HW / Exam medians 50-60%

Prof. Kleinberg is an excellent instructor who is very good at explaining deep concepts, from NP Reductions to Turing Machines to Network Flow problems. His homeworks are quite difficult (some have had medians close to 50%), but I have learned so much in his class.

He basically gives the answers to students he likes and students who have no shame when asking directly for the answers to problem sets. He is also not useful in lecture. The textbook was the only way someone could learn in that class. He just tried to show off and act cool during lecture.
great lecturer. fascinating course material. challenging weekly homework. super useful class.

Bobby is, no lie, a genius and is well-respected. Lectures can be slow, but are very intuitive. #3 on problem sets can be very difficult sometimes. Exams are pretty easy. Advice: start psets the day they get released and rEAD the TEXTBOOK!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is extremely intelligent and very committed in helping his students learn the material. He can be a little brash when dealing with administrative issues in the course, but seems genuinely interested in his teaching duties. Would highly recommend taking 4820 under him if you want to seriously test your understanding of algorithms.

Professor R. Kleinberg was excellent for Algorithms, Spring 2014. He is very open to student questions and attempts to make a sometimes-challenging subject clear. Not an easy professor by any means, but assessments fair. Relies on the textbook a good amount, but also references outside research.
His lecturing style as well as his mastery of the subject matter are both top-notch. He also seems like a great person. It's an absolute privilege to have him as a lecturer.

Had him for both 4820 and 6820. Great lecturer (he writes a lot, so it is hard sometimes to keep up with both listening and writing down nots).
