Amazing personality (will go overtime to answer your question). In OH, he will insightfully lead you to think rather than just giving answer away. HW can be super challenging.

R. Kleinberg is an amazing teacher and super smart. His lectures are organized, exciting and the material is super fun and challenging. The HWs are super super challenging. Every HW has a question which is so  hard that sometimes the TAs arent sure on how to solve them. But it is fun to solve the HWS. I really improved my problem solving skills.

Great teacher--you get out what you put in, and I definitely put in mid levels of effort for an okay grade. Awesome lecturer and a total math nerd. I felt like some parts of the class were taught in a very unintuitive way that just didn't mesh with my learning style, but the assigned textbook generally explains things well.

Kelly Delp is clearly very passionate about math, but one of the issues I had is that she would focus lots of time on the conceptual aspect of problems whereas Math 1920 is more of an application class rather than a proof class. Her notes are very helpful and posts skeleton and final notes after lectures. She's great but do more practice problems.

Focused a lot more on the general idea of the math and why it was cool rather than how to actually do it. We were told why something was important before how it worked. Because of this, I ended up learning mostly from posted notes and the textbook. You could tell she was passionate about the math though, and that was not always contagious.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class itself was hard, but Delp at least made it bearable. She was always very energetic and gave really good lectures. She was always very friendly and seemed to know the names of many students in the class and would greet people as they entered the class making it a really nice class environment.

Delp is great! The policies for her course are very clear and straightforward, and she provides skeleton notes before every class so people know what we are covering. The lectures aren't my favorite environment, and I often relied on the textbook to supplement them, but that's ultimately a skill issue: Delp teaches incredibly well.

Professor Delp was the best math professor/teacher I've ever had. She provides skeleton notes to all her lectures which make it easy to follow and understand. Prelims are generally easy and she gives 3 long quizzes in discussion throughout the course. Homework is the best way to learn in this class and also asking questions is a must if lost
The tests were graded so brutally, and barely any partial credit was given. Delp is fine, but her lectures aren't super helpful. You probably have to rely on the textbook mostly.

Amazing lectures, her notes are super organized and she explains things very well. Her lectures pair well with the textbook, honestly best professor I've had so far. She's super sweet and genuinely cares about all her students. I personally think 1920 was way easier than 1910. Would recommend Delp to anyone who can take her class.
absolute queen. her notes were very organized, making it very easy to follow. great explainer. very passionate.
Did not miss any single lecture. Professor really kind and helpful!

Delp is kind, but represents the issue of assigning senior lecturers to intro/low-level classes; they're overqualified thus don't take the low-level courses as seriously, leading to lapses in lecture quality and pertinence to exams. Read the textbook in Finite Math because you'll learn more than in lectures. She's incredibly nice, however.
Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures were extremely well planned and organized, and the homework questions were chosen well . If you can get Delp, get Delp.

Amazing lecturer, really cares about students, and is very accessible. Entertains all questions without making anyone feel silly. Final kicked my butt but course was otherwise pretty fair if you read the textbook outside of class
go to lecture and do readings ahead of time if you dont want to grind before exams. do every homework problem at least once
Multi was very cool to understand. Delp does an excellent job in really providing a conceptual and intuitive mastery of the material. Challenging but very fruitful. Would take again.

The textbook is the saving grace of a Delp course; relying on lectures would leave you desperate, stranded and alone. You will have no choice but to take 1920 with her, but only having the previous reviews to set expectations is a sin- you will be sorely disappointed. Honestly, I am not positive that I had the same professor as other reviewers.

Loved Professor Delp she has skeleton notes for all of her lectures making them so easy to follow and fill in, and she will answer any question you have in office hours. Clearly loves math and wants us to love it too
Amazing professor who is really passionate about what she's teaching. Made a huge difference in the class despite its difficulty.

I didn't show up to 1920 lecture much, but whenever I did she was an amazing lecturer. Expectations for quizzes and tests are clear and if you do the homework and study it well you will do well. Deadlines are a little flexible. If you have the chance to get her, take her and you won't regret it.

Professor Delp is a cool dude. You'll probably get discouraged while doing the homework since some of the problems are straight-up impossible, but the questions on the quizzes and prelims always seem to be fair. She goes pretty fast in her lectures, so stay focused and don't get distracted by things such as the majesticity of her hair

Professor Delp really cares about her students, and is such an inspiring, fair, and passionate person. I thoroughly enjoyed taking multivariable calculus with her, and learned a lot from the course. I came in with no experience in the subject, and now feel confident with all the material. Quizzes and Exams(except maybe the final) are all very fair.

Heard multi can be very bad. However, I was very lucky to have Delp as my professor. I actually ended up liking multivariable. Homework is helpful and prelims/exams very fair. Discussions are helpful.

The only good thing about this class is that hw is worth 30% of grade. She adjusts grade cutoffs very fairly, but that doesn't take away from the material being hard and boring. She is a nice person in general, but her lectures are terrible. She is scatterbrained and gets distracted easily, making it difficult to follow the math problems.

The material itself is hard but going to lectures with Professor Delp and participating makes all the difference. Professor Delp is so excited about math and cares so much about her students, her lectures are great. Wish I could take another class with her.
I don't go to lectures that often since it's 9 am, but when I do go, I never regretted it. She's great at explaining difficult concepts with simpler ones. Also, the lecture note is amazing.

Professor Delp is fantastic! She is really passionate about what she teaches and brings good energy to her lectures. Her exams are really fair and are based on understanding of how everything works rather than just giving really hard questions that are meant to stump students. She is kind and understanding, as well.

Great professor! Truly cares about students, makes an effort to engage the class and keep them awake during the early morning lectures. Very passionate about the subject which comes across in her teaching. Pretty fair weight of homework/assignments, great grading scheme, very accessible especially over EdStem for doubts all semester long.
I have never met a professor as passionate about their course material as Professor Delp. Her lectures are fantastic and engaging. Truly an excellent teacher.

I dropped the class last sem because of another professor, Connelly. I was on track to get a C+ or at most a B- in the course, as Connelly's lectures didn't work for me. Delp's course organization is phenomenal. Love the "skeleton notes" Now on track to get an A/A+, and I have a solid grasp of multi now. Great lectures, textbook is a supplement.
Prof Delp is by far the most engaging and thorough math professor I've had. Multivariable calculus is a difficult, boring subject that she makes enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I actually really enjoyed math 1920 because of professor Delp. She gives very clear and engaging lectures which make the course material much simpler and more comprehensible. The homework is reasonably difficult and prepares you well for the exams.

Professor Kelly Delp is a real gem. She has a passion for teaching. Her homework questions really make you question your major. I am lucky to be in her Math 1920 class. I respect Professor Kelly Delp a lot. Sometimes she can speak in Calculus 9 during her lectures so you should know the material well

Dr. Delp is a great teacher and her passion for math really shows in lecture. She's good at explaining difficult topics and very open to questions. Makes very fair tests and wants everyone to do well.

Delp is an amazing person and professor. Extremely kind, passionate, and helpful to all her students. Though the lectures were just what the textbook says, her breaking down the topic in lecture was helpful for me. The lectures were enough for me, no crazy amount of textbook readings, but reading a bit before lecture was always solid.

Lectures didn't really help me in terms of understanding material so I just stopped attending. I basically learned everything from the textbook and did fine. Professor is really kind, caring, and makes lecture fun though. Exams were not too bad; very manageable if you did the homework in my opinion.

Professor Delp taught this class in an extraordinarily approachable manner. The lecture was fun; she may seem a bit disorganized but she is extremely knowledgeable about the material, is passionate about the content, and successfully manages to inspire students with an eager sense to learn. The textbook is a must. Restored my joy in mathematics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is literally the best. She is so caring for her students and really tries to make sure you understand the material. Office hours are super useful and thats where she gets to know her students. Even on zoom she played music and made it a really fun environment. She was also really good at answering questions in the middle of lecture.
Kelly Delp is an amazing lecturer! I was intimidated by multivariable calculus but she made it quite easy to understand. It is the best class i have taken so far.
Professor Delp's office hours were extremely helpful. Don't be afraid to schedule an appointment with her as wellshe'll go above and beyond to make sure you understand a difficult topic.

Great Professor. Unlike many professors here she cared about us learning the material and having fun along the way. Dynamic lecturer, and she really goes deep into the visualization of the nitty gritty concepts, which was a lifesaver for a visual learner like myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Delp is a passionate, energetic, and dynamic lecturer who made me love multivariable calculus. If you have to take 1920, take it with her--the class and her exams are FAR more fair than other professors who teach the class. Lectures are essential for understanding conceptual parts of the course, which she loves to test on her prelims and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gives sample past exams but doesnt give solutions. What's wrong with her brain?
Delp is a really cool person who is obviously very passionate about math. Lectures are sometimes tangential and the tests are way too hard (especially prelim 1)

She ditzes out - a lot. And her voice is annoying. And goes on tangents about graphs, and the "+, -, 0" game. For Example - she didn't know the name of the fingers. and then spent a couple minutes telling us about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kelly's lectures are energetic and she's enthusiastic about sharing her love for math. She also tries her best to provide visuals for a better understanding of the material. However, it is multivariable calc, and won't be easy.

Multi is notoriously a hard class; however, Professor Delp has great energy so far this spring. She's a great lecturer and seems like she really enjoys teaching multi. She has her lectures prepared before hand and does not get side tracked. I really like her so far.
Her lectures don't make any sense and don't help with homework or section. Alot of notes aren't given and the group work is stupid.
She is very energetic during lectures and is open to answering questions. Uses a lot of visual representations, which helps with understanding the 3D structures in multi.

She's really sweet and nice but the problem is she can be a little scatter-brained and she makes a lot of mistakes. She's very good about catching and correcting them but by that point you're already confused. Multi is hard enough even with good lectures.

He's good at explaining things in lecture. He's caring and always willing to answer questions during class and after. It's a tough class and problem sets are long but the work is helpful for exam prep. If you have to take this class, I would recommend taking his!

His class IS difficult. the PSs are pretty long but good practice for the tests. He really cares for his students and WILL try his best to help you if you reach out, and he's genuinely passionate about what he teaches. To get good grades, make sure you understand the concepts and do the sections and really listen to the lectures.

Such a difficult class BECAUSE HE MAKES IT THAT WAY! Get your ECON 3030 credit somewhere else because this class genuinely is so difficult for no reason. If you care about your GPA, don't take this class. He has extremely difficult content in problem sets (6 a semester), after lecture quizzes, and most of the time he couldn't finish his lecture.
Engaging, yet informative lectures. The material is difficult but the criteria for success are clear cut so it's not impossible to do well.

This class is genuinely brutal. Just one of those classes you need to get through for Econ major but it's frustrating the entire time. P-sets are actually absurd and the entire course is multi variable calculus despite half the class not having taken that class. Prof seems like a good dude but it doesn't really matter when the class is unreasonable
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: immediate no. Can't fit his lectures into class time so he always posts a video of what he didn't cover in class. Usually these videos are posted NEXT DAY.ew

Sweet professor who cares about course and students, but very difficult course. P-sets would take upwards of 8 hours each (6 p-sets for the course and one drop). Exams are much easier than p-sets. Lectures are difficult to follow, but posts lecture slides. Accessible for OH. Would recommend, but be ready to put in a lot of work outside of lectures

Pretty nice guy but could not make any sense out of his lectures. Talks about how content is easy but likes to jump from one thing to the next without a ton of conceptual explanation; slides aren't the best either. I learned the most from this class by just figuring things while doing the psets, but felt like exams questions were a lot different.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer, but sometimes struggles with pacing content. Make sure to do the reading (BEFORE you take the quizzes) and go to class. Not too many p-sets, but they take forever. Exams are very fair--if you understand the problem sets, you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very sweet man and tries to be accommodating, but oh boy he does not lecture well. Tries his best, but exams are crazy hard too. Annoying part is that he just keeps talking about how easy the exam was, and just doesn't explain well. Better off just self studying tbh

A good lecturer, but the slides can be a bit lacking, with a bit too heavy an emphasis on theory at times. Tests can be difficult but graded fairly, and if you study you will do well. Problem sets are difficult but definitely reasonable. Overall he is a caring professor who takes feedback well and is willing to accommodate his students

Such an interesting class and the professor is clearly well informed (rambles a bit too much). Only issue is she barely gives out As and doesn't give proper feedback. Super nice during office hours and overall a great teacher.

Her grading criteria was very unclear and she didn't give us good feedback on how to improve our writing. I would say that my AP Lit/Comp class taught me like 5x more about how to write well, than this class did. It's unfortunate because it means that we are not making good use of our tuition/time/energy here at Cornell.
Do not take this class.

If you choose to take a class by this professor... don't. If you have to take a class from this professor... good luck. She is hard to listen to and rants for ages. The class has no clear rubrics or standards for writing. She grades harshly with little to no room for improvement no matter how much time you may spend. Save yourself, please.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: she teaches everything really well, and the quizzes help you keep up with studying. grades pretty fairly.

This class covers a lot of content, but is not hard if you memorize. Unfortunately, Dr. Nicholson is one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. Her slides are so unorganized: she attempts to fit the entire lecture in like three slides, jumps around from material to material with no clear organization and her lectures are too fast to take notes

Professor Nicholson is one of my favorite professor at Cornell. Her biochem lecture is manageable if you attend lecture and spend some time to study after class. No tough questions on exams and she's very fair on grading. 

She is approachable, kind, and caring for her students. Definitely recommend her lectures

Prof. Nicholson is super caring and wants to see students learn. There's a lot of content to memorize but that's just how biochemistry is. The TA study sessions are life savers and will probably teach you more than lecture. Class is not curved and average is A-. Something like 25% of your grade is essentially participation.
great professor wants to genuinely see you succeed. one of the classes that many premeds take, class is uncurved. you will get what you put in from this course, and you can get a lot.

Prof Nicholson is extremely nice and approachable. she is willing to help answering the most basic questions and always make fun jokes in class to bring more joy to the students. we have weekly quizzes, a midterm and a final, which are all fair questions.  in general, she is so great to work with

Prof. Nicholson has been by-far, one of my favorite professors here at Cornell. There are so many resources in the course, including the undergrad-led study sessions (which were so good), and if you go to everything, do all the practice (esp the prelims), and study ~30 min every day outside of class, it's pretty much guaranteed A.

nicholson was so kind and reasonable-- while biochem can be a lot, nicholson was super clear on what to expect for the weekly quizzes and exams (1 midterm + final). plus, we got 4 drops for quizzes and had other straightforward assignments that made exams weigh a little less
overall i actually really enjoyed the class and biochem as a whole now :-)

Professor was extremely clear cut on what you should know and be able to do. Her slides were a little crowded, but she still conveyed concepts well. Quizzes were helpful and not stressful and exams were very fair.

Linda is a genuinely kind person who wants students to succeed and provides clear learning expectations and objectives. However, she is not good at conveying information or explaining concepts in biochemistry. Although this course isn't autotutorial, it might as well be. You will be teaching yourself everything in this class, and it will be tedious

Her slides were kinda bad but she explained the concepts fine. It was very memorization heavy so attending lecture was necessary. We had weekly quizzes that helped me stay on top of material. The final was worth 40% of our grade with one prelim being worth 35% and the quizzes worth 25%. She also gave some practice problems which was helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Linda an incredible lecturer. She clearly put tons of time into her lectures and she provides a large number of resources like recorded lectures and written out notes. She is also very engaging, funny, and cares. She emphasizes exactly what you need to know for exams and practice exams are exactly like exams. Best professor Ive ever had.
She explain concepts pretty well and only test things that have been covered in lectures. This class has little homework, but is VERY test-heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very understanding and lenient. Coursework is challenging

Excellent professor! Linda cares so much about her teaching , was very respectful of students' questions, and presented the material in a very clear manner. Prior to the class I had little knowledge of proteins and didn't like protein chemistry. I learned so much and now really enjoy protein chemistry!

Great professor, very in-depth and comprehensive coverage of the material. Over 1/3 of the grade is a group project. Unfortunately, she leaves all the assignments to be graded by her TA, which made the grading somewhat inconsistent with the lectures.

Grad level course in protein folding and dynamics.  Intense coverage of material, but more math than most people will probably use, and not enough coverage of software tools available.  Lecture slides disorganized.

Leah teaches college students like an elementary school teacher. She will wait till everyone stops talking, spends most of the lecture talking about inclusivity, and rushes through the overall material. Avoid her at all costs.

My first time sleeping in lecture after 20 minutes. She is not always organized and the quality of presentation is sometimes unprepared.
Be ready to self study or go to ask TAs.
Lectures were really disorganized, hard to follow, and unprepared. Exams were mostly easy enough to compensate. Homeworks took a lot of work and didn't really feel that beneficial for learning.

You can tell she's really trying her best, but her lectures are harder to follow and feel less content-dense compared to Professor Eichhorn. Went on tangents sometimes about non-related course material when there wasn't even enough time allotted to cover the actual course content. Hope she's able to hit her stride and shoutout Xi'an street food!

Great lectures and great lecture notes. Really supportive professor who is very willing to help outside of class. Provides practice prelims very similar to real ones. However, homework assignments are long and very harshly graded.

I felt like whenever she did lectures instead of Matt I always would have to review notes since the lectures were harder to follow. Although she was very engaging, I felt like she tried to hard to bring it outside topics into the course that made us run out of time to focus on what were expected to actually learn

Prof Shuster is patient if you don't understand a topic. He will take the time to thoroughly review theory concepts. In my experience, if you really want to understand music theory, both 2101 and 2102 are essentials at Cornell. My musicianship has greatly improved since taking these classes. Puts the fun in fundamentals in my personal opinion.

Not to invalidate anyone else's experience, but I personally didn't see any of the concerning behaviors reported in the other reviews. He seemed like just a well-intentioned guy, perhaps with a strange fascination on Chinese martial arts (and some concerning YouTube recommended videos). Lectures were a bit unclear at times, but grading was lenient.

Extremely disrespectful - especially towards women. Made a joke that a student who was majoring in Philosophy and Music had parents who were disappointed by her. She cried. Passive aggressive in email as well as in person.

prof shuster loves to cold call and make targeted and passive aggressive comments when students are struggling with the material. he seems to insist it's all very easy even though it is in fact quite difficult at times and he doesn't really explain most of the material. he's also very disorganized and made some weird comments about autism and women

This class was incredibly disorganized (no syllabus) and fast-paced. Students weren't given adequate materials to be successful; there are no class notes, instead he writes on a chalkboard and cold calls with questions about information that has not yet been taught. The professor picks on students who do and don't know the answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm so traumatized by this professor that I've come back ten years later to share my experience. In fall 2016, I was extremely depressed, and she took that personally. She would often call me into her office and berate me like she was my mother. I always left sobbing. I wish I could go back and stand up for myself. It's just a class.

Someone else said this and I agree (took last semester): "A very eccentric professor, wants the class to be free and open but grades harshly when you do not specifically respond to the ridiculous questions that occur to her when reading your writing. I'm not sure how I feel about her she's okay but I would not recommend taking a class with her."
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cecilia is a very odd instructor and it was obvious that very few in our class trusted her. She does the bare minimum and never provides any feedback but gets upset if you ask about grades. Quite obvious to everyone that she just wants to come to class without being prepared for the lecture. I'd rate her teaching skills as very poor.

A very eccentric professor, wants the class to be free and open but grades harshly when you do not specifically respond to the ridiculous questions that occur to her when reading your writing. I'm not sure how I feel about her she's okay but I would not recommend taking a class with her. Also she never gave grades so my final grade was a surprise.

One of my favorite teachers/professors ever! It felt less like a formal student-teacher relationship, and more like a relationship of mutual respect. She's happy to meet with you for office hours, which you might need, since she's picky about thesis. She is very eccentric, but it creates an incredibly lively and entertaining in-class environment.

I will agree that she is very scatterbrained, but she keeps class very entertaining and is passionate about what she teaches. Does say some very odd comments but she was not racist in MY class (I have seen some comments saying she was in theirs, which I don't doubt). Lots and lots of work, but easy grading. Brought homemade bread on last day!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: No African American would ever claim another African person's lived experience with racial microagressions to be untruthful. This is all I will say about the comment below.

She is chaotic but her energy is infectious and if you put in effort she responds really well in her grading. 

I had no problem as an African American student. I obviously am concerned by the comments on this site but I asked other former students about their feelings and they were all super positive.
Why did this site remove the comment where i said she asked me why I, as an African, looked and acted differently from the other African she had met???
Avoid at all costs. Extremely disorganized and if you are a student color, prepare to be intimidated.

I agree with past comments that she's all over the place. Her class is literally a chaotic mess. Also, shes had a few "problematic" comments to say about peope of color. I dont recommend taking any class with her.

Like some of the other comments mentioned, she is a bit eccentric and her instructions are often unclear. However, the class was a genuinely enriching experience and fostered an intimate, introspective environment. She can be intimidating and does call on people at random, but sincerely cares about students. My Spanish noticeably improved.

Genuinely cares about students and takes time to meet with them outside of class. Passionate about her subject. Somewhat disorganized and gives instructions that are often confusing. Can be hard to figure out what she expects from students on the assignments.

Great professor! She is kooky in a good way. Her class is structured like an AP English class but with Spanish literature and of course only using Spanish! There's a lot of reading and a lot of writing. But that's about it---no tests! She's very easy to plan a meeting with and will give you feedback. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunit
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's nice and flexible about deadlines, and her grading isn't bad. The papers themselves are short and easy, but there is a lot of reading for a "writing workshop." Her instructions are often confusing/unclear, and it feels like she imposes her own perspective of the readings onto us, so any conclusions we make about them are heavily guided.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She's really wacky and amazing. I love her. She does grade a lot of papers like you'll get homework every day but it's super easy to follow and she offers lots of extra credit.

This lady is bomb. Many people can't handle the class and thats understandable but if you are ready to be challenged and learn Cecelia is the ideal prof. She makes you work for your grade but the classes she teachers are wildly different from the rest at Cornell and it's a very fun break from the norm

I am seeing a lot of negative comments below, but Cecilia Lawless is one of the best professors at Cornell. She definitely pushed me beyond what I thought my limit was and this class perfected my Spanish writing. Yes, perhaps she would forget some deadlines, but as long as you check your email, all of her instructions are there. She is the best.

She's amazing teacher. I was quite competent and spanish and still needed a tutor for her essays from time to time. I ended up with an A in the class (i was actually aiming for an A+ since i went to soooo many extra credits) so I am happy. She is incredibly sweet, interesting, and fascinating!!!! I was forced to take the class b/c of the rquirement
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My Spanish really improved in Cecilia's class.  For introductory level courses, I'd imagine she's a bit overwhelming, but if you're a Spanish Major/Minor, you already have a passion for the language and would enjoy her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class can be a little unorganized and homework-heavy, but she's very approachable and definitely cares about you if you show you're trying. A

Cecilia cares most about the quality of effort you put into the class. The essays are not too long, and she makes sure your writing and speaking improves over the semester. The reading material, discussions, and assignments are interesting and relevant. If you participate, don't miss class, and care, you will do well. Fair grader. Highly respected.

Absolutely incredible. She definitely makes you work for the class, but she often allows late work, gives extra credit, and gives meaningful feedback. Plus, she's always enthusiastic about class discussion, she'll genuinely care about you (if you put effort in), and her assignments are very open and thought-provoking. I wish she taught above 2180!!

I absolutely loved having Cecilia as a professor.  She is quite scatterbrained but she is so passionate about what she is teaching and she really does care about students.  My writing improved incredibly this semester, not just in Spanish but in English too.  I'm hoping to take a class of hers next semester, too.
Prof. Lawless changed my life; I will never forget her.

No, she doesn't know what time it is and yes, she is eccentric, but Cecilia is a passionate, articulate professor and I will be forever grateful I signed up for a class with her. She cares personally about students and is incredibly encouraging if you put in the work. Take the time to go to her office hours, even if it's just to chat!

she's an amazingly passionate teacher who really knows her stuff. sure she's disorganized but the assignments are super open ended so you can literally write about anything. she's a pretty interesting lady who will genuinely care about you and how much you learn. EASY EASY EASY GRADER. if you show genuine interest you'll get at least an A

She takes a bit of getting used to. She is a bit disorganized and never knows what time it is, and her assignment directions can be a bit confusing. However, she is very goodhearted and genuinely tries to help students if they tell her they are having trouble. She is passionate about Spanish and indigenous peoples. Class helped my Spanish so much!!

She is a little bit "loca."  Often arrives to class in a fluster and is somewhat disorganized.  Sometimes her assignment directions make no sense.  However, she is a thoughtful professor who is willing to extend deadlines if needed.  She also cares deeply about her students and is always willing to help.  She's worth putting up with.

Cecilia is a professor for people who really care about spanish. She knows who's serious and who's just filling a requirement. I've taken several of her classes. She's a bit confusing in terms of assignments and her style is a bit peculiar, but if you want to have legitimate skill and experience w/ the Spanish language, and you work hard, shes 4 u

Horribly disorganized & unable to properly communicate. Gets angry with class when we can't figure out what's supposed to be happening. Assignments are somewhat bogus & a lot a of work. Discussion is repetitive & focuses on irrelevant details which we are expected to find & understand.   I love the Spanish language but can't stand this class.
I would not take another class with her even if I had to switch to French.

My Spanish improved by leaps and bounds in this class; my writing is now more or less automatic, and my speaking is more fluid.  Of the 2 professors teaching this course, Sra. Lawless the more laid-back one.  All assignments and exams are written, and the focus is more on analyzing Spanish lit. and films than filling out grammar worksheets.

I really liked Spanish before I took this class, and she's not horrible or anything, but I just didn't feel I learned very much.  She seems disorganized and though she starts out with a syllabus, it quickly becomes modified-again and again. We didn't use text books so much--more in class discussion.  Homework regularly
Pretty bad, avoid at all costs.
Ridiculous essays. A bunch of psychobable and pseudo-philosophy. Horrid accent.

At first she may seem a little bit distant or above her students. But if you do the readings and truly participate she absolutely has a lot to offer, though her arguments can be complex sometimes, especially if you have not done the readings!

A really enthusiastic educator....watch out for her distinctive smell, you'll start to notice that all your Spanish notebooks smell like her. She's not good with technology or emails so make sure that you get on her class list serve.
You have to try in her class, as long as you do, you will be ok. A's are rare in her class, but it's pretty easy to get B's. Just go to class and participate every now and then.

Though not an easy class, Cecilia tries very hard to get you interested. Some students may say that she is tough, but how else are you going to learn Spanish? Overall, I really like her teaching style.
No Comments

I REALLY liked Cecilia. After my first spanish instructor left on pregnancy leave with only 4 weeks left in class, Cecilia came in and blew us all away. Thought extremely eccentric, she is a great teacher. She really pushes you to speak spanish which only helps you. She obviously cares about making you learn and not just get though the class.
An excellent teacher who instills analytical strategies into her students while challenging them to develop their own unique voice to nurture.
Horrible teacher!  Unorganized and even ****.  I would not advise anyone to take her EVER!  It's a shame she is still teaching.
HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE!
Very unorganized(ie never came to class with a watch, never even brought pens!). During office hours she does not help at all, and only seems to want to leave.
Very kind professor.  Extremely helpful if you approach her.

Funny and always accessible. A lot of readings but only the parts discussed during class are covered. Clearly cares about his students and always available for unscheduled office hours. Unfortunately, he's sometimes unprepared and can't answer some basic questions. Midterm graded very reasonably.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the laziest professors I have had. Every class was exactly the same and he just liked to listen to himself talk. He was often condescending and grading was completely arbitrary.

Every day in class, you do the same boring activity. He is a lazy unmotivated faculty member who created the curriculum years ago and has never once revised it. He would come to class having not reviewed anything related to the material. Additionally, he provides 0 feedback on your work and doesn't explain why he takes points off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is fascinating, and even students with a Jewish education background will learn a ton. There's a lot of reading and writing involved, which can hit hard in the middle of the semester when it's 10 degrees outside. He is accessible outside of class and encourages students to participate.

Professor Mokhtarian is an incredible professor who cares deeply about seeing his students learn and succeed. The assignments are beneficial to your understanding of the information and never feel unnecessary. He will push you and your writing skills, but it is 100% worth it and you will be proud of your assignments by the end of the semester.

He teaches pointless information in 9am lectures which is later covered during 3-hour, unskippable labs. Getting an A+ in his class is just about impossible, and lecture attendance can be done remotely(most days). When the course is helpful, it's not directly due to his teaching, but because of the lab TAs. His teaching needs more direction.

The class itself is quite trivial if you have any experience in biology, but an easy A. Sarvary's lectures are quite fun, just make sure to do the PollEv for attendance. The labs (and getting out of them early) heavily depend on the TA, but generally really straightforward and easy. Very flexible assignment schedule.

These other reviews must be lying because BIOG1500 is not a great course. It insists upon itself and is a tad bit pretentious. Nothing against the professor, it's just that the course is a lot of busy work and not very informative.

Mark was passionate about the class, but the class has a lot of busy work and seems kinda pointless. It's pretty easy, but unfortunately, the class is not formatted in a way that is very exciting or intellectually stimulating.

Sarvary is really nice and his lectures are chill and enjoyable, but ultimately the lab TAs are a lot more important in shaping your experience with the class. Grading is annoying, as an A+ is nearly impossible (99.00+), and my grad TA was really stingy with points. Sarvary is great and deadlines are flexible, but be ready for boring 3-hour labs.

The class really really serves no educational purpose whatsoever. The lectures are sometimes engaging but again there is no point in attending apart from answering polling questions. The labs are needlessly long and do not need to take up 3 hours.

He seems like a sweet person, but I truly didn't learn much from his lectures. The three-hour labs were really tedious and painful to sit through. Definitely an easy A class, but it's virtually impossible to get an A+ (the minimum grade is 99.00%)
Useless morning lectures, extremely boring lab sessions. I don't know why the lab is 3 hours long. Please make a test-out option for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Don't really learn much in lecture and things are mainly taught by the lab TA, but his lectures were easy to follow and he seems like a nice guy.
This class is horrible. Mandatory course for my major and it's just busy work and dry content that I already know. There needs to be a system to test out of this garbage.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course is required, but in the end I was glad I took it as I feel much more prepared for my summer internship and advanced courses next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely boring class and kind of useless. You think you'd learn real lab techniques but it's just simple things like micropipetting and how to use a microscope. He's a nice guy but the class is just boring to sit through. It is a requirement for any pre-health majors, but it's 2 credits and an easy A so just get through it.

Worst class ever. He is sneaky when it comes to justifying the material. This class is literally middle school level and so boring to sit through, even the lab TAs agree. His assignments are set up to confuse people and lower their grades to keep everyone from getting an A. DO NOT TAKE IT UNLESS YOU HAVE TO.

This is an extremely boring class. Grades mostly depend on your GTA, which is annoying if you get a bad one. The assignments are annoying and tedious and some are pointless. There's one exam, a research paper, and bunch of other trivial assignments like presentations and stats work. If you put in the bare minimum, you'll get an A or B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely boring and excruciating class. Sarvary and the other professor did virtually nothing the entire semester. I got stuck with the worst GTA who graded as harsh as she could for good work. GTA was on a power play the entire time and used that to be threatening and harm students grade. Easy class but a horrible class structure

It's very easy to get an A. Professor Sarvary and his TAs take feedback very seriously. The class was interesting but a bit long. However my graduate TA let us leave earlier if we finished early so it wasn't that big of an issue for me. Overall I recommend the class and the assignments we did helped me in other lab settings.

It is an unnecessarily long class for the amount of content covered. You're expected to pay $80 for a lab manual that isn't used often. He's the author and advises against reusing old versions so you'll buy a new copy even though the maybe 5 useful pages could be on Canvas. You'll get a (not so) free A though.

Most boring class i have ever taken. Labs are 3 hours long, unnecessary, & unhelpful. The grading scheme is completely unfair. It's def an easy A, but an A+ is basically impossible because he increased the cutoff (99.000+). The only thing i like about this class is the extended deadlines without penalty. DO NOT take unless u have to.

Most boring three hours of my week were spent sitting in this lab. You don't even do labs, the class includes learning how to email professors about research opportunities, using R coding software, and reading scientific journals. The one lab that we were supposed to do ended up being cancelled and they gave us fake data to use instead. Easy A tho.

The labs are incredibly annoying, you have to sit there for all three hours, but all of it could be covered in an hour if they wanted to. He doesn't do much during the lectures each week, so it seems like he mostly is the class coordinator.

Most boring class I've ever taken. Grading scheme makes completely no sense - I forgot to add a picture of something to a single assignment and got a 100% on everything else and I got a B. Labs are uselessly long and the textbook is a scam.

Only take biog1500 if you have to, or if you want to do research. Otherwise, it is boring and useless. The lectures were all recorded videos which was nice, but the labs are three hours and we barely did anything Luckily there was not a ton of HW. Expensive textbook. I rarely saw Prof. Sarvary except for lecture vids and popping in and out of lab.

Labs are the most boring thing ever and always take 3 hours long. Class does teach some useful skills, but the required 70$ textbook is a scam!!! We barely use the textbook and they require it. Lectures were recorded and we only had to show up in person for one lecture. This class is an easy A if you do all the work but it's so annoying.

I took this course over the winter session and it was great! Mark is a wonderful teacher and really cares about his students. It is not a very difficult class but it is a great resume builder and a great introduction to scicomm, if you're interested. The zoom calls were long but we took breaks. Not bad at all for 3 credits in 3 weeks.
This class is easy, but it is very boring because the labs are just very long. The workload is average, but I would not want to sit through this class again.

Super easy A but one of the most boring classes I've ever taken. The material is extremely simple, but it takes so much time to get through. Prof Sarvary himself is kind, lenient when you need an extension and overall cares about the course.

Literally you could learn the entire semester's material in a day on your own. The labs are stretched with ridiculous questions for material that could be covered in 15 minutes but actually take 3 hours. Take it for the free A and move on.
Go to lecture to answer questions to receive credit. Lab is not difficult. Prepare for lab practicals. Take class with people you know because lab gets boring and there is a group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures used clickers when I took it, and I had a night lab taught by a grad student. The lab usually was let out early, thankfully. Basically the course was fine and taught basic scientific design and literacy through a biological lens. The prof also helped me land a spot despite the course being full.

The lectures were early and mandatory; I would get breakfast and eat it during lecture because there was nothing of value being spoken most of the time. However, there were clicker questions to make sure we were there. The labs were slow and were very easy, so just show up, stay for 3 hours a week, and you'll get an A.

Sarvary is a quality guy, but lectures are useless (but mandatory) and labs are unnecessarily long and tedious. The lab skills are relevant and applicable to research, but the course is paced at 1 mph. Overall, the workload is negligible and the course is an easy A so long as you put in minimal effort.
BIOG 1500 was an excellent foundational course. Dr. Sarvary is a great adviser!

BIO 1500 is an insult to everyone required to take it. Lectures are mandatory, but don't teach anything useful. Labs are three hours long, and you aren't allowed to leave early, even though the material takes 15 minutes. The only upside is how easy this course is- if you passed 5th grade math, you will get an A. Avoid this course if you can.
Take caution because Savary has an accent like Tommy Wiseau from The Room. Take this class freshman year because it is taught at a snail's pace.

If you have ever taken a biology course before, you will pass. If not, this is a good way to get hands on experience with lab techniques. definitely take this your freshman year, you'll hate yourself otherwise.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Don't buy the online textbook, as everyone else said. Get the free trial. Overall, this is a fairly easy class; it was my favorite, because the labs were pretty interesting and there was a light course load. Definitely answer poll everywhere questions, and find some good people for lab partners since you'll be stuck with them for most classes!

This class is incredibly dull. It is taught at a Kindergarten pace and your experience really relies on your TA. Sarvary himself is boring, arrogant, and patronizing. I hated this class and the only reason I ever went was for participation points.
You don't need to buy the online textbook or go to lecture other than for Poll Questions.
Good lecturer genuinely enthusiastic about the class, but labs are long and boring. Tests are easy and papers and projects are clearly outlined/understood.

This class is super easy. The material is easy to understand and the lectures are straight forward. Don't even really need to go to lecture to do well in the course. Dr. Sarvary is a great guy. Does have an accent so can be a little hard to understand sometimes. The online book is worthless.
I would second the disorganized comment. Lectures too seem useless.
This class is easy but disorganized.

The online book is fairly useless as a study tool. However, you will need it for prelecture and during lecture questions. Expect the TAs to have different approaches to grading and handing out studymaterial that is allowed and not allowed. The course staff decided not to hand out study guides, practice prelims, and answer keys to homework problems.
Sarvary is a great lecturer; he almost makes going to a 9am bearable.

This man is amazing. He's brilliant, really approachable, sweet, and always willing to help. If you think your TA is unfairly grading he's willing to look over anything for you. Highly recommend this professor in any course.
Sarvary's lectures are easy to understand, and the material is really simple. If you have a good TA, this class is a piece of cake.

The class is super easy and even if you can't understand his lectures (which I totally could anyway), very little of the material is new as long as you had decent bio in high school. He's funny and friendly, even though some find him intimidating. Also I love his accent.

He teaches about half of the lectures.  His accent is horrible and can sometimes make it hard to understand him.  He isn't the clearest professor in the world either.  All in all, the class is fairly easy and straightforward (if you have a good TA).
good guy. But hated his tests and hated his lab course. His lectures are clear tho.
He seems like a good professor overall.  The class, on the other hand....
Very helpful man, lectures were clear and entertaining. Really nice guy if you ever go to office hours.
Sarvary was a clear lecturer and I enjoyed his teaching more than any of the other guest lecturers.

Assistant Prof to Dr. Turgeon- I love him and his accent. His way of presenting material is very interesting and he's a funny guy. I kinda hope he replaces Turgeon because he is a much better lecturer

He's awesome. I took him last semester for bioethics and he made the class really enjoyable. Creates a great environment for discussion of arguments and objections, too, which is helpful for a philosophy course. Just make sure you do the readings (there are occasional pop quizzes) and ask questions when necessary. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good FWS professor! Had him for Bioethics and he was very chill and made discussions engaging. Super down-to-earth and nice. Gives good feedbacks on essays and readings are minimal. Beware of occasional popquizzes in class, but they're not hard and worth very little. Not a harsh grader--do the readings, participate, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Paskell was a pretty chill professor. Five essays in total, with each being weighted more as the semester progresses. Attendance in lectures and discussions were mandatory, but going is helpful just to gain further clarification on the readings and insights to write the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had Professor Paskell for my FWS Bioethics. Super interesting class, and he always made discussions very interesting! There were usually readings for each class, but most of the time very short (and very minimal compared to other writing seminars). Also gave very good essay feedback (although he is a slow grader). Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was for an FWS on Luck and Morality. There were a lot of readings, quizzes, and small assignments, and attendance was mandatory, so the class took a decent amount of time. However, he made the class discussions pretty interesting and gave really helpful feedback on the essays, so the class was worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Best professor ive had at cornell so far. Genuinely makes class so intresting and made me fall in love with economics.

Professor Sanders is a great teacher and person. He actively looks for ways to make the class better for the students in it. The two different grading methods provided a lot of flexibility. The two midterms were definitely a lot easier than the final but overall they were all manageable.
Great lecturer and teacher and gives you a lot of opportunities to do well. Honestly should've gotten an A but sold. Don't rly need to go to class since he posts the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: what everyone else says is pretty accurate. his first 2 prelims are easy as long as you do the bare minimum studying. maybe it was just me but the final was not it even though i spent a good amount of time studying for it. definitely make sure you know your stuff for that but outside of that this class is light and much better than 1120
He's honestly the goat. Easy class if u pay attention. So many resources like office hours and the microecon help center. 2 dif grading methods to help u get a better score in the class.

Very good professor with multiple grading schemes; even if you bomb one of the prelims, a higher grade is possible if you do well on final. Great lecturer and is helpful in office hours. He's the GOAT ;)

Grading is very clear, just don't underestimate the class like I did before the first prelim. Don't fall behind even though it seems very easy and chill, the professor is amazing and you have lots of resources but you do actually need to put some work in. Wonderful professor though, super fun and chill, made econ fun and interesting.

I knew he was going to be a great professor when his pollev question in the first lecture was about his son's favorite song in kpdh. He explains concepts well, is extremely responsive and gives detailed explanations on ed discussion especially before exams. He also gives 5 practice tests for each exam. Exams are very fair and even fun sometimes.

Great professor, includes real world examples in lectures to make economics topics easy to understand for beginners. Tests are extremely fair and modeled after previous years prelim/final exams so not difficult to prepare with effort. Beware that exams are 80% of your score in this class though.
Very clear lecturer, makes Econ easy to understand if you've never taken it before. Kind, flexible, and organized. Not too much HW, but definitely put in effort to study for the tests.

definitely the best professor for taking intro economics courses by a long shot. Such a nice, caring guy and also a really good professor. you can tell he really cares about teaching and explains things in super effective ways. also has cute stories about his family and supports women. hes him

Super passionate, cares about his students. It's a big lecture class but he is a great lecturer and I'm rarely falling asleep (even during an 8am class). Exams are fair, you're able to have a sheet of notes. He gives a lot of practice exams that prepare you well for the exam.
No complaints, amazing professor
Great Professor for Microeconomics! Highly recommended
Great Professor. Very accommodating and understanding of personal circumstances.

While lectures are not required, they are very fun and easy to follow. Would recommend reading textbook although not required. HW is not too frequent and pretty easy. Plenty of review offered for each exam. Reccomend participate in extra credit throughout semester. Very nice professor and hosts lots of OH

As others have said Prof. Sanders genuinely wants you to succeed. I highly recommend going to lecture as he is very good at explaining concepts in ways that are easy to understand, and his deadpan humor keeps it interesting. Discussions are optional. Very willing to meet outside of class for help. Exams are very fair and match the practice tests

My opinion of Sanders is mixed. He is definitely the easiest 1110 prof. He gave up to around 2% extra credit (depending on grading method). Unfortunately he mismanaged online exams, which led him to make a cheat sheet only final, despite 1110 not really being a course you could fit into a single sheet of paper. Sucked up tons of finals week for me.
Literally the best professor here. He is so kind and helpful. He also gives so many extra credit opportunities. If you put in the effort you will get a great grade.

I was expecting to be bored out of my mind in my econ class. Professor Sanders ended up making the class much more interesting than I thought an econ class could be. He had fun interactive things. The class wasn't a walk in the park but he does want you to succeed in it.

Extremely energetic at 9:05 in the morning, cracks jokes that I thought were funny during lecture, responds pretty quickly on the discussion board (especially before an exam). Sometimes went a little too quickly in lecture. There's a textbook but it's not necessary. Exams were online and entirely multiple choice, and very fair.

Professor Sanders is SUPER nice. Really really like him. Just seems like a good guy. He doesn't want you to fail. He really works to make sure you can get the best grade possible in the class. Totally respect him and would be more than happy to take another class with him. Super helpful as well.
Great professor! Smart, good lectures, interesting class.
Such a good lecturer. He is exceptionally kind and helpful during office hours. Overall, a fantastic teacher!

Took his class a while ago but couldn't ask for a better intro micro teacher. Was pretty organized and always tried to make the class material relevant and interesting, which is hard for a 400+ person intro class. Class isn't hard if you at least pay attention, but even if you don't he's very approachable for help.

Such a great professor, he released every prior test he has ever given to study off of. His lectures were well organized and fun to listen to. He was very accommodating during the shooting and bomb scares that happened in fall 21. You can tell he wants the best for his students. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! They help so much!

Sanders was a good lecturer for an introductory econ class. His classes always started by briefing recent research related to topics being covered in class at the time. The homework is not a great representative of the exams, but the exams themselves are very easy and he provides plenty of past exams to review.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders is an amazing lecturer. Hes charismatic, funny, and is soooo passionate about economics. Would definitely recommend him. He comes up with his own exam questions and they always have a whole theme to it; its so funny. Our final this year was Animal Crossing themed!
Very good prof. Extremely good lectures and helpful in office hours. Exams reflect content well.

lectures werent helpful in terms of calculations, didnt always best explain the material. He records his lectures though so you can go back and listen to them. Makes himself available , great explaining in office hours. If youre good at math you'll be okay. If math isn't your forte it's going to require alot of work. Do all the practice prelims!
Amazing. Incredible. Phenomenal. Best professor at Cornell. Give this guy tenure.

Professor Sanders is the best professor I have had at Cornell University. He is always extremely caring as well as being an excellent lecturer. Professor Sanders is quick responder on ed discussion and you never need to be scared to ask questions in class or online. I would take definitely take a class just because it was taught by him!

Professor Sanders is one of my favorite professors in Cornell, he is very caring and respects every students. He cares about student's mental health and try his best accommodating with students needs. Lectures are mandatory but I strongly recommend people to attend lecture because it's very useful and he is a great lecturer.

Amazing lecturer and is really great at explaining concepts. Puts in a ton of effort to help his students. Overall stand up guy. The class isn't too hard if you have at least a bit of background in Econ, but the tests and assessments are doable through doing the past practice exams and asking questions.

Easily the best lecturer I have ever had. You can watch the recorded lectures later so attendance isn't necessary but if you do not watch the lectures you will not pass the class. The tests are fairly simple and very straightforward and he provides plenty of practice prelims. The homework is easy but of no help on the tests. Textbook is useless.

ECON 1110 had a light workload. Only attended a couple of lectures all semester and still had a solid grasp of the course material. The exams were similar to previous years so you knew what to expect. The required homework was not helpful to prepare. Median was a B+ but if you have any background in economics it is a stress-free and easy class.

Such a passionate professor and really cares about his students. Lectures were really clear and he spends a lot of time explaining concepts and graphs. DO THE PRACTICE PRELIMS, though. The questions are extremely similar and the homework is often too easy to be that helpful. I honestly never read the textbook, just pay attention in class.

Professor Sanders is such a positive guy. He makes class stress free and truly cares more about your understanding of the material than just a grade. Lecture is very important, as long as you pay attention to the concepts he explains, you will do very well. I highly suggest taking any course you can with him, I definitely would take another!
Amazing class! Lectures are very engaging. I found the tests to be challenging but fair.

HW - multiple choice, 3 tries for every Q, easy 100% on HW. Lectures - quality slides, but sometimes skips calculation examples that could be helpful. Discussion - optional, not rly helpful. Exams - fair. Make you think, but easy Qs too. Grading - gives different % breakdown options and assigns the best one for u, this semester could drop a prelim
I loved Econ 111 with Sanders. He made lectures exciting and interesting. There was a fair amount of HW, but he gave us three tries on each question so it was easy. Highly recommend Sanders!!

The best professor and the best course I have ever had I have been crying for hours after taking his last lecture. Nick is really awesome! I even want to take ECON1110 again next semester. He is incredibly good at teaching and bring students warmth during such a crazy pandemic period. The homework is sometimes easy, but prelims are moderate.

I had Professor Sanders for intro Micro and Economics and Environmental Policy. It is obvious that he loves what he teaches. He backs up all his statements with engaging research papers. Also, he has a deep respect for the students that can be hard to come by in a professor. Econ3850 was easier than micro.

Prof Sanders is a really great guy! You can tell that he is passionate about economics and the well-being of his students. Piece of advice: make sure you study past prelims/finals in order to do well on that year's exam. Definitely loved having him as a professor because of how engaging he was and how concisely he was able to explain concepts.

Sanders is a great person to introduce you to econ but he does tend to run behind schedule so he gets a less thorough as the semesters go by. You don't really need to show up, the textbook is decent. My TA was terrible and so were a lot of others so don't bank on that. Do a couple of his past tests, his testing is quite different from the hw.

Moves quickly through lecture slides and doesn't always explain the quantitative/calculation parts, but is great for the most part. Posts the slides online so you can skip lecture if you want. Discussions were useless. HW is easy. Exams were straightforward and similar in structure to previous years' exams. Nice guy, makes jokes during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. As long as you go to class and pay attention even though not required, exams are easy. Use previous exams he provides to study. He keeps lectures interesting also
Great lecturer. Makes class very interesting. Very accessible outside of class, with tons of extra office hours before prelims and finals. Not an easy class, but if you do the work, you can do well.

Professor Sanders is a great professor that has interesting real-world examples that make me look forward to class. His tests are very fair and make you learn the material. If you do the previous prelims and read the book you'll be fine, but I suggest showing up to the lectures to learn about the world.

good professor. he tries to be really interesting so the material actually becomes more confusing (ik lol). He will provide examples for topics without providing a framework to apply that example onto. The textbook is a must if you have never taken econ. His tests are fair, but short, so you need to be very accurate to do well. Nice guy.

Sanders is a great professor everybody loves him. However go to his lectures and spend time actually learning the homework or you won't do well. The class is fairly easy if you put in the time. The office hours are great too. Discussions are pointless and very optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super easy class. I went to 2 lectures (I should have gone to more as he is a good lecturer), did not study for any of the prelims and did not go to my section a single time. I think if you just go to lectures and section and pay attention an A is pretty much guaranteed. I had two other friends who actually did the work and they both got A+'s

Not a hard class, but not an easy A bc it is SUPER easy to underestimate it. HW takes 5 minutes & isn't helpful for studying. I got a C+ on Prelim 1 bc I thought it'd be like the HW and that messed up my final grade even tho I A+'s on Prelim 2 & the final. Focus on practice problems + lecture slides. Super nice guy, & willing to help.

Interesting and engaging lecturer who clearly is passionate about the material. Presents material in a clear, understandable way. First two thirds or so of the class the material was pretty easy; got difficult near the end. I especially appreciated that he had lots of extra office hours at convenient times prior to prelims and especially the final.

Sanders is unbelievably dedicated to his job. His lectures have everything you need to know conceptually. His love for econ is contagious and his office hours are fantastic. Don't bother reading the textbook--use it as a supplement if needed. The class is not a lot of work but also not an easy A. Do lots of practice problems to study for prelims.
Great guy, boring lectures. your grade relies on your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: super chill guy

Honestly, this is an amazing class. Take it. It has a pretty simple format: one midterm, two essays, and some in-class assignments/ quizzes. He also gave an option for extra credit. Every assignment allows you to explore what YOU are interested in. He is so flexible,open to connecting with students beyond the classroom, so passionate. Trust me-TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly he is amazing. This course you get to explore so much of what you are interested in. I wish he explored more Latin history. But he is so much fun, love the music he plays in class and the topics we discuss. Really dynamic format. Super great. Easy if you try on assignments. Trust!.

Lectures were all over the place, he YAPPS about irrelevant information 80% of the class. We had 6-7 different books to read almost at random across the semester. Papers are extremely long for an intro class, and even longer readings. Extremely boring lectures, only survived because of my TA! (They are 100% responsible for all the grading).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Nagaraja is one of the sweetest professors in ILR. We had several papers in the class that TAs would grade, but Nagaraja was always willing to review your paper and answer any questions you have.
Professor Nagaraja is great. He's really passionate and knowledgeable, and is always willing to meet with you.

He is very nice and approachable practically begging students to ask him questions and go to office hours. Slides are way too text-heavy, but he posts them making attending is unnecessary. The TA does all the grading so I can't comment on that.
Very nice person. Approachable outside of class. Does not grade harshly. Lectures are confusing and not particularly helpful.

Very nice and passionate professor but his lectures were confusing and hard to follow. Attendance is mandatory but I did not learn much within those lectures. I found doing the readings and going to office hours much more useful. Overall, he is a generous grader if you do the necessary work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, but he's a chill guy and doesn't grade too hard.

All papers. Your grade lives and dies by the TA. This semester, there was a probably a 1.5 gpa spread between the two TAs and nothing was done about it. Your grade is about as meritocratic as a roulette table. Lectures are circular, directionless, and unnecessary. Just read the pertinent readings a week before the papers are due.

I kinda disagree with comments for Professor Nagaraja. I first thought he was not good at teaching. However, as I started to listen carefully what he was talking about in class, I learnt a lot. He was very informative and knowledgable. Moreover, he also gave me the freedom to explore my interests under the course framework. Very nice guy.

He's a really nice guy, but an AWFUL professor. Lectures are incredibly disorganized. Very little correlation between readings, lectures, and assignments. TAs do all the work and were pretty short staffed. Do not take him if you do not have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nagaraja seems like a good dude who is interested in the subject matter. However, it is clear that he is uninterested in teaching. His lectures are long, boring, and confusing, and his communication outside of class is terrible(cannot use canvas to save his life). Really disappointed becasuse I thought this would be my favorite class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Simply not a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would REALLY not recommend

Lectures are boring and unnecessary -- read and take good notes from the books and participate in discussion and you'll be fine. Grade can really depend on your TA but go to office hours and have them look at your essays at multiple steps in the process to make sure you're doing what they want to. He's not a bad guy he's just not a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not a great lecturer, His powerpoint slides were really hard to follow and chaotic. He was a really easy grader though, so that was nice. There was lots of assigned reading that you didn't really have to do, and his content was very one-sided. Overall okay experience but I wouldn't recommend if you want to get a lot out of the class.

Professor is clearly very smart, but his classroom management isn't great. He assigned a lot of reading for this class and didn't get assignments back to us for a very long time. The three essays he did assign were essentially the same prompt each time? Interesting class to take if you're invested in the books but hard to get a lot of out of him.

It takes a special type of arrogance to believe you deserve the undivided attention of 50+ people from 8-10AM. He practices what he preaches, seems to care about students. A bajillion assignments going on at all times. In a huge group all sem, felt ridiculous begging adults to study for a test because my grade depended on theirs (group average).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is so strict about attendance, but it's actually not worth it. I've never seen a professor take attendance like that. I remember in the first class, he asked the students if they knew how many assignments there were. He said there were hundreds... I felt like all the assignments were meaningless, and I even made up things to complete them.

I had the worst professor during my first semester at Cornell. We had to take an emotion quiz every day. You could complete a few very simple questions, like "How are you feeling today?" and still not get a perfect score. I hadn't bought an iClicker in my four years of undergraduate studies, but I did for this class.
Undoubtedly the worst lecturer I've ever had at Cornell!

He may come off as intimidating at first but as you go along, you realize how much of a good teacher he is. He really loves helping students. Reach out and schedule OH whenever, you wont be disappointed.

Would not recommend! The amount of work assigned is going to be way more compared to other classes with similar credit levels, and the lectures are not engaging enough for how early they are.  Slides and homework have typos, and you don't need to take this class to learn what is taught.

Self-centered and arrogant and treats his students like children while rarely offering insightful answers to genuinely meaningful questions. For a class so centered on emotional intelligence, I think he could benefit more from taking this course himself than any student enrolled currently. This course is a waste of time and money.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is a joke. You drag yourself to an 8am for zero useful info—just nonsense rants and breakdowns. He warns against "amdalga breakdowns" but literally has them himself. Tests are garbage and make no sense. Haven't learned a single thing. Absolute waste of time.

If you expect to learn real-world project management skills, you won't find them here. Prelims are bizarre and harsh. You must show up before 8 AM for every lecture, phones and laptops banned, or this jerk will destroy your grades. This is the worst instructor I've had since middle school and I strongly recommend him resign from this position.
boring, useless with lots of hw, prelim, final

He's definitely the worst lecturer I've ever had throughout the past five years! Avoid his class if you can, otherwise you'll have to show up at 8 am in the classroom and your electronic devices will be banned. He assigns tons of useless HWs and you won't learn anything helpful but he brags how impactful his classes to students from time to time.

Would NOT recommend. He treats students like little kids. He should understand students only pay attention in classes because professors talk about interesting things, not because phones and computers are banned. For a class that repeats industry leadership jargons and outdated concepts, 2 cumulative prelims and 1 final are more than excessive.
His classes are fun and insightful
Despite being at 8am, I really enjoyed the lectures. Learned a lot of applicable skills and Prof Newman is a great lecturer. Can get stressful when group project work picks up.
The workload can be a lot, but is doable as he gives plenty of in-class time to work on it. Appreciated the team learning environment. Great lecturer and participation is encouraged.

Having taken other 4 credit STEM courses here, I can say Newman gives an unreasonable amount of work for a 4-credit class. He gives us limited time (e.g. 48 hours) do a decent amount of work over the weekend. He often doesn't even create the content for us to work on until right before the weekends yet tells us not to procrastinate - hypocritical!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Group projects did not provide much learning and too focused on who was considered the best. Too much reliance on participation grade. Feedback received was elementary and hardly focused on descriptive content, rather on length of presentation or minor, irrelevant details. The discussions allowed for critical thinking. Disorganized at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Thinks that a 4-credit course is valid for giving hours of work for participation homework. Not even including the other individual homework, team project, team project homework, quizzes, final project, and a final exam we also have to complete for this class alone.
He was one of the best professor I could have asked for to introduce me to the PMA department.
