PK is an excellent teacher and I would take any course he was teaching without even knowing the subject matter. He encourages students to think more deeply, to seek nuance, and to resist the temptation of easy answers to complex problems.

Absolutely loved Katzenstein's class. Even though I am a Hotel student, I took his Intro to IR class in my freshman fall and it is still my favorite class to this date. Would recommend anyone to take a course taught by Katzenstein.

I regret taking this class. All the other hype about PK from the reviews is extremely misplaced. As a junior, I've had much better professors than him. His lectures are irrelevant to the tests (and boring) and you can skip. The amount of reading is atrocious and the sections can barely cover it. The TA's are hard graders as well
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: An incredible scholar. It was an honor to have been taught by him. His analyses on readings - both simple and dense - provide you with depth and very necessary clarity. This is NOT AN EASY class. You have to be willing to read, read and read! If you are interested in IR, this class is a must. He loves his students and wants everyone to succeed!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Katzenstein changed my life. This class changes your perspective on the whole world and teaches you to think in a completely new way. PK teaches you to think, read, and write critically. This course is a lot of reading and is challenging, but you will come out of it feeling so rewarded. TAs were all ridiculously smart and extremely helpful.

Didn't know what to expect from this course, having heard all the hubub from its appearance on Fox News, but each lecture left me thoroughly impressed. PK is a great lecturer and brings an interesting perspective to pol. That being said, we need more TAs!!! Sections were way too large and made it difficult to feel comfortable speaking during them.

PK is a fabulous professor, the best I've come across so far at Cornell. He changes the way you perceive the world, doesn't force you to agree with him, has a fabulous sense of humor and teaches you to think critically. I recommend everyone at Cornell to take at least one of his classes. The skills he teaches are useful in practically every field.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Would take again

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor - I appreciated how insightful his lectures were, and how often he gave us a chance to share our thoughts and opinions on a given topic. The material he covered was very interesting, and the readings often pretty thought-provoking. Overall not too difficult of a class, and I definitely appreciate taking it.

This was probably one of the best classes that I've taken in my university career. PK is truly a fantastic professor that invests a lot of thought into designing his classes and knows exactly what he wants students to take away from them. This being said, class would greatly benefit from having more TAs and smaller sections!

He often speaks without a microphone a bit too softly to understand with his accent. When you can hear him though, Professor Katzenstein comes across as an incredibly humble, knowledgeable, and genuinely enthusiastic professor. Makes lots of jokes during lectures, and cares passionately about what he teaches. I learned A LOT in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: The course is hard because the material is hard, and he views his students as intelligent and capable, so he has high standards. He is an excellent professor, truly inspiring. He says for the first half of the course lots of things won't make sense and he's right, but by the end he's right that it does make sense and changes world views.
one of the most amazing academic experience I have ever had.

AMAZING CLASS. There's a lot of reading, have never seen so much in my life. However, this class does make you critically think. Everyone at Cornell should take one of his courses. He makes the class fun, even though itll consume a lot of your time. He's also very funny. Great fashion sense, lots to turtlenecks.

This class is truly challenging but rewarding. Definitely expect a lot of readings but I learned how to skim by the end of the semester. PK is very knowledgeable and the classes is very organized. One of the best classes I took at Cornell.

Professor Katzenstein is truly an incredible professor, deserving his fame. Lectures can be dense at times, just like the readings, however, they are still incredibly insightful. The course is an insane undertaking, but if you put in the time, the gains are incredible. PK is also extremely accessible, and office hours are extremely fun and valuable

A lot of hype around PK. As you see by other ratings, people view him as an amazing professor although most all of the teaching happens with your TA. PK even says he's the last resort when you have inquiries, consult every TA first. Lectures lack structure and connection to readings is extremely weak. Readings unreasonably hard for an intro level.

PK made the lectures very interesting and helpful. I found that discussion led by the TA's was the most helpful part of the course and helped explain the readings. The lectures are amazing, but be prepared to read like crazy. If you are willing to put in the work this class will reward you.

Great teacher, great class. If you get the chance, take it, because I learned a lot (but be ready to read a lot for homework). If you do the readings, the class isn't that difficult, definitely not too stressful. You can get away with not buying/reading the Drezner book, but it may help you understand the concepts a little better.

PK is one of the most respected professors in the Government Department. Although he tries to make class fun and wants his students to be engaged, his lectures are often extremely difficult to follow and notes (for readings or class) are indecipherable. Be prepared for this class to take over your life as the readings are lengthy and abundant.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Katzenstein is a wonderful professor, and I greatly enjoyed the time I had taking Intro to IR. The course itself is a very difficult course without question, but it does a good job of paving new ways for you to think and analyze the world. Katzenstein has a great approach of placing students first and being a guide through this course.

PK is the someone I'd want as an interesting grandpa, but not really as a professor. This class is completely different from what I expected of the title (Making Sense of World Politics) I almost feel more confused. It is without a doubt that I've learned a huge amount of material, but how I actually feel about the material is hard to answer :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: PK is a gem. He is a master conversationalist and a gifted speaker. He cares about what you think and isn't afraid to say what he feels. He is biased toward his school of theory, but can provide explanations in many. I can't recommend him enough.
I wish I attended the lectures more, but when I did I learned a lot. Everyone at Cornell should take his class
One of the greatest professors I have ever seen, deserve any admiration. Anyone who has a chance should take his courses.
It's my honor to take his class. Although reading is alot, his class is really inspirational. Humorous and nice guy. Accessible. Will take his class again.
He is good, but his lectures have little to do with the material read outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best part of the course -- great lectures Worst part of the course -- irrelevant readings

The case-based approach is unique and incredibly rewarding. Teaches you to analyse a country by understanding macroeconomic indicators in combination with political/historical considerations. PK is strict, kind, hilarious and seems to know something about everything. He pushes students to be the best version of themselves - demanding, but worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Would take again

reviews.comment: Katzenstein is probably the most famous professor in Cornell's Government department, and there's a reason for that. He is a really interesting lecturer and learning during his classes happens naturally. Sometimes he shows his age but not worse than any other professor over 30. Not particularly hard but lots of reading and writing.

Professor Katzenstein is the best professor and person. Unbelievably knowledgeable, unbelievably strict and unbelievably kind. His class is well worth the effort. The TAs are also great and allow for a class like AEM3547 to be possible. I feel grateful and inspired by this class. I have learned a lot about the world and I want to learn much more.

Professor Katzenstein's class is one of the best I've taken. lectures are organized & thought provoking; class discussions are well moderated and interesting. He encourages you to think & grow critical skills rather than memorize info The research paper is daunting at first but bc its broken down its manageable. TAs are great & key to doing well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very informative, gives an overall sense of whats happening in the global political economy by reading interesting cases from different countries around the world. if you have no economics background you need to put too much effort, but it is worth it and you will have a good background of the current global economic and political situation.
PK is the best professor I met, and this course is the most impressive course I took in Cornell. This course changed my mind to pursue my political journalist dream.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: PK is a real gem. I've taken multiple classes with him and wish I wasn't graduating just so I could keep taking his classes. Requires hard work but is substantive and engaging (HBS case+research paper). Definitely take 3547/3557 before graduating. If you're in the social sciences, your Cornell experience will be incomplete without PK.
Prof Katzenstein did a really great job with my course. He's an interesting speaker and knows how to create dialogue. Definitely would take the course again.

Best professor at Cornell it's not even close. One of the smartest minds in his field and the country, you should be required to take his class. I will do everything I can to take more PK classes in the future.
The combination of the lecture, and the discussion section with the TA's was invaluable!

PK is incredible! Highly invested in not only his research, but the world around him. He is very nuanced and inspires students to take responsibility for the world around them w/o inserting political bias. Lectures are dense, and you definitely get the most out of them if you read assigned articles before. Sections are too large, but TAs are great!

This course with professor Katzenstein lacked signifgant structure, papers / policy memos while easy to write are irrelevant to lecture and reading material. Lectures were very dull, but the TA sections and discussion were fantastic. Overall, what I learned from this class was insignifigant despite engaging with readings and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Truly an amazing class with very engaging lectures. He wants this class to be fun and enjoyable for his students. This was the first time he taught this class, so I project that it will be even better going forward. His political biases did not affect the course material. Highly recommend to anybody interested in learning more about IR

I took PK's class "America Confronts the World." The class was incredibly interesting, but very difficult. Get ready to engage a lot of abstract conceptual theories and do a lot of reading. The work is worth it, though - if you are willing to engage, you will learn a lot. Not to mention that PK himself is esteemed, funny, and incredibly smart.

PK is probably the most renowned and highly esteemed prof in the govt department, and it's true that his lectures are captivating. He is brilliant. Take his class for the inspiration and to hear his words of wisdom. But don't expect an A, and expect to read your butt off. This was probably the hardest class I've ever taken. Very bittersweet.

Best class I've ever taken! Both Katzenstein and his TAs want you to succeed and think critically. He really wants you to engage with an care about international relations in any context. The open mic sessions really help you and your friends engage in debates and informal presentations. He is also very funny and interjects this humor in slides.

GOVT 3557  makes you think critically about the intersections of politics, economics, and history in novel ways. It's also one of the very few classes that allows you to write a research paper on any subject of your choice. I am forever grateful to PK for giving us the opportunity to think critically and to produce my first serious academic writing

PK is one of the most inspiring professors I've had at Cornell, and taking GOVT 3557 was a privilege and transformative experience. This course will enable you to think more critically, challenge existing ideas and build your own arguments through a research paper. Do not graduate Cornell without having taken at least one of PKs classes.
This class is what distinguishes an Ivy League institution from colleges. PK is super well-prepared for each lecture. Be prepared for a lot of reading and writing, but totally worth it.

By far the most memorable and worthwhile course I've taken at Cornell. It really gives you a new perspective on world affairs and history through the HBS-case method with absolute awe inspiring lectures by Professor Katzenstein. Cannot stress enough how rewarding taking 3557 has been. Do not graduate without taking at least one PK course.

Professor Katzenstein reminded me exactly what I was looking for when I applied to Cornell. His lectures are outstanding and, although the workload is heavy, he manages to keep you interested and keen to work and read more. I feel privileged to have had the opportunity to be part of his class. I would recommend this course in a heartbeat.

Hands down the best class and best professor. Learned more in this one course than in my three years here. Class structure (HBS cases + real research paper) makes you think, work, and speak. Workload is a fair amount for how much you gain from this class. Very inspirational professor. Courses like this make the tuition $$$ & Cornell name worth it.

PK's latest class is indispensable to the education of anyone interested in politics, economics, international relations, monetary policy or financial markets. The interdisciplinary nature of the course, and the case study method through which we study and discuss, are incredibly valuable. It is precisely what I wanted out of my Cornell education.
Amazing course. Amazing Professor

Amazing class. By far the hardest class I took this semester, but also the most rewarding. Currently suffering while studying for his final but Professor Katzenstein makes you WANT to work this hard. Keep up with the readings, or at least have a google doc with reliable people to make summaries of all of them.

Wonderful class. Admittedly quite hard, but it is worth it beyond belief. Prof. Katzenstein will give you some of the best lectures of your time in college, along with unexpected humor and insightful discussions. Would recommend to any Cornellian.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best class I have taken at Cornell bar none. Amazing orator who challenges his students while providing an ample support structure for when they need help. Very rewarding.

I absolutely loved this class. It's definitely not an easy class, but it's an important class. Professor Katzenstein is knowledgable and an amazing lecturer. I will definitely be taking more classes from him in the future.
Hard class with lots of reading material, but lectures are very interesting, and the professor is brilliant and funny. TA's may vary but mine was helpful and nice.
One of the best professors I've had at Cornell. Genuinely cares SO much about his students and the material. Lots of reading though!

Introduction to International Relations is a difficult class. It was also the best class I took this semester. This is a professor who truly cares about teaching us to think and who knows the value of a liberal arts education. Through open mic, open forums, and engaging lectures, he creates a lecture hall that feels like a community.
He's amazing. Best class ever!

Professor Katzenstein's intro to IR class is probably one of the most interesting and involved classes I will ever take at Cornell. There is a ton of reading, but by clearly summarizing and understanding the most important parts of each reading and the paradigms they cover, you will do very well in his class.

PK's course was on a level all its own. Case studies, daily debates, a research project, and a crash course on political economy rolled into one class. If you put in the work, it can be one of your most rewarding experiences at Cornell. Essential for any serious IR student.

Lectures were amazing . The discussion based nature of the course was one of a kind for a lecture of that size. The length and time given to the research paper  allowed students to do in depth research on their topic. The professor was  unbiased in his lectures, but would never hesitate to challenge students on their assertions.

PK is the best professor I have ever had, and his class on American Primacy was the most beneficial and enriching academic experience I've ever taken part in. He lives and breathes for teaching and will do anything possible to help his students. Head and shoulders above other professors.
I was told that this class would be  memorable and it was for many positive reasons.

This class enlightened me in my understanding of the complicated relationship between politics and economics, both at an international and regional level. The HBS case study method was challenging, requiring consistent in-class participation, which led to thorough engagement with assignments. TAs helped tremendously with the long research paper.

This class was hands down the best course I have taken at Cornell. I recommend it to anyone who is remotely interested in international affairs - any aspect of it! We had a very diverse class in terms of academic interests and that's what made the class great. PARTICIPATION is important!!! Besides, one research paper, which is not TOO tedious.

This was one of the best classes that I've taken b/c of how much it pushed me. But, if you are not interested in stepping outside your comfort zone, do not take this class. The TAs were a huge asset helping us learn the nuts and bolts of int'l finance, case study analysis and how to structure our large 25-30 pg paper.

Professor Katzenstein is an inspirational professor. GOVT 3547 was a demanding class as far as participation, but PK is a fair grader. As long as you prepare for class you will be able to succeed. For anyone with a genuine interest in international relations and achieving a global perspective, this is a great class and fantastic professor.
Great course with a unique setup. You must come to class prepared and ready to talk. The 25-30 page paper at first was very daunting but the TA's are extremely helpful and great. Learned so much.

Great course. One of the best I've taken at Cornell. Loved the setup with the case method. The 25-30 page paper at first was very daunting but the TA's are extremely helpful and great. Learned so much.

PK is my favorite professor at Cornell so far. I took GOVT 3547 with him during the Fall 2015. For the course we wrote a 25-30 research paper, read several economics/finance books, and read and debated many Harvard Business School case studies. I gained a lot from the course and feel more prepared to apply to MBA programs after graduation.

PK is a fantastic professor! I took GOVT 3547 with him this fall, having heard so much about his lecturing style and insights into world politics. Though I think he's still working out some of the kinks with the course's unusual style (case study-based, with a heavy emphasis on class participation), I learned so much from his lectures.

I took Gov 3547 with PK this summer. Having taken his Gov 1817 class as a freshman, I had high expectations. I wasn't disappointed. The lectures were wonderful, the class discussions valuable, and the TAs incredibly helpful. I would recommend this class to anyone with even a remote interest global politics/economics.

Took Govt 3547 in Fall 2015 with PK. Easily the best class and professor that I have had at Cornell!  I loved the combination of HBS Case Discussions along with amazing lectures by PK. I learned immensely and it really stoked an interest in the field of international political economy. Take a class with PK (esp HBS case method) before you graduate!

PK is as amazing in GOVT3547 as in his other courses! One part to highlight in this course, besides its HBD case method, is the requirement to write a full-length research paper, which you choose your own topic. The weekly TA session really helps to let you make step-by-step progress finishing the paper from literature review to the conclusion!!!

PK is finally back from Harvard. Actually, he brought back HBS case study method. Although an experimental course, GOVT 3547 run extremely smoothly during the semester and student participation rate, as I noticed, reached almost 80% at last, quite abnormal at Cornell, even at Hotel School. The course is really for every major!

GOVT3547 was the second course I took with PK. Similar to GOVT1817, US Primacy Challenged was one of the most inspirational courses I took during my time at Cornell; different from lecture style courses, GOVT3547 used HBS case method to study political economy of regional powers around the world. Full length research paper was assigned but no exam!

Katzenstein is amazing. Not only is he a funny lecturer, he also clearly cares about the students. Govt 1817 was a difficult class, because of the many readings. grades depend on TA. do readings or die
Will definitely not take his class again.
Tough class. Prof is brilliant in the classroom, possibly some of the most interesting lectures at Cornell. However, grades are at the hands of the TA who are often quite unfair.

Great Class, Great Professor - There's ALOT of readings but its totally worth it in the end. Took it as a freshman and it was overwhelming but I don't regret it at all. Got an A at the end of the course because I put in so much effort. It's do-able. You just need to care enough
Brilliant professor, delights with wit and knowledge in equal measure. Busy, but still willing to help outside of class.

The class is worth taking just to be in the same room with the guy. The readings, however, are unnecessarily long, and international relations theory sometimes has painfully little to do with practical events. But Katzenstein is truly an amazing professor. OK class, brilliant mind. Expect a B / B + with an average amount of work put in.
So much reading it was difficult to keep up. The lectures were interesting, but the tests are based off of your ability to memorize over a thousand pages of reading.
Tough class, difficult readings, brilliant professor

This is a very difficult class, although amazing in terms of how much you learn. The readings can be extremely overwhelming. Katzenstein himself stated at the end of the course that it was by far one of the hardest classes an undergraduate could take at Cornell. Save this amazing course for junior/senior year.

I loved this class! Professor Katzenstein is truly an expert in the field of international relations, and he is an amazing lecturer. The TAs are also very helpful. It is a difficult, and there are a lot of readings, but it is worth all the work. Just study super hard for the final!
Amazing professor. Interesting lectures. Difficult class and lots of reading, but it is worth it. Take this class.
GOVT 1817 is an amazing class.  If you take this class and really pay attention, you will not regret it.  Katzenstein is simply one of the brightest minds in International Relations.

Professor Katzenstein is an amazing professor. He is an expert in his field, and a great lecturer.  I sincerely enjoyed going to his class.  Yes, the material is tough and there is a lot of work, but the TAs are very helpful and knowledgeable. Professor Katzenstein challenges his students immensely, but you will learn a lot.

KATZENSTEIN IS THE MAN!!! This class is very difficult, but worth it. Even if you don't do extremely well, the material is fascinating (and I am not a Govt/ILR major). Tons of dense readings, but mainly INCREDIBLE TAs that help immensely dissecting them. Go to office hours. Study hard for the brutal final. This class is WORTH IT

One of the few professors I have had who takes the teaching part of his profession seriously. He expects a lot of reading, but the work load is completely worth it. He is extremely smart, a great lecturer who has perfected teaching this subject at the introductory level. High emphasis on critical thinking.
The discussions were really interesting but the lectures were always boring by the end because he was just talking (albeit about interesting topics) for an hour and a half straight
best IR professor, his class is intensive but the TA (nicole) made it clear. this class is less difficult than labor law with gold.
Hardest class I've ever taken at Cornell with the hardest prof, but the material I learned was all worth it... even the decrease in my GPA.

A great prof.  I was lucky enough to take his Senior Govt. Major Seminar and it was a real challenge but being in such an intimate setting really helped us think on a higher level, one fit for an Ivy League school.  He was rude with his comments via e-mail, and the workload was a challenge, but i'm glad I took his class.  He is an expert.

The readings are extremely hard. Katz is very interesting, but he can be confusing. He is unavailable out of class, and a lot of what you get from his classes depends on the TAs, who will practically determine your grade/whether you understand the readings. Lecture is for your interest, not the tests - which are totally based on the readings.

Insanely difficult, but no other class will measure up.  Tons of reading, you need a study group, but Katzenstein is such a good professor that you show up for lecture 10 minutes early.  Changes your whole perspective on the world.  Get to know your TA's preferences because they grade the essays and care about different things.
Hard class, grades not very fair

Though called an 'Introductory Class' this is by no means introductory. Katzenstein said so himself in his final lecture. This is the most amount of work I have ever had to do for a single class. Expect A LOT of readings, and expect them to be very hard. Katzenstein knows his material very well, but his lectures are not straightforward. VERY HARD.

There's no question that this class is a lot of work.  Nonetheless, Katzenstein does an amazing job teaching the material, and the class is well worth taking.  It is possibly the most eye-opening class I have ever taken.  It really gives you a whole new perspective on world events.
god-like. that's all i have to say about that.

absolutely brilliant. i can't stress enough HOW interesting this class is and how much of my hero prof katzenstein has become. no doubt it's very very tough, the readings are insanely intense and large in number, but it's worth it. this guy is unbelievable. TAKE HIS CLASS.

This class is a bit of a shock. There is an unmanagable amount of readings (which I still mangaged to complete before, but now have a study group for). It is, however a very interesting and informative class. Professor Katzenstein is one of the most brilliant professors at Cornell and is highly regarded in the government field.

Interesting lecturer, going at a comfortable pace; interacts with students. Spends beginning of each lecture going over current events and emails from students. Knows his subject well; one of the best in field. Readings fairly interesting, though WAY too much for 3 credits. Concepts learnt, though, will last you well beyond this class.

One of the hardest classes i've taken, but also the most interesting. He's a brilliant teacher who really knows the material and makes an hour+ lecture very interesting. The only thing that took away from his class was the horrible section. However, a good TA would only help improve his class bc the material can be very difficult. I RECOMMEND IT

TAKE THIS CLASS! It's a difficult course (lots of reading, abstract/theoretical concepts) but Katzenstein is a brilliant, engaging lecturer, and actually not that difficult to follow. Absolutely worth the work. Best class I've taken at Cornell by far.

An incredible lecturer.  I looked forward to his lectures, he knows a lot and makes the information interesting and accessible.  That said, it is a very hard class with a lot of reading, but it is all worth it.

He is usually a funny engaging prof. Yet, the amount of reading given was extreme. I have not seen more reading in 300-level government classes here that are even in the same field. He is an expert in IR, unfortunately his brilliance does not shine through in this intro-level course. Try one of his upper-level courses if you really want to take him
Great guy, fun lectures, but often confusing. The reading were good, but there were far too many for a 100 level class.
Take this class! Very hard and lots of reading (all on the exams) but SO worth it. Katzenstein is an amazing intellectual and professor at the top of his field.  He's my hero!

Best class ever- not easy, a lot of reading... but very interesting... almost nothing on the exams are from lecture- but it's worth it to show up, to do the readings, etc. Very relevant. The prof really connects otherwise abstract material to what is going on in the world.
Take this class... it will make you think hard, a lot of reading, but gives a new perspective on the world.  Especially important for this era we're in.
He was ranked by the economist as the most influential scholar in international political economy. His lectures are great, but you have to come prepared. Not an easy class

best class at Cornell. DO the readings. you cheat yourself if you don't. there is a lot to read but unlike other gov classes, this is all great. his lectures are extremely informative. he's also a genius. this is a MUST take. clear your schedule. this class taught me how the world really works.
Interesting, but had trouble staying awake during lecture.  Also, A LOT of reading.

Without a doubt, the best class I have taken at Cornell -- and also the hardest.  Seek out the TA's for help, and be sure to do most of the readings at some point.  In all honesty, this is the type of class makes Cornell a legitimate Ivy League school.  He expects a lot, but you'll learn so much about the world and be forever grateful you took 354.

He's very smart and has a lot of knowledge. Can be arrogant, but overall a nice guy (read lyrics of Sunscreen song on last day of class). A ton of reading, much of which you have to do. Exams are comprehensive and to do well you have to prepare far in advance. Also some basic economics knowledge is helpful for this course, though not necessary.
An amazing professor.  Katzenstein is brilliant and funny.  He's the best professor I've ever had and thanks to him I'm now a government major.  Be prepared to work a lot, but it'll pay off.
Lecture notes are a bit confusing but the man is a genius.

Best class I have ever taken.  Seriously.  Also perhaps the hardest class I've ever taken, but it's well worth it.  Katzenstein is absolutely amazing and now I'm gonna have to take every class he teaches.

If you have come to Cornell to learn how to think clearly and sharpen your mind, then don't waste your time on **** easy courses.  This course is life-changing and it is rare to find such a gem.  I hate to end on a cliche, but nothing really good comes without hard work.
He is one of the most pointless convolluted teachers I've ever had, what a waste of time
almost 2000pages of readings!  readings have no correlation to the lectures, though lectures are interesting.  he is very liberal.

Its a real shame this guy's not teaching this semester. Really smart and ties themes to current events very well. Class is not easy, lots of reading, but you can manage. Sometimes puts very personal, liberal opinions into lectures.
One of the most intelligent people I've ever met. Extremely friendly and helpful. A fantastic teacher.
nice man. bad lecturer.

Professor Katzenstein's grasp on political economy is amazing.  He is intelligent, articulate, and a great lecturer.  He adds current events into the class, making comprehension of the material very simple.  It's not a cakewalk, but not too hard either.

At risk of hyperbole, I'll just say he's the best professor I've had. period. His IR seminar is four hours at a stretch, and the class just never drags. What a fascinating mind, and as available as anyone would ever need outside of class. He is a gift.
Great Prof!  But it's a hard intro class.  He is one of the most brilliant professors you'll find at Cornell.  Make sure your in a good section that will help you handle all the reading.

Interesting course.  Nice teacher who listens to students.  Not always clear how the lectures tie in with the readings.  Never-ending reading. Still, good class.  Learned a lot.  Nice teacher--really knows his stuff--almost intimidating.

Goes well with the course, he knows his stuff. He, however, continuously bashes America too much. We understand he's a citizen now, but that does not mean he should force his negative personal views of America on his students. Overall, though, not bad.

Absolutely brilliant professor. You can't miss a course with him if you have any interest in Politics. The course is hard: lotsa reading. But you'll find him quoted on your readings! He's very knowleadgable.
Accent kinda rocks, even though it makes him harder to understand
Very interesting lectures. Great class

This is def. one of the best courses I've taken. The reading load is close to crazy but they're discussed in section so I wouldn't worry about it. The exams are not difficult and the lecture is very enjoyable!
Great professor... Great Guy... Great Lecturer.. Funny...and Hot as hell   If you do the readings (there is alot), the class is easy

This was probably the best class I ever took at Cornell. He is an amazing lecturer and absolutely brilliant. There's no doubt that it's tough, but you don't have to do absolutely all of the reading (as with any government class).
Lectures and course material are really interesting, but be prepared to read more than you probably will in most 300 and 400 classes.
This was the first government class that I took at Cornell.  He's a great lecturer but the amount of reading for the course was ridiculous.  Make him do the Terminator voice
Far too much reading for a 300 level course.  Interesting topic, however overt liberal bias evident in some lectures.
He is my dad so like he is the best and everyone who said 1 star is lying and failed the class

Honestly, Pepinsky is pretty rude towards his students. I felt it was highly inappropriate when he screamed at students in front of a large lecture hall. (Stop taking my reviews down Pepinsky)
Class was not hard, did well. Just many better government teachers who are far more engaging and kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pepinsky is the goat, and this was probably my favorite class taken so far. Lectures are very engaging and well structured, and the content is interesting. You can easily tell Pepinsky loves what he teaches and is very welcoming in class and office hours. A lot of readings but not any more than most other govt classes. Highly recommend :)

Professor Pepinsky is an excellent lecturer, and one of the best in the government department here at Cornell. His lectures are clear and organized, focusing on a particular theme or subject. Just be aware that he doesn't post his lecture slides on Canvas. Exams are fair, and students are allowed to bring a cheat sheet the size of an index card.

GOVT 3443 is not an "easy" class to put on your schedule. It covers a lot of content and comes down to basically two prelims and a final paper. Attendance is "not mandatory," but slides are not posted, so if you don't show up you will not do good in this class. If you find this topic interesting, go for it. It's fun, deep, and very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgable about his area of expertise

Professor Pepinsky clearly cares about the subject and ensuring that his students succeed. VERY knowledgeable. Fair warning, he is extremely lecture-heavy, and slides are not posted after class. Though attendance is not required, it is necessary if you want an A range grade. Lecture, reading, and section material are all fair game on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. Professor is rude and inconsiderate of his students. Felt like he had a superiority complex over Cornell kids because he went to Harvard. No text on the slides and refused to post them online- hard to take notes. And then exam content was solely based on lecture. Overall lectures were extremely boring and hard to follow.

Lectures can be pretty boring, but definitely do attend them because there are no online versions. He's pretty funny and has a great personality though. Tests aren't that bad, just review well, especially focus on lectures in my opinion. Haven't gone to office hours, but he seems like he really cares about his students. Good personality and nice.

Lectures matter quite a bit. They can be difficult to understand or boring because of the content, but Pepinsky makes things as clear as possible, and has great energy. Maybe my favorite lecturer I've had at Cornell.

Prof. Pepinsky is a great lecturer, he is clearly very passionate about the subject and is very prepared and organized for his lecture. He also knows a great deal about SE Asia. I also like how he deliberately gives examples from all parts of the world for concepts.

Though, his grading is really tough, and the readings can be overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Essays graded too heavily

Professor Pepinsky is amazing! Even as a STEM major, I found the material super engaging. Attendance is not mandatory but you HAVE to show up. Prelim and final MCQs are 98% lecture-based. The two papers are easy and your TA grades them. Cons are the heavy reading (60 pgs/week) and little grade flexibility (missing one check-in can tank your grade).

Difficult tests that make it impossible to come back from a single mediocre score and lectures that you have to fight to stay awake for. Very little content is even covered in the mandatory lectures and most of the interesting material is in the readings.
an extremely boring class

Pepinsky as a lecturer is near perfect. He is incredibly knowledgable, doesn't go off on tangents (too often at least), and passionate. Also, I'm leaving the class feeling like I learned lots. Grades depend on TAs and try to follow formats asked. You'll be graded harshly. Make sure to come to class every time or have a friend who takes great notes.

Professor Pepsinky is great professor and probably the best I've had at Cornell. The class is not easy, but it is very fair and rewarding to people who show up to class and put in effort. Great lecture style and he is very engaging, I never got bored in class. Highly recommend
very hard dont take

Before Pepinsky, GOVT 1313 was supposed to be an incredibly easy introductory class for the major. Now it's quite difficult, tests/papers graded harshly, dense lectures(if you miss lecture it is near impossible to make up the material). That being said, Pepinsky himself is a great lecturer/professor. But take any other required intro GOVT class.

Professor Pepinsky is AWESOME. I learned a ton about Southeast Asia despite being from there myself, and even with the abundance of information I still felt like I had agency in forming my own thoughts. I looked forward to every lecture despite them being held during sleepy afternoons because they are that good, and I'm not even a government major!

The two classes I've done with Pepinsky are hands-down the best I've taken at Cornell over three years. He is so superb that his recalcitrance to give flat A's can and should be overlooked. Clearly one of the best Profs at Cornell and I would sign up for any class he teaches, regardless of subject. He is that good.
Probably one of the best professors at Cornell. He is very knowledgeable and makes the classes very interesting and clear. This is one of the classes where Ive learned the most, would take it again!

Lectures can get heavy on history, but are always relevant as knowledge to use to analyse political situations. There is a strong emphasis on comparative method and he sells the class well to people uninterested in Southeast Asia. Does a great job at being neutral during lecture.

The professor is smart and approachable. He apparently knows his stuff very well and tries to involve students in discussions during lectures. But overall it is a hard class especially if you do not have an economic background.

Recommended: take Intro Micro before taking this class - it will make the more technical readings in this class a lot more clear, but Prof Pepinsky does a great job of walking you through the most important takeaway points. A great lecturer, and brilliant mind.

Class was Politics and Markets. Good professor, can come off a bit full of himself but not in a terrible way. Definitely will learn a lot. Does not ever post lecture slides so basically have to attend class.
One of the best lecturers I've had. Interesting and clear. But a hard class...

He's a very good lecturer.  Even for people who have no general knowledge about Southeast Asia, this class is still exciting and interesting.  Definitely take his class!  As for grading - I believe it was rather fair.  But then again, I took this class in 09.

Great professor who is very willing to help students and improve the class experience. Class discussions are always interesting. Workload is definitely managable. Very reasonable grader-ask him for advice if necessary, he is very approachable. You will learn a lot from this class!

Very clear and easy to follow. Leads interesting classes. He's very into Southeast Asia and Economics, so even though you don't need to have any background, its good to know some stuff on economics. If you don't, it'll be a little tougher, but he explains things very well, and you'll be able to follow. If you do the work, you'll do well.
Pepinsky knows and loves Southeast Asia. Lectures were organized and interesting, and assignments were straightforward and fair. A bit of a hard grader, but study and you can do fine.

Very good chalkboard lectures for class, very dry content. Worst part of class is group homework and group final project -- if you get a bad group / group member that just does not want to meet, its hard to learn the content. Learn by working with friends, group with them if possible. He does not know Python, but has great theoretical knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Diamessis is great. No matter how challenging or coding‑heavy the class can feel at the time, the ideas will only become more relevant. Definitely go to class and participate!

diamessis is a great guy once you get to talk to him, this class can be difficult and I understand why he might get a bad rep, but if you put even an ounce of effort to talking to him about needing help with the class he will help you!

I don't know what happened last year, but he literally implies he could give extra credit in return of a good review. I think he needs to focus on the quality of his course rather than finding a way around.

Very funny guy. Gives off the energy of the basketball coach who's forced to teach a class, except he's actually a decent lecturer and not actually a basketball coach. The psets are pretty long and require a solid background in coding. Idk why last years class resented him so much. People generally seemed to like him and the class this year

In most cases, Prof. Diamessis gives you a feeling that he just learnt the material a night before the lecture but not fully understood. Overall, the lack of quality in his class makes you question both his knowledge of the subject and intellectual rigor.

Prof Diamessis is a great guy and is very accommodating towards his students. However, his lectures are very difficult to follow. Psets/ Final project were difficult and TAs were unable to answer many questions in office hours, leaving students even more lost. Exams were doable but grading was extremelyyyyyy harsh on all assignments.

Prof D is a great person, but a terrible professor. He struggles to break down concepts to an understandable level, does not post lecture resources, has difficulties answering student questions, and never works through example problems. Worst of all, his TAs often don't understand the content and thus prelims and finals are graded SUBJECTIVELY.

He chooses his course time for a slot that is honestly waay too early, you'll notice that fewer students show up as a result. Problem set every week but assigned for teams of two, which makes things a little easier. Nice guy, though sometimes a little jumbled. Receives and utilizes student feedback effectively.

Probably the most down-to-earth, friendly professor I've had. Extremely helpful, responsive and pragmatic. Good with posting notes, homework, and practice exams that are relevant so missing class isn't a huge problem. He is the kind of guy you want to sit down and have a beer with.
Cool guy. Know his stuff and helps and cares his students at all times. Lots of coding for homework, but some are very conceptual as well. Exams are hard, but grading is fair.
not understanding at all, very abrasive

He doesn't teach the class. Loved the guest lectures but if he's gonna have prelims in this class, they need to be based off guest lectures, not an external reading that makes no sense. Grading is so vague. Got a 60 on the first prelim and 80 on the 2nd one. This class should go back to being pass/fail. Students skipped anyway and chatted prelim.

He is a pretty nice. Quizzes after every class can be rough at the beginning. The guest speakers are interesting, and there is barely HW. There are 2 time-consuming prelims, and quite a lot of reading & understanding for prelim prep. He's a fast email replier. Harsh grading, the final project brought my grade from A to B.
This is the first time I've been motivated enough to write a review on a professor. Harsh grader, barely teaches, drove the whole freshman class insane. Just make sure you glaze him.

Preszler believes in learning through guest speakers who share experiences in the business world. The course is centered on the UN Sustainable Development Goals and wicked problems, forcing critical thinking about complex, real-world challenges. Prelims are based on out-of-class readings, and short quizzes follow each guest speaker for engagement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bad professor, harsh grading and very unclear grading criteria. Professor does not teach himself, and relies solely on guest lectures. Prelims are based on material not covered during lectures. Reviews are accurate.

Professor is a narsacist. Very hypocritical when it comes to grading. Most people chatted his prelims. Does not curve at all. Final reflection assignments matters a ton (took me from an A to a B). This class should go back to being S/U.
Not good AT ALL. Intentionally grades harshly to get the class median grade down. Good luck all freshmen who have him.
Bald man. Bad man. Hurt my grade man. Bad tests man. Bad grading man.
He doesn't teach. Prelims were on material never covered in class. Harsh grader. No remorse.

Let me put in caveperson speak so clear. Much read. Professor talk many word, say nothing. Sassy. Condescending. Self-center. Grade tough for fun. TA ridiculous. Guest speaker come. Professor no care. Me no care. Give test on thing never teach. Exam long. Time short. Me still confused. Me learn by self. Professor bald. That all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Preszler is a professor who thinks his class is more important than anything else in your life. He heavily picks favorites, gives little grading criteria then grades extremely harshly without giving a rubric back, and his prelims are hard for no reason (and he doesn't teach you the content in class). He makes me want to go into investment banking
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very dependent on exams. Prelims are based off reading that is outside of the class. Tough grader and purely gives grade based on whether or not he knows who you are.
Worst class. Grades without clear guidelines and a clear curve down. Doesn't even teach as he relies solely on guest speakers.
Subjective grading without clear guidelines in the instructions.

His foundations class is an absolute joke. All Dyson freshmen are required to take this course and he grades way too harshly for someone who doesn't even teach. The class is just guest speakers who come in every class (aside from prelim days).

Professor appears nice. Speakers brought to class are all interesting and unique. Prelims are definitely rough, and readings can be challenging to understand. The small quizzes are difficult, depending on the speaker. The final presentation has strict guidelines, so make sure to meet every expectation.

Very caring person who is passionate about the course. Some guest lectures were more on the boring side but most were great. The prelims aren't too bad as long as you're a decent writer. The final presentation is easy and he seemed proud of everyone's work. He's also flexible with any conflicts that athletes or anyone have with the class.

Trent and Lennox taught this when I took it (Fall 2024), though it's changed since. The class had guest speakers (UN SDGs focused), and you could volunteer to host one (join their dinner). Easy course with reflection writing and mandatory attendance. Lectures were boring & people started to skip, so they added Poll Everywhere with location tracker.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The new 1101 is really hard, this was the first year attendance was mandatory. Quiz after each guest speaker, prelims are a little rough unless you study a ton for them. Do the readings ahead of time (but he doesn't assign it til a week before the prelim). He's a nice person but isn't the best teacher I've had.
Preszler is a narcissistic a-hole to some, or a great resource to others. participate and be engaged and you will have the latter relationship.

Preszler is a very nice guy who takes an active interest in student's work and puts a lot of effort into each lecture. For the class you have to write several essays which are graded very harshly and require lots of revision. This class does make you a better writer and you learn a lot, but only take if you have an interest in the subject matter.

Trent is a nice guy, but his Grand Challenges Writing course is incredibly hard. For the love of God, do not take his class. Compared to other grand writing courses, this is so much more work. Please do not do what I did. Save yourself and take another class.
Honestly liked his lectures. The class itself is... well, good luck!

Mr. Perez is an extremely enthusiastic lecturer, and the emotion in his voice makes his teaching powerful and engaging. The class is largely run by the TAs—you are assigned two who oversee your cohort of about 20 students. The course has weekly case studies focused on real-world business problems, all graded with a high level of detail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Genuinely blessed with the TAs I got for this class. The professor himself is very passionate about the topics; however, it is hard to understand him at times because of his thick accent, and his lectures were unorganized. TAs are the backbone of this course, and the final project is heavily weighted, so plan accordingly.

Very TA grading heavy, which can be unfair if they are tough. You should try to participate as much as possible, but most of the time the lectures won't make sense. Try to talk to everyone around you because you'll have a group presentation with them worth a lot of your grade
This class was genuine hell. Learned nothing and had to pull a couple of all nighters.
Generally random and pointless lectures, TAs grade everything (very harshly) but put in the work and you can do fine
Perez is very passionate about the course. Overall not bad, but it really had me stressing near the end. As long as you get a somewhat reasonable TA, then it's all good.
Lectures do not relate to assignments at all. Grade is dependent on if you have a good TA or not. One prelim that is based off everything he's taught. Extremely unorganized.

I really liked Professor Perez, he's great and funny. However, his lectures tend to be a bit boring and the class is very homework heavy. There are case studies every week and by the end of the course there are two every week. Grades are dependent on TAs and participation is pretty important. Good experience, but would I take the class again? No.

Pedro is obviously a Dyson rite of passage, and it's fun to meme this class, but it's honestly just annoying. Mandatory lectures consist of nothing of importance, and the case studies are dependent on whether you can figure out how your TA wants you to write. It could have been way worse, but I'm so happy this course is over.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The professor himself is nice, but basically he isn't involved in the class whatsoever other than giving lectures where he rambles on about nothing really. The biggest problem with this class is the grading system, where your entire grade rests on the TAs. The final project is horrible—TAs said we could try regrade but then brought the grade down.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was the worst class I've ever taken. Prof. Perez is actually great, but it's the class itself that's awful. So much work and you don't learn anything. Very anxiety inducing and get prepared to give a high stakes presentation in front of 100 people. Everyone tunes out during the lectures because they don't matter but then we get sm hw.
not good. unfortunately mandatory. professor is quite disrespectful
TA's grade everything so it's not very standardized as a result. Either suck up or fail.

Course is subject to your luck in landing good TAs. TAs grade everything! Case presentation will be traumatizing for some. Case studies will make you crash out weekly. The professor rambles. Final project will make or break your grade. Prelim is just memorization with a few areas of application. Attendance and participation are tracked constantly.

Grade is soley based on your TAs. Lectures are just yap. Prelim isn't too long but just memorization. You get little instruction on how to complete assignments so you're kinda on ur own. Final project boosts your grade from the case studies so just work with your group to get it done and follow the instructions on the website to a tee and ur good.

The professor is nice, however, the lectures are just him rambling and barely has connection to the content. The prelim is purely memorization based. The weekly case studies are really heavy workload with tough grading, and there is no clear criteria. Weekly office hours are basically mandatory, and attendance is really strict for presentation days

Pedro's lectures are very entertaining and dramatic! The class has lots of case studies, and you'll be assigned to a group with two TAs who grade your work. Grading on the case study write-ups is tough. There is 1 prelim & 1 final. Overall, it's a hard but required course, and in hindsight I really enjoyed taking it with my whole freshman class!

Took this as a required course, terrible. Reviewers are accurate: lectures are just him rambling and is not content based at all. For the case studies, you need to go to OH. How the class is for you depends solely on the TA's you're assigned.

Going to office hours outside of normal class time is mandatory. In class lectures have little no to relation to the homework, which is long and tedious. Very vague and unclear instructions, but very harshly graded up to TA's discression. Very unclear explanations of all assignments. Very passionate but rambling lectures.

Super passionate lectures about NOTHING. You will not learn anything in this course. He just rambles on with no direction, and asks the most nonsensical questions during discussions. No idea why this class even exists. Waste of time

The class is ridiculous. Title business management and organization yet the class is anything but well organized. The professor rambles on with zero intention and the classroom is full of students distracted by anything else. The cases are a ridiculous assignment that you have to learn exactly how to write. No clue why this is a mandatory course.

Honestly, Pedro didn't do much in this class other than ramble. He was entertaining, but his lectures are not something you actually have to listen to in order to do well in the class. Just figure out the framework for the case studies and study before the prelim, and stay on top of the final project. You should be absolutely fine/

Pedro is just Pedro. Arbitrary grading by TA's was a common complaint, but I can't say I had that experience. TA's basically run the course, so get to know your TA and go to their office hours each week and participate. Make a good relationship with them because your grade is in their hands. Pedro makes some simple topics quite difficult to grasp.

No set grading rubric, which is a nightmare for weekly case studies. Professor often has oddly specific requirements that are not mentioned anywhere. The only prelim was based on pure memorization and focused on topics that have little to no application outside of the class. Do not recommend, but it is a required course nonetheless so best of luck

Inane class material and case studies, terrible professor, and genuinely one of the worst academic experiences I've ever had. Assignment instructions are purposefully vague, and attendance at OUT-OF-CLASS office hours is mandatory for participation credit. Expect arbitrary grading, rambling lectures, and over-intellectualization of easy topics.

The class is engaging, but the heavy workload and inconsistent TA grading can be a challenge. Utilize Unstuck AI, office hours, and the textbook to stay on top of the material. With effort, you can succeed in this class.

As previously mentioned, this class is based entirely on your luck with TA grading. Prof seemed nice and got us all to think critically. I had 8 assignments that weren't graded and my Final project was graded entirely incorrectly (which the head TA confirmed) and this was not rectified. Prof ignored my emails when I asked about grading

I thought Pedro's lectures were extremely interesting and that he was a fun professor. The class overall is not that difficult once you understand the concepts and most people get As. Definitely meet with your TAs and you should be fine. Also make sure to participate in the class because Pedro does have the final say for grades.

Absolutely loved this professor. Very interesting class and he was amazing. However, it's important to say that the class is mostly led by TA's with the grading. I personally did not like that because my TA was a very harsh grader, but that's just my opinion and the only disadvantage of the class.

Perez is sharp, but the class teaches little of substance. 85% of your grade is in the hands of someone your age who took the course the year before and grading is incredibly arbitrary. The TAs are notoriously unprepared, with the requirements for cases often changing the night they are due. That being said, work hard and you will do well.

Professor is nice; the course layout is egregious. Be prepared to:
1) Attend 2+ office hours with confused TAs since the assignments aren't explained well
2) Get outline of the final project 2 days before it's due (25% of the final grade)
3) Experience different grading rubrics based on the TA
4) Look over 350+ slides for a prelim without direction

At least one case study due a week that got more difficult as the semester progressed. Most of the lectures consisted of him writing something obvious on the board, like "the goal of a business is to make profit" then run around the room and jump up and down. Lectures had 40 slides with entire essays on each slide, which would all be on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably going to be a little hard at first but once you get the hang of it, it's pretty okay. Just have to write papers every week, and 2 quizzes that were lecture-based weren't entirely too bad.

I personally loved this class. My biggest advice is go to office hours and get to know your TAs (they do most of the grading)! Final project is a bit long and the prelims are kinda random but just listen in lecture. The case studies are fun if you do them on time. Love Pedro!

I love the guy's energy, but this class is not it. The workload was heavy, and grading between TAs was inconsistent (that is, if your TA graded at all). The previous years had a curve, but this year's head TA decided not to have one. You have to pull off a miracle to get an A if your head TA decides not to curve grades and your TA is a harsh grader

Many complain about Professor Perez because many people in Dyson prefer classes where they can learn math, take an exam, and keep it pushing. AEM 2200 is the opposite of that. If you are a reader and writer, you are literally fine. This class is UNDOUBTEDLY a biggg learning curve, but what you learn helps you for the rest of your Dyson career.

It is way too much work for a class that is this useless. Lectures are unnecessary, but some TAs take attendance. The only good thing about this course is the friendships you make through the communal suffering on Tuesday nights. Besides that, this class completely fulfilled the Dyson stereotype of easy and stupid classes. Total waste of time.
The course appears to be structured but every single aspect of the class is subjective. Vague cases, terrible TAs, pointless lectures that you need to attend for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: unnecessarily difficult class with pointless lectures and annoying case studies. pedro gives very little direction for assignments yet has insane, particular expectations. be prepared to get a ton of points off for things that nobody told you was wrong. he is also pretty rude, he abruptly cut off an entire group's case study for going overtime

Even though there are downsides, Pedro truly cares about his students. His lectures do not affect your grade, but it is beneficial information. If you want to succeed in this class, go to TA Hours and go to class.
Borderline useless class with a ton of busy work. Grading gets easier as semester goes on, but largely evaluated by TAs
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The worst academic experience of my life. Notorious for being the dumbest class in Dyson. Insane amount of work. Completely useless lectures that are irrelevant to the assignments. Grading is completely dependent on TAs who often take off points for the most arbitrary reasons. The Professor passionately blabbers on and on about random topics.

Horrible in every way possible. Truly the worst academic experience in my entire life. There is no content in this class. Lectures are a complete waste of time. Case studies are braindead. The course is so bad it is hard to even believe that this is a course offered at Cornell. If I could give a rating of 0 out of 10 I would.

Literally does nothing for this class except lectures that have nothing to do with the course material. Just goes on long tangents about random topics. TAs do all the grading and your grade is highly dependent on their judgement. Tedious weekly essays that take up so much time and don't help at all. Final project is always a mess - good luck :(

Perez is nice, enthusiastic, and knowledgeable. That being said, the class is terrible. Lectures were basically pointless if you did not have to present a case and there were roughly 2 cases due every week. There were also many pointless modules and grades were not given back until months after the assignment was submitted.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Oh Pedro. Great guy, clearly very smart and caring, but this class is a bit of a mess. You'll never get grades back, and there are a LOT of case studies. Lot of work with little feedback, little knowledge on how to improve your work, really only learned about how to write up a case. Perez really cares about his students though a bit scatterbrained.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Disorganized & a lack of communication. Expect to complete around two case studies per week as well as some unrelated modules without any feedback (all case studies I completed September-November were not graded until the end of December). Large final group project. I recommend you befriend your TA because they are the people who grade everything.

If you want a good grade for this class, try to get on your TA's good side instead of the professor. Go to as many office hours (especially your TA's) for the case studies as possible and you are sure to get something in the A range. The class is very easy if you come in with some background knowledge in finance.

Heavy workload. And I just don't understand the optional final policy. You got your expected grade four days prior to the exam, and you have to make an instant decision whether to take the exam or not (and study for it). It just adds too much burden to students. Plus it is extremely unfair for students who already have travel plans.

He should go teaching electrical engineering since he can't stop talking about it. This class made my worst cornell experience so far. Didn't really learn anything from those time-consuming cases and superficial lectures which he tried to make them seem deep.

Terrible, really terrible. Basically you learn nothing. And he TAKES ATTENDANCE, 2 points, 1 for attendance and another for paying attention. Your grade on this class, to a great extent, depends on what kinda TA you are assigned to. So basically, your luck counts a lot if you want to get a good grade.
Great teacher. We had to write a lot, but you get used to it.

If you are not a hard worker, you will not perform well in the course. There are a ton of cases, and they actually are pretty intellectually challenging. Perez himself is incredibly smart, but you really have to attentively listen to him to understand the depth of his lectures. I highly recommend participating as much as you can in this course.

The weekly cases (sometimes 2 or 3 a week) can make the class seem so long. Study the previous lecture for the quizzes. Lecture heavy. The final group presentation project isnt bad, just have to have an understanding of the case. Not a bad class overall, can be on your laptop.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: At the end of the semester, he even refused to tell you your overall score, such as participation grade. Even though he taught nothing in class, he is a very tough grader, and cares nothing about the students' feeling. This is the worst experience that I have ever had in Cornell. Cornell really should find another prof.

Professor Perez radiates passion and vigour. He inspires his students to think analytically about business cases. He entertains as well as teaches, and often jumps vigorously on and off tables in a melodramatic fashion. One learns a lot from his classes. A great professor but one who may not always give his undivided attention to his students.

Prof. Perez enjoys what he lectures and tries to make seemingly-superficial material relevant. The course was somewhat disorganized, but Perez was very accommodating. As long as you do all the work, the class should be fine.
Took this class on a Friday afternoon for about 2 hours. Fantastic discussions regarding ethics and a bit of philosophy with interesting cases. Graded on reflections which are fairly short.

The majority of my work that semester was from his class (case studies and 2 large projects). The quizzes were literally impossible, and reading the chapters they were supposedly based on didn't help. However I  managed to get an A in the class so looking back I'm okay with it. Take advantage of all extra credit and try to participate in class.
You do not really learn that much in lecture, and the quizzes in class can be tough, but overall everyone does well and it is a great first business class at the Dyson School.

One legit question on a quiz he gave us is "Is quality expensive?" (Answer was somehow 'false') Studying for the many tests is almost useless since he will ask the most arbitrary irrelevant questions just to make sure no one gets 100. He's pretty passionate/animated about his subject, but it gets in the way of letting the lectures be clear.
Smart guy but very unclear in what he expects for assignments.

Overall a fine class, but the information presented is utterly irrelevant. My biggest and probably only problem with this class is that he doesn't tell you what he wants and relies too much on the TA's who don't really help at all. But bottom line, as long as you show up you're pretty much guaranteed a B.

Pedro's class is not very straightforward in terms of his expectations or material that is covered. That being said, I did poorly on my prelims, but still ended up with a good grade because I went to class and got all of the extra credit opportunities. Not a great class experience while you're in it but you will be surprised with your grade

Pedro is a a below average professor. His lectures are incoherent, and the class provides you with such minimal information about different areas of business that I left each class without having learned much. His teaching assistants grade unfairly at times and are not the nicest people. I was not impressed or happy with this class or professor.
easy A+ as it is

Get an easier TA! Quizzes are often a surprise, mostly based off of power points, that at times doesn't make complete sense. Participation is needed but pointless as the same idiotic loud students take over the discussions.

The quizzes were, at times, very arbitrary. Perez lacks organization in his lectures at times. The TA grading is subjective and Perez often has mood swings. He is a nice guy though; he will answer questions after class. This class requires a significant time commitment. Make sure to spend a lot of time on the final project.
Horribly confusing tests, useless class, a complete waste of time. Do not take AEM 1200 unless you have to.
Can't stand him

He is extremely passionate about his subject.  His quizzes are fairly difficult, especially if you don't read the textbook.  Also, TA grading can be fairly subjective.  I highly recommend going to TA office hours to talk about cases.  Overall a great and informative class!  Pedro knows a lot and is willing to share if you speak with him.
Terrible tests... super easy with awfully unfair grading.
Great class, workload is very manageable and Perez is a great guy. Highly reccomended!

You never know what you'll get with Perez.  He's polite, intelligent and focused on exposing students to important topics in business.  However, he's also vague, does not explain grade criteria and sometimes does not even appear sure of what he expects.  TA-heavy grading contributes to this.

Mostly, the class is not too hard if you do the work. The material of quizes at times is not what is assigned, but reading the chapter reviews is very helpful. FInal project grades are usually universally very low which brings everyone's grades down.

epitome of wildcard. You never know what you will get with professor Perez. Overall a great guy, but is very hard to understand. You have no idea how you will be graded or what is composed of the grade. Still, its worth having a class with Perez! Awesome Guy!

Took AEM 1200 in the spring (for non AEM majors). Class material was pretty interesting, but, Perez covered everything pretty quickly - for the sake of the exam rather than teaching. Tests were not challenging but the questions were unclear - most were not covered in class and the textbook. We never even received the correct answers before the fina

One of Cornell's best.  He may come off as a stickler only because he expects a manageable amount of respect that unfortunately very little students have.  I suggest taking AEM 1200 strongly, he is an excellent guy.
Pretty boring class, pretty easy though. In the spring he gives practice questions on-line. All the material for the 5 in class tests is on them. Do the on-line questions and you'll do well
I love this man.

Perez is definitely one of the most humorous and knowledgeable people around, but his quizzes' questions can be quite vague and unexpected sometimes. The lectures and books (to a small extent) are helpful, but a good TA helps a lot, especially with cases. Oh, and do participate in class, that'll help any grade a lot at the end of the course...
Pedro is a very interesting and entertaining lecturer. However, his final exam is difficult. He does offer extra credit, which offsets it.

Noticeable Spanish accent (humor value?), too much material to cover in a class. Confusing sometimes, explanations are interesting but not useful for the tests. No homework at least until the final project (~50 hours of group work). Ridiculously confusing & difficult tests even with canceled questions. The extra credit is useful and even necessary.

He is a better professor than people are giving credit for.  Yeah, some of his questions on the tests are ridiculous, but he manages to keep the class' attention.  He actually purposely raised the classes grade by the end, and the average grade was a 86 which is acceptable.

He is probably the worst professor at Cornell. It is ridiculous how the median grade for spring 2010 is hovering around B- range. Even after reading every chapter and taking detailed notes, his tests are biased. Spare yourself the $200+ for textbooks, because the course isn't worth it. And this is coming from an econ major with straight A's.

Pedro knows his stuff but his tests are hit or miss. It is the questions not the material that are challenging. Not helpful with explaining material. Don't even buy the book. Your best move is taking this soph/ jr year after you know the material. He expects you to know the material as well as if you took accting/mkting. Got an A but bad class

The class was a good class. We had two textbooks but the contents overlapped a lot so it was like reading the same stuff twice. The workload was sometimes overwhelming, especially the final project. He gives extra credit and he is very nice. His quizzes are sometime vague but the cases were fun even though some took a lot of time to do.

just want to point out to the poster below me that the average of last spring WAS a B... and this is directly out of the cornell registrar... if you want to be condescending, at least do YOUR research beforehand. I guess it's true then, Perez does seem unlucky in that he keeps on getting such students.
Useless class.  Didnt learn a thing.  As long as you read the simple lists in the textbook you will do fine on the test.  No true knowledge of anything business is actually applied to tests.

Pedro definitely needs help when it comes to teaching (even more so, his TAs which seem to come from the same frat or sorority). However, I often felt bad for him because he tends to get the worst students. Even the ones who post here denote a truly sad inability to do basic research... DIRECTLY FROM THE REGISTRAR'S OFFICE: AEM 1200 MEDIAN: B+.

This is not a good class. He has a tendency to spontaneously freak out. He puts crap on the exams that came from nowhere. He just copies the book onto powerpoints and reads them to the class. I thought I would like this class and was very wrong. It was not an easy A, even though I did all of the extra credit.
don't take it unless you have to. not hard to get an A, but you can definitely spend your time somewhere else. this class is.... NOT worth it. i have learned NOTHING!

NOT AN EASY A! He made up a bunch of crap on all his tests - material was never covered in lecture or in books. No way to study for the class OR learn biz! Means for each exam: 79, 77, & 71. Opt project mean = 85. Even w/ lots of extra credit, the mean grade is B-/B (not curved). FOR AN INTRO AEM CLASS THIS IS RIDICULOUS! coming from a bio major.

One of the worst profs at Cornell. His lecturers are extremely opinionated and his tests are just stupid lists that do not help you learn how to manage a business. His teaching is way too theoretical and doesn't apply to the real world. If you want to learn business management, take a Hotel School course; at least those profs have some experience.

Horrendous teacher. Lectures are boring, and he just reads off his poorly made powerpoints. Has no idea how to design a test. Group project takes a  lot of time, but was the only useful experience I got out of the class.  Perez is an arrogant, arbitrary, thinks he knows it all, short little boy who knows NOTHING. Got an A+ in the class though.

Perez is extremely passionate in lectures, which makes class entertaining and lively.  He makes useful points and follows the book closely in lectures.  The only downside to his classes are tests/quizzes are extremely subjective.  I studied the book and attended all lectures, and reviewed my notes and yet tests were frequently dissimilar
