Pedro is not a good professor when it comes to learning in class.  He goes into tangents and does not get through all of his material.  His mannerisms are entertaining but distract you from the material.  Overall it would be an easy class if it wasn't for his subjective tests.  The tests are horribly made and based on his opinions.

This is a relatively easy class, be sure to study the lecture notes and definitions of terms prior to exams- notecards definitely help.  And go to the review sessions, they actually tell you what to study so you don't waste your time reading over everything.  The tests are somewhat arbitrary though, and Pedro is a terrible professor.
hard to understand. can be an okay class, but you have to work for it. exams are somewhat arbitrary
This is one of those classes where you can ship it on a regular basis and still earn a good grade. Or attend it a study for something else.

I agree with the person below me, this class is not too hard. I took this class as an elective, and I can say that it's very easy to get at least an A, and Pedro isn't all too bad. All the complaints you see are probably coming from dumb AEM majors who do zero work, so disregard them.

Everyone complains about Professor Perez, but in reality, the class is 100% memorization.  Getting in the A range is easy if you just memorize all of the random lists on the powerpoint slides (flashcards are a life saver).  Even if you don't like this class and you are not doing well, you will be in love with Professor Perez and his mannerisms

Pedro is not really as bad as everyone makes him out to be.  He tests the material in ways you haven't seen before which can be confusing but there is enough extra credit where, if you put the time in, you can easily get an A. Because the class is so large, if you want help you need to ask for it. But if you ask for it, he's a pretty caring guy.

Take this class if you don't want to learn anything, but want an easy A/A+.People say that his tests are not common sense, because they're not;to ace his tests,you need to study his notes and know his (often supremely illogical) opinions and viewpoints on things.Answer questions on the exams based on what he said in lecture, not based on logic.

Sigh.... what a waste of my time and money. Complete arbitrary lists on test. One of his colleagues said this class was poorly taught and low and behold, it definitely is. Some of his TA's are cool, but some suck, esp J. cancion. She must have chronic TOXIC PMS. There is extra credit & lowest test grade dropped if u do op.project. But again...sigh.

The tests are VERY subjective. The person who said you can have a textbook and still be 70% unsure about the test is SO HONEST. The TAs are really incompetent and do nothing except stand around during lecture. There is extra credit but who wants to run around doing extra credit. The course sucks.

this class is a joke. easy A+ if you are smart enough to go to class and you can write a legible paragraph response to a guest lecturer. 1 view point each week; 1 book report(2-3 pgs); 1 final essay (2-3pgs). if you don't get an A or A+ in the course you shouldn't be at Cornell

take this class if you are good at guessing since the quizzes and tests are extremely random.  the TA's are useless (just like most AEM TA's) and will tell you the wrong answers in the review sessions.  you should probably just buy take note--thats how i got an A after getting C averages on all of the quizzes
Easily the worst professor I have had.  He is an embarrassment to Cornell.

It's a good thing there are many guest lecturers, as Perez does little to capture your attention.  Lectures are uninspired, and Perez abdicates responsibility to the TAs for any problems you may have.  He seems unable to make a decision for himself.  Interesting course topic, bad prof!
Perez is an ok guy, and the material is interesting, but somehow he manages to make it incomprehensible.  The tests are disorganized and arbitrary.

Nice guy! In addition, an embarassment to education, let alone an Ivy League education. I wouldn't let this guy teach fourth grade for fear that the students my develop a habit for drawing pictures on standardized test bubble sheets. If you are are really good at guessing, take this course. If not just watch CNBC for an hour or two.

Pedro's inability to teach is only matched by his personal lack of success in the business field. He will shout very loudly and wave his arms, but then words either do not make sense or are blatantly incorrect. You will do well just memorize the textbook. However, there are bucket loads of extra credits. Tests are irrelevant and largely arbitrary.
Really interesting class! I had a hard time with the accent at first cuz I am not used to it but after a while, I got used to it. He is very lively, passionate and good. I loved this class.
his tests are entirely irrelevant to the material so you cant prepare for it at all.  If it was open book and there was no time limit you would still be unsure abot 75 percent of the questions
Tests are unclear, material is boring.  The only good parts were the guest lecturers and the extra credit opportunities.

Prof Perez is a great guy!  His tests could get into specific details sometimes, but if you got in the 80's on them, you could still get an A in the class based on extra credit and the project.  He's awesome if you ever get to interact with him- definitely make use of the opportunities (like the guest lecture luncheons).  I def recommend the class.

Professor Perez covers the material really well. a whole lot of useful information, and people who kept telling me it was common sense ended up getting a grade in the 70s on the exam. the exams were really are tough. all of the extra credit and doing well on the final earned me an A+. and many people got As with the extra credit.
Given the material the course covers, he does an OK job teaching AEM 220.  But his tests are not very balanced, and your grade is based only on the three tests.  Best to avoid this class if you can.

First off, the person two or three bellow said the average grade was in the 60s - that's not true, his average grades are around 80 on each exam. The exams reflect business situations, which if you haven't prepared for hte exam, you won't understand. He's a great professor, willing to help his students, and he learns people's names! Love the Class!

Hey, what's with all of the Pedro-bashing out there?  This guy is enthusiastic, energetic, and most importantly, he likes working w/ students.  Itook this class b/c nothing else fit into my schedule, but I loved it. You do have to work for your grade, but there are lots of opportunities for extra credit.  Put simply, you get out what you put in.

Pedro was is a good professor but only for this class because you can interact with him on a more one-on-one basis. He doesn't grade anything only the TA's do, so if you have a problem with him it doesn't affect your work. Papers are kind of annoying but the class is required for AEM and he's the only one that teaches it.
I've had four classes with this guy already and more than sick of it. The first two were a mistake and the second two were required. If you can avoid him, I suggest you do so

Don't take this useless course unless you absolutely have to for a prereq.. you will learn nothing useful.  He's a nice guy but he can't teach and his tests are incredibly unfair ( as in the questions make no sense and the answers are all opinion).  The class is an embarrasment to Cornell.

Pedro is a really smart guy but his tests make you hate life. Its not that they're hard... they're really not. Its just that they are so freaking confusing that they'll make you compare fruits to animals (almost literally). I made almost a 100 on one of his tests, and had no idea whether I had done well or not. FYI, the median for that test was 64.

Some harsh words from other students, and I don't know if they are completely warranted.  The tests are tricky (the mid term was at least, not so much the final), but a fair grade is completely attainable if you put forth some effort.  Pedro is a really good guy, and absolutely hilarious.  Take his class, but be prepared to work for your grade.

Perez makes absolutely no sense, & neither do his tests.  This is an example of an actual question: "True or False, is it possible to controll the rate of mental & physical decline that comes with age?"  One would think "True" to be the logical answer, but surprisingly this is not the case.  What are doctors for then? & isn't this an AEM class?

this professor shows absolutely no compassion to his students. his only concern is to make a 2 credit class feel like a 4 credit one. ridiculous statements such as the book is wrong are common occurences in this embarassment to cornell university.
Very unclear teacher. All questions have multiple CORRECT answers but he doesn't know that!

Prof Perez is a great guy and he manages to pull off great dynamics in such large lectures.  He writes tricky exams.  The TAs are really helpful so utilize them.  Overall a great introductory class, but it's not a guaranteed A, and Prof. seems to take a lot of crap because it isn't.  It's not very fair of people to complain bcse it isnt an easy A.

Class is a waste of time, everything is common sense and incredibly boring. seems like the easiest class until you get to the prelim, which was the most poorly written test I have ever taken, dumb questions on minute concepts, and answers that disagreed with the textbook, made class average terrible.

Perez is the worst professor I've had at Cornell.He doesn't know what he's doing AT ALL - its a waste of life to actually show up to class.The professor favors people who really suck upto him a lot,and never knows what he is talking about.He tries to make it hard by asking sneaky questions & making a big deal of stupid stuff, but u learn nothing.
Overall class is good for those who don't have much background in business.  Tests weren't bad but felt somewhat unreasonably tricky on some parts.

This is the easiest class I have yet to take, and professor perez is phenomenal if you listen to what he has to say. You can learn a lot from him if you are genuinely there to learn and not for the grade, he seems to know everything about anything you ask about-take time to get to know him if you can
worst teacher ever. period.

Not a very good professor at all, his choice of undergrad TAs were very bad. He never responds to emails in a timely fashion, the secretary for the class is not friendly, and the way they graded our huge projects is insulting. Overall, one of the worse professors I have had at CU. Very nice man but as a Cornell prof, I hope he doesn't get tenure.

the most disorganized class i have taken . i took the class for fun, to learn business. i havent learnt a thing. he squeezes in too much information in one lecture. he is a relaly nice guy , and i hate to say anything negative, but he should have GRAD TA's in his class. undergrads dont know how to run the class. and HIS OPINION answers are only rit

I turned in a 30 page project on one day, and they graded and returned it on the next.  There is no way they read every student's project and returned them in one day.  (the grades werent stellar, either). enough said.
class is incredibly disorganized.  tests are tricky and confusing.  lectures are boring.

Pedro's lectures are just taken straight from the textbook, and would be pointless if he didnt have the mandatory attendance with the clickers. his prelims arent that bad, but you have to memorize a lot of useless info.
No Comments

He relies on his TAs to do all the work, who are definitely not there to help students. Nice guy but I haven't learned anything useful. His tests require you to memorize that useless info.. you'll end up with an OK grade with extra credit.
No Comments
great guy/posts slides online

Do not take this class. The exams are extremely tricky. They totally screwed up my grade and added everything up wrong and now when I am trying to contact them to change it they are just ignoring me. Also, you will learn absolutely nothing important.

Let's play a little game... the name of the game is easy. Go to class (eh-viewpoints), do the extra credit, and it wont even matter how you do on the test. If you do not get an A in this class you shouldn't be at Cornell, period.
fun and entertaining professor. points come across clearly..easy A with several extra credit opportunities such as viewpoints and experiment participation.
fun and entertaining professor. points come across clearly..easy A with several extra credit opportunities such as viewpoints and experiment participation.
It's an easy A.  Pedro Perez (P.P.) is hilarious.  The class is pretty much common sense, but it's fun to attend just to see PP do stunts like jumping on tables and screaming at people.
No Comments

this class is deceptively easy, the midterms is killer and there aren't tons of opportunities to make up los points. the class material is a waste of time, either you get it or you don't. do the reading to study for the ridiculously unrelated test.
the material is easy

This class is a waste of time. Easy A, but a terrible professor and terrible curriculum. Every lecture you go to makes you dumber and dumber. Do not take it unless you have to - and if you do take it, don't go to lecture as much as possible.
This class is very easy.  The material is very easy to learn, and Pedro sounds like Desi Arnaz.  You can't get much better than that.

This class should be renamed Common Sense 220.  Frankly, I found the material pretty boring, but Pedro is entertaining and a nice guy.  The one thing that bothered me is he never responded to my emails, so I dock him on helpfulness.
pedro! pedro!  he's great, he remembers people's names, and helps you get internships, and he's just an awesome guy.  highly recommended pedro!
Pedro, you rock!

Very interesting class.  Not much work in his class, and lots of extra credits.  If you want to have your own business in the future, these two classes will help you to shape yourself and gain knowledge of how to be a entrepreneur.
Great class. Very enthusiastic professor.  Teaches well, very real world material.  Gives various opportunties to make you do well.  Take this class.

Perez is like the Venezualan father a WASP like me never had!  He's the nicest guy, the most dynamic lecturer.  He's one of the few profs that teaches a class of 400 kids and gets more than 3/4 to come to every lecture.  TAKE HIS CLASS!

I thought this class was extremely pointless.  But, he allowed us to improve our grades and had a lot of extra credit opportunities.  I personally did not enjoy his teaching style, and he has an accent, which makes it a little harder to understand him.
Great lecturer, very interesting and clear. Gets the point across really well. Class recommended as an enjoyable introduction to business. Lots of room for grade improvement.
Very easy course, entertaining leactures, and an over all great professor. There's no stress here.
Interesting professor, entertaining.  Lots of extra credit!!!!!!!!!!
No Comments
Nothing's better than the AEM department for an easy A!
What a freakin pointless class.  Cornell is so retarded for making us take this class!

Did not learn a single thing. Never taught in class, not once. Misinformed me about when the last day of class would be and made me miss a crucial assignment. Then when asked about it, her response was that she believed it didn't matter since I "wouldn't have done well on it anyway". None of my peers nor I took a single thing away from this class.
It was very hard to learn from her because of her language barrier, bad explanations in videos, and structure of class.

For how ever many supposed "degrees" she has, she actually might be one of the least competent profs I've ever met. She has zero common sense. She makes tests intentionally hard, tricky, & unfair. Just know that email-her and in-person-her are two completely separate personalities. Email version chooses violence. IRL version is sweet as pie.

Conniving. Her flipped classroom method is very ineffective. Class starts really easy and gets unimaginably complex very fast. She seems nice but don't be fooled, she's not. She doesn't know how to teach because she herself just finished school. Sections get treated differently, you'll see why. Just try to keep up and work with others

BS from Tsinghua; PhD from UC Berkeley. She's “nice,” but the flipped classroom feels like buz 💻, which is expected. No rubric, so assignments are unclear and feedback is vague (“minus 1 point for blah”). Individual and class assignments are tough; the curve spans all sections—think twice before sharing what's on the exam 🫵🫵🫵 no partial credit

Did not like the class structure. Professor Meng is very nice and accommodating, but you learn nothing from the class, even if you get a great grade. Sometimes the grading criteria are also a bit confusing, but overall not hard to get a good grade.

Flipped-classroom. You copy videos for homework, then do a harder version of the content in class. No explanation of the material. In-class TAs do not grade and cannot provide clear feedback or help, and the grading criteria is unclear. Students submit identical work and receive different scores. Assignments due @ the end of class. A waste of time.
You genuinely learn nothing
she's a nice person, but i genuinely learned nothing from her classes.

The class is flipped and you have to come to class with the model prepared. If you watch the video and/or read the notes before class you will do well in the class. The quizzes/prelims are open internet and are similar to the models used for the regular assignments. If you come prepared and do the bonus you will do very well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. Flipped class. All you need to do is copy what she does in the videos and you don't have to learn anything about statistics. She doesn't make her grading guidelines clear either.

Ernesto was the most laid back professor I've ever had and this was probably the most chill class I've ever taken. Also the second half of class you watch movies once a week and discuss the other day, final project is also a 5 min video on any topic you want. Goated class.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super laid-back. Classes with him are really relaxed. He points out great writing advice and tips I never knew about. He's just not too into fantasy writing and head's up: not good with remembering names. I've taken two classes with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ernesto was my professor for True Stories (FWS). He is a great and will really work with students. He assigns few papers and gives good feedback. The class is about radical political movements in the US, and we sometimes watched movies and did light readings (less than 5 pgs). Would 10/10 recommend this class to anyone!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The fact that this is my first time giving a review here is testament to Ernesto's teaching ability. He's sharp, open-minded, funny, experimental, inspirational, and doesn't BS. He won't sugar-coat, but he will make you a better, more aware writer. And if he pulls you aside to encourage you to send your work out... you know you've made it :)
If you put in the work, you will do very well.
Friendly, but provides no useful feedback and no help improving work. Doesn't pay much attention. Easy grader but you learn nothing.

Didn't think creative writing was going to be this interesting.  Ernesto, and he never wants to be called professor, would play a film clip and then have us read a short story and lead us to see the same narrative techniques being used in fiction. Amazing!!!  He is very cute but he wears the same black shirt a lot.  Easy grader.
Interesting guy, extremely laid-back and passionate about the material he teaches. Dynamic, creative professor. Very easy grader.

Professor Qian worked with me on my doctoral thesis and is a lifesaver in every definition of the word. She was the main advisor for our research team and saved us so much time and energy on our projects. She helped us get our findings published, present at conferences, and advocated for us at every step of the way. Can't say enough about her.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor at Cornell. She's a great mentor, accessible, and willing to work with you on every level. Taking her class redefined my entire life and career.
So great to have a professor that actually cares about their students. Her lectures changed my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
Dr. Qian is one of the most intellectually stimulating professors I've worked with at Cornell. She pushes us to question assumptions and find design solutions that are both elegant and ethical. She also genuinely cares about her students' growth. 

She gives tough feedback, but it's always constructive and deeply insightful.

Dr. Qian was definitely challenging, but she's incredibly supportive and always willing to talk through ideas or give thoughtful feedback.

By the end of the semester, I felt like I had leveled up as a designer and as a thinker. If you're ready to put in the work, she will absolutely meet you there and help you get the most out of the process.
She's the best professor I've ever had.

Loney is honest & funny, but MATH-1100's flipped format relies on a TERRIBLE textbook that sets students up for failure IMO. 

The real problem is grading--which is shared with Prof. Kaminski whos unbelievably harsh, inconsistent, & nitpicky. So be aware, if you take Prof. Loney in the summer, you're stuck with her grading too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Quincy has to be the worst professor I've ever had. He would often get confused by his own questions, struggle to explain basic concepts, and nitpick every HW calculation to his exact standards. Be prepared to teach yourself. He is a horrible professor, and a rude person who tries to make you feel dumb instead of helping you during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Loney (wishes to be called Quincy) was an extremely animated professor. His course was super difficult for me, but most students seem to do just fine. A majority of the course was all about the textbook so the textbook is a MUST! He's super excusable outside of class and only wants to help the students succeed.

Very personally invested in teaching and improving every student's Chinese skills, though that sometimes means being harsh with her students and assigning large amounts of memorization-heavy homework. She takes attendance and diligent completion of homework seriously. Her grading practices are predictable; you directly get out what you put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty strict but wants you to improve. Skilled at teaching the material and getting conversations going. In class exercises are repetitive but improved pronunciation a ton. Sizable daily HW + daily writing quizzes. When you make a mistake, she is strict with you, making you repeat until you get it correct, which can be stressful (Whiplash vibes).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: It's a ton of work, but my Chinese did improve a lot, both over CHIN 2201 and 2202. I wasn't on her bad side, but if she doesn't like you, it gets a lot harder for you to finish out the class.
My Chinese improved a lot after taking Intermediate with her. She really wants everyone to practice as much as possible, which was encouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's very helpful and reasonable, but it is a tough class with many pop quizzes. I had to work hard, but I am now able to spend hours with my Chinese friends without speaking any English, which ultimately is the only true measure of a language teacher and course.

Took both Chin 2201 and 2202 with her, she can be really funny sometimes and make the class interesting with some fun dialogue. However, she sometimes carries the crazy high maintenance mother persona which scares me. Besides all that, shes a really great Chinese professor who will teach Chinese in a very painless way and make you laugh.

I took IMPAC over the summer with Teng Laoshi and liked her. She has her moments of snappiness and strictness but usually she's really nice and patient. She also teaches you a lot of useful vocabulary that isn't in the textbook, which is somewhat obscure. Her tests are manageable and her expectations are reasonable. Teng helps move students along.

Compared to He Laoshi in first year, Teng Laoshi gives students a much more time-consuming workload. And she expects all students to have a fairly high ability to understand conversation. Her teaching style may not be the most effective nor lucid for everyone, but students at least get a solid background in vocabulary and grammar, if nothing else.

Though I hear she's a lot harder on her 200 level class, I took 4411 with Teng Laoshi and loved every moment of it. Relative to the other chinese faculty, she's easily the most sane and reasonable, plus probably the most intelligent and driven. You'll learn Chinese with her and not hate your life doing it.
Nice, helpful, knowledgable and interested professor.  Some of her in-class review games are a little tacky, but they get the job done.

Don't know why Quan has so many haters. You can literality fup the Prelim (miss almost half of his 25 MCQ exam) and still get an A. He is THE BEST professor in hotel school. Years of experience in  Real Estate. 

YOU need to forget about what your $10000 career coach tells you. Just go to class and learn!!!

One of the worst classes I've taken at Cornell, 100% wouldn't recommend. Posts no grades, exam averages are god awful, and curve isn't published until grades are finalized on transcript. He reads off of word documents during lectures and makes them unbearable. Called guest lecturer by the wrong name and fell asleep during another guest. No good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: tests are extremely tricky... lectures and slides do not prepare you well enough for them. all MCQs, no partial credit. answer choices include a lot of none of the above, not enough information, or all of the above. easy for him to grade but hard for us to take as test-takers.

Professor Quan tricks you the first day. He makes fun of his grades on rate my professor which makes you think that they are fake however they are real and he is one of the worst professors at Cornell. Do everything you can to avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His grading can be a bit obscure with one M/C question being worth 15% of an exam and his case studies are a headache but overall good professor. Not impossible getting a good grade. He'll give you an A if you do better than everyone else as its subjective at the end of the semester. (grad students tend to be bricks and bring grade average down)

Quan sees himself as infallible, which is ironic because he is the worst professor I have had at Cornell. He's defensive and will snark students. During lecture, he mindlessly reads off Word documents. He does not prepare you for the case studies at all - e.g. he just assumes you know how to make a 2-tier JV equity waterfall on excel lol. Good luck

Professor Quan sucks the life out of real estate. Your grade is mostly consistent of 2 exams, both only 20 multiple choice questions designed to mess with your head (lots of "not enough information"). Lectures are dry as he only reads off the same pdfs he uses every year. If you can avoid him, please do!!!

The worst class Ive taken at Cornell by FAR. The classes quite literally are just him reading the lectures and hes a horrible lecturer. Tests are nearly impossible, and he doesnt respond to emails with questions either. Should really consider retirement ASAP since it seems like while alumni from years back respect him, current students do not.

Literally just reads off of the notes. Class is miserable to try to sit through. Sasses people who participate. Your grade depends on 2 home-works and 2 exams that are only 20 multiple choice questions. Did not learn anything.
Makes no sense. Can't understand professor Quan. He rambles during class.
difficult class but one of the most rewarding! many drop out after the first prelim but should def stay around. GPA isn't everything..this class is great learning!!
GENIUS
Excellent professsor
If you don't take a class with Quan you are missing out on one of best professors not only at Cornell, but in the Ivy League

Prof. Quan is amazing.  His real estate and finance knowledge are unsurpassed, and he's got some great contacts when it comes to job hunting.  His courses aren't easy, but you'll get more out of them than 99% of other Cornell courses.

Obviously biochem is going to be hard, no matter who teaches it. I thought Prof. Qian did a good job of presenting the material in as accessible of a way as possible. He was also really kind and somehow kind of funny. I appreciated him even more compared to next professor who switched in halfway through the semester.

He is a demanding professor and covers a lot of very important content. That being said he does move fast and it is hard to keep up at certain times in the semester. I spent about 10-15 hours a week fully digesting the material and it was a course I will remember because it reminded me why I love biology. Would take it again in an instant.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly, I felt like he went pretty fast through the slides during lectures, and he wasn't very helpful during office hours. Make sure you go to class because he will test you on things he says, but are not explicitly in the slides. He did throw in a few jokes though. Not the most understanding prof. The TAs will be your best friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He throws a lot of information at you at once so be ready to record his lectures. He also is hard to understand sometimes. The test questions are based on minor details so when you study make sure to throughly look through your notes.

Professor Qian is one of the worst professors I've had. Hard to understand lectures. Prelims are ridiculous true/false questions that don't test actual understanding of material. Very rude! Makes fun of questions in lecture. Doesn't accommodate students needs. But! It's easier than the other biochem classes and is more pre-med/vet focused.
Good professor in general! But the material covered is more like cell biology and I am a bit disappointed by that... Would love to see more chemistry.

Professor Qian definitely challenges you. If you want to do above average in his class you need to put in the work for it, but he's extremely helpful if you utilize his office hours. He wants to see you succeed and definitely believes in you.

Took NS 3200 in Fall 14.  Did not like this class and would not recommend. Professor Qian taught 34 of the class and he was not very clear due to his accent.  Also, by cramming it all into one semester, you do not go very much in depth. Fell more like a Cell bio than biochemistry. Easier than 3310 but I would recommend  3310-3320 to learn the most

Avoid if possible. He is not easy to understand and his lectures are so lackluster.  Even though I found the material interesting, I only understood the slides by studying them on my own... basically, Khan Academy was my best friend taking this class.  He is terrible at answering questions.  His exams are manageable, but nonetheless difficult.

Truly the greatest of his kind. Robby was a solid 5 stars through and through. Genuinely cared for the students. He speaks a bit like a cartoon character but you get used to it. 
-signed Robby's #1 fan
Tries to act like he's nice and understanding but nothing he said was that helpful when you went to him for help. Also tries to make grading clear however I was curved down at the end.

A little funny but he clearly doesn't want to teach. He's definitely not a terrible person but I found him very inaccessible towards the end of the semester which was frankly aggravating. 

Lectures were just textbook but he sometimes helped clarify some details. Maybe I should've just skipped class and watched youtube videos on the subject.

He is a pretty good lecturer but his exams were the complete opposite of the practice problems he provided. the previous year's exams that he gave were 10x easier than our exams and the material taught during lecture was not reflective of exam materials at all. he is very knowledgeable of the material and kind, but the exams were way too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great guy who cares about his students and makes the time to help people, but his tests are pretty difficult and does not provide enough materials to prepare for those caliber of questions. Lectures are straight from the textbook and I would recommend reading the textbook, especially parts you're having trouble with. Great dude, mid teacher.
Curve sucks. Lectures are uninspired, straight from the textbook. Exams are too hard for it to be curved so poorly.

DiStasio is a great professor. The material comes directly from the textbook and is easy to follow. The exams are straightforward and there are many opportunities to improve your grade. He is very open to feedback and meeting with students one on one. Genuinely one of the easiest classes at Cornell just read the textbook and do the practice.

He's actually such a sweetheart. People dislike the class because it's hard but thats not this professor's fault. Such a breath of fresh air compared to my other prof's he was so great, always encouraging and willing to help.
Good lecturer! Exams were super tough, but the curve was generous. Average on one exam was a 26%

DiStasio is a good lecturer and I found it easier to attend class when I read the material- even skimmed for ten minutes - before coming because he's organized with the topics. Go to office hours to go over back of the book questions/conceptual (!!!) understanding - heavy on concepts - and don't fall back on lab grades, it can seriously hurt
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Didn't like it. Lecture material versus test material didn't match too well.

CHEM 2080 was a very difficult class for me. I didn't love how his questions were worded - left me very annoyed when I could solve something but simply didnt understand what the question wanted. But the DiStasio is a great person - ever-willing to help, stay extra time, etc. His prelims are TOUGH but the curves usually compensated. Best of luck!

Professor DiStasio makes the content interesting and funny, so I'd recommend attending lecture. Material is straight from the textbook. Discussion sections weren't helpful, but their problems were good practice. Prelims were hard but well-curved; good preparation with the textbook, practice problems, and practice prelims will help you succeed.
no
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked his lectures. He definitely gives you everything you need to succeed in his class, given you put in the effort. One thing I didn't like was how difficult the prelims were, but that meant the curves were really helpful. Just do EVERY textbook problem and you'll be fine.

Dr. DiStasio cares deeply about his students. This was a difficult semester for me and he was more than understanding. I recommend going to office hours. It's an 800-student class, but only seven or eight people go to his office hours. He went over my exams with me and helped me understand course material in a one-on-one environment.
Distasio is THE MAN! His exams come directly from lecture and his explanations are extremely clear. Go to class, do practice problems, and attend sections and you're good!

Robert is great. As others have said he really cares about making sure you learn the material. Lectures not required but I highly recommend- he's always telling some funny story or analogy. Exams are very fair just do the practice tests. 2080 labs SUCK but not Robert's juristiction so can't blame him
He really likes chemistry and wants his students to as well. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students and just wants us to appreciate chemistry like he does. He's a funny bloke also.

DiStasio was helpful in making a hard class more fair; he let students have one-on-one meetings with him and even gave me points back for two of my exams, he listens to student feedback and is easy to talk to; the class itself is difficult but I felt a lot more comfortable having him as a professor!
Good professor, exams were mostly fair, genuinely wanted us to succeed.

Robert is a beautiful soul. People say humans make mistakes, but rob doesn't. He is the closest thing to perfect a human can be. His kindness and caring nature has almost brought me to tears. His class was actually very good, difficult but since Rob is so amazing he got us through it, unlike in chem 2070. He also frequents goldies often, so pu.

I genuinely adore Prof DiStasio-- I haven't had such a lovely chem professor since high school. His lectures are well-paced, engaging, understandable, and informative, and he makes it obvious how much he cares about our success and well-being. Exams are fair and he regularly asks our opinions about the length and difficulty. Overall lovely guy.

Professor DiStasio is a great! He's accessible outside of class & cares for the students. Curves the exams(actually tries to benefit as many people as possible). The exams are fair and similar to PS problems. The lab for this course sucks it's not in sync with the lecture and you have to make up your own procedure. Only responsible for lec though.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: heavily relied on the textbook, but lectures were well organized and easy to follow. tests were fair. if you go to lecture, follow the textbook, and do the practice problems and homework, you should have no problems with the class. definitely learn a lot and dr. Distasio was great!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures come straight from the textbook and are recorded (very easy to watch in 2x speed). Discussion sections were pointless since they would go over the easy questions. Problem sets were a must do before every exam. Basically understand how to do every problem on the PS and the class is cake. Lab depends on TA, some good and some very bad.

He's kind of boring during lectures and basically rewords the textbook. He was very behind on content and that kind of messed with the lab portion of the course. Exams are at a reasonable difficulty if you do practice problems from the textbook + discussion sets, but a bit too many questions in my opinion (have to rush to finish them).

Dr. DiStasio is not a bad professor, but he's just very boring. His lectures are live readings of the textbook and aren't very engaging. However, he pulls straight from the textbook problems for prelims so if you do a lot of the problems from the end of chapter, you'll be fine. Gives lots of opportunities for grade improvement through mini prelims.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor DiStassio was a great teacher and I would highly recommend taking a class from him. Very kind and caring toward his students and you could tell he genuinely cares about student success. 2080 is a hard class but DiStassio was always available to work through difficult concepts in-office hours. The grading breakdown was also quite fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. DiStasio loves chemistry, and it shows in the way he speaks during lectures. He makes content interesting, easy to understand, and is accessible for 1:1 meetings with any student upon request. After the horror that was CHEM 2070, 2080 was a breath of fresh air that made me realize why I'm passionate about chemistry.

So surprised to see the comments about the exams being difficult--the questions were based on the problems in the textbook! If you studied and did all the problems in the chapters/back of the book, you wouldn't be confused at all. All the DPSs were prelim level problems. Oh, and Kinsland runs the labs/TAs, not DiStasio. Truly one of the best Profs!

Professor DiStasio is understanding and caring. Doesn't try to harm you with grading but grading could be tough due to the difficulty of the content taught. Tests are reasonable, but challenging. Professor DiStasio makes himself clear and available. Lab portions are hard. lectures are strictly followed by a textbook. Overall good professor.
Nice-ish guy but does not give enough practice problems to prep for exams. Lab portion is unreasonably difficult. Do not take this course if you don't absolutely have to

Sweet man who loves his students. However, prepare to be confused and struggle on those exams. A lot of 2080 is assumption based, so if you're like me and prefer things to be exact, you will find this class difficult. If you don't need to take this class, don't. Not too many resources but use the book, but exams are harder than the examples given.

The content in this course was relatively easy, but the lab portion was unreasonably difficult. Professor Distasio gave clear lectures, however he went slow and we did not finish the course material. He is a very nice and engaging man, you would be lucky to have him as a gen chem professor.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very good lecturer and cares about his students. Solid professor

Lectures are awesome and he closely follows the textbook which is good because you always know where to reference information. Wasn't a fan of how tough he graded the class considering that the material was less difficult compared to 3890. Super accessible outside of class and always willing to help during office hours.

You'd think this man has a pizza place in Brooklyn, not a PhD from Berkeley in Quantum Mechanics. Crazy hard tests, but he made them shorter so that he can get out of campus earlier to his hot date (aka wife). Take this class, you will not be disappointed (except with your grade).

TAs make or break this class. Content is very dry. Professor does a lot of examples during class which are worth doing in the long run, as they give you extra practice. They are also what is tested. Recommend learning LaTeX notation for this class. Assignments were a pain and not helpful usually, but ZyBook HW was. Final was ridiculously long.

Lectures were dry and heavy on theoretical information. Recitations were somewhat helpful but the many assignments were extremely difficult and required asking questions or stumbling through searching for specific coding functions. The class felt like it was preparing students for a PhD rather than just a masters level course. High expecations.

Daziano is a good lecturer, but outside of lecture the course was really disorganized. The recitations felt useless, and the online homework portal was really frustrating. If you studied the slides and did the homework, it was fairly easy to do well enough. Also, some lectures were way too R/Stata/Minitab heavy to be engaging.
Genuinely the kindest professor I've ever had, you won't regret taking a class with him.
Such a nice guy!!

RVR is one of my favorite professors I have had at Cornell. Knowing that you're being taught OS by someone who worked at Bell Labs with the creators of Unix and C is very compelling and inspirational. He is hilarious and his office hours are immensely helpful, more so than TAs. He is also very active on Ed. His demos in class are also insightful.
Man is a legend of his field. Super smart and caring!

I loved having RVR as my professor. He can come across as disorganized at times, but it wasn't a big deal for me. I found that he was a hilarious professor that obviously knew the material he was teaching so well yet was so down to earth and super approachable. I thought all the homeworks and projects weren't difficult and the prelims were fair.
Prof. RVR's lectures are quite good, even if they move slowly.
good professor but class is often disorganized. grading and exams aren't representative of the content covered in lectures.

RVR's weekly assignments were sized appropriately and reinforced the lecture materials, reasonable workload. He was helpful after lectures in answering questions, and walked through difficult assignment questions. I wasn't a fan of his exams and this was my downfall - it required a deeper understanding of concepts than what is provided in lecture.
He's one of the most genuinely caring and personable CS professors I've had at Cornell  I feel lucky to have him as a professor tbh
he is a really caring person, and I found his lectures easy to follow
the whole course is a mess and won't teach you much stuff. The professors and TAs are unhelpful. You'd rather self-study instead of taking this class
Although he is kind, its clear he did not spend much time preparing for lecture. This resulted in a very disorganized course.

He's not a bad person, just a bad professor for teaching freshmen chemistry. He went too much in depth and wouldn't explain the basics. He also loves to ridicule students who have the nerve to ask questions about the material. Overall the course was curved to a B so grades were okay but no one learned the material (test averages in the 40s).

Peter, while he may be entertaining, does not teach us anything. His slides are discombobulated, and he does not explain stuff well. He also insists that we not use the textbook as "they are cheap and incorrect." Organic Chemistry Tutor is your best friend. Your only saving grace is that while you may be completely lost, so is everyone else.
Caan't teach.

Wolczanski clearly doesn't want to teach freshmen and the freshmen don't want to be there. I skipped every lecture and homework, literally just showed up for labs & prelims and mostly guessed and got a C-. Class averages for prelims were all under 50% so the curve was insane. He's rude but hilarious. Engineer trauma bonding starts here.
Worst prof ever

Trying to decipher the incomprehensible babble that bubbles from this poor banal soul's mouth was the first and only sin that many new engineers have commited. The class is not hard, chemistry should not be his hard, but when you've got it out for the kids... godspeed to the next year who takes him.

Lectures were poorly organized and had little information on relevant material, yet extensive information on "bonus topics", which cluttered lectures. Despite this, it was expected to locate the rare pieces of actually relevant information, which would then appear on prelims. 
Extremely disdainful towards students, for some reason.
Does not know how to teach.

Peter's lectures were not the most interesting but he definitely knows what he is talking about. Very confusing in the beginning but it takes about 1 prelim to figure out how to do well. Study the lecture notes of course, but I did text book problems and did fine on the exams. Easy grade since averages were
put me a step further towards the ithaca gorges. should be named in his honor

The professor was funny but not a good lecturer, and it was hard to separate essential information from what is mentioned in passing. The course needs a better focus on the basics as it was very sporadic and made it hard for anything to truly stick. Mostly self studied since the course material given were hard to decipher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Did all the work myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I played Geometry Dash in the back of class most lectures. I think Peter was a fun guy but the lectures didn't help much and content was a little all over the place. We started with nuclear chem. I found the best way to study was to UNDERSTAND the problem sets. Most of the learning happened by referencing problem sets to posted lecture notes.
Worst class I have ever taken. Do everything to not have this professor.
6 point font, reads off the slides, and inconsistent lectures. Lectures about his research instead of the actual content. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! Also, hard prelims with a 40 average.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The only problem with Peter is that his lecture notes are very hard to understand, rest are fine. Going to lectures don't really help to be honest, but the office hours were surprisingly helpful. Exams are fair as they ALL come from his lecture notes, but decoding his slides was the hard part. As long as you spend time studying you should be fine
Peter was a great teacher! Truly a grateful experience to be in this class.
Somehow got an A in this class. Ride the curve. OChem Tutor is your best friend.

PETER PETER PETER PETER PETER PETER PETER
DON'T TAKE THIS MAN'S CLASS

Taking Pete's class is truly an experience (a bad one). The lectures teach you about everything EXCEPT Chemistry. I've left the class knowing the same amount (if not less) about chemistry. He makes it a point to show his disdain for students every lecture, and gets mad at the class when only 5 people out of 500 score above 75% on his prelims. Bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: PTW and the administration highly discourage students from seeking accommodations for their needs protected by the government of New York State using the loophole that granted these accommodations is "high effort" and "logistically inconvenient"
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you don't need to take his class, don't take it. If you need to take his class, lock in.

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Peter Wolcanski is a unique professor for his deep hatred of his students. He assumes you already know the basics of general chemistry and will spend majority of his lecture going over advanced topics , assuming a foundation. Exams are atrocious and based on an all or nothing approach. Youtube is your best friend, if there is any hope to be had.

He's a hard and confusing teacher in lecture. But there is not much homework. And he grades harshly but fair. The class is curved to a B so if you work hard you will be fine. On one of my prelims the average was a 39% but that got curved to a B.
Wow, don't take this class. I would HIGHLY recommend taking this class over the summer or a semester where he is NOT teaching. I should've known after seeing these reviews.
You should know already by how many reviews are here. I concur HEAVILY.

This was by far the worst professor I ever had at Cornell. Prof. Wolczanski is a terrible lecturer, runs a poorly organized course, and completely underprepares his students for his exams. It would be difficult for him to try to make his students' lives any more difficult than he already does. He lacks compassion and adds unnecessary stress.

Please do not take this class I took AP chem and I swear the prelim is so god dam hard nothing like the homework prelim questions follow each other so one wrong everything is wrong. Loves to talk about bomb although its not mandatory the lectures on the slide are most of what he says but he will add additional information outside of it. beware

Ok so here's a REAL evaluation of PTW's infamous 2090 class: it is not that bad, IF (and let me emphasize this) you have had prior Chem experience (AP or otherwise). Honestly, a lot of people here are complaining because they dont show up to lecture or dont pay attention. But if you show up, put in good effort studying, you will do fine

Not a bad person but teaching a genuinely impossible class. Admin designed it in a way to make you hate yourself and chemistry and succeeds in doing that by prelim 3. Overall, in general, not just with Peter but with any professor, CASE out of the course. You could have Newton teach it & it would still be shite. Pete: 2/5, CHEM 2090: -5/5

boo tomato tomato

ps. MY EYESs

arguably the worst professor at Cornell. Run, unless you're stuck here because of 2090. Be prepared for confusing and incomprehensive lecture slides and hard tests with questions you have never seen before.

Peter somehow finds a way to crush curiosity and the will to learn in his students with his boring lectures that focus more on random bomb facts than the actual material. He really loves bombs.The slides are not organized and the topics covered in class are not sequential. A class could cover quantum physics and the next class we balance equations. The information is scattered throughout the slides and u have to find information like a puzzle for some reason. Blames students for bad scores based on his teachings.
Don't do it. Don't even think about it.

For the love of lord, never take 2090; moreover, never take it with Wolczanski. The course is designed so that students learn 4 years of chemistry material in one semester. Knowledge of quantum mechanics and thermodynamics is a prerequisite.

This professor is smart but doesn't know how to teach. I took AP Chem before and every lecture he overcomplicates the topic and in general his lectures are very unorganized. He judges people that ask questions that he thinks are easy and already in the lecture slides. Also for some reason he loves explosions.
Berates students for asking questions, blames them for not studying when exam average was 43%.

Blames students for the test average being 40%, accuses students of "laziness" for allegedly not reading his lecture slides that are borderline incoherent. Jokes and puts down intellectually curious students for asking questions. 

Please, if you can, take the CASE exam to try to skip this course. If you must, rely on your TA.
This class will obliterated your self-esteem. I genuinely believe 95% of Cornell engineering students have imposter syndrome because of him (and the other 5% are the ones who get to skip this class)

Ok lecturer but very difficult prelims. Given the amount of material that has to be taught he goes over everything quickly. However if you are prepared to put the hours in you will be fine. I haven't taken chem past a sophomore year of basic high school chem and have scored above median on both prelims thus far. Just be prepared to ride the curve.
Avoid at all costs. Professor berates students for not studying after the class averages a 43% on an impossible exam. Expects a very strong background in chemistry coming into the class.

run. do not take. the whole distribution for exam 2 was literally a uniform graph around 40% and he blamed US for not studying when the whole class failed. its clearly a him issue and he needs to have his ego checked.
just literally don't think about taking this class AT ALL please avoid him in any way possible

came into this class with very minimal chem background (just hs sophomore year), and this class did NOT help me gain confidence. it seems like everyone else already took AP chem and even they are extremely confused. the test averages reflect how lost we all are. the slides are hard to digest and I'm so cooked, this should NOT be an intro course!!!

please please please do NOT take his class for chem 2090. you will regret it, it will tank your gpa, and destroy your self esteem. i know people hear others saying that they should drop a class and ignore that advice but for this one DONT. get the credit from a community college instead, i promise you this is not worth it.
Smart guy, bad teacher
Expects you to know a lot more than you already do coming into the class. Organic Chemistry Tutor is amazing.

Wolczanski is undoubtedly the worst professor I've ever had. His lectures and notes were incoherent, making it extremely difficult to learn the material. Him, one of his past students Devika Pokhriyal, and other students of his are cyberbullying students on facebook.

In 4 weeks of class (intro class for non chem majors btw, some of whom had no chemistry experience) he taught us practically everything that I learned from high school and AP chem classes. reviews.comment: I had Prof Wolczanski during my first semester at Cornell. After completing my degree, I can say with certainty that he was the worst professor I had during my time here.

Not the best lecturer... doesn't rely so much on the textbook as on his own class notes, which are extremely confusing. Many of the topics he chooses to cover are above the level of a first-year chemistry class. That being said, the insane difficulty of his exams forces you to study the material on your own and learn a lot.
Horrible lecturer. It's clear he's smart as a whip and knows a lot about chemistry, but he has no idea how to teach it. Goes way beyond what should be taught in a general chem course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Horrible guy, unwelcoming, gives you a thousand judgements if you don't know something. Homework is wayy too hard.

Wolczanski's Inorganic class was excellent. He covered all of the basics and did a solid job simplifying the more complicated concepts. The material might be a little hard to grasp at first, but I seemed to grasp it without going to office hours. Overall, a great professor that likes to challenge his students and grades fairly.

- very bad professor . He goes in depth in what you don't really have to know and therefore has you confused the ENITRE lecture . His exams are unimaginabley long and difficult . He wants you to be able to derive hard concepts rather than understanding the concepts you actually need to know in gen Chem. Terrible !

Lectures are long, boring and meandering. He has a somnolent effect on students and expects too much prior knowledge. Self-study is essential to pass. He  made no attempt to make the lecture interesting and it was jarring compared to Professor Crane. Tests set by him are unbelievably difficult. All in all, the worst teacher I have ever had.

Smart guy, but not a very good teacher. Taught concepts well beyond the scope of the course that were largely irrelevant to the vast majority of students without a lot of outside research; then tested for how well you were able to manipulate his lecture notes as opposed to for understanding of the material. Tried WAY too hard to be funny...

Hated this class the moment he stepped in. He rambles a lot, and I think half the time he did not follow the curriculum. Instead, he discussed his own personal research and went far beyond what was necessary during lecture. Was very disappointed with his ridiculous exams, but he is occasionally funny and is truly, extraordinarily brilliant.

Chem 2090 with Prof. Wolczanski sucked.  His lectures are not worth attending; just read the lecture notes he posts online.  Tests are hard, you'll somehow be saved by the curve.  I still don't understand chemistry.  He also has a wicked sense of humor (not in a good way- think mean).

Lectures can be  long and draggy. You can tell he is really smart and really into his research, however, he is just not right to teach an introductory chemistry class. He spends a greater proportion of his lecture talking about some abstract concepts and the worst part, is you can barely find the topics in the prescribed textbooks.
Poorly organized lectures that ramble for too long on irrelevant material. Assumed much too high a level of understanding for a general chemistry course. Lectures are absolutely useless.
worst professor I have ever had avoid taking a class with him at all costs that is all you need to know.

If every TA has to say "I don't know how to explain this to you guys in the context of what you're learning since I learned this in advanced inorganic chemistry," then something is wrong. He teaches all these terms and concepts without explaining what they are, and he teaches stuff that is nowhere in the textbook, so the textbook is useless. AWFUL!
Spends half the lecture doing complex derivations, then tells you it's not important and won't be on the exam.

Professor Wolczanski is said to be a very tough teacher, but everyone should go to his office hours and actually have a conversation with him before judging. He's an absolutely amazing professor and he truly is there to help. I wish I realized this earlier, so that I could've taken advantage of the time I had with him as a professor.

Clearly very knowledgable, but he is unable to pass information to students in an effective manner. His lectures are disorganized, and he assumes far too great of a basic level of understanding for a general chemistry clas.

This guy is the worst Professor I have ever had in my life. I have had professors who don't speak English that I would take over this guy. I would rather have my right ball chopped off than have to take another one of his classes.
absolutely terrible

Worst professor I have ever had at Cornell so far. Doesn't teach relevant material to the textbooks and teaches students as if we all understand physical chemistry on his level. No one ever understands his lectures and he mumbles a lot. He killed chemistry for me. Would avoid him if possible.

Talking to TAs or peers or reading your book is the better option for this class. He makes weird (and unnecessary) references in class that don't pertain to the lecture. His content is confusing and hard to comprehend.
You're better off staying home and reading the textbook
Lectures were not useful. Tests were hard and too long for the allowed time. Homework was fair, but learn the material from the textbook because it's not covered in lecture.

Lecture was useless I couldn't understand anything, take an AEW if you can get into one it helped me a lot. Tests are really not that terrible as most people are saying, most of the questions follow directly from the non-textbook hw questions. The mean is consistently pretty low so you're not expected to know everything. Final mean was 161300
useless lectures. hard exams. textbook material seems irrelevant.

Professor Wolczanski teaches a lot of interesting things that are not really contained in the textbook. If you have a TA that knows what she is talking about and can help you with the homework, it is possible to do well in the class. He assigns extra homework problems that he writes that end up being exactly like test questions.
Easily the worst professor I have ever had
He makes a lot of drug references in my class, maybe he likes to party? But this class is no party for the students; he makes everyone regret not placing out of this class.

Prof. Wolczanski covers interesting material not found in the textbook in his lectures. So, if you tend to skip classes, chances are that you wont get good grades just by reading the book.  The pdf notes he puts up before class are super helpful.

Lectures are virtually useless, as he gives material that not only fails to appear on the test, but that the TAs don't even know how to teach because they only just learned it in grad school classes. Also has a very monotone voice and uses high-level terminology that makes lectures almost impossible to understand.
I wish he would just be more respectful to his students. No one appreciates his disdainful comments about engineers when we ask for help.
One word. Terrible.
He takes pleasure in his students failing. He relishes in the feeling of superiority and enjoys picking on his students' struggle in the class.
he's impossible to understand and lectures about everything we don't need to know but leaves out everything we do. Sometimes it's actually funny how confusing he can be
I see him at parties, what a guy. Not a guy during lectures :
8th grade math yo, actually though just CASE out

One thought comes to mind when I think of PJ: What is life? This man simultaneously does not care about his class while still enjoying his class more than anyone else in the lecture. His lecture is completely useless and totally ruined my interest for chemistry. If you must gain credit for chemistry, take the placement test and avoid this guy if it is possible! Prelims and final are kind of irrelavant to the course material.

Horrible. He is out to get you. He is so condescending when you ask a question too. Know the extension problems and his HWs very well. Barely uses textbook material. Tested us on ridiculous stuff that was totally irrelevant to chem 2090. Go to his lectures or else you will fail. It is hard to hear what he is saying cause he mumbles a lot too.

Here's the advice to get through.  Go to all the lectures and read his notes before class (class has more meaning this way), thoroughly do the problems.  to study make sure you know every lecture and every extension by heart.  I promise if you do this you will beat the curve on every exam.

Avoid this guy! Lectures became useless very quickly. Teaches further than the curriculum requires. Makes a attempts at joking around during class, especially when it comes to bad grades. Prelims are OK if you study extension problems on HW... however, the Final was madness. Says he is an exceptional teacher, and that's why he "gets the big bucks"

OH MY GOD!  Professor Wolczanski is freaking amazing!  This guy must know everything possible about his field.  He's the Wayne Gretsky of organometallic chemistry.  Anyone who has Professor Wolczanski is amazingly lucky
did not learn a thing. horrible lecturer. tests are impossibly long but not too difficult. using his practice hw problems helps a lot with tests.
Avoid this professor at all costs. Especially is you aren't a ChemE. If you do end up in this course, use the previous exam questions on the problem sets to study for the tests. and good luck

The tests were by far that hardest I've taken at Cornell, more so than MATH 1910 which is supposedly to weed out the under achievers. He told us it would be one of the easiest classes we would take at Cornell. So not true.

To sum up CHEM 2090 as Wolczanski taught it: useless lectures and hard exams.  I generally did ok because I had a high quality non-AP chemistry course in high school; had I the AP credit, I would not have wasted my time with this class. In general, there was nothing I learned by going to lecture that I would not have by reading the book.

I learned so much in this class. It was a lot of work and we covered much more material than we were supposed to, but I loved it in the end. Prof. Wolczanski is just brilliant. He seems a bit mean initially, but he's actually really nice and extremely helpful.

I took advanced inorganic chemistry organometallic chemistry class from PTW when I was a graduate student spode. I was initially terrorized, but broke my ass and did OK. PTW recognized and appreciated that. If you are a whiner, you are over.

The absolute worst prof I've had at Cornell. His tests were killer (and the means reflect it), his demeanor in lecture can be summed up best by his sarcastic sneers at what he believes are stupid questions or stupid students, and he has no desire to help his students. Don't count on his office hours being any better either.

Had him for Chem 216. A total disaster. I remember the day when the mean on the prelim was a 26. But I have to agree with one of the other posts here, by the time i got around to chem 410, things had definitely improved. not sure if it was teaching non-freshmen or the subject matter or just a lot of therapy, but whatever it was, it was not too bad.

It's apparent that this guy is in academia to do his research and views teaching as an unfortunate liability of his job. Moves very quickly, doesn't stop for questions, and not much fun to listen to.  Rarely gives you any background info on WHY you're covering the material you're covering.  Looking around the room it's amusing to see so many confounded students.

Had him freshman year for 216 and thought he was pure evil.  But by the time I had him again senior year for 410, I had come to respect his intelligence and humor and stopped being so scared of him.  Plus, he's really good at drawing icosahedrons!
While demonstrating wave propagation with a long slinky: "I'm a married man, so I haven't had much practice with my hand." --Wolczanski... these are the only words I remember from his course.

It was the material that this course covers that is very difficult (take 207), not the teacher. Although the professor was not overtly enthusiastic, he was by no means Evil or sadistic, he just did his job and that is why he is only a mediocre professor.
Absolutely Evil man.  His only interest in teaching is so that he can prove he is smarter than his students.  Steer clear at all costs.  Avg test scores of 41%

Steer Clear of this class at ALL costs.  Take the alternative chemistry for engineering majors (207?).  You will be happy you made the choice

MEAN MAN. He is the epitome of a Cornell professor who cares more about his research than the students. Even the TA's for the course could not do some of the exam questions. Why is it necessary to trick students when we are here to learn & graduate? W
he teaches VERY FAST and too much in one semester-- he may go into too much depth...  but hes a funny old man, and a good professor i gotta hand it to him, hes really smart and knows his stuff.

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Participation is heavily important in this class. Grade is not given until finals week, important to contribute to class discussions and perform well in presentations. Gives great feedback and is a fantastic lecturer. Also brings in great guest speakers.
Very nice professor but you never know what your grade is until the end of the semester. Participation really matters. Only one final and hard to study for.
Participate as much as possible. Prof Tang is very nice, brilliant, and professional.
super dedicated to the craft and knowledgable. best class of my semester by far-- everyone loves Prof Tang. Exams were hard, but paper and group projects were reasonable. Highly recommend

The class is very discussion-based, and participation matters. Aim to participate once a week (every two classes) to get an A (A+ if your average is above this). The class only has one final, so make sure to do well, but it is reasonably easy since it's open-note. She is a great professor, is very smart, and makes the lectures very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tang is awesome. She is an engaging lecturer. She is also cares about her students. The class is participation-heavy (participation is a large part of your grade), so make sure to speak 1-2 times per class. The final exam is difficult, but if you actually understand the concepts and know how to apply them, you should be fine.

Professor Tang's lectures are decent at best, but her grading system is unclear and terrible. She does not make it clear how much participation/attendance counts for a grade, and your grade can be SEVERELY deflated at the end of the semester.

Professor Tang is sneaky. She led me on the entire semester, had me think I had one grade, then suddenly dropped me a full letter grade due to class participation. I would say I participated an average amount for people in the class, maybe even slightly above average. Lectures were interesting and engaging and exams/papers were difficult but fair.

Professor Tang is amazing!!! She makes the course interesting and engaging. She is definitely my favorite professor this semester. She is very caring and accommodating. Participation in class is very important. There are many works in this class, including exams, reading responses and papers, but she grades very generously.

Tang is my favorite professor this semester. The class is very chill and discussion-heavy. Her exams are a little challenging, but she will curve the exams. She also gives out extra credit for movie nights and participation in researches. Very accommodating during covid.

This man is the GOAT. Truly so understanding and kind and always willing to help you out. Also incredible at responding to emails. I had to take this class for my minor, and I am glad I took it with him. It is a difficult course, but he does his best to make sure you succeed. THE GOAT!

For such a boring subject, Professor Szpiro was an extremely kind and helpful professor. I had conflicts with every exam, and he worked tirelessly to help accommodate other students. Additionally, he has given some very helpful extra credit! Also, he starts every class with a joke, so that's fun.
nice professor
Amazing, supportive professor.
exams arent cumulative but can be hard sometimes, allows us to have a cheat sheet every exam, lots of opportunities to get extra credit. prof szpiro 10/10

Dr. Szpiro is very caring and understanding. That being said, the lectures honestly didn't help much for prelims. Just grind Mcgraw Hill and read the textbook. With so many cracked ppl in this class, the curve isn't lax but an A or A- aren't difficult to achieve. You're allowed a page of notes on tests, so the exam vibe is pretty chill.

The professor himself was an amazing person. This class was extremely difficult partly because of him and myself. THE TAS WERE VERY WEIRD THO. I once met with a Ta and he spent the time yelling at his girlfriend on the phone... Pay attention to lectures and the moment you get confused talk to him about it. He is very open and kind! lots of respect
Great professor, goes over content really well and class is organized in a way that makes learning easy
Professor Szpiro is the undisputed GOAT. Very caring, responsive, and understanding. The man wishes the best for the students and is very humble, one of the best at Cornell.

pros:
 - dr. szpiro is extremely kind, caring, and accessible. if you go to him with questions, he will devote his time to ensure you understand.
 - quick with emails

with accounting, practice makes perfect and the textbook is extremely helpful. couldn't recommend a better professor to teach this course.

Definitely my favorite professor so far at Cornell, his lectures are very clear and communicate the material in multiple different ways so that you will understand it. I had no experience in business but was able to do well because of him. Tests are open note, and there is plenty of practice material available. I'll miss the class for sure.

Amazing professor. He is very passionate about the subject and will make sure that you understand everything needed for the tests. He wants to see you succeed. The grading structure of the class is designed for you to do well, with 25% of the class grading being based on online HW and quizzes that you should easily be able to get 100s on.

One of the best professors I had. Lectures are decent and he really was passionate and excited everyday. Started every lecture with an accounting joke. Explained everything to you in a friendly, non-condescending way until you understood it and was very knowledgeable. Wouldn't want to learn accounting from any other professor. Exams are a bit hard

The nicest professor ever. He's a good professor, goes over the content in a way it's easily understandable, also explains any questions you may have really well. He makes sure you understand the concept before moving on. Just one slight issue is that he doesn't let you view the prelims unless you scored below the mean.

Great professor, he really tries to make the subject engaging. Attendance is not mandatory, grading is clear and fair, and there are lots of practice materials provided. Overall would highly recommend both the class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Szpiro is an amazing professor. He lectures at just the right pace, making some of the more complex material accessible. I especially appreciated his use of Panopto recordings, which are a valuable resource for reinforcing learning. Both the exams and homework assignments are fair.
Probably the nicest, most caring professor I've had a Cornell. He is truly exceptional and makes accounting fun and interesting.

Professor Szpiro is the best professor to learn accounting with! Not only does he try to make every class fun with a joke, he also explains concepts very well. Homeworks and pre-class quizzes are very reasonable and exams were very straightforward. Overall would strongly recommend taking this class with Szpiro.

Professor Szpiro has been one of my favorite professors at Cornell. His class is well-run, fairly structured, and he genuinely cares about his students. Professor Szpiro offers plenty of resources to succeed in his class with extended office hours times, extra practice assignments to prepare for exams, and chapter summaries to aid with studying.
Nice guy, put a lot of effort into organizing the class and tried his best to make accounting interesting. Exams were open book so not very hard.

This might be the worst class I've taken at Cornell. The lectures are nonsensical, unrelated, and redundant. She rarely engages with the course material and instead veers off on tangents throughout most lectures. She has little to no knowledge about AI, so anything she teaches about it are more speculative than grounded in reality

The class is very easy, but you won't learn anything.  Professor typically rambles on about random political topics, and she doesn't really understand technology.  I don't know how she got this teaching position.  Attendance is graded but it's not worth paying attention.

I really loved Professor Mitrano. Now I will acknowledge she is not everyones cup of tea. If you prefer very structured classes with strict schedules/ assignments, don't take this class. However, I thought that this class was helpful in addressing the societal impact of AI. Mitrano is so passionate and willing to meet students where they are.

Seminar-style class with a lot of readings, but is easy to do well in even if you don't read all the books. I appreciated prof bringing in guest lecturers (Google employee, other profs) to explain technical topics. Sometimes disorganized lectures but if you participate in every 2 lectures, you'll get full credit. Attending OH helped with essays.
