reviews.comment:
She really teaches to teach, not to get students ready for exams, and cares about your learning. 
The course is challenging. I was almost dropped since the history and constitution slavery etc lost me. But the work broadened my perspective. I think it all paid off

She means well, but her lectures are disorganized and poorly planned, with scribbles on the whiteboard and no clear connection between topics. I LEARNED NOTHING from it.
Great Professor

Prof. Mitrano is the most passionate, caring, and interesting Professor I've had at Cornell. Her teaching combines the history, legislation, and background context surrounding technology which helps tremendously to set the scene of what is going on in our world today. Amazing professor and person.

In one class, we talked about AI, copyright,  the constitution,  American revolution, slavery , Ancient Greece/rome , Slavery , non racebased slavery , Feudalism, Ferdinand and Isabella , Christopher Columbus ,incest,  and nation states. I did not learn anything. Please save your time.

I have never met a worse and distasteful professor in all my time at this school. A FAILED politician who is out of touch with students, class expectations, and reality. Her class is a disorganized mess with no grades in. Assigns 8 books for the semester and cold calls to see if we meet here unreasonable expectations. Shouldn't teach. RUN AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fantastic Prof! Made physics fun and engaging. Very cool in class demos + always available to students after class and in office hours. Super reasonable guy- if you need anything just ask him!
Amazing lecturer. Loved taking E&M with it and the grading is very fair.
He is such a cool guy. You can tell he's really passionate about the material. His prelims were fair and the workload was on the lighter side.

Tapping is the kindest and fairest professor you can get at Cornell. Lectures are easy to follow along, and he makes every class enjoyable. You will LOVE this class. It's not too hard to get a B in the class, but DO NOT slack off.

Super sweet and enthusiastic guy. You can genuinely tell teaching is a passion, and he does it well! Always receptive to feedback and willing to help everyone. Class isn't as easy as everyones making it out to be though, its still pretty difficulty, ESPECIALLY when magnetism is introduced. So participate in ur COOPs and stay on top of it :-)

Ryan Tapping is by far my favorite professor at Cornell. He cares so much about all of his students, and is truly enthusiastic about what he teaches. It is easy to do well in his class, because 45% of your grade is participation/homework. The exams are very doable. I hope Cornell recognises professor Tapping for his exceptional teaching.

He is a really nice guy and puts in the effort to make a nice learning environment. He seems to really care about his students and goes out of his way to try to make his lectures more enjoyable. The work is not light though its a physics course so you do get a bunch of homework and everything else that comes with a physics course.
chill dude. A little overrated in my opinion (people act like he is the best prof at the entire school which I don't think is true) but still deserves the five.
The single best professor I've ever had at Cornell. Go to lectures and sections and you'll do well.
Amazing dude, genuinely cares about student feedback and makes needed changes.
Teaches E&M in a very good and easy to understand way, fair exams, and is literally always happy and enthusiastic. the goat of E&M for sure
Goat of physics
Great lectures and honestly just an amazing person as well. He clearly cares about his students and tests are pretty fair. This class is very well taught. OH are very useful as well.

Dr. Tapping is one of the best lecturers I've had at Cornell. He puts a lot of effort into making the lecture material easily understandable and engaging despite it being inherently difficult to understand. I love the jokes and the enthusiasm he brings to each class. Exams are super fair, and lots of practice material is provided beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing person and professor. He was always genuinely excited about the content he taught. Now that I am in PHYS2214, I've never appreciated him more. Hes the GOAT.

I loved the in-class demos. Prof Tapping is so good at explaining concepts and demonstrating them. He genuinely cares for his students and helps anyone to understand. He is positive, and very passionate about what he's teaching. I enjoyed every single lecture and discussion.
Tapping is the GOAT!! He is super kind and will make surprise appearances at the LSC and TA office hours because he loves his students. The most iconic professor at Cornell.

Tapping is engaging and wants to help all of his students. He made a large lecture class interesting, even in a subject I wasn't that interested in. Tests were on par with material, but do the homework and practice problems.

Great professor!! He genuinely cares about teaching and engaging his students. I also liked how he had paper handouts of the lecture notes available as well. Exams were slightly difficult but fair. Problem sets were harder than the actual exams, but many office hours were offered.

Not only does this professor deliver amazing and engaging lectures, this professor is amicable, accommodating, and approachable. Exam content and homework grading is very fair. Supportive TAs. The class is structured very well and content is well reinforced. Pacing is the right balance to cover enough topics and have deep content understanding.

Tappings is one of the best proffesors I've had at Cornell! Super joyful and teaching engaging lectures. This class has discussion 2 days a week which is super helpful, exams are reasonable and similar to COOPs, PSets, and Lecture coverage. They also have office hours like 6 hours everyday of the week
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Tapping is unlike any other, he is so great. He is an amazing lecturer and actually seems like he enjoys teaching us. He is very approachable and responds great to student feedback. He makes learning E&M fun and his lectures are my favorite. I will miss the cat memes and the way he says hello each day.
DJ Ryan is the undisputed goat. In all seriousness, he is a great lecturer, very understanding, and the class is fair and super well organized.
Best professor I've ever had. Super understanding. Very reasonable work. Dr. Tapping, we love you and are lucky to have you!

Taken Spring 2024. Textbook is optional, he teaches so that you don't need it, it's just a reference. He teaches very concisely. Office hours are great. He even hosts office hours in between lectures. He puts in a lot of effort to help students and you can easily tell. Easy to talk to, open to feedback, and very humble. Thank you Ryan Tapping.
Extremely hard course but Ryan Tapping does his best to help all students. Make sure you attend all co-ops bc that's so much of your grade it will help makeup for the inevitably difficult exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had so far at Cornell. Very patient, encourages questions and makes sure you really understand the content in office hours. I loved attending office hours and thought they were extremely helpful. E&M itself is a hard subject but he explains it well in bare terms. He's very humble and open to feedback. Overall great guy.
Fun guy. Made an effort to go through many example problems in lecture which helped understand so much more than bullet point notes. E&M sounded very scary but this guy made it not that bad

Professor Tapping is one of my favorite professors so far at Cornell. I came into Cornell with a weak Physics background and have struggled at times because of it, but Tapping's excellent lectures and being extremely well-organized overall have made E&M so much more bearable for me.

Professor Tapping always makes sure lecture will be interesting and never comes to class without a demo prepared. I do not love physics but he makes it much more enjoyable, and also has a very fair grading system. The tests are not too difficult if you understand the homwwork assignments, and he always ensures you can get help if you need it

Prof. Tapping is wonderful. The class is very well organized, his lectures are clear, his homeworks and exams are all very fair. Tapping very clearly just wants everyone to do well and have a good time with the content. He's also just an all around really nice guy. He makes a historically hard subject accessible, even enjoyable.
I cry every night reminiscing about PHYS 2213. I will miss Ryan Tapping so so so much :'(

Ryan Tapping IS THE MAN. Best prof I've had thus far. Lectures and demos are awesome, COOPs are engaging, and I've learnt a ton. The best thing about Ryan, without a doubt, is his ability to listen and respond to student feedback - be it regarding a specific HW deadline, or even regarding the course structure as a whole, he is always on top of it!

Professor Tapping is the best STEM teacher I have ever had. He is so funny and an incredible lecturer. This is coming from someone who made a C in mechanics and is looking like they are going to make an A in this class. Beyond thankful to Ryan who made me feel like I can actually do this again. If you want to learn something, take this class!!!

Dr. Tapping is an amazing professor. He is truly one of a kind. I have so much respect for him. He made phys2213 enjoyable even though it was a hard class. His office hours were very helpful, and he is very patient with students. Thank you for everything Dr. Tapping and to all students taking his class in the future, please be nice to him.

Ryan Tapping is one of the best professors that I have had so far at Cornell. He completely turned around the Phys 2213 program, making a notoriously difficult class into something fun and interesting. His tests were fair and lectures engaging. Tapping is probably the most genuine and considerate professor I've seen.

literally the kindest and most amazing human being! i went to OH after our first prelim and it was completely empty. mans literally came in and talked with me for 3 HOURS; he came back at 11pm to see if i was still there, saying he felt bad for distracting me. he didnt leave till we finished the coop i originally came to OH to do.

Prof. Tapping did an excellent job with 2213, and it was clear from the start how important the class was to him and how much he cared about the students. Lectures and demos were engaging and fun. Though work was intensive, everything was fair.

Fantastic lectures, genuinely caring. His class is involving, and the material is difficult. But unlike others with the same description, he also makes you feel like you are respected, and there is a high level of tolerance.

Tappings is a very caring professor. It is very intentional that he makes 2213 an incredibly chill class. Compared to previous semester, the psets are very relaxed. The prelim is reflective of the psets and coops. Lecture wise, the demos are very cool and aids in conceptual understanding of the concepts. Honestly, no bad comments about 2213.

Dr. Ryan Tapping made sure that students were heard, advocated for, and made active efforts to make PHYS 2213 a better experience. I was originally scared because I heard horror stories about 2213 being tough, but he seriously made lectures enjoyable to attend. I would really recommend his course!

Funny dude - I really enjoyed his lectures. The course does not cover much content so discussions were constant review, didn't have to spend much time outside of class (please still study though). Exams were straightforward. You are set up to succeed in the class - wanted to put this review so students are deterred from taking his class, he's good.

Great lecturer excited about the material that tries to make sure that all students learn in his class. It is an interesting and enjoyable class if you stay engaged, as he also definitely cares about participation. Class doesn't have too much homework but requires paper reading. I and other friends all had positive experiences

Grading criteria never clear, terrible handwriting, poor time management, teacher doesn't care what student learn, too tough on details, recitation class misleading, encourage memorizing rather than learning.
The worst professor ever in my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is one of the worst professors I have ever had at Cornell.  The guy does not care about his students, never answers emails, barely gives any homework (which makes it impossible to study) and is so boring in lecture.  I think he really doesn't care if you do well or not and makes his tests really hard.  He also has awful handwriting.
Amazing teaching. Well organized study material and very helpful on asking questions. Lucid presentation on self assembly.

Very crappy professor. No website, not enough homeworks given, poor handwriting, and no assistance before examinations. I honestly think that he is one of the most lazy and unmotivated professors who simply does not care whether or not you learn anything. I learnt nothing and he sucks.
great professor, funny, clear, has a good understanding of material and seems very interested in what he teaches, helpful

The project has no rubric no matter how much you ask. Then you get a random grade a few peers come up with. Your project can be better than others but you will get a worse grade. learn very little in this class. Avoid this class please. Its just a shame there are not other good ML classes available. it forces people to take this class.
Her lectures are pretty interesting, and has a project-based approach.

very accomplished person but atrocious professor... put out one of the most poorly prepared prelims i have ever seen at cornell and came up with a very unfair and universally hated peer grading scheme that students abused to help themselves in terms of the curve
It is a difficult course, but if you work hard you will learn a lot. Recommend!

I find it difficult to believe that Cornell University would include this professor in its team of excellent professors. You can just skip class because the lectures are worthless. Support from TAs and Professors are also non-existent. The group projects are graded with unsupervised peer review, incentivizing people to sabotage others. Don't take.

Rarely am I compelled to post a review on Rate My Professor but this class was so horrible and utter garbage that I must insist. The class is hard for no reason at the expensive of learning, I can probably find more help from Scooby Doo than the Professor and TA team. There is no transparency in grading. Don't take any of her classes stay far away.

Udell's explanations were so unclear to the point that I had to google everything she said - the Internet did a much better job than her in teaching. Grading was not transparent - hw instructions and grading rubric were very vague. She made us do peer grading - this coupled with non-transparent grading incentivized students to sabotage their peers.

Probably one of the worst classes I've taken at Cornell. Udell is a confusing lecturer, and the TAs for the class are very focused on not giving you the answers to problem sets, even if it comes at the expense of a student's understanding. Very unclear and somewhat arbitrary grading rubrics. Avoid at all costs.

In MSE, you will probably have to take a decent amount of classes with Umbach. He is pretty not well-received as he doesn't teach well and tends to give grades arbitrarily based on personal feeling. You probably won't learn much in his classes and will def feel frustrated, but if you BS effort and try to seem nice, you'll get a better grade...

Umbach is a super nice guy and his office hours are key for the problem sets! However, the class itself is super disorganized and nanotech is such a broad topic that it sometimes seems like we're just learning random stuff. Prelims were okay, but quizzes were pretty bad
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: exactly what others talk about. He expects too much prior knowledge about chem and physics even if its engri class and the class is really boring and long.
Great professor! Definitely take as prospective ChemE or MatSci

Umbach, although tough, is an entertaining lecturer and a kind professor. Arguably, Nanotechnology is one of the hardest ENGRI classes, and as such, many people are disappointed with workload. However, the class was inspirational, and it completely changed my personal career path; as such, I highly recommend the class for motivated individuals

Decent professor. His lecture notes are extremely dense, but he posts all the power points which are very convenient for reviewing for prelims. For the most part the tests are fair. The homeworks didn't seem particularly useful but they weren't very hard. The material is often interesting, other times not so much. Overall a decent experience
horrible teacher. expects you to know too much. ridiculous tests and unfair grading policies. do not take nanotech!
He's super awesome. Love this dude.
No Comments
Long, long, boring lectures. Expects you to have prior knowledge about nano before the class. Class was very difficult.
Easy class, easy professor. Take it with Umbach.
i failed finance w another professor. ukhov makes info clear, practical, & understandable. it's almost like having a good professor can make a subject feel easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about his students, especially  if you go to class and get to know him. Loves athletes. His lectures tend to be long and a bit boring but great professor overall.

Such a cool guy. The stories/examples he uses in class are hilarious, but also teach you the material. If you go to him during his office hours he is extremely helpful! You don't have to attend class, but he may boost your grade up if you do go.
Legit professor of finance. hotel school sucks less with real finance professors like ukhov

Awesome professor/ class. Very funny and engaging lectures, often sidetracks to relevant current events. Straight-forward material, easy homework and exams. If you are looking for easy A and a practical, interesting class, this is it
Best prof in the hotel school

This guy is a boss.  Doesn't really care if you come to class but will bump your grade up if you do (not that you'll need it).  Class teaches you the basics of finance and he keeps it pretty simple.  A quality professor who knows his stuff.  Highly recommend it.
EASY TO PASS

My favorite professor at Cornell thus far. Extremely smart and knowledgable, and also willing to help his students in office hours. Go to office hours and get to know him-- he's a great guy with funny stories, and it will help you in the class. If you show up and pay attention, no reason you can't do well.
Took this class based off the rate my professor reviews and it went great. He's knowledgeable but sometimes disorganized when posting HWs/cases. Favorites blonde girls so you might be in luck.

This guy is hilarious. Has a heavy Russian accent, which makes his stories even funnier. Cares that you learn the material. Exams are much harder than the practice problems and homework he gives. But all in all, one of the best professors I've had simply for the pure entertainment value of his stories.
This guy and class are awesome.

GREAT Professor. had him for advanced corporate finance. new guy, but dont be scared, he knows what he is talking about and has a genuine interest in the students. Very helpful at office hours, and makes advanced corporate finance interesting. Oh, his random facts about the finance world are the great. All hail Buffet!

I had the privilege of taking three classes with the late Professor Uri Possen, including an independent study. He was one of my best and favorite professors at Cornell. He taught financial economics, a subject I loved. He helped me sign up for an internship, because of which I got the visa papers. Always there for his students. I miss you. RIP!

He doesn't explain the models in detail during the class, rather you should study on the textbook. However, he and his TA like to help students preparing the exams. He provides good insights on the current macroeconomic situation especially on fiscal policy and financial economics . Generous grader.
The problem sets is all that will prepare you for the tests. If you miss lecture, be sure to get the packets you missed.
His lecture is a bit tedious, but he is personally nice guy and always willing to help students. When you rely on textbook, which is the best i have ever seen, you can ace this course
Horrible teacher. Disorganized. His TA was worse than he was. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

Good Professor. Very interesting course. Go to all lectures and take good notes; cross-reference with the book and go to office hours for whatever you don't get, he'll appreciate you all the more. Start the paper assignment EARLY!!
Very interesting class, and a professor who has a great grasp of the material.
Really interesting course. I enjoyed it. Professor very clear and helpful.

I had literally already taken finance when I took this class, so it was kind of a joke. But he's not a bad guy. Strangely though, I got a higher grade in the Johnson school finance class I took previously than I did this one. Odd.
Hard to get by on just his lectures because they're so disorganized. Tests are fun though and he's very entertaining.
Cute professor. Probably one of the easiest chem professor in Cornell and I am not complaining. Good and helpful guy

This guy is so enthusiastic about his job that he makes me want to be a professor. And he loves chemistry and his lectures are always interesting. But wow, some of the homeworks and tests are pretty hard. And the concepts. The only issue with this guy is that he doesn't actually TEACH very well...

He's a great professor in one sense - he's very kind and funny and overall a really nice person.  Open to questions etc.  He sings in class and shows us amusing videos  But I don't feel like I learn chemistry from his lectures.  he just demonstrates calculations.  As with Zax, I feel like I learn the most from the supplemental prof Dr. Johnson.

Some like him since he's funny and charming, some don't since he wastes some time singing and telling stories.  I liked him not only for his stories and jokes, but because he really does know what he's talking about.  If you follow his lectures, you'll do well.
nice guy, but is one of the worst professors here. He moves very slowly, and lectures are absolutely pointless.
He is a cute person, with his silly songs that he sings and whatnot, but he is not a very good professor. Moves at a glacial pace through the material and lectures are generally useless.

Amazing Chem teacher who makes use of class time to make sure everyone understands the concepts by going over examples and demonstrations in detail.  He makes class fun and enjoyable with his personal anecdotes and songs.  Overall, great teacher and is a class everyone should take before graduating Cornell.
really old and cute with the besttt accent and i love when he sang opera he was so good! kind of a sucky chem professor though...

Love, love, love! Usher is a great professor and an outstanding opera singer. As long as you understand the lectures, textbook chapters, and how lab demonstrates what you're learning in class, you should be fine! Do plenty of practice problems, read the textbook, and go through lecture notes! Not a bad class if you know your stuff...

Going to his class is entertaining because he's funny and sings. But he doesn't go through the material fast enough, his homework assignments and labs involve material before it is covered in class. What he says in class is easy to understand, but he goes on tangents also.

he was fun (sang opera every day at the end of class, went off on funny tangents, had a preoccupation with the blackboard erasers), but did not get through enough material each week--had to learn a lot of  it on my own just to be able to do the homeworks and labs
awesome professor. exams are very fair and very similar to practice exams (20% of it comes from homework problems). he definitely makes the class interesting with his photos from greece and opera.

105 was kinda hard.  Only because his freestyle lectures were not supplemented with a textbook, so exams were pretty tricky.  He doesn't TEACH you how to do the problems in class, just shows you what you should know, but with no textbook this is hard to deal with, though I gotta love his singing, family slide shows and random episodes of Buffy.

His exams sometimes tested things that were specific examples during lecture. There are 3 prelims, 1 final, and no homework. This saves you time, but also gives you less of a grade buffer. I hate orgo, and even though he was entertaining with singing and stories, I couldn't wait for the semester to end. His digressions got annoying after a while.
His lectures are not particularly useful in learning the material. Use them to see what material will be tested and use the book and study guide.
A great professor and a great guy.

I was a little irritated for the first month of class when it was clear that the Chem 357 people were moving faster than we were. Than, Usher's pesonality, his genuine love for students and the realization that less work in Orgo was not necesssarily a bad thing won me over.

I loved orgo.  That has to say something about the teacher.  Yes he sings and digresses, but if you take notes, do the reading and the (optional) problem sets, you should be fine.  The LSC review sessions were helpful too.
We don't learn much, but you gotta love David Usher.  He sings us Opera and tells funny stories.  His New Zealand accent is charming too!

Very good lecturer.  First half of the class is really easy, because he won't teach much.  During the second half of the class, he will start to do a lot of catch up and cover many chapters in a week.

Very engaging lecturer. Prelims were based directly from the text and lectures. True/False of DEATH were useless... He could have prepared us better for CHEM 360, but the course was nonetheless entertaining and demanding.
Classes were very engaging. I love orgo because of this man. He rocks.

Very entertaining. Will definitely keep your attention in class. But from a learning point of view, this prof doesn't really cut it. He goes off on to so many tangents that we do not learn as much. He does well on the stuff he gets to.
Usher is the best! He makes class interesting, he sings opera to us, and he has a great accent.  I wish he was my grandpa!

singing was great and entertaining, but he did not really care to teach us! 357 people learned more than we did! even their prelims were harder than ours! so 360 turned into hell, cause we did not know enough from 359.  But can't argue, he is a great guy
I came to this class to learn orgo, not to hear some guy play his guitar. Someone should fire him.
I suck at the class, but I love him anyway!
he is a funny dude, and sings opera in class sometimes!
He made orgo interesting, and his tests are fair... tricky, but fair if you know your stuff.
This guy is CrAzY!!  in a good way...
He sang to us! Charming accent.
Highly entertaining class, especially for orgo.  He even sang to us
Hilarious and quirky! Love his accent.

I took this class over the summer, so idk if Thomas is different during the school year, but overall the class was fine, the hw was time consuming and the lectures were quite boring. prelims and final were open notes but still quite difficult.
Many kids are struggling in her classes. You're only graded on 3 exams and 5 homework sets. Office hours are limited and unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only slightly redeemable quality about this professor is her lectures are moderately enjoyable things about her class. I have given her the benefit of the doubt but it is clear she does not care if her students pass or fail. She is mean and nasty, I just sent her a question I had for exam and she replied "it depends" with no other explanation.
DO NOT TAKE! I earned an A, yet I still regret choosing this course. DO NOT put yourself in this situation!
Doing the HW and going to the lectures ain't enough. Half the stuff that are on the exams don't make sense. Gets mad for no reason and she's boring.

Extremely disorganized and poorly managed course! She is very unhelpful during interactions and dismissive of student concerns. She often creates unnecessarily difficult situations for students and lacks clear communication. Final exam was a complete disaster, 40+ mins late with no organized seating plan. Ppl were literally cheating in line.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I started the year attending every lecture... I quickly realised that was foolish and a waste of time. Her slides are poorly made and horribly taught. It was far more useful to spend class time self-learning all the concepts from the textbook readings. Also, her exams are 25 MCQ with no curve. Get 2+ questions wrong, and u can kiss an A/A- goodbye.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People who say Thomas is a 'bad teacher' or 'doesn't know what she's doing' simply don't go to lectures or do the homework. The class is extremely straightforward if you put the work into it. 1. Read the textbook, its not that bad. 2. Ask questions in lecture, she is very helpful. That's it. I never went to office hours but I'm sure they're helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Disorganized + careless. Professor mishandled the final: some students seemed to start 30–40 min early, discussed questions, took photos, and bragged about ChatGPT with no enforcement. Exam was nothing like practice/MindTap. Lectures felt rushed, questions dismissed, expectations unclear all semester. Grading felt arbitrary too. Avoid at all costs.
She's a lovely person and I had several insightful conversations with her during her office hours that I really enjoyed. Economics is just not for me, unfortunately.

lecture slides, hw, and practice prelims are SO UNREPRESENTATIVE OF THE REAL EXAM!!! not enough practice problems, class is 75% graded on exams, and exams are 25 MCQ!!! NO CURVE!!!! if you take this with her, be prepared to self-teach yourself EVERYTHING.
Do not take her ever.

Avoid intro with her! Lectures are boring. Her practice exams are in no way an appropriate reflection of the actual exams, and all exams are 25 question MCQs so if you get more than 2 wrong be ready for that B! Highly ineffective and made students line up to get the final exam which wasted more than an hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: THIS IS A JOKEEEEEEEE. Do not take this class no matter what like seriously. The prelims and final exam was literally insane, like the questions were so hard and nobody was prepared for that level of difficulty. Also she is actually evil like she made a class of 300+ students line up and sign in for the final exam, which wasted 45 min, like what??

Avoid Econ with Thomas if you can. I left lecture every day feeling worse about the content than I had self-studying. Her slides are badly done, horribly explained, and whatever "group work" she had us do was irrelevant to the test. Prelims are 25 questions, no curve, so the difference between letter grades is often 1 question wrong. HW also sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's really hard to study for the exams—her practice prelims and homework's don't reflect the difficulty of the final exam at all. The exams basically decide your grade so they're really important, too. No one goes to lectures because she doesn't teach well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Stephanie Thomas is an ineffective, disorganized teacher. She will cover surface-level material during lectures, but you'll have to know the material on the bottom of the iceberg for exams. There were dozens of typos on the second prelim, and a question on the final had no correct answer... in a class with 15+ CAs.

Greg Mankiw is the GOAT!

Consistent exam errors and refuses to curve despite low medians. Claimed the historical median was a B, after our final, contradicting the syllabus stating that it was a B+. Extremely disorganized—made two sign-in lines for 200+ students, wasting 40 minutes of our time. Ironic for an economics professor who preaches efficiency but practices none.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE ECON 1110 WITH THOMAS! All of the exams were the weirded in the worst way possible you would probably get a better score if you guessed. Also constant typos and errors in exams.. For example she forgot to put THE ENTIRE ACTUAL QUESTION for one problem and just gave a graph and answers and then "forgot" to add a correct answer to another

ALERT: DO NOT TAKE. Lectures are useless as she just reads off the slides. Prelims and finals are only 25 multiple-choice questions, worth 75% of your grade, and she refuses to curve. Also, she drags lectures way longer than needed. Worst class I have ever taken. If she took her own class, I don't think she would pass. I would give 0/5 if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The actual tests were very different from the practice tests. Also, many people were able to cheat on our final due to the way she organized it.
actual exams are so different from practice exams and only 25 questions on each gives little room for error. poor at answering student questions and dismisses concerns about exam difficulty.

Take Econ 1110 with any other professor. Her lectures are very elementary compared to exams. This class was much harder than it should've been and I did almost all my learning through youtube (DrAzevedoEcon you are the GOAT) and through the textbook. Also, do not be fooled by her open note policy as I found it was not as helpful as it seemed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pt1) This class was unequivocally the single worst organized class I have ever taken in my life. In fairness, to  Prof Thomas I never went to lectures so she might be a good lecturer, but the difficulty of the material was far from the problem in the course. 25 multiple choice questions does not work.
do not take this class

Professor Thomas can be a tough grader, but going to office hours makes a big difference. The class requires a lot of work, but using resources like unstuck ai can help with study prep.

I only went to one class, then skipped every lecture. From my experience, the lecture was very surface-level and not worth your time. However, this course is completely doable through the online textbook. Major benefit is that all her prelims are online and open-book.

Everyone here is so dramatic, the open note part of this class makes the tests completeable without studying lol

not good

Actually going to class is not necessary. nice person but super boring lectures. reviews.comment: Prof. Thomas is one of the most amazing and involved teachers/professors I have ever had! I took ECON 1110 as part of the summer session, and, as only a rising junior in high school, was initially worried I would struggle in the class. But, Prof. Thomas helped me so much and made sure to explain everything in a way anyone could understand! Amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Spends too much time on very simple examples, doesnt always cover all the material that is on the homework.

Prof. Thomas is great. She's always available for one-on-one meetings (as long as you schedule a week or two in advance) and really explains material in a way that YOU can understand. She'll break lecture questions, homework/prelim questions, and textbook jargon down a thousand times without getting the least bit upset or frustrated. Solid 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took her class over the summer. It wasn't too hard. Her review lectures were extremely helpful. I liked all of her lectures. She made the class very interactive. She used students as examples in some problems. The only tough thing about this class is the homework. There's a problem set that is due about every other class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: There are three major exams in one semester: two premiums and one final. The first premium is very easy, and the second one is harder, and the final is the hardest one. Her class is lecture based from the textbook. I recommend you to read text book first before taking class. Her homework always takes one to two hours to finish.
Tests can be a bit tricky sometimes. But if you get to know her and meet her during office hours, you can definitely do a lot better on exams and get full credit on your homework!!

She seems like a nice person from her first lecture but this is extremely misleading. Over the semester she went from nice to terse and this also was evident in her lecture slides. The material itself is decent but the final is actually unbearable. If you can, try to find a different professor.
Good class, good lectures and not a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Gave ridiculously low participation grades out of nowhere to the entire class, grades way too harshly for a class that has no difficult material, but since her lectures are useless, you learn nothing
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor, but the final was a joke. She claimed that it would be "slightly more difficult" but it was significantly harder. The first two prelims are ridiculously easy and the online hw and attendance will help your grade. If you don't want a class where essentially your entire grade depends on one test, don't take econ with Thomas.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Thomas relies on online problem sets, the grading system for which can be confusing/frustrating. The prelims are underwhelming but they leave you unprepared for the math-heavy final if your TA doesn't make problem sets. As long as you put effort into attendance, homework, and the prelims, you should still do well even with a rough final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prelims are very easy- direct questions from the practice prelims. Homework isn't that bad if you read the textbook. She makes the final impossible though so that she can have the satisfaction of failing a few people. Take her if you think you can reteach yourself all the course material for the final otherwise try to find a new professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She uses iclickers to take attendance, so be sure to show up. Her grading is easy (makes the lower prelim grade worth less) and the prelims were almost identical to the practice. The class is fairly easy and she is very clear in lectures. Read the textbook and you can get an A.

Class was easy, didn't do well because I didn't put the effort in. If you read and study (maybe an hour a week), you'll easily get at least a B+. Online quizzes (answers online too) are the homework and you can miss like 3 or 4 of them. Prelims are tough and test on material mentioned for maybe one paragraph. But if you study, you'll be fine.

Her lectures are almost completely unrelated to her problem sets and tests. Goes over very broad, general topics in class, then expects students to do a lot of math and whatnot on the problem sets. So, you have to carefully read the textbook and the accompanying appendices (which are pretty confusing) in order to do the assignments.

It was her first year teaching. Having taken AP Microeconomics in high school, I was cruising through the course with a 94 average up until the final, where I received a 68. The open ended of the final was nothing like the other prelims and purely on memorization, not analysis or critical thinking. Overall, not bad but she has to restructure.

What a great professor! Lectures are very clear.  I walked away from each class feeling like I had really learned something. Tests are VERY fair based on class and textbook material. Highly recommend.

Stephanie Thomas is an amazing lecturer. Her lectures are clear and you hardly leave without understanding the topic she discussed. She's also very funny and knows how to relate theoretical concepts to real life, which is really hard to do for a theoretical subject like Economics. Would definitely recommend.

The first two tests were typical economics tests, if you know your stuff you will do fine. Multiple choice was fair, short answer was fair (just graphs and numbers). However for final exam the short answer was memorization. Memorization should not belong in short answer. The mean and median for the final exam was much lower than the two prelims.

I still haven't gotten a final grade, which is absolutely absurd. Half her exams are done on a scantron (only 2 short answer questions, plenty of TAs).  There is no reason for her to take over 2 weeks to return grades, other than not managing her class/TAs sufficiently.  Ended on a bad note. Wish I knew my final grade to comment on other aspects...

Her wait time for grades is absolutely ridiculous sometimes. Plus, her tests are also very irrelevant to what we're actually taught in the course so it's very easy to wait a long time for a frustratingly bad grade. Overall though, she's not a bad teacher.

Lectures reiterated the textbook. This was the first time Thomas taught 1110, and it showed in my opinion. Tests were not relevant to course material. I found Thomas to be abrasive; when my scantron for the final was not initially read I received a very accusatory email stating I would be receiving a 0 for the final when it was a computer error.

Her lecture quality and teaching is fine, but she needs a lot of work on the grading aspect. People learn econ pretty well, yet only 3 exams are given and they're mostly irrelevant so most people do bad, thus their grades inaccurately represents their knowledge. Plus, she has the longest wait time for grades I've ever experienced for a professor.

It's not that Thomas is a bad professor, it's just that her tests didn't reflect her lecture material whatsoever. Our final didn't have any of the most recent material on it and the average was a 72. Enough said. This is an intro/basic business class. It's not the type of the class that should have a C- average on 2/3 tests.

Exams are not easy, and you need to study very hard for them. You know who goes to office hours or not because she calls on some kids by first name, so it probably helps to get to know her. You must go to lecture, and you have to stay on top of your work.

She wants you to do well and is willing to provide extra help if needed. We have iclickers so you must attend 20/25 lectures. This was her first semester teaching intro micro so she had limited material for us to usse which was difficult. When I was studying I felt like I wanted to study more but had no worksheets or anything to study off of.

Thomas is an amazing teacher. For those who may have not understood econ prior, she is able to break it down in a way that actually makes sense. She assigns just the right workload -- not too overwhelming, but not a walk in the park. She is also able to make the topic interesting, which is a huge plus because Labor Econ can easily be boring.

I'm not completely sure how this professor is at Cornell. I've ever met a less engaging and more annoying person in my life. I mean truly the worst experience of my academic career. I look at the clock and it doesn't move in this class. I've learned nothing. Made a course that should be interesting so incredibly boring.

reviews.comment: The least engaging course I've ever sat through its a complete an utter waste of time and money. They cannot lecture whatsoever. My friend is sleeping as I write this

ICL is an easy class, no idea why the grade is this low. Her section is about Europe (particularly France/Germany), which is probably the section you'll go into with the most understanding. questions 1-5 on the final are worth 10% each. DO THE LAST QUESTION FIRST its worth 50% and takes a lotta time. Lectures were interesting readings were helpful
Solid professor.

Writing this before I get my grade back on the first exam. She assigns ~50 pgs of reading/week and isn't the best lecturer. IMO she could improve on linking examples in class to key concepts needed for exams. (this is coming from someone with a >4.0 GPA). This class would also REALLY benefit from having a discussion section (idk how it doesn't)
How does she expect students to write so much techincal explanation requried writings in such  a short span
She can't teach, the study guide could be alot better but is making the whole process a torment.
Lots of reading for this class but if you keep up and pay attention, and work on the study guide you will do well. In class, you sometimes have discussions with your peers.

The worst lecturer of the four professors in this class. Painfully boring, disengaging lectures, and a droning voice. I'm unsure how she became a professor because she has zero public speaking skills. The content is all over the place and doesn't follow a logical sequence. I managed to get an "A" by cramming the study guide.

Good lectures with a lot of reading. The professor makes the class interesting with a good balance of lectures and discussions. Tests are based on the study guide, but grading is done by TAs, which can vary. My TA was harsh and inconsistent. Beware of the final and potential grading issues, but the professor is nice, and you'll learn a bit

reviews.comment: Enjoyed her portion of 2350 the most. Very clear lecture slides and teaching. If you do the readings and pay attention in class it is easy to do well.

Prof K is the man! The first part of the course is tough - but once you get used to the style - proofs, quizzes, assignments, things click nicely. His lectures are amazing. Plus he is a really nice guy. I learned a lot too.

This is one of the best courses I have taken at Cornell.  The professor is great and super enthusiastic. I love the lectures and the office hours were very helpful. Really good TAs too. I am seriously considering switching to an ECE major.
Professor Krishnamurthy is the most caring and sincere professor I have had at Cornell. Homeworks were difficult, but his lectures were awesome. Loved his class!!
nicest professor I have ever had
Very kind and went out of his way to help students

I did this class in spring 2024 and enjoyed it a lot. He is a very smart guy, and he is very caring too. ECE 2720 is offered both semesters but the instructor changes each semester. One of the best ENGRD courses I have done

The best sophomore class at Cornell I have taken. Prof Krishnamurthy is inspirational in the class. He went out of the way to  explain the assignments in the office hours. I strongly recommend this course as an ENGRD requirement. The assignments are difficult and time consuming but u learn a lot. Prof. K really knows his stuff.
Ok instructor. Bad PhD guide

Professor Krishnamurthy is #1 professor. I really liked the way he structured the class and focussed on what you learn rather than cramming for the quiz. He would stop by in TA's office hours and would ask every student if they have any questions/concerns which is super nice of him! He is genuinely the best professor I have ever met :)

Very caring and understanding professor! He actively takes feedback from students and is generous about giving extensions. Assignments were difficult but interesting and engaging. Final was take home, and he deliberately tries to maximize grades. So long as you hold up your end of the deal and stay engasged, he'll take care of you.

One of the best classes and one of the most caring professors out there. He took constant feedback from students and implemented it in the classroom. Grade determined only using in-class quizzes and a take-home final. Definitely recommend taking the class with him!

This is an excellent and mathematically heavily rigorous course. I am a CS-major.  I did not know that linear algebra had so many real world applications. This guy seriously rocks, he is very approachable. The assignment take a lot of time. But no prelims :)  One of the best courses at Cornell by far. Final exam will be take-home.

(FA2021) He spent a lot of time on how very basic calculus he would re-teach (a course prerequisite) is graduate material and that the course material was invaluable for interviews. He taught algorithms by putting code onto slides in one giant PDF. Generous grader, but stressful since you need to rely on Google to complete homework.

Vikram is an amazing prof if you are looking for a mentor who pushes research like a company CEO and is into publishing paper like a product. He extensively manages his students keeping track how much time they spent on research etc and if the money is being utilised well for the time you spend on research. If you like that style, you will love him

Best ECE professor at Cornell. I learnt a lot in the course, lots of cool math with real life applications. The professor was super enthusiastic and accessible. His lectures were fantastic. Homeworks were hard, but very useful for understanding material.

I took ECE 2720 with Professor Krishnamurthy in Fall 2021. It's definitely one of the best classes that I've taken at Cornell. The course introduces students to numerous topics in data science and ML. Homework assignments were always challenging but fruitful. Exams were very similar to practice exams.

Professor Krishnamurthy made sure to give insight on data science and statistics throughout lectures, often explaining how this type of material may come up during tech interviews. Problem sets focused heavily on Python, often making it tedious, but he made sure to give good practice problems/expectations for the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He genuinely wants his students to do well. He is really passionate about what he does. He cares more about us understanding the content than getting the exact right answers and his homework and exams are graded accordingly. He actively asks for feedback and follows through on it. A really sweet and understanding guy who cares about his students:)

Professor Krishnamurthy is extremely intelligent and passionate about the material he teaches. He is very easy to contact outside of class and would respond to my emails about the class almost within an hour. In addition, he took measures listen to our feedback by giving homework drops and notes on slides. Overall a great professor!

His ECE 2720 is the most versatile, rigorous course I have taken. Feels like a proper 3000 level course. Covers an insane variety of very useful topics. Everyone should take this course. Although the instructor for this course changes every semester.

Super chill, very accessible and encouraging. A very intelligent professor who knows his stuff. His lectures are math-focused and he covers a lot of materials, and he gives a quiz every lecture (but they are pretty easy). But no prelims so what you get out of the course is entirely dependent on your own interests and initiatives.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The grade for this class is primarily based on attendance. Each class, you have to submit printed copies of either three poems or three pages of prose. There is no feedback on these submissions unless you bring them to workshop classes. Prof. was often very serious during class, which made her feel unapproachable and discouraged participation.

Lyrae is one of the most incredible teachers, and inspiring people I have ever met. I came into her class hating poetry and left after every class understanding something knew about poetry, literature, and life. She cares about her students, engages the class and facilitates great discussions. Take her class. She's amazing.

Lyrae is art incarnate. She's inspirational and brings out the artist in everyone. If you don't have semi-thick skin expect some exfoliation, especially if you have little exposure to creative writing. But if you stick through it I promise she'll make you a better writer and a better human. I love her  and you'll love her. Go for it.

Lyrae is a walking inspiration. I took Advanced Poetry with her, and I can honestly say that she completely changed my perspective on writing, and transformed me from a dabbler to a poet. She has given me confidence. She is also sassy and hilarious. Take advantage of this opportunity to take a class with such an amazing human being.

S:106. Avoid if possible. More than half of the initial class dropped w/in the first week. Harsh and biased grader. Quite mean when things don't go her way. Has stated that she does not like the KIfW. Assigns "group essays". Course books are perverse &/or boring. Deceptively changed the course title. Does not use internet. Great poet, bad teacher.

Both the midterm and the final were very similar to the practice tests, so everything felt very fair. He clearly puts effort into making the course run smoothly and explains the material well. The homework was lengthy, but it helped reinforce the concepts. Overall, he is a strong instructor and I learned a lot from the class.
Homework does not relate to the test. Lectures are confusing. Final are much harder than the review. Do the test review and one page he give you. You can pass

No curve. Cares more about the TAs than the actual students. Boring lecturer. Truly the worst experience ever with a professor. The final was uncharacteristically hard and he really doesn't seem to care about the student. He shouldn't teach this course!

reviews.comment: good class. fun homeworks. little hard exams but very helpful TAs and very accomodating professor

reviews.comment: I dont know why his rating is so high. His lectures are boring and why did he yell at us saying we needed intro stat and then explain slope to us. Like everyone in the class is IS or ORIE... we do not need to relearn this. move on. Also he's not funny.

Wilkens is a good lecturer, but p-sets were long and didn't always directly connect to lectures. ChatGPT helps a lot. The course was more technical than humanities-focused, despite the title. It didn't feel terribly different from other intro data science courses. I had high hopes for this class, but it fell short for me. Not horrible though.

I do not recommend this class. Random class attendance quizzes and lectures were not useful for the problem sets. The problem sets were beyond impossible and everyone used GPT for them (and still struggled). When it was time for the final project, everyone I know did very badly bc there were no guidelines. don't take this course, the median was B-

Incredibly long and tedious psets. Could be done adequately by chatGPT, which defeats learning objectives of this course. Unclear grading criteria and bad assignment turnarounds such that we could not improve for future assignments, particularly for the final.

Unclear grading criteria. Good chance you get like a letter grade lower than you think. Not really open with us, and would often say in office hours stuff like "yeah this would be fine" and then mark off points from you. Amazing TAs (especially the head TA, who would give out help to anyone who needed it, bless her), but I don't like him.

Wilkens is an excellent professor. I took 2950 with him previously, and he never fails to explain concepts slowly and meticulously. While the psets are challenging, Wilkens and his TAs are very approachable and helpful. Clearly passionate about teaching, Wilkens definitely belongs among the best at CIS.

The lecture could only help with about 3% of the homework. I spent two nights trying to understand the codes, but the grading just proves that GPT wins the human brain. I don't understand now what is the point of going to lectures and doing the homework if eventually we are all forced by the homework to use ChatGPT to get high grades.

Surprised to see so many positive reviews. So far, everyone I know in this class has complained about how long the homework is. Questions are marginally related to what he talks about in lectures and grades take way too long to release. People who buy ChatGPT premium receive the highest grades, which says a lot about how this class is run.

Professor Wilkens is one of the best professors I've ever had. He is incredibly engaging and makes the content that he is teaching so enjoyable. He is accessible outside of class, and shows care for each and every one of his students. He wants his students to learn and enjoy learning at the same time. Without a doubt best professor at Cornell.

Professor Wilkens is indubitably the most caring and passionate professor I have met. His lectures are engaging, and he genuinely cares about students' understanding. The grade was based on a semester-long project, 8 problem sets, a midterm, and a final. The workload can be challenging, but Professor Wilkens and his TAs will help you succeed.

Wilkens is by far one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. He's a very captivating speaker, great at answering questions, charismatic, and funny. He does move slowly through content, but as someone who is relatively new to stats and data science, I appreciated the pace. I would 100% take a class with him again!
I love his classes. The level of difficulty of lectures and homework is perfectly set. I also love how he organizes the contents
My favorite professor at Cornell so far. He's extremely approachable, explains stuffs really well and genuinely cares about students.

Hands down one of the best professors I have had at Cornell, and that was in his first semester here and during the pandemic. He did a great job balancing the CIS side of the course with the implications/impact in the humanities. He was extremely caring, made sure the teaching staff was flexible, and actively sought out and implemented feedback.

He began every zoom class by chatting with students, frequently asked if the material made sense to everyone, and granted extensions.

Writing assignments were primarily completed in class, which means the only real homework was reading! This was my favorite class ever. We read engaging books, watched an awe-inspiring documentary, and had our emotions wrenched by two spectacular films. I loved this class because I feel more knowledgeable and more intellectual for having taken it.
Amazing lecturer. Gets sidetracked sometimes but mostly interesting, educational content. Dry humor. Tough grader at first, but gives great steps to improve.

reviews.comment: ITAL 1113 is one of the best courses I've taken. Her lectures were incredible, each on a different reading focused on historical and social contexts of the 20th century. She is also very kind and really cares about her students. A great class!

Professoressa is such a delight to learn from. Having had her for 2 semesters now, I can confidently say that she is one of the most understanding professors here at Cornell! If you are going to learn Italian I HIGHLY, HIGHLY, HIGHLY recommend it be with her. You will thank yourself for picking one of the best Cornell professors around!

Professoressa KVW was my favorite professor I have had at Cornell so far. She is so elegant, intelligent, caring, and has an incredible sense of humor. There was a lot of daily homework that was went over each class (she cold calls), but it is not too hard to complete and is helpful. She genuinely cares a lot about her students and the class a lot.

Best professor i've ever had at this school. She is the coolest, nicest, funniest teacher who truly wants you to succeed. Never a dull moment in the class either. Would highly highly highly recommend taking any class you can with her.

I loved this course!! I left the class with a concrete understanding of Jewish Italian life before, during, and after WW2. We had a lot of reading and were given short quizzes on each reading. The majority of writing was short, nontraditional pieces that allowed me to apply my learning to emails, grant applications, and fictional pieces.

She is an incredible person in every way. She is very knowledgeable and hilarious. Every class is a lot of fun with her. This course requires regular studying, and there is a lot of homework, but it is not an issue as long as you pay attention to what is being done in class. She is also very understanding when you have a problem.

Hands down one of the best classes I've taken at Cornell and the best language class over all. Professor Wittelsbach is not only a great teacher but extremely kind and considerate. The work load is pretty intensive but as long as you conplete it diligently you will do well on the exams and projects.

Professoressa was the best Italian teacher I had. She is so funny and also really good at explaining difficult grammar. She was never mean or aggressive like other Cornell italian teachers were when explaining even the most basic things. There is a lot of homework but you go over it in class and she explains everything.

Professoressa is one of the smartest, most caring professors I have had at Cornell. This is an amazing class that teaches both a broad overview and the nuances of Italian art, architecture, and fashion. Very engaging lectures with minimal homework (only meets once per week). Would highly recommend to anyone with any Italian background!

Took this class due to the lack of other FWS available. On the first day, she said she would assign the maximum number of pages of reading per week and assigned a quiz for the second day of class. Heard from a friend that quiz was extremely specific and needed to know many miniscule details. The first lecture was extremely boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework was minimal for ITAL 1213. All the texts were in Italian - they're not easy, but the she breaks it down in class so you can understand it. The content was interesting, although it prioritizes breadth over depth. Professor von Wittelsbach is very knowledgeable and her passion is contagious.

I gained a love for Italy and Jewish history. The wide variety of topics covered provided a vivid picture of Jewish life in Italy as it evolved through time. Prof's knowledge on the subject is unparalleled, and her passion contagious. She brought guest speakers in with different perspectives and backgrounds, and I was encouraged to ask questions.

The professor is very knowledgeable and knows what she is doing. I've learned so much in just one semester and enjoyed the class a lot. Be prepared to study and have hw daily tho. I had a background in Spanish so it is easier, but I imagine a lot of effort needs to be put in if one doesn't know a Romance language. However, it is totally worth it!

Professor Von Wittelsbach was an amazing professor. She is extremely informed on the topic that she teaches and has a wide range of knowledge on this fascinating topic. This was the one class that I did not want to miss because I felt that I would miss out on true learning. Show effort and interest in the topic and class and you will do well.

Easily one of the best professors at Cornell. Clear passion for the language and loves to teach it. Each section is filled with cultural and historical anecdotes. Witty, funny, intelligent, and genuinely cares about each of her students. Strongly recommend Italian at Cornell, especially with KvW. Prepares well for study abroad as well. Must take!

Truly one of Cornell's finest. Professoressa offers a wealth of Italian language and cultural knowledge. Her class is work, but languages are her passion. She is very professional and cares about her students, rewarding genuine effort above all. She's incredibly witty and intelligent. Thanks to her, I feel quite prepared to study abroad in Italy.

Wittelsbach is a fantastic professor! The class is very speaking heavy, and there is a lot of paper homework that the class period is dedicated to checking over. There were tests, a final, and an oral exam, but they were easy (about one page long). You learn so much Italian in her class; she is hilarious!

It was a paper-based class, so will need to get textbook and print stuff. I personally liked the Friday lectures in language learning center because she showed us some fun materials besides textbook, such as music, opera and interviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Be prepared to speak in class but overall a great professor.
Great instructor who teaches a lot about Italian language and culture

I didn't really learn a lot of Italian from this class, although I did appreciate the Italian culture that was taught. I think it's hard to learn much when the course is held only once a week, but it did make homework easy. Be prepared to speak, whether it be holding a conversation or reading class material.

Extremely attentive and kind with a wealth of knowledge of Italian as well as other subjects; creates a positive, fun, focused environment; encourages students to be joyful and inquisitive; teaches many creative, effective strategies, applicable to other languages; thanks to her, I can now write, read books, listen to music and speak in Italian.

Professoressa is easily one of the best professors I have had at Cornell. Each seminar was planned very well and classes were filled with cultural and language anecdotes. It really is amazing how much of the language you learn in one semester. Don't be scared by the 6 credits -- the work is fun and manageable. Must take a class with Professoressa!

Easily the best professor I've had at Cornell. Professoressa von Wittelsbach is witty and sharp, and beyond Italian language, she brings many cultural notes that textbooks don't teach. 1401 was work but honestly very manageable--don't let it being six credits scare you. I improved so much thanks to her and am even pursuing an Italian minor now

Wow. There is not much to say. One of the most professional professors I have ever had in my educational career. Although the class has a lot of work, it is very manageable and super interesting. Professor Von Wittelsbach has a passion for what she is teaching and it shows. Take this class!

Professor von Wittelsbach is witty and caring. Her lectures are so engaging and detailed, and she covers the material well. In class, she tries to form close relationships with each member of the class. Each session is delightful and full of learning. Highly recommend to take this FWS and potentially an Italian language class with Professora.

Professoressa von Wittelsbach is a wonderful and passionate lecturer who truly cares about each of her students and ensuring that they learn the language. This class was interesting and I had a lot of fun with interacting with the language in various ways and it helped me strengthen my knowledge in Italian. It was a great experience overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I was originally not signed up for Professor Von Wittelsbach's FWS, but I am so happy that I moved into her class. Every class is very entertaining, with tons of personal anecdotes and quips. This class is somewhat reading-heavy, but every book we read was super interesting. Professor Von Wittelsbach is truly one of the most wonderful professors.

Take this class!!!!! It's amazing how much Professor von Wittelsbach genuinely cares about her students learning the material. She's also extremely knowledgeable and a very entertaining lecturer who isn't afraid to speak her mind. Her brilliance shines in every class and I will definitely remember some of her quotes/advice for years to come.

Professoressa overall is a good professor. I will say this class was much more challenging than Italian 1 and 2, and was more commitment than I was expecting for a simple language requirement. However, I will give credit where credit is due and say that Von Wittelsbach pushed me out of my comfort zone and did improve my knowledge of the language.
no comment
Everybody has to take Professoressa's class once at least. So witty, intelligent, and honest (also beautiful as a bonus!). Learning a language has never been more fun.

I was only so lucky to have taken Professoressa von Wittelsbach's Italian class for my last semester, but I was able to make considerable progress in my understanding of the Italian language and culture. Her lectures sprinkled with personal anecdotes and references from Latin, Greek and many other languages were always interesting.

I feel very lucky having participated in this wonderful course of Professor Von Wittelsbach. She is caring, humorous, and very methodological regarding the learning approach. It helps us a great deal get used to new languages and absorb hard grammar material. Every lesson was filled with laugh. I had a great time being her student.

Genuinely Professoressa von Wittelsbach is such an amazing lecturer. She has a very rare kind of old-school intelligence you do not see often in professors here (most just want to churn out students who can repeat the right things). If you want to learn the cultural nuances of Italian in a chill environment, she is definitely the professor to take.

Professor von Wittelsbach is without doubt one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. Not only is she an engaging lecturer, but she also really cares about her students. She never hesitated to give extra time on an assignment when I needed it and was sure to give really helpful and detailed feedback so I could do well. 

Definitely take!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was extremely difficult, but it improved my Italian skills like no other. Profesoressa definitely demanded a lot from us, but I thought that it was worth it in the end. I didn't realize that I learned so much until halfway through the semester.
Get ready to be yelled at, have random work assigned at random times of the day due two hours later, and not want to come to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Loved Professor Wittelsbach's class so much! Definitely take. She's super caring and is a great lecturer

She is without hesitation the finest educator I encountered at Cornell, with an extraordinary ability to connect with students on a personal level while, on an academic level, encouraging them beyond their comfort zone: a critical ingredient for building linguistic confidence.

Took this 6 credits/5 days a week. Sign up if you want public humiliation, class anxiety, and a lot of work. I admit to learning a lot of Italian and great prep for 2201 but very tense Zoom classroom. Only had her camera on once in the whole semester. All the A/A+, best students were previously fluent in a Romance language.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: For ITAL1401, don't expect her to hold your hand. You'll need to do lots of work outside of class, but really it's your fault if you signed up for an intensive and can't handle it. She's a bit scary at first, but after a few weeks you'll realize that as long as you prepare, she's an excellent guide, super understanding, and genuinely hilarious!

Professoressa von Wittelsbach is one of the most caring, compassionate, and kind people you'll have teaching you. During covid, she was always ready to be flexible and understand that we might need more time to finish assignments. Her lectures were also always interesting and given with humour and wit! TAKE her class!!

Professoressa knows what shes doing. Its crazy how much Italian you learn in one semester, and it really doesnt feel like work. You have to study for this class, but the tests are fair and very stressful. She has an amazing heart, and cares about her students a lot.
There really is no reason not to take this class. Profesoressa is funny, smart, and really cares about her students. If you show up, do the readings, and be respectful, youll do well.

Professor von Wittelsbach is amazing! Every class is interesting, and you not only learn about Jewish Italian Lit and writing, but also about culture and life. This class helped me become well-rounded and to stand out in job interviews. Although the class isnt easy, the workload is manageable and her grading is very fair.

Professor von Wittelsbach was the best professor I've had at Cornell. Her teaching made my writing extremely concise and I genuinely enjoyed attending her class. If you have the space in your schedule, you should make an active effort to include her class.

Professoressa made lectures interesting and fun while allowing you to practice Italian with peers in a comfortable environment. She also provides helpful study tips and does all she can to help you succeed in learning the language. Follow directions closely, participate in class, and send all your emails to her in Italian! Great professor.

1401 was the first Italian class I had ever taken and Professoressa von Wittelsbach pushed and encouraged me to learn the language with every class. Her teaching style is a great balance of challenging, but fair and rewarding if you put in the work. She genuinely cares about your progress in learning the Italian language and culture. Great class!

Professor von Wittelsbach truly cares about her students. She provides thorough feedback on assignments, and is always willing to help. The material was interesting, valuable, and the classes were very engaging. The coursework was heavy at times, but manageable because of how understanding she is. I would strongly recommend this FWS!

Participation and preparation matter in Prof. von Wittelsbach's courses. But if you put in the (usual) effort, you will be rewarded with a great grade. Moreover, I think Prof. is the kindest professor on campus. Always willing to help out with coursework and with ventures outside the classroom. Must take a class with Prof. before graduation!

Professor von Wittelsbach was one of the most accommodating and understanding professors I have had this semester. The coursework was engaging, fun, and manageable. She grades assignments thoroughly and provides great feedback. The class was collaborative and very interesting. I recommend this course to everyone as it was my favorite this semester!
Not a fun class. Very demanding with unhelpful and rude professor

FRESHMEN, TAKE THIS FWS!!! One of the most interesting classes I took my freshman year. Professor von Wittlesbach is so knowledgeable, and I could have listened to her talk about anything. A great mix of reading, movies, and guest lecturers. You learn essay, email, and fiction writing. I think everyone got an A, some an A+

This is the best class that I have ever taken. Professor Von Wittelsbach enhances the class with interesting materials and top notch lecturers. Lectures were given by journalists, authors and filmmakers. She was very accessible after class. For someone who has never been to Italy, my experience in this class makes me feel as if I had.

Professor von Wittelsbach was an amazing professor in my FWS ITAL1113. I highly recommend taking her FWS as you not only learn a lot about the course material but Professor von Wittelsbach is simply a well of knowledge who is ready to share her brilliance with you at any time. You simply have to ask.

One of my favorite professors! I loved GOVT3323 & Italian-Jewish History FWS with Kora! Always so helpful and accessible for questions, she managed to make in-class discussions insightful & gave constructive feedback on papers. She seamlessly oversaw different activities for GOVT CiT & made sure everyone was safe. I learned so much from her!

One of the best professors I've had the honor to learn from. Not only did she go above and beyond during the Cornell in Turin program, she mentored me and helped me even after the program. From CiT in 2015, we are still very much in touch and I can always count on her for a recommendation letter and guidance. She truly cares about the students!

My favorite professor, whom I cannot recommend enough. Not only is Prof. KvB attentive to all of her students, she is one of the most diligent and inspiring instructors/administrators I have ever had. The GOVT CiT course in Turin was expansive but never overwhelming, as were the Italian courses I have taken with KvB in Ithaca. Can't go wrong!

This is by far the most outstanding prof. that I have ever had the opportunity to work with. Not only did she lead the course well (CiT), but she has served as a continuous mentor even after I left her classroom. Because of her support and encouragement, I was able to pursue an internship which related to the class that she led. Highly recommend.

A wonderful Professor and person. Professor Wittlesbach cares about her students both inside and outside the classroom. She has been one of the nicest Professors I have met at Cornell. Definitely take!
Really tough grader. Class was not enjoyable
A wonderful intellectual and always engaging.
She's really nice and definitely cares about her students. As long as you put in the effort you will get a good grade.

Professor von Wittelsbach truly cares not only about her students' learning, but also their well-being. She's very understanding if you need an extension, let alone being an excellent teacher. She's really funny and makes the class feel like a mix of shabby-chic and professionalism (you have to have her if you wanna know what I mean).

Brilliant professor. The way she incorporated her knowledge of Mediterranean literature, history, culture and her personal experiences of the Mediterranean made every seminar extremely interesting! She is very sweet and approachable, cares a lot about her students and is very passionate about what she is teaching. I truly learned so much from her.

Professoressa is one of the most incredible teachers you will meet at Cornell. Not only does she teach you Italian, she also elaborates on Italian culture and extends on modern issues around the world.
