Not too difficult for a computer science introduction class either. This is a class that can make you switch to computer science major after taking it. Would recommend to everyone I know.

Walker White is a legend. Honestly, I don't think I would be a CS major if I didn't have White, Walker. He is such a great lecturer and all his assignments and labs really make sure that you leave having a great understanding of computer science.
Pretty easy class although I did have a lot of prior experience with Python.
Fun lectures, teaches well

Walker White is an amazing professor, the best one I've had at Cornell so far. CS 1110 is very well-structured and the lectures are on-point. After the class I felt that I had a great foundation in CS and was confident in my abilities going into CS 2110. Ditto.

Walker White is an amazing professor, the best one I've had at Cornell so far. CS 1110 is very well-structured and the lectures are on-point. After the class I felt that I had a great foundation in CS and was confident in my abilities going into CS 2110. If you have the choice of taking CS 1110 in the fall with Walker White, I highly recommend it!!
Great class, great lecturer, great experience.

He's seriously the best. He is extremely fair and helpful, as well as a clear lecturer. If you come from any CS experience, the class will probably be quite easy and no readings will be necessary as his lectures are detailed and clear by themselves.

An amazing professor. CS 1110 was an introductory course, but assignments can be fairly rigorous for those with lesser CS backgrounds. He is a fair grader--lenient, really--and help can always be found when you need it. Taking his class almost convinced me to switch to a CS major.  He is very fair and his lectures keep interesting. I'd recommend.

Grading is very fair. He does really try to help you and wants you to get the best grade. If you come in with experience don't get cocky, met a few kids with a good amount of CS experience who didn't study and got B's on the first exam.

Professor White is a very fair grader, sometimes lenient, and he responds to your online questions quickly. There are regular labs and assignments, some of which are very long (10-15 hours to complete). White has a very extensive group of TAs and helpers, so finding help is very easy to do.

A talented lecturer. Slides posted online and there is a large network of consultants available online and in-person. Class was well-designed and I learned a lot. This is the sort of class everyone with even a passing interest in CS should consider taking.

Prof White is a great teacher and will help any student that asks. Granted, the assignments/tests are tough--especially if you haven't programmed before. Lectures are good, but not mandatory; if you study you'll definitely get a B/B+, which is good enough to move forward to CS 2110.

Prof. White was an excellent professor. His After taking his class, I am leaning towards majoring or at least minoring in CS. I loved his mentality about learning CS as opposed to learning a language. Would HIGHLY recommend taking 1110 with Prof. White in the fall as opposed to the professor in the spring.

This course has changed my mind about computer science. Before this course I was entertaining the possibility of a CS major or at the very least, a minor. However, after taking this course, I am completely assured that I will never take another CS course at Cornell or any other institution. Instead of being fun, this course was extremely tedious.

Best Professor I've ever had in any subject.  Lectures are extremely clear and well-made, and he explains complex computer science concepts in ways that a human can easily understand.  I'd recommend taking his CS course just to have him as a teacher.
Great Prof!
REALLLLLLLLY good with notes and resources

Prof. White really goes out of his way to make sure that his students understand everything he says. Lectures, labs, and assignments are well-designed. Office hours, consulting hours, and Piazza are really helpful. Also, not many professors would print out handouts and lab instructions for all students, esp. when the school tries to restrict that.
Best professor I've had at Cornell though the class isn't that easy
He's a great professor, but if you are new to programming, the class is a lot of work. You will need all the help you can get, but as long as you ask, help will be provided by the truckload.

Professor White is a good lecturer. He's really straightforward and makes the material very easy to understand.  As far as grades go, as long as you pay attention in class and study a bit for the exams, you should be able to get an A.
Strict and stern.  But otherwise, informative. Sometimes the responses he gives are really terse. But he will answer everything.  Also, genuinely helps students get better.

When I went in I hated computer science, but this guy was just awesome. My favorite lecturer at Cornell: really clear and does his best to make sure everyone understands what he's teaching. Would recommend any class with him
probably the best lecturer i've ever had in a computer science class, though that's not saying too much. the tests are quite difficult, but not unfairly so.

Prof. White is a fantastic lecturer. Very clear, concise, engaging, organized, and entertaining. Even when the material gets tough, he is always enthusiastic. I would highly recommend him. Likely the best lecturer I've had at Cornell so far.

I loved professor White. Great lecturer, great since all lectures are online, lectures are very organized, assignments are well explained and while grading can be a little rough for exams it's fair. Helpful in office hours and on piazza when I needed it as well. Highly recommend taking Python, or any class, with professor White
White is an amazing teacher, very clear, organized and interesting. His grading is a little harsh but he's a great teacher nevertheless.

White is amazing. He knows his CS, will answer every question, is very passionate about CS, and is incredibly organized. Also two of the major assignments are really fun and they'll keep you interested. He has an army of like 30 consultants who always seem to hanging around in the lab to help. Also, take it if you are undecided about your major.
Great Professor. He is a really good lecturer and is always there if you need help.
I loved his lectures and he is very helpful and willing to explain things if you do not understand them. Overall the class is not too hard and fun and definitely worth taking.
Very good prof, but hard class for non CS or ENG majors. I took it on a whim (for some strange reason). He really does want his students to do well.

Such an amazing professor. I came in with no programming experience but he made the class really fair and it wasn't anything too difficult. Assignments take a lot of time but he provides a lot of help for those who need it. Class is graded fairly and he actually wants everyone to do well.

Walker White is a great professor. Although sometimes he might come across as arrogant, he is very passionate about computer science, and very accomodating; He is always willing to take time out of his schedule to meet with students, and cares to see that you actually learn the material. The projects were interesting, but quite challenging.

Mr. White was pretty good. His lectures were decent and he thoroughly covered the material. Pretty touch grader though--he nit picks assignments and exams, for sure. but for someone who is a prospective CS major, he does a good job at a providing a thorough introduction.

A great class structure, and a somewhat above average teacher. With the labs and assignments, you get a ton of practice with coding and quickly learn a LOT. He is friendly and piazza, the online cs question page, is very useful.

He is without a doubt the most helpful professor I've had at Cornell. He will explain anything and everything during office hours & had 30 minute time blocks you could sign up for if you were really struggling. I would walk in with zero clue about how to finish an assignment and walk out being able to do it on my own. Awesome, awesome guy!
Professor White was a great teacher, and he took me from no interest in computer science to a computer science major.

Most entertaining professor I have had at Cornell.  Definitely made me more interested in the subject matter.  Very clear lecturer goes back and forth between lecture slides and actual examples in the program.
Prof. White is extremely clear, engaging, and I enjoyed having him as my professor thoroughly. He's very friendly and approachable, and I wish more professors lectured like him.
homework are far away from the test. just study the test review

The more clear, organized, and through of the 2 instructors for this course. Material was not always explained well initially but he is very willing to help. The class was very disorganized and problem sets were often far removed from lectures. Be ready to wait until the day before a prelim to receive answer keys/grades from assignments

Course was a bit disorganized but professor Yin always posted his material on canvas and really tried to make sure people understood the concepts which weren't too difficult. The problem sets for this class are written by TAs so sometimes it was not synced with the lectures. Overall good professor but the course did lack organization.

Professor Yin is an alright professor. Very accomplished: he's on the 30 under 30. But the course was disorganized. Topics did not clearly relate to one another and were not explained intuitively. He was the better of the two professors for the course, but often the old lecture videos and textbook were more useful than the actual in class lectures.

He gives the study guide beforehand, so it's easy to study in advance for the first two prelims. Final is a take-home with 3 short answers and 1 long essay question. Relatively easy, but grading varies by your TA. 3 short op-eds throughout the semester, but the rubric is odd, and TA feedback didn't help me much. Prof. Young is a great prof though!

There are 3 short essays throughout the semester and2 prelims and 1 final with a long-essay question. The 2 prelims come with study guide, so you can prepare before. Everything is basically graded by your Grad TA with the help of Professor Young. Does not take attendance frequently and is more spontaneous so you'll never really know when he will
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is very easy. Lecture is late at night and they occasionally do random attendance checks at lecture, so try to go. Dr. Young is very approachable. Your grade is based on 3 opinion based memos, 2 prelims & a final (great study guide posted for prelims), and section/lecture attendance. He posts slides that correlate with assigned readings.

Had him this year, and he is literally the sweetest guy ever. His lectures were pretty entertaining, and he always makes good jokes during class. The tests were not that hard because he gives a good study guide, but the grade is based on basically 3 tests. Highly recommend!

Young's super chill. Lectures could be understood by a middle schooler--if you really understand something, you can explain it to a 5-year-old. Young can do that. He delivers lectures in a casual and unpretentious manner. Study guides available w/ all possible questions for the prelims. Papers: ez opinion pieces. Actually riveting content!!!

I took 2 classes with Professor Young back in 2023 and 2024. Great guy, extremely accessible & down-to-earth. 
If you are struggling in his classes, you are clearly doing something wrong because the professor posts a list of possible questions. While some of the topics we discussed were a little outdated, the topics were generally very interesting.

This class is tough to succeed in since your entire grade comes from just two exams. The grading is super unclear; we never really know what he's looking for in answers. Overall, it seems like the professor puts in minimal effort, and I wouldn't recommend this class if you care about your GPA or want a clear learning experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade will mostly depend on two exams. He never specify what he really want to see on the exams, like graphs, examples, etc. The exams are not very relevant to the lectures. Avoid him if possible.

One of my favorite teachers of all time. Extremely good public speaker with great lecture slides. Incredibly honest tests with extensive reviews done with TA's. Grading was very fair and even open to debate once we got tests back. Memos were easy. Young is a funny teacher, loves to answer students question. He reminds me of Cam from Modern Family.

Young doesn't deserve all the bad reviews, but he could approve a lot. He was very monotone and wouldn't post lectures, which was frustrating. His views are questionable but he often had a variety of views. He gave us prelim questions in advance. His class structure was fair: 3 small papers, 2 prelims & a final. My TA was great, fairly easy A.

A pretty average gov class. Even though its "controversies about inequality", we only really talked about wealth based disparities. Prelim questions were released beforehand which was nice, you can skip some of the readings if you go to lecture. Memo grading wasn't clear and is dependent on TA. Prof is very monotone but lots of guest speakers

Don't listen to bad reviews, definitely recommend this class for an easy A. Mostly read off slides which made classes boring at times but easy to follow. 75% of the grade is based on 3 tests--he posts a list of potential questions before the prelims so you know exactly what will be on it. Lots of guest speakers which was cool. Reading manageable.

This Professor openly praises elon musk and other billionaires and remarks how "poverty is motivating" and "blue states have caused the housing crisis." He hates welfare, housing subsidy, & minimum wage,. Test was just regurgitating right-wing propaganda from lectures. Uses his own works as sources for the class. All data cited is 20-60 years old.

Tedious and disconnected. Dude has never met a single nonrich human, and lacks fundamental empathy. A penchant for social darwinism. For all that his research allegedly critiques the rich, he basically worships wealth.

Did not care at all about the class, and it showed. Tests had ultra specific, rigid criteria for written responses that didn't always make sense. Topics didn't even always relate to inequality. Professor essentially made the class buy his book and put it on an exam when it didn't really connect to the class as a whole. Massive disappointment.

Professor Haskins taught the class, and she was an amazing lecturer. Unfortunately, she left, and he is now teaching it. He reads off the PowerPoint word for word in a monotone, and he leaves everything to the TAs, who didn't know what the test would be like 3 days before the exam. As long as you do the readings, you will be fine, but his lecs suck

The class itself and the professor are a little dry. You cover new topics every class and speed through lecture slides. The class itself is very easy, especially if you put a good amount of effort into it. As long as you know the key takeaway from each lecture you are good for the test. If you want an easy class to pass this is it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The TAs would literally say how little the professor cared about the class. He was a very uninspiring lecturer, often not even practicing. It was the first time running the class for him, and the rubric they graded with used bulletpoints for each question that you had to mention. Of course, the TAs failed to mention this in the leadup to the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very clear grade breakdown. Interesting subjects covered but because there's nearly a new topic every week - each warranting their own class, it's pretty surface level.

Hes a super friendly guy. The class is supposed to focus on CONTROVERSIES about inequalities not inequalities 101. Rude students interrupt his lecture for not discussing the basics of inequalities, but thats not what his class is supposed to be. Its a capstone course, if you dont know racial inequality is a thing, what are you doing here.

Prof. Young is readily approachable. Great personality. He tries to make the everything as fun as possible during class meeting time, and he's very good at keep students engaged. I recommend going to his class just because it's really interesting. It's half lecture and half casual conversations, pretty chill. The workload is also very light as well

Cristobal just came from Stanford and he really has that California chill vibes. The workload is very manageable - several readings and one short memo for each week. He doesn't take attendance, but if you go you will get high participation grade. The class is more like a conversation than a lecture, so it can be really fun. Would strongly recommend

Peggy grades very harshly, but gives good feedback and is super helpful during meetings. The class requires several essays, twice-weekly discussion posts on readings, daily quizzes, and an optional extra credit class-leading assignment. The extra credit is substantial, which makes it easy to get an A+, but be prepared to read and write a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The difficulty was manageable but the workload is definitely on the heavier side for an FWS with weekly writing journals, quizzes, and discussion posts. On the flip side, Peggy is a nice person and puts in the effort to help you succeed. Overall, a solid class, but consider how interested you are in the course material before taking it.
Compared to other FWS I think this class is more difficult, but the content it covers is very interesting, so I think it was worth it. Essays are graded pretty harshly, but good feedback is given

Peggy is a tough grader, but is very knowledgable about her subject area. I enjoyed being in her class, and I would personally rate her a 5, but I know that she wasn't well liked by many others in the class. It was her first time teaching, and I think she did a great job. Her feedback was always articulate, and she was always very direct.

The slides genuinely do not help you when you are reviewing and you have to come to every class to understand. She doesn't teach you all the content you need to know. The multiple-choice questions are sometimes confusing. The content is pretty interesting though.

Professor Zayas is a great lecturer and made class engaging! The key concepts she provides for each unit were super helpful for studying for exams. The grading system is clear and unbiased, and I found attending lecture to be incredibly useful.

Zayas is a really great lecturer. I found class very engaging and interesting. However, there is a LOT of content to cover in this class. Lecture can move very fast and cover a wide breadth of content. Prelims also cover a ton of content and can be hard if not prepared. Extra credit is nice though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zayas is a great teacher and this class was very interesting. Much of the final grade is based off of three prelims and an optional final and there are smaller assignments throughout the semester with generous extra credit offered. While the class was fairly easy, there are definitely a few topics that can be difficult to understand.

Really interesting subject matter and really good use of real world examples (ex: from The Big Bang Theory). While the tests are difficult and sometimes confusingly worded, Prof. Zayas gives extra credit opportunities as well as easy bi-weekly discussion posts and open notes quizzes to get your grade up. If you put in the effort it will pay off!

Loved this class and professor! You have to go to lecture. The exams are based on lecture materials. Readings are optional. Plenty of opportunity to do well -- drops the lowest exam grade and there is extra credit. Prof. Z.'s lectures are engaging. Would highly recommend.

go to lectures since slides are impossible to understand. super content heavy, 2 pages of learning objectives per lecture. prelims are tough and weirdly worded, need to understand everything about every concept. extra credit is worth 4% so do it. dont cram, try to understand the big picture of how things are connected and why we need to know them

This was a fun class. I enjoyed taking the personality tests and learning about Freud. Grading is based on exams, but Professor Zayes gives quizzes throughout. I mostly enjoyed the lectures and the use of videos to illustrate concept. Although there is a textbook, the exams are based on lectures.

I loved this class! The professor makes the topics engaging and relates it to daily life. I loved the videos of the big bang theory and the office. I have a hard time paying attention in lecture, but I enjoyed these. The prelims are multiple choice and short answer and you can drop the lowest grade, and there is extra credit. Highly recommend!

The comments here are unfair. Prof. Zayas is an engaging lecturer, caring, and funny. Her exams are tough, but there is a significant curve and easy to get an A. But you need to attend class and review the lecture notes.

Exams 90% of your grade. Gives no practice questions for exams. Chapters of assigned reading (barely helps).  Lecture slides are packed with information so she oftentimes finishes the class by speeding through the rest of the material. If you want to take this class out of interest, find another class unless you are willing to devote a lot of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know how or why she is allowed and continues to teach. She is the sole reason for a decline in my mental health this semester. I reached out asking how to best approach the final (which has no study material) & her response was just shy of "go to h-ll". If she needed 50,000 signatures to be fired, I would ensure 200,000 before end of day.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class since it seemed like an interesting topic and a break from my STEM-heavy course load. The material is interesting enough, but Professor Zayas makes the exams quite difficult and has not mentioned a curve despite low averages. She is generally unapproachable, and her TA's are unaccommodating. I would not recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst prof at Cornell and I have been taught by notoriously difficult professors in classes with far more difficult course content (STEM). Do everything in your power to never take this class. RUN. Worst grade at Cornell in all my years here.
Worst prof at Cornell hands down

Lectures and readings did not line up at all. Extremely vague and arbitrary grading on general concepts that would be marked wrong if it wasn't exactly what the TA said. Supposedly an Intro level but the quantity of information and the poor teaching made it more difficult than Organic Chemistry. 1/10.

Horrible prof. She took what would normally be an interesting intro subject into an extremely difficult and boring one. Her lectures are not clear, and her exams are specific to things she never addresses. Her TAs are harsh graders and take points off for no reason. She wants you to fail her class even though it is an INTRO psych class. Never again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zayas is very knowledgeable and her lectures are very interesting, though a bit long. Grade consists mostly of 3 prelims and an optional final that can make up for a prelim. Other assignments are a few canvas quizzes and assignments that are fairly easy. Overall the tests were hard but I loved the professor and there is SONA extra credit.
such a bad professor...unapproachable and has no empathy at all

Literally the worst class and professor. Is so disorganized, unapproachable, and un-empathetic. Piles on work and thinks it's ok and fair, doesn't post exam preparation materials until the day or two before the exam, and never answers emails. Worst class and worst professor I've ever had.
This was the hardest course I have ever taken at Cornell. This literally dropped my GPA. She is nice but her class is not nice. It is so hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and organized but, but an easy A she is not. Genuinely interested in her students and how to best support them. One of my favorite professors Ive taken this far.

Honestly thought I would have received a worse grade, but extra credit helped exponentially! Amazing ideas and concepts that are applicable, stayed awake every lecture. Test questions are tricky, so really know everything front to back. Worked the hardest for this class out of all of my classes. Use the learning objective questions!

Prof. Z is a great lecturer and a really cool person. She often cites her own studies which I love. You need to go to the lectures even though the slides are posted- otherwise you won't understand them. And you need to read the textbook and outside readings. It's work.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Honestly, pretty easy class. I took it as a freshman and had no problem with the class. The study guide IS EXACTLY the same as the prelim.. if you know the study guide, you WILL do well. The lectures helped but I skipped a bunch and still did fine because everything was posted online.. Readings weren't mandatory; you just have to know the main idea
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Class is much,much harder and more intensive than it should be. I have no clue why it isn't a 4 credit course for the amount of work it involves. Overall, not worth it if you just need an easy psych course. There are plenty of better, more interesting, less time consuming psych courses offered..

Very intelligent lecturer, but her class was incredibly challenging. You will need to study very diligently just to pull off anything above a B from personal experience. The amount of readings for the class are through the roof. I learned a lot from the class, but seriously, only take this class if you have strong interest in the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Reading according to schedule is the key. She is a good lecturer but not at all an easy professor. Lecture will just help you understand but actual contents for the prelims will be from textbook and readings. Take advantages of all extra credit opportunities. Only take it if you're interested in this area. Challenging prelims but doable if you try.

There is a ton of reading, the exams are very hard. I find this class harder than organic chemistry, which is the worst class I've ever taken. The means are low, and there is no curve. Professor Zayas is a very good lecturer, though. Most of the information from lectures is not on the slides, so it is important to go to lecture.

Would recommend if you place out of intro. Personality is a complex topic, but Prof. Zayas is great and boils it down to six different paradigms' views. She is nice, mellow, and easy to like. Her tests are not unreasonable for an Ivy league school you just need to read every assigned passage and take diligent notes.
one of my favorite classes at cornell! the exams are reasonable but you have to study and there are lots of readings.
I really like this class. Professor Zayes is good lecturer and keeps it interesting. The materials is just interesting. I also think it is possible to do well if you get past the first prelim
I love this class! Material is super interesting, but there is a lot of it. Prof. Zayas is great. Engaging. The prelim is reasonable if you focus on the study guide.

Even if you think you know all the material, something is bound to pop up on every exam that you've never heard of. She's very clear during her lectures and makes the topic seem stupidly easy, so much so you won't want to read the assigned readings, but she WILL get you during the exams. Suggestion: READ ALL THE READINGS ACCORDING TO HER SCHEDULE!
Material is super interesting and the prof does a good job keeping it new. The exams are fine if you study.
FUn course. Love it! The tests are challenging, so you have to study! But there is a curve and extra credit options.
thumbs up. there is too much reading for the three credits, but it is possible to do really well, and the material is interesting.
Great professor; very intelligent
Best methods class on campus. Way more than 4 hours of credit worth of work. student led lectures are hit or miss. Prof. Z. should lecture more.
One of my favorite classes. Prof. Zayas is a dynamic lecturer, but can go off topic. There are two writing assignments and 3 exams. Topic is interesting, and it's easy to get an A.
best class i've taken at cornell so far! brings in tv clips from friends to explain concepts. exams are hard, but there is a curve.
fun course. profesor zayas keeps it interesting, but exams are long and nitpicky.
not an easy class. not an intro class for sure. exams are hard, but she curves. lectures are interesting with clips from tv shows.

This professor knows her stuff!  And though she may not be the easiest or clearest lecturer, she is able to clear up any confusion if you go to her after class or during office hours.  She is a new prof, so she is still getting the hang of teaching.  Interesting material, difficult tests.  But she practically hands you points (i-Clicker, essays).

this professor is horrible. she has awful lecturing skills and the majority of the class falls asleep during class! the only reason you'd go to class is for clicker points; she doesn't even calculate those properly. guest lectures are the only interesting part. i love psychology; her class crushed my expectations. the ta's are b*tchy and useless.
I loved psych until I took this class. By far the worst class I have ever taken. EVER.
Professor Zayas is really good at explaining complex ideas and terminology. She is insightful and interesting. and she's a great ultimate player.

The worst professor I have had so far. Completely destroyed my interest in psychology and has no idea how to lecture. Reads off the lecture slides yet refuses to post them before class. The only times I actually went to class I fell asleep. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!  to the poster two above me: she had to curve it (i.e. add points to everyone tests which is not curving) because everyone did so poorly. and then she told us that we needed to study better!

Shes a really good professor. She brings enthusiasm to the lectures, and explains things clearly. She tries to cover a little too much in lecture, so it can be hard 2 keep up. The test are challenging, but not that bad, they just can't be blown off.

She was helpful and unpretentious during office hours, and she's given me useful advice about what other classes to take at Cornell. She also helped me get a RA position in one of the social psych labs. I think she somewhat shy which leads people to think she's cold. She's obviously new at teaching, and that's where mots of her pitfalls lie.

Don't take this class unless you have to. The prof is unreasonable and makes the tests hard for no reason. When someone asked for a study guide, she said the 35 slide powerpoints for each lecture were the guide. For the final, she said the previous prelims were the guide, but she never gave them back and wouldn't let you have them. Ridiculous.

Useless class. Lecture is mindnumbingly boring (went maybe 3 times all semester), exams don't actually test real knowledge, the book is painful to read, and Zayas is new (it shows). That being said, I somehow managed to pull off an A-, though I attended class at most 5 times all semester. Maybe you can too.

One of the worst classes I've had at Cornell.  Tests trivial information, doesn't show up for her own review sessions.  She seems sweet but I don't care!  She is unpolished and I would strongly advise that if you want to learn about Personality Psych to simply buy the book.

Lectures: not engaging, dragging, undynamic, way too easy to skip. Tests difficult, not in the good challenging sense, but in that they don't really test your knowledge at all, but seemingly unimportant random minutia from lectures and textbook. Cold, distant, and unresponsive at office hours. As psych major, this class was a waste of my time.

She knows what she's talking about. She's new at teaching so there are some things she still is learning, but she's a very very smart person. The class can be interesting if you are into the material, but don't take if you're just looking for an easy elective

She is a good professor who knows what she's doing.  Lectures are occasionally boring, but they are always clear if you pay attention. She's incredibly sweet and helpful if you ever visit her office hours, and because she's new, people really take advantage by complaining/picking on her so much. Tough class, and well worth it.
BAD PROFESSOR. MAKES BAD TESTS AND CAN'T TEACH IF THE WORLD DEPENDED ON HER!

Her lectures are SOO boring -most people didn't show up. She basically read off the slides. Her tests were pretty hard and had lots of ambiguous questions (she usually ended up giving credit for 3+ questions because of ambiguity or just a bad question). She's new at teaching and it shows! This class could have been so much more interesting.

I would not recommend the prof.  Test are impossible and many questions are ambiguous.  She is new, and doesn't really know what she is doing yet. She was a little nasty at office hours and really fake. The material learned was really interesting even though she is so bad at teaching it. I'll probably get a A-, and I still don't like her.

No personality. Horrible lecture, can't master ppt slides (clicks through all the important stuff in a sec and spends 30 min on a blank slide)  Also can't write test questions well.  Random useless knowledge tested, not concepts (eg was a test given in tibetan or bushman, what was word 36 on page 321, etc) Speaks at 2 microdecibels. Poor TA contact
extermely difficult person

He is knowledgeable of the content, but doesn't seem to care much about the class itself. Many times, his lecture slides are incomplete in class. Course material is covered in lecture once, and never again. Prelims are incredibly in-depth and he provides no additional material for studying. Pop-quizzes are on very specific details from the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Mallett is very knowledgeable and I enjoyed the content, but I found the grading structure to be difficult to deal with, and ultimately dropped the class. Expect unreasonably hard pop quizzes occasionally. If you don't ace every test + the final paper, it's hard to get above a B+ as there is no curve and questions are weighted heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable professor of urban planning. Lacks personable skills to relate to students and takes topics too seriously. Harsh grader and brutal critic. Limited grades throughout the semester, many readings required, with potential to do poorly on pop quizzes due to exact fact memorization required. Learning potential is high, work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lectures weren't great but you can't blame him when not even a third of the class shows up. Quick to reply to emails and Ed and helpful in office hours. Exams are fair but HW is time consuming. The final project takes a while but isn't worth much.

Dude's a legend. Takes time after class to explain anything you had problems with. Yeah the homework is a lot for sure, and he expects some basic fluency in excel/python for some assignments, but he's really good at introducing Differential Equations. Handled the online transition like a champ too (Spring 2020)

His explanations are super clear and I actually found his lectures very insightful because he brought up many interesting real-life problems and how diffeq could be applied to derive models to solve those problems. Even when the class went online, he still managed the course logistics very well. It was my most favorite class for Spring 2020.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tough but rewarding. Some lectures are hit-or-miss. Overall not bad though. I would not dread taking the class again. If you take 2930, you might need to know how to program and graph for some homework assignments.

Assigns way too many problems for homework, get ready for over 20 pages of problems that really are just a waste of your paper. Doesn't teach well, gets most examples from Paul's Math Notes. Since moving to online (Spring 2020), the class has become a nuisance.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tells subtle but great jokes

Good prof, explains things pretty clearly, but by no means goes in detail.  Teaches how to solve problems, but no more, so all context of problems is lost.  Not hugely interesting, either.  Nice guy though, and very understanding.
He's really boring. I usually end up sleeping in this class and read the textbook later. He makes a bunch of math mistakes too.
I went to a few of his lectures and they were clear and organized. He is great in explaining the material in office hours.
he's kinda cold in person but he knows how to teach. Well prepared and organized. 202 stuff is his specialty
Best of the three profs who teach this course (not saying much).  Clear and easy to follow, if somewhat like a robot.  Goes into long-winded example problems that no one can follow.

Professor Zacher is a wonderful professor who truly enjoys the subject she is teaching. Her enthusiasm makes engaging in class much easier. She is also not a harsh grader by any means so it is easy to do well in her classes. All that is required is that you engage in the class. Overall her class was very easy, informative, and fun.
Just okay--a bit overrated on here.

This was easily my favorite class at Cornell. Dr. Zacher is super sweet and will always help you, as long as you're proactive about asking for it. Super fun person to be around too, she's funny and even brings her dog into class sometimes! Highly recommend.

Professor Zacher is absolutely wonderful! She brings enthusiasm to the class and makes the material engaging. She makes sure that we won't feel stressed but also stay motivated enough to keep on track. I took the course for requirements but ended up really enjoying Old English. This is one of the best classes I've taken at Cornell!

It is true that she ignores student emails, but also true that she is a good teacher when you are lucky enough to see her in class. It's a privilege to even see her and students should appreciate the privilege. Zacher is amazing, and just to see her in class is a delight. Don't expect more than you need

ENGL3280 Prof. Zacher makes high-level material accessible. You can be in any class year and take one of her 3000-level classes and succeed if you put in the work. Her class involves long readings and in-depth lectures, but doing the readings is enough to score high. She has a warm spirit that always brightens the day and makes even old texts fresh
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was so nice! I was dreading taking this FWS because it was a requirement but she was a pleasure. The work was not bad at all and she is very understanding. I would definitely recommend participating in class.

Zacher is an incredible professor and such a kind and caring person. Her classes are always interesting and informative. She is a fair grader but pushes you to be the best writer that you can be. Do not miss out on taking a class with her at Cornell.
Samantha is incredibly nice & fabulous! She's so energetic & passionate & enthusiastic, making obscure topics really interesting. Will definitely take her class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class one so well thought out. There was a flow between topics that really made sense and the texts we read were fun! (Especially the section on John Mandeville). Would highly recommend taking a course from Professor Zacher!

As my first four-thousand level English course, especially one on the roots of anti-Semitism, I was nervous as to what this class would be like. Professor Zacher was amazing. Not only did she her happy energy lighten some of the heavy readings, every lecture was engaging. This class (and its professor) are wonderful. Would recommend highly!

Professor Zacher is incredibly knowledgeable, funny, and gets you thinking far beyond the classroom in "The Imaginary Jew." The course is a brilliant interweaving of films, manuscripts, books, and poems. There is lot of writing (which was a good thing) but the class was not only English majors. Fascinating and very well taught- TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Samantha Zacher is an incredibly warm, funny, engaging individual. Her enthusiasm and her teaching abilities make class easy and really enjoyable. She is also invested in her students and their work. She takes the time to read and comment closely on your papers, improving your knowledge and your writing abilities at the same time.

I love Professor Zacher!  She made an obscure topic (Icelandic lit) fascinating by her enthusiasm and obvious expertise.  She wants her students to do well and learn and is willing to spend time helping them do so.  Her class was not easy, but it was not stressful either.  If for no other reason, take her class to learn how to be chic!

Professor Z is an energetic and well-prepared teacher.  She works hard to get the best out of her students and is always fair when assessing them.  Don't miss out an opportunity to take a class with her!
No Comments

Professor Zacher is thoughtful, funny, fascinating to listen to, and extremely competent in her field. She is approachable and generous with her time, bends over backwards to help students understand difficult concepts, and teaches energetically, creatively and with heart. One of the best teachers I've had.
Horrible, pretentious, affected woman.  Boring class, dead discussions, nit-picky grader.

Brad will push you to deepen your analysis and ground it in textual evidence and close-reading. He's not always super clear with his feedback but gives plenty of room for improvement. He rambles a bit in class but is a good professor overall and has very flexible deadlines. He will definitely push you to improve your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brad is hands down the GOAT. Class will improve how you write and think. Do anything you can to snag a spot in pre-enroll.

Brad is the professor I recommend to anyone needing to take an FWS. He is an amazing storyteller and seems to know so much about everything! He was pretty flexible with deadlines especially if you have a lot going on. He is always available for office hours and will work around your schedule, so take advantage of that. Your grade will thank you!!

Brad always knows what's going on and allows rewrites for almost all the papers. Unlike other writing professors, he is not only good at writing but also knows physics and math, has easy grading, and is the best professor

One of the best prof at Cornell. Write whatever ideas that into your brain, Brad is always neutral and will be 100% respectful to them, and he likes us to come up with 'special ideas'. Great and deep lectures, great and deep feedback on the paper. You will have revision chances for each paper, and you can show him the draft for each paper.

If you just wanna gain a S grade in FWS , this course is your best choice. Pro. Brad put the whole grading and workload pretty little and the estimated time spending per week is 5 hrs or less. But he is willing to listen to your advice and if you want to dive in deep topics, you can still talk with him in person.

Hands down the worst professor imaginable. His grading system is a complete joke, no logic, no transparency, just random punishments disguised as “feedback.” He doesn't teach; he demoralizes. Every class feels like psychological warfare.

Worst professor ever had. Completely unclear grading standards, random and nonsensical feedbacks. Seems to enjoy discouraging students rather than helping them improve. I've consistently received A's throughout my academic life, yet got a C in ARCH1101. If you're assigned to him taking a gap year would honestly be a better choice.

In my entire time taking this class I only saw him on lecture days with the exception of one pin-up where I received vague and confusing feedback.

I wish I had more time to create a rapport with him, and maybe get more project clarification from him, but he was gone for a significant part of the year.

Sasa often skips classes and gives vague feedback, but he is quite flexible with deadlines (don't take that for granted) as long as students stay healthy. He also doesn't tell us how to think about drawings and spaces, which makes us think of more radical and unconventional ideas and solutions. He really pushes us to challenge precedents and norms!
I had sasa and throughout the entire time, he gave me such little feedback and mentorship. He feels more like an spectator to my work rather than a mentor.

Put so much into this class to receive only a B- I did what I was told and made changes to assignments to the professors liking and still had trouble. The professors were barely around in the class compared to the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: SO

Ignore the 1 star reviews. They are from misogynists who can't accept the fact that a woman can be extremely talented and competent at Physics. A handful of students would consistently berate her with unrelated comments in an attempt to convince the class that they are somehow more qualified than her.

Prof. Crites' lectures definitely needed some reorganization, but she was overall very pleasant and willing to help all of her students. Though I did not learn as much as I think was needed for future classes, much of this was due to students interrupting the lecture, not Prof. Crites

Prof. Crites' handwriting was hard to read, often layered with old chalk. She trailed off mid-sentence, stuttered, and seemed unsure. Lectures flipped between math and concepts with no clear connection, and derivations lacked explanations -- she recited steps without clarifying why, making demos and worksheets feel disconnected.

Prof. Crites is one of the most caring and approachable professors I have ever had. Unfortunately, many of the other ratings are correct in that her lectures tend to be quite scattered and lack the foundational base I feel is needed in EM. Exams are also very odd and non-representative of psets. Report assignment was very fun and unique though!

High pass low pass
This was not an honors class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As someone who has consistently enjoyed Electricity and Magnetism before this point, much preferring it over mechanics, I have found this class to, finally, have the opposite effect. It drained significant interest that I'd previously had for the subject. If you have the choice, take 2213 instead. You'll learn something in that class.

Professor Crites is a terrible lecturer. What is taught in lecture is not even remotely close to the level of difficulty of the problem sets which aren't even insanely difficult; the class is just taught so poorly that you are on your own for the homework. The prelim was confusing and almost impossible to prepare for even with the practice prelim.
Lectures weren't helpful. Used textbook to study
Did not use chalkboard at all for any formula derivations and mathematics solutions .(This being an honors physics class) Did not get good intuition behind E&M.
Very bad professor. Please don't take this class with her.

Doesn't teach well, loses chain of thought mid sentence and moves to something different
Didn't give good intuition behind concepts, could not answer questions properly
Spent half the classes giving unhelpful worksheets, making people discuss among themselves
Did not use chalkboard much to write derivations (ironically this being an honors class)
[PHYS 2217 review] Very kind and extremely intelligent but also very disorganized and hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: nice prof but a terribly useless class

If PHYS 1110 is with Prof. Crites, take it. While yes, the class was disorganized throughout the whole semester, Prof. Crites always put on the front that it was all going to plan. Even if 10 kids showed up for the 8am, she was always psyched to be there. Overall, very nice, lenient, caring, and will always be there to help.

Professor Crites is always incredibly bubbly and positive, even when only 15 out of the 200 students show up to class. The labs barely have any instructions, so you just make up random experiments or sit there and do nothing. This class was a mess, but it was so entertaining watching people complain on the ED Discussion. 10/10 would recommend.

There are 6 final essays in this FWS. Each essay has one draft. There is basically one piece of writing due each week (she assigns them Thursdays and they are due on Sunday). Essays are short (1-2 pages, double spaced).

She edits them, but if you write a bad draft, she will deduct points off the final essay. Attendance is 10% of the grade.

This is definitely a class worth taking, the writing is relatively easy just annoying that its due sunday. The prof is hilarious, many times unintentionally and it's overall a fun time. Lots of reading (DO IT) but not unbearable, work totals to about 2-4 hours a week. Feedback is not the best but you'll eventually learn what she expects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most unpleasant professor I've had. She provided no avenues through which to help her students (never responded to emails, prohibited student collaboration, no TA, no office hours), and she talked down to students who asked questions. Frequently singled out students in class with no clear intention but to say what they had done wrong. Unacceptable.

Class time was used to read aloud the readings that were assigned for homework. She is generally presents material in an unclear and inefficient manner, and sets very unclear expectations for papers. She also only likes essays if they are super basic, clear, and elementary, and is very inconsistent. Generally, very confusing and frustrating class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The professor is generally rude and unpleasant. I would not recommend this class if you are a person who is easily offended or discouraged. The only decent thing is her feedback which goes a bit in depth. However she will call you to read out loud and will scold you for the most basic things.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Not the best english, but not so bad that she was impossible to understand. Class material was interesting, but often presented poorly. Be prepared to read your essays in class if she liked a point you made.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Blunt and generally unfriendly both inside and outside of class. Disengaged students from participation. Confusing presentation of course material and unclear about what she expected from students. Difficult to understand, not because of her accent but because of her convoluted manner of expressing herself. Not recommended.
Fairly hostile and consistently late for class.

She obviously cares about the students, though she seems to pick favorites, but it's hard to understand her. Her accent is very thick and she often makes mistakes on the board without realizing it, making it nearly impossible to understand the already dense subject of semantics. But, she's nice, if she can remember your name (probably won't).

The tests weren't that hard, and she would try to make everyone get a good grade, but she was very hard to understand. Her accent and manner of speech can get in the way and she often makes mistakes on the blackboard. Sections were important to figure out what was going on.

Her English can be poor, especially when you confront her, and she often pauses and gets confused with her proofs in class. The material is very interesting, but she presents it poorly and inefficiently. She is friendly enough in office hours and willing to help, but don't expect a competent teacher who cares about connecting outside of her field.
No Comments

Material is very challenging and she has an accent and bad handwriting (otherwise I would have given her another point on clarity). She challenges students and makes them work, but doesn't assign final papers (except for grads) or exams (except for proble

Lectures are good but also kinda unrelated to the projects. Projects take up ~60% of your grade, there is only one midterm and no final exam. Abe is too busy. Grading criteria is very vague everywhere. Better sell your soul to the project otherwise you only get completion credit (~85%). It'll be real tough if you have bad teammates.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love everything about this class, except that it's mostly group projects. If you don't have good group members, you're kind of stuck.

Assignments can be extremely long and tedious at times, lectures are not as helpful as needed, pretty much just verbatim from slides. Would not recommend if you are looking for an easy 3 credit CS distribution.

Professor Davis does a good job explaining the conceptual matter behind concepts in the lecture, focusing heavily on understanding as opposed to focusing on memorization. However, Abe was quite unprepared for lectures this semester, because he was loaded with tons of paper deadlines.
AniGraph is just a nightmare, horrible documentation.

Professor Davis is still new, so I'm sure that he will continue to get better, but the class was rather disorganized. Assignments were being written and bugfixed while we did them, and lectures, while interesting, were unrelated to any graded content. The grading was rather lenient to adjust for these issues, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Abe is a great professor and CS6682 is SUPER FUN! The lectures are well organized and engaging. Assignments range from technical stuff like Fast Fourier transform to making your own digital music. Abe also gave useful demonstrations and feedback on how to make presentations. Very cool!

Abe is good at demonstrating concepts with engaging materials, such as code demos, animation, and high-quality explainer videos. He wrote his own package for making graphics web apps, which can make the assignments more fun if it's better documented. Abe is super approachable and he held lots of extra OH. His organization does need improvement...

Professor Davis was a new professor Fall 2021. I'm sure he'll get better at teaching. His biggest issues definitely stemmed from a lack of organization. His lessons were hard to follow and he eventually just gave us videos from the previous professor, without making it clear which to watch. The assignments were difficult but good.
Great professor, would definitely recommend.

not a very good teacher, impatient, defensive when challenged, particularly nervous around grad students.  not sure prof nanji has the training and background to be teaching at this level at this University
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best teacher ever.

Get there early. He starts writing notes before lecture that you need. He makes mistakes-just writes the wrong stuff, and has gotten corrected on concepts by students. He starts 3-4 sentences at once and finishes 1. He does everything he can to avoid answering questions. Hes very smart, but get ready to teach the class to yourself. Tas r chill

Jumps back and froth between topics during lecture. Legible handwriting. Long problem sets. Was missing for some crucial lectures that the grad TA ended up giving which resulted in an average of 50 on the final.

Prof Stroock is a great professor. Not only does he engage the students in class in via posing questions, but cares to get to know them on a personal level too. He's great 1-1 if you're having difficulty with the course, but just raising your hand and asking the question during lecture doesn't bother him in the least (unlike some other professors).

His lectures were always pretty clear. He was precise with how he worded things, and I was rarely ever confused by how he taught. Not an exciting lecturer, but he certainly gets the job done well. Pretty nice guy.
Pretty good professor - has clear lecturing style and engages class by posing questions frequently.

knowledgeable person and very fair grading, i enjoyed lectures and we covered a good variety of interesting content. my TA was also great, some readings were dense but she tried to make discussion sections engaging as well.

Dr. Ahmann is incredible. Not only is she a knowledgeable, and passionate anthropologist, but she also is relatable and approachable. She even took the time to speak to me about my interest in switching to anthropology as a major. Her lectures were Ted Talk quality and grading was more than fair. Couldn't recommend taking her classes highly enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is interesting but Prof. Ahmann often uses language that can be confusing for a person who has not taken an anthro class before. Her slides are helpful so I recommend taking notes. I also think the readings were a little tough but attending discussion helps (Attendance is mandatory for discussion). You can bring notes to exams which helps
Very intelligent professor who gives well put together lectures. Make sure to take notes in class because lecture slides aren't posted.

Organized and enthusiastic professor. Very accessible and we had individual meeting sign ups with her for our papers too which shows she cared. I'm not particularly interested in anthropology but the material for Time Travel was pretty interesting.

Had her for a FWS on time travel. The nature of the class meant it was really reading heavy but they were all interesting and nothing felt like busy work. She took the time to get to know her students and clearly cared about our wellbeing. I would reccomend

I think he's a nice guy, but I didn't really find his lectures to be that helpful. He writes on the chalkboard and it's hard to follow along, and his notes are hand-written and just not presented in a super clear manner. The tests were a bit too hard in my opinion but he did release practice exams with solutions.

Genuinely an aweosme professor, I can tell he knows a lot about what he's teaching. Lectures sometimes rehash from the textbook but I like the real-world examples + exercises he gives us. Lots of emphasis on tests which are pretty difficult but fair. I feel like you get what you put into this class, if you put a lot of effort it's really enriching

Class started a little tense but he eased up as time went on and the course was relatively enjoyable because it didn't require too much work and tests had the right amount of challenge imo. I wouldn't say lectures were terribly interesting, more of dump from his notes. Overall ok class and chill professor while a good lead into to math stats.

Tests are worth a lot and are not very comprehensive. The best way to describe them is that they tested a few specific topics but tested them very in depth. Lectures are completely useless if you are brand new to the material. You will spend most of your time teaching yourself and then trying to figure out what he wants you to know.

Nice guy, but as many of these others comments say: lectures weren't that helpful since it was review of textbook stuff. However, I think he gets a worse rep than he deserves. Tests were doable despite the median of around 50%. Nonetheless, the final median grade was an A-. Two tests 20% each, final 40%. Not too much hw and could be found online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He seems like a genuinely nice guy, and its possible he may improve in the future bc this was his first semester teaching. The lectures were bad. Chalkboard writing of textbook examples. Students offered plenty of feedback requesting PowerPoint slides, recorded lectures, notes posted before class, etc., and he refused to make any changes.

It's a valuable class if you enjoy learning through proofs and theories. For a more applied course, 2700 might be a better choice. Hws were pretty fair as all the concepts needed was covered in lecture. Tests were computationally heavy under time constraint, but it was a good representation of what we learned. Genuinely a professor but it's tough

Lectures were poor regurgitations of the textbook, so I just read the textbook instead. Each homework would take 12+ hours because they were insanely long and difficult. Exam medians were 30% and 50% and the professor still did not adjust his difficulty and it just made me feel dumb and stressed. Class felt like multivariable calc part 3 not stats.
He seems like a genuinely nice person, but the class structure, lectures, and exams were NOT it.

Literally only 30% of the people go to lectures, not because the class is easy, but because the lectures dont help at all and people would just give up. The professor literally reads from his iPad and copies onto the board, and his notes on iPad are copied straight from the textbook. Hes a nightmare.

This professor is a good example of how not to teach. Firstly, for lectures he only reads off the textbook and does not elaborate when speaking. He often went too fast and when students wanted him to go back he struggled to back track and explain his work. Test means were also less than 40%, and destroyed our mental health getting such low scores.
Worst experience ever.
A very helpful course for your data science and AI career. I got some questions in my recent job interview that were so close to the homework problems. Thank you Professor!!!
Like his courses! Rich and useful content. Fair grading. Very supportive.
I would give between 4and 5 but most people gave 5 so I follow. He is in demand as others said.
A very popular professor. I am so glad to get into his class again this semester

Ed Discussion was excellent.
Lecture content preparation and delivery with high quality.
Excellent course. Very useful of operations and with wide variety of application to multiple domains.
Overall the course was well structured and organized. The seminars were especially interesting in terms of the topics and research covered.
I appreciated how the lecture notes displayed and explained the practical applications of particular optimization techniques in industry. Grading is fair and reasonable.
Professor You is a good lecturer and speaker overall and he has a very unique teaching style that is highly respected and adequately engaging to students. He is also very knowledge and an expert.
Interesting course on digital agriculture. There are diverse speakers and there expertise on the work
I like the flexibility offered by the professor. The topics are interesting. A great experience overall!
Interesting topics. Fair and reasonable grading
I learned a lot from the course. The professor seems an easy and fair grader.
Great course and interesting topics. Many emerging ones are covered.
Lectures are clear and organized. Very understanding about end-of-semester stress. Dropping HW at the end really helps with the workload. Would definitely recommend!
Nice professor and very DL- friendly. Super responsive in responding to my questions
Five star professor! Very responsive and accommodating.
As a distance learning student, I was impressed with how well the course was adapted. The asynchronous format worked great for my schedule, and the material didn't feel watered down at all.

Took the course last fall as a distance learner. The extra office hours during late evenings, on weekends and also on need basis helped significantly in getting the required support and I am thankful to Prof. You and the TAs for the same.

Not an easy course, but you will learn a lot. Professor is very supportive, and grading is quite fair with reasonable workload. I'm so happy with taking both courses with him and earn the data science certificate as part of my Cornell Master's degree.

Very knowledge professor and TAs. Great outside class support. Exercises very applicable. Homework not overwhelming. Easy grader. If you get the chance to take a class with him, take a class with him!

Professor You executed the class with high quality. His course content was highly organized. The content in the lectures directly supported the concepts being taught and the homework assignments related directly to the lectures and discussions.
Even though I am a distance learner, I felt engaged in the classes which helped understanding the content.

Ed Discussion was excellent.
Lecture content preparation and delivery with high quality.
Optimization Wiki was very helpful.

Prof. You is a knowledgeable and supportive instructor. Took initiative to ensure students' enjoyment. Assignments and projects were valuable; unstuck AI was a helpful study tool. Reasonable workload, easy-to-follow content.
I liked the learning through application, I felt like I learned a lot better by doing assignments and a challenging, creative project than by preparing for exams in other classes
An easy A course. Intelligent, well-spoken instructor (Prof. You); he took initiative to ensure that all students were enjoying class; Use of projects, instead of exams
The availability for office hours and the promptness of the professor in providing a schedule for office hours each week was extremely valuable.

The content is very inspiring, I could learn a lot from it. Instructors are very very helpful. Also, I learned how to do some application with what I learned in this class and got some basic understanding of the use of the machine learning methods.
This course was a perfect blend of theory and applications that no other machine learning course at Cornell could provide. Learnt a lot. Look forward to another course with Dr. You in the fall
Homeworks were very useful and You was a generous grader. The best teaching professor at Cornell SE!!
Excellent curriculum for non computer science background people to transition into Machine Learning.
Very interested topics and very timely. It covered ChatGPT and many LLMs.
I really value Dr. You for the flexibility that he extended to students like me, Distance Learners, in the office hours and deadlines.
This my favoriate class I've taken at Cornell and hope it never changes. TA Akshay was amazingly helpful throughout this course.

The balance of the course was very enjoyable. The lectures covered a wide variety of concepts in the field,
and the assignments/OH provided more of a hands on application of the material.
Good course and supportive instructor and TAs. I will take his deep learning course in the fall to learn more. Very exciting!
Easy A professor. A truue gem in Cornell system engineering
Good course. Learn a lot about AI and machine learning. Highly recommended by my LM co-workers. I am glad I took it this semester.

A wonderful machine learning course! I did not take 5800 in the fall, but the professor made an exception for me to try it out this term as he may leave Cornell next year. Super DL-friendly course! The best one in Cornell System Engineering. I hope other DL students could benefit from Professor You's classes while still here

Great Professor. He is very much concerned about how you will be able to perform in the outside world when people know you have taken his class. I learned more in this class than any other SYSEN class that I had taken.
Nice professor. Always grant permissions for reasonable requests.

Great course, great professor, great TAs! Many office hours. The professor is highly experienced in teaching distance learning students and very accommodating. I plan to take his another course in the fall.

The professor is very accessible, accommodating and knowledgeable on data science. He always teaches in the classroom even when there were very few students there. The TA Yvonne is unfamiliar with the subject. TA Bryan is much more knowledgeable about machine learning than Y. A great course but hopefully the TA would be better next time!
Nice professor and useful course. Take it if you could! I heard You will be on sabbatical leave next spring. Not sure if he will still teach in the fall.
Nothing more can be expected from an excellent course. Professor You is the best!! Take his course(s) if you can when you (and he) are at Cornell.
Nice professor and easy ML course with no exam. Attendance not mandatory. Very effective use of electronic platform like Ed Discussion and Canvas. I like it!

I am so confused why so many ppl are commenting so positively at the beginning of the course without even knowing what is going on in the lecture. Professor is teaching online for this semester even the university no longer accepts hybrid instruction mode. No Python instruction for the heavy project assignments (30 pages required.)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: It's just been a few weeks, but I really like this course. Professor makes it very FLEXIBLE! No exam, no mandatory attendance! There are timely support and replies on Ed Discussion on various issues. No wonder the class is so popular and hard to get in. I appreciate the Professor sent me a quick email when a slot was opened to sign up.

Another great course by Professor You! The recent Fukushima nuclear disaster example is very inspiring. It looks like the workload this semester is actually lighter than the previous course (less homework and assignments). Look forward to the exciting weeks in the rest of this semester to come!
Professor Fenggi is simply awesome. Tkae his class if you can!

One of the two courses for Computational and Data Science Certificate. A no-brainer choice to take. I look forward to the second one in the coming semester - heard most seats were taken in the pre-enrollment ... lol

I am a full time employee and working a part time job. Having the ability to work on assignments without the stress of tight deadlines and no possibility of extensions greatly helped me be able to earn a good grade in the course. Thanks for the patience and flexibility throughout the class this semester!

You have been an absolute inspiration for learning the basics of machine learning. As someone who is interested in the field but has had little experience in computer science he has made the learning experience manageable and extremely valuable. It has encouraged me to continue thinking about pursuing a career in data science and analytics.
All the "rumors" are true, yeah - 5-star course and 5-star professor. Needless to say! Will take his spring course again!

Nice professor much more accessible than many ORIE professors. He runs office hours on weekends and gave deadline extensions if you request. Although this is a chemistry course, it has nothing to do with chemistry at all! I do not know chemistry and I am happy with the materials. A much better course than the ORIE one! Will take his course again.

its much easier to get the optimization one in the tall after the spring ML course. You and his TAs are very considerate. if you need help with problems or project, just ask them for help. You never said no to deadline extension and always replied very fast. He is a true gem in cornell systems engineering!

I took the spring machine learning course before the optimization in the fall. it was a difficult start for me b/c of the prerequisite, but You is very encouraging and helpful. Akshay, the TA, is awesome! I dont encourage you to follow my reverse sequence, but if you have to do not worry - You would help and he is quite chill. Happy with my A+
If you a cs + math elective, sysen 6800 might be a part of your electives. Avg grade is A /A+. Of any of the courses offered by Prof Fengqi You. Easy A

I like the way Pro You does not take attendance and offer much flexibility in assignment deadline extensions due to the difficult semester at Cornell University this fall. The course materials are not that easy, but the professor and TA worked hard to make everything accessible to us. It's an enjoyable learning experience overall. Highly Recommend!

This is my first Cornell System Engineering course as a DL student located in Europe. The tools and skills I learned are very useful. I am actually utilizing those skills immediately in my job on reducing costs in our company. The professor is very accessible and TAs are great. Good course to take!

I also took 5888 in the summer. Great lectures, helpful professor and TA, interesting material, and fair assignments/workload. I would definitely recommend the class to a friend. I'm very happy with the experience!

Examples of application were extensive and applicable to all industries. Lectures were very through and interesting. Content was deep theoretically but had examples to show applications. Supporting, operational lectures were provided to help those students who had not taken prerequisite classes in a while which was appreciated!
Best professor at Cornell Systems Engineering Graduate Program! Wanna become a data scientist and get a high GPA, take this course with Professor You!
I really enjoyed the two courses in optimization and data science. Look forward the summer course on deep learning soon!
You is A TRUE GEM in Cornell Systems Engineering faculty! Great course materials on data science and machine learning! Student-centered pedagogy!

Any one could take this machine learning course and suceed! I am a live example! No python experience and little knowledge on stat and optimization, but professor and TAs are quite helpful - many tutorials and office hours and giving me much courage to continue on this course and finally got an A. I am grateful to Professor You. HE IS THE BEST!
Excellent course; excellent professor; excellent topic! No textbook, but the lecture notes are well organized and nicely illustrated - much better than a textbook.

Fenqi is very helpful outside the class. TAs are great. I am happy with getting an A in this class. It would be better if I took the fall course before this one, but the overall outcome is good. I'll take the other course in the coming fall for sure!

There are five homework assignments, but the lowest score would be dropped. The course project is team-based. Workload is manageable. Materials and lectures are interesting and cover many details. A great choice

Great course for System engineering students. I learned a lot. Grading bases on homework and project. Very fair and reasonable workload. Lectures have a lot of stuff to digest, but they are for good reasons. The field of machine learning is quite exciting and I'll learn more in the summer course with professor again!
Got my first A+ at Cornell. feel pretty good. A five star course without saying!
Great professor, fair grading, and much flexibility in deadlines. We need more professors like "You"

Great course - much better than the ORIE and CS ML courses that I have taken. It's taught by Zoom under the pandemic. Attendance is not required, so you could watch videos. Homeworks and project are quite practical. no boring proofs! No exam! The slots were taken very fast - I was lucky - grab a seat asap or you'll have to sign up for chem session
Good courses for M&A and Application electives. You will also get the data science certificate by taking his two courses. Dont miss his courses when you are in the program!

Course is well developed, from basic to very high level. Also, all the difficult topics in machine learning are presented in a simplified way, which makes it very easy to understand. The last few lectures on neural networks are amazing - I wish I had spent more time on those topics.

this course requires coding throughout the course, but it was not mandatory to have prior knowledge to coding. The professor and TAs were very useful in walking through the code and guiding whenever needed. I feel this course is so helpful to my thesis research.

As a ORIE student, I would say this course is MUCH BETTER than most ORIE courses that I have taken. I am glad that I chose this one with professor you. It covers many recent topics, as opposed to some ORIE courses that were updated after many years. ORIE students should consider this machine learning course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A great course for machine learning. I registered for his summer course for deep learning as well. workload is quite affordable that you could take another systems engineering concurrently with this one as a distance learner. Professor You offers great flexibility on deadline extension, etc.

I did not have coding and stat background before taking this course. The professor and TAs are quite helpful. Lectures are not mandatory, but I wish they were. The project piece is quite interesting and helpful. a good ML course to take

I think it is a 4-star course. 1 star lower because of the kids in the classroom did not interact with the professor. prof has been working hard to engage them, but kids are dull. kids might be more interactive at in-person classes. however, this is nothing wrong about the prof. given many 5-stars, I run a clustering to group mine into 5-star also

Great course covering many topics on machine learning. I learned a lot. Projects are quite interesting. NO EXAM IS GREAT! Professor is very kind and flexible with deadline extension. I will take his course again in the summer.
Instructor does a great job condensing all the important information into one semester. A very useful course to take

Four homeworks and one project. Reasonable workload and no exam. Professor placing heavy emphasis on project work greatly enhanced my learning of the material, especially vs. a purely exam-based course
