The course gives very good overview of machine learning algorithms and introduction to using them in real life. An excellent one!

Dr. You's courses (1. Computational Optimization and 2. Big Data and ML) are the best courses I've ever taken. Dr. You is an outstanding professor that works to actively include all students in his classes. His expectations for understanding and knowledge are reasonable, and the content in his course is so well laid out and prepared.

Great content and overall effective teaching with a hands-on approach to state-of-the-art machine learning techniques through projects. The professor is able to effectively break down difficult concepts for the students.

Professor You does a great job of explaining even some of the more difficult concepts and does a great job of using graphics and charts to help visual learners. He has accommodated all the requests that I made. Professor and the TAs are also very quick to respond to questions on Ed and always try to answer our questions.

The professor is so knowledgeable about the subject. I love that there are many interesting and actual topics discussed in the lectures. Lectures very clearly explain difficult concepts in a manner that is understandable

Even if I do not fully comprehend everything, I get an overall impression of what I am doing. I picked up two software and a broad range of concepts in ML. The homework assignments are really good for learning.
The class is recorded so I can go over the lecture at my own pace. Prof. and all the TAs are very supportive. The assignments help me connect real world implementation with the course material.
Dr. You is an excellent teacher and his light-heartedness is breath of fresh air compared to Uber-serious and dull lecturers Ive had in the past.

Professor Fengqi should be teaching other professors teaching techniques. I think the university will benefit a lot of having Professor Fengqi as couch to other professors and help them to successfully deliver their classes.
The professor is so knowledgeable about the subject. I love that there are many interesting and actual topics discussed in the lectures . The grading is very fair and reasonable!
Professor Fenqi is committed to students success, makes an extremely complicated topic easy. Take all his course if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: World class support from the Professor and his 3 TAs in my humble opinion. Offers a Ton of office hours for different schedules and time zones for students. During office hours questions and explanation and extra help with a smaller audience is very helpful for the subject. Very useful addition of forum called ED. help is there if you want to seek
+1 great professor and five-star class!
very engaging class, speedy replies to all my emails, flexible deadlines, abundant office hours. I had a great time at his class!

Absolutely one of the best cheme professor at Cornell! He is quite knowledgeable, caring, and supportive in may ways, while not as harsh as other professors in cheme design. It has been several years since I took his course, and he is very kind recently helping me on my PhD applications. Take his course if you can!
Nice professor. helpful course. helped me navigate the college life. hope I would have him as my professor in another course.
Thank you for a great summer course, professor. And thank you for helping my graduate application. I hope to take your other courses in future years.
Awesome professor and five-star course. I will graduate soon and won't take his course again. Take this summer course with Prof. You if you could.

The course content is really interesting and very useful. I feel like I learned a lot and am much more capable in the field of optimization, and at the same time the course wasn't very challenging as far as the workload or project were concerned. Take this class if you can!

Homeworks could be challenging sometimes, but the TA and Professor are quite generous in offering time to help and in grading. No exam - an obvious plus. I live the group projects studying COVID-19 vaccine distribution - I wish my team could consider that topic. I plan to take the machine learning course next semester, and really look forward to it
Great professor, interesting topics, fair grading, abundant office hours and helpful TAs. A five-star course!

Professor You is an expert on optimization and even a better teacher. He know s how to explain difficult concepts well, and also draw real life applications to motivate the study. I had great experience with Professor You in this summer course, and wish he would offer more ORIE courses in the future.

Took this course in the summer as an elective requirement for my CS major. The experience is much better than expected. Prof is nice and caring; rigorous content and well organized lectures. I like he provided slides on all details and interesting connections with data science. Take his course if you can and he teaches this ORIE course again

This class was intellectually challenging and the final project took me 25+hours but You is the best professor Ive had so far, he is very caring and accommodating. Super easy grader. Grading is super fair.
This course is great. Professor You is awesome!
Given the topic, the content of the class provides a really good set of tools to tackle optimization problems. Content was well structured and managed.

I found I could get a lot more out of this class during the summer than I could get out of those same class being taken concurrently with three others during the standard semester. This course is very good, and very well organized. I value most the lectures and recitations.

Prof You was a great teacher and was great at explaining the concepts and their real-world applications. There was a lot of time allotted for practicing examples and asking questions, which I valued greatly and do not see often in other classes. The lecture forces you to think and understand instead of passively listen.

I don't think any one needs to take this Engineering Seminar course again, so the question of take this prof again is inapplicable. Prof You is very kind and caring. He spent a whole Sunday morning helping me with pre-enrollment and course selection. The course covers all aspects on college life. He is a much better prof than others I met so far.

I can tell that Professor You cares that the students are learning the material. I appreciated that he gave us so much freedom in the project as it really enabled us to think about what we learned this past semester and how to apply it in a meaningful way. The hws were relevant and challenged us to think outside of the examples shown in the class.

I do not exaggerate but Professor Fengqi has exceeded all my expectations. We are talking about a TRUE teacher, who knows the subject, make you want to learn more and study. For assistance to DL students we are talking about daily support and care! In my eyes, he is a real top University professor and I feel very proud to be a member of his class.

Prof. You is the best professor I have had in my 22 credit hours of experience at Cornell. His lectures are engaging, course content is relevant and interesting, and gradings are fair. His focus on students and their success makes me appreciate my time at Cornell. He has set the standard to which all other course delivery should be measured.

Professor You organized his lecture slides by topic so we didn't have to open a million different slide decks to find the material to study. He provided so many real life examples of the material and their model formulations so the content felt especially applicable, relevant, and understandable. Help was always available with the office hours.

Prof. You is an excellent instructor. His command in Optimization topic is outstanding. The course slides/materials are of high quality. Prof. has explained all the solving methods in detail and with examples. I can clearly connect these methods in Machine Learning, since machine learning is an enhancement of Optimization.

The course slides are very well prepared and were all that was needed in order to be successful in the course. The homeworks are very good resources or student to better understanding the course material. The lectures are well-structured and very clear. I appreciated and enjoyed course material being presented with many real world applications.

My first course at Cornell. I like the Mr. You's style - very chilled, caring and flexible. I thought he would be upset after I told him I am less into ChemE and more towards CS, but he instead was very supportive and talked to me a lot about AI and data science. I will unlikely have him as my advisor after moving to CS. A great professor for ENGRG

Course learning is minimal since Professor an TA's goes over material very fast, focusing more on historical context, without much focus on application aspect. Grading could be look arbitrary, since marks distribution is not always specified.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. You learned our names and made an effort to extend help to anyone who needed it. The class was easy, even for those with no-coding background like myself. Learned a lot. The expectations aren't that high. If you take advantage of OHs and put in the effort on homeworks and project, easy A. Take his course if you can! Highly recommended!
Given the topic, the content of the class provides a really good set of tools to tackle optimization and data science problems. Content was well structured and managed.

This was one of the most beneficial courses I have taken. The lectures are very well organized, and Professor's' slides are clear and self-explained. Grading is quite fair. A lot of fun with coding. It should be mandatory for all Systems Engineers!

I took prof You's machine learning course in the spring, and this is my 2nd course with him. 6 HWs + 1 project + 1 optimization wiki. workload is reasonable and grading is fair. Similar to the spring course - very well organized and a lot of flexibility to choose the programming difficulty. I wish there were more courses with him that I could take.

I took this course remotely from a different time zone. the prof is very caring. he makes all lecture videos available and always replies to emails very fast. His lectures are well organized into 8 modules, and lecture slides have much better quality than other courses that I am taking. I feel that I learned a lot, especially on Python coding.
Very kind and helpful professor. Spend the whole Sunday afternoon helping me debug my code. Always very considerate and supportive. Thumbs up! I will take all his other courses next year.
I am very appreciative to Prof You. He is a great professor and even a great person!
Interesting professor and innovative teaching style. The assignment of developing a wiki is quite unique. I am fond of his course!

Professor You is the best professor at sysen! After he knew that I am located in Europe and the evening office hours would be too late for me, he immediately added afternoon office hours to accommodate my schedule. The class is not so easy as some told me, but Professor You is always helping outside classroom making learning much easier.
Amazing professor! Plentiful of office hours! Wonderful teaching support! Very responsive replies to emails and piazza. I plan to take all his courses at SYSEN distance learning program

You is the best professor Ive had so far, he is very caring and accommodating. Super easy grader. Insightful homeworks and fun in class lectures. He helped me a lot when I have questions after the class.

I was attracted to the course because of the certificate, but I now find the course much more useful to my work than I expected. Optimization has many applications to all fields, and the professor did a good job to cover the applications without too much hard theory, while making the course interesting enough to challenge us. Abundant office hours.

A five-star professor! Very speedy replies to emails; generous in grading and deadline extension; amenable to all requests; helpful in organizing teams; exceptionally supportive and patient. He is a good reason for us to study at Cornell. TAs are great as well. Highly recommend this course to all DL students!

Second the best CBE professor at Cornell! There is no exam in this course, giving fair assessments through homeworks and project without the exam pressure. After Prof You learned that I am taking the course from a different time zone, he acted promptly to make attending lectures an optional choice by students. Very chilled and caring professor!

I am taking the course online due to travel concerns this semester. NO exam! Lectures are not mandatory to attend. Videos, piazza and office hours are very supportive. Very responsive replies to all my questions. Professor You rocks! The BEST CBE prof!
An excellent course.

Hands down the best class I've taken at Cornell so far. Professor You is hilarious and very smart. While it's not an easy subject, You makes it very manageable and you will learn a lot of real world skills in this class.
Professor You is very engaging and makes himself available to help. I enjoyed the course and his lectures.
Took this course in the summer. Very reasonable workload. Assignments were a fair judge of applying knowledge and expectations were clearly communicated and reasonable.
Too partial to some students. Often makes the TAs handle classes
Very timely assignment feedback and clarification to questions, especially with the weekends.

Deep learning and machine learning is done on the job where I work and would like to get into the field that is why I took the class. very good material and applicable to real world examples. Grading scheme and expectation for projects clear and fair.

I loved this course. Incredibly interesting area of study. I felt compelled to learn more throughout. Having to complete a project really helped to learn the nuances as well on a practical level. Not only say we understand deep learning but that we've actually done development using deep learning, a critical distinction.
Projects were great way to learn and presenting helped to address any other aspects that we may have overlooked. Professor You is the best.

The professor was always available over email when I asked questions even on the weekend and was prompt to respond. I was very impressed by this. Every time I sent an email to professor You I received a response typically within 12 hours.

Great professor. Very responsive to questions on piazza and by emails. Homeworks are the right level of difficulty to help us comprehend the material without placing an unexpectedly difficult burden/challenge on the students.
Professor You is the most professional, most helpful, and most well prepared lecturer in my experience as a distance learner at Cornell. Very GOOD class!
Professor You is a good professor, however I would say some reviews are very generous...
Excellent professor. I have taken all of the classes that he offers and enjoyed every single on of them.

Very engaging class and interesting applications. Professor is extremely knowledge about course topics and always ready to help. Great class overall. One of the best in the Systems Engineering Masters track.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: take this class. meet with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you go to his lecture you will do well. He is a wealth of knowledge. Ask him anything, he knows. Do the work.
Professor Ahl is a GENIUS. Genuinely an old-world gem. Otherworldly intelligence that can be hard to follow, but once you embrace his thought processes you begin to think differently too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you love greek stuff you will love his class. He is very devoted.
GREAT

An absolutely amazing professor and person in general. Show up to his class and just listen. Write a few notes but really just absorb the content. Most importantly DO THE READINGS!!!! If you go to class, participate and do the readings this will be the most fun and amazing class. A class with Professor Ahl is an experience no one should pass up!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The most fascinating and engaging lecturer I've had at Cornell, and in my top 2 or three all time (I have a BA elsewhere).  Like another reviewer said, sometimes you just put the pen down and listen. Assigned very creative and effective essay prompts, one of which I now use as a writing teacher. Opinionated for sure. Progressive white British.

Fred Ahl is an all-time great professor. I was his student 43 years ago and he was one of the most impressionable professors I have ever had in my life. Fred has no hubris. He is what he is, and he is excellent at what he teaches. I learned Attic Greek From Prof. Ahl, and he was the best Classics professor I ever had.

The man certainly knows his subject but his pompous attitude and lack of respect for opinions other than his own make class aggravating at times. He was not helpful with grading and just difficult to work with in general. Avoid unless you are a die-hard classics fan.

This professor is very opinionated and does not grade fairly. I wrote a paper about religious themes in a certain play and he objected strongly to everything I wrote. He has a pet theory for every play he assigns. And he shows very little respect for students. He would mockingly read little bits from students' papers.
If you haven't taken a course with Professor Ahl, you're entire university experience has been a worthless waste of time. He is undoubtedly the best professor at Cornell.

I took a few courses with Ahl almost ten years ago and his remain the best lectures I have ever heard in my life.  I sat through his classes riveted and anticipating whatever it was about antiquity he would say next.  It was amazing and I am grateful I happened into his classes.

He knows more or less everything about Ancient Greece, and never once used notes during a lecture. Also a very nice guy. Lots of reading, most of which is enjoyable, but make sure you keep up, or else you will be sorry when the midterm and final come around!
I'm the curly-haired greek.  Hot!
Lots of dense reading for this course, but great lecturer and interesting material to write about.  Tough midterm and final, but learned alot
Forget ratings; forget grades.  A class with Professor Ahl is a memorable experience not to be missed at Cornell.

I love professor Ahl. He tells histories like he knows the people he's talking about personally and sometimes it turns out he does. If you're good he'll have the class over for dinner and prove his cooking is as incredible as his lectures.

I would sometimes just put down my pencil and listen in awe as he told greek history/myth like a bedtime story. This man is a great talker and I came away feeling like I'd lived in another century for an hour.

As a Latin teacher, Fred Ahl is tough. If you don't work hard, you will be toast. That said, he is something of a paper tiger; as long as you ARE trying very hard, don't worry too much about his threats. He's tremendously devoted to his students. Occasionally goes on liberal rants in class, which can be irritating if you don't agree with him.
Professor Ahl is THE MAN. That's all I have to say.
Great and challenging professor and an excellent person.
No Comments

Professor Ahl has a great personality; brilliant, knows what, 20 languages?  Very full of grand ideas and schemes.  This makes him a very good lecturer, though he rambles a lot.  The semester I took Tragic Theater he set up and directed a play for our class to participate in.  Afterwards had a nice party in his home with nice wine!
very erratic in his moods, impossible to find in his office, full of grand ideas but not helpful on specific points. Charming personality, but not reliable as a teacher/mentor.
Makes you think in ways you've never thought before.  Extremely interesting and the best professor/teacher I've ever had the pleasure of learning from.
Best professor I ever had
Fred Ahl is the best professor at Cornell. Period.
Very timely and organized just as a lecturer should be. The material is useful and applicable to the real world.

What are you guys talking about, Miss Ahlers is the easiest grader I've ever encountered at Cornell, she runs a wonderful class, speaks clearly, and the work load is light compared to any engineering class.  Highly recommended.
Tough class

There is a LOT of work for this course, and she is a HARD grader. If you are taking a tough engineering courseload, it's probably not a good idea to take this class with her.I decided to switch to the ENGRC  335 class taught by Rick Evans and he was a substantially easier/better professor. I would recommend taking the class with Rick Evans instead.

Very good instructor.  Sharon's very easy going, willing to go out of her way to help students and truly cares about the course.  The workload is fairly light throughout the semester and the assignments actually do serve a purpose.  Overall, a very good class

Organized, clear and hefpful this professor really makes an effort to that your presentation and writing skills improve. Excellent course to take regardless of your major. Do not be discouraged by seemingly intense course load, its really is not that bad and help is always there.
Excellent teacher, great class.  Highly recommended for all engineers.
She is wonderful! Very helpful, and the class is super interesting...one of my favorites! She keeps it interesting and fun, and is a really nice and approachable person.
she tries to be helpful, and she is nice, but Class lectures are boring.  Must go to class because nothing useful in the textbook

This class is also listed as ENGRD 251. She lectures clearly and strives to incorporate relevant current events into assignments and broaden knowledge. For most students, this is the first class where students will be assigned case studies and will need to write up an engineering report. She assigns no textbook, you buy the notes from her for $10.

While the professor is nice in person, this is an introductory physics class that is VERY deflated. It functions by "anything that can harm you will harm you."  The subject matter is pretty interesting, but this is not a well-structured class.

The class itself is interesting, but the tests are incredibly unfair. I feel as though I learned a lot, but it is difficult to demonstrate that knowledge on tests, as it reaches farther than what we have learned in class. He is also difficult to follow and has a very old-school way of lecturing. May have been good in the 80's, but now should retire

I loved being in Prof. Sadoff's class, but his tests were extremely difficult. The subject matter was interesting, and his lectures and book explained it very well, but the exams went so far beyond anything we'd learned in class. And he requires answers word-for-word. Also, your TA really matters-- and frequently they aren't very good.

Prof. Sadoff is really passionate about his work.  He loves to take extra time out of his evenings multiple times a week to meet his students for dinner to talk about physics or anything else.  He is sometimes a little picky about answers on exams and homework, but it's pass/fail, so the exam/homework grade doesn't matter a whole lot.

A great man and teacher who tries to instill his passion for physics onto his students. Most of the class is based on his book with some stuff from his lectures as well. There is homework and a few exams that require time and effort, but the class isn't anything crazy. That doesn't mean this class is an easy A, though, because it's not.

Warm hearted man with a whack sense of humor. Very passionate about his material & wanted us to know HIS book, word for word. Lectures were more often than the not, WORD FOR WORD of his txtbook. Test questions can be worded VERY poor. Interesting subject until he battered it to a pulp. I say go for it if you're ready to memorize a novel :)

I really enjoyed this class, but none of my classmates seemed to as much as I did. Just read his book, it's like a detailed outline of his lectures. Easy to do well if you read and interesting material. I had no experience in physics and it was very doable. Emphasis on relativity the last 3 weeks which is pretty interesting.

A silly professor past his prime. His arrogance and subjectivity show up where they hurt the most:on exams. Even the TA's don't agree with this man. Go take a fair and at least an interesting science class.
This is for Why is the Sky Blue? He is a really nice guy, and he really cares about making sure that the class is basic, for the people who are not really into science. Overall an interesting class
He is a really nice guy, but his class is really hard. This class should not be worth one credit. It takes too much of your time. Not a fair class overall. Really like the guy, though.
Genuinly tries to interact, which for a big class at Cornell is saying something. Liken him to a less comedic version George Carlin.
A little too much work for one credit but the class was very interesting.

I'm the same person who wrote below comment. The prelim today was hard, because I didn't study hard. I think if you study hard this subject, you will get much out of it before taking more harder Quantum mechanics courses. However, you should know that it requires much effort despite of 1 credit. Besides, dinner with the professor everyweek is nice.
It's not a 1 credit course. You should consider the ratings on this page before enrolling. I agree with below. I should have considered that comment, or at least dropped it.

In my opinion this class is a joke. i didn't study for the first pre-lim and beat the mean by 30 points. studied for the second and beat the mean by 50. he teaches you like a five year-old and requires very little of you in terms of actual understanding. The homeworks are easy, my only complaint is that attendance is mandatory.
I dont understand why cornell hired him. His class is a nightmare, I used to be interested in quantum physics and now he just ruined it. Didn't even cover the whole book and i learned nothing useful.

Worst class ever! Sadoff uses his book notes to teach the class, almost word for word. He has to check attendance or no one would ever show up! Tests are infinatly harder than his lectures prepare you for. Soooooo boring!
No Comments

Sadoff needs to stop recylcing the same course verbatim from the 1980's. Exams have too many questions with arbitrary grading, and many problems whose sole purpose is to test whether you were in lecture on day X. Definetly not as good as I hoped for.
Sadistic Sadoff is the worst professor ever. He is boring, and does not inspire us to learn. His tests are very unfairly graded and have trick questions. The TA's are cool though! :)

This review applies only to Physics 117, not 201.  117 is not fun.  It is not just concepts(many formulas and calulations that you must memorize).  The problem sets are broing and tedious.  You must work for the credit.  Don't take it, spend + time on 116
The class was informative and covered a lot of different topics. He gives extra credit opportunities and the exams are reasonable. Pretty straightforward for 4 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I think he's okay and tries his best, but his teaching style isn't really my favorite. Usually we read before class and have a pop quiz on it. It's ✔️-, ✔️, or ✔️+. Take note cuz they help for exams. Overall, I probably would not choose a professor with this style again. Too much reading and some are hard to understand...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is very kind! His feedback on essays is thoughtful and encouraging. The class readings were also intellectually stimulating, and it is clear he is knowledgeable in his area of study. Highly recommend this class for anyone looking for a survey course in the Asian Studies department (or if you're an English major, for LoA or GS).

Really amazing, kind professor! Had him for my English seminar class this semester. Upholds attendance policies and syllabus guidelines, but cares about students and the texts so much. Highly recommend :)

Weirdest class ever, 1.5 hour long lectures where he basically j quizzes u on the reading for that day, makes you finish specific lines from 30+ page text. Would also say class is very extreme w social politics and pretty outrageous at times e.g. asked a student how they felt abt being a person of color in finance as it aligns w imperialism
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class, show up and participate and you will do well. Fun to talk to people you wouldn't otherwise and you can see the tangible change the material facilitates within both yourself and your peers.

If you need to take this for your ILR diversity requirement just wait for the other diversity ethics course. this class is graded so unnecessarily harsh for no reason, one of my hardest courses for this semester and you really just don't know what they are looking for in those reflection papers. Participating in class session is easy.

I took the course and then became a facilitator after. Yes, it can get tedious to read so many papers and write the weekly essays so it's supposed to not feel easy -- it's supposed to challenge students' critical thinking and reflections. The payoff is so worth it and is truly a unique experience for students from all backgrounds.
This is the worst class ever

I absolutely hate this class. I have gotten C's on half of the papers. They don't care about how well you write or how deeply you incorporate the class materials -- they care about how much discrimination you face. The same 3 topics are discussed every class for 3 hours. You can't miss a section. A diversity credit should be an easy A. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I thought this was a chill class. Show up, do the work (write papers, reading comments, and talk in class) and you're guaranteed an A. With a little effort, it's not hard to get an A+. Was kinda cool to talk to kids who you normally wouldn't have overlapping social circles with so I would take it if you need an A or a requirement.

The curriculum is tedious since you have to write a paper essentially every week on top on doing the readings. The papers were graded inconsistently depending on who graded it. The feedback was circular and just kept recommending writing resources on campus. I feel like my writing was not the problem, but rather the dry prompts that lacked depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: EDUC 2610 is an annoying and tedious class. Much of the curriculum and content in every 3 hour class period is pretty much spent on discussing how good and valuable the class and program (Intergroup Dialogue Project) is. There's lots of talk of changing society through education, but this class does nothing for that goal. Lots of work and it sucks.

An aimless class with no goals or meaningful takeaways whatsoever. Weekly sessions are led by student "facilitators" and 3 hours long -- but still accomplish nothing. Tons of reading that serves no purpose b/c irrelevant or repetitive. Strict grading criteria for annoying papers. Can't discuss grades over email as they claim it's "against FERPA."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: EDUC 2610 is the worst class I have taken at Cornell. 25 students have a pointless discussion for 3 straight hours. The content is useless and you spend the first 8 weeks covering common sense topics like respect. I got a B on my first paper, and I only got an A after I started making up stories about discrimination (that's what they want to hear).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is definitely a tough and harsh grader, I was not aware of the circumstances of her teaching and grading style before enrolling in her class. I just wanted to come on here and share that you will really have to work and give your everything to obtain the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was mainly boring and non enthusiastic, grades weren't easy to maintain in the class, overall wouldn't recommend
Respectable professor, but harsh grader and is not flexible with any grade related content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader, must put in full work capacity.
Prof Reyes means well (I think), but can be dreadfully boring….so much so that I can't even focus on what she's saying. Like would it kill to not just read off the slide?
She is removing reviews. Very boring and has a few loose screws. Class is graded by a few things. Most things covered in class are intuitive

Not enthusiastic, somewhat boring, but tries very hard to be concise in lectures. Sometimes it is hard to see why lectures are important, or how things connect. Grading criteria are fair and well-documented.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Reyes is very sweet. Her lectures are not the most enthusiastic but the content is interesting and she clearly knows what she is talking about. The class wasn't too hard either. iClickers are used to track attendance, 5 short papers on the readings, a book report with a group presentation, and policy brief. Great/easy class for HCP minors.

Dr. Hoffman was a great and interesting lecturer. The class is super easy if you come to class and study (my class was at 8:40 in the morning, so many people missed class). The assignments are a little bit annoying, but I still enjoyed the material and professor, so I would take the class again!

Loved Prof Hoffman and this class even tho it was 8:40 am 🫣 but he made it interesting and I stayed awake! Plus if you go to the gym before class you'll prob see him there getting hyped lol 😆 Honestly, an icon and super dedicated to student learning. He brings guests to show different stages of human development & that's super cool and engaging.

Professor Hoffman was a great instructor, and the course material was clear and easy to understand. The class mainly uses lecture slides and includes two assignments. Attendance is optional, but lectures often include exam hints (attend class). The course is memorization-based, so reviewing notes and using Quizlet makes the prelims much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor was great. Lectures were optional but I highly recommend attending them as he gives test hints during them. He provides extra credit which can be beneficial if you do poorly on an assignment once so its not like your grade will fall from one bad exam/assignment. Exams were super fair and based on the content and he doesn't trick questions

Professor Hoffman taught a very easy yet interesting class. The grading is 3 prelims, an infographic, and a 2-page paper. Attendance is not mandatory but in class he will give "hints" about what is on the prelim.  He also offered extra credit for completing the class survey. Overall, if you are looking for an easy HD class this is a great option.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An absolute G. Exams were more than reasonable, lectures were very interesting. 3 exams (all doable) and 2 assignments. Extra credit as well. Very nice dude and chill lecturer. Would recommend to anyone.

Hoffman's lectures were a thorough breakdown of the material you'd get from the textbook, and he made clear what material was necessary for exams. Fascinating material, straightforward exams (attending lectures is helpful), and an engaging lecturer overall. A couple of papers, but they're short and not bad at all. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
8:40am lectures = 20% show but everyone and their mom showed up when the prelims came around.
The class is graded on 5 things: 3 prelims (50 MCQ), 2 papers.

Oddly, I stopped showing up to class and got a higher grade on the prelims and papers. LOL
However, he does hint what will be on the exam if you do show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures weren't too interesting and was mostly reading off the slides, but he is generally cheerful and passionate about the course. He gives out hints on exam questions during lectures, so go to them! Exams are heavy on multiple-choice questions so get ready to use flashcards.
Super sweet professor! You will do well in this class as long as you study the slides! Consists of 2 prelims, 1 final exam, and 2 papers. I would 10/10 recommend this class to anyone!

HD1130/PSYCH1131, awesome class. Prof. Hoffman is funny and a breath of fresh air, clearly cares about what he teaches. Even though he reads off of slides, he applies useful scenarios, and relays the content in an interesting way. I recommend going to lecture but its not necessary. 3 prelims, final non-cum, 2 papers. Textbook not needed :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: just him reading the slide! don't need to come to the lecture at all

He is very nice and fair. Lecture is optional, there's no homework, and there were 3 prelims and 2 papers. All were fairly easy. You can study just by reading the textbook or reviewing slides/flashcards and you'll do good. Interesting, easy A class!

Prof was basically reading off slides that he posted on Canvas so going to the lecture isn't necessary, however, I did think some examples and extra details he gave in class were helpful. The tests are multiple-choice and pretty easy as long as you review all of the slides (No need to read the textbook, the slides have all the info you need).

Great and very understanding professor. Lectures are dense, but he gives amazing review sheets with everything you need to know for the exams and the final wasn't cumulative. I would definitely recommend this class.

- not a bad professor. however, lectures are just him reading off the slides -- slides are straight from the textbook reading and are posted online. not much motivation to come to class
- his study guides prepare you for the content he puts on the exams. exams are very straight forward.

not very engaging class but very interesting content overall
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, so engaging and genuinely all around great guy. GO TO CLASS and TAKE NOTES it will make a huge difference because you will not be able to just study based off of notes posted. Most of the important formulas and solutions he will ONLY talk about in class.

Absolute aura farmer of a professor. You must attend class AND take notes. If note-taking is neglected, you will struggle on the exams bc a lot of the material is gatekept & left off the slides. Tests focus on depth rather than breadth, so ensure you understand the reasoning behind each concept. Just knowing how to use the formulas will not cut it.

Professor Addoum is a pretty great teacher. I think hes pretty funny and his lectures are all pretty informative. Just get ready for the 3 exams since thats really the only thing your grade is dependent on.
aura max professor of finance
chill professor but tries too hard to be funny. does not provide any practice for exams other than the 4 easy homework we had that did not help on the exams. take the hotel version instead.
Very chill guy. Tests are very similar to HWs and were curved like crazy
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite professor on campus hands down. The finance class he teaches is critical for any business student to take as the concepts you learn are invaluable. He is a fantastic lecturer, and keeps things clear for everyone to understand. The material can be tough but curve is huge, he is awesome, and I couldn't recommend a class with him more.

Took finance with him. Lecture slides are very useless. Doesn't provide any practice materials that are useful for his exams. The content we're presented on exams are nothing like what we learned in class.

Great professor, actually made people do some work for once in the major. Lectures are absolutely necessary as tests count for 75 percent of your grade, and there are not many other options to learn the material. Exams are curved very generously

Professor Addoum is one of my favorite professors in Dyson. His class (corporate finance) is, by far, one of the most useful courses I have taken. His lectures are captivating and well structured. He is reasonable and never asks you to do impossible tasks.

I learned soooo much about Brown v. Board through this class. The reliance on group discussions was a nice difference from other courses. He's also VERY accessible outside of class. You really only have to lock in for the last assignment; everything else is super chill. Make sure to participate consistently, or else it may impact your grade. 10/10.
This is the greatest class I've ever had, taught by the greatest prof I've ever had. I am so serious, take any class taught by Lee Adler if you can

Great professor and interesting topic, but class is unorganized. Readings and assignments are sent in long/confusing email chains. Otherwise, Prof is very knowledgeable and shares many personal stories about the topic of the day. Lots of reading, but no need to do it all. Participation/attendance and a final paper are all that grades are based on.

Prof. Adler is one of the best professors in all of ILR. He has amazing experiences to tell and truly cares about his students and the material he teaches. He may go off-topic a fair amount but only because of his enormous breadth of knowledge in literally every topic imaginable.

Professor Adler really cares about his students and caters his lectures to the class. Most of the work is reading court cases and then discussing them in class. His papers are tough, but you will learn a lot in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does everything he can to get you to participate and engage with the material. It's a fair amount of reading but it's worth it. He's a passionate and wonderful man.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Really easy to get to know. He will remember you if you participate in his class discussions. He has helped me figure out my goals both academically and personally. If you show him that you're passionate about his subject matter, he will advocate for you and score you well. The best professor in ILR in my opinion.
Amazing professor. The kind of professor that embodies the true mission of ILR. He has real world blue collar union experience, and is extremely smart.

HE IS THE SMARTEST PROF AT CORNELL. If you have the opportunity to take his class, take it. He has given his life to help those who need legal labor help (pro bono): coal workers, firefighters, police. He is what the original charter of ILR was all about.

Professor Adler is the man.  Kept us engaged with current events as well as well-selected cases to demonstrate changes/progressions in public sector labor law history.  He's very funny and has a ton of old-time sayings that are hilarious.  Has great connections for guest speakers and events.

this guy is terrible, he is the most unclear professor one will have at Cornell. Everyone walked out of class totally confused. He  also never stays on topic, even if u ask him a question and this lends itself to his unclarity. Very hard grader, dont expect more then a B, in this class

The professor is a really down-to-earth type of guy who can really relate to students.  He challenges students to analyze things in a more comprehensive manner.  The cases are very interesting to read although they can be rather lengthy.

ABSOLUTELY do not take this class. While homework and overall work os very manageable. Class is not a good environment. Can feel very scared to make mistakes and picks on certain students for no teason. He actually picks on students that are struggling in the language. Never had anxiety until started this class because of him.

Compared to other language courses, this is definitely one of the best options. He is EXTREMELY disorganized which makes the course much more stressful, but he ultimately gives everyone a good grade (A- or above), unless you are really bad then maybe he'll give you a B+. Much less work than other language classes. He acts a lot and is fun also!
He's a good professor, his grading is haphazard though and there's more emphasis on speaking the language than actual tests

I really enjoyed this class! ADEMOYO IS A GREAT PROFESSOR! He aims to have his students learn the material but does not overwhelm them. The class is totally manageable and the professor is extremely helpful. Best language class I've EVER taken :)
Insane teacher!! Really animated and funny. Subtly disguises heavy philosophy in jokes. A good class to have in Freshman year.

Very nice professor. Likes to encourage students. Informs us on ongoing political and cultural issues. He's very animated and enthusiastic about teaching. Sometimes he's a little too nice to undeserving students. It's not even a hard class! Simply attend and learn Yoruba (the best language and people in the world! :-) )

Pretty light workload, but when exams come around be ready to spend a lot of time figuring out what you were supposed to be learning all semester. Extremely poor organization, 60% of lecture recapping last lecture. Review material almost nothing like what gets tested and is often incorrect. Check EdDiscussion constantly for corrections of mistakes
Don't bother. Take the class in the spring.

Every lecture, repeats 70% of content from previous lecture, yet somehow still makes it incomprehensible. Disorganized course with zero feedback from grades, students are left on their own to figure everything out.

Such an unorganized class. The prelim is in a few days but nothing about the prelim has been answered on Ed. The only thing given was a past prelim as practice material given on Friday when the prelim is on Tuesday. TAs can't even tell us if a note sheet is allowed for the prelim. Overall we, including the TAs and professor are all confused.

The lectures for this class are very boring, and have no substance. What makes it even worse is the fact there is no real "book" that you can look at to self study. The discussion sections are even more boring as the TAs are very lost and disorganized. The whole class structure is disorganized and questions in ED remain unanswered.

Literally such an amazing professor! Super enthusiastic about what he is teaching, always encourages questions. He really makes everyone feel really positive about coming to his class. His lectures are AMAZING, but somehow he always apologizes. 

My absolute favorite professor (+most humorous professor) at Cornell!
Love this professor! Absolutely my favorite class at Cornell since 4 years ago. The professor is very inspirational and he really wants to help you learn. Highly recommend his class
The course is theoretical but inspiring. It seems he has spent a lot of time on the course materials. You will definitely learn a lot if you put enough time on it.
The material is a mess and the professor seems to be unable to explain ideas clearly. Also, he has a strong accent.

He has a reputation for not caring about classes since he's near retirement, and can be a bit ethereal and touchy as someone else mentioned. He's really brilliant, but during the pandemic kind of lectured about something off topic. Kind of moody, and maybe even rude at times

Professor Aching is awesome! He is extremely intelligent and knowledgable of the subject he is teaching while simultaneously open to hearing and understanding the opinions of others. He is also really understanding when it comes to extensions, missing class, etc. Grading is a bit tough but you get used to it and there's not that much work.

He is a solid professor overall and likes to answer questions. He does not give rubrics for his few graded assignments. I found that he contradicted himself sometimes ideologically and seemed to respect his own ideas more than students' or just had a hard time relating. He says he is understanding but also puts you off a bit too, so tread lightly.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ehsan seems really smart, but he is the worst kind of professor to have. He isn't helpful outside of class, and assigns labs and homeworks that take upwards of 10 hours to complete, every week. He is great in lecture, but makes the class unbearable.

This guy is smart, but teaches stuff wayyyy too fast, and gives homework way harder than anything we've done in class. If you have the time to read the book for hours on end outside of class, then this guy is great, but with the assumption we all have other things to do, this class was way too difficult.
He taught the course really well
Great teaching made this not so easy course much easier to understand. Helped my understanding in other courses as well.
He spends enough time on all details and goes deep to the heart of the subject. Overall the course was useful, but not easy at all.
Great course and organized lectures.
Always willing to help out, answer questions, and get to know students. You can tell he truly cares about his students and their learning. Exams were a good reflection of homeworks/practice prelims

Amazing guy. Great lectures and very approachable in and out of class. For exams, as long as you do the homework and review materials you're already very well prepared. If you get a chance to take class with him, don't hesitate!

Taking a course with Marcelo Aguiar is truly a privilege. His lectures are well-structured and inspiring. In office hours and even after lecture he is super approachable and answers all questions clearly. His exams are on par with the review materials he provides.

His notes are immaculately organized + he always provides concrete examples of the abstract/convoluted theorems that we learn. Super accessible outside of class + always answers emails + stays up to over an HOUR after class helping students. Extremely clear when answering questions. Exams are SUPER reflective of stuff covered in class. 100/10.

Professor Aguiar is definitely one of the best professors in the math department. If you pay attention in class, you should not have any problems following him and do well in the course. He would always stay after class to answer questions. If you do ask him questions, he would give an answer appropriate for your level of mathematical maturity.
80% of your grade was based on exams. The exams were really difficult and did not match the level difficulty on homework and review material.
He is amazing!

Hands down a GOAT professor. Puts an incredible amount of efforts into preparing for class and helping students. Explains things clearly and concisely so try not to miss lectures. Truly cares about his students. Questions are always welcome and help is available almost whenever. Much-appreciated accommodations were made during covid19.

Aguiar was so lovely. He encourages students to ask questions and tries to link the class to real-world examples. He has a good grasp of how much students can viably absorb in one class and usually doesn't try to overstuff the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is amazing. He explains math so carefully/simply that anyone who pays attention will understand everything eventually. This was the only class where I didn't miss a single lecture because if you do you'll miss his great explanations. Go to class, do your homework, and do the exam handouts before every exam. And you'll do great
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far, this was the most amazing math professor I have ever had. Sit in one lecture and you'll see why, every definition and example he works through is explained thoroughly and instead of just giving formulas, he derives them so you really understand. I felt prepared for exams because of him. My only complaint is review sheets don't have answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a really good teacher and offers clear explanations. Although assignments are not easy, if you do go to office hours he is more than willing to help you out. He is very approachable. Try to take as many classes with him as possible. One of the nicest and genuinely concerned teachers.

Marcelo is the best teacher I've had at Cornell. His explanations are impeccable and he makes every concept in the class easy to understand. The guy loves math. If we finish class early, he'll take a few minutes to explain how what we're learning relates to cool random things in nature, like astronomy, network connectivity, biology, etc. Great guy.

This class was easy to do well in, but hard to get an A if that's what you're shooting for. The prelims are a bit knit-picky and the online textbook can be a bit boring but I would otherwise totally recommend this Intro. to Bio course for non-majors. The lectures were the most dynamic ones I've seen considering the size of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked this class a lot, and Professor Agrawal was such a great professor! While it isn't too hard to catch up if you skip, there are in-class "Poll Everywhere" questions for attendance.
Super great lecturer, and very chill class. Not too difficult and would recommend

Excellent lecturer in an intro bio course. Found lectures on monarch butterfly ecology (his area of expertise) fascinating. I thoroughly enjoyed the course, although I wish practice prelims or any sort of exam questions were given. Wish he lectured more than the other professors.
Class was interesting in terms of material, with weekly homeworks that weren't too difficult. Professor was genuinely interested in teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer,  nice guy

Great professor. Clear and concise, and absolutely love to teach. Clearly wants his students to learn instead of just stuffing random bio information down your throat and expecting you to regurgitate. He is very approachable and engaging in lecture. I really wished 3690 was taught only by him instead of a group of professors.
cool

Anurag's very appearance and his wonderful mien inspire me to galvanize myself into action, grow a magnificent neckbeard, and go out into the world to explore the uncharted wilderness. He also wears entrancing t-shirts.
Chill class

Not the most useful course but easy and extremely interesting (read: senior course). Teaches by telling awesome stories about chemical ecology phenomena in nature. Good humored, fun, really smart, approachable. Great prof.

She made it really hard to enjoy the class, since she either moved through the material too quickly, or brought in guest lecturers who didn't know what they were doing either. That being said, this class is not difficult if you do the readings in the textbook and look through and memorize notes before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: wow. just. wow. she managed to make the final exam nearly impossible to study for, and put the most random questions on the test. truly, no words to describe how disappointed I am with this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Absolutely wack. Is VERY rude to students when they ask questions, ask her to slow down, or question her data. Treats students like children (i.e. clapping to get attention) and somehow manages to make a relevant topic very boring. She also makes it difficult to study; lecture slides are not posted, class moves quickly, little guidance.

She is nice. However, the fact that version A and B of the prelim did not have the same questions is unfair to both the students who had A and the students who had B. She needs to compensate for this mistake. The first prelim was manageable but the 2nd one seemed to ask very specific and hard questions that she nor the textbook covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is a nice person but not fit at all to teach this course. She gave an exam that she just took from last year's class and realized halfway through the exam that almost half of the questions had not yet been covered in class. Material is not difficult at all but she is a boring lecturer who conducts the class as if it is a middle school class.

Worst Professor I have had at Cornell by far! Makes information that would otherwise be interesting drag on. Doesn't use any of her own material and it shows with her subpar knowledge on all subjects covered. She even gave an exam that wasn't even on the right chapters. She is careless, unprofessional, and truly terrible teacher.

It is unbelievable how unprepared one woman can be. She made me hate the adolescent development, even though it could be good if taught right. In addition to making ridiculous comments like, "The US has the highest rate of pregnancy in the world," she uses childish methods to make her class settle down such as, "If you can hear me clap twice."

Worst professor I've ever had at Cornell. She doesn't post the lecture slides online, she's extremely aggressive, she goes so fast and then gets when you ask her to go back. If you don't have to take this course, don't! (from her at least, I've heard good reviews about the prof that taught it before her).
Muna Aghawani is an awesome teacher with a beautiful soul.
very cool and cute
She is so nice and helpful, made me interested in the Middle East, class was fun

Prof Agrus is hands down the worst teacher I've ever had. I was a senior taking a lower level class and he tried to make the class as difficult as possible. He believes he is above everybody he doesn't even teach his own class he leaves that up to is students.He is so vague on what he wants, but then grades students as if they should read his mind
I leave class frustrated every day
No Comments
I am not an undergrad and I was actually taking this class because I wanted to.  And this guy managed to make me hate it. Avoid him. He is awful.

This class went REALLY slow, relatively small amount of material, and it was hard to stand out enough to get an A+. Graded only on three exams and each had very few questions. If you had a headache or illness on the day of an exam, you could tank your grade just by misreading a small part of a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: too many NGMIs saying he's bs, and it's probably because they don't review and take notes on the lectures to build a solid foundation on the content. it's an easy course, but it's also easy to fall behind since there's no required homework. i wish he had made homework required, both as a means to enforce concepts and as another grading component.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course structure is frustrating. Your entire grade is based on just three exams. The exams themselves are extremely challenging and bear little resemblance to the practice problems. He doesn't respond well to legitimate concerns about grading and is hard to contact. I wouldn't suggest taking his class, and I know a lot about computer networks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's very engaging and teaches an interesting topic. However, you are graded on only three exams, with no partial credit. The exams are hard and completely different from the practice material. He ignores valid questions about grading. He is also difficult to reach, and his lectures are difficult to understand. I would not recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy is one of the nicest most engaging lecturers I've ever had, yet simultaneously created (arguably) the most unfortunate class I've taken in college. This class has a really interesting topic, but easily the worst grading scheme and most unfair exams I've taken. Random topics are emphasized, and little prep is given. Unorganized.

The worst professor I have ever had at Cornell. His exams do not align with the problem sets released throughout the semester. On the most recent two exams, he made them both about one topic (out of dozens) and refused to test on additional material. Either you know it, or you don't. There is no partial credit. The exams do NOT test your knowledge.
The prelim is so hard and never similar to the practice he offered.

One of the best lecturers at Cornell. The class requires discipline since the homeworks aren't mandatory, they're just prep for the tests. Our final grade was fully determined by 3 exams, but they were fairly easy. The questions were almost all extremely similar to the problem sets.

Lecture is good but the tests are stupid since they test how well you can do hand simulation of network algorithms instead of your understanding of network architecture. Homework solutions sometimes riddled with mistakes. Overall the light workload compensates for most of its faults.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice guy and definitely will make time and exert the effort to help you. But... in lecture, he came across kind of snarky. Curses a lot. But simultaneously demands a lot of respect. Explains things relatively well. Almost all homeworks are required to be done in groups (of 3+, I think?). Which is actually nice, in a way.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved him while taking OS. Really cared about students' learning and their experience.

I took this class and dropped it half way. The material is interesting but he's a nightmare to deal with. Every problem in the class was always someone else's fault, never his. Seems pretty full of himself. Won't be taking a class he teaches again.

Rachit was an amazing professor. He taught the course as one long story about how and why the internet came to be designed the way that it is. This class was not really about the specific implementations of protocols, but it focused much more on what problems the protocols try to address and how to design future ones. Take this class !!!

Prof Agarwal is by far the best CS lecturer I've had. He breaks down complicated concepts in an easily accessible way and makes it his personal mission to ensure his students are confident and happy with the material. I'm a pretty apathetic student overall but his lectures made me rly excited about networks. Def recommend, he goes above and beyond!

Amazing engaging lecturer. Really cares about the topic and makes it very interesting. Great low stress course. Optional Homeworks/Projects. Only graded items are exams, which are really fair. Cannot recommend this course enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Every good rating in 4450 was done during the pandemic where 50% of their grade was a course eval. In normal times, your entire grade is based on exams, which are horribly written. He gives you ZERO prep for exams and the psets he does give have no relevance to the exams. Everyone bombed the first prelim and he did not curve the class. DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Rachit is a nice guy, but actively misleads students about the difficulty of his tests. He will tell you that going to lecture is what it takes to succeed, but that is a lie. He gave us a prelim that was so hard that even the grad TAs said it was too difficult, and he still refused to curve the exam even though the median was a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Minimal effort required outside of class, but attention required during class. Concepts are simple but tests are made really hard. Pop quizzes are easy as long as you pay attention in class. The most accessible professor in Cornell, willing to stay really late for office hour. I really like him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Agarwal is perhaps the best CS lecturer I've had here. He starts from the basics and then builds up to more complex topics, but always goes back to foundational ideas to bring everything full circle. He's also willing to help students anytime after class hours. Tests can be tricky, but go to class and a good chunk of the questions are gimmes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Computer networks class, wow! One of the best professors at Cornell CS. His lectures are amazingly well crafted. He starts with the most fundamental questions and builds the entire protocol around those questions. It is clear how much Prof. Agarwal cares about students and about teaching. One of the best classes in my four years at Cornell.

CS6455 was a new graduate class on advanced computer networks. We read a couple of papers every week with topics varying from classical papers in Internet design to recent papers in datacenter networks. We then discussed papers in the class. The class was very interactive and professor had great insights about past and future of computer networks.

I took his graduate class on big data systems in Spring 2017. I was one of the few undergrads in the class, so I had to catch up on the terminology. However, Prof. Agarwal was always available to help me catch up. He has truly interesting insights about the area and an in-depth knowledge about all the papers we discussed. I liked the class.

Prof. Agarwal is one of the most amazing lecturers at Cornell. He is engaging, funny and keeps the class interactive. He cares so much about the students. He often stayed in his office until late and came back early morning to help us with home works. I hope he improves the course organization ( and have better TAs and co-instructor in future).
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: New Professor. I find his enthusiasm and knowledge to be awesome. Was very unorganized, and this undermined the learning of this class by a lot. WIll hopefully get better soon!

It was his first time teaching, and he did a great job in the lectures (some mistakes, but the lectures were very engaging). The class was unorganized, but he was very approachable, always ready to help and really cared about us students. There are very few other professors who stay in office until 11PM to help students and come back at 8AM.

I learned OS in the 48 hours before the final exam, by studying from previous finals.  This professor provided support through unreasonable homeworks, vague expectations, and the assurance that "grades don't matter" right before he released low scores on 6 homeworks on the day the semester ended.  Enroll at your own risk.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The other responders are being a bit harsh; he's a nice/helpful guy and his lectures were pretty good, but the class was poorly organized by him to the point where it was extremely frustrating. Blowing other deadlines to get this class's work done on time, only to have him constantly shift the due dates back, was unfair to say the least.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I learned more about OS from other courses that I was taking than from this class. I just learned that instructor assignments can also have seg faults, HW grades are arbitrary, and remember kids, in a hard drive, the head spins. Clearly knows what he's doing

Worst class I've ever taken. Homeworks and projects were assigned randomly (we once had 2 Psets and 1 project due in one week). Repeatedly insisted the small details don't matter, just the underlying concepts, yet the homeworks and final exam both had really tedious questions that were never even touched on in lecture. Avoid at all costs.

I blindly stumbled through this course, consistently failing with minimal support or feedback. Professor often seemed frustrated with students being so lost and wanted to improve but didn't know how, while students were frustrated our time wasn't respected. He does have potential, and I hope he takes some feedback and becomes a great professor!

This was his first time teaching the class. I could fill a textbook with all the mistakes he made as a first time lecturer. But that won't matter because if this class has taught me anything, textbooks are worthless. Homeworks are largely just googling answers or begging TAs for help. Please take this class another semester if see this professor.

HAHAHA isn't it funny when you work all weekend to finish a project and then you get a month long extension because half the class didn't finish and you fail a prelim for another class  in the process. Good times. But in all seriousness, this class was pretty annoying. Being a guinea pig for a semester is not fun. Rachit said this would be fun :(.
Awesome!

Overall a good course. Attendance is not mandatory for portion of grade. While slides are not provided, the textbook is enough for keeping up with the material. Homework and exam mainly cover basic concepts in information theory, which may be a bit tough for students more focused on coding. Two projects emphasize novelty over programming skills.

I took Wagner for ECE 2720 and initially didn't like him.  I matured a bit since then in terms of school preparation and took ECE 4670 with him recently. Wagner will not hold your hand --- you need to go to lecture, office hours, and understand the material well. But if you do, he's a fair guy, great lecturer, and the coursework is very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved professor wagner, he is a very nice guy and cares about his students, but his content is difficult, at least in 2720. Tests are hard, and we had a final project and final exam which was a lot. However, he is super helpful in OH and encourages collaboration between students.

Professor Wagner is one of the BEST professors I have ever had, you can sense his passion through his teaching. We had a great connection with him as a class.

Having a professor this invested is definitely a big motivator for me to continue with ECE.

Thankful for Professor Wagner!

One of the best in the ECE department. Obviously an expert in information/communication theory. Took data compression with him; was challenging, but rewarding. Always willing to help during OH. Lectures are very clear and well planned out. Workload is moderate, but exams can be difficult.
GREAT CLASS
Clear and engaging lectures along with helpfulness outside of class make one of the hardest classes I have ever taken an extremely worthwhile experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wagner is one of the best professors at Cornell. He organizes lecture in a clear manner and always tries to keep it interactive so you don't fall asleep learning a ton of math. Projects in the second half of the course are extremely well designed and educational; however, they are very challenging. Exams and problem sets were also difficult.

Was the most interesting ECE class I've taken yet. The class takes all the theory from ECE3250 and ECE3100 and let's you use it to do interesting things. Prof. Wagner is clear and quite friendly. There is only one prelim. Don't screw it up or your grade will suffer. The final project (OFDM through a box) is really cool.
Great professor!

Excellent, if a bit quirky, lecturer. Really cares about students. Extremely helpful. Exams require not only mastery of material, but cleverness. Minimal amount of homework, with flexible policies. One of the best professors I've had.

Sachs is a good lecturer and he puts a lot of passion into his Environmental History course, but I get the vibe that he wishes he was teaching a literature class. We fixated on a few specific books at various points rather than covering various perspectives on each period. The class is well-structured, but I expect more variety in a history class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sachs was very passionate and kind. Lectures were a bit more vague than I expected and the essays were also very arbitrary, but the grading is not too harsh and you learn a lot of really interesting aspects of American history through the lens of environment that you wouldn't expect.
Loved this class. Def long/annoying readings to do every week for discussion, and also coming to lecture is important as he doesn't do slides. Would recommend this class to anyone.

Great lecturer, incredibly caring person. Assigns a lot of reading, and quite helpful feedback on writing assignments. One of my favorite profs I have had, would highly recommend taking a course with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are not mandatory but they are essential (no slides, only talking). Handwritten notes only. He'd lecture for most of the class and then do a Q&A at the end. I found him to be really funny and engaging. 4 papers and they're graded pretty fairly. Really (really) long readings every week for discussion though. Def one of my fav professors tho
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I cannot stress enough to anyone considering taking the course: take it. As long as you do most of the readings (enough to gain a general understanding), the essays are not hard (and they aren't long either). He is such an amazing lecturer, and it feels like he is telling stories rather than information dumping.

First time Environmental Justice was offered. Good professor who lets the class run the discussion (seminar). Gives good feedback on assignments. Graded on two short papers and one big final project. Class is very-left leaning but there is room for some more moderate opinions. Small class so you must participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gives great lectures, is a very understanding and caring person. He clearly loves teaching and interacting with students. His papers are hard, but not long, and he gives good feedback so you can improve. I would totally take his classes again.

Fascinating lectures, has challenged my preconceived notions about human impact. Writing assignments require time and effort, but he gives great feedback and recognizes those who care and want to improve. Readings are long but always engaging and lead to discussions that are thought-provoking and have allowed me to broaden my perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Not sure why there are people saying his lectures are great. I find them unbearably boring and dry, and his no technology policy applying to discussions as well is senseless. Cool topic but, in my opinion, he butchers it. Not what I was hoping for when I enrolled.
Great lecturer. Take his class.

Took Enviro History with Prof. Sachs and would recommend for anyone who is interested in the topic. Readings are lengthy but usually interesting. Only 3 papers, and prompts allow you a lot of flexibility to be creative or explore a topic of your interest. He takes the writing process very seriously but if you put in the effort you'll do well.

Wonderful lecturer, very interesting class material. Expects too much on papers for a class that is not an English course. However, he does allow for re-writes and is open to talking about papers outside of class. If you are willing to put a good amount of time into writing papers and contributing to course discussions you will probably do well.

Sachs is an excellent lecturer and you will definitely learn a lot in his class. He will also push you to improve your writing. Nevertheless, the class is difficult and you will have to work hard for a good grade. I would highly recommend the class if you are willing to put in the time

I learned nothing about history in this course (it should be an english course). We talked about the same thing every class, what you learn on the road. If you don't write in his style or do not follow his politics and personal beliefs, I would not recommend this course. I don't feel that I gained any  knowledge about the history of travel.

Not open to opinions that don't match his own. The class was way more like an English class than a History class. Also, all of the readings expressed the same viewpoint, namely the professor's. Would not take a class with him again.
more interesting than most lectures, no tests and a few papers, but all sections were spent discussing the books you wrote the papers on..

Hard prof, but more than helpful when it came to writing papers. Your critical thinking/writing ability will certainly improve if you enroll in this class. A bit too much reading to start with, but he acknowledged this in class, and reduced the workload. Only assigns papers, doesn't give tests. This might work for or against you.

Highly skilled discussion leader. Lots of reading, but really interesting and fresh material. Interested in helping students develop writing skills and encourages taking "intellectual risks" in papers (ex. lots of self-reflective writing). This class was by far the coolest class I've taken here yet: included a weekend-long backpacking field trip!

Big-headed and completely full of himself.  Not very open to opinions that don't match up with his own.  Likes to brag about his education.  Formatted class so that presentations took up all the time and he didn't have to prepare anything.  Was very interested in class material, he ruined it for me.  Would NOT ever take a class with him again.
