Sachs is obviously passionate about what he is teaching and makes the topic fairly interesting. Great reading selections, however they are somewhat heavy. He is not the worlds easiest grader but he lets you do rewrites, which is nice (but also increases workload). Paper assignments are kind of tricky. Deserves recommendation.

Sachs really is interested in what he is teaching, and it shows.  Class is lively and he really is interested in what students have to add to discussion and even lecture.  One of my favorites for sure
Typical liberal prof. If you write what he wants, you will do well.

I really loved Prof. Rock-Singer's lectures because they cleared up anything I didn't understand in the pre class readings. His class definitely packed a lot of information about pre-modern Islamic civilization, but coming from no previous knowledge on this topic, it was easy to succeed if you do the readings and attend lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Rock-Singer is a passionate teacher who is invested in his students as people.

Professor Rock-Singer was disorganized and messy. I took an intro class with him, yet I felt like I was super behind all of the students because I didn't have any previous knowledge of Islamic Civilization... the class brought down my GPA even though I was working super hard, and the readings weren't helpful!

I took 3040 with Prof Applegate, and it was a really interesting and well-constructed course. Readings were amazing, Prof Applegate is really smart and compassionate. Only lame thing was the other students-almost all of whom clearly didn't read or care much.

P. Applegate is genuinely one of the most caring professors I've ever had. While his course is challenging and requires effort + reading, it certainly pays off. He also clearly cares about his students and their success. Definitely consider taking this class as a history distribution for ILR. Really really recommend it!

Just wanted to say that in all my time at Cornell this was one of the very few professors that I felt cared about me as a human being. The course was definitely dry and not the easiest thing ever for me, but Professor Applegate is as genuine and kind as you will find in a Cornell professor.
A true gem of ILR. Solid guy inside and outside of the class. Loved his quirky comments, highly recommended

Hands down my favorite class at the ILR School. Applegate is an excellent professor if you like historical analysis! I can see how the subject matter can be sort of boring but between the readings, you're bound to find something to spark your interest. Professor Applegate gets an A+ for both his teaching and his charming character. HIGHLY RECMD.

Applegate is well aware that subject matter is not the most exciting (for many students), but tries his best to get students engaged and is extremely clear/detailed. Beyond academics, he is authentic and compassionate. 3040 is reading/writing intensive course but def working taking for a history distribution.

His classes make a great choice for an ILR history elective. Grade was based on a short essay, prelim essay, and a final essay (all take home). His grading criteria is very clear and he explicitly lays out everything you need to do on the essays in order to do well on them. He also provides a lot of feedback on essays that I found helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: My favorite ILR professor! Really cares, course was very interesting if you like business history.

Professor Applegate is a must take professor for Labor History. Though the readings are "mandatory" you don't actually have to do them. If you read the chapters that the papers are on, then you can avoid thousands of pages of wasted time. Reasonable grader if you follow ALL instructions. Lectures are boring but often informative. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Probably the most boring lecturer I have ever had.  Otherwise, fair and interesting, but will make you work to get a good grade.
Can be very dry but is super sweet and helpful. A lot of reading.

Lectures were extremely dry and hard to get through for this course. The reading wasn't unbearable, but definitely a little on the tougher side. A nice course in the sense that it is a lift from the traditional "labor history" of the LR department but I thought it was challenging. Expectations on assignments were pretty vague.

Prof. Applegate is a great professor and genuinely cares about his students. His lectures, however, are very dry. Even as someone who has a big interest in labor unionshistory I found myself struggling to pay attention. Applegate's background and life story though is super interestinginspiring! I definitely suggest going to his office hours.

very good guy. means well and if you talk to him outside of class you realize the material is pretty interesting. Not bad workload and just overall good guy. One of the more reasonable and objective professors in ILR, which is a nice relief

Very nice guy, lectures can be boring sometimes, especially if you have done the reading.  They tend to be long summaries. He does try very hard to give each student individual attention with their final papers and goes out of his way to be helpful
A tad boring at times. Overall he "gets the job done" and the class wasn't a waste of time. He'll talk forever though.....

I hate to dis this guy because he's very caring and loves his students, but he's an incredibly boring speaker.  Also, a****LOAD of reading to do, and even then it's tough to put together a compelling essay you're proud of given the weird material you have to draw from.  If you like history/reading, though, it will not be that tough.

He is the one teacher that cares for the students and shows taht he does. His class is easy but you do have to do the readings becsue the essy questions aren't just about information but also partly on events that build up a feeling or a view comparing two groups. Great guy, funny out of class BEST!

He is very easy.  He gives you the test questions a week ahead and all you have to do is memorize your answer.  I did not attend half the lectures or read any of the books because a person from section writes a summary of the reading assignment weekly.
Unfortunately he's not related to Christina Applegate...that's false advertising with this last name.  The class is easy but without stories about that fox, it's disappointing.
awesome professor. must take him

I don't think I heard a word he said all semester.  I did no reading and went to class only for the face time.Folks, the man gives out the questions before the exam, a blind dead guy could get an A in his class.

Applegate is a really great teacher. If you can handle the fact that he lectures the entire class and there is almost no participation, take him. He tells you everything you will ever need to know! And take home prelims!
No Comments

Not enough space here to describe how horribly unorganized this professor is. Its like they poured researched gathered online and put it on random powerpoint presentations that were full of errors and messy. No clarity or explanations on assignments, very dry course teaching, no interactive experience on such an importance study of a course. Awful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took a course with Prof. Mize at Oregon State University and the course organization was a disaster from day one, he gave almost no instructions on how to participate in the class discussion board, and then graded rather harshly. A majority of the class had their grades fall in week 3.  Doesn't answer emails on time or at all, do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He really knows what he is talking about. Though he is very distractable and goes off on tangents sometimes, he is always entertaining, and will get the class laughing at/with him at least once per class. The reading is heavy, and necessar. You can choose to make this a hard or easy course depending on how much real thought you put into it.

The best teacher I've had at CU. He made lectures interesting and engaging. I couldn't ask for a better lecturer. It's a bit reading intensive (~150pgs/wk) but worth it!!! Take his classes. He's even got a fanclub on facebook!

The class is so easy its embarassing. The prof, though, really shouldn't be at Cornell. I have little problem with a liberal bias but he has no basis for half of his conjectures it's really a disgrace. The textbook is so jaded it's indescribable. And he has no insights at all, just jabs at anything conservative. Class's easier than h. school though

He used statistics, history, & a few specific case studies to describe the communities, but never went deeper than that. No analysis, no insights, almost nothing about culture. Just when I thought it was going somewhere, he would move on to a different ethnic group. Bland, superficial, uninteresting. Not bad, just not good.
Excellent Professor! Great teaching style and definitely knows how to make the material interesting. LOVE HIM!
Very interesting professor.  Topics of discussion were extremely interesting.  He's a fair grader and more than willing to assist any student when in need.  Take his courses.

Covered a broad range of topics concerning an incredibly broad range of racial and ethnic groups. He assigns a lot of readings but it's all really interesting. He really challenges you to introduce new thoughts. Extremely fair grader. AMAZING professor. Take any one of his classes.

Aaron has devoted a number of years of his life to the subject matter he teaches. Having said this, he is very passionate and intuitive about his work. His sincere care about philosophy reflects a deep concern about human nature, and in a larger sense, the nature of nature. He is a wonderful instructor and I recommend taking his class.

Aaron's class really freaked me out at first. I think he hated my first couple papers. The trick is to really listen to what he says in class and take notes. He says lots of key stuff you can use in your paper. I think he likes that.
Aaron is a really professional instructor who really cares about philosophy... and it shows!  He may seem strict at first but he always gave really helpful comments on papers.

Prof. Ke seems like a competent researcher and overall nice guy, but he's a terrible teacher. Lectures are dense and boring. The course was directionless and disorganized. Exams were essentially test of memorization, which seems like a waste of time in a course level this high. I regret taking his class.

Gives way too much information in each lecture. Lectures are monotone and dry. He is inaccessible outside of class and exams are very difficult. No additional resources are given to understand the material and the objectives are not made clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class has the potential to be interesting. But Prof. Ke is often late to class and presents the material in a difficult and convoluted manner. The homeworks involve using PYMOL to analyze various RNA structures. His exams are very long and difficult, testing obscure details he talked about in vague terms. He does curve final grade though.
Class was about 1/2 grad students and 1/2 undergrads (with easier grading for undergrads).  All there is to know about RNA!

One of the most insightful, cool, and inspiring teachers I've ever had. Aisha went over the material in many different, interesting ways and made me very passionate about the subject. Probably the best class I've taken with the best prof.
She is a very nice and approachable teacher, always willing to reach out to students. She gave me a lot of good advice for my essays. She is not hard on grading. I did pretty well for this class.
Aisha is a brilliant writer and professor. She was inspiring and pushed her students to becoming so much better. Her class was enjoyable, interesting, and helpful.
She was helpful during office hours, and very nice, just a picky grader/wants things to be perfect.
Essays are impossible.  Had to rewrite papers three times and still got average grades.

Tests are unlike homework or any random stuff he will talk about during his lectures. I think he means well he just has no clue in the world how to prepare his students for a test, be ready for the hardest topics in each chapter, get a grip.
One of the worst professors of

Professor Edwards has a hard exterior but he really is a sweet man at his core. Go to his office hours; he will help you. He will make you "think," not just tell you the answer—he really does want you to grow as a learner. Protect this man at all costs.

For AEM5241- Edwards is one of the most impressive instructors you will encounter at Cornell. Incredibly knowledgeable, unparalleled experience, cares deeply about his students - it doesn't get much better than that. Not many top universities have former heads of their endowments taking the time out of their schedules to teach.
His lectures ain't helpful and very boring. Almost feels like he is wasting my time. Odd grading system and tests.
Boring moody professor, long dry lectures, and difficult tests that are different that the homework. Avoid.
Exams are very tough and are nothing like the homework. Lectures are very dry and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All I'm gonna say is "I'm not a gotchu guy"

Don't get me wrong Professor Edward's is a very caring professor and wants his students to do well. However, lectures are unfortunately very dry and long. Exams are worth 80% of your grade and are not similar at all to the homework and can be a bit harsh. I would recommend taking this course with another professor if available.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: not the most interesting lecturer, but he definitely made the topics made sense. you still have to put in a lot of work outside of class to do well

Easy to access outside of class during office hours. Class format is extremely test + hw based and lectures are a bit dry. Professor is super helpful, and if you do well on hw's you should be able to get a reasonable grade in the class. Exams are very similar to hw as far as question format, and the class is straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not only is Professor Ajunwa a great lecturer, she also cares about her students and is easy to connect with beyond class.

Went from live to online. Taken for ILR soph writing requirement. Prof is nice and pretty knowledgable about her topics. She struggles to communicate how to do assignments and when they are due but doesn't grade harshly. You may have to ask her multiple times. Not too much work and it isn't too difficult or tedious. I think participation matters.

Prof. Ajunwa has been my favorite professor at ILR to date. Shes a knowledge powerhouse and was terrific at teaching labor law in a way that would benefit non-lawyers. During the pandemic she was also very flexible with students, which is a true gem regardless. Dont miss a class with her if you can help it!

Professor Ajunwa is very smart and a great teacher. She knows a lot about law and technology, and many of the class readings were her own papers. She grades pretty lightly, and class discussions can be pretty interesting. Her one flaw is that she sometimes struggles to communicate assignment expectations and deadlines.
Standout professor at Cornell. Challenges students in a thought-provoking and respectful way, and does not take sides -- instead kindly pushes all ideas. Unique teaching message. Strongly recommend.

This was an excellent class. I truly enjoyed the class and found the material to be current. The prof. is extremely knowledgable in the subject matter. The couses leades to and to ann understanding ofthe changing nature of work as influenced both by technological advancements and changing attitudes about the role of work and work/life balance.

She is nice and willing to help students during and after the class. In the class, she will prompt you to think and discuss the real-life decision-making scenarios in a variety of ways. The reading materials, though heavy loading every week, also help a lot before in-class discussions. I am glad to have those articles and books finished.

She does a great job in leading really thought-provoking discussions and challenging our assumptions. I especially liked her efforts to help us apply business and legal concepts to real-world cases and her flexibility in adapting to the class's needs. She's a fair grader and gives clear feedback. Anyone who takes a class with her will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lowkey a goated prof, cares about students, explains concepts very well, passionate. Exams were all fair, basically no HW, u needed to just study yourself. Exams includes proofs, some were chill, some were harder.

*math 2930

Makes sure students understands the material and grading system reduces work on future exams. Explains concepts very clearly
YES THE BEST
great prof but I fumbled a bit too much on exams

One of the most wonderful and caring professors I've had at Cornell. His lecture slides were amazing for learning all of the content necessary. The class was very hard because of the lack of a curve and very proof-heavy exams, but completely doable if you put in the effort to do the problem sets.

Very cool lecturer, has GOAT potential imo, but for a class called "Linear Algebra for Engineers", he really expects you to learn the material as if you were an upcoming mathmatician in the 1600s. Extremely proof heavy, prelims containted T/F sections but also sections where you prove theorems you learned in class.
Very hard semester overall. The course was much harder than it was last semester from what I've heard. You do need to prepare and go to office hours.
The MATH 2940 curve was harsh on a lot of people this semester. The class was harder than it needed to be, and the curve didn't help anyone. Much harder than Lin Alg from previous semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Mosunov actively wants you to succeed. His lectures are great and the iclicker questions are actually really helpful for learning (shocking I know). The hw was easy altho there were optional problem sets that better prepared you for the exams and quizzes but they aren't necessary. Pay attention early and you will be rewarded.
Nice guy and cares about his students but made the class a million times more difficult than it had to be
THE BEST PROFESSOR TO EVER EXIST! Anton is such a mush and should be celebrated! TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM! Very good at lecturing!!!!
Prof mosunov is the gooooaaattt!!!!
he is the best! so wholesome and cares so much about his students. his lectures are fantastic and the notes are really easy to follow afterwards. i will actually miss bro
Anton is kind of the goat. Lectures are extremely detailed and basically hold your hand through learning new concepts, and his slides are like the best thing I've ever seen.
anton mosunov is the goat

Ana Howie is one of the best lecturers I've had during my time at Cornell. She's extremely articulated and her classes combine insightful attention to details but also connecting it to breather topics and themes. She welcomes a wide range of discussion and interpretations as long as its materially and historically grounded.

Prof. Howie is a good lecturer and very approachable. There are only a few graded elements in the class and she's a tough grader on papers, but she does use a UK grading scale so it's a little lenient in that respect. There's a lot of reading every night as well. Make sure to participate in class because it contributes to your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Best professor at Cornell. She guides you through each lecture using the most relevant artworks. Each class is a masterpiece -- a very entertaining history lesson that is incredibly well-organized and carefully planned. I feel so much more cultured after taking her class. On top of that, she's the most eloquently spoken person I've ever met.

Amazing lecturer - having never taken an Art history/art class before, I had so much fun taking this class, and it was extremely interesting. The lectures were great and I genuinely learned so much from this Prof.
Great professor and she uses UK grading scale (90+ will be an A+)

The best Art History classes I have taken! Ana provides valuable context and great insights along with super detailed visual analysis of each artwork discussed in lecture. I've learned so much and deepened my understanding of eight early modern European countries/states. We did two essays, no graded homework, but the tests were challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her class on Early Modern Art called Cosmopolitanism and Empire was a pleasure. She delivers an old school "survey" art history class while keeping us in touch with the material culture and global impact at every turn. Seriously, we learned so much and the course work was lighter than expected for ARTH with this knowledgeable, graceful lecturer!

Pretty awesome professor, gives great and comprehensive lectures. Homework can be long if you haven't done this before, but honestly pretty chill + easy if you have experience. Lots of room for your own direction, lots of fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lectures are amazing, as are the course notes. There are pop quizzes that count for credit, and they're often placed at kinda evil times (such as right after thanksgiving break this year). The homework is very hard, and takes more time than you'd expect. They teach a lot of content and they teach it very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very demanding and time-consuming assignments, but lectures were great, and the final project was extremely rewarding.
Explains things very clearly in lecture. Moves very fast, making it easy to get lost if you miss anything. But if you're paying attention, you learn a lot.

Prof Myers is the GOAT! Clearly, he knows a lot about Java and programming logic as a whole, however, some of it may be outdated (one time he mentioned a "recent" java release and it was from 2014 😭). Lectures go by fast but not so much so that the content is overwhelming. If you're stuck on anything, office hours should be your #1 resource.
amazon lecturer
Similar to Previous years, Compilers is just as difficult and rewarding as ever. Group wrote over 15k lines of code. Well worth the grind!

His lectures are okay and he is good at answering students' questions in an enlightening manner. Perhaps things would have been different in a smaller class format, but he was just middle of the road.

Prof. Myers is a great person for people who have had experience coding in java and with the concepts taught in the course. He is clearly not, however, meant to teach 2110. The only coding experience I had before the class was CS 1112, and this was a huge step up. Lecture pace was WAY too fast and course was pretty disorganized. Exams were fair-ish

Myers lectures at a level far too abstract for 2110, and doesn't seem to understand his audience. I did well because I came in with a lot of knowledge and taught myself everythign new. He also decided to rewrite many of the projects, and released with many bugs. I once spent hours finding bugs in my code only to find out the smoketester had a bug.

Very obvious he loves Java and is very knowledgeable. However, he teaches so quickly half the times I am just scrambling to get all of the notes down in lecture. He teaches quite a bit of honors material (even though this is 2110). Java syntax is not taught at all (unlike in 1110) so Java Hypertext and googling is your best friend for assignments.

Myers is definitely incredibly knowledgeable, but his lectures were fully useless. If you have a tough time learning on your own, a course with him is not wise, and I found participation being graded to be super annoying. You can get an A if you just read the notes thoroughly and do the assignments, which are well-designed.

Great lectures, interesting material. Assignments were updated somewhat unexpectedly, but it's understandable since the assignments this past semester were new. Could have given more study material, but notes were well-organized and assignments were fun. Very knowledgeable about the subject.
Poorly run class, Professor was not helpful even a little bit.
some rocky issues with assignments (last minute corrections to design that werent publicly announced), but overall great class. easy but fun assignments

I took this class in the fall of 2020. Professor Myers completely transformed the way I viewed computer science through this course. The assignments were very involved, but they also taught me so much about principles of software engineering and how to design large-scale systems. Myers is easily one of my favorite professors I've had here so far.

Prof Myers's lectures are engaging and entertaining and he manages to make incredibly difficult concepts understandable. His courses are difficult, but are transformative and absolutely worth it if you're ready to put in the work. Do not mistake salty reviews from students not ready to make an effort to be an accurate representation of Prof Myers.

This has been one of the worst run classes I've ever taken. The assignments are very difficult and he does not teach well. Office hours are always packed and you can sometimes not get help for hours. Whenever there is an error on the staff side of things the students are left to suffer the consequences (ex. Multiple OH canceled/ last minute changes
Worst class in the history of classes, DO NOT TAKE!!

cs2110 this semester has been horribly organized. for some reason helping the student out when harmed by an error on the administration's part is always the LAST option, rarely taken. I've basically been told 'Oops! Deal with it' a dozen times when I'm the victim of admin error. lectures too fast. class is also much harder than previous iterations.
Just not a good experience in his class
Thanks for making CS 2110 like hell. I'm retaking in next semester.

Wow, what a wonderful guy. I mean, he's contributed more to Security and PL research than anyone else currently alive, and continues to have the time to welcome anyone and everyone interested into the PL community. Before taking 2112, I was going to study ML. Now I've seen the light (Professor Myers's light) and I'm going to study PL. Thank you

I came to this by chance since I saw some post about Andrew Myers and thought to myself, "that name is familiar". I took this course close a decade ago and he was a great professor.I was a senior taking this class for additional context. What added to the course was the small size instruction, which I hope is still the case
Tests are impossibly difficult and completely irrelevant with teaching materials. make simple ideas impossibly difficult. it's a joke.

Myers is very knowledgeable and you can really tell that he cares about his students through the way he carries himself in lecture. It's crazy how much work is in the assignments (200 hours total for me), but the online course notes and TA office hours are a god send. I've never learned this much from a professor and a class before.

Myers is the best prof I've ever seen. His lecture is always inspiring, and he genuinely cares for his students. TAs, classmates, and just the spirit of the class is amazing. It is a VERY heavy workload class (like a solid 10 hours per week just on coding projects on average), but it will be fun if you love programming.
Probably the best professor and class ive taken at Cornell. Also the hardest class Ive taken, but the amount you learn is well worth it. The compiler project is no joke and extremely fuffiling.

Prof. Myers' courses are extremely difficult, but his lectures are excellent and you will never learn more in such a short time as in his class. He is also friendly in Office hours, if you have any questions about the course. Take his class if you want to be challenged like never before.

He put in a special effort in remembering everyone's name, and that's really something. Extremely organized lectures. Exams were fair. Projects were hard (120 hours of coding for the whole semester). Lots of fun.

Professor Myers is knowledgeable and his lectures are amazing. He might get a bad rep because his classes are hard, but hes extremely helpful and is always willing to answer your questions either after class or during office hours. And if you cant make it to his office hours, he has a website where you can book an appointment with him.
Really hard but one of the best teachers I've ever had.

I love the guy so much. He's a genius.  Don't mix up the courses with the teacher. Let's separate the two:  Professor Myers is: Well spoken, focuses on big picture, focuses on good programming, understands everything. Nice.  The classes he teaches are: honors/heavy duty CS courses at Cornell University. HW is 10+ a week. Lube is advised.
2112 is plenty of work, but well worth it if you love CS.
Good teacher. Explains well and helpful if you ask for clarification. Assignments are long but the grading is quite generous.

Lectures were always very clear and interesting and were a good learning experience. Taking the honors course resulted in a hefty load with seemingly unreasonable projects and deadlines. In the end was worth it. Prof. Myers was always very helpful when we had questions as was the rest of the course staff. Take this course if you want a challenge!!

This class is simply way too hard.  Problem sets in this class are longer and more tedious than comparable 300 level computer science classes, and the TA's grade them in the most anal retentive unforgiving manner possible.  Myers is a pretty good lecturer, but don't let him organize the assignments.
Nice guy, tries to explain things. Projects are WAY too long!!!!!!

Don't take his course if you want an easy ride! His classes are tougher than almost anything else you'll spot in college. And yet, if you need help, he's always there to help. Plus, if you survive the course load, I got more out of his courses than any other class.
If you like to stay up nights and programming for over 30 hours at a time, have fun with this class.  personally i think he's on the crazy side of cs.
Above average teacher but not amazing.  He hates C with a passion so do not get into an argument about programming languages with him.

Likes to focus more on the logistics (comments, specifications, etc) of programming rather than the actual code itself.  Has very long complicated projects.  Class concepts are obtuse and difficult to understand.
Amazing professor, very caring. Her lectures make difficult concepts much more intuitive and understandable.
It is very tough to feel positively about her. She makes up convention on-the-go and confuses me more than helps. I learnt best when I skipped lecture and read on my own.
Spams Work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very disorganized
Disorganized and unprofessional. Did not take care enough about her students.
Not very organized, teaching style was not good
Taking online online classes with this prof explains everything very well

CS 1110 was organized well—as someone who has not used a single computer program before. That being said, the assignments were sometimes a pain and some exam questions were really difficult. I took this for a distribution requirement, and while I really liked the coding, I would not go back. Remove the (HANDWRITTEN) exams and I'm on board.

Anne Bracy is definitely one of the better professors in Cornell CS (which isn't saying much, but I digress). She is a great lecturer, yet still has a strong non-teaching background. I liked how she handled 1110, but she made the labs too inconsistent in workload and made the prelims far longer than was realistic, leading many to not finish.

reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great, encouraging professor with clear, easy-to-follow lectures. Holds helpful office hours and review sessions. Projects in the class are a great balance of challenging and engaging. Learned a ton in the class and would recommend to anyone who is trying to get into CS!

Anne Bracy is one of the best professors I have at Cornell. I came into this class not knowing anything about CS, and I walked out of this class with an A. The materials were very interesting to me, and I enjoy them substantially.
I loved Professor Bracy- she is truly a great lecturer and has a very impressive professional background. She made me want to major in CS!
Good lectures, very accessible and caring about students. Difficult class with a lot of workload but Bracy does a good job at navigating the course.
Crazy analogies. Intense workload. Interesting content. Compassionate professor. Can't ask for much more.
Amazing professor! Very kind and inclusive. Lectures always very well organized and prepared. Engaging lectures.

CS 3410 is no joke. The projects are challenging and ridiculously time-consuming. I think Professor Bracy makes the course fair and is a great lecturer and professor. My only criticism is the exams in the course are much more difficult than they should be and are frankly really hard to study for.

Wonderful lecturer! CS3410 is a challenging and difficult class, but Prof. Bracy's lectures makes it bearable with her jokes and funny/good examples and comparisons. She is also super accessible outside of class, and is supportive of students with disabilities. I think anyone who says otherwise has to reflect on their (internalized) misogyny.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class
Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bracy is great at what she does, lectures are very content-heavy but always worth going to. Do NOT procrastinate projects or you will come to regret it, office hours are available all week and very helpful. She gives lots of relevant practice materials for exams and although the tests can have hard questions, they are all graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: (Note that she gave a textbook but literally no one used it) Very clear lectures, assignments are pretty straightforward, tests are fine if you study well. The class, in my opinion, is not meant to be a class to take "for fun." It's pretty time consuming, and Bracy expects a lot, but she made a significant effort to ensure students are prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class, feel like I learned the fundamentals well. Lectures are not the most helpful, but the labs and assignments are great to learn.

This is more of a review of CS 1110 than of Prof Bracy, but I have zero prior coding experience and learned a lot and liked the course without being too stressed by assignments or exams. Class is heavily weighted and a few exams had very low unweighted averages (60%-70% range usually), so it's usually possible to recover from a bad test/assignment

Great class and great professor! The material could be challenging at times but she explained things amazingly clearly and often worked in fun examples to keep it engaging. The class does have a fair bit of work, specifically time consuming projects. Luckily projects are very interesting and there are lots of office hours.
Spring cs1110 is much easier than fall cs1110. Bracy didn't really impact me during the class, but I thought she was fine.

I don't have any experience with her in other classes, but in CS1110 she was great! Not perfect, but I certainly felt it necessary to attend lectures just because of how fluent she was in explaining the core concepts. The class itself was very difficult, but I think she certainly alleviated that a great deal.
A professor that forces financial hurdle on students by requiring physical iClicker.

I was a repeat cs1110 student this spring (took walker white last fall). Bracy and Lee are a great combo for teaching and I found the assignments more interesting than in the fall, and therefore I was more engaged and completed the course successfully. If possible I would wait until the spring to take this course. I feel more confident in cs now.

3410 is a tough class because material is new to most people and there's A LOT of work, even if it's mostly just busy work. Concepts usually build on top of one another so you do not want to fall behind. Class will seem overwhelming at first but gets better. Felt that Bracy makes the class doable contrary to what others might say. She's also funny

Fantastic lecturer! Makes CS clear to all, whether you are a first time learner or more experienced. Professor Lee writes tests and assignments, but Bracys lectures are super helpful for these. Would highly recommend taking!

Prof. Bracy was awesome, and I was pleasantly surprised by the way she taught CS. This class is definitely not easy, and requires a lot of effort, but if you put in the time and effort you will learn so much. Bracy was very nice, helpful, and accessible. The tests are hard but curved, the course is quick but help is given to people struggling.

Professor Bracy held all lectures for this class and ensured that all concepts were easily explained in class. While, many of the topics were extremely difficult to a first time programmer, it was clear that all topics were learned in a professional manner with clear examples that were performed in class.

Clear lecturer who's very passionate about the subject, and makes many references to Wegmans during the lectures. Went through numerous examples during class when covering more complex topics like caches, and reduced the difficulty of the assignments to accomodate for a hybrid class format. Had a reasonable slip day policy for project submissions.

Professor Bracy's class was so incredibly difficult for the sole purpose of being difficult. Lectures move so incredibly fast, projects have virtually no guidance and are difficult, and exams are not super related to projects and are still hard. I did more work for this class than any of my others classes and was miserable for each second of it.
Bracy is an excellent lecturer and really cares about her students. That doesn't mean the assignments and prelims aren't insanely hard...
Terrible person. I was hospitalized for a week and she forced me to use all of my slip days instead of just granting an extension like a human with empathy.

Bracy is a great teacher and clearly knows her subject. Her lectures are well-designed with clear language and she drops hilarious lines from time to time. This class covered a lot of highly technical details and sub-regions of CS, and not attending the lectures would make it hard to understand the slides. That said, the textbook is comprehensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really I wish I could give her 0 star. Just dropped the course, and do not understand where those good comments come from.
Not intelligent in teaching at all. Confusing lectures, baffled homework... I hope someone could let her know how awful her lectures are. By the way, she is rather mean and arrogant in the same time.

I love Bracy! She's a great professor and her lectures are done in a way that is easy to understand and accessible. Assignments are always geared towards what we have already learned; if you can do the assignments, the tests should not be too difficult. There are clicker questions to log attendance, but they're only 5% of your grade.
One of the worst classes I have taken.
Unintelligible class.

Bracy is a god among men. Never have I seen such a professor so passionate about both the material and her students. She gets so excited teaching and talking with students that it makes lectures my favorite time of the week. Yes, the class is difficult and condensed, but if you pay attention in lecture, the class is very manageable. SHE IS AMAZING!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Bracy is a talented and funny lecturer. Her lectures explain material extremely well while also being fairly concise. CS 3410's projects were hard (10-20 hours per project) and its exams harder, with means around a 55/90. I would highly recommend taking her classes she teaches.

Bracy is an amazing lecturer and made this class (which could have been terrible) pretty enjoyable and interesting. I really loved her classes and thought the assignments were pretty standard for a CS core class. Also, she's awesome to talk to outside of class and genuinely cares about her students. 10/10 would recommend!

Bracy is so great that I'm taking CS 2110 with her next semester. I loved her teaching style because I am a very visual learner (she's won teaching awards). She inspires great questions from her students in lecture, and the lecture material clearly laid out what was expected on exams. Beware of the tricky assignments and make use of office hours.

Her lectures were usually pretty good, but sometimes slightly disorganized. She's super nice though and has plenty of office hours! Apparently her assignments were a lot harder than the fall CS 1110 professor's, but they were doable.

Bracy is by far the best professor I've had at Cornell! She is passionate about CS and her lectures are clear and enormously helpful. The assignments were quite difficult at times but prepared you greatly for the prelims and final. I came in with zero coding experience and learned so much in a semester. Challenging but immensely rewarding class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. Her lecture style was clear, and I the examples made tough concepts easy to learn. Her expectations were clear and it was easy to gage how I was doing in the class. Not an overbearing amount of work, and makes CS really fun to learn. Also, she is just an awesome human.
I really loved cs3410 with her :) I maybe only scraped past tests, but it was worth it for the interesting lecture and great content.

Best undergrad professor I've had. She turned systems from a hated subject of mine into my graduate focus. Negative comments below are reactions to unconventional teaching. Lectures focus on concepts, exams are difficult but test your grasp of concepts in terms of big picture. Not a cookie-cutter professor/lecturer - what makes her great.

Great Professor. The lectures are very clear. Attend the classes since It takes more time to figure out the lecture note than just attending the class. Not sure why are there so many very negatives comments. I took 4410 in the Fall semester. The lectures are a bit slow and repetitive and the projects are pretty difficult. But t's fine overall.
Super difficult class, but the best proffessor I've had at cornell
Awesome teaching with low scores. Think thoroughly before you enroll!!

Fun lectures that fly over topics at the speed of light. Be sure to read up before lecture begins (there's HW before every lecture to help with that) and take notes like a good student. Tests are difficult and annoying as they often test a concept that you know well but contorted so that no one knows how to answer. Still, great, fun person.

The class is harder than it has to be. Concepts in lecture are briefly touched upon, with the majority of content being self-taught. Lectures and projects have little overlap, and tests are hard to predict. Bracy is good at teaching in lecture, but little of what she teaches is actually useful for the tests and projects.

Overall, I wish there was more thought put into the course. Projects were not well planned, had too much time to complete, but little support. Having weekly problem sets would have helped students know what to focus on. Many difficult topics on the exams were covered in the book, but glossed on in lecture. Had to self-study to do well on exams.

Little to no TAs use the piazza, and some of the answers are rather rude. Tests have means in the 50s and are unrelated to anything learned. Lectures have minimal overlap with projects, and the projects are very hazily laid out. For one project, we were told to simply google any questions. It's a shame this course is mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very tough test, so many assignments that do not match it's credits. unclear lecture notes, skip the class? you will not clear about what leature notes talking about. besides operating system, the course also contains computer network and security. if you have choices, never choose it! it does not worth in any way!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Take 3420. This is the worst course I ever took in Cornell.
Take 3420
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I took ece 2300 with David Albonesi(whose notes are ece bible) and cs 3410 with Bracy. The lecture note is unclear, messy and full of small errors. The lecture is  also unclear, messy and full of small erros. Bracy  loves using analogy to make the material less bland, but  3410 material is something that requires accurate and technical language!!

Never take 4410 with her. She clearly knows 3410 well, but completely messed up 4410 to the point of making (the very new) Prof. Agarwal look bad. She is mean and extremely useless in her office hours. She even co-organized the office hours for the two courses she was teaching that fall. Messed up the entire course and worst part were her lectures.
Go to office hours. Nothing in lecture can even compare to the evils of Logisim and malloc.

I don't know whether my negative experience with prof bracy owes itself more to the overbearing nature of the class (and I mean this class approaches levels of work akin to 19th century industrial revolution standards of labor), or to her stone cold, stoic conveyance of the material. Bracy was relentless and didn't even try to help make it palatabl
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Bracy is a great lecturer whose skill was sadly undermined by the incompetence of her co-professor.  I had her for both CS 3410 and this class, and I would say without a doubt that Prof. Bracy will go out of her way to help anyone who needs it, and is capable of much more than she was able to demonstrate in CS 4410 when I took it.

Bracy is unorganized, uncaring, and mean. Unwilling to help students and a very boring lecturer. In several instances, she would release grades for assignments 2 months after they were due. Her class organization is poor, has no accountability, and is not a good nor fair lecturer.

Despite Prof. Agarwal's messing up of the entire class, she was actually a good lecturer and you can tell from piazza and office hours that she actually cares and wants students to learn and succeed. She was organized and clear. 10/10 would recommend

I really like Anne as a lecturer but this class was just awful. 3410 was good but 4410 was by far the worst class I've taken at Cornell. I'm not a big fan of the material to begin with and the fact that this class was a logistical nightmare did not alleviate that issue. I really hope they get it together.
One of the best professor at cornell! Homeworks can be a little disorganized but her lectures are always interesting, informative, and entertaining.

Professor Bracy is one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. I took a class with her, and also was a TA for another class that she taught. Her classes definitely aren't easy, but she really cares about giving her students the best possible experiences and does everything that she can to help them succeed. Would definitely recommend her.
Nope
CS 3410 is a mandatory CS class and Bracy made it as painless as possible. As long as you make use of all the resources, you should be fine.

As Anne Bracy describes it, CS 3410 is like "trying to drink from two firehoses." This class is a TON of work, and the concepts are very hard. However, Bracy teaches them really well. She knows her stuff, and can answer any question you throw at her. This class will be near impossible, but Bracy and the TA army will help you out.

Wow, Bracy yourself for 3410 cause it's the bomb dot com. While the projects/ homework aren't too hard, they are time consuming. The 3410 TA army and Bracy is there for you though, so you are in good hands.

Professor Campana is maybe the best professor I've taken a class with here. He's a wonderful lecturer who's extremely passionate and knowledgable about the subject, and always makes really interesting points which challenge your thinking. His grading policy is very fair and not overwhelming, and he's kind to students and always willing to listen.

easily the kindest and most understanding professor i had this semester. professor campana doesn't cold call on students, so it's sometimes upsetting because it seems like no one cares. my only regret is not putting in more effort into the class. would definitely take another one of his courses just to have him as a professor again.

Easily one of the kindest and most genuine professors I've known at Cornell. When I needed an extension, he never said no. His courses were well organized, and his lectures were always a joy to attend. I think he legitimately loves what he does and wants to share it with his students. Often went to his office hours just to chat, which was fun.

You get what you put in with Professor Campana's classes, but the content he goes over in class is so interesting it's hard not to be invested. Great lectures, great organization of course content, would highly recommend if you are interested in hearing about games and animation as a reflection of japanese popular culture!
hard but rewarding. my favorite professor at Cornell University
Prof. was pretty good

One of the lowest grades I received in an ECE course at Cornell yet I felt like I learned so much more in this class then any other. Professor Molnar is truly a genius. His homecooked homework problems are very difficult, and the labs are harshly grades, but if you apply yourself through and don't worry about your grade here you will learn so much.

Took 4450, 5540, and 5790 with Molnar. Hardest classes I took at Cornell, especially 5540, but learned more from them than pretty much everything else combined. Amazing lectures, you walk away from his classes with an understanding and not just a knowledge of the material. Best Prof. in ECE in my opinion. There is no learning without pain!!!
Super hard but worth it

Amazing lectures, lots of problem sets and labs, but ultimately worth it. He and the TAs put a lot of time into the course to ensure a full understanding of analog circuits. Also really interesting uy to talk to outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Expect lots of work and a lot of learning! Go to office hours and become friends with him! He puts in a lot of effort.

Despite the overwhelming amount of work we were assigned, most of it was not worth much. It was a very leniently graded class and the professors and TAs spent well more than the required amount of time to ensure a high level of understanding.
Challenging but very dedicated to his course.  Excellent selection of TAs.  Attends every discussion and some labs to help out.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He really cares about his students/teaching, is very understanding, and is always willing to help. However, this was also the hardest class I have taken (prelims were pretty rough, labs and homework sets were long/difficult). This class will teach you to care more about learning than your grade

Professor Molnar is a fantastic guy. He's an absolute genius, super nice, and always willing to help his students. You will learn so much if you take ECE 2100 and try your hardest to understand the material being thrown at you. That being said, do not expect this class to be a breeze. Homework sets take forever and labs are tedious. Come prepared.

Prof. Molnar's 2100 will consume your life with coursework if you let it. Overall, it was very educational and worthwhile. And he's a really nice guy. Many students suspect he has (not so) secret superhuman ECE powers.

Prof. Molnar is many things, easy is not one of them. His problem sets/labs are positively sadistic, but he holds himself to the same high standards he holds you to. He is incredibly dedicated (teaches his own discussions, writes own labs) and is super-helpful when you talk to him in person. Overall, a great guy/teacher who will teach you  a ton.
A nice and interesting guy. Seems to care about his students and is willing to help them when they ask for help. Lectures are very good, but problem sets are difficult.
talks extremely fast, ridiculously long and hard problem sets

Her studio is extremely demanding. I often feel that my previous understanding of design is utterly shattered by her, and yes, those moments are frustrating. But I couldn't be more grateful for her pushing me out of my comfort zone and challenging me to be a better thinker and designer. If you're ever lucky enough to take her class, take it.
Genuinely doesn't know how to teach architecture at all
makes students miserable

Simitch is the most vitriolic personality I have ever witnessed. She is generally disrespectful, mean, and full of herself. Takes pride in making people feel small. Narcissistic. Bitter. Some people like it. Do not allow her to take the joy out of architecture because if she can, she will.
Was generally terrible to her students, had a sort of mothering tendency, but not in a good way.

For what Andrea Simitch lacks in intellectual capacity, she compensates through the intimidation of her students and a suffocating and often necessary workload. Simitch puts each student in a box and has great difficulty learning new technology - "do you still use Zip-A-Tone?" It is no wonder that she drove her competition studio into the ground.

Amazing! One of the best professors I've had at Cornell. Tough, critical, to the point - Andrea will not beat around the bush, but also won't let students bullsh*t their way through presentations. Highly recommended. Although she has a reputation for being scary, she is just very blunt and opinionated. She is however, very open to student's ideas.

Best Cornell Arch professor I had. Definitely tough, but architecture school HAS to toughen you up. She had a clear agenda of what to teach even if some people don't realize it. She makes a difference in the Cornell education.

Great professor for undergraduate students. HORRIBLE professor for graduate architecture students. Teaches grad students like kids with no architectural foundation. Could not connect with the studio. In short, take if you're an undergrad, DO NOT take if you're a grad student, unless you enjoy rolling your eyes for 4 hours three times a week.
Great, super intense. Tough love.
Andrea is amazing.  She has inspired me.  She is tough but I have the utmost respect for her and all she did for me.

Thought I was having the worst semester of my life with andrea until it was over and I realized I learned more about architecture and myself as a designer than any of the other professors combined. She is almost impossibly demanding, but it works out for the better.

Andrea was always unprofessional in class and a classic bipolar personality.  Sometimes happy, most of the "intimidation part of the fun of teaching".  This is a direct quote from her with witnesses. she played favorites for to the popular, attractive students and ignored the rest.  Her crits were funny, because she would just repeat what Val said.
Very poor communication skills. And enjoys to uselessly intimidate students.

By far the best professor I've ever had. I am now a professor myself and often reach back to my experience in Prof. Simitch's class for reference. I'm happy when my students call me 'tough'. Makes me feel like I'm living up to good standards.
worst class I have taken in my entire life. I feel like I am worse for taking it. teacher is negative and does not exhibit skill in this area.
Professor Simitch is tough, but very good. in reviews, she provides very good constructive criticism. her advice is direct, which can be hard and frustrating at times but often very helpful.

Amazng professor, you will learn so much. Very critical, very sharp, frequently sees right to the crux of your project with no problems. Expects huge amounts of work-- won't settle for less. Also fairly sympathetic for an arch professor, will make projects due before break to pace you.
graduated several years ago and now licensed despite doing horribly in her class. Still the worst professor I have ever had. jaded and self-absorbed.

DO NOT TAKE HER. She just have no idea about architecture, therefore she just cant get what you are up to and she turns it back to you. She would tell you to do stuff that don’t make any sense for your project because she don’t know what else she can tell you. Just avoid her.
No Comments
greatest teacher ever, you learn so much.
AVOID AT ALL COSTS!! Incredibly disrespectful to students.  Talks down to everyone.  Thinks she is the queen of the world.  If you have any self respect do NOT take classes with her.
Really amazing teacher. One of the best I've had. You have to put in some work but really not that bad. Def recommend taking this class with Professor McAdams.

Really a great class. The professor is great and she really cares. She will introduce you to amazing new music shows movies and podcasts in Spanish. The class really improves ur Spanish with lots of speaking exercises as well as a lot of immersion with Spanish media.

I absolutely loved having Professor McAdams as a teacher! Class didn't feel like a chore, and I definitely improved my Spanish skills though the course. Her lectures were very easy to understand and in class activities were fun, engaging, and helpful. She is very kind and clearly cares about all of her students and their success in the class.

Lecturer McAdams graded harshly regarding participation and often gave unclear instructions for exams and expected attendance during office hours to understand oftentimes necessary elements. She was very rude when interacting with various students which soured the learning experience. In the future, I hope she practices more empathy.

while her class can be stressful at times (cold calling! presentations!), she does her best to make the class chill and challenge her students to become better speakers and writers. however, if you don't do your work, you will not have a fun time. 

(1230 w/ her also involves a lot of spanish music, so you can pad your spotify playlists with this.)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor McAdams is very disrespectful and discouraging to students. She answers all questions in a snarky manner, states that any question that she does not want to answer is "stupid", and she insults students if they don't immediately understand a concept. She will destroy your interest in studying Spanish.

Dr. Esposito, or Alex as he prefers to be called is genuinely one of the best Professors I've taken in my college career. Doing research in his class was great and he is always down to talk about your work or just chat about what's going on in your life. If you get the opportunity take his class.
Professor Big Purr is very good at illegal screens
Super chill, had applied ethics FWS!
Applied Ethics FWS Fall 22. Amazing course with great in class discussions, a great, flexible, and chill guy.

Stay away from this professor and this class, offered as an intensive 4-credit history seminar over summer/winter sessions. Workload is impossible for this short time. Class is listed as virtual, but you will have exceptionally strict deadlines every single day, including weekends, with no forgiveness. Grading is fierce; supremely nitpicky. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Alano is an excellent instructor who really teaches you how to write historical analysis. I had never taken a history class before, so this was definitely a bit tough for me, but with her feedback I was able to improve drastically throughout the course of the class. The class requires a lot of reading and writing, but the work is worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Excellent prof! She is really responsive and helpful. You get plenty of time to do the assignments and essays with ample support

Professor Heinemann's course was excellent. What a warm person.

The workload's daunting, but she'd been forthcoming about expectations and afforded students endless opportunities to access help or supplemental materials. And notwithstanding this course occupying more time than all my others combined, Heinemann clears all other ILR professors.

If you want to learn about disability studies would definitely recommend her. Overall, it is a lot of work but she gives great feedback and really helps you become a better writer. Only graded on participation and a 25-page essay with checkpoints along the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I love this professor. She is perfect. I am not gonna lie: This class is a lot of work. I got a great grade, but these assignments take hours and hours. There are three big assignments all writing-based. But her feedback is amazing. She makes you improve so much in writing. She is so kind and helpful, answers all questions, and is very accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If Professor Heinemann has a million fans, then I am one of them. If Professor Heinemann has ten fans, then I am one of them. If Professor Heinemann has only one fan, then that is me. If Professor Heinemann has no fans, then that means I am no longer on earth. If the world is against Professor Heinemann, then I am against the world.

Professor Weiner Heinemann is the best professor I have had at Cornell. She is incredibly knowledgeable about disability studies, is very accommodating, and makes her students better at research and writing. While the length of the final paper may seem daunting, she breaks it up very well and is there for you every step of the way.

Professor Heinemann is honestly one of the best people (let alone professors) I've gotten to interact with at Cornell. She is such a knowledgeable, caring person, and the class is super interesting and relevant! Super sweet and VERY helpful, so even though the course papers are not easy she makes them A LOT more manageable.

Professor Weiner Heinemann is one of the most flexible, understanding, and caring teachers I've ever had. She truly cares about the subject and her engaging teaching style makes students care as well. I've learned so much  in her class, and my writing skills have improved so much.

Professor Weiner Heinemann is the kindest professor I have ever had the pleasure of having. She is understanding of student struggles and helps to find the best solutions for any issues students may have. She is knowledgeable in the subject and is a fantastic lecturer. I would jump on the opportunity to take a class with her again in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing class and professor! There are weekly reflection papers, a take-home exam, and a major group project (Covid-19 breakdown). One of the best professors I have had at Cornell. Really cares about her students and will give more feedback on your papers than you write. Take a class with her!!

Professor Weiner Heinemann was one of the most influential professors I had during college, and I still think about her class and her teaching even though I've already graduated. The class was informative and relevant to current events, and discussions were impactful. I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Weiner Heinemann.
Incredibly caring and helpful professor. One of the best classes I have taken at ILR. I learned so much about disability studies and my writing improved a ton. Definitely take her writing seminar!

Her disability law writing seminar only has two papers. She will provide line by line feedback from your draft on both papers, and you are required to meet with her at least once for each paper. Seems like a tough grader but grades are forgiving in the end.

I can say unequivocally say that Professor Heinemann is the best professor I have ever had. Her lectures are always so interesting and helpful in understanding disability studies. I specifically took her Writing Seminar in Law class about disability studies which was wonderful. She gives a lot of feedback on rough drafts, it's great!

Professor Weiner is absolutely incredible. Her class is hard, but the work is meaningful and useful. She provides extremely helpful feedback - line by line feedback in the writing seminar. There is no textbook, just readings from articles. However, there is still a decent amount of reading. Also learned sm about disability studies. Take her class!

Professor Weiner is an absolute gem of a human. She is so kind and really cares about improving her students writing abilities. She gives really detailed feedback on each draft of your essay. I highly recommend taking a writing seminar with her.

Professor Weiner is by far the best professor I have ever had at Cornell and in ILR. I loved this class and am trying to take another one of her classes again. My writing improved so much because of all of her detailed feedback.

Incredible, tremendously thoughtful and helpful professor. I grew as a writer and a thinker from this class. I have never encountered anyone so invested in the students. I will admit the material was difficult, but she is always willing to help. It was a delight to take a class with Professor Weiner Heinemann and I highly recommend it.
Amazing professor. She truly cares about your growth as a writer and a thinker. Best professor I've had at ILR.

Although the class is long (2.5hrs), the lectures were always interesting. There were 3 reading quizzes (only 2 counted), a midterm & final. Otherwise, u write a quick 5 sentence reflection at the end of each class. Grading is clear cut and class is reasonably easy. There is a lot of readings (go to office hours and she will give you tools to help)

Professor Weiner Heinemann is easily one of the best professors at ILR. While her course is definitely not the easiest way to fulfill the sophomore writing requirement, it is definitely among the ones that will teach you the most. She will challenge you and you will leave her classroom a better writer. Needless to say, her grading is also very fair

This professor is one of the best I have had while in the ILR school at Cornell University! Though her paper assignments are difficult, she is extremely helpful and will go out of her way to assist you. My writing has improved exponentially and I am so glad I took this class.

Hands down one of the best professors that I have had at Cornell. She’s brilliant, funny, approachable, and (genuinely) interested in her students. She is always willing to go above and beyond to make sure that you understand the material.

Professor Weiner is an exceptional instructor. My writing skills improved dramatically from taking her writing seminar. She expects A LOT of work, but is very willing to offer help if you ask for it.I would recommend her class, but am willing to admit that it was not an easy way to fulfill the advanced writing requirement.

Professor Weiner is a brilliant person who cares deeply for her students. She gives extremely clear lectures and is willing to provide all the help you may need to do well in her class. If you have the chance to take a class with her, definitely do it.

Dr. Frith is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about nutrition and her students. NS2060 is a great and low-stakes class. I really feel like I bonded with my GPHS cohort. I'm not sure that it was super helpful in finding my ELO, but I enjoyed this class and it's an easy A+. Your grade is just attendance, reflections, and a group project.

Dr. Green was one of my chillest professors this semester. The class within itself it's a chill class aimed for an easy A, so as long as you show up, participate, and work hard on the group projects and critical reflections your fine. She wants you to succeed, and its low stress in my opinion.

She is very nice and understanding and clearly cares about her work. The class was slightly unorganized but the workload was low and it was easy (mostly focused on career exploration and exploring global health to prepare for ELO). Not super useful but I enjoyed it.

This is the worst class I have taken at Cornell. The professor doesn't care about her students, the feedback on assignments is unhelpful, the class is completely unorganized, and the content is pointless. When talking to her one-on-one, her tone is very condescending. This class is a requirement for the Global Health major/minor, so beware...

Great professor, really cares about his students and improving their writing. He's very passionate about semiotics but the topic can be difficult to understand. this class is less about understanding the topic and more about effectively writing. His critics are always helpful and he's truly made me a better writer.

Ti is an awesome professor who is flexible, caring, and fun. He meets students where they are, and is more than willing to help if you fall behind. Took ROMS 3210, History of Romance Language. He focused on us learning the material over simply getting the grade. You will do well in his course if you are present in lecture and doing your best work.
Such a sweet man- one of the most interesting classes I've taken at Cornell. The recorded speaking homework definitely piles up and was hard to find time to do in a quiet area, but great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ti is really kind and caring. He will treat you well if you put in any amount of effort. He is also really smart and an interesting teacher but I found his course was hampered by a lack of participation and interest. I'm not sure how much of this was in his control, but perhaps he could have more strongly enforced attendance/participation.
He is very considerate and accommodating. He is very enthusiastic about what he teaches and takes care to integrate a variety of interesting activities.
Had him for FWS Fall 2021, Ti was an amazing professor. Very understanding of deadlines and gives good feedback. Discussions in class were interesting, as well.

The professor is amazing and makes the topic easy to understand. He's understanding about deadlines, which is helpful towards the end of the semester. If you ask him for feedback on a topic or on your writing, he will definitely help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Ti was an amazing professor. He wants his students to succeed and is a genuinely nice guy. Highly recommend!!
extremely unclear about grading but gives u rly good feedback as long as u seek it. classes are discussion-based and u rly don't need to have read the book to contribute
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor and fun classes
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Just horrible... Ti has constant mood swings an is very unclear about everything.  He never seemed to know what was going on, and exams were handed back weeks late.  Ti tried to act like he was a chill guy, yet every single one of us were having panic attacks by the end of the semester (let's just say our class did not give him good course evals)
Pretty easy class. When you didn't hand in homework he would give you another opportunity to give it in, even if it was a week or two late.
Excellent professor! Great personality and makes the class comfortable. He is truly concerned with our academic success and interests.

Ti is entirely responsible for my sudden, powerful interest in French. So much that I think I might major in it now. He's sincerely enthusiastic about the material, and understandably so, because it's interesting.
Great teacher, still talk with him years after having taken his course.

Ti is great whether you're interested in italian or just trying to get rid of a requirement. His classes are fun and he'll meet with you any time to cover a lecture (even if you just skipped) He's really knowledgable, but not very tough about sticking to the syllabus. Feel free to ask questions. If you do any work you'll do well

Ti is simply amazing. He is extremely helpful and easy to get along with. I learned an incredible amount from him. The only--and I mean ONLY--frustration I had with this course was in the use of the Language Lab, which could be tedious or frustrating due to software problems.
Very enthusiastic (sometimes maybe even overly enthusiastic).  Understanding about deadlines and confusion; very responsive to student needs.  Can be boring and redundant--it was a slow class.

Ti is a very casual, nice guy.  He is VERY knowledgeable of the material (would spend several minutes of section talking about Italian culture), and, other than some very subtle frustration, he seems like he really cares about students learning.

The only reason students love Ti is because he tries so hard to be liked by them. Ti is your teacher if you are just trying to pass the language requirements cause he'll let you pass even if you do nothing.  He likes hanging out with the students who are brownosers.  He's a nice guy but not a very good teacher.  Plus, he has major mood swings.

Excellent, excellent professor.  Goes out of his way to make sure you learn.  Very interested in students who are interested.  Hilarious, easy going, a great guy.  Very understanding with deadlines and all.
ti's awesome, you're lucky if you're in his class.

Ti is so cool. He is an awesome, really easy going prof. A very fair grader if you are interested and do the work. Also very approachable and eager to make a difference for his students experience w/ foreign language
No Comments

TERRIBLE! SOCIAL ENGINEERING CLASS! Newman feels Any challenges, failures, or misery non-white people face in life is not their fault. And, even worse, there is nothing they can do to change their circumstances. So, just stew in your bitterness and hatred for White males along with her and her like, so goes the leftist campus orthodoxy of the day!!

Prof. Newman is calm and talks slowly. Sometimes she was not able to control the class. As each class of Cornell University worth a ticket of a Broadway show, Prof. Newman's classes obviously do not worth that price. For instance, she asked students to do mock interview one by one for 3 consecutive classes while she did not give much useful feedba
She is nice and helpful, especially when you actively seek her help.
Tough grader. Very friendly.
Prof Newman is one of the best Man Comm teachers. She's about as interesting as you can get for this course, and truly a very nice person.

Man Comm is Man Comm and she is better than snow. I thought she was pretty good for Man comm, she is a good mix between Snow and Arlisse/Dahl. You actually will learn something and she won't harass you like Snow.
better than snow but still man com

Really nice lady. All the mancom teachers are hard graders so it's understandable that she is also. Assignments are reasonable and applicable for the future. However, I felt her feedback was weak. Overall, it's a good class and I'd take her over Snow anyday.
Passionate about computational biology, and tries her best to make lectures engaging. Cares about her students, and responds to both questions on Piazza or via email.

Prof Williams is a fantastic teacher who cares deeply about her students. She is passionate about the material and manages to take complicated machine learning algorithms and makes them manageable. Be warned that projects are always longer than you expect, though they tend to be graded nicely. She is extremely responsive and a great professor.

Professor Williams is very caring about every individual's success in her class. Assignments are challenging but doable if you put in the time and ask questions and they are very relevant to course material. Her lectures were often times not the most clear, but she does try her best to be engaging. Graded on five problem sets and one final project.
Mike is a tremendous leader in the dairy industry. Actually being able to know and work with him in classes is truly amazing.
great professor, very intelligent
world renowned professor. Negative comments below are because people never bothered taking classes this man actually offered.
He is so biased its ridiculous. He loves you if you're a dairy student or in agr he hates agsci students.  Overall I dislike him.

He is a really nice guy, and does a pretty good job keeping the class interesting, by telling jokes and talking about his life.  But the class is only about dairy cows, not other animals.  A lot of field trips, not much homework, no prelims, but there are 5 quizzes, 4 different professors take turns teaching.  Overall unfocused

This class has a lot of potential, but falls short. When Mike speaks, you can tell that he's both extremely intelligent and extremely biased towards dairy and Italy. You can't blame the guy since dairy is his life, but you can't help but wish he would try to show all sides of the arguments he presents.

Great class and professor. He really helped me in my ability to see both sides of an issue. Teaching style is different than most other professors, but in a great way --makes you pay attention. He also expects input from his lecture students.

Lectures are really biased towards the meat industry.  It's an easy A, but the lectures all seem random and unfocused and skewed opinions are presented as fact.  It's not a requirement for the an sci major, so if you can possibly skip it I would-- I can't imagine much of a practical application for the information presented.
