Manages to turn extremely interesting subjects into extremely boring academic droll. Class forces liberal media and ideas down your throat. Took it to learn about Tupac and Biggie, not trans rappers from Puerto Rico that no one knows about.
She was incredibly disorganized and difficult to understand.

Fun and interesting class; you'll learn a lot about African history and culture while doing some cool music workshops. Professor clearly enjoys teaching the course  and is always available to help you improve your papers and assignments.
Good professor, always enthusiastic, and very approachable.  Clearly enjoys the subject matter, and always responds quickly to questions and concerns.

Everything about her is unprofessional. She refuses to speak audibly, she gives no trust or respect to her students, and she scans material too quickly for comprehension. Her lectures are painfully tedious, and her essays are contorted and impossible. She is an atrocious grader, and doesn't mind failing everyone. Avoid this class at all costs!

The moment the course moved into more conceptually difficult territory Apanasovich pretty much became incoherent. But she was still really helpful and often dedicated entire classes to explaining concepts about which students expressed confusion. It also doesn't hurt that she's extremely attractive...
This professor was very soft spoken, and awful in her teaching methods. Her PowerPoints were useless, and exams were extremely hard. Avoid this professor unless you want to ruin your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Prof Apanasovich is hard to follow at times. She gives good tests, not many homeworks, fair.  What really helps to get through the class are her looks, she is hot in a quirky, nerdy kind of way.
The prof is very approachable and clearly understand the material. It really helped to be comfortable with asking you questions and talking to her.
fun ...not boring at all...the material is very interesting and cutting edge...and it helped me to get a job offer, very glad I took it
Great class, the professor is very sweet and helpful. Learned a lot, would recommend  anyone who is interested in Data Mining to take it.
WORST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL EVER!
Boring class. Learning to use SAS Enterprise is cool. Learning useless mathematics is not.
Booooooring!
Professor Tanya is a very sweet, wholesome young woman. ... She is a great person and a good teacher...
HOT

She is kind, personable, & easy to reach. Encourages participation, but in small groups. Tests are easy bc they are all grammar & vocab. The hardest parts of the course were the amount of work (so much hw!!), essays (bc she is a very harsh grader), & oral presentations. Overall I found the course to be easier than AP Spanish, if that helps anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Silvia is honestly a great professor, but her class is really hard. I had to drop it because it was taking too much time and was going to lower my GPA. Lots of work and a really tough grader. She cares about your learning deeply and wants to see you improve your Spanish. I am retaking with a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: VERY HARD SPANISH CLASS and she is a harsh grader. would not take it again

Silvia is a wonderful professor and an expert in the Spanish language. The course is not easy at all, but Silvia's job is to improve your Spanish, and that is exactly what she does through constant conversation and comprehensive feedback. Silvia makes herself extremely available for outside help, and it is very clear that she wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Literally the worst part of Cornell by far. Spanish has actually ruined my whole semester and, in running the Intermediate Spanish program, I can see that she clearly doesn't actually care about teaching. Tbh she seems more like the type of teacher that prides herself in making her class hard even if the material doesn't help us learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are rarely instances where she is actually teaching spanish because the entire class is done in small groups. She cares more about if you do exactly what she says than if you are learning the language. It feels like there is an exam every day. Curriculum of SPAN 2090 is merciless, and she just makes it worse. Try to take it with someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was intimidated by these ratings but IRL, Silvia is great. After months without practice, she refined my Spanish and empowered me so much. Make use of office hours and make sure she gets to know you. Her feedback is super helpful on ensayos and she will go over your test errors personally. Silvia made online learning feel more doable!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The content of this class was not difficult coming out of AP Span in high school, the challenge was the workload. The class meets 3x per week, and there is at the minimum 2-3 hours of HW due the following class every single class. However, if you are struggling, she is sooo accessible in office hours and will genuinely try to help you succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Silvia is one of the best professors I have ever had. She's a tough grader and the material isn't easy, but she's super helpful during office hours and I was in her office every week because I liked talking to her so much. She cares a lot about her students, so put in the work and you'll get good results!

Silvia isn't a good professor. She has single-handedly ruined my passion for Spanish. Every class of hers feels like torture. She is a super tough grader and expects you to talk, speak, read, and write like a fluent native speaker. Plus, she assigns many hours of homework per class so you can never escape. In short, don't take a class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Silvia will make you work for your grade, but you will inevitably get what you put into the class. I started off really lazy and my grades reflected it, but she gave me a nudge and knew I could do better so I picked it up towards the end of the semester and my grade improved. She's a little contradictory sometimes with what she expects in homework.
Professor is a solid OK. Definitely not entertaining but bearable. A ton of busy work. Attendance is mandatory. Easy A, especially if you took AP Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The small class size facilitates interpersonal dialogue, and Silvia is AMAZING. She is caring and wants her students to succeed at Cornell and in her class. I definitely think Silvia's great teaching would allow any motivated student to succeed. Does a virtual exchange with students in Colombia, which was a great experience. Lovely person.

Silvia was my favorite professor this semester. She's caring, reasonable, and highly encouraging. The class was definitely a lot of work at times, but it was always manageable and within reason-- your Spanish WILL improve. I initially took the class just to fulfill the language req, but now I've been inspired to continue Spanish throughout college.

I was initially very intimidated by the syllabus and considered dropping the class, but she encouraged me to stay and I am so glad I did. She is the best Spanish professor I have ever had, and I learned so much more from her in just one semester than I did in all my years of high school Spanish. And she returns things promptly. Amazing professor!!

Best Spanish teacher I've had at Cornell. She's pretty strict on the Spanish-only policy, which is good I think. Gives feedback on rough drafts for every essay. Class activities are generally pretty interesting. She was very helpful in office hours.

Silvia has been one of my favorite professors at Cornell so far. She is very patient, and makes Spanish fun! I learned way more with her in one semester of Spanish than I did in 5 semesters of high school Spanish. I would definitely recommend her and her class.

Silvia is SO nice. She is super friendly, personable, and welcoming - I always felt comfortable. I always got the feeling that she really wants us to learn Spanish properly. I do have to say that it isn't an easy course. She is really tough in the essays, it's pretty impossible to get an A, BUT I cannot believe how much my Spanish improved.

I'm in a class she coordinates. I like the person who teaches me, but not the coordinator who creates the syllabus. The work that this crazy lady makes us do is just absurd. I probably learned much more with other better professors who actually engages us in Spanish, not just drown us with useless works.

Agree with her ideology to get a good grade. What happened to "ANY PERSON any study?" She dislikes wealthy people and/or americans. The whole class is about white americans discriminating against hispanics. She did equate conservatives with materialistic people and tested us on this "fact" which was ridiculous. Horrible.

Don't try to even discuss politics. She's from Spain, living in america, yet claims america sucks- really frustrating and demeaning if you try to discuss things she doesn't agree with- half the time she's wrong anyways. like the one time she said that rightists and materialistic people were the same b/c all republicans just want money. :(

Likes things done her way. Does not help with verbal skills; she will finish sentences for stumbling students, rather than letting them figure things out. Grades papers severely, and essays must be written according to her stylistic constraints, which conflict with those taught in most English departments. Neither friendly nor helpful.

This is a great class if you are all about spanish. However if you are in it for an easy grade dont take it. She doesn't offer any extra help other than her office hours which fall on class times, and is very strict on grading in regards to essays and tests. Orals saved my pathetic grade.

She's very knowledgeable and clear, but she is mean and completely surprised and  offended when you don't understand something or her class isn't your first priority. She accused me of cheating, and even though I wrote an essay in her office and proved that I hadn't, she never said anything, no apology, nothing. Don't take her unless you love Span!
Very good teacher.  Helpful with explanations and very open to giving extra help.  If you make the extra effort to meet out of class time, she will make the extra effort to help you too.

Her class was easily the most frustrating and terrible class I've ever taken.  She's nice, she's helpful, she's overly demanding and often shocked when students don't understand "easy" concepts.  I don't know how much of that is her fault and how much is how Cornell structured the course, but either way - you're in for a LOT of work.  Watch out.
She SEEMS nice but I thought she was mean!! She embarassed students when they didnt know the answer and she graded tests and essays really hard, with little option for rebuttal.

Silvia was such an amazing instructor.  I had her for 2 semesters, and I learned more spanish from her in a year than from the combined efforts of all the teachers I ever had in high school.  She's helpful, enthusiastic, positive, and awesome in general.

Nice professor. She is really knowledgeable. She is helpful during office hours, but she asks you to think hard instead of giving you the answers straight out. Exams were tough, material is extremely tough. But a great class to take if you are interested in analog IC design.
Lectures weren't very stimulating. Basically followed the book word-for-word. Homework assignments and lab reports were a pain. As long as you study the material, the prelims aren't difficult.
No Comments
Lots of work, but overall a good class
she knows her stuffs.  And when I took this class, she is really good.  She gives lots of help and I simply choose my career path after taking her class. I want to do what she does.

She's smart, no doubt about that...but she lacks coherence, organization and enough of an intuitive approach to teach the class...she expected students to know way too much; homeworks and test are long and difficult; labs are worthless and she's very inconsiderate of students' time; don't take it

She's a smart woman, but she REALLY doesn't know how to teach. Her "lectures" are just straight out of the text. Homework takes too long, and class isn't exactly a walk in the park. She isn't that helpful either unless you hound her with questions.

Very difficult class.  Lecture consists of reciting the book... better off just reading it instead.  She has a very heartless and uncompassionate personality.  Final project expectations were ridiculous for time given to us.  I hate analog design now because of this class.
She is one of the greatest teachers that I ever had!
she's actually very nice in lab, knows her stuff and is willing to help. she's not that good at lecturing, but definitely someone who makes an attmept to help her students.
She's better that Lal at lecturing and she helps alot in lab...doesn't seem very approachable, sorta serious personality but once you ask her for help she'll be sure you understand what you're doing
I can't believe how bad the two professors for this course are.  how do they expect us to learn anything from such an important class when we don't have any good professors or ta's?
No Comments
No Comments
this woman is not a very good teacher, all of her lectures are straight out of the book. will sometimes also test random bits of information too.

very boring professor, very monotone. i thought this class would be fun and relatively easy, but it is not interesting at all. shes not a very good lecturer. basically reads right off slides, so going to class is not needed. tests are pretty fair though

Immunology was very interesting and I learned A LOT!  Appleton is one of the nicest and fairest people at Cornell (curves test to 88%) and she is very interested in her students doing well.  Guest lectures were great.  Downside is 8:30 AM in the vet school...I fell asleep a lot so reading the text was crucial to doing well.

Basic Immunology is a demanding class:  meets for an hour and a half twice a week, and covers a lot of material.  Very interesting, though, and Dr. Appleton is a really excellent professor: fair, understanding, timely with posting material, while maintaining high standards.  Powerpoints are comprehensive study tools and expanded on in class.

There are no "tricks" to this class. The exams can be challenging on occasion, but if you can achieve a baseline understanding of the slides in her presentations you should be able to master the tests no problem, which doesn't seem like too much to ask from someone who goes to Cornell... Prof. Appleton is extremely nice and very helpful

This professor teaches Immunology.  I thought this class would be fun but unfortunately this professor is extremely boring.  It doesn't help that the class is at 8:30 in morning.  Also, the tests are ridiculously tricky for no reason and her lectures are sooooo long (about 38 slides each).  I suggest not taking this course.

A bit montone but still sweet and very knowledgeable. Lots of extra credit and quizzes were easy. The final essay was gradely very leniently. Quiz questions are a bit rough unless you take notes from the slides. Prelec recordings were a bit info heavy. Besides that really easy and straightforward class.

I mistakenly uploaded the wrong final file. Over break I sent an email, asking if the project despite missing revisions could be graded. She replied by pasting my words, said nothing could be changed, and signed off with a snarky “use this as a lesson,” which felt mocking and unhelpful. The tone left me discouraged. I could not recommend her.

I was disappointed with her quality of instruction and the course's extremely unclear grading criteria. Without any mention that the class before spring break was worth double the points for attendance students were forced to receive a lower grade. Similarly, for course assignments, grading was unclear and her answers to course questions were rude.

Cider is twice as much work as Wines and Vines in half the amount of time (seven weeks). Grade depends on weekly quizzes which may cover complex topics not mentioned in class. Two papers around sensory evaluation, apple production, cider fermentation, and/or marketing/economics graded (harshly) by peers. Very fun daily tastings and guest lectures.

As a VIEN major, I take a lot of courses and labs taught by her. She's very nice and available when you have questions. However, the lectures are difficult to follow and not structured. Most of the time she reads off the slides and adds random pieces of information. Most work are done in class with groups.

Attendance is a huge part of your grade, and specific notes in class are a must. Quizzes are based on what Kathy says in class, but may not be on slides. Points lost on quizzes add up on final grade. Extra credit final exam to bring your grade up. She knows what shes talking about, but sit in front because the acoustics in stocking hall are awful.

She knows what she's talking about when it comes to wine, and does a really good wine tasting evaluation. The lectures tended to be a little dry in terms of interaction and engagement, and it's hard to get her attention to ask a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took Wines and Vines with Kathy and found it to be very interesting. I took the class coupled with an online program recommended to me by another professor who also teaches for the National Wine School and that really helped me understand the lectures. Getting a sommelier certificate along with an easy A was a great result.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took VIEN 1104 because I thought it was interesting and I am taking the major, but Professor Arnink is very hard to pay attention to and the slides are impossible to follow. She's very nice and willing to take your questions, however, but this requires you to be proactive. Class is extremely easy though, but don't expect to retain much information
Professor Arnink is great. She is really well read in wines and a very interesting lecturer. Her classes are easy to pass if you care. I wish I could take more classes with her!
This class was the easiest A+ I've ever received.  There's so much extra credit available that if you show up, you will get at least an A. Definitely recommend!

I really enjoyed Wines and Vines and would take another class with Kathy in the future, as she was friendly and willing to help her students. I learned a lot about enology and had the opportunity to sample a wide variety of wines from all over the world. Highly recommend this class, not sure what the other guy is going on about.

The courses Kathy teaches are all extremely unorganized and there are lots of little assignments with unclear instructions. When you ask questions about due dates, lengths, etc she tells you to look at Blackboard, which usually doesn't help. I receive good marks on everything, but if you like organization, DO NOT take her classes.

Absolutely adore Dr. D. He made the somewhat difficult thermo material understandable, was always available for extra office hours or answering questions. 2 prelims were not too hard, final was harder than anticipated but still very doable. Super kind and awesome. GOAT

The lectures for this class were not the most straight forward, but the in class assignments and homework helps to reinforce the material. The tests are fair and generously graded. He is very accessible outside of class and corrects mistakes very quickly.

Professor D was great. The online part of the class was convenient and the lectures were very engaging. If you have any background in any physics this class will likely be way too intro level for you, but sometimes you're looking for that easy class. 5 tests felt like a lot but you end up dropping one. Material is a bit random at times but is easy.

Dr. D is a good professor all around. He is really kind and wants his students to succeed. If you need help, he will help, and his behavior will never dissuade you from going to lectures. My only issue is that the lectures were sometimes pretty confusing and required extra studying.
Oh, and there are 5 tests.  Luckily you can drop one.
Overall a manageable and comfortably paced course in thermodynamics. Course consists of quasi-weekly problem sets and two prelims which were fair.
can be disorganized on the lecture materials but otherwise cares about the class and the students.

Dr D had Interesting lectures and was knowledgeable about the subject but it was hard to go back and follow lectures without rewatching them as PowerPoint/class posted notes weren't stellar on their own. Homework and climate math (quantitative quizzes) were manageable, plus no exams during covid semester, only weekly multiple-choice quizzes w drops

My favorite professor so far! Lectures were super clear and he was very encouraging and helpful to everyone in the class. He didn't have specific office hours but was really easy to schedule a meeting with outside class. Definitely make sure to pay attention in class because he may call on you to answer a question & you'll do better on the homework

Taken online. The lecture slides are confusing but the prof does a good job explaining them. Grading was very lenient and based on weekly quizzes, take-home quizzes, and simple assignments. Not sure if he will go back to tests once online is over instead of the weekly quizzes. Take this class if you're interesting in scientific climate change stuff

A very animated and passionate lecturer - you can tell he cares about the subject. He also genuinely wants students to succeed and always answers questions. Prelims are pretty straightforward and similar to class examples, and he gives good study guides.

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. The course is challenging, but interesting. Professor DeGaetano will make you work for your grade. Great course, attendance is key; he says things in lecture that you will be tested on and they are not in the lecture notes/slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was amazing, 10 out of 10 would recommend.

Cracks a good joke once in a while, but otherwise monotonous. He's so relaxed about everything and does not gaf, which is exciting at first. However, the fact that he does not gaf will be reflected on your first prelim score. He overcomplicates the entire instruction of econ. Got a good grade but learned very little, which sums up his class.
I felt like I didn't learn much. 😕 I know he's trying his best to teach, but it was really hard to understand him. The prelims and final were open book, but most students just used AI

By far the funniest professor I've had, half the time I was wondering if I signed up for a comedy show instead of office hours. Which he would just cancel if he didnt feel like it lol. Somehow managed to roast us, teach us, and make us think, all in one breath. Actually cared, helped, and made every lecture worth showing up for. I loved his class!!
Helped me out a lot and was one of the most forgiving teachers I've ever had. Very good guy.

His lecture style is pretty dry but once you get used to it he's kinda a funny guy. Says things like "this is boring im falling asleep" and "eh this is easy teach it to yourselves at home". Class seems confusing at first but if you go to lectures and write down everything he says (open note test) its not too hard at all.

I feel like he is pretty good at explaining key concepts, but his lecture slides aren't clear. Transparent about what will be on the exams. The quizzes are straightforward, and the tests are fairly easy, with a good curve

Basu has no passion to teach so his lectures were absolute hell and super boring. However, he also wants the best for his students so he made exams open-note which really helped boost my grade. Just take really good notes and you will do fine in his class.

teaches things that aren't on the internet, hard to understand lecture and lecture slides are super difficult to understand, I took macro in high school so I thought I'd be fine in this class regardless, but he teaches things you cant even Google. some prelim questions, even AI can't understand how I get them wrong and neither does the LSC center

He is a chill dude. He is not the best lecturer, and he knows that. But he curves the exams and he gives different ways to weigh your prelims and final, so he wants everyone to end up with a decent grade.

I think Basu is an okay professor, but he's certainly not for everyone. You really need to read the textbook AND PRACTICE to do well in this course. His lectures helped clarify the content and he literally tells you what you need to know for exams. While not the most excited to teach undergrads, Basu does want students to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Basu is not a bad guy, don't get me wrong, but he definitely isn't made for teaching. His lecture style is pretty dry (and a little repetitive) so it's hard to pay attention in class. Partly because of this, paying attention pays dividends on prelims, which are curved. The class is moooostly easy, but do study extensively for exams.

Basu is an absolute baller. My guy understands students' pain and actively tries to condense material to reduce frustration. He'll flat out cancel lectures if he or the class isn't feeling it. I loved his dry, deadpan lecture style. Literally just show up to class and you'll do well on the prelims. Quizzes were free and helped a ton on prelims.

Basu doesn't teach the best, even he acknowledges that, however: open book exams (canvas, lecture notes, notes),  ALL MCQ, weekly quizzes, 3 grading schemes to give you the best grade. Discussions were super helpful, lectures not so much. Compared to the other prof teaching econ, I'd take easy exams over teaching quality for this intro couse

Basu is a nice guy, but his class is just insufferable. One of the most boring and unhelpful lecturers I've ever had. Doesn't teach material well and the weekly quizzes don't match up to the topics learned in class. Not necessarily a bad class, just a pain in the butt. He does curve grades, but take another professor if you can.
I wasn't sure about Econ 1120 until I realized that my professor was Arnab Basu. The median was graded to an A- and more importantly, he gets us.
He is very nice with grading. Fun dude, would take again.

Basu is a pretty boring lecturer however he makes the lecture materials accessible and the textbook is very informative. Lectures are not super helpful because he tends to rant a bit and oftentimes ends class early as hell. I think this class is very passable and comprehensible with a little extra effort. I would recommend skipping lecture!

Intermittently throughout lectures, Arnab would emit an exhausted, deflated sigh. I'd say that is an accurate summary of my sentiments toward the class. It is very obvious he despises teaching and is here only for his research funding. Sometimes, he'd end class an hour early. Just a bad professor. Thank the dyson curve.

The most unorganized professor I have ever had. I took AP Macro in high school and figured it wouldn't matter what 1120 section I enrolled in since I knew the material, but he only confused me. His slides cannot be understood, he makes up material that's not even on the internet. Taught me the professor is pertinent to the quality of the class.

Personally I enjoyed his class, he seemed like a decent enough guy and lecturer. 

Criticism is that some slides in his lectures were hard to decipher.
not an engaging course at all

One of the worst professors I've had in my life. Tests and quizzes were very tough, I don't even know where half the questions come from. Very boring, almost never went to lecture. Had to switch to pass/fail so I wouldn't have a B- on my transcript.

Despite other ratings, I liked Basu. His exams were online and open note, and he uses 3 different grading schemes to then select the highest as your total grade in the class. He clearly wants his students to succeed, and he even tells us exactly what chapters/problems to study for exams. I especially enjoyed how he let us leave class early often

Honestly not a blast. Seemed to not like teaching which was weird since he is a professor? Huh. 
Ended class early, read off of lecture slides that he did not make, etc. Learned basically nothing.

Professor Basu was honestly one of the worst professors I have ever taken. Almost nothing that he taught made sense and the online quizzes, especially Prelim 2 and the Final were downright impossible. Half of the time he showed up late to class, ended class very early, and at the end of the year he didn't even care whether the lights were on.

Professor Basu was honestly one of the worst professors I have ever taken. Almost nothing that he taught made sense and the online quizzes, especially Prelim 2 and the Final were downright impossible. Half of the time he showed up late to class, ended class very early, and at the end of the year he didn't even care whether the lights were on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Even though my grade may not reflect it, this class was an utmost horror. I was very disturbed by the way the class was run: disorganized lectures, no engagement with students, no lights, and very poor TAs. Just don't take this class guys, it was so bad.
I emailed Prof. Basu to set up a meeting to discuss Prelim 2, and he simply didn't show up to the meeting. He was so unhelpful, don't take this class!
If I could give Prof. Basu a 0, I would. Made this class difficult for no reason, and I was shocked with how he basically came up with his own facts!

I'm sorry but what teacher gives a Prelim with an average in the 70s for an Introductory Economics course and doesn't give the answer key to the test. He is so absent and never there to help students. Never take this class.

This was the worst class I have ever taken at Cornell! The class is so disorganized, and the lectures are taught way too fast and don't correspond to what's on the test. Moreover, Professor Basu made Prelim 2 way too hard and caused so many students to fail. I wish I knew not to take this class. Plus, the class is basically taught in the darkness!

Prof. Basu is the worst lecturer I have had in my time at Cornell. He is impossible to pay attention to and his Prelim 2 was impossible. Never take this class unless your life depends on it. This was my biggest mistake at Cornell so far.

He went AWOL after the final exam and did not respond to emails. His lectures were boring and too fast. He did not seem like he cared about teaching the subject and did not seem to care that students did not understand the lessons.
Basu is the man. Great professor, you wont regret taking this class at all.

Basu is amazing. Good at teaching, extremely flexible grading criteria to get you the best grade possible, and a great guy. Tests are moderate and he pretty much tells you what will be on them. You don't have to do work or show up if you don't want to , but I would recommend doing it.

Very smart and engaging lecturer. Really cares about his students and always makes sure that everyone understands the topics. Homework is somewhat challenging but going to office hours is super helpful. Tests were relatively easier and the final project is super interesting! Great professor, great class!

Very solid professor. Posts every previous exam online and tells you exactly what will be on the exams. Provides different grading criteria based on what will be most beneficial for you. Not a very interesting course, but worth taking nonetheless.
He seems nice and smart, but his lectures are quite boring and his accent is hard to understand. However, as mentioned in previous comments, he gives multiple grade criteria which is AWESOME
Great professor. Interesting class. Fair exams. The professor is very helpful outside of class and tries his best to give you a good grade.
Massive class but he's a great prof and pretty accessible. Lets you choose grading criteria, and it can be just prelims and final if you want (which is dope, especially since the tests are cake).

arnab basu is literally the greatest man on this planet. one of the most qualified and successful professors at cornell, he is so smart. willing to work with students and genuinely wants everyone to understand his class

Absolutely fantastic and passionate lecturer! He's very helpful and willing to guide you thru the fairly complex psets. Exams were 50 minutes in-class which means the questions are fairly conceptual. Would recommend, great professor.
Made me find my love for physics!

The best and the most "physics" physics course I've ever had! Truly inspiring and interesting! The materials were very tough, but Prof. Arias made it engaging and thought-provoking through his clear, logical, and amazing lectures. Recommended to all who want to learn and understand physics! Very helpful for future learning!

Arias is so great and makes such an effort in his courses! I would definitely recommend taking a class with him. The material was tricky but he's always available to ask questions to and wants his students to do well and feel passionate about physics.

[Rating for honors waves] Very theoretical and math-heavy. Lectures are very clear and well-organized, with a focus on derivations, not applications. Gives very useful lecture notes. Provides loads of useful support and office hours. Exams are fair and much easier than problem sets. Problem sets are difficult and VERY time-consuming!
I didn't actually take Professor Arias's class for 3316, but I pretty much did, considering I substituted all of Jian's lectures for Arias's lectures.

Truly some of the best lectures I've experienced at Cornell. Prof. Arias' unique PSets were really long and hard, but were some of the most insightful I've ever done. Very knowledgeable professor who can also help with all sorts of physics and math problems.

Prof. Arias is the best lecturer I have ever seen. The class was at 9 AM, but each day I woke up excited to climb the slope and watch his lecture, being sad when it ended. The homeworks can long, but extremely informative and rewarding to do (arias makes his own questions). Exams are fair. Arias is a rigorous (mathematically) source of knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Arias explains things very clearly and his class is extraordinarily organized. Although Psets were hard, taking 10-15 hours (I never went to office hours bcuz of time conflicts, which may have reduced the time ), I gained a really good foundation for quantum mechanics. Exams require you to work really fast but they're fair and easier than Psets.
Arias gives fantastic lectures. Course website is well prepared. Homework are quite a lot but generally inspirational.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Arias was one of the most passionate professors I have had at Cornell. Even though I despised physics, he somehow managed to make me enjoy the class.

Arias is a nice guy, but is not very accessible to get help from. The P-Sets were incredibly difficult, covering material not taught and requiring 5-12 hours a week in office hours. The TA's often weren't sure how to do the questions (citing them as being harder than some of their grad-level P-Sets). OHs were ALWAYS packed (50-80 kids at a time).

Professor Arias is a wonderful professor that really cares about his students. The problem sets and lecture videos/pre-class exercises are a lot of work, but Professor Arias' dedication to his job makes it very enjoyable and worth it!!
Take him now - it will be a fun ride.

Good teacher, only complaint is that the tests questions were asked in very obscure and confusing ways. Many of the tests were based on randomly plugging in formulas, without the need for much physics.

Arias knows A LOT, and wants to meticulously prove things to his students. He is a GREAT lecturer, and is very open to talking to students both in and out of class. Homework was really difficult and took many hours (for me, 8-15), but I did come out of it a lot better at math.

Arias is very passionate, which makes lectures more enjoyable. Other than that the class is crap. The discussion section is not representative of the difficulty of prelims. The problem sets are WAY too hard and do not help you for the prelims. In my experience, you feel like you know your stuff and then the test rolls around and you don't.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I liked the flipped format of the class but I found the homeworks to be unnecessarily difficult. The tests were difficult but nicely curved. The lecture videos and questions were informative, organized, and easy to complete. If you put in the time to understand everything and attend lecture as the course goes on, you can do well.

Physics E&M was a lot of work and demanded a lot of time that I sadly did not always have. Prof. Arias is a really nice guy who genuinely cares about his students and is truly happy when the median grade on exams is high. Don't sweat the problem sets too much, as long as you understand the Co-Ops you'll be okay for exams.

Arias really cares about the students. He gets very happy when people in class understand the topics in lecture, and if they don't, he does his best to clear things up. This course is very fast-paced, and Arias doesn't like to waste much time. The problem sets are incredibly challenging, but if you understand the COOPs you'll be fine on the prelims
He really wanted to see us succeed and seemed genuinely happy when prelim scores were high.  Probably the most likable professor I've had so far.

He kind of reminds me of a dad. He was very approachable and encouraging during office hours. I started off struggling, but he was always willing to accommodate my learning style. Some people liked the flipped classroom method, and things really started to click once we switched to videos.

Prof. Arias is a good teacher.  I learned a lot through his 'flipped classroom' method of teaching.  I would highly recommend watching the video lectures at  a faster pace, as Arias speaks kind of slowly and pauses a lot.  You can take a 45 minute video lecture and turn it into a 12 minute lecture.  Major time saver. Definitely attend lecture.

Professor Arias is the best professor that I have had in my time at Cornell. He is kind, approachable, knowledgeable,  and an all-around great guy. When students voiced concerns, may it be with format or content, he listened and acted, at one point even starting to produce hour-long video lectures to help. He is amazing, and deserves high praise.
Clearest professor I've ever had. Empathizes with what the student knows and doesn't on a intimate level. However, you'll have to do a lot of work for his class (if you want to do well, that is).

Arias is truly dedicated to making sure his students understand the material. The exams (with the exception of the multiple choice on the first one) were very fair and very straightforward. Problem sets were challenging but very doable. He also made himself available for questions and pretty much wouldn't let you leave until you understood it!

Best professor I've had in my four semesters thus far. He's extremely helpful and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. He's also very passionate about the material and teaches is better than anyone else could. If you have a chance to take a class with him, don't pass it up.
Simply the greatest

Arias is an amazing professor. If you ever have to take 2213, make sure he is teaching. Arias is so caring about students performance, and he is genuinely a nice guy. This is a really difficult course, especially if you struggled in multivariable like I did. The problem sets are hard, but they prepare you well for the exams which are pretty fair

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. His lectures are theoretical but he make tough topics extremely clear to understand with a lot of enthusiasm. He cares a lot about his students and truly wants  them to learn the material. Tests are slightly challenging but the homeworks prepare you well for exams.
Wonderful professor; however, he curved the class to a lower grade then normal, so that contributed to lower grades. Very clear and enthusiastic.

Best professor I've had at Cornell yet. If you're the type of person who just wants to memorize equations and apply them then you will probably not like this class. However, if you  find the subject interesting and want to truly understand the fundamental concepts then Arias is a spectacular professor.

Probably one of the most brilliant people I've ever met. Lectures were indeed mathematical- but in the best way possible. Contrary to what some would say- his derivations go far beyond what's written in the book. He generates his own problem sets that are tailored to what you'd expect to see on an exam. Phenomenal instructor for a phenomenal class.
HORRIBLE! do not take a class with this professor. literally did not learn a thing. makes me fail every prelim because he does not teach us how to approach the difficult problems he presents.

If you don't enjoy the derivations involved in learning physics, then you don't enjoy physics. They're the point of it. That said, this class is amazing. Arias approaches electromagnetism intuitively, and teaches all of the fundamental concepts and theories by deriving them. If you really do like math and physics, you'll love Arias.

Does a pretty good job explaining derivations during lecture.  Pay attention to these as they are pretty close to what the problem sets and tests are like.  I do admit the class is very "mathy" although it's really not bad.  The problem sets are good at bringing up old material so that you are always practicing what you've learned
He spent all of lecture going over derivations provided in the book, and just made us do math heavy problem sets. I would recommend not taking the class with him.

Absolutely brilliant. He focuses a lot on theory and mathematical calculations during lecture and doesn't really give much application and problem-solving, but he is very organized and extremely clear in his explanations. Would definitely take another course with him.

For electromagnetism this semester, the lectures were not very helpful with regard to exams, feel free to skip them and read the textbook. The problem sets were excessively time consuming and calculus heavy. He's not that bad, but I recommend taking this course with another professor in the spring semester.

This is a review for how he taught electromagnetism for engineers. He gave extremely difficult problems sets, but the prelims were fairly easy. His lecture is very easy and simple, on the conceptual side, but that will not help with the homework which all rely heavily on vector calculus. The lectures were not all that helpful for exams either.
Hes the professor now for autotutorial physics. Take this class. He's good at explaining things and a very smart man. Course is time consuming but easy grade.

Pretty much what everyone else said.  Very good teacher, knows how to explain things in a way that's easy to understand.  The class wasn't too hard in my opinion, but I think they curve the class to a pretty low mean grade, so you need to work pretty hard if you want an A.

this was one of the harder classes i've taken.  this guy really has a solid command on the subject and it able to communicate and teach very well.  i should have put more time into this class to get a better grade.  exams and homework are hard.

Best physics professor I've had, but that's probably because honors physics profs aren't that great (Veit Elser, Pollack...). Really loves physics, and does a good job explaining the stuff. Exams are pretty tough, and homework is tough! (it goes step by step though, so you'll know what to do) Go to his lectures and do the homework!

fantastic professor and course! problem sets can be a bit challenging, but they're well thought out and you really feel like you've learned a lot when you're done with them.  most helpful professor i've had at cornell.
Very Very good teacher, though HW sets were kind of hard, exams were all relevant to his homework problems. Highly recommanded!!!
Very good teacher, excellent explanations, made a tough class a little more bearable

I took this class a while back and didn't do well on it (C+). But it's not an easy class, my TA wan't that good, and the class itself was competitive (std dev is like 5 points on prelims), so it's not his fault. He's clear and helpful, and I definitely should have gone more. GO TO LECTURES!!!
Quality lectures. Exams are fair. And that time he dressed up as Morpheus from the Matrix... What more can you ask for in Cornell?

This is simply the best physics teacher I've ever had. He really loves teaching. If you are taking Physics 214, take it with him. He will challenge you, but you'll end up loving the subject beacause of him.

Great Teacher! I usually skip classes, so it doesn't mean much, but for the times I was in class, I understood what he was talking about even though I missed half the material before that class. It was also immensely enjoyable to see such an EXCITING smile on his face all the time.
His excitement is clear, but he should really drink less coffee before lecturing!!
No Comments
Prof. Arias is way too organized (prelims had tables of contents). Great teacher and nice person.

Lecture was presented clearly and orderly. He really knows the material! A little of it went over my head, but I'm an ECE major, so that's ok. He added a lab at 8AM on Friday!!!  I wouldn't have taken the class if had known!
A really great prof -- knows the material and enjoys teaching  Publishes notes online -- helpful
This guy rules.  He enjoys what he's teaching immensely, and makes physics lectures interesting.  The subject is tough, but he's more than willing to help you if you need it.
Yo... he is da man... not

He's a really great prof!! He wants students to do well - if you are struggling/need help/want something to be different, tell him. Super accessible outside of class. Make sure you find a friend to do the end-of-class quizzes with (it's allowed). He is so nice and enthusiastic. Applies concepts to specific examples really well.
I loved this class, the lectures were very interesting and accessible! a rare for cornell classes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Okay class. DeGeatano clearly cares, but he's just a very poor communicator, and the class is not organized in a way that makes it engaging. Would be a lot better if it were split up into sections so that we can discuss rather than listen to lectures. Also, dense with material, yet geared toward non-science majors. Reinforced my dislike of physics.

One of the coolest profs at Cornell! Very clear, funny, personable, informative.  Excellent at explaining material, but you have to go to class. The slides he uses only have graphs and figures that you won't understand unless you actually go.  Gives a few short homework assignments that are helpful to reinforcing class material.

So this is one is coming from a meteorology major. The man is in his element with the smaller classes, like EAS 341. He's a very nice guy, more than happy to help you out in class and in his office (he never has regular office hours). Likes to call on people at random though, and gets flustered when he loses his place in his notes.

This is coming from someone who took this course to satisfy a science requirement. That being said, the course is dense with material, and no sections don't help. Take this if meteorology is your focus. Also, don't be that kid who tries to wing it w/o talking to Art. He's a good man, and very approachable.
Great class in which you learn about the cool stuff in Meteorology(Lightning, rainbows, halos, radar...)
The nicest man ever.  The tests are exactly from lecture notes, don't read the book.  Only about 6 homework assignments.  Lectures are interesting.  Would take this class several times over.

Physical Meteorology is really tough, and your notes will just be derivations, and then derivations won't be on your test. His problem sets are tough, but there are only three.  He is very approachable and a very lenient grader, although his exams will make you (want to) cry.

He went at just the right speed during class. He is very friendly and always welcomes students who need extra help and have questions. He always showed how he got equations, rather than simply writing them on the board, which was useful. An overall good guy!

Excellent lecturer... Worked through in-class examples very thoroughly, and made sure everyone understood... Always available for homework/pre-exam help...  Be aware the tests can be tricky, and he WILL call on random people during class.  Otherwise, made thermodynamics almost enjoyable!

Prof Fuhrmann is a wonderful lecturer and is very knowledgeable and passionate in her field. The way this course was structured was quite interesting as a bulk of it were guest speakers within the Asian Studies department and I enjoyed learning the course materials through those different perspectives. The workload was normal and pretty manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Fuhrmann is extremely nice, and very accommodating with extensions. Always willing to talk with students after class. Extremely easy grader. Class median was an A+. I think I had a perfect 100 average in the class because she and her TA Anna, who was also great, gave me full marks on every assignment even when I thought they weren't so great.
There is a lot of reading. Prof. Fuhrmann is very accomodating if you have problems, though.
he retired but im giving him a 5 for the vibes

Chill prof. Test questions can be a little vague and confusing sometimes, but overall still very easy. There's a group "community project" that's pure busy work. Graded on 3 prelims, discussion attendance, and that project. A+ is very doable, but first prelim always trips ppl up. Great way for non-STEM ppl to coast through their bio requirement.
Chip is a really cool guy. The lectures can be boring at times but the workload is very doable. I'm more interested in genetics just because of his class!

Chip was one of the kindest professors I've had at Cornell. 1290 was easy and only required a weekly discussion post and take-home prelims and finals. The lectures can be a bit boing, but attendance is used as extra credit. Easy A/A+ class except the take-home exams can be a little tedious but TAs offer a lot of help
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: fun class and kind professor.

The lectures are tedious and the take-home prelims are long and challenging. You go into them with essentially 0 understanding of how to answer and just have to sit through office hours until a TA spells out the answer for you. Ridiculous class.

BIOMG1290 is perfect for the PBS requirement, but it's not a waste of time either. Chip is caring and invested in this class, and though he makes it easy to do well, you still learn a lot. One of the nicest professors.

great class. take-home prelims and a take-home final. exams require a decent amount of thought/time but chip and his TAs will help you in office hours! go to class and discussion and you'll be fine. wish i could take this again, was really interesting and not too too hard

The best prof I've ever had here. Some of the lectures are a bit boring but Chip does a great job connecting material in class to the real world! Is always available for help, is smart, and cares deeply about his students - always says hi, checks in, and even takes time at beginning of class to congratulate student-athletes in the course on wins.
Wish I could take this class again. Such a kind person and professor who cares about his students so much. Not too hard and grading is fair

Chip is hands down one of the best profs I've ever had. Cares deeply about his students and the subject matter he teaches. Is there for you to help at any time, and exams are fair if you do the reading/pay attention in class. He goes out of his way to keep students engaged by doing DNA testing/bringing in guest lecturers. Really smart and kind.
Seemed like an easy class. Exams were unreasonably detailed. TAs were awful (except one). Discussions were pointless. It was cool to get our DNA tested. This class needs some serious tweaking.

The material is quantitative and kinda boring. HOWEVER, it has some extremely interesting applications. And Chip is a pretty good professor, always approachable with questions. He's really challanged me as a scientific thinker and I actually feel smarter thanks to his class.

Great professor. You do actually have to study for the tests but they aren't too bad. He is a fantastic lecturer and I've never enjoyed a class that doesn't allow technology so much. When he talks about chimps there's an art of storytelling there and its quite enjoyable. I look forward to class every time I have it.

Super well organized. Took the summer course, asynchronous. Everything was meticulously organized and easily understandable. Grading was fair and content was actually super interesting. He touched on real world issues, beyond just facts of biology. Highly recommend.

If you need a bio distribution requirement, especially as a humanities major, take this class! The readings are short and relatively interesting (not too much hard science) and they are not tested on the exam. While you do have to study for the exams, they are not particularly intense. The lectures are also engaging and easy to understand.

I had professor Arcadi for a FWS that turned out to be all about canoes. He is a chill and nice guy, you will write 10 essays over the course of the semester but with a guaranteed A if you do the work and come to class! You will have a solid amount of work but I am glad I was in this class

I wouldn't recommend this class if you're merely trying to fulfill the A&S bio requirement. This is an amazing class if you have strong interest in the subject matter. His office hours are very helpful. However, do not expect an "easy A" out of this class -- the medians for the exams were quite low, hitting the C+ and B- range (without a curve).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Even if you didn't have interest in chimpanzees prior to taking the class, you will by 2 weeks in.

Such a nice guy. Super accomodating to my family member's illness. Can follow along with online lectures, but in person is much better and better for retaining knowledge. Cares so much about the topic, and is really descriptive allowing anyone to ask a question about whatever during class. Spots usually fill up so mostly seniors. Bio distribution.
makes chimpanzee science fun!
Professor Arcadi is an amazing professor. He has left a tremendous impact on me, and ultimately influenced my major.
A very reasonable teacher. This class was a decent amount of work but was manageable. Professor Arcadi is a witty teacher who inspires thought and creates a fun class environment. #superfun

Prof. Arcadi is a wonderful professor and is really passionate about the subject of biology and primates. His lectures are clear and well-crafted and the readings he assigned were also interesting. Through this class, I learned more about the lives of chimpanzees and their similarities with humans. I'd highly recommend everyone to take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love this man with all my heart. Caring, compassionate, thoughtful, smart, everything you want in a professor. Professor Arcadi understands what matters.

This class was really interesting and Prof Arcadi structures his lectures very well. The tests weren't difficult (24 hours, open note) but it definitely required knowing the lecture material. Prof Arcadi was super nice and loved the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Arcadi is great online. He crafts his lectures with so much care, and they are very well-organized. The prelims are 24 hours, which hasn't been hard thus far. He knows so much, and his enthusiasm is contagious. The flexibility of the asynchronous lectures and the optional office hours are great too. He's just a nice dude

Professor Arcadi is hilarious, interesting, and very experienced in the field of anthropology/primate research. He's surprisingly approachable and likes when students go to his office hours. GO TO CLASS (on time), pay attention and don't make the fatal mistake of pulling out your phone in class. He's a great professor and gives amazing lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tests are lecture-based, no Multiple Choice, essay based. Exams are not cumulative take really good notes, you will need it for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Arcadi is a really good lecturer; he conveys the information in an interesting and engaging manner. He's funny, but if you're late or have your phone out he'll be (justifiably) pretty rude. I personally liked his tangents and occasionally subjective ways of describing things. I ended up learning a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, conveys a lot of info clearly and concisely. Read a total of 4 books with 8-10 about them at the send of the semester. No final only prelims. Lectures aren't mandatory but you will miss a lot by skipping. Section is bi-weekly and either you go or write a two page paper about the reading. I would highly recommend this class.

Professor Arcadi is engaging and passionate. His class on chimps was easily the most interesting class I've taken. It was very fun. You absolutely need to go to class and take notes. He only lectures, with no powerpoint behind him. I was surprised at how much I liked this approach.

The most appealing aspect of Intro to Anthro is its low difficulty.  Arcadi's organized and you will learn a thing or two, but he also makes the occasional rude comment or focuses more on giving his opinions than objective info.  Textbook is officially required, but you can probably do fine without one.
Discussions tend to go off on tangents but this is decidedly a good thing; one of the main reasons why class with Arcadi is interesting.  Very bright guy and very opinionated.

I took this class on a complete whim, and it was by far my favorite of the semester.  Professor Arcadi was a great lecturer who seemed to really care about the class, even though it's an intro level.  he was organized and engaging and very, very knowledgable.  take this class!!
Interesting class...Prof. Arcadi is clear and has well-organized notes...class is not really hard but exams can be pretty tough if you don't study enough
he's fun, and spent a lot of time hanging out with chimps... so he knows his stuff.

This is a good guy.  The classes are surprisingly interesting for a science class.  It's also not hard.  It's definitely a good class to fill requirements, fairly easy, and the labs are just sections (not real labs).  Definitely a reccomended course.

Prof. Arcadi has a very stern attitude and he likes to scare people during the first week of class by embarassing those who come in a couple of minutes late - but he is very clear and knowledgable, and he can be fun. I think he looks a little like a mix between Hugo Weaving and a wolf.
He's such a nice guy! His lectures are organized pretty well and he likes to engage his students. He makes his course material fun to learn.

Pretty easy grader for a good writer, BUT Make sure to ask her about her grading criteria at the beginning of the semester ESPECIALLY structure. Not very engaging as a lecturerer. Overall, she's not a bad professor and nice but I would only take her if you are interested in the subject matter.She gives 2 projects and 5 6-page papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: unclear grading

Lectures were often difficult to understand and follow. Regarding papers, she would often deduct points for errors and not explain how to correct them, even if you already tried to correct it. Grading criteria was not always easy to understand.

Taken online. The lectures are honestly difficult to understand if you are not somewhat versed in the topic area already. However, there isn't any work except for the papers which aren't easy but graded very leniently and the average grade in the class was an A. Lots of discussion in class but you don't have to speak if you don't want to.

When I took his class, he failed to foster cohesion in our group. We eventually dropped the course because we couldn't build a rational connection with him. Although meetings were accessible, his feedback and understanding of our situation were consistently discouraging — not something I expect from a senior professor.

The GOAT. Best professor you will have in BEE. Really cares about his students. BEE 3500 is hard just by the nature of the material, but if you show up to class and his OH, everything will work out for you.

He cares about his students' learning but struggles to teach them effectively. The theory behind the course material is very relatable to real life, but the testing includes material that you may not cover in class. Attendance is graded, but you'd likely be better off (for your knowledge and achieved grade) learning the material outside of class.

Datta is a great professor who truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. The class itself was really difficult but it was well supported by office hours and the TAs. He really emphasized problem solving and understanding the problem itself before beginning the actual solution.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Datta is by far the best engineering professor I've had at Cornell . The courses structure, the spiral bound course notes, lifesaving problem solving charts and his ability to teach, really allow you to develop a true understanding of the topics. Unlike other eng courses he actually wants you to do well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is overall a good class, if you struggle on the homeworks, do as many problems as you possibly can before the prelim. Also -- MEMORIZE THE PROBLEM SOLVING MAPS -- thank me later
One of the best professors I ever met in Cornell! Very considerate, and always there for his students. Love him!
He's great! Best lecturer I've had so far.

Professor Datta is extremely invested in his students and it shows.  Even though his prelims can be tricky at times, if you do a bunch of problems from the back of the book and go to office hours for homework help, you'll be in good shape.

Professor is a little condescending and often goes over the time limit for class, which is rough when it's all the way up in Riley Robb, but the class is very well-organized and he is more than willing to help people who are struggling. I highly recommend attending the discussion section.
Great professor who knows his stuff. He really wants his students to understand the material, so I recommend meeting with him personally if you need help.
Very explicit about expectations and the conceptsskills he expects you to have down. Several resources to learn by, including text and lecture notes.
Great professor. really cares about the students and takes the time to meet with students. Great organization. Class was alot of work but i learned alot too
Probably the best professor I have ever had.
Amazing prof. Genuinely cares about students, and his lectures are extremely clear and helpful. Course is also very relevant to BEE. One of the best profs in the BEE department and at Cornell.
I had Professor Datta for both 3500 and 4530 and i have to say he is the best. He really cares about his students and wants them to really learn and love the subject as he does.

He's welling to help and he wants to teach well for sure, you can tell from the enthusiasm.  However, some of the homeworks and prelim  problems are poorly worded/made.  It's just so hard to figure out what the question is asking or what the diagram is showing. You have to talk to him and after awhile you get it but there's no time on the test...
Great academic professor. You will learn a lot,and if you don't understand him he will definitely help you out. Not the coolest guy, unfortunately.

Professor Datta is one of the best professors I've had--if not the best! He sincerely wants everyone to understand the material. He makes a lot of effort to help each student who asks for help. Lectures are clear and informative, and recitation is a great way to learn how to approach problems.

Datta is awesome. He really wants everyone to understand the material, and explains things well. I feel like I may actually remember the material for some time. Homeworks and tests were fair, and he is good about reviewing for exams.
Datta is really nice and pretty good at explaining things.  Plus, the textbook is just like the lecture notes so if you miss class its not bad.

Professor Datta really likes helping people. He really encourages us to go to office hours. Although, I do admit his lectures are rather boring, he is still a really nice guy and wants his students to do well.

Quite possibly the best professor I've ever had. He explains complicated ideas clearly and easily. I've never met a professor that put so much effort into his classes. He'll definitely help you any way he can, and he wants you to do good (opposed to most engineering classes).
very helpful, he actually loses sleep when he doubts his class' understanding of the material.  plus you get your own mailbox for the class.
Very nice and always looking to help students. Grades were high.

Terrible!  His course notes (that red book) were awful--typos, unlabeled diagrams, poorly worded sentences.  I couldn't believe he called it "the best book out there on biological mass tranfer".  His "demos" also sucked! Glade air-fres
Did not enjoy this course at all. The professor assigns wayyy more work than any other 3 credit courses I have taken. Was a pretty inconsiderate professor, I don't recommend taking her course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Super nice and caring prof, put in the work and show that you care and the prof will be super nice and helpful. Accessible outside of class & loves meeting with students to talk out ideas. A LOT of work and reading, the content is interesting but the workload is extreme for a 3cred course (many indicated this in eval's so workload may be decreased)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class for a distribution requirement for Arts & Sciences. Would never recommend this professor to anyone. My participation grade was completely inaccurate and we were told final grades were "non-negotiable." Instructor made me feel extremely uncomfortable when discussing grades or anything regarding this class.

Each lecture was based on a short reading from the night before of relatively few pages and a few short readings in class + discussion. The class essentially boils down to a final paper and some reading assignments.
Loved the class, Professor Van Oyen loves her work and makes learning about ancient economies very interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Compassionate, caring, understanding, interesting course material, and easy grading. Really could not ask for much more. Would absolutely recommend to any major.
I took CLASS 2712 and thoroughly enjoyed it. Prof Van-Oyen is very knowledgeable, and the way she organizes the lessons and lectures is engaging and is undoubtedly conducive to learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took Roman Archaeology with prof Van Oyen fall 2021. It was my first archaeology class and was overall very interesting, very low stress, and she presented the material in a very organized manner. Honestly, this very chill and not hard at all, just make sure to write a good final paper and participate occasionally and you will do well.
Very engaging and interesting topics, not much work at all. Professor was really nice/knowledgeable and always gave insightful feedback. Learned a lot about the romans too

I had an awesome time in her Archeology of the Roman World class. The class was taught online, and it was clear that she had spent so much time organizing it to fit an online format. Awesome lectures and interesting content too

Astrid is amazing. This class is a seminar, lots of writing and reading, but overall a great class. It is not a show up and pass, but she does give good feedback on your essays. Complete the essays, be prepared for presentations, participate, you'll be good. Take this class, you may learn something about yourself too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Asis is one of the sweetest professors at the hotel school and you can tell by how personal he makes lectures. He puts in the effort to know EVERY student and don't be surprised if he knows your name first day of class without introduction. The class is hard but put in the effort to do the problems before class and you will find it a lot easier.

You have to come to lecture prepared with the problems and cannot arrive late. He is strict, but he has his reasons and is very reasonable if you communicate with him. The tests are hard, but he curves them and if you redo the problems / go to OH you'll be fine. The median grade is an A- and the tests are super curved.

Asis is one of the best professors in the hotel school and he is incredibly fair. If you follow his instructions (i.e. participate in class and try the problems beforehand) you will easily do well. These bad reviews clearly come from people who wanted to get an A without putting in any effort. Also, he's super easy to reach if you have questions.
Asis is a great professor. You will learn a lot.

Exam questions are too flexible and he didn't give us enough materials to prepare for the exam (only limited 2-4 in-class exercises can be used to review before exams). Class participation is too strict and meaningless. Accounting class should focus more on helping students understand concepts, instead of penalizing them for not being active.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he would be a great prof if there were 48 hours in a day

He does not teach the material in a way that is productive. No one knows what is going on. The same man that has typos in nearly every assignment is in charge of grading our assessments - this is a problem when he marks a correct answer as incorrect, refusing to release an answer key after the assessment.

This class is probably one of the more difficult class that I've taken at Cornell but I definitely learned the most. Asis is the sweetest man ever. He is so accessible outside of class! You will have to grind (do hw problems over and over again for like 5 times) but if you put in the work, you'll do well. He also curves a lot.

The bad reviews come from ppl who didnt listen. We were to read and do homework before class so we could discuss in lecture. I did so and learned a ton. I participated more than anyone. It irked me that so many of my peers wanted an A handed to them when they failed to do what he asked. Do what the prof wants; they shouldnt bow to entitled hotelies

I really enjoyed taking Asis's class even though I did freak out in the beginning. His teaching style is different from many other professors as he really wants to help students to build up a critical thinking mindset. He has a lot of cool experiences and is willing to help students both academically and professionally.

I really enjoyed having Asis for Managerial Accounting. He is tough, but his class set me up for success in the rest of my classes in the Hotel School. He took the time to get to know everyone . I really appreciated how much he cared for his students, and he was always available for extra help (which really helped me succeed in this hard class).
you can tell he really cares about his students and gives tons of opportunities for OH. he wants his students to succeed past academics.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: the hw probs r different from the ones on the test bc the ones on the test require u to apply multiple topics, and many students are used to only being able to do the same types of q. however, he wants u to think like a manager, and u don't always get the same types of q irl. asis is very caring and u can tell he spends sm time on this course:)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I have only taken Asis for higher level classes so that's all I can speak towards, he reasonably expects preparation for class and it creates a great environment where we can go in depth. Mastering Strategy Execution is a small class and discussion based and Asis leading these discussions have been my favorite class taken at the Hotel School

Asis is a nice man, not a great professor. He puts a lot of effort into class and wants his students to understand it (e.g. asking students who are participating further questions to make them think) but this just ends up making student more confused. My best advice is read the textbook, teach it to yourself, and stop listening in class

I love Asis so much as a professor; he always took the time to hold extra office hours if you need it, and you can tell that he truly cares about his students and their future. Have an open mind!! Hes really a gem.

Was the absolute worst ... made me hate accounting so, so much. Get ready for 2 hours of homework before every class. He's also super disorganized, so you're also going to be confused throughout every class. Everybody I know complained about him. Prelim averages were 60-70 ish (he did curve, though). Would try to avoid this prof if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Taking care of students. It was hard at the beginning; however, when understanding his teaching style and the basic logic of the problem sets, the tests are not as terrible as I imagined. Really nice professor and will learn a lot.

Dont take his class,teaching style is such that he really doenst explain much in class. expect us to understand the concepts beforehand and he would just solve a problem based on the concept in class,says that the questions he would put in the paper would have never been seen by us before. Teach yourself the content. Only good is Curve, too many hw
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class concepts aren't too difficult, so as long as you practice the in class assignments and make sure you understand things conceptually, you will be fine for the exams. The workload can be pretty heavy, but he's a nice person and is accessible outside of class to answer questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Verbally harasses students and pushed all exams together so we would receive your last exam grade right before the next exam. Impossible to learn and prepare yourself. He refuses to teach, and instead walks through problems while answering them completely different from the questions asks. Broad questions mean missed points and he hates critiques.

Asis does not care to help struggling students and has taken away ALL outside resources. You know he's not a good teacher when the tutors AND the TAs can't even understand what this man is teaching. He does not teach you any fundamental principles so you are completely screwed for the exams so you are left to teach everything by yourself.

His teaching style just isn't suited for this course. He adopts a Socratic style which works for Master's programs and concept-heavy classes, NOT a math-heavy class like man. acc. He fails to teach the material that ACTUALLY matters; leaving students to fend for themselves. Love him as a person, but it's very easy to dislike him as a professor.

Asiss class is a struggle. Hes a very kind and fun-loving person but he is not an effective professor. Most of the material covered in exams are never gone over in class or homework. The exams always have low averages but he curves them so everyone can do decently. The lectures are hard to follow and youll have to teach yourself the material.

Gives insane amounts of hw and has no empathy for struggling students. Assigns an average of 5 assignments/week, and praises himself for giving you a "break" every few weeks and assigning 4 assignments, all WAY longer than normal. Doesn't follow the syllabus at all and won't teach any content in class. Yells at students after cold-calling them.
Don't take the class with him. Run away.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ashley is the best professor I’ve had at Cornell. She’s very relaxed and class is a nice atmosphere and the time passes quickly. She also encouraged me and made me feel confident in my writing for the first time whereas teachers in high school would only criticize.

Ashley is the best teacher Ive had at Cornell. Ill never look at reading the same way after taking her class. She starts from ground zero on how to analyze stories and then shows you how to use the various narrative elements as a springboard to write your own story. The only class this semester I actually enjoyed attending.
