Its early on in the semester but every class has been awesome. Im excited for the rest of the course. She breaks down the readings in a way that will sort of blow your mind. Shes also super hot and funny so that doesnt hurt either.

I absolutely loved coming to this class. Ashley is so caring and so funny. She makes you look at reading in a whole new way. She also teaches you actual strategies to get better at writing. The course isnt demanding per se but she makes you want to work hard and give her your best. I wish I could take it again!

Ive learned so much from this class. Ive liked reading and writing at a young age but at high school, English classes have been taught in a way that discourages that. Hand is caring and passionate about writing. Her class is a breath of fresh air. You will learn to become a much better writer in this class.

Ashley is one of the most caring profs at Cornell. Her prompts are broad, so you're really able to run with the assignments and do what you want with them to make it your best work. You'll get out of this class as much as you put into it. Ashley made me view literature in an entirely new and exciting way, and I'll forever have this class to thank.

Hands down the best teacher I've had at Cornell. You're lucky if you get into her section -- the class is pretty easy, but it's memorable and makes you look at the world differently. Assignments are pretty open-ended. Lots of freedom to do what you want!

She is so unbelievably kind, you can tell she actually cares about you as a person. I do find myself spending a lot of time on the assignments. The instructions can be sort of complex but she's a forgiving grader as long as you put in effort. It does take a while to get your papers back, but she gives great comments and is really encouraging.
She's charismatic and kind and keeps class interesting. Favorite prof so far.
worst professor at cornell
Most horrible teacher I've ever had. If you like a course, reconsider taking it if he's teaching.  He maybe nice to you, but when push comes to shove, he's a terrible human being from the soul.
The professor is really unhelpful and the assignments are way off the topics that are discussed during the class. Really unorganized class material.
The professors has difficulty in communicating the theory and also the home work is much more unorganized
I found the classes were not structured properly. The professor does not teaches the basics and in case you have a query , he is not able to explain the queries in a proper mathematical manner
take this class only if you have taken other ai classes before. instructor assumes you know the basics. i had hard time catching up.

Does not have the best teaching skills. But wonderful for research discussion related to class project. He comes up really quickly with examples to explain the hardest concept. Strongly recommended if interested in robotics. Best roboticist the Cornell has to offer.
I was so interested in this course prior to attending Cornell.Sad that I would not be taking this course again. The classes were vague and the professor has problems in communicating.
Classes were confusing and material used was not very relevant. Bad experience. Not going to take again

I had taken many courses in the AI vector at Cornell. This class used many algorithms and discussed applications to robotics. I really liked the way homeworks were designed that helped understand the material and how to apply it.

I really loved machine learning, and this class's applications on robots connected my theoretical understanding to reality. The lectures on Kalman Filters and Reinforcement Learning were fun, although it helped to prepare a bit in advance before the lecture.
Very helpful in class projects. Had fun!

The rant I just wrote for my course eval was double the size allowed here. Suffice to say Saxena is horrible. I had him for CS 6758 last semester and should have known better. Say away. 0/10 stars. Would not take again.
Easily, the worst professor I have ever had. He never gave a single helpful lecture or comment. He also doesn't listen to students...it's like talking to a wall.

He seems to be a good researcher, but he just cannot teach. He cracks pathetic jokes. Has problems while communicating, rather than sticking to slides, he wastes times around the blackboard. I agree with earlier reviews, probably not the best one Cornell has to offer, sadly not even average.

Jesus tap dancing Christ! I can't agree more with the previous comment. This guy is the worst professor I have had so far by a long shot. Lectures are useless, he does not know how to explain the material. He uses another prof.s notes, no textbook. HW is a huge time drain. Not helpful at all.
Worst professor at Cornell. No exceptions. Cannot lecture, test, produce homeworks, grade or use proper mathematical language well. The course is a timesink and waste.
I love him (I didn't read at all and never went to class, but I read SparkNotes before every test and that was enough!).

KEVIN ATTELL MY GOAT. Take ENGL 1102. This class is so much fun. It's basically just reading books written by Cornellians and talking about them with the professor. KA has so much background knowledge on the books and authors and his interpretations of the books are always so enjoyable to learn about. Exams are light. Paper is light. 11/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A passionate guy. Relaxed structure. Just do the reading (in 1102's case, read some fiction every night) and you'll be fine.

The lectures were minimally helpful, and Attell is at best a merely average reader of poetry. The main problem was his lack of enthusiasm. I was very excited about the course, but Attell did not make the experience worthwhile. The readings are hard (DON'T BUY the packet; ALL of it is free through the library or online) but the grading was very easy

Kevin was a great professor in Short Stories. He openly facilitated an environment where you could really explore your ideas and share them in discussion. I really enjoyed this class and the ability I had to expand my writing skills in a way that I had not had a chance to before. Would totally recommend. Also light homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Attell is one of my favorite professors at Cornell, and I enjoyed his class very much. It is challenging, but I have learned so much and gain so much confidence from his class. He is definitely an accessible person and willing to help. Its a class where you should be a perfectionist though.
Decent class. Relaxing. 3 papers, insightful, nice.

This is a guy you would WANT to find outside lecture. He cares about his students' experiences just as much as the lecture material. Although he cracks jokes and likes to make students laugh a lot, his anecdotes and rambles tie into class material, creating cohesive stories that teach the material at a competent and memorable level.

I took Dr. Ault's EAS 1330 and 1310 courses. Dr. Ault explains the material in a way that's easy to understand for both majors and non-majors. He offers plenty of extra credit and is overall a great professor. Easy A, definitely take him for distributions. He was also recently nominated for the CALS Chancellor's Award for Excellence in Teaching!

This review is actually for EAS 1300. He's one of the greats at Cornell. He wants all of his students to succeed, only ones that wouldn't are who to refuse to show to class. Take a class of his not only for a requirement, but if you need to reach 120 college credits. Lectures were awesome. Not much homework either. He is the GOAT

AWESOME PROF. Prof Ault understands most people are taking this class for distribution and doesn't try to make the class too hard. Genuinely, he just wants to make people understand the threat of climate change and need for action. Rewards people who come to class with extra credit opportunities. Tries to make lectures engaging and class not hard.

For an easy A class that fufilled two of the annoying Arts & Science distributions at once, Professor Ault understood the assignment. He knew most people didn't care about it and was taking the class because they had to, so he made the lectures interesting within that context. He was fun and gave tech breaks, absolute G!
Master T-Dog was the best teacher ever! Never afraid to bark - or to call people out for barking in the back! I was so happy to take this class: I met animals that are in my lifelong pack

I LOVED Toby and this class! Learned a lot about climate and Toby is the most passionate teacher I've had at Cornell! Class was very easy, as everything is take home (including tests). Everyone was treated equally (as if we were all dogs) and there were so many unique people in the class - I met lifelong people in my pack! Would recommend 10/10!
Professor Ault is endlessly kind and always striving to make lectures engaging, accessible, and easy to comprehend.
He doesn't what he is doing, nor do students have a clear expectations of what the class aims to give. He can mess up the Canvas site a million times while nobody really understands what's happening.

Great prof and a really interesting class! Professor Ault made an attempt to get to know students, and made an effort to ask about our mental health. He is very interesting and engaging, and the class has a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Most caring prof I have had so far at Cornell!

Incredible class, with an even more caring, knowledgeable, and engaging professor. The class is really easy, and Dr. Ault makes you actually want to learn the material regardless. 200 kids in lecture and he makes an effort to get to know everyone. Best experience with a professor!

Prof. Ault is very smart and definitely means well when planning out lectures for his students, but execution is very disorganized and poor. Hopefully this is a consequence of not being super experienced with teaching undergraduates and he works on this.
great professor, cares a lot about material and students learning it, which is really nice

One of the best teachers I have ever had in my life, both at and outside of college. If you are interested in screenwriting or even just reading and analyzing screenplays, take this course. Amazing lectures that he puts a lot of effort into preparing, and he brings in great guests from the film world. Accessible outside of class as well.
Great Professor! He always was bringing in cool people to help give us a sense of the field. Truly awesome class, would love to take another one like it in the future. 10/10

Prof. Austin Bunn is one of the best professors at Cornell, Screen & Story is one of the best classes at Cornell, BUT he sometimes isn't that nice of a guy. He pokes fun at students in class and makes the class laugh at them. He will also mock your opinion if he disagrees with it. He's incredible at his job, but when the joke is you, it's not fun.

Lacks professionalism needed from a screenwriting professor. Rude to students and out of touch with experiences outside of his own. Condescending and inexperienced in the subject that he teaches. Inconsistent when giving notes. Unqualified.

Intimidating but brilliant. workload is alright, BUT he holds the honor of being the first cornell prof who's ever denied me an extension (I'm a rising senior)... so don't expect a lot of flexibility.  still, I learned a LOT in Screenwriting and if you're lucky enough to get into the class, you're gonna get a lot out of it.

I took Intro to Dramatic Writing and can't wait to take Screenwriting with him next semester! Bunn is an amazing teacher, very accomplished, extremely talented, and incredibly funny! Our class became super close and I was actually extremely excited to start my hw when I returned to my dorm after class.

Well organized blackboard lectures, and course content is paced really well (I can easily keep up with writting my notes, and he takes time to review concepts from the prereq classes when needed). Not too much homework outside of class, and homework¬es are very representative of content on exams. Definitely knows his stuff. Great class
Prof. Avedisian is really nice. Do your part; you get good grade.

Lectures were organized.  Subject was interesting and relevant to my summer intern job.  Avedisian is passionate about heat transfer and clearly knows the material.  Good guy - reach out to him and you won't be disappointed.

One of the most boring professors in MAE. Tries to present the material from the book, ends up over-complicating everything, and failing miserably. Just read the book, at least it makes sense. He just likes the sound of his own voice. Preach.

Lectures were example based and not too difficult though presenting a more generic solution technique could have helped the clarity a bit. The textbook was only really useful for the summary formulas. Homeworks were fine, and the best part was that tests were open book/notes.

Avedisian is a really nice guy. He kind of has a grandfatherly air about him. But he expects a lot of heat transfer students- the material is definitely really hard, but he tries to make it make sense. The prelims were atrocious, though- study your butt off beforehand!
Prof. Avedisian is a fine professor and really nice guy. He is an excellent lecturer and shows a caring attitude to his students.

This was a great class mainly because of the professor.  Prof. Avedisian is a wonderful teacher. Clearly, he is smart and communicates difficult concepts easily.  Plus, he always showed a caring attitude.

Avedisian's a rambler, that's for sure. But he "keeps it real" as he's said on more than one occation. I don't know if I would have learned any less had I never attended class, but the book is very good and he puts all his lecture slides on the web. It's worth going just to hear him talk about "getting the rust done" on his Volvo.
Avedisian cares about his students and makes a strong effort to communicate.
One of the least helpful classes I have ever had.  I get the feeling that he's real smart, but just doesn't know how to apply it towards teaching.
Cares about his students, but the class was often very boring.

Professor Avgar cares more deeply for his students than virtually any professor I've had. He takes seriously the responsibility of teaching and is fully committed to teaching undergrads and grad students alike.
Ariel Avgar is an incredibly knowledgeable and engaging Professor. He is very helpful in office hours. Labor Relations can be dry at times but he made the class worth while. Overall great guy.
One of the best professors at Cornell

I love his lecture because he try to explain why you should learn concepts, properties, and theorems in the graduate students' point of view. Especially, he tried to make connection between probability and your research area, how to adopt what you learned from this course for your research. I got A, but I heard that he had tough grading policy.

Absolutely no learning in class, lectures are same to same content from text book. Exams r hard. Tough grading policy , professor does not make clear his grading policy he will talk in terms of mean and median , normalization if yo ask for grading criteria and will make you confuse. Better not to take this class ever. Professor is in USC now.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You won't like probability at all after taking this class. You would not learn anything in lectures, lectures are dull and boring, lecture notes are from book only (same content). Exams are very hard . Professor shows no pity even though nothing of that sort is taught in class as he ask in exams. Recommend, to avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probability is a very hard course and he made it harder. Does not give grades in exams and sets them too hard. His grading scheme is also too hard to get past - he expects you to get 85+ to get a B, which is very challenging given the nature of the subject. Not friendly at all.  Do not study under him. It is a disaster.

This class was great! The structure of this class made it easy to balance with other courses, reading, writing short discussions posts, and writing essays. The short stories were enjoyable. You will not regret this class.

She is an amazing professor who genuinely cares and respects each of her students! I enjoyed taking Creative Writing with her and our class discussions were always insightful and fun. She always encouraged us to share our own thoughts, ideas, and stories, and to know that our voice matters. I've learned so much more about writing, thanks to her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: amazing teacher. made me feel really heard and included in class; i am personally not very strong in english, but she made me want to try and want to raise my hand in class. she makes sure that everyone is engaged in class (it is not difficult to be, at all!) and is super accessible & flexible in office hours (they were over zoom, by appointment).

Ms. Ayaz was an amazing professor. She was very kind and professional and understood that students have other commitments outside of class. The feedback that she provided for each essay was extremely thorough and she truly shows how much she cares for each student.

Ms. Ayaz was a joy to have. Classes were very orderly and meaningful. She cared about us and even extended due dates when necessarily to accommodate the class. You will pass as long as we follow her reasonable grading criteria. Helped me develop as a writer. Always gave impactful and constructive feedback. Kind and always made me feel included.

Aye was the most amazing and inspirational professor I ever had. Her material is very hard - I struggled immensely with her material, but at the end of it all, I felt rewarded with a wealth of knowledge that has forever impacted the way I understand chemistry and biology. I felt that I had learned, rather than studied, organic chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof Aye is definitely one of the most intelligent professors that I have ever had, but she has a hard time slowing down and breaking the material down into helpful and informational pieces. She either teaches a concept in a way that is too simple or too complicated and then she tests on multiple concepts combined.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Aye is really challenging, but her lectures weren't entirely bad. There's a bit of a language barrier and she tends to focus on drugs/biological applications. SHE WILL TEST YOU ON THEM. She only gives answers to in-class practice problems during lecture, so make sure you show up ready to write really fast. Tests are rough but interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: When I searched in google for one of the concepts, I realized that it was an unproven mechanisms published on NCBI that she wanted us to know. I feel like if I master all the mechanisms she wants me to know I will be able to synthesize a new cancer curing drug or something by myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Aye is the worst avoid at all costs, try to take Dr. Ruttledge his class is not easy by any means. But, Dr. Aye is not engaging, her test involve unnecessary reading that further complicates orgo. Her test are horrible, at least in Ruttledge's class you are clear on instructions even though the problem may be really hard.

Professor Aye is definitely a bright individual who should be teaching Organic Chemistry, but teaches this Intro to Organic Chemistry class as though we have already taken her section of the class twice. The class overall is test heavy and those are what determine your grade. Professor Aye makes Dr. Ruttledge's tests look like middle school quiz
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is amazing! An exceptionally caring man and he brings that attitude with him to class every day. Papers and the exam are graded fairly. About 30 pages of reading each night which was not bad at all, and if you didn't actually read on time you were still in good shape. Definitely would recommend.

Professor Rana is an amazing lecturer - he has no notes but still presents information in such an engaging way. Also makes an effort to be accommodating and makes it a point to learn everyone's name and asks how you are doing. Assignments are not too bad especially if you go to office hours. One of my favorite government classes at Cornell!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've taken a few political theory courses before and none were as engaging and thought-provoking as Professor Rana's. He is an incredibly smart guy and makes the material so interesting! Essay prompts really make you think but they're fun. Attendance is mandatory, but I would've showed up to class even if it wasn't.

Following his lecture is like watching thriller movie. You think you know something, but it turns out that you don't. He teaches us a theory (or model) and its strengths very clearly, and in another session, he will open up the theory's weaknesses, and ask us to be wise in using it. A highly recommended course.

Got an A in his class and I still wouldn't take any other course with him. He is not a good professor and his concern for students is highly questioned. I wouldn't be surprised if the two previous comments were written by him since they seem identical.
wonderful and useful for real world application
Complete waste of time. Avoid at all costs.
Rude and obnoxious
Very kind and helpful, course was very useful for real world application
The most useful class I have ever taken in my entire time at Cornell
No Comments
Bitter, unhelpful prof, a shame to the CRP department.

Horrible lecturer. Inconsistent. His lecture is ok, but gudelines of the term paper are very unpredictable, which never showed up in the syllabus. Never plan ahead of writing a term paper, since he changes his plan very easily. Bad personality. Not helpful in office hour.
Very painful class
the least organized prof ever. you will get absolutely no feedback all semester and deadlines will constantly be moved around!!
Yeah - just read the other reviews. What an unfortunate joke of a class.
Very disorganized and unprofessional
THE WORST PROFESSOR AT CORNELL UNIVERSITY ! ! !
most unorganized and difficult class in ORIE, prof needs to make exams easier and actually grade them instead of waiting till after classes...
NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS!

It is currently November 24th... here is the fact pattern:

We have had 6 HWs due throughout the semester. 5 have been graded
1 Exam on 10/16, have not gotten it back
A final he said was 12/2, then said 12/4 and is now unscheduled for next week, with no practice 
A final project with no details, no due date
A final HW with no details, no due date

The class is pretty disorganized 😅. We have one more week of classes: still need Prelim 1 back from October😅, the final date is a mystery😅, project is due same day as final.. don't 
Know what project entails😅.Lecture content jumps around😅, some (quite a few) questions on Ed go unanswered😅. Honestly, I am scared😅

He's REALLY disorganized. We have not gotten our prelim 1 back from October. We don't know the date of the final (there's only a week left of class), our project is supposedly due the day of the final (we know nothing about the project), there has not been a single lecture where he goes in order. He avoids questions on ed he cannot answer. vibes 😃

Horrible prof. Worst I have had during my time at cornell. doesn't teach properly, doesn't post proper materials for the class, is absent or irresponsive half the time. Prelims are insanely tough and he misleads students by saying they are easy.
Amazing prelim! Hope everyone can try!

Released final project details two weeks before the final exam and decided to have a it due on the day of exam (with a presentation). Also absent and very irresponsive throughout the semester like bro u good
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very bad professor, and not responsive AT ALL. He never cares about his students, like posting midterm grades in December and not coming to classes several times. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS

Bad professor. Lectures are unorganized, and you must spend tons of time completing the HW. You probably have to read the textbook for the HW completion (or use ChatGPT if you want). Have to attend recitations and complete questions assigned. The final exam was harder than expected. Not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very bad teaching skills. Unorganized lectures. Most of the time, he got confused by his own questions. Expect a lot of homework assignments. Nothing useful/substantial taught in second half of the semester. I would recommend taking ORIE 5581 if you still want to take this course unless you want to earn extra 2 credits without any efforts.
Interesting course that turned out to be more helpful than I imagined
This whole course is an unorganized messy crap. The most unresponsive prof ever in my life ....... don't think anyone can beat him on this.
Really charismatic and extremely competent in complex mathematics.
Good amount of homework with the lecture modules, but literally the best professor and class ever. I had 0 background in anything stats, and he made it so easy and made me actually enjoy it.

Great guy, decent class. Basu tells good, interesting, content-relevant stories during lecture. Homework and tests tended to differ a fair amount, but he is explicit about what you need to know for exams. He's fairly receptive to student concerns, this is a good class to take.

LOVED PROF. BASU!!!! Take his class he was a wonderful professor who actually carried about his students. If you go to his office hours he is super helpful and ensure that you thoroughly understand the content. Intro to R was so great too! TAKE THIS CLASS

King. He is so funny, caring, and just a great professor. His lectures can be a little boring if you're not interested in data science, but he finds ways to keep you engaged. The quizzes and homework were easy and the group project would have been if I had better partners (choose wisely). I looked forward to going to lecture every day.
the class was light (very fair grading and easy exams). he was lowkey funny too

Great teacher, paced the class extremely well in a combination of in-class lectures and out of class Canvas modules. There is a participation grade with occasional in class/in lab polls, but is explained clearly in the syllabus. As someone who took Stats during high school, Professor Basu brought back familiar material in an easy to understand way.
Really nice and funny. It was his first semester teaching but class was really easy as a non-STEM person. Def take for requirement
very easy class and not mandatory to listen to lectures, and great caring professor who checked if students felt stressed or not!

Professor Basu is funny and caring and makes an intro STATS class easy! He teaches in R, and assumes you do not have experience. The class contains 3 prelims, a final group project, weekly homeworks, and preparation videos. The work is very doable, and there are a lot of resources if you need help! A great professor, and even better person!

Presents course material in a very organized way so that it builds on itself. Exams were reasonable, labs were interesting, and provided a good introduction to digital logic. Recorded lectures helped with exam reviews. Used Ed discussion actively to answer questions. Prof. Batten was a great lecturer, and I would take another class with him again.

GOAT of the ECE department. Still developing the course and it changes a lot year to year, but best lectures in the ECE department and really fair exams. Labs are a decent amount of work but interesting enough.

Batten is the GOAT. He clearly cares about his students, helps out during lab sections, is a fair grader, answers ed discussion posts 24/7, and most importantly is an engaging + comprehensive lecturer.

Professor Batten was so good at explaining things. He talks fast and has a passion for what he's teaching. I enjoyed his lectures and the class in general. The class is quite heavy though, so would not recommend taking it with a heavy workload.
You need to take this class if you are at all interested in Chip Design. Prof. Batten is a great guy. Extremely well organized and fair with grading.

The best lecturer I've had at Cornell so far! Really clear, organized, and enthusiastic, very responsive and open to questions, and while assignments/tests can be difficult it's in a way that stretches and challenges you instead of bewildering you. Wayyyy better than CS2110.

Professor Batten is hands down the best professor I've had at my time at Cornell. You can see how passionate he is about what he teaches, and he gives so much support as long as you put in just as much effort. It's easy to score well in this class but you need to put a lot of time into it. Lots of emphasis on the reports.

Professor Batten was a great professor who taught material clearly and had good organized lectures; I probably got a better understanding of data structures/algos from ECE2400 than CS2110. Also cared about his students' mental health and pushed back assignments if needed.

One of the best professors I've had at Cornell! I'm from another engineering major, took this class for fun. Great lectures, super responsive, you can tell he really enjoys teaching Coursework is reasonable, there's clear criteria for getting a good grade, and you're not curved relative to other students.

Hands down one of the best professors at Cornell. Although some of the reports are rough, you can always seek help at his office hours or his great TAs. I extremely recommend that ECEs take ECE2400 instead of CS 2110.
One of the best professors in the Engineering department, if not Cornell. If you pay attention in class, you will do well for sure. Only hard part was the long lab reports we had to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: His lecture is great and you do need to put effort to study

Great professor who really goes in depth to make sure you understand each topic he teaches. He's always accessible outside of class and gives helpful feedback on exams/homework assignments. Pretty tough grader and assignments are challenging, but you'll learn so much from this class.
best professor of all time

Batten is simply one of the best professors at Cornell. He is well prepared before every lecture and explains concepts very well. Video-notes are still very helpful. Homework is  long and difficult but you can learn a lot. Project can be challenging, but Batten will help you find your bug. He is as dedicated a professor as they come.

One of the best professors I have ever had (I am a Master's student whose undergraduate institution is not Cornell). He is funny, he knows his stuff really well. He is extremely willing to help students learn. He explains concepts remarkably well. Very enjoyable class. He is tough on grading though.

He is an awesome Professor. He helps us in learning every concept by giving a real-time analogy. All his assignments help us in strengthening our knowledge in all of the important concepts. He makes us approach every problem from a different perspective. We are confidently able to talk about design trade-offs after attending this course.

Hands down one of the best professors in the ECE dept. Class is challenging but the effort from the prof to help out, in class, in his office or on the online forums makes you an expert in his subject. Explanations and notes are clear and always encourages constructive discussions! Labs are hard and do require time, but you'll be proud of the work!
Turkish is cool :)
Goat. Just the Goat.
She is a really good and understanding teacher. Usually a very small class (mine only had 4 people). One of the easiest languages in the school... highly recommend.
take turkish!!

Should take Pubpol 2301 in the spring. Prof Avery is very nice, but the lectures consisted of slides with outdated statistics and videos. She is not very involved as the undergrad TAs do essentially everything. Long and difficult group project takes up most of the semester.

A very well-respected professor, but I wouldn't necessarily recommend this class. Lectures are required for exams, but Avery sometimes goes on tangents and mixes up statistics that are on the slides. Exams are weighted very heavily and often require knowledge of specific figures and statistics, but the curves are fair. Exams are hard but manageable

Professor Avery runs the course much like a high school teacher might. She and the TAs care deeply about student success and are very particular about content and matching public policy analysis formatting. It is a Brooks intro course, after all. Classes are fairly large but the TAs are approachable and kind. It's a hard class but I recommend.

+
Interesting content 
Class Dinners 
-
TAs are clicky 
Avery had many backhanded remarks 
No leniency granted for extreme personal circumstances
Spiteful 
*
Do readings, as many example cases are on the prelims 
Understand graphs from slides 
Record prelim review sessions,slides notpost
Do not take this class if you already have a heavy work load

Amazing professor. The class is very difficult, but it is rewarding. She is also a hard grader. 

BEWARE the TAs. The tall class of ‘27 one is arrogant, full of himself, and only there to impress her.

avery is honestly one of the worst profs i've had at cornell. I took the class in 2019. I hope she's changed. discusses and examines policies in class while leaving out factors such as poverty, race, etc. I recall one time she said the reason food stamps are only for food rather than cash is b/c impoverished people would use it for drugs over food.

Professor Avery is always willing to chat in office hours and is caring . However there's a clear disconnect within her class. This class felt like a predatory weed  out class and the TA team was insufferable, egoistical, and narcissistic. Her exams also felt predatory as very minuscule details were expected. I recommend the spring class.

Prof. Avery is a brilliant, kind professor and is objectively strong in the department. But this *introductory* course felt like more a weeder for incoming Brooks students (of which only 75 exist), and was ultimately characterized by the excessively hard exams and cliquey, self-important TAs. Take the spring class if you want your money's worth.

Prof Avery is a good lecturer and the class itself is actually so interesting! Tests are ALL memorization which makes it really easy to study. There are 2 really long and grueling assignments (1 individual and 1 group) and while they are SO much work, the average is always an A. If you just do the work, your grade will be fine.

Avery is a brilliant lecturer, but sometimes moves too quickly through slides and topics. I learned a ton in the course, but it's difficult. The prelims are strangely worded and the fictional state of “New Avery” is just self-aggrandizing enough to be a little funny. 2301 takes itself way too seriously- beware of power-tripping UNDERGRAD TAs.

This class was extremely difficult/time consuming, but it was also extremely rewarding. I felt like I truly grew as a student and learned a ton about public policy. Prof. Avery is really nice and it's clear that she cares about her students. TAs put in a lot of effort and they create a great environment in section. 2 prelims + 2 research papers.

Avery is literally a perfect professor. Her work is challenging but incredibly rewarding and she is incredibly nice outside of class (even if she can be a harsh grader). However, her TAs are a completely different story. Specifically, two of her Class of '27 TAs are arrogant and egotistical and love the power trip of being a TA.

Attendance policy was completely wack, no drops and will count against you unless you tell them way in advance (even if you become sick). The course was very difficult but worth it. Professor was sweet but also biased in her content. I enjoyed the content and the flow! Discussions were boring though

This is a difficult class, but you get a lot out of it. Tests are pretty hard and require alot of studying, but they do get significant curves. Professor is nice and is very knowledgable.  TAs are also really great and gave a lot of help on assignments and test prep. But if you don't pay attention and work hard, you're definitely going to struggle
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Caring professor and gives engaging lectures. Exams are tough but rewarding. She's a lenient grader but sets her grade brackets pretty high. Felt like I did A quality work but because she does't round a 93.6% remains an A-. Definitely deflating and makes me reconsider taking a class with her again because in any other class that would be an A.

The most caring Professor I've had at Cornell! Concepts covered in class are foundational for any PAM Major, and the projects are a decent amount of work but prepare you very well for future PAM classes. Lots of resources to help you succeed (she posts 2 years of past exams, sample papers/presentations and is super accessible outside of class).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Avery is amazing! This class is one where you get out of it what you put into it. It's definitely time consuming, but extremely relevant and interesting. Grading isn't very harsh, but you need to do the work in order to pass. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor is really organized and is a good lecturer, learned a lot about different federal policies. People say the class is a lot of work, but you're given a lot of time to actually do the assignments. Grading was very fair - if you put in the work you will get an A.

This was not an easy class, but at the end, the median was an A or A-. It was a great way to start my freshman year, I feel like I learned a ton and also learned how to study in college. The TAs are really attentive and helpful (and chill since they're undergrads). Had to study a lot for the prelims, but they got curved up by 15%.

Nice person, but I hated this class. Took it last semester and it made me drop the PAM major. She expects you to memorize random facts + statistics from lecture slides that are just almost impossible to memorize. Even though I got high A's on the homeworks, papers, and group project, I ended with a B+ just because I got mid 80s on prelims.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you have to, and even if you have to I would recommend against it. This class led me to drop the PAM major entirely. The lectures were so dense and she would make you recite random definitions word for word on the prelims. This is the most intense class I've ever taken and the amount of work assigned is absurd.

I would not recommend this class even to my worst enemy. There are two major papers that require you to read so many academic papers - more than what you should be reading in your whole freshman year. The TAs are condescending, forcing you to go to a library even when you are going through personal matters. This class will make you question PAM.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can basically learn everything in this class online as the content has barely changed since she has started teaching. The assignments and exams are unnecessarily difficult and overall the class is not engaging. You have to take it to be in PAM which makes things even more stressful.

Professor Avery is super knowledgeable in her field and really cares about her students. That said, this is a work heavy class, much more than a normal entry-level class. The TAs are great, but don't expect to do well if you don't show up to class and especially do the readings, as they definitely appear on the tests. Super informative professor.

Her class was a lot of work. The individual and group papers required way too much time and effort for an introductory level class. Had to study a decent amount for the exams but they are similar compared to previous years which made things easier. Required class for PAM majors. Avoid if your are not PAM major because it is too time consuming.

Professor Avery is approachable and knowledgable! The class is a lot of work, but manageable. Prelims are memorization and she does look for specific wording in the answers. Lectures are interesting and make you think. She tests readings heavily and they've been cut down, so take notes while you read! GPP groups are hit or miss. TAs are amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: She loves what she does, is a strong lecturer, and obviously cares about her students. The course itself has a LOT of information (most of it in lecture) but as long as you go to class and pay attention/take notes, you'll be fine for the tests. Grading is also fair/easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: There is a difference between hard & unfair. Avery's class is hard- intense, but rewarding. Prelims and papers require devoted studying but concepts are crucial for future coursework. She provides multiple office hours and extra credit. She cares so much for her class and students- she memorizes every students' name. 2300 affirmed why I chose PAM.

Prof Avery is fantastic! She really cares about her students and is a good lecturer. Her course does involve a lot of studying and essay writing, but it is 4 credits and most people end up with an A or B. TAs are very involved, the class is interesting and focuses on current events, and is overall a great intro to the PAM major.
gpa is based on socializing skills. tons of hw.
All of the comments below are true.
The prelims for PAM 2300 or pure memorization and the class is simply a ton of work. Prelims combined with the policy papers take up an enormous amount of time.

Professor Avery goes too fast through the slides, doesn't leave time for questions, gives Herculean projects, the tests are memorization of material you'll never use again or could look up easily, and the TA's form a cult of personality around her. Avoid this class if you can.

This class was not fun. I am definitely switching majors next semester. I don't like the way this class is run, really encourages students to kiss up to her to try to be come a ta or research assistant. Feels more connection based than merit. Most of the content from lectures was useless. she made a point to take attendance after a break or project

She's nice, but her class is the worst I've ever taken. Material isn't difficult at all, but there's an obscene amount of memorization. Prelims are killerher questions are poorly worded & ambiguous and you get points off for not phrasing things exactly how she wants, and for not including things she didn't even ask for. 0/10 wouldn't recommend.

The GPP was the worst assignment I've ever done, especially since a member of my 3-person group did nothing. Prof. Avery should have mid-semester group evals to weed out free riders. Lectures were dry and hard to follow, prelims were absurdly difficult and she took off points for not mentioning things that were not asked as part of the question.

Hated this class. Interesting material, but her teaching was terrible. Obscene amount of work outside the actual class. Not accommodating & expects u to prioritize her class over others. Narrow-minded in that she can't see how less-privileged ppl might b affected by policies. 2 other PAM majors I know switched out of the entire major b/c of her.

The actual material for this class isn't particularly difficult, but the way that it is presented in lecture is confusing and hard to follow. The group project took up a ridiculous amount of my time (easily 80+ hours over the course of 2 months) and the prelims were hard- average raw score was a D for both of them, but they're scaled to a B.

Useless readings. Killer prelims, b/c there's so much material & b/c the way she words questions makes it hard to know what she wants. No final, but a group project. Thinks her class is the most important & schedules mandatory events over ur other classes. Hardest class I've taken in two years. Lectures are 60+ slides long & convoluted. Great TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class has so much potential but Prof Avery makes it the worst course at Cornell. Her slides are poorly executed--each powerpoint is between 60 and 70 slides, lacks structure, full of text, and she flies through them. Her class is scattered with no focus, and there is endless useless and over-tested dense reading (lack focus/meaningfulness)

She's a wonderful person, but she flies through hr lecture slides that no student can actually catch up with what she's trying to teach. This class is a LOT of work. I feel like I did learn a lot, but because of the fast pace of the class, I don't think I have retained much. If you want to learn about policy (and turn cynical), I recommend taking.

I always got the sense Prof. Avery was talking down to us  while it is a freshman-heavy course, it isn't the first exposure to college work for a lot of us. Her lectures contain a lot of material. The group paper was absolutely awful and allowed for a ton of free riding, which was ironic since she taught about the negatives of that in lectures.

Best class I've taken so far at Cornell. Material was interesting and Prof. Avery was engaging. Prelims/final were tough to study for (lots of memorization) but if you put in the work and studied a few days in advance they were fine. TAs are incredibly helpful. Do the extra credit. I think class average was around A-/B+ range.

Incredible educator concerned about the practical application of her teaching and well being of her students.  There's quite a bit of group work and assignments, but it's manageable if you pace yourself.

Her lectures are pretty fast-paced. Her powerpoints are quite dense, but she flies through them. Fortunately, she does upload all of her powerpoints online. Very helpful, but the material is quite difficult and heavy.

Not as great a class as everyone says. A huge tease: seemed interesting at beginning of semester but got more and more boring. Avery is a nice person and good communicator, but has way too much text on her powerpoints and isn?t all that engaging. You?ll do fine though. Papers aren?t too bad and tests are lecture-based with huge curves. No final!

Prof. Avery is an outstanding professor. She really shows interest in her students. Even made it a point to remember everyone's name. Be sure to keep up w/ the readings to the best of your ability and go over slides for exams. She is always willing to help if needed. A very interesting class and she has amazing TAs.

Study the powerpoints. They are the majority of what's graded. The readings are too intensive...you can get by if you only do some of them. Short policy paper is hardest assignment of the year. All group projects are automatic A's. Avery is a very nice teacher and is very clear! Love that accent! TA's are great too.

Very good prof. She gets to know each student's name, which is quite impressive. She also holds plenty of office hours and picks outstanding TAs who are knowledgeable in the field. I'm not a PAM major (or anything close to it), but I found the class very informative and a good portrayal of what an ivy league course. Do the readings and go to class!

i took this class after reading all the comments here but honestly i don't really think this class is as big of a deal as some on this site has said. it was good, but not the best class ever. the professor talks very fast and very broadly about many topics so you don't feel like you learned that much. TAs bascially show films in sections.
ok
Very good teacher.

you will definitely work hard in this class but all the material is interesting.  professor avery never misses a lecture and she takes attendace.  her ta's are very well trained and helpful.  the prelims are curved a lot.
Professor Avery was really interesting and her tests were long, but curved pretty high. It was a lot of work for a PAM class, but that's not saying too much. You need to do the reading though.

Professor Avery is the best professor I have had at Cornell, and this is the most incredible class/experience I have had here as well.  She learns the name every student in the class and cares about how everyone does. Lectures are interesting and the class is just completely satisfying.
Her lectures are pretty interesting (+ mandatory) Definitely harder than spring semester PAM230. . .but it was worth all the effort

This is the best class I have ever taken. I have never worked so hard in my life, and I would do it again in a second. I learned more from Professor Avery than I have learned in all of my other classes combined. You will have to work, but it is an incredible experience.

You will work very hard in this class, but as a professor she's very nice and friendly. The tests are ridiculous, but she does this in order to curve it. Work ahead of time on your papers. Love your TAs because they can help you out a lot.

this class is a full time job. it should be a 5 credit class. it's kind of really boring and the prelims are abs. horrendous. but she's a good teacher, v. friendly, helpful, nice. she knows everybody's names which is kind of creepy.  great teacher****ty class
Great Prof, very friendly and approachable but will work you hard.
She is an amazing professor, she'll work you harder than you've ever worked in your life but you will learn so much from her. She's always willing to help you.
No Comments
No Comments
shes so nice, works you to the bone, but it prepares you for the future, really learn alot and tests your limits.
No Comments

Avery is awesome. Everyone says shes the best teacher but you don't get it till taking her class. Although you may not appear to be doing well in the class at first, she fixes that for you by the end of the semester (easier quizes come later, gives an A on every group project = 25% of your grade)
No Comments

Avery makes you work, maybe harder than you've ever worked, and her anal retentive attention to detail might buckle the weak at heart.  She is a huge fan of group projects, is a sucker for presentations requiring business attire, and has clout within CU.

Very warm and friendly.  Excellent lecturer and actually takes an interest in her students...maybe too much interest.  Her method of picking TA's is a mystery.  Some are blatantly incompetent.  Must be something going on behind closed doors.

she is AMAZING! she ask alot from her students, but it is all well worth it. i learned so much, and people tend to do well in her classes (I also took PAM 230 w/ her). Her classes always have the same format, 2 prelims, indiv. paper and group project.
No Comments
interesting class, but too much work for a 3 credit class.
She is an excellent teacher, but expects a lot from the students. Although she can be tough at times I learned so much from her class, and a lot of it was stuff I will actually use in the future.
No Comments
pretty hot for a 50 year old...can sometimes be really fake or have multiple personality disorder...very intense but dedicated to teaching.  Be wary of the ****y side.

Dozier is a pretty good professor. Teaches almost directly from the textbook, but nothing negative other than the fact that lectures can get dry and the lack of slides. However, he is very articulate and attempts to make the class fun. 1920 is naturally a very difficult class so make sure to be on top of things.

Professor Dozier is a very easy to understand lecturer with neat chalkboard notes. The lectures aren't the most exciting, but I recommend going anyway because by paying attention and taking notes, you'll save yourself a lot of time on the HW. 1920 is a hard class with hard exams, but if you do the HW, you will be pretty well prepared for the tests.

Despite his approach leaning more formal and conceptual, lectures are full of valuable information and problem-solving frameworks/workflows, and clear to follow as long as you concentrate in class. Prof does a great job giving you physical intuition for concepts and is open to questions. The course textbook is great as a supplementary resource.
Lectures were boring and followed the textbook almost exactly.
Very boring

Note: I took multi at an extension school and retook it.
Lectures uninteresting and exactly follows textbook examples instead of his own material. HW not bad, but office hours necessary and carried by goat TA. Prelims + tests have some tricky problems, but overall fair if you study well. Didn't provide practice for prelims, but did so for final.

Super interesting class. Prof Basu is very knowledgeable in this field and he is very passionate about teaching it to others. The problem sets are optional are but definitely helpful for preparing for tests. The TAs were very nice too.

The professor was funny and sweet. Lectures were good if you were paying attention, but sometimes they were very boring, and it was not easy to pay attention. Lectures were a bit all over the place. The class was not too difficult and the curves were generous

Easily one of the most respected professors at Cornell. One of the most famous living game theorists on Earth. Lectures are full of anecdotes from time at World Bank and Indian government. Extremely interesting class that is mostly logic based with almost no homework. While difficult, very rewarding. Highly recommend for a 3000-level elective.

Basu is an amazing professor -- he uses anecdotes from his experiences at the World Bank and at the Gov't of India! I loved his lectures and it really forced me to think differently about problems as well as more strategically. I found myself reading the optional material. Great class and prof; one of Cornell's best. The right amount of challenge.

Great lecturer, but after the first prelim I realized I could skip every class and just cram from the textbook before the exams. Extremely easy course, though I had some familiarity with game theory and come from a more cs background. The course was really interesting, and I found myself reading some of the optional material out of interest.

Able to give informative lectures with no notes or slides. It's honestly impressive how he's able to give an interesting and engaging presentation straight from his mind. There is little to no homework so your entire grade is based on tests but they are open note.
Easily the best professor I have had at Cornell. His lectures are engaging but prelims and exams are rather difficult.
He's the best.

Phenomenal lecturer. Draws from his wealth of experience to give some truly fascinating examples. The class has no homework at all - your entire grade is based on your exam grades, and the exams are quite easy.

Really interesting content and a really cool professor. He tells a lot of interesting stories in class, but his lectures tend to be very disorganized. Unless you're paying attention 100% of the time, you can easily get lost. If you plan to take this class but don't have a lot of time to dedicate to it, TAKE IT PASS/FAIL.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, has wonderful stories. The class material is hard and there aren't enough things that you can be graded on. The TA's were ok at explaining. What he taught in class was very different from p-sets and VERY different from exams. Beware of that. Otherwise, awesome guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Disregard the comments pertaining to the intro econ classes... that is a different Basu. Very nice guy and most engaging lecturer I've ever had, but in-class examples are often filled with errors and exams are wayy different from problem sets. Highly recommend taking this course S/U

Really disorganized in the beginning ... engaging lecturer. However, the grading for exams is brutal as it is either right or wrong. If the algebra is wrong, but the right steps are used ... it is wrong. Answer keys don't show steps. Final is 60% so watch out for that which is atypical for the states. I would recommend taking this pass/fail

Writes down the wrong numbers so often that the students have to correct whatever he writes on the board. Notes are unorganized and does not a good job explaining the concepts. Takes forever to post the solutions to the problem sets.
Great lecturer, makes the material very interesting.  A bit unorganized in his lectures.  Difficult but fair tests.  Brilliant guy.
This is the most interesting class I've taken at Cornell.  I highly recommend it.  The lectures are interesting and the professor doesn't try to stress you out grade wise.

Without a doubt one of the best professors at cornell. He is a genius, but conveys the material in a manner that isn't very difficult to follow. Very funny in lecture. The final exam was stupid hard though, but everything is heavily curved, and he is approachable in office hours.

This class had very little assigned work - 2 prelims, 2 problem sets, and 1 final worth 50% of your grade. A very clear, funny, and brilliant lecturer (he worked with John Nash!). However, he made the final exam stupidly hard. Never had to actually think so hard for an exam...be careful, this course requires PLENTY of deep hard thinking.
Great professor... there is hardly any calculus unlike a previous rater described.  One of my favorite classes.
AMAZING PROF! HILARIOUS LECTURES!
Best economics class in the department, as well as best professor!  Makes class fun and interesting.
He made the class. His test are very fair and his grading/testing policies are very generous.
Great lecturer, very entertaining.  367 course is very easy -- if you're looking for a good survey of game theory, it's perfect; if you're looking for more complicated analysis, maybe not.
Hands down best professor in the Economics department! Clear, engaging, exciting teaching. Clearly a man who is at the top of his game.
Possibly the best course and best professor I've had at Cornell.

If you aren't that good at calc... STAY AWAY!  he told us calc would not be necessary... that is a lie. As soon as the A/D period is over, he threw more intergrals at me than I knew what to deal with. Interesting class, but have math to back you up.

EXCELLENT lecturer (though I'm ECE and ECE profs sucks collectively in lectures). I didn't take many notes and I didn't need to. I just listen then go home and read. Concepts get harder, so ask questions. Make SURE you understand the material, because his exams all ask you to apply the concepts.

Brilliant man. You MUST take his class. One of the funniest and most entertaining professors you will ever encounter (also coming from a senior). Also very well known in the field so worth having experienced his class. Can't say enough good things about him and his class. TAKE IT!
The last review was a little harsh. The course does get harder but it's not completely unmanagable. FANTASTIC lecturer and an utterly brilliant man.

Don't let the easy beginning of the course fool you,   this course is HARD! Plus, Prof Basu has very bad handwriting which makes note-taking a chore. He also seems reluctant to hold office hours even though 75% of the class appeared utterly confused.
Love him. Very interesting, good lecturer, and great concept of when economics does not always apply
Awesome prof.  Very helpful.  Interesting material.

Basu is probably the best lecturer in the Econ dept (coming from a senior). He is an incredibly intelligent man and can make the prelims challenging, but he will keep you interested in the class...definitely take his game theory class.
No Comments
Fun, but hard course.  Suggest calculus.
fun teacher. easy A. intresting material
No Comments

grading wasn't very clear. the class consists of lectures with in-class mini quizzes and group projects and a final solo project. it seems like they are trying to implement a curve on this class now. my progress in the class was on track for an a and then the final grade was decided by some arbitrary process (lower than it should be)

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS (2475). She makes attendance mandatory and there are quizzes during each lecture. Grading criteria is super unclear, I didn't receive above an a- on a single group project and some even got c's. I got an A on the final and ended up with a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Belot is not a great instructor. Unclear grading criteria. Constantly forces us to put away laptops mid class. Attendance mandatory to do daily quizzes. Intro-level economic concepts, learned nothing new. Imposed a negative curve for the final grade (70% of my average was an A-, but got a B+ in the class). DO NOT TAKE! NOT WORTH IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes offered at Cornell. The grading criteria on her stuff makes no sense and they try really hard to force a distribution in the class. The TAs are not helpful and the professor isn't great I honestly learned nothing all class. It's one of those classes you take thinking it's gonna be easy and it ends up being a ton of work

This course is very easy from an economics perspective. The professor obviously cares about the material, but since lectures and assignments are not related, students do not pay attention. Would recommend as an econ elective, but course got bumped down to a 2000-level. Easy, chill professor and chill class where most students get As. Little work.

Don't be deceived by those ppl who give 5 - the average for this course is B+. Don't let this course ruin ur life. Spent a substantial amount of time on this course, but the grading criteria were unclear, making it hard to understand expectations. The final grade is disproportionate to the work required.

Underrated prof. Lectures are very clear and easy to understand. Attendance is optional but make sure to go because there are so many concepts that make sense once he explains them in class. Definitely the harder man econ professor but there is a generous curve applied at the end of the course. Dedicate ample time and effort into psets and studying

Leyden was a great professor. His lectures were clear and engaging, and he was very easy to reach outside of class. TAs had office hours frequently and were very helpful for problem sets. The exams were difficult but fair, and going to all lectures and reviewing problem sets helped. Leyden is also very understanding and clarifies any confusion.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Most students who do not do well typically don't show up to class. The prelims can be difficult, but the class is curved. Also, the prelims have parts that are very similar to some problem-set questions. If you show up to class, do the problem sets, and study or go to review sessions, then it is reasonable to get an A/A-

Leyden is an amazing professor. He cares for his students, and if you talk to him he is very understanding. His class is very difficult and I felt like I wasn't going to pass it, however, it is designed for you to understand it and to think outside the box. If you like econ, take him, if not, take Terry. Curve is very helpful for his class.

One of the worst professors in Dyson. Leyden tries as hard as possible to make his students fail; incorrect/vague lectures, dry, and (very) arbitrary grading. Lectures are useless and mostly irrelevant to exams. Going to TA OHs and learning concepts on your own is enough to get an A. Huge mistake to take his class over Terry's, who is much better!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Leyden has a dry humor and a fair sense of grading. To do well in this class you have to understand the material and not memorize it. The TAs and professor give plenty of opportunity for 1-on-1 sessions and office hours. Although some people find this class hard, it is one of the most straightforward classes in Dyson. Recommended!

Some people love Leyden some people hate him. I personally thought his class was extremely interesting, but it is definitely geared towards people who are very naturally smart/good test takers (I believe tests are 70% of your grade). The class rewards students who don't work that hard but are very naturally intelligent
If you go to OH, you will ace the class. He is clear about what is on the prelim. Very patient with students.

Ngl, hard class. Relatively tough material, but definitely work-thru-able. Leyden has tons of office hours and is flexible about meeting. Lectures can be boring but you learn cool stuff occasionally. Prelims are much harder than problem sets and limited practice questions given. Take advantage of OHs and ask questions. Super patient guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Made the class harder than it needed to be. And graded super hard. Would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment:
Worked so hard for this class only for his grade breakdown to required a 97 for... not an A+, no, but a regular old A.  

I used no AI, I slaved away over this class, and then I get an A- because too many people did well.

If this grading scheme was made clear to me in the beginning, then I would have not taken this class. 

96 = A-

Amazing lectures with clear explanation. Very caring and approachable professor. High scoring class. The class has become very popular over the years. This fall has around 225 students. I highly recommend this course if you want to get started with robotics.
Do not take his foundations of robotics class...
Seems like prof didn't care about the class too much.  He taught from PowerPoint, which made class extremely boring.  Also didn't cover all class material--didn't even touch antennas!
Clarity of thoughts and good teaching skills makes him my favorite prof
He is awesome
Whether you like him or not, you can't deny the fact that he is so smart! His lectures are pretty inspiring as well.
Wow, I couldn't disagree with the first two more!  This class teaches nothing!
what the previous poster said was nonsense. horrible course.

Prof. Bhave is among the top teachers in Cornell ECE. He really puts effort into his lectures, making sure that everyone understands the fundamentals. The topics are always interesting and useful. And he's damn hot, which makes coming to class so early in the morning bearable. ;)

One of the best professors that I have had! Full points.. HWs for half the course are constructive and help us understand the material better.. and an end term project for the remaining half helps us do something of our own interest. If you plan to take ECE 432 take it under him.

His class is relatively easy. Participation in class lectures is graded as well as in labs (mostly field trips to surroudning ag facilities). Super chill class the exams are not hard at all as long as you study. He might not be the best at responding on emails but he genuinely cares about his student's success.

Good professor but his tests are hella difficult and u'll probably fail if you do not have prerequisite knowledge on plant sciences. His tests are super specific don't listen to him when he says that it will cover the exam broadly...he will NOT. The only good thing is that tests do not make up the majority of the grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is a super kind, knowledgeable, and funny professor. He is very clear in outlining the expectations for grading criteria in the course, and gives ample time for assignment submissions. Class is entertaining, informative, and interactive; a great course for anybody with interest in plants, regardless of your major. He's a great professor!

Dr. Miller is incredibly respectful and kind. Although the 1101 class is mandatory for many of the people taking it, I'd still highly recommend it, or any other taught by him. Dr. Miller works hard to accommodate the needs of his students. Overall, Dr. Miller is a very funny and relatable guy who made learning enjoyable.

Dr. Miller is incredibly kind, caring, and intelligent. All the material in his class (PLSCI1101) is presented clearly, and as long as you attend lectures, you will do great in this course. I would recommend anyone to take this class (as long as Dr. Miller is teaching it)--even if you have zero interest in plant. He is a wonderful professor!
Great guy, interesting lectures
Prof. Miller is a great professor and a genuinely caring person. Made lectures engaging and always open to questions and re-explaining concepts.
Just a genuinely nice guy, very knowledgable, answers all questions, very chill about deadlines and gives a lot of small graded work to spread the grade out. Midterm and final were very fair.
Professor Miller is a great instructor. He's very interactive with students and makes the lecture engaging and interesting. Very approachable and humorous.

Bill Miller is an amazing professor and person. With anecdotes and other funny comments, he makes lectures interesting and engaging. The labs are very enjoyable, as we get to see firsthand different plant science research taking place at Cornell. I would highly recommend this class to anyone, even if you don't have a background in plant science.

Great professor and loves to joke around. Someone you can have an actual conversation with about a variety of topics not just tulips. The first half of the class is spent learning materials and the second half is just guest lectures. There is a group project at the end of the semester that is equal to the amount of 2 prelims but the grading is easy

I thoroughly enjoyed my time in PLSCI1101. Bill is a fantastic professor who genuinely cares about his students. He is a down to earth guy and clearly passionate about his field of work. Bill is always willing to work with students to aid in their success in the class. I experienced zero stress in this class and learned so much about plant sciences

Bill Miller is an awesome professor. Lots of anecdotes and keeps the discussion flowing throughout class. He is very knowledgeable in his field and has a lot of info and experience to offer in all things greenhouse-related. The Wednesday labs are particularly fun as you go into the greenhouses and grow your own flowers!

This was Professor Miller's first year teaching this course and it greatly showed. He was very unorganized, as the initial syllabus was completely ignored and he ended up changing all the grading percentages right before finals. The TA's were not very accessible or helpful to us either. If possible, avoid this class and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Benjamin is a nice person. The PPT of the course is detailed, but has HEAVY homework that must take the time to fix all details well【many little points for deduction】All his big exams, 2 midterms & final exam were F**king DIFFICULT. He will give a curve, before curve, scores may be less than 1/2, or even 1/3. RUN AWAY PLZ.
If you are considering taking any of this guys classes, RUN the other way. Seriously, worst professor i've had at Cornell.
I am convinced that the non-1 reviews were him just reviewing himself.

This course was incredibly terse and difficult to get through. Every part (especially exams) were made unnecisarily difficult and soltoff is not easy to work with. Take 2950 in the fall, avoid this prof at all costs.
NEEDS TO BE FIRED!!!
A a senior, worst professor I have ever had at Cornell easily. Negative contributor to the Cornell community.
The man needs to be fired. Provides little to no help. Rubrics are intentionally vague. Even if you ask for clarification he just says “I'll be grading on whether I think it was a difficult project”
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid avoid avoid

Typical Professor Soltoff behavior. Terrible rubrics that emphasize things not present in the assignment description. Gets upset with students when they fail to understand a topic quick enough, failing to realize that this is the result of his own incompetence as a teacher. I don't know why Cornell continues to allow him to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Took 3312 and now 4940 (applied ML) 

Ben is extremely gifted in his craft, he is a masterful statistician and understands coding like no other. 

That said, his soft skills are so garbage. He is terrible with feedback and talks to everyone like they are an idiot. 

Application Exercises get messy and he doesn't care about overworking you.

This dude is actually a terrible person. He should not be a professor at Cornell. He should not even teach at a kindergarten level. Terrible grader. Does not give any feedback. TAs have no idea how to help students. He is extremely picky with what he wants but never tells the students how to achieve those criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not learn as much as I wanted to in the course, first midterm was incredibly hard, lectures were often rushed and always confusing.

I believe this man should be fired. There are such a large number of students who don't enjoy his class or his personality. I waited until the last minute to take this class as a senior. I wasn't able to get my degree because of his ridiculous curriculum, unnecessary amount of overlapping work, and unfair grading for the group project.
he'll go out of his way to screw over your grade in the class, 10/10 do not recommend
Sometimes I would not wear a seatbelt driving around campus hoping I would crash so I wouldnt have to go to his classes anymore

This professor is genuinely not only the worst professor to exist but also one of the top ten worst humans ever. If you see his name under a class you are planning to take, save yourself the trouble and don't. You have have been warned.

Grading is extremely unfair & TA's are not helpful when you go to office hours. Rubric is completely made up at the end & they will dock huge amounts of points for things they never told you to do. The exams are also difficult & the medians are extremely low. Professor admits he's doing this for a paycheck & doesn't even like teaching the class.

I read the reviews, it was worse than they said. Professor was awful, bad teacher, demeaning to wrong answers, something due almost everyday, grades extremely hard. First time there were in person exams and the highest grade was a B, he then disabled grade calculation and blamed us. STAY AWAY, just take it in the fall with the other teacher.

The most impactful course I've taken at Cornell is INFO 2951, period. The content is so applicable & extensive. However, beware this was also my most workload intensive course—think three to four assignments a week for a total of 15 hours. This prof gets a lot of hate, but he is genuinely one of the best lecturers I've had, just a bit intimidating.

Talk too fast in lectures. Talk a lot, but vague most of the time without delivering a clear focus. Loads of homework (projects, in-class exercises, homework, etc.). Very bad workload/grading scheme design (i.e. too much homework and trivial exercises to the point that it loses focus of what should be more important.)
Previous ratings got deleted because of how explicit I was - that should tell u enough. Horrible professor. Do not take any courses with this menace.

The fact that this guy has a job—at Cornell or otherwise—is one of the great mysteries of the universe. He has no redeeming qualities—he is below par in every metric as a professor and as a human being. I believe the sole purpose he was hired was to demoralize enough students to debloat the InfoSci major.
Horrible professor
Never take this class by him. Would be unresponsive in help and completely unhelpful for exams. Do not recommend

In all my time at Cornell, I have never encountered a more unaccommodating, rude professor in my life. Joined the class a bit later (but still before the add deadline) and he told me "I wouldn't get credit" for any work I make up. Gave me a nasty, "I don't care" vibe. Not to mention his voice is UNBEARABLY patronizing too. Who hired this man??

let me be clear
1. INSANE WORKLOAD (hw + lab + project + ae + exam + extra credit... should be 8+ credit course)
2. AMBIGUOUS grading criteria (most TAs don't know what they mean either
3. 50% OF WORK COMPLETELY OUT OF CLASS MATERIAL 
4. DISORGANIZED PROFESSOR (speak too fast with no meaningful info)
5. 0 HELP FROM EXAM ("just review the material")

Mandatory lectures were lighting fast, yet mind-numbingly dull. Homework/project grading criteria was vague and subjective. He administered a final with no precedent of written work (hw/projects completed in R modules/Quatro documents). Tries to connect with students via pop culture references (genuinely cute), but is abrasive when approached.

Rude professor who refuses to help students. Provided 0 information for our final exam (which is structured completely different than anything we've done in class) and when students asked questions about it on the discussion board, his answers were days late and extremely vauge. Harsh grader with unnecessary workload.

Snarky individual who refuses to help his students. Snarkily answers most questions with "check the reference materials". Turns the class space into a toxic environment that is extremely hard to learn in.
Awful professor. Gives extreme amount of work and makes it a big deal when accommodations are asked for. class is also way too fast paced to truly learn the material, setting students up for failure.

I write this review at the very edge of my sanity. There is simply no rhyme or reason to how this man runs his class. Assigns an inane amount of work that takes a huge portion of time for no good reason. Grading is completely arbitrary and students are left to guess his expectations. Even the TAs are confused about how to do the assignments.

The worst class I took at Cornell, only took it because it was required.
