Professor wasn't terrible and at least tried to make it fun, but he was stuck teaching the worst subject, never gave the rubric for homework, didn't teach, and no one in class understood or learned anything. His voice is piercing and annoying.
dont take this course if you can. the lectures, homeworks, and exams are completely different, and you will get 0 help. he is a terrible instructor.

if someone were to ask me who the worst professor at Cornell is, I'd without skipping a beat say Benjamin Soltoff. His lectures are dull, homework penalties are arbitrary, and one of his finals took well over 16 hours to complete, on average. Avoid like the plague.

Took 3312, and everything about the graduate-level course (5001) is true. Lectures and labs do not align with what the HW's are asking us to do AT ALL. Do not take unless you took 2950 with him and have extensive R knowledge, TAs don't know what they're doing besides reading off the answer key.

Could give a 0 if I can
Homework rubric was super unclear and he said he had no obligation to tell us the rubric (???)
Instructions of assignments was unclear, grading was based on his own expectations. 
OH was not helpful at all, and TAs knew literally nothing other than comparing your work with the answers
Could give a 0 if I can
Grading is extremely tough. Grading not only based on rubric but based on his own expectations. The workload is heavy throughout the entire semester.
Low score maker. No one can even receive A
Monotone lectures, can get boring.

The course is very structured, and I learned about R having no previous knowledge. The lectures were fine but a little bit dull at times, but the projects and assignments were interesting to do. The exams were very fair and easy to prepare for. Overall he is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His homework setup is not making sense as it sometime requires codes outside the class, which is not making sense to me. Expect a heavy workload.

Well-organized and interesting lectures
It is fulfilling to take his course
The professor have changed his teaching style and now it is pretty good to have his classes

The only point is that the work-load is a little huge, except for that, he is a perfect professor

not the best lecturer but i think the class was quite organized and appreciated how there were no in-person tests. the final group project was fun depending on your group (we got to choose) and open ended-- we were given quite a bit of freedom. Overall very reasonable prof and I don't get the hate.

Avoid this professor at all costs -- despite asking for feedback, he never tried to change or cares to listen for constructive criticism. Disrespectful and uninterested during lectures, and agree with all the other posts about him being a tough grader and unreasonable workload.

This was my least favorite class at Cornell so far. Despite my love for data science, this class was so disorganized and down right bad. The prof. was unbearable to listen and lectures were a mess because RStudio kept crashing. We learned from watching the prof code, and the workload was too high: prelim, homework pset, lab, and project in 1 week!

This professor is a disaster. They have no idea how to effectively teach data science and seem to be completely disengaged from their students. The assignments are unreasonably difficult and the grading is arbitrary and unfair. If you have any other options, do not take this class.

actually terrible professor. info sci department just hired him but should get rid of him immediately. least accommodating professor at cornell and very inconsistent with workload. would have weeks where there are homework assignments, lab, project, and an exam all in the same week.

My favorite part of ICL she felt the most enthusiastic about her section. Also probably the easiest test but even ignoring that, she's still my fav. The way she broke down the section felt the most informative about her given area compared to other sections and lectures felt less monotonous

The topic fluctuates between being interesting and boring. Reading is required to some extent, but you don't need to spend hours on it. There's a solid amount of writing on it, and she's not the easiest grader, but she is fair, provides thorough feedback, and typically allows you to submit early to get feedback before turning it in. Compassionate.

Professor Bishara is an extremely nice person, very knowledgeable, caring, and understanding. This review is more about the class itself. It is very boring but extremely easy. You don't need to pay attention in class but she does take attendance. As long as you know how to read and write 2-3 page essays every once in a while, you'll do fine.

Professor Bishara can be a bit shy, but she really cares about her students and gives a variety of assignments to complete. She is a fair grader and has a genuine interest in her field. She also asks the class for feedback about assignments and projects so she can adjust due dates and make changes for future classes. I highly recommend her!

Prof Bishara is the nicest person and has such a genuine interest in her topic (middle eastern revolutions) you can't help but get excited as well. Can be shy but if you talk to her during an office hours she loves helping and will tell you her experiences and will give you abundant resources to further examine.
Don't forget to proof read!

Worst class every. Course not curved. Not given a single point to extra points problems, even if you did all of them and received full credits. No response in email and failed to answer students questions during classes. Told you quiz tested on a certain chapters, but actually tested on different chapters.
She is a kind, caring person who is accessible by email. She did not curve the class at all, so many people hate her for that. Many people did not like her teaching but I found it okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Terrible instructor. A black box grading process and you lose points for NO explanation!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely awful. 10 minute quizzes that are worth 5% of your grade each that are hyper specific to the textbook. No drops. Lectures are very slow. Sadistic grading on exams, youll lose 10% for a mistake on a question, does not matter how big or small, minimal partial credit. Horrible communication, gives no information about means/medians.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: do not take her class period.
Do not take her class, She give bad grade.

Very disorganized and incomprehensible grading. On multiple occasions, she's randomly deducted points from my exams and when I ask her about it, she can't remember why she took off points and refuses to fix my grade. One of the worst professors I've ever had.
A nice person, but not a great lecturer.

One of my favorite professors I've had at Cornell. Math and Politics is a great class, and she taught it well. Prelims were fair and had an easy final project instead of an exam. She will sometimes wait to get to the same number of votes every time for every iClicker question, which can get annoying. Knowledgeable about game theory altogether.

Like another commenter said, she is a nice person, but her lectures are quite poor. She'll often ask the class a question, then wait about 5 minutes in silence for someone to figure it out, and when no one does, she just gives the answer. This can happen about 1-3 times per lecture.

She's a nice person but just not good at teaching... Her lecture is not well organized and her notes are very unclear. She seems to be a happy, helpful person and she tries...  I found the lectures not helpful at all and just learned most of material from the textbook. The book is very good and cover all the material fairly clearly.

I think she is a very good lecturer. Her lectures are clear and organized and summarize all the important points in the textbook. Homeworks are not always straightforward, but they are in general a lot of fun! Enjoy this class very much!
Lectures are quite useless
The worst teacher I have had at Cornell. I couldn't understand when she spoke english words let alone calculus jargon. Don't take calc with her!!!
Try to have another professor.
No Comments

It is true that you do have to go to class every lecture, but that is because attendance is 40% of your grade! Thats awesome! The material is not hard, and is actually interesting.  It is easy to get an A+ if you just do the work.

It was supposed to be an easy class, but every class you miss, you get reamed. I even wrote 3 extra credit papers, forged a dentist appointment, but she is a Nazi for grading. I was smart enough to get an easy A, I got a C+ from missed classes. If you like coming to class and listening to her babble, you are golden. If you like to party... Pass

She is a nice person and helpful when approached, but her lecturing style is just terrible... it basically consists of writing some stuff on the blackboard, stating some claim that seems obvious to her at least, and waiting ages in silence for us to get it on our own. Glad she's not the DUS anymore.
Truly the worst professor I ever had at Cornell. Math is known for abysmal teaching, but she truly stands out as a leader in her field.  And nasty  to boot.  Avoid like the plague.

Without hyperbole, the worst class in the CS department. Dry lectures, devoid of content, full of meandering anecdotes that didn't go anywhere, content at least 15 years out of date, half the semester wasted on unrelated material, and a staggering number of just factually false statements made by the professor in lecture.

Lectures are dry, hard to follow, and riddled with random tangents unrelated to the course. It seemed like Ken really didn't care much about the class and didn't enjoy teaching it. It felt like he wasn't invested in our learning and was just waiting for the semester to be over from the first day of class. He was a very poor professor overall.

He is smart and achieved many things. But he is a terrible instructor. Each lecture goes into so much details which only obfuscate the main theme of the course, if there is any. Background knowledge on several domains are assumed. He is hard to approach.

Thank god he is leaving Cornell. When he made his post on LinkedIn annoncing his leave, he ranted at the fact that only 60 out of 375 students showed up to lecture. Is it more likely that 315 students are the problem, or the common denominator, 1 professor?

Birman's lectures often went on tangents about his technical acumen and how prideful he was of his work across companies/domains. Prelims were easy, and the grading curve was extremely forgiving. The knowledge you gain from the class depends on how much work you put into understanding concepts/C++, but you can get by with an A without much work.

Ken is a brilliant scholar and kind professor. He does like to ramble and lectures are sometimes unfocused, but his stories are always insightful. He is a very generous grader, and the workload is equal to or less than other CS classes. Highly recommend this course, but only after 3410 (it's a recommended prereq, but it should be required imo).

The course is really what you make of it. You can sink a lot of time into projects and understanding the material if you want to.
However, the course is graded such that only basic knowledge is needed for 100% credit, which is not ideal.
Birman is very smart, and he'll have a good answer to any question.

Birman is super knowledgeable about the field, but his lectures just really aren't that good. The class covers a lot of super interesting content, but I think it would be much better taught by a different instructor.

lectures were challenging to follow and exams did not accurately reflect material emphasized in lecture. Homework writeups were often missing key information on output formatting and were poorly written. condescending if you aren't a top student + very unforgiving late policies. crushed any motivation I had to pursue this field further

Prof. Birman would reply to ed posts even on weekends, so very accessible outside of class. 
However, his lectures are not very friendly for students without lots of knowledge in systems and whose learning style is to comprehend fundamental materials before jumping to high-level ideas.
Was not born to be a good teacher

reviews.comment: Before attending this course, it would be better to have some background in distributed systems. This course seems like a breeze at first, but it's not. In particular, it's very useful in system design interviews. The workload is reasonable, and it's doable to get A+ since there are multiple extra credits.

Cornell CS degree from engr school early-90s. Birman is a highly regarded scholar/researcher. He was either an asst or assoc prof when I was there. PRO: his research is a good thing for Cornell CS rep. Ugly truth: he was a marginal undergrad instructor, annoyed at having to waste his time teaching, condescending tone, completely unapproachable.

The most interesting in this class is that for the same homework, two TAs can make the grade very different one TA just gave 60 points but another gave 90 points which is very unfair for some students like me :) because of very unclear grading criteria and unresponsible work attitude. Moreover, the lecture content is not well organized.

The professor pretends to be approachable but he is actually not. If you ask questions that are not appropriate in his mind, he will rudely interrupt you and ask you to go back to review the material. Once, I was actually teased for being "poor" in English because I didn't understand his explanations... Well done!
kuai tao!

The lecture content is good and I did learn a lot about the field. However the lectures and slides are not well organized and he is not a very nice professor towards students. 40% of the final grade are on 1 guest lecture in discussion which makes me feel what I learned in class is a joke :)

Was extremely unclear with assignment instructions then would insult students who asked clarification questions saying they aren't smart enough to work at J.P. Morgan. Assignments had no relation to lecture material. Mandated attendance halfway through the semester; people would just sign in and not listen to anything but made prof feel important

Started deducting students 1 percentage point from the final score every time they failed to show up to class. Lectures weren't related to assignment materials. Seems to think that students are lazy for not showing up to lectures.
Good class and professor. Has plenty experience and relevant stories to share. Lectures were fairly interesting. First time course so there were only a few assignments and quizzes, but useful.

He seems like a nice guy who really wants students to learn a lot from his class. However, he comes off as very arrogant when answering questions, and is extremely unclear with assignment requirements. He changed the requirements of an assignment after many people had started it, but he blamed students for being lazy. Lots of errors in slides also.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures felt very dense sometimes. But I walked away with a strong grasp on important concepts in cloud computing. The professor was also really nice and went out of his way to help students during covid which was really nice of him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ken is a giant of the field. He was light-years ahead of his contemporaries in the 80s and 90s, and came up with the foundational systems that run Internet services today. He's responsible for not one but two paradigm shifts (Virtual Synchrony and Gossip) in distributed computing. I am still applying things I learnt in 614 in industry years later.

The worst professor I have ever met. Not friendly helping students,  but only expect students to find solution all by themselves even suggesting you to read tough paper or try yourself for over 10 hours instead of giving you a hint or answer in 10 seconds.   Poor professor.
Not someone I would want to be friends with.  Very arrogant, not helpful.  The class is doable but projects do not relate to lecture.

He is an ok professor but it is not easy to follow his logic in lectures since he spends a lot of time talking about himself and his own research. Exam questions were somewhat unclear and it is not always easy to understand what is required from the student. In his course, prelims are very heavily weighted while assignment almost have no weight.
I really liked him. He gave most of the lectures. Seemed to genuinely care about teaching. I wish there had been more variety to the projects though.

The class overall is very interesting and can be fun if you enjoy Java and learning object-oriented programming. I found Birman's lectures quite boring and dull and ended up learning most of the material on my own time by reading the lecture notes that were put online. You probably would not need to attend class.

This class was very poorly designed.  The Exams, Lectures, and Codding assignments were three disparate entities.  There was a ton of support from TA's and lots of Office hours.  Birman had this incredibly pretentious attitude in his lecturing that evinces his arrogance.
Awesome professor. Lectures were extremely interesting; he did a great job explaining the material. You can tell he loves teaching.
Very well constructed and interesting lectures. Prof. Birman was very helpful to anyone who needed it.
If you need help beyond the lectures see the TA not Birman

He's a pretty nice guy, but only if you establish yourself early as someone who is there to learn and not simply sit in lecture bored all day. He can be arrogant at times, but his lectures are clear, at least. The TAs help out a lot. The assignments have nothing to do with what you're learning in lecture, so start early.

On the surface, Prof. Birman seems to be an excellent and engaging professor.  His lectures are fairly clear, and assignments are challenging but fair.  However, as the semester progresses, a different side of him begins to show.  He is highly condescending and egotistical.  If you're an undergraduate, HE DOES NOT CARE ABOUT YOU.  That's it.

The lectures were vague and not related to the material that we were tested on. The example code given in class or on quizzes was wrong on multiple occasions. And Birman's arrogant attitude did not help matters. While Birman was at one point a key player in his area, he has not stayed current in a changing field

The worst professor ever solely based on his condescending nature and ego.  So what if he is a major player in any field.. most professors care about their students and is not only trying to fulfill a teaching requirement.
Very caring towards students and easily approachable.  Can be vague in classes but in person great, and an important player in his field.
Best class I ever took - a guided tour through the past, present and future of distributed systems.

Extremely helpful guy. Is really a big shot in his field. Has lots of exciting stories to tell and is extremely caring. However a pre-requisite to attend his lectures is a good interest in the course else the lectures do seem vague if you don't concentrate.
Knows his stuff
No Comments

Birman dislikes assignments and grading, but his lectures are engaging and lucid.  He enjoys tooting his own horn, but this is understandable since he's a very major player in the field of distributed systems.  His disengagement from teaching tends to mean confusing assignments, but high grades.  If you can cope with him, you'll benefit from him.
His mediocrity in teaching is overshadowed by his cockiness and complete lack of respect for his students.
Easy prof. Lectures are interesting too, though they tend to be unclear at times. Exams are straightforward, from the text or from written assignments.
Always had to be right and seemd to enjoy shooting students down.  Also seemed more intent on bragging about his own past projects and accomplishments than teaching the class.
Course was disgracefully easy.  Bizarre essay-question style homeworks.  Optional final = slack teacher
Easy prof, but gives very handwavy lectures.
Had no idea about optimization before this class. But I learned a ton and it has been really useful for upper div ML and data science.

Overall nice professor, very accessible outside of class and helpful. Cares a lot about his students and offers opportunities to improve grade. Material is difficult. Organization could be better - the timeline for the class in terms of homeworks and grades were a little confusing but other than that, I thought he was a great professor.
Fantastic professor!

Bitar's classes are super engaging because he uses the chalkboard for all his lectures. No PowerPoint slides at all! It's a nice change, but you definitely need to be on top of your note-taking game. The class is tough, with a lot of proofs, but he's really patient and explains things in a way that actually makes sense. Just be ready to work hard!
He's gives great lectures and is helpful in office hours too. Just make sure you start homework early and don't wait till the last minute. Prelim and final were fair.
One of the more challenging classes that I've taken at Cornell, but lectures are crystal clear. Also Bitar is very approachable and helpful outside of class.
Is very slow - takes too long to post things like homework solutions

Took in Spring 2016 - his first year teaching ECE 3100. I thought he was awesome, can be really blunt/quick at times, but will help you understand it esp 1-on-1. Good lectures. I had no idea what probability was before class, but left with a solid foundational knowledge that has been really helpful in later classes (ML, robotics, etc.).

I really enjoyed this course with professor Bitar and it made me interested in pursuing the American Studies minor. The class had a decent amount of readings that were all very accessible and posted on Canvas in a reasonable time frame. Additionally, the TA Patrick was also great and he was very educated and knowledgeable about the course. Easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is literally "food studies." There is absolutely no reason why this class (essentially an elective course) should have mandatory attendance 3 days/week and a 13-17 page final paper. This class is not important enough to be taking up that much time and commitment out of any student's week and semester. Not sure what Bitar was thinking.

This class is AMST 1110. 
The instruction of assignments is too vague and even flawed. Many of the feedbacks on my work gave me the feeling of "what? She is looking for that?"
Overall, be sure to have your assignment checked by your TA before submitted it. I ran out of space. But the blog post was a big mess at the start of the semester as well.

Very enjoyable course. Grade consists of participation, biweekly blog posts, a few small papers, and a final paper. Papers can be graded harshly but the rest of the assignments pull your grade up in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Bitar is the best professor I've had at Cornell. Extremely passionate about her topic, gives interesting readings (although long), and engages with her students. You're given a lot of freedom to study what you want for the final paper. Too many group tasks for my liking, but overall, the lectures were really incredible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She assigns a lot of readings and writing assignments, but they're mostly short and also very interesting. She tries to make the class fun, and you can tell she is extremely passionate about the material and making a difference. She is very invested in her students and cares more about what you learn than about how well you write.

Dr. Bitar is really a great professor. She cares about her students and isn't a stickler over little things. In addition, you can get a lot out her classes. I'm not the most "school-person' by any means, but she can you to learn something. Overall, great experience

I don't know how she is in other courses, but she shined in Schooling & Society. Readings were perfectly chosen and effective. Class discussion was engaging, never boring. Essays were honestly easy imo; you just had to engage with the material and organize your thoughts. Definitely a doable amount of work. Made me love education sociology!!

Prof Bischoff is a pretty good lecturer. The course is broad and covers a lot. There were 3 assessments and a final paper and a good amount of readings. The prelims are doable if you skim the readings + look at the slides. My TA was very helpful too!

Not the most engaging lecturer, but willing to help students outside class hours. Nice professor who definitely knows what she's talking about. Readings are necessary as the prelims are entirely based on them, and discussion section is required. There's a new reading for every lecture.
Too many discussions breaks in a large lecture. In class assessments were too long for the time allowed and graded quite harshly. Decent lecturer although the content was a bit boring.

Kendra was one of my favorite professors at Cornell. Her lectures were detailed, it was easy to tell that she was inspired and truly dedicated to her work, and her classes were always enjoyable. She especially was very accessible outside of class during office hours and gave really detailed feedback on paper drafts, etc.

Professor Bischoff was great even in online lectures. The weekly quizzes required that you do the readings and pay attention in lecture but were not too difficult. The readings could be quite long but it really varied from week to week. Reflection papers were simple and graded very leniently as long as you answer the prompt.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Especially for an online class, lectures were very engaging! Professor Bischoff explains concepts well and incorporated fun aspects like group polls and videos into class.

Professor Bischoff is an amazing professor! She gives interesting and easy to follow lectures that are very engaging. Definitely an easy A if you put in the time for the readings, which I found to be mostly interesting anyways (there were only a few really long/dense ones). Made me consider double majoring in sociology. Take this class if you can!!

Way too much active learning. Get ready to be in awkward and silent zoom breakout rooms for nearly half the lectures. Only take this class if you enjoy active learning and self study as most of what she wants you to know are in the readings and not in her actual teaching.

She is nice but not a great professor. Nearly half of your grade 45% will be quizzes based on long readings. It was hard to remember the details of the readings for the quizzes especially because she does not go into depth with them in lecture. She IS going to test you on very specific information that she does not include in lectures. unfair imo

Loved this class! Prof. Bischoff explained the concepts in a straightforward manner, since the majority of the students are not going to become sociology majors. Tests were only short answers, and the TAs look for precise, word-for-word answers when grading, so a bit of general memorization is helpful. Discussion sections on Fridays were mandatory

This class is easy if you show up sometimes and take good notes outside of the slides. You don't have to do the readings to get an A because she goes over them. She is super sweet, knowledgable, and tries to get to know everyone. The memos are easy 100s: pick one sentence or point made in the reading and connect it to your everyday life.

She is a very knowledgeable professor who takes the pretty straightforward subject matter and delves deep. You can skip every class and still get an A on the prelims (she posts slides online), but if you go you will get a great understanding. She will make an effort to learn your name and the weekly homework is abundant but easy. Would take again!
The readings were excessive. At least 80 pages of reading a week.

One of the best professors! Very passionate and energetic, seems like she really cares about students doing well. You don't really have to show up to get an A but I would def recommend going to lecture because shes really engaging. As long as u put a little bit of effort in, you'll get an A

The kind of professor that will learn your name if you speak up often, even in a huge class. She is an engaging lecturer and she explains all of the reading in a very comprehensible way. She gives lots of extra credit opportunities and doesn't give homework or have class the week of a prelim. Overall, a very pleasant person to take a class from.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take this class, you will be happy you did. Professor Bischoff is knowledgeable and approachable, making her a great professor.

Professor Bischoff is an asset to the Sociology department and to Cornell University. Her sophistication and intelligence come across clearly in her highly articulate lectures, and she challenges you to engage with the sociological perspective to see the world in a different light. If she is teaching a class, TAKE IT. You will not regret it.
Wonderful class. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Excellent class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's engaging and takes time to remember students' names even in a large lecture. Her readings can sometimes be tough but she breaks it down in class. Lectures ARE important. Writing down what she says (not just copying her slides) as well as the examples that she gives helps for answering exam questions. Her exams are fair if you are attentive.

Bischoff is a professor. She's energetic, but that doesn't mean anything, since everything you learn is based on the readings. Lecture is useless. Section is useless. Her grading is terrible. In her own words, "Getting the question right only means half credit. You need to really go beyond the question." Not even 2 pages on one question is an A.

Dr. Bischoff is why I am considering changing my study path from art to sociology in grad school. I took 2 classes from her; both were wonderful, informative, and inspirational. She encourages everyone to speak about their (relevant) opinions without judgment, and goes above and beyond to help students understand class materials AND their passions.

She's young and has fresh energy which isn't too common in the soc. department. She has good research credentials and assigns informative readings although some might be a bit advanced if you've never had soc before. You will NEED to study for the exams thoroughly but you can really take a lot from her courses. Speak up in class, too!
Nice person

Blalock-- what a guy. Very nice and approachable, teachers an easy writing course. I actually did learn about writing, but he goes off on a lot of tangents, which make lectures pretty fun. Sometimes he seemed like a mess but the class was bearable, essentially participation-based, and very casual
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Blalock was by far the most amazing professor I had at Cornell. He was extremely friendly and passionate about what he taught. He tied personal experiences into the class and really inspired further thought in students. I would recommend taking any class he teaches as he is absolutely amazing.

He gives really great lectures that keep the materiel as interesting as possible. 2601 is far better than 2600. His tests are pretty easy and based heavily on problem sets and lectures. Content is very well presented and its easy to learn for the test. Outside of class he's a really interesting guy and I would recommend getting to know him

Lectures are a little bit hard to follow since he talks quickly, but you don't *really* need to attend lecture (only on the days that problem sets are due or they're handing back assignments). The prelims are the same as the problem sets/discussion questions, so make sure to study those. He seems kind of cold but he's not mean.
He is a really great professor and I like attending his class

Go to lecture, pay attention, go to section, follow along the problems, do the problems sets. If you do all those plus a quick review (maybe 1-2 hours) before the exam you will do well. The exams are exactly like the problem sets.   Go to class, do the hw, be a good student for once and you'll do fine.

Professor Blalock seems like a really genuinely nice and caring guy, but he really can't teach for his life. When I found out he graduated from Yale and TJ I couldn't believe it, because he could not do simple multiplication problems without getting himself confused. It's really a shame that he can't teach, super qualified guy.
Awkward, cold and standoff-ish

Nice guy, but his lectures are disorganized and mostly irrelevant to the problem sets & tests. After everyone got an A- or above on the first exam, he put really weird, unclear questions on the second one so we wouldn't do well even if we knew the material. Can't prove equations or do arithmetic, and refuses to do any of the math in office hours.

Tests are directly from problem sets. Lectures are about as unorganized as they come, and have nothing to do with the prelims. That being said, a very interesting guy. Lots of research and general worldly knowledge. Super nice and always has students' best interests. Class is fun, typical Cornell kids hate it because it's out of the box. No book :)

Professor Blalock is one of the best professors at Cornell. Even if you aren't interested in his classes, I recommend you take one simply for the sake of spending a semester listening to his lectures. Ask questions about his research! A lot of it is really interesting. He is intelligent, well traveled, funny, and an all-around good guy.
Every professor should strive to be like Professor Blalock.
Blalock is a great professor with a huge distance to himself and life in general. The class is quite easy, interesting and absolutely worth taking.
Very helpful. Uses games and gives cash prizes to demonstrate lessons. Tests aren't easy, but are graded on a pretty lenient curve.
He is the man.  Great guy and great professor.  Smart too.

Made the course fun and interesting. He encourages lively class participation in lecture and homework is rather light. Will give what ever time is necessary to help students. Exams were reasonable. The competitive strategy game applied core principles and was great fun. A really great guy.

Interesting class on sustainable business. Bill tends to go off on tangents, but he has a super interesting background and is able to provide insights regarding his own research to topics brought up in class. Super easy A, take home midterm, and final presentation is simple and he allows you to choose your own groups. Take this class. Easy A
Taught us about love in econ terms and was interesting to listen. Prelim questions are all multiple choice and covered during lecture. Didn't do the readings but still understood everything.

Not a very good course on behavioral economics. There's barely any teaching and the only thing that composes the grade are two joke assignments that are scored rather unusually (relative to other students' work). The best thing about this class was the labs; but that doesn't make up for the quality of the course.
Great professor, class was easy and I learned a lot
Easiest class I've taken at Cornell
eh

Schulze is the man. He kept lectures interesting and didn't require too much reading of the textbook. He does rant a bit, but go to section, do the MyEconLab problems, and try to do well enough to utilize Kentucky Windage and you're golden in his class.

I took this class last spring. I attended a total of 6 lectures and one section. I failed the midterm, and I am certain that I failed the final.  I managed an 80ish average on the homework, and ended up with a C+ in the class.  Schulze utilizes Kentucky Windage, and it WORKS.  I didn't learn a whole lot, but I got through it.
I LOVE THIS MAN

Horrible professor, seemed disinterested in teaching and focused on research. Hard to get in touch with. His merits are that he's quite a character and humorous. Expect to be teaching yourself the course through takenote.
No Comments

This class is a joke. The single easiest class at Cornell. Schulze is a cool guy but he expects WAY to little from his students. Unchallenging to say the least. The most interesting part of the course is the lab experiments. I would take it just for that: easy money!
uses JD in all of his examples, teaching not really hi strong point
Went to class about once a month - a pretty easy class, but lectures are very repetitive. Extra credit experiments are awesome - you get points and paid. A lot less work than ECON 101.

Okay Professor.  Half of every lecture is history/politics and other stuff that isnt tested.  His tests are kinda hard but he tells you exactly what to study.  Plus he gives extra credit, so you can end up with a pretty decent grade.  I hear better things about him than Wissink.

Definitely sucked me into liking Economics ... of course, once I took micro, I hated the field, but Schulze definitely made the course easy (only a handful of ALGEBRAIC equations to remember for an entire final!!!).
No Comments
Just a terrible professor.  There is really not much else to say.
No Comments
Professor Schulze gave us a "Schulze Day" where we did not need to come to class. Enough said. Great Guy.

Probably the easiest course since 3rd grade.  Seemed like he repeated his lectures enough to go to every other lecture (or once a month!).  All you need to understand is one equation and put numbers into it.  Missed only one question  all semester!
Nice guy, makes material easy...kentucky windage (will give your second test more weight if you do better on it)
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
I think he showed up **** to class quite a few times...
very clear and intuitive lecture, TakeNote was great for the course - great guy.
Teaches us intuition. Priceless!
His fondness for Jack Daniels is in most graphs he uses. Very opinionated.

Material was clearly explained during lectures, then effectively reinforced during labs. Treat the Lab manual like the holy grail when it comes to understanding the crosses. Listen to the TA's and learn how to accurately draw the crosses because that skill will earn you 20% on every exam.

Make sure to attend lectures for the exams. Dr. Blake is one of the most caring people on this campus, and even though the material can be tough, I really appreciate that the grade for this lab course is independent of how successful your experiment was.

Normally I would not grade this professor as low as I did. I feel like it is not only this professors fault but the class is organized in a way that is not conducive to learning. She is passive aggressive both in class and out of class, and the lectures are often incredibly simple which then is frustrating when it makes a sudden leap in prelims.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: ***This is for BIOMG 2800, NOT the lab class 2801. Dr. Blake is an amazing professor. Genetics is tough but her lectures are so clear and make difficult concepts easy to understand. Go to study sessions to help understand things better and go to office hours when you are struggling. It is very possible to do well in this class.
Best professor I had in the bio department by far

I've literally never had a better professor. So clear and concise during lecture and explains genetics in a way that's so easy to understand. Extremely approachable after class and gives very fair exams in my opinion. If you go to class, you 100% should be fine. The TAs are also super helpful with quizzes and any questions on lab stuff.
Professor is not great and has boring lectures. Makes work harder than it has to be for no particular reason.

Lectures and labs are extremely clear and structured, and the lab manual is super detailed. 55% is participation, lab exercises, and assignments, which you can get close to 100% by going to OHs and working hard. Lab is graded on participation rather than accuracy. The midterm and final were fair, and okay if you understood the assignments.
Great professor. The best in the genetics department. Makes incredibly clear and detailed slides.
I highly recommend taking a course with Dr. Blake, and definitely go to office hours. She is very receptive to questions and is great at explaining concepts you are having difficulty with.
Really helpful professor, it pays to go to office hours with her. The class is a lot more straightforward and fair with her teaching the class than it was before.

Iconic. A breath of fresh air at Cornell. Organized, thoughtful, clear, communicative and committed. No pretension, just dedication to student learning and a justice-oriented classroom. Bonus if you get to work with her in the CF+TC! Highly recommend - she goes above and beyond, shows up to all the student events to support, and is 110% engaged.

A very dedicated professor who is organized, thoughtful, and caring. She is genuinely concerned about learning and wants students to be engaged and uplifted. She has a calming and encouraging vibe. One of the best professors at Cornell - loved going to class every day.

If you don't like group projects or going to class outside of class time, beware. Thursdays are just people presenting group projects, and you need to do extra credit events (lectures, fashion exhibits, etc) on weekends or during non-class hours to do really well. She is forgiving and changes grades all the time. Nice, but a boring lecturer.

Fashion, aesthetics, and society is a fun and interesting class w a minimal workload. We had projects (one group, one individual), discussion posts, and an attendance grade. The prof is so sweet and gives ample time to complete assignments

ASIAN 1118 FWS: Power, Protection, and Liberation: Buddhist Paths to Flourishing

Lectures were VERY dry, 1/2 class was falling asleep. But overall, EASY course to get an A in. You don't really need to do readings to excel, but having some background knowledge is helpful.
She gives clear feedback, is very kind & understanding + lenient
Good class

She was exceedingly boring and the only thing drier than the lectures was her personality.  I was so interested in the topic, she's just not a very engaging instructor.  She would be better off in a library somewhere than in a classroom.

Professor Blackburn is a great teacher! I learned a lot about post-colonial studies, and as long as I kept up with the readings, the seminars were interesting and engaging. Lots of difficult reading tho.

After the awful comments on here, I was worried.  But this is the easiest class I've ever taken here.  She is nice, and while her lectures are confusing and dull more often than not, the individual projects assigned are quite interesting and enlightening for your information.
She is the most terrible teacher I've ever had for sure.
What's wrong with taking a class to fulfill a requirement?  Does this mean she has to be nasty?  Does this mean I don't work hard?  I felt like she was more than a little unreasonable and moody.

Boring, uninformed, talks endlessly about barely related concepts, and does play favorites.  I went to her office and thought she was quite nasty with just the two of us there.  She might be the worst professor I've ever had.

Prof. Blackburn is very intelligent and nice, although a bit boring. I found her lectures to be slightly dry but dense with information, which to me suggests that any problems are my own. As far as grading, I thought she was good and fair (which doesn't mean giving an A for every student).
Grades too harshly, plays favorites, appears to have more problems with female students.  She's taken away my interest in India, that's for sure.

It's best if you have an actual *interest* in the course before you sign up.  I found her grading to be legitimate and fair.  She's passionate about her work and is quick to sniff out those who take her courses just to fulfill distribution requirements.
I want a refund on this stupid class.  She's awful.
Worst class ever, worst prof ever. She's unclear and awful. Very boring. Don't bother.
It's only good when she cancels class.  Boring and I don't learn anything.  Waste of my time.
Worst ever.  She's never in class, doesn't prepare, and doesn't make sense when she does.
Dull and nonsensical lectures, unreasonable in grading.
One word: terrible.  Do NOT take a class from her.  You and your GPA will be very sorry.  It's not worth it, you will only be bored to death anyway.
No Comments

The class was largely structured like a conversation related to the readings. The readings, however, are heavily biased so conversation is limited to a mediocre regurgitation of an agenda. Not only this, but the conversation had little to no direction so it felt stagnant and useless.
Incompetent lecturer. She brings very little information to the lecture other than just describing the image on the slide.
Her lectures are very disorganized and unprepared

If you want a professor who cares, Theo is your man. He brings incredible enthusiasm to the classroom and not only cares about you as a student but as a person.

I HIGHLY recommend taking any classes you can with him. There will be lots of reading, but the pay off is well worth your time, he always brings out the best in you!

Professor Theo is extremely welcoming and encouraging, and especially supports the students who work to be better actors. His love of Shakespeare, Ecological and Social theater is contagious. And when he performs in class, he commands the whole room!
Amazing teach with great talent!! Honoured to have learned from him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: incredible instructor. extremely caring. puts so much effort into teaching the class. amazing class too.

Class is unorganized. There's barely any structure to the materials. He basically teaches whatever comes to his mind. No quiz answers were given and problem set solutions were not followable. The TA does all the work for the class and all he does is show up at lecture. The majority of the final was materials NOT discussed in previous assessments.
boring and unorganized

He is disoriented, disorganized. He takes wrong notes to class several times. He is good at making jokes and telling stories but not giving lectures and explaining things. He gets impatient when you ask silly questions. I would have done better if I started working by my own earlier.

Blume is a poor explainer of the concepts in class and then when the tests arrive they contain material you have never seen before. He neglects to inform the TA of anything that will be on tests so the review sessions are worthless at best. He hands out no syllabus and cites simpsons paradox when talking about grades (look it up).

Definitely the worst professor I've had at Cornell. Lectures were scatterbrained and only covered basic concepts, while problem sets were difficult and exams were impossible to study for. The TA had no idea what was going on half the time. It's honestly worth pushing intermediate micro off for a year to avoid taking a class with Blume.
if you're going to take game theory 3680, you might as well skip lectures and watch these http://www.academicearth.org/courses/game-theory

Lectures are essentially useless - Blume goes over the concepts broadly, but the homeworks and tests go much deeper than what he covers in class. The textbook is close to useless and Blume insists on holding makeup classes when HE misses class. Terrible class, if at all possible, do not take.

"Considering recording lectures for his superiors to see!"  Lol... like Easley?  He is very smart, arrogant, a pain in the ass to deal with, yet broadly interesting; he enjoys and has knowledge of lots of random things. He's not out to get you, he is just extremely disorganized and teaches as if you're having an intellectual chat over coffee.

I have taken two of his classes, and can attest to all the ratings below. Tried many times to find a redeeming quality over the past year, but he is simply an arrogant, pompous buffoon. Lectures are beyond worthless, in that they detract from the time you have to teach yourself the material. Considering recording lectures for his superiors to see!

Completely useless. TA's are the key in learning anything from his courses. Does not teach, no textbook, could care less about how students do or feel about him. The Econ dept. should be ashamed but then again, they dont.

Worst prof ever-- disorganized, a poor lecturer, pompous, arrogant, and a power-tripper. Relies on his own incomplete lecture notes that are filled with typographical, math, and grammar errors. Grading is opaque. You're on your own with this guy.

Bad textbook, mostly useless lectures.  For some reason I went to them though.  There was marginal entertainment value, and occasionally I learned how to do a problem.  Mostly he just talked about the existence of concepts, without actually explaining them, though.
Lecture is useless...be ready to learn everything on your own...
Worst professor ever... he will randomly cancel class and demand to have make-up class at the most inopportune hours.  Wouldn't really matter because his lectures are beyond useless.
don't take it.
Very disorganized, teaching has nothing to do with the book, useless lectures.
I was going to throw my opinion here as well. Luckily, others have already done so. Nice guy. Disorganized. Unclear. A bad teacher.
Disorganized, unclear, unhelpful and condescending.
I would never take a class with this professor again.

Very nice man once you spend some time with him. Extremely smart- engage him in conversation about his work and he responds well. A little fazzled but if you take the time to listen and do the work it comes together.

This guy makes such an interesting course easily the worst class in the Econ dept. He does not teach at all but will go on and on in lectures how smart he is...take the class with Basu if you can. He is incredibly rude, too.
When you get nothing but bad ratings from your students after so many years of teaching, does one need to say more?
Everything I learned about game theory, I learned from the book by Gibbons, not this class. I attended every single lecture and unfortunately I didn't get much out of them.

This professor is perhaps one of the worst that I've ever had in my many years of being a student. He acts very smart but very often he doesn't seem to know the material that well. He also comes in late and doesn't prepare his lectures.

HE DOES NOT SHOW FOR HIS OWN OFICE HOURS!!! and then complains no one comes to them. This guy is very unhelpful. wants to waste your time talking about everything but the course also goes about talking how dumb the students are.
no good
Nice guy, very funny, but very bad instructor. He knows the material but he cant convey it. I wouldn't recommend any course with him.
Smart guy, TERRIBLE course!
Very nice guy. A bit disorganized. Knows material. Have to spend a lot of time going over stuff yourself to get most from class.

This professor is honestly the worst that I've ever had in my many years of being a student.  He acts very smart because he says he is, but he doesn't seem to know the material.  He also comes in late, doesn't prepare his lectures and talks about innaties
Avoid this very rude teacher, thinks he knows everything. Very smart, but probably not as smart as he thinks!
He's a nice guy but the lectures are not organized well.  Problem sets and exams don't reflect lectures enough.
Econ 368 is extremely difficult and his lectures/book choice do not help prepare for the tests. Do not take this class unless you are extremely creative mathematically.
He's actually a nice guy, and his lectures are fun. The problem is that they don't prepare you for the tests and neither did the book.
talks too much, teaches too little!!

Pretty good professor. Really knowledgable about what he teaches. Probably one of the most knowledge in the dairy science field to be honest. Courses are not content heavy and easy. But grading is mediocre.

Honestly my favorite professor at Cornell. I had him for ANSC 2500 and ANSC 3540 and its obvious he enjoys teaching/the material. The information is very straightforward & you don't need previous knowledge of dairy to do well. Just show up to class, pay attention and you'll do fine. Blake wants you to get tons of hands-on experience through labs.

A delightful professor, and a genuinely good person. He's got a dry sense of humor that he uses at unexpected times, which keeps things lively. He makes an effort to actually get to know the people in his class. His previous experience as a practicing vet makes his teaching that much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Blake is one of the kindest professors in the Animal Science Department. He has a dry sense of humor and tries to make you laugh during lecture. He is very specific on his tests and wants you to use the terminology from class. Blake wants everyone to succeed in his class and labs are very fun!

Dr. Nguyen is one of the most intelligent professors at Cornell. Though lectures are sometimes a little dry, he presents information in an easy to understand manner and is always available to answer questions after class. As the manager of the Teaching Dairy, Blake is one of the people at Cornell who really walks the walk and talks the talk.

Prof. Bloomfield assigned a lot of reading at first, but lessened it when told by students that it was too much. Essays were graded fairly, always gave good feedback and was available to help. Towards the end of the semester became lenient and allowed us to do whatever we wanted for the final project, such as a group project on a current event.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bloomfield ensured that material load throughout the semester was always at the right level and offered substantial feedback throughout essay writing process. An already interesting topic was reintroduced to students in more formal readings such as scholarly articles and primary documents on past climatic events. Good first year class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The amount of readings assigned was an overload and I wasn't able to balance the rest of my classes with his class. He talks extremely pedantically and makes overly worded jokes that make no sense. Also the amount of essays assigned were a lot, it was like 4 to 6 essays per month each being minimum five pages with a ten page research paper later.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Excellent teacher, amazing person really wants you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I have never worked so hard to still get a grade that wasn't great. All the work has to be done by yourself, and you essentially read an entire textbook. He also talks incredibly slowly, so I always had his videos on at least 1.5 speed to make it feel normal.

Insanely tough. This class broke me, and I definitely bled a little... Exams waaay harder than practice prelims, and curve is competitive (if there is a curve). Each exam is a puzzel with all sorts of unexpected twists, memorizing provides tools to solve them. Be good at taking exams. If you can think beyond the objectives, you will go far kid.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Blankenship is a great teacher. Biochem is difficult, but there are tons of office hours staffed by multiple TAs. Make sure you thoroughly answer the objectives for each unit by reading the textbook, watching the review videos, and talking over the objectives with a TA. If you do this, you are bound to get a decent grade.

Jim is a nice guy, but his actual tests were 5x harder than the practice tests(actual tests from previous years). It could also be that this course was completely online this semester due to COVID. During the semesters where this class is offered in-person, the class is usually fine. Stay clear of this class until in-person instruction resumes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is great, and the material is very interesting and applicable. The auto-tutorial format is well suited because biochem in general is memorization heavy. Jim is available to answer questions, and he has a great teaching team to help out. His review sessions are great too, and he's a sweet person who loves teaching!
He is very dedicated to all students. Exercises tough love.

Auto tutorial classes substitute genuine educators for student laborers, bulk memorization, and arbitrary weekly assessments. Any student that says that they enjoy this kind of pseudo-learning must, in fact, detest learning and instead be enjoying the mindless parroting of uncontextualized information. BIOMG 3300 is definetly not worth your time
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed 3300; one of my favorite courses at Cornell

Makes mud as clear as water. Excellent professor! His review sessions are short and sweet. Material can seem a little heavy, but is actually not that bad, especially with all the tons of help he and his assistants offer. Always wandering the study center asking if students need help with material, and asks for feedback on quizzes and tests.
Awesome class! Jim is really cool.
BEST CLASS I loved biochemistry, and I loved his teaching method. He knows what he's talking about, and wants you to learn!

Doing well on the weekly quizzes will take up hours each week.  However, studying for quizzes makes studying for prelims relatively  easy and the material you learn in this class come back again and again in many other science classes and especially the MCAT.  I've learned more in this class than any other at Cornell, but be prepared to work for it

Autotutorial biochem was very difficult in terms of material that you must learn.  However, there are always TAs on staff to help you out during the day.  Prof. Blankenship gives optional lectures, which can be helpful.  He was one of my favorite lecturers, which really says something, since this was an autotutorial course.

took this molecular cell bio. class during the summer during the 6 week session. if you can, take it! covering something as deep as cell bio in 6 weeks means at least 25+ hours of work per week for each of the 6 weeks, but if you keep up, you will be rewarded with a wealth of knowledge. Also, there were only 4 people in the class- amazing.

This is a hard course heavy on information. Yet, Jim made it one of the most fair, interesting, and rewarding classes I have taken at Cornell. I did not enjoy "hard" science until I took this class. Key to success is simple: study the objectives (exactly what is on prelims.)It's unfortunate Jim doesn't teach a lecture class, he would be brilliant.

Autotutorial biochemistry is no cakewalk, but Jim outlines exactly what he wants you to know in the course packet.  If you study those objectives and know them by heart, you'll do well.  Unlike orgo, you can actually get a good grade if you put in lots of effort.
The autotutorial class is so absurdly hard I bled a little. I still enjoyed the material and learned a lot. The prof constructed a really solid challenging class.

You will remember this class for your entire life. Excellent auto-tutorial course. The optional "review" sessions led by Jim are good refreshers for exams or before Unit tests. Workload=life consuming. Talk to TAs in the center and clear questions up ASAP. Jim is always in the center helping TAs with unit test, grading, tutoring.

Best autotutorial class at Cornell. Possibly best Biology class. Jim is clear and organized and WANTS YOU TO DO WELL. Class is organized around this basic motive, so oral tests are not graded, written tests are fair, and prelims are very fair too! No complaints. The material was really interesting too. Workload not too bad.

Like with most auto classes, what you get out is directly correlated to how much time and effort you put into it - you can get a lot of out this class by learning the material thoroughly. Didn't  have a lot of contact with the prof, but his review sessions were great and he seemed accessible and helpful. Actually one of my favorite classes here.
This class has a huuuuuuuuuuuuuuuge workload, but in the end you learn alot and it's pretty interesting.  The prof was helpful and nice.

In BioBm330, I didnt have too much contact with Jim. The class itself was very intense and rigorous. You dont have to wake up for lecture and you can skip material you already know, but reading text book alone can be depressing sometimes. You dont have to read the text book, just *memorize* the objectives, good way to develop study habits.

He's an ok guy, personally though, I thought he was sorta condescending to certain students at times- so for that I think the guy is a bit of an ass.  I'm guessing all these great reviews he's getting are from his "favorite" students.  Review sessions were helpful though, the test were hard but if you studied you would do fine.
He should be a professor teaching a Real class.

Hard class (seriously, whatever amount of time you expect it to take multiply by two and add a few hours).  Great professor, one of the best I've had.  Go to the review sessions!  They are tedious but very helpful.  Don't do what I did and take orgo at the same time.

Jim Rocks!  He is hands down one of the best professors at Cornell if not THE best!  I finished this class hoping he would teach another class.  If you have any interest in biochemistry whatsoever, this class is a must!!! You won't regret it!
Awesome guy.  Genuinely wants you to learn and understand the material.  Very approachable and always willing to listen.

This class takes a lot of time, but is worthwhile in the end.  Between the study guide, the TA's, review sessions and the prof, lectures are not needed and although i was very opposed to autotutorial classes before taking this one, i would recommend it over the lecture class.

This class isn't just about memorizing, esp. the last unit about metabolism.  Memorizing is essential but will only get you so far; you have to integrate your knowledge.  That said, Jim is a great teacher and very helpful.  I would recommend this course to anyone.
Great professor. Too bad he is teaching an auto-tutorial course.
Jim is a great teacher and is fair to all of the students. (Some other person thought he only helped pre-meds). He is a wealth of knowledge and will help anyone who seeks him out.
the class is autotutorial. And yet it has some of the best lectures I've attended at Cornell. Odd don't you think?

A really nice guy, even though the course is hard, he doesn't mind helping you out, although he will refer you to the undergrad TA's for help first. I think he prefers dealing with the administrative end. his help sessions are VERY thorough re: the tests.

Definitely don't be narrowminded.  It's not hard material, but it's definitely a lot of work and a lot of memorization.  The review sessions headed by Blankenship are extremely helpful as long as you don't get distracted by his personality.
Jim is an awesome guy and a great teacher. He makes the material easy to understand..it's a shame that such a good teacher is heading an auto-tutorial course
Jim is the Best!!!
No Comments
this class tests one thing - ability to memorize.  any form of reasoning is highly discouraged.  i did learn a lot though.
No Comments

Jim was only helpful to pre-meds.  He made it very difficult for me to get extra help with him, and reserved his hours for his favorite students.  This is BY FAR the worst class I have ever taken at Cornell. Even Genetics is a cake-walk compared to this.
No Comments
No Comments
This guy's not only very knowledgable, but extremely nice in person. A word of general advice, though: don't be narrow-minded.
auto-tutorial biochem is a lot of work...stay on track and ask the ta's for help

Had him as the first professor for Work Labor Capital. Very passionate about the subject matter and had lectures memorized. Straightforward and fair test, provided a study guide, sample question, and breakdown of the final. Was the only professor in WLC to do this. Great sense of humor and enjoyable lectures. Would take again.

Out of the professors so far, Boyer was the best. The test was fair and covered exactly what he said it would (2 short answer questions). Graded pretty generously too. He'd make jokes here and there in lectures which made class more lighthearted, would 100% take his class again. Slides were detailed, just skim the readings and you'll be fine.

First module of ILRGL 2350. Boyer kept the class engaged and I found the material to be very interesting. Exam was fair and covered what he said it would. Readings covered the same material as lectures

Boyer is a great guy and he keeps lectures interesting. Highly recommend taking this class! Material is interesting if you like history. Graded by 2 exams and optional paper only. Exams are straightforward if you prepare well. Review sessions before each exam and comprehensive slides posted. You don't really have to read or attend class.

One of the best professors ILR has to offer. Could not recommend more highly for the advanced econ requirement, especially if math is not your forte, since grade is based on two tests which are entirely written and a paper. Very nice guy who really cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at Cornell. Lectures and slides contain all the info needed for prelim. Offers helpful study session before exam. Super chill and tells bad jokes to keep lectures interesting. Definitely take his class if you get the opportunity!
lot of reading, lectures are dense with information, his opinions on course material have an edge on them but he makes jokes and is humorous
Posts notes but you also have to read and study, grading criteria is tough, wants specific details on tests, know your stuff
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy who'll be helpful if he trusts you're making an effort. He presents the material in a helpful, organized manner without making you work extra to learn it. I think he doesn't always understand the ability of his students, though; you may have to prove your interest or ability to him if he pegs you as less of an achiever than you are.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: George Boyer is by far the most engaging professor I've taken at Cornell. Only 2 exams and an optional paper. If you attend lecture and take good notes, you should do fine. He is really funny, too. I always look forward to attending his lectures.
I Love this Guy

The homie Boyer was really funny and got the main idea across in each of his lectures. Super entertaining and a genuinely nice guy. It was easy to get excited about the topic and then the test was straight forward. What else do ya want?

Boyer was by far the best of all the Work, Labor Capital professors. Clear with his material, and a very funny and likable guy. His test is very straight-forward, asks you questions about overall themes and patterns. If you have him for this course, you'll be pleased I'm sure

This class is kinda interesting. Boyer is hilarious! Dont need to do the reading, just take really, really good notes. Tests are fair. The study guide is helpful. I'd recommend this class to anyone needing an advance ILR elective. Only 2 tests and an optional paper.

Great lecturer, relatively easy prelim which had a median of about a B+. If you go to his office hours he lets you know almost exactly what trends/info you will need to study to do well on the exam. Tells terrible jokes in class, but they keep you awake and in focus

Good lecturer but used so many handouts and graphs that showed up on the test that it was really difficult to remember all the countries and trends which was useless and unfair. Either take really good notes or read the book for this class, don't need both. Median is a B for his prelims. Damn near everyone got a B...Givan's paper boosted the avg.

GREAT lecturer, and even his bad jokes keep things interesting.  He makes a habit of explaining why this or that MATTERS, which prevents the material from feeling obscure.  Only complaint:  way too much reading assigned, a lot of which is COMPLETELY unnecessary.

He is simply a fantastic professor! He makes history logical and narrates it in a natural and very entertaining manner. He answers any kind of question with full interest. I have had no formal background in history whatsoever, but I found it no problem to follow his class. Helpful, extremely entertaining and a GREAT professor overall!

Great professor. Lectures are entertaining. Do either all the readings or attend all the lectures. Both are not required. As far as economics classes go, this is one of the best. It's a more historical account, but very interesting. Boyer is not out to get you, he wants you to learn. Take the class!
One of the best I've had at Cornell. Very funny and interesting lecturer - 75 minute lectures fly by.
Lectures are a lot of fun with Boyer.  You definately need to devote some time to studying, but the grading is relatively-fair.
Class is about average for hardness.  There are a lot of readings but if you go to section and partcipate you should be fine.  He makes lectures fun.

Required for ILR, material isn't too interesting.  However, Boyer makes lecture interesting; nice guy who's really funny and good to talk to.  Tests are a bit tricky, and you have to know a lot, but study and it's not bad.  Boyer rocks!
Boyer is awesome!  The tests are a bit hard, but he is an amazing lecturer, and definitely keeps you awake with his humor.
simply the best lecturer I will probably ever have. tests are easy but the grading is harsh. he delivers with such enthusiasm; it's almost like every class is a performance.

The class is extremely fun to go to. I always look forward to attending his class. Professor Boyer is never boring. He's always making these random comments that are soo funny, you can't stop thinking about it even after class.

I've had Professor Boyer for two classes, the introductory ILR140 and "Social Policies in Britain and America". He's extremely easy to get along with and his tests are straight-forward. Sometimes you feel like he's in the classroom to practice c
Though he seems very nice, he doesn't answer questions asked in office hours. He likes to have his ego stroked and loves it when you just agree with him. Interesting material, not the best class.
George Boyer, if your reading this, I LOVE U! :)

It's too bad that all the joy of Labor Econ is frontloaded in Boyer's class. By the time one reaches the absolute hell of 340, the will to live having been sucked out of their soul by Larry Kahn, the genuine genius that is George is a forgotten dream. '03

His lectures are clear and straight-forward- the reading is a lot but he lets you know what to know and explains it all thoroughly. Plus, he is hilarious and one of the most intelligent teachers at Cornell.

An extremely brilliant man who really wants his students to do well in his course.  He is not out to fail students like most teachers are.  He is very funny and tries to make his lectures as non-boring and possible.  Very enjoyable class to take.
No Comments
The class would be more interesting if he only spoke about baseball.
Rather entertaining lectures for the subject he teaches and he wears sweater vests, now that is stylin!
he is an awesome professor, plus you have to take his class if you are in ILR
amazing and funny
An absolutely amazing professor.  Extremely funny and very interesting.
Really clear lectures. Very funny!
the man
This guy is hilarious! Its like learning economics from a stand-up comedian!
He makes the historical events of 145 years ago come alive and uses them to illustrate his ecomonic point.
No Comments
No Comments

Awesome professor. Very knowledgable about his work and incredibly understanding to the different levels of comprehension his students have in statistics/economics. The course work is NOT difficult if you come to class, ask questions, and participate. I highly suggest you take his course if you are willing to participate as you will get an "A".

Very kind professor and engaging during lecture. He allowed problems sets to be worked on with a partner but they were still very hard and sometimes not covered in lecture. I would take another course by him though!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: great professor, I really enjoyed his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Lectures are really interesting and explain the topics quite well. Need to do a lot of textbook reading outside of class. She also offers plenty of opportunities for extra credit and seems genuinely interested in your success. Moderatly difficult, but with hard work can earn a good grade.

LOVE this prof, her lectures are easy to understand but make sure u take notes on what she SAYS, discussion sections super helpful, READ and UNDERSTAND the case studies. They are very useful, especially for prelim. Prelim was fair and most people did rlly well.
I wish I could take this class again, Prof Bohns is def one of my fav profs here
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Was truly one of the most unreasonable test administrators I have ever experienced in my entire life. She gave us lectures that had nothing at all to do with our prelim. Gave us no guidelines for the essay assignment that she had us do. She lied to us that a practice test she put up had nothing to do with the test, the test was the same questions.
A great professor really engages students and makes them appreciate their intro courses

The class is interesting but her grading is inconsistent for group projects. She did not provide constructive feedback which made it difficult to improve on future assignments and theres a lack of guidance for the last group project even though she graded pretty tough. It seemed like there were people she liked more and would grade more lenient.

Bohns is an interesting lecturer and she tries to make the content engaging. Very few grades, so you can't really make mistakes, but if you do the readings you'll be totally fine. Not a bad class at all.
Read the provided readings, go to class and pay attention and you will do well. Your TA is also helpful.

only teaches the first half of the course, 2nd half is with Professor Bell. preferred her half, felt more engaging and not just reading off slides. Very easy to get an A and extra credit is offered. 2nd half with Bell was similarly easy but lectures were way less interesting.
As long as you do the readings and attend lectures the prelims and papers are relatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Bohns is an amazing and well-respected teacher. Her lectures are very engaging — though as others have pointed out, incredibly fast-paced. She does post slides online as well as supplementary textbook readings, and reviewing/reading both is definitely helpful. She is easily accessible outside of class and offers easy extra credit.

She goes ridiculously fast and is not the most attentive to students who are struggling. She kind of just throws content at you and makes sure you know her credentials. She has a forced median which results in deductions that are seemingly unjustified. Does not set her students up for success and hinders the learning process with fast speed.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The sweetest, most engaging professor and lecturer ever. 100%. The lectures, however, are extremely fast-paced and content-heavy, so I recommend—although I did NOT do this—reading the textbook ahead of the lectures. ILRID1525 has her for only half the course, unfortunately, but I enjoyed it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Her lectures were really good and I enjoyed the class. My only complaints are how long it took to get grades back and the way there were very few assignments worth so much. But it wasnt hard to do well on the essays, and if you study a bit you'll ace the final
She always kept the class engaged during lectures. Didn't like how the final was 50% of the grade, but she is a great teacher.

Bohns took 22 days to post the exam and essay marks, even though they were graded 2 weeks before. The essays have a forced median, resulting in grade changes. Your mark is based on 3 grades, thus I had 1 mark prior to the exam (plus participation and attendance). The final has ambiguous questions, and she promotes her book and uses profanity often.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are only 3 assignments in the whole class and she takes FOREVER TO GRADE! Waited 22 days for my final grade and last paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved this class. Bohns is a super engaging professor that made this material interesting. The tests cover both lecture and the textbook (and sometimes super specific details of them), so study hard for them. The papers have clear expectations and aren't graded harshly.

Professor Bohns was my first college professor, and I took for granted how good she really is. Her lectures are very interesting and clear. She moves fast, but posts everything online to look at if you miss something. I plan to take more of her courses and I highly recommend her.
Professor Bohns was solid. I didn't enjoy the course that much, but her lectures were clear and helpful.

Professor Bohns is an amazing lecturer! You can tell she actually puts effort into her lectures which is why they're so engaging.
