You're on your own. He wastes a lot of time telling fictional stories of other scientists. His presentation skills are inadequate, and he mumbles a lot. Honestly, the textbook will be what saves you. He will punish you with unfair questions involving reagents he breezes over in class, so make sure to note every. single. reagent. mentioned.

Ganem is great. Don't go to office hours to ask something that can be learned by you just reviewing your notes or reading the book. Or he will be pretty mean to you. Only go to office hours to ask hard questions!

Ganem has an inflated ego; he thinks that he is a genius, on par with the likes of Linus Pauling. He also loves to name drop his Nobel Prize winning acquaintances. He is fairly obnoxious, but he does teach well and knows the material. The tests are definitely challenging and require a lot of patience and skill on the part of the student.

Ganem is decent. He moves pretty quickly in class, and his office hours weren't very helpful. He does follow the book pretty closely. Working in depth with the book and problem sets in addition to studying the notes is the best approach.

He makes a very tough subject seem a little more manageable.  He does an AWESOME job of pulling his lectures directly out of the textbook, so if you're lost or miss a lecture, all you need to do is look at that day's section in the book and you'll be fine.  The tests were tough as to be expected, and he seems a little impatient at times.  Good guy.
The lecture are very clear and easy to follow, but he's very condescending in office hours and not very helpful.

Ganem is amazingly clear and extremely good at lecturing. Still, it's orgo, and it's going to be tough - Ganem just makes the course more pleasant than it normally would be. Do the problem sets, read the book, study the notes, go to office hours, and stay caught up and you'll do great.
Ganem is a great guy. Unbelievably rich, but still gives off the vibe that he wants to be there and enjoys teaching. Very good lecturer
Great prof. overall. Very clear lectures, fair tests. Made Orgo as decent as it can be.
Amazing lecturer, extremely organized notes, makes lectures seem interesting, never monotonous. He gave great exam prep questions so you could be very prepared on his exams, no tricks.

A truly gifted lecturer who has a gift of conveying difficult material clearly and skillfully. A true whiz in his field, don't let his Harvard/Stanford/Columbia/MIT training make u intimidated. He's really down to earth and wants to know you in office hours. Def. one of the best profs at Cornell or academia period!
His lectures are crystal clear, and he goes through all the details he wants you to know.  Go to lecture, pay attention and you'll do fine.  He prepares you well for what he tests on.

Ganem is exceptionally clear. Practice test style mimics real tests. Ganem loves questions that ask you to apply your knowledge to a new problem, can be tricky but fair. Is warm and helpful, i suspect that some find him cocky because he tends not to answer directly but rather address your deeper understanding, which is more helpful in the end.

This class was ph'nol-menol. The best part of the class was when he says the word "ph'nol"(phenol) and "goash"(gauche). Be sure to check out my vocaloid ganem phenol remix. Oh yeah, he's a great lecturer btw.

Ganem is an excellent lecturer, very organized and poised. Orgo is tough; you have to really work for it if you want to do well. I've been to a couple of his office hours. He's a nice guy but a bit cocky. I don't blame him. He's a Harvard alum. The prelims are fair but he doesn't award partial credit so there's little room for error.
Very clear, engaging lecturer. Makes orgo interesting and understandable. Can be a bit cocky, but overall a very good professor.

Class wasn't hard. Not to be boasting but I managed a great grade. Most of the material came directly out of the textbook and the tests weren't too bad. He speaks with a businessman-like air so beware...you might fall asleep like I did!
Didn't go to class very often yet got an A+. For the times that I went, he wasn't bad at lecturing.

His lecture is pretty straight forward but tough to follow if you haven't already read the book. Just read the text. You just have to learn it all on your own since you won't pick up enough from just the lecture to even get a passing grade. He's extremely cocky and degrading during office hours. Beware the Ganem.

I decided the rumors aren't true. Orgo is a fascinating subject and not THAT difficult if you keep up with the reading and do the P.S. However, the prelims are annoying. This guy doesn't really believe in partial credit. And you are better off going to TA hrs, or asking friends. I went to his OH, but he felt very uncomfortable and stiff.
Good professor, despite the rumors. Very well-organized lectures with reasonable exams. Seems like a rather nice gentleman, as well. May have a thing for Movados.
Boring. He's a nice guy though
don't have to go to class. got a+, went less than a dozen times all semester.
He has dry humor and is boring! His lectures do not follow the book and he is obessesed with solvents! Made me hate orgo and the only thing useful I learned was the IR, NMR material.

Anyone who talks bad about Ganem probably got a bad grade in his class and is blaming him for their mistakes. Ganem is a stellar teacher. You really must put the time in if you want to do well though. I MISS BRUCE IN 358!

Not bad. I didn't find Ganem to be as cold and heartless as people paintt him, but the material of the course is hard, although he does try to make it easier in some ways. Not easy, but not how the rumors paint him (although the averages of the class ARE pretty low sometimes).

i never really do reviews, but ganem deserves one. Took 357 with him, made organic chem 100x better than what it's known to be. brilliant lecturer, clearer than the light of day, and engaging. Went to office hours before prelims...never made people feel like an idiot. He was always trying to help.

Horrible professor.  Was snide and clever during the first day of class which made me dislike him instantly.  His fake personality and the mean stories i heard about him just made me do even worse in the subject.  If you can get over his stupid personality and find SOME interest in the subject, then you'll do fine.  Absolutely hated the class.

Lectures are pointless...All the material comes from the textbook. First and second prelims are not bad. Third is rediculous. Does not believe in partial credit-thus either get everything right, or get a bad grade. Not allowed to make mistakes on tests, expects you to be a genius.

Ganem's an excellent lecturer, but he's a pretty fake guy.  He gives off the impression in class of being nice and caring, but if you get to know him in office hours you'll see hes pretty much a creep.  He makes you feel like an idiot when you ask a question and like you're wasting his time.  Go to TA office hours instead and you'll be fine.

He seems friendly enough, a good lecturer. His first test is not too difficult at all, but watch out for the 2nd and 3rd. He did nothing for my interest in the subject, I still dislike orgo, though. I've been to office hours,  he hasn't been a jerk to me, but he does expect us to be geniuses.
He is an excellent lecturer.  Overall his class was good, but I would not go to his office hours.  He was slightly mean, but other than that great course.
He is an okay professor. Seems friendly, but watch out he can get pretty mean during office hours. His prelims had too many questions that had no partial credit. Much more harder than general chem.
The tests were wayyy too difficult. He is pretty fake. At first he seems friendly, but he really isn't. Lectures are okay. Unfair sometimes.

one of the most organized and clearest leactureers i have come accross. I learned ALOT from his class. tests are harder than chem 358, but not inmpossible. regualar work is needed. go to his office hours. never gives doubtful answers. if you ask hinm what needs to be focused on, he is very clear on telling you YES or NO.
This professor is very cool, tests are exactly what you expect/prepare for. Somehow makes this mind-numbing subject interesting.

best chemistry class i have taken at cornell.the lectures are very clear and follow the book. read the book before going to class. ALOT of material to take in. Do the problem sets and go to "00" office hours. exams are not hard if you have read the stuff and done the problems.very clear lecturer and well organized. never gives doubtful answers.

His lectures are pretty clear but I hated his multiple choice tests.  It's hard to know what he wants to focus on for the tests so I suggest studying everything well. Try doing the problems in the book; it's a lot of work, but worth it.

Lectures are pretty clear though you do have to concentrate to follow them by the end of the semester. Book is very good, but definitely a class where you need to keep up and study hard- you really get out what you put in, grade-wise. It's quite possible to do well- you just have to work hard for it.

Organic Chemistry. The material is not easy, but the book is very clear. I learned all the material from the book. I didn't really use the lectures. I now realize that if I read everything before going to lectures I would have done a lot better. So prepare for lectures. Also go to the "00" class, or maybe just their office hours - very helpful!

Read the book before you go to lectures and before you you the prelim!  Exams are not that hard if you have read the book and understood his lectures. This course uses one of the best organic chemisty books.  Go Ganem and Loudon!

If you keep up with the readings the lectures will be a clear and useful summary of what's in the textbook.  Otherwise, they won't teach you everything you need to know.  The textbook is excellent, and I found myself learning all of the material from it.  Ganem obviously knows his stuff, but it's impossible for him to go over every detail in 50 min

not a great professor..lectures are unclear/boring, you'll learn it from the book or not at all.  i didn't like him in office hours, he was just a jerk. there is no need to be an ass when someone comes to you for help.  cornell's seen better, in my opinion...
best chemistry teacher i've ever had. go ganem
Not a hard class, but it's helpful if you go. Prelim wasn't hard, but it woulda helped if I didnt cram last second. Study maybe a week in advance, and you'll be okay. Orgo's not as bad as its rep.

bruce dominates; i think he might be the smartest prof. at the university.  like his attitude or no (you probably won't), but i think it's hot when a prof. knows his**** forwards and backwards...that is bruce.  the hardest "c" i ever worked for, and i'm damn proud of it
His lectures are quite useless, and his pre-lims don't cover what he says they will.  He's a jerk in office hours.
Orgo is a terrible experience.

Lectures are completely useless. I went to 0.5 lectures, yes, i left halfway during the first lecture, just read the book and pulled off an A+ in the class. But i did read the book and knew my stuff. Anything in lecture is vague and must read the book to do any of the problems on the prelim. overrat

He was extremely unhelpful in office hours and was derogatory to students not only in the office but in class as well, often making comments such as, "what, are you dumb?"  Also, the problem sets were in no way related to the prelims and wer
His lectures are outlines of the book-- completely unnecessary.  I don't even know what the guy looks like because you don't need to go to class.  Just read the book.
No Comments
Not very interesting
he is a great lecturer, but I've heard he can be a jerk in office hours. stick to the tas if you have questions. it's a hard class, but he does a good job.
I took the class nearly 15 years ago.  I still consider it one of the best taught classes I ever took at Cornell.  I am a professor now and still admire the clarity of his lectures.
Excellent lectures - great speaker.  His tests are clearly written and fair.  There's a good balance of material so that you can do fine if you don't get it, but you're still challenged if you do.
he was a great lecturer...although i was not a fan of orgo, he made it as fun as possible and made sure i learned a lot. very helpful whe ni went to his office hours.
he made the exams ridiculously hard, and they were unfair since there is no partial credit. i do not like this man at all.
Wonderful teacher.  Explains concepts very clearly, but is condescending when you ask questions in office hours.
This class is impossible. But we're not taking it because we want to...so I guess we have to stick with it. Dr. Ganem is a really good lecturer though.
helpful lecture notes but he will but he will definitely run you over on the exam.  he will also make you inferior for asking questions
you spoiled fall 03 fools don't know anything, wait til you see prelim 3
Businesslike air during lectures. He'll try to crush you with his exams.

He is the man Cornell hired to crush the aspirations of dreamy pre-meds.  Even outside the characterization of a tyrannical orgo professor, he is malicious and harbors a massive amount resentment.  As per lectures and exams, he is deadly clear.  Give him
Very good lecturer.  Also has a nice balding pattern.
Good Lectures, Clear, Structured. Tests are fair and if you know your material, you can ace orgo. :-)

Dr. Ganem is brilliant, and gives very clear, organized lectures, but his attitude is poor.  He brought a box of kleenex to the final exam, and passed it around before the exam itself was distributed, saying we would need them since the exam is so hard.
Bruce Ganem is the greatest professor that chemistry has ever seen.
hard tests, but fair i guess
dr. gamen is hands down the best organic chem. prof. that i have ever heard of, and that is coming from someone who got rolled out of o-chem b/c it was just too hard for me
Good teacher.  Some students think he's a jerk, but I never got that impression.  Lectures are very clear.  Responds quickly to emails, and helpful at office hours.
Good teacher. Actually made Orgo easy.

Tests seem real hard when you take them but the simple after you know the answers.  He likes concepts, not memorization so that's cool.  And considering the low fun factor of organic chemistry, his lectures are pretty bearable as he is so energetic
Ganem was an awesome prof it you weren't smart enough to figure out his tests that's your problem.

Hates students, wants to them fail, or seems that way, encourages questions, then gives you lectures about being an adult when  you ask them, discourages all who are pre-med, but is a very good lecturer
He is a hot bald man who looks like a troll, likes to give motivational speeches, hard but very fair tests, excellent lecturer
Devoted professor and chemist. A jerk in office hours, I hear, though.
No Comments
No Comments
First test is the kicker; decent overall; weird sense of humor
Tests are real tough, Don't mess up the first one, it's the easiest of the smstr
hard class...hard tests... but very helpful with questions and in office hours
No Comments
Challenging, but wants students to succeed.  Likes trick questions on exams.
i loved professor buckley's lectures and he is very kind and helpful. i really enjoyed microbiology bc of him, his lectures were engaging and interesting
Great professor, hard class. Very approachable out of class and wants to see students do well. Tests are memorization heavy

Such a caring professor. He really wants his students to succeed and actually learn. Cornell should have more science professors like him. But, I did SO bad in the class because the exams were just ridiculously hard. But, I think the homework grades will save your grade.
Really helpful and caring guy - he reached out to me individually when I wasn't doing well and it meant a lot.

Professor Buckley is an amazing teacher, I went to his office hours every week because I didn't understand a lot of the lectures. He really took the time to help me learn and understand. With this class though you can not just memorize. You really have to apply the concepts. I think I could have gotten an B or A if I really tried. Lec is boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lecturer that cares a lot about his students and will do anything to help you out!

Absolutely amazing! Best professor I've ever had. Takes all the bio concepts and info and relates it back to everyday life. Lectures are extremely interesting and go at the perfect pace. Definitely take this class!

One of the greatest professors! He made me a lot more interested in biology. He respects the students a lot and as well as every silly question a student might ask, whenever in class or office hours or emails. Additionally he always smiles at you!!! If he is going to teach another higher level class, I would definitely take whatever the subject is.
One of the best biology professors! Very inspiring.
In  my opinion he gives the best lectures in all of Cornell! Absolute gem! He teaches with a style that just gets to you and makes you want to learn more about microbiology.

- struggles with classroom technology to the point of wasting class time

- struggles to present coherent lectures, most are a disjointed direct reading of the slides

- never prepared for class

- lacks any clear expectations for assignments, presented various several year old rubrics and struggled to provide any clarification

Other review was definitely not accurate. She picks favorites and then is rude to those who ask questions. Grading criteria is unclear, and she gives unclear answers about it. Very few assignments, which is nice, but not worth being held hostage for an hour because she won't let you leave if theres nothing left to do or you finished the assignment
Do not take this course. Do yourself a favor and take regular oral comm.

Good communications class, especially for E&S/plant science/agsci majors. Assignments included: mock newspaper article, video, elevator talk, and final presentation. Carlyn was a riot (affectionate), and I thought the assignments were reasonably graded. Only con was that she was disorganized at times & expectations weren't always straightforward.

This professor's employment makes the school look like a joke. The most disorganized and unfair professor I've ever encountered. Our entire grade was based on a singular research paper that was given to us 2 weeks before class ended, without any instructions and a misleading rubric. The presentation we worked on for 3 months had no weight. Fire her

While Professor Burton is lovely, ILRID 1700 was among the least organized of my Cornell career. There is a ton of weight on group work, making it almost impossible to succeed if you get a bad group (speaking from experience) and lectures are generally all over the place. She obviously cares a lot about the material but the class was a real pain.
Not a great instructor. The lectures were poorly organized and the group project was arbitrarily graded.

Overall, the class was very disorganized. There were many small assignments, that were difficult to keep track of, and many difficult group assignments. Grading criteria was completely random and generally unclear. Would not take this class again.
Absolutely the worst experience I've had with a professor at Cornell. Her feedback is condescending and she will belittle you if you don't agree with her pov. Avoid at all costs

I'm disappointed to see the other reviews here. Prof. Burton is honestly a gem and I loved listening to her lectures throughout the semester. She really cares about her students and works hard to find interesting, relatable material. Unfortunately, many students jump on her in class and try to take advantage of her kindness, derailing lectures.

As a management class, this has been one of the worst-managed and least-organized classes I have ever taken at Cornell. It's great that she's so passionate about the subject matter, but vague lectures, poorly-defined grading criteria and a lack of awareness of how much work she assigns are massive detriments to her teaching style. Bad website, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class wasn't so bad (besides being way too much group work for my liking) but Burton was the worst lecturer I've had at Cornell. Unprepared for class, talks in circles, doesn't make any sense, etc. I wanted to like her, since she's super enthusiastic, but she was just not good at teaching.

Professor Burton is very enthusiastic about students but she speaks VERY fast and to be honest, she's not a very good teacher. She's hardly clear and very difficult to follow. Her lecture slides are also absolutely horrible. Its literally a sentence and a bunch of pictures and is impossible to comprehend after lectures. I wouldn't take her again.

really nice and easygoing, contract grading system so you decide what grade you want and do the amount of work for the grade you want. no technology in class or slides only writes on the whiteboard so hard to focus on what is said a lot of the time

Dr. Bulthuis is an exceptional professor & explains complicated content in a clear, palatable way. He makes you want to learn the material. This course was on the Philosophy of Aquinas--heavy duty stuff--& Dr. B he made it enjoyable and exciting. I was blown away at this course from beginning to end. He wants you to get it & is very approachable.

Bulthuis explains course concepts very clearly and in an engaging way. Even when readings initially seemed incomprehensible, Bulthuis managed to make the material seem simple. I was always excited to go to class (even though it was in the morning!). I am hoping to major in philosophy because I loved his class so much. He is my favorite professor.

Professor Bulthuis was very good at explaining the different topics we covered especially since the assigned readings were sometimes long and difficult to fully grasp. Lectures were interesting and he was usually very accessible during office hours to go over things.

I went to office hours to catch up on classes I missed, and Professor Bulthuis helped me to understand things about philosophy I didn't even know I didn't know. He is the reason I want to be a Philosophy major, after taking his INTRO class. His lectures are phenomenal and engaging. His grading is tough but undeniably fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bulthuis did a good job of explaining the concepts in each unit. There was a decent amount of reading (some weeks easier than others, watch out for Hume) and our TA gave us the option of in-class quizzes or responses (500 words) based on the reading. Exams were fine if you did the reading and studied well. Papers were tedious but fairly easy.

Way more reading than expected.  TA grading often seemed subjective.  I took the course when Prof. Bulthuis just introduced prelims, making it significantly harder to obtain an A or an A-.  A B or B+ is attainable without much effort, but if you want anything higher you will really have to work.

Regarding his film class at DU. He refused all criticism and brought up his Playboy career, calling Hugh Hefner a “good guy.” Then he'd show films mocking lesbians. He obsessed over AI tools, pushing students to subscribe to ChatGPT and Grammarly Premium instead of actually teaching writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Byrne is the GOAT. I loved his Sports COMM class and I think any student interested in sports would too! The topics are very interesting, and it was a pleasure to attend class.

At some points, Prof. Byrne shows you what he can do as a professor but at others has you questioning why he's there. He's laid back but seems to teach the course because he's interested in random topics. Not because he necessarily cares about student growth. Unfortunately, don't take it unless you plan on going into media or have to.

Prof. Byrne is one of the best comm profs. He is knowledgeable and genuinely a good person. He gives good feedback to improve on assignments, and is generally reasonable with grades and has clear rubrics. Due dates are fairly spaced out, and overall he's just a great person and professor
Such a caring and compassionate professor who is passionate about his work. Has fantastic energy!

Stay away from this woman at all costs. Don't risk your grade whatsoever. If she doesn't like you it's over for you and your grade. Has no structure to her class and is honestly the worst professor I have ever taken at Cornell. Listen to this please. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This professor is a menace. Her grading was completely unclear and she obviously gave students bad grades for no other reason than she didn't like them. Taking this course was like watching a child on a power trip every day. stay away

You have no way to figure out how to improve because there is no grading rubric and no feedback. You will be expected to read upwards to 150 pages before every class. Very arbitrary grading and excruciatingly long lectures with no breaks as promised in syllabus. Grading is a mystery even with 1 week left. Expects thesis level work with <1000 words.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Oh God please, do yourself a favor and stay away. No clear grading rubric. Impossible to please. A class where hard work doesnt pay off. Unreasonable amount of reading. Long, boring lectures. Dont, just dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She really knows her stuff but definitely assigned way too much reading. I ended up skimming a lot because it was physically impossible to read everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Byfield knows her stuff! She knows a lot about the things she teaches. She  is always willing to help students out if they need extensions on papers etc. She is an engaging teacher and encourages discussion during discussion sections, otherwise she lectures in her other classes (still interesting).
Boring at times, extremely interesting otherwise. Lots of long essay writing unfortunately.

Interesting, but a LOT of material. Readings tedious at times, I ended up skimming a lot. Lectures LONG; prof mostly lectured nonstop, reading from her notes for 75 mins while students struggled to keep up with notes; no visual aids such as powerpoints. Discussions the best part of the class; fair grader. I'd give the class a B-
mean to students

Ms. Bunea is pretty good at lecturing. The exam problem is very similar to the problems she goes through in lecture or the ones she gave in recitation. The class is easy as long as you pay attention in class. She also posts all the notes on canvas which is very helpful. Recommend taking this class with her!

Mostly good. 95% of grade is three prelims, rest from an optional homework. You don't turn in the other homework for credit, but do them to do well in the class! Also do all the discussion problems. If you can do all those, then exams are not bad. But each exam is 5-6 questions. I messed up 2 questions on 2nd prelim and tanked my grade to an A-.
good lecturer, lecture notes also made for good review material. exams were straightforward especially if you pay attention to lecture and homework content
Skipped 3/4 of the lectures, didn't read any textbooks, good class

She is an AMAZING professor who teaches clearly and explains the material well. I put in effort, did my work on time, and received a good grade. She has a slight accent and uses a blackboard, but overall she's an enthusiastic and kind woman. I was confused by the negative reviews I read, anyways this is a great class and professor. 100% recommend

The class is pretty straightforward, and Bunea teaches it well. She's funny, and she's accessible through email and outside of class. She posts her lecture notes online but the lectures are still helpful as she tends to add context that is not present in her posted notes.
My favorite professor i've had at Cornell. As long as you pay attention and do the homework you should really be fine.

BTRY 3080 with Bunea was one of the lighter classes I've taken at Cornell. I came in without having taken any calculus or stats since high school but all you literally need to know is basic integration and differentiation. Bunea was chill, homework wasn't bad at all, and there was no final. Genuinely don't understand why this class has a bad rep

Bunea's class was hard for me. Definitely wouldn't recommend for someone who doesn't have background in Stats or some calc. That being said, she clearly likes the class and her students. She said some of the funniest things in lecture and was really open to helping me when I did poorly on a test. She gets a bad rep: unjustly.

Absolutely the worst course I have had. She makes the course and the material unnecessarily complicated. If it wasn't for the TA, I would have failed the class. Attending her lectures were the worst hours I spent on campus. She writes on a blackboard and her handwriting is just way too difficult to read and goes too fast. Take ECON3110 instead.

I enjoyed Prof. Bunea's lectures very much. Some people might say otherwise but honestly I think it's very difficult to teach a statistics course and keep it engaging in general. She really does a great job and I really appreciated everything I learned! Final grade is 90% prelims/exam though, so be careful if that's not your cup of tea.

The text book is so much better than her lecturing. The class is pretty cool and straightforward. Just read the textbook and go through the example problems and you will do well. A lot of students do very well. Make sure you can integrate well (double integrals too).
Lectures were always boring and unhelpful, so I learned everything on my own time to even do remotely well on exams. She can be quite funny occasionally.

She's been teaching this class for a long time so it seems like she has lost interest. Lectures are pretty boring and people usually stop showing up to class halfway through. She does post all the notes online though and the material itself isn't too difficult. The TAs are also not great. Make sure to review the discussion questions and do homework

Worst professor I've had for a statistics course. Makes it extremely difficult to understand and the course is very theorem-based when exams are not. Her notes are also very hard to decipher and the grades take forever to be posted.

Great teacher. Her lectures are easy to follow and well paced. Overall, some more difficult concepts, so would not recommend if you're looking for an easier class. However, sassy, fun, and by far my favorite prof.

Professor Bunea is always willing to help students (replies directly to students who have specific questions in class and by email), but has some really boring lectures.  She's stated that the course is more rigorous than in past years. I feel that grades  have to be earned with hard work now. 3 tests make up 90% of your grade, so study hard!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are not engaging at all. She attempts to get people involved by asking questions, but is just greeted by awkward silence. Going to lecture/recitation is not necessary to understanding the material. Just read the textbook. Prelims are based on recitation and homework problems, so if you do those, you're set. Low effort to get an A-.

She really cares about her students and wants everyone to understand. Very approachable. I've heard this class in the spring was impossible but as an average student I thought this class was pretty easy. The tests were exactly what we did in class.
Avoid at all cost. Very distant and disorganized.

Literally gives you copies of handwritten notes at the end of each class -- so even if you didn't go to class, you're able to understand the material. She's very friendly, approachable and while she does have an accent, it's not difficult to figure out what's going on if you pay attention.
horrible

Literally one of the best professors at Cornell. When a classroom's desk space was too small for an in-person prelim during COVID, he immediately moved the exam online. His lectures were engaging, and some of the few recorded ones that I looked forward to watching. Honestly the best.

Professor Hwang is fantastic. The class was set up to work at your own pace, but help was always available when needed. He is fantastic at explaining things, very friendly, flexible, and approachable. Even if he taught more boring classes, I'd still take it if it were with Hwang.

Professor Hwang has been one of my favorite professors this semester and it's a shame I didn't get to take his class in person. He explains the material very well and in a way that makes it fun. Sets clear expectations and clearly cares about his students. 2240 is an easy class but I'd recommend it even if it wasn't because Prof. Hwang is great.

Prof. Hwang is there best in the business. Whether your into Fi or not, you will need to thoroughly understand the fundamentals of equities and fixed income if your going to be big in this game. Hwang is a world class Corporate Finance prof, and renown researcher in Behavioral-Fi. World class prof, in a world class program. Sit up front.
A great professor, super accessible and a wonderful guy. He is extremely helpful and wants you to succeed in his class. Would really recommend!
This professor makes intro finance super engaging and easy to understand. Doesn't take attendance but going to class is valuable. Tests are fair and he gives practice problems beforehand.

Hes a super nice and helpful guy, and a great lecturer to top it off. There is a good amount of self learning for this course but it is not too challenging. The stock trading game and portfolio projects are fun and easy. Lectures give you career insight as well as basic finance knowledge 10/10 professor
The lectures are super clear. He is a really good lecturer, super nice, and is always available for help. The class overall is easy. Little reading and the tests are easy.

Professor Byrne truly cares about her students and not just their success inside of her class, but their outside involvement as well. I was fortunate to have her for COMM 1101 in person this year and she was so understanding about all the struggles of online learning for the kids who were not on campus and pushed back assignment dates to help.
This is a chill and fun class. You won't regret it

She is so amazing. The material is not super interesting but she makes it enjoyable. She is also super understanding. Attendance is mandatory but she gives a fair amount of absences. I definitely recommend taking a class with her if you can.
She seems like a very genuine and caring person.
She is one the most inspirational prof I have ever met. She is a really nice and caring person with very good teaching skills. She is my favorite prof so far.
Fantastic professor. She gives you many opportunities to succeed in the class. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well.
Sahara is truly the best professorperson at Cornell. She really cares about her students.

Great teacher. Engaging, interesting and pertinent lectures. Creates great study guides that is incredibly clear what will be on the exam. In office hours, very helpful and fun to talk to. Projects were fun and final paper was not exceedingly difficult.
Exciting lectures, interesting topics. Constant class discussion (very enlightening)

Best professor and best class I took in my 4 years at Cornell. Prof Byrne respects you as a student and person, and if you're willing to work hard and put in an honest effort, you will learn more in her class than any multiple choice/test based class. Amazing professor, even better person!

LOVE HER! Great class, very interesting, very relevant. Really knows what she's talking about since she worked in the field for so long. Probably my favorite class I've taken. FOR TESTS STUDY THE TEXTBOOK. Love her, recommend media/sahara to everyone!

Byrne's is awesome, I love her! That said, don't take the class for granted. Make an effort and THOROUGHLY read the assigned chapters in the book and pay attention. It will pay off in the end. Byrne's is such an exciting prof, and I'll miss not having her next semester. Great Personality!

Best teacher I have had at Cornell. Professor Byrne is an engaging speaker who truly cares for her students. She takes interest in what students have to say and tests are straight forward. She makes awesome study guides too, page numbers in all.. Take the class!
Sahara Byrne is the best professor I've had at Cornell so far hands down. Super nice and caring about her students, and a great teacher. Take 2200 if you can.
BEST TEACHER EVER!!!
No Comments

She is wonderful! Her lectures are well organized, concise and engaging. The exams are straight-forward - she doesn't try to trick you. If you attend lecture, at least skim the readings, and turn in the projects, you will have no problems getting an A.

Sahara Byrne is the best professor ever! Very helpful and makes the subject matter interesting. I can stare at her all day long. The exams were very fair, as long as you read the assigned readings and go to lecture, you should have no problem.

In Byron Suber's ballet class you will get an amazing work out, spiced up with tidbits of dance history. He makes you reevaluate the Ballet aesthetic and think about its socio-cultural implications. His style is based on classical ballet, however, be prepared for unusual combinations that will challenge you to ditch your habits.

This class was definitely not what I expected.  DANCE 232 (Modern Dance Technique II) was really more yoga than dance.  Sometimes we rolled around on the floor or did strange acting exercises.  If you're free-spirited and hippie-ish, you will probably enjoy the class.  If you're looking for something similar to a jazz class, this is not it.

This class can be as challenging as you want it to be, depending on how perfect you want to get with all of the exercises. They're not intricate, but they are useful for developping good form, etc. Prof has some interesting thoughts on ballet- it's not a traditional ballet class at all, but can be a great experience no matter what your preferences.
No Comments
really bright, really funny, really motivated, and really ****. just the way i like my dance teachers.

A difficult class made extremely frustrating by the professor. Unable to end a sentence with the same thought he started on, hearing him talk actively hurt my understanding of circuits. He lectured by coming in and happily rambling until we got up and left. A nice guy, and grading was okay in the end, but anything I learned was from the lab manual.

He's really nice and means well, but he can't teach. Grading scheme is unclear, tests don't always reflect the content, & lectures aren't helpful in any way. His strategy is to look at the slides he took from another teacher for the first time in class, which means he has no idea what he's doing and sometimes gets his own iClicker questions wrong.
Carl is really helpful and cares about his students (ie. meets up with individual students to discuss labs and writing reports). However, he's not particularly clear at times.
Very confusing recitation.  It would help if this instructor learned to talk more slowly, and not jump so quickly from topic to topic.
Carl is really nice, but he's an awful teacher. Basically didn't teach or spell out his expectations for anything (data analysis techniques, experimental methods, report writing...).
Great professor and great class. My friends at other elite universities do not have classes on bees, and they wish they had
I honestly expected an easer class kind f like other non major bio major classes but i am really glad i took the class because it was super interesting
I can't believe how much I learnt in this class and it was really fun
Funny and passionate. Her exams are NOT easy and very specific.
yay bees! great class and professor :)
She's a great professor! Very friendly and very fair. If you have a genuine problem with the course you can bring it up to her and she'll probably agree with you and fix it!
great class, bees are cool!
amazing class, professor and person. Vey clear and engaging presentations, slides, and grading criteria. As long as you show up to class, you'll do well on assignments

Professor Caillaud is a great lecturer and I really enjoying learning about the fascinating biology of honeybees. It was always interesting to be in lecture and very often fun. I wish her slide shows were a bit shorter so we can get to everything in class
I swear to god just show up and get your A

Taking this course right now and really loving what I am learning. the course is super intersting and well structured with pre and post lecture quizzes that keep me on my toes and engaged. The in class activities help with that too. Definitely a great course for non majors

TAKE THIS CLASS!! Mrs Calliaud is literally the sweetest little French professor and her energy lights up the room every time she speaks. The content is also super interesting! Best class I've taken at Cornell so far

I love Professor Caillaud!She is funny, passionate, about honey bees and wild bees. I really liked the structure of the classwith the activities during lecture and the weekly online quizzes. It kept me engaged and on top of the  material covered and made prep of exams easier.
Professor Caillaud is a great lecturer; she goes the extra step to ensure her students are engaged and interested in the topics she discusses.

She was the best and a fantastic lecturer, very understanding with regrads to needs of individual student, and very responsive. The active learning material during lecture was useful even though it slowed down the pace of the lectures. Great class! We need to save the bees!

A great class about bees, really interesting, and taught with care and thoughtfully. Weekly homework involves pre-lecture videos and readings, plus an online quiz. The final project is awesome and I had a lot of fun with my partners. Loved this class! And professor Caillaud too!

Without question, the greatest professor I've ever had the pleasure of studying under ever. You guys will learn so much being in her class and the commitments for the week are minimal at most. Would definitely take again, and no, this isn't a paid review. Prof. Caillaud is an 11/10.

She has great knowledge of the subject and she is very enthusiastic which kept me very engaged during lectures. Using polleverywhere also helped me stay motivated during class, the weekly online quizzes were super helpful but she never posted the key

Professor Caillaud is so lovely, kind, and intelligent. Her lectures are engaging, and while there's a ton of information, most of the work is just busywork. Her quizzes are kind of poorly written, but she clearly cares so much about her students. Definitely would take again.

Marina Caillaud was the best professor I had in my four years at Cornell. She is caring, kind, intelligent, and she is absolutely hilarious. I took the course in 2019 and was a TA in 2021 and can honestly say graduating without taking one of her courses is a travesty! She has inspired my passion for public health advocacy and I am so so grateful!
just taking that course rn and loving it.
Super kind prof and passionate about material. Need to study for exams but questions are straight-forward if you know the content
Great professor with really interesting lectures. Professor was very accessible and accommodating when I tested positive for Covid-19. This was by far my favorite class at CU so far (i am a senior)

Lectures by professor caillaud included latest information on the topic at at hand and that was really unexpected given that this class was described as a non major, and I definitely had several friends in the class who were not biology majors yet they enjoyed being treated with latest info
amazing lecturer, and I learned so much from her course
very interesting material taught with enthusiasm and care

If you are interested in learning about diseases and epidemics, this class is great for you. The material is pretty interesting but Professor Caillaud often reads off the slides. The tests aren't so difficult, as long as you know the material, but the sections are a little unnecessary.

Great professor-- cares about your learning. This is one of the few classes where I felt like I learned a LOT but didn't feel like I was until I got to the end of the course and realized I know a lot more about the process of epidemiology. She's super nice and very helpful and accessible during OH and through emails.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The course was really interesting. If u read the articles she sends out (there is no textbook), you should be able to get 100s on the prelims. There were some quizzes, but they were not hard at all. There is no final just a final project. Definitely an easy A. I would take it over again if I could.

Professor Levine is passionate about both the course material and its application towards advocacy and political change. Her lectures are very interactive, and she grades based on in-class writing, out-of-class essays, and participation.
Attendance and interaction are 40% of the grade, and there is a lot of reading before each lecture. The assignments are not difficult. The content is interesting for a humanities course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy 2-credit class taken for a GPA boost. Just 2 papers and a final paper. Attendance required unfortunately. Her lectures are so awfully dry. It was an easy A but probably not the most worthwhile class I could take.

I took ENG 3795 Communicating Climate Change, and I genuinely believe it was the most important class I took in Fall 22'. Caroline is personable, lenient, and a good lecturer, and I feel that I came out of the class as a much better climate communicator. There are many essays and readings, but IMO they are all worth your time- 9/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures and demonstrations were clear and engaging. I used to dislike physics in high school but I enjoyed his class. The content can be hard to process, but there is also a lot of opportunities to attend office hours or ask questions after class. Gave me a solid foundation in physics.
Honestly you don't learn physics well from this class at all. I was lucky to have taken physics in high school and completely relied on that knowledge. Incredibly poorly organized and taught class.

Very poorly organized and failed to properly support his students. Office hours were incredibly full, to the point where it could take hours to get a single question answered. Answer keys for discussions and practice exams didn't exist. Heard him use a mocking voice to answer a student who asked a question he thought was easy to answer.

Very eccentric guy, makes a lot of mistakes working out problems during lecture. Gives vague answers to students' questions in class. Extremely poorly written tests and no answer guys given for everything but homeworks.

Phys 2207 has one of the most awful course structure. I paid to learn and they give you a online resources instead of teaching in class and call is "flipped class." Also they don't provide answers to practice exams. Which does not make any sense since they are meant for "practice," but how can I practice without knowing if I am doing things right.

This is the poorest taught class I have ever taken. There are no real lectures, you watch videos recorded by another professor years ago, which are super unclear. He doesn't put the effort into providing practice exams, review, or exam statistics. It's not terribly difficult to do well, I got an A but I still don't understand a thing about physics.

Glenn really cares about his students. Grading scheme is somewhat unclear but has a nice policy that allows a good final exam score to replace one or both prelim scores. Stay up to date with lecture content because it's easy to fall behind.

Professor Case was super accessible outside of class, and never makes you feel dumb at office hours. Having never taken physics, this was a tough class, but still feasible if you thoroughly understand lecture material. Also not calculus heavy, just know basic differentiation and integrals.
Best prof. I've had at cornell so far

Prof made lectures as fun and engaging as he could. Clear he cares about his students and enjoys teaching. Overall the workload was very manageable compared to the prior physics course I had taken but labs were a little long and felt a bit more tedious. The content was interesting if you enjoy physics.
Very engaging lecturer. Also willing to help if needed and always excited to discuss tangential physics topics. Very forgiving grading policy.
Hard class and a lot of assignments per week, but good prof who is passionate about physics and wants you to learn and succeed in the course.

Professor Case was a good lecturer, although the lectures were very slow-paced and pretty boring - very monotone. Thankfully they were pre-recorded and posted so you can speed them up. The material itself is challenging, but Professor Case presented in helpful ways. Exams were fair. Overall an okay class.

Professor Case is kind and passionate about his work. Admittedly, I would get pretty frustrated with the difficulty of the homework, as sometimes the questions were not covered in lecture or instead required a lot of conceptual thinking. However, he is ready to invest time with you at his office hours and he loves student feedback. Grades fairly

Extremely caring professor, incredibly fair and accommodating towards students. Lectures are clear and organized, although the content itself can be difficult and abstract. Exams are very fair if you've put in the effort. Grading policy is extremely generous (several drops allowed for homeworks and quizzes).

Amazing professor, clear lectures, answers questions extremely well. His class is hard, but you will do well if you put in the effort. I never took physics in high school but you don't have to in order to succeed in his class.

Glenn Case is an incredibly fair teacher. The tests and quizzes are derived from his powerpoints. If you can truly understand what is going on in the powerpoint the prelims and finals should be very doable. Clear lecturer but ppt are not simple to understand so make sure to review ppt at your own time
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Why Glenn was downgraded so much. Each time I had a last min question on hw and straightly broke into his office, he would stop to help even sometimes he was having lunch. He was this patient to everyone in our section as I can tell. Even when he couldn't answer a question, he still sincerely tried to inspire you and ask you to teach him back.

Professor Case is a competent lecturer and he places extreme emphasis on understanding. However, he also offers few (and often poor) review materials so preparing for exams was quite challenging, particularly because his exams covered several niche topics while leaving much of the important course material untouched.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Glenn was my professor and my section TA as well. I can say that he is very knowledgable and cares about students learning. I worked extremely hard in this class and I really enjoyed E&M because of him. I don't know why people are complaining about him when half of them don't even show up to lecture.

Terrible professor. Does not cover necessary material in class. Lecture was complete waste of time. Pretends to care but is actually rooting for your demise. Talks a lot about integrity but does not follow through. This class made me despise physics and I would advise anyone debating on taking this class to run away.

Lectures were not clear. Difficult to study for tests as never taught how to solve problems in class and never presented test-type questions. Teaches a lot of irrelevant theory using equations that are difficult to understand. Would not recommend, take auto-tutorial course to save time and stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: AWFUL PROFESSOR AND AWFUL COURSE. Glenn was extremely into explaining the theory behind concepts, yet never covered test level questions in class. Tests were super difficult and hard to prepare for adequately owing to the fact that half of the tests were student-created questions. Problem sets were impossible without help. Incompetent lecturer. BAD
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures were very ambiguous. Did not learn much from coming to lecture, although I do realize it was difficult to cover as much material as this class presents. I just feel his lectures could have been more productive, and that he was not very helpful, more exam-like questions should have been provided in homeworks and in clicker questions.
Really helpful if you talk to him. Not the greatest lecturer but one on one he's very good at explaining concepts.

Very clear and useful lectures. Tests are challenging. There are questions relating to labs and very specific concepts, which are given large point values. If you forget one of many concepts, you will lose significant points on the exam.  There is no curve, but a fair grading scale (class average will be a B). Prelims are optional with him.

Glenn is a nice guy, and is passionate about physics.  He seems like a dry lecturer, but that his actually his dry sense of humor.  The class is hard though, you have to really work for it, since there is no curve.

Glenn presents things clearly in a well prepared lecture, and really cares about students. Lectures may be a bit dry, but do make an effort to know him outside of lecture. He is way more engaging and caring then he may let on from lecture. Really amazing command and passion for physics.
Very clear in lectures, and very eager to clarify and help students understand the materials. Very nice prof, would definitely recommend.
Amazing lecturer, caring, simply one of the best professors Cornell has to offer. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was by far one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. Papers are peer graded and the median grade is the grade you get. There are 6 papers, 6 discussion sessions, and 12 quizzes + lectures. 6 extra credit points are offered. The lectures are quite long but are usually very interesting. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course was enjoyable and Ceci gives thought-provoking lectures. The books are actually interesting, unlike some FWS classes. There's extra credit opps and the 6 essays are peer-graded, so getting an A is totally possible! The 3-hour lectures do get a bit tedious. The class was a bit disorganized (esp. paper deadlines and PollEv quizzing).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but posted wrong essay prompt to Canvas. When students pointed out the mistake, they said to answer the prompt on Canvas. 4 days before the due date, they changed their minds and said to write a different prompt. This was after many students had already completed and submitted their essays. Never taken a class that was so mismanaged.

Ceci is incredibly kind, a great teacher, and extremely well-respected in his field. I haven't met a single person who doesn't like him/his classes. He is flexible and caring and incredibly knowledgable. Get to know him if you can!

Six Pretty Good Books was co-taught by Prof. Ceci and Prof. Macy (and has been taught by Prof. Hancock before). I took it to fulfill requirements, but it turned out to be a REALLY interesting class. Authors included Duncan Watts and Malcolm Gladwell, and some visitedskyped in for Q&A. Definitely talk to Prof. Ceci after class--he is SO nice!!
I learned mostly on my own from doing her homework that lined up well with the exams. Her lectures were...interesting to say the least. Beware the final was harder than the prelims.

Super funny and caring professor, very willing to help even outside of class. Her homework is harder than her actual prelims, and sometimes you wonder in the middle of the exams how the questions can be so simple. Just go to class, do the homework, and do the most basic studying, and you can get at least an A-. Lots of partial credit in exams.
One of the best Professor at Cornell!

Canina is perhaps one of the best professors at Cornell! She cares deeply for your understanding of the principles and will take time to go over the material before pre-lims. Speak with her early, let her get to know you and she will help you along. Also very involved in the entrepreneurship community at Cornell. AMAZING PROF!
Professor Canina is great! She cares a lot about her students learning the material. She also wants students to get comfortable speaking up in class.
Tough but direct and cares enormously about her students. I learned more in this class than any other last semster.

Horrible professor. Her class is completely unorganized. You feel like the class content just get thrown at you from no where. There is no slides available, everything is just talked about and written down. Even the readings, she just says to read them once in class, and then would cold call random student and expect you have done everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Linda Canina was one of my most memorable professors at Cornell. Her unique sense of humor and lecture style kept me engaged throughout the hour-plus lecture, and I felt I learned a lot from her class. She LOVES to call on students- it kept everyone on their toes and definitely made class more interesting. Would highly recommend this course.

Attendance not mandatory, but GO TO CLASS. Book is not as important as her lecture slides. All the concepts on the test are on the slides. Take notes of her explanations in class. Copy everything she writes in class. Redo the problems. Understand the concepts behind each step. Problems on prelims and final  problems from lecture. I learned a lot.

Pr. Canina's lectures are interesting, and should be treated as a supplement to the book. Tests are usually drawn from the book, but by going to the lecture it is possible to determine on what they are going to focus. She obviously cares about the class and students, sometimes to the point of making  disinterested students care about the class.

Fantastic teacher. Smart, funny, and extremely helpful. Class was challenging, but not impossibly hard. Grading is fair, lectures are interesting, and I've learnt a tremendous amount more about Finance. Would definitely take another class with her. One of my favorite classes this semester.
Very Harsh grader. The lectures were very tedious and not overly helpful. Even the most studious will find success in this class to be challenging. I would avoid.

Really great class. One of my favorites if not most favorite one. Material is interesting and teacher is engaging. Class is mainly comprised of case studies and quizzes, none were easy but she explains the material very well so it's easy to follow. Very open for questions/concerns after class ends. Not an easy A class but highly recommend it.
Although this class is not easy, I definitely learned a lot.  Prof was clear and prepared for every class.  She keeps you alert and thinking about the material by calling on everyone!

This is an advanced level class, and consequently is not easy. However, she is very organized and presents the material in a very logic and comprehensive way, which makes it easy to understand. Case studies used are interesting and supplement her lectures very well. Exams are fairly difficult but manageable. Overall, awesome class & great Professor

If you're looking to take an easy class this is not the class for you. However, if you want to learn finance through a challenging yet rewarding course this may be the class you're looking for. Professor Canina is a wonderful person who cares about her students and will go the extra mile in trying to make you succeed. I highly recommend this course
Assumes prior subject knowledge and doesn't prepare students for exams

This is a great class.  If you have any math experience whatsoever, you shouldn't have a problem doing well in this class... although doing the practice homework problems is pretty essential.  Prof. Canina is funny, helpful, and amazingly kind and will work with you to make sure you understand the material well.
Professor AI is a great person. He truly cares about his student, and has a kind heart for grades. Would like to take his class again.
Most practical classes at this university.3838
Very demanding and fair. So informative that many lazy and spoiled children whine about the difficulties that the material of his classes present.
Lectures are useless. And he's grading is really arbitrary. At the end of the semester a lot of people had issues with the grade.
He's a nice guy.  He really cares about his students.  He helps you get a job after graduation if you haven't found one.  He looks mean, but he's really a teddy bear.
Very helpful once you prove you know what you're talking about, very intimidating otherwise.
No Comments
Not a very nice person.
Not very helpful; overly sarcastic

This is NOT a stats class, it's a financial mathematics class. You will be plugging in formulas - start memorizing early. Multiple new concepts are introduced in every lecture and there is no discussion, just a three 75 minute lectures and office hours. Homeworks are not like the lecture examples but do reflect the difficulty of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The lectures are really long and tedious, going over very simple topics for a very long time. However, the homework is nothing like the lectures and are almost impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a nice person, just not a great teacher. Her explanations aren't always what the student asked about. Grading is 90% 3 prelims and 10% homework and you can have a one-page formula sheet on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Homework problems are nothing like the examples done, over and over again, in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Earls is great at explaining things during office hours. I just think the nature of the course and the crammed curriculum makes it harder  to explain everything so easily, especially during a 8:40am lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures are the worst. She just reads off powerpoint so fast, you have no clue which things you need to jot down (if she even stays on that slide for that long), literally my second semester with her and I only understood the first 3 or so lectures of each semester and the rest is just trying to understand her cluttered powerpoint. NoBook4Help

Dr. Earls' lectures aren't the best: she reads a lot through slides; however, during office hours, she does an amazing job to clarify each and every single point of what she explained in her lectures. The homework is based on the material covered in the lectures and the labs. Work through the homework and the exams shouldnt be too hard.

Knowledgeable, approachable, and very helpful at office hours. However, she does speak very fast and go through a ton of information each lecture, so be ready to go through lectures before/afterwards on your own time. Be ready for 40+ slide power points in 75 minutes...
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is not clear, and even some youtube videos make clear points than she did. She basically just read through slides. Morning class!! Attendance is not mandatory but there is a weekly quiz on Thursdays. Appropriate homework load. Not many practice problems. Use R to do homework but didn't require to code in exam. Allow one self-made formula sheet

Dude hasn't taught here for a year...but in light of the below comments, wanted to say one of my better classes. Make an effort, talk to him, and you're fine. He gives a damn and a lot of people end up with crappy grades cause they can't deal with having something asked of them..

He shows up late to almost every class. But more importantly, he is perhaps one of the hardest graders at cornell. I am a great writer, and have always done well in english courses, but in his class, i struggled more than i  ever have in my life. His grading was incredibly harsh and unfair (at one point the class average was a C-).

For some reason, does not give out many A's. Teaches a very hard class, but ENGL 1108 has a high average grade, becasue the other TA's are easier. do not take this calss if you want an easy writing seminar at all - you will do a lot more and harder work than you have to.

great guy. intimidating first couple of weeks but warms up, everyone in the class ended up loving him.  knows his stuff.  put effort in and you'll do well.  shows up a little late sometimes.  more based on fiction than poetry.  great class!
Rockin' bod.  Very strict, but you learn a lot.  Very wide face.  Frequently shows up late.  Not married.  Family lives in Michigan, crazy older brother.

Cecil is challenging but at least he?s doing his job. Unconditional praise is not my idea of education. I?ve seen the stuff my classmates write in peer reviews, and it?s dribble, disrespect for a guy trying to actually teach something. You want the praise that you feel the ?Ivy League? warrants you? Take the time to write a halfway decent essay.
He is condescending and crude.  He is not helpful, in fact, on the contrary, he destroys independence, confidence, and interest levels. He is an embarrassment to the Ivy League.
No Comments

I've had two classes with her and she's wonderful! Can be tough at times but is seriously dedicated to helping you learn the material and is often quite funny. You obviously have to participate a lot since its a language class so I don't suggest taking it early in the morning or you'll be too tired to want to do the exercises
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Flaminia is great; she keeps class lighthearted and fun, but also really helps to jumpstart your Italian.  She knows how to work with students at all levels and is a genuinely nice person.  She takes our work seriously but is always good for a laugh during class.  If you don't slack off, you'll really enjoy and get a lot out of this course
i love this professor!

I hear the intro (101) with her is difficult, but 109 was a blast.  Small class of 25 or so where I made some of my best friends.  Flaminia is a sweetheart and a wonderful woman who sometimes cooks at ZaZa's (it's nice to see her there).  I don't know about lower levels but she's amazing in 209!
Just because she's cute and from Italy doesn't mean that she's a good professor.  Picks favorites, pretty damn condescending, not much of an intellectual.
fantastica. if you can take a class with her, don't hesitate...if you're at least somewhat interested in italian, you'll love her and her class.

Flaminia is amazing, and I've had 3 classes with her...She is so patient, beyond helpful, and has no problem giving As if you pay attention and  keep up with the work. She also has a great sense of humor and seems to really care about her students.
Great professor, awesome classes...she makes Italian worth taking
Best professor at Cornell - brilliant and extremely fair...you have to do the work though....
Flaminia always seems bored in class.  She doesn't seem very smart, but that is probably because she hates her job. She can also take out this frustration by making fun of students in class.
awesome, smart, hilarious
No Comments
Fun, sassy, very intelligent, and good at getting discussions started. Willing to help out, fair grader. Can get testy when provoked.
She's so cute!! She can be tough, definitely hard-core for the Italian dept.
Amazing - best prof at Cornell.  If you do the work she is the greatest!
The worst prof ever
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst courses I've taken in Cornell partly because of the lecturers and partly because the tediousness of lab. Chen conducts the class with professionalism and with an iron fist. She is very strict but don't be afraid because she's like that with everyone. As a lecturer, she was monotonous. Wished she  made the course more interesting.
Two faced. Classes were close to useless. It was all up to the students to cover the work. She ditched lectures very often and handed us to the oblivious TA's. Very moody as well.

Learned a lot in lab and became more confident in my research skills, but she is too strict, especially on those research papers. Good lecturer but course is too time consuming, especially for a measly two credits!
Great class, everything was very clear and well organized. Dr. Chen is really nice and more than willing to help you out.

Professor Chen is extremely dedicated to teaching. Her lectures are well prepared and she will spend a lot of time during office hours helping you out if you need it. She is a very tough grader, but there are 400 students in the whole course, so she needs to be fairly strict. Overall, she is a very intelligent and dedicated asset at Cornell.
She's pretty helpful, especially during office hours. Although quizzes/tests/papers were fair, she could be a tough grader at times. She really wants to help you learn, and it shows in her teaching.

The orginzation in this class is extremely poor. No notes, answer keys, practice answers are posted so it doesn't feel encouraging to learn anyting someone might've not understood the first time. The actual content should be very sraightforward and simple, but due to the organization it makes everything unecessarily confusing and laborious.

Terrible experience, avoid at all costs. Assignments are tedious and do not contribute to learning the material itself. Lectures didn't make any sense because of his completely incomprehensible accent. I had to self-study the entire course because lectures were all useless. Please hire a new prof to teach this class.

One of the best CS profs I've had, really fun class where you actually use what you learn at on the final project, the assignments and the midterm are pretty chill, attendance does matter, prof teaches the material pretty well for everyone of all backgrounds (no ML or ML), and is really passionate about IR system designs and the Kardashians. 10/10.

DNM is super funny and is a great professor. The class gives lots of opportunities to gain extra credit, and the grading for everything is very lenient. You will learn a lot of applicable information retrieval techniques, and although the class might have some questionable/annoying policies, overall it is worthwhile and fun thanks to DNM!

DNM's class is really good in information retrieval if you are in the mindset to learn. He is an understanding and proactive professor that cares about students and learning. He is an expert of the area and makes this class very fruitful.

This was one of the most frustrating classes I've taken at Cornell. Mandatory participation in a large lecture just doesn't make sense. There are milestones for the project due basically every few days, which made the class feel way more stressful than it needed to be. The structure of the course felt more like busywork than meaningful learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easily my least favorite professor / teacher in all the years I've ever been in school, college or lower. His lectures were boring, and he will dock you a full 10% off your final grade if you don't satisfy some minimum bar (not explicitly given) of participation in classes -- no warning, no clarity, full discretion on his part.
condescending and slams you with way too much homework at the beginning of the semester. not a nice person when you talk to him

Overall, class is fine, interesting content, easier CS class. He as a person is not great. Not only is he hard to contact if you are having any issues and need assistance, but also simply doesn't care about his students unless you are doing everything right. Also, if you miss class good luck bc no textbook or note posting which I think says it all
good guy
Really funny and overall interesting guy. Class is fairly easy compared to your average 4000 level CS class.

Ridiculous class policies, he doesn't allow you to use pencils on prelims or write on the actual exam. 

When asked why he said, "If you are looking into a teaching career and want to find out more about the motivation behind each of the decisions, please come to my OH and I'll be happy to share my experience with you."

Class is very popular as it is easy and interesting. Christian is a decent lecturer, but class felt very disorganized (took it in online Spring 2021 semester), and a lot of the times I felt like I was learning something simple in a more complicated way. Overall good class and teacher though, kind of what you put in is what you get out type class.

Fair, quick, clear and thorough (to me, maybe depends on the way you think), nice-ish, can come across sharp/spiky, don't take it personally. Accent and occasional spelling mistakes are hardly an issue. The material isn't crazy or anything that difficult, but the class does take time and some effort. He's very focused on very specific things.
Dont like his personality
One of the best classes ive taken at Cornell. His lectures are interesting/funny and the content is relevant. I Learned a lot.
Quick sharp excellent fair grader

Hard to believe DNM doesn't have his page yet. He is AWESOME (except maybe for his accent?). Great lecturer, lots of information in the lecture, very helpful after class. He is a professor who knows what actual humor is. The project is super instructive and preps you for real-life projects.
great class.

Genuinely the GOAT of hardware accelerated ML. His lectures are so tuff and often go into the math derivations behind a specific method i.e. he proved the decent lemma from the top of his head AND he can write torch code in real time (wow). A very nice guy during OH too, willing to work through examples together for clarification which is awesome.
Genuinely enjoyed almost every lecture. Covered a good range of material, and the problem sets and programming assignments did a decent job of forcing you to understand it.

Most concepts taught in this course are very very useful. If you want to pursue your career as an ML/DL engineer/researcher, this course is basically mandatory, although many concepts are indeed difficult to understand.
Hard core course but moderate exam (for the year that I'm taking).

He is very good at lecturing and clearly explaining concepts. However, CS 4787 has many assignments; I believe he managed to squeeze in 6 programming assignments, 6 problem sets, 5 paper readings, and 2 exams into a 15 week semester.
AWFULLLLLLLLLL

Great lectures, delivered with a lot of passion and vigor. Clear explanations. He is a genius so often time you have to ask him for clarification when he jumps 5 steps in a derivation, but other than that he's great. Exams are hard, but he gives a nice curve

De Sa was super nice, helpful at his OH, and gave awesome print outs of his lecture notes. The programming assignments (in python) build off each other so sometimes your just copy/pasting code and didn't take too long to complete. Overall I learned ML much better than CS4780 and used many of the concepts at my AI/ML internship, highly recommend.

The course covered a lot of interesting topics, but since there were few homeworks and no exams you'll only learn if you engage with the material yourself. Chris was exceptionally approachable and a genuinely caring/considerate person. Lectures were organized really well and not too hard to follow. I highly recommend taking any class with him.

Highly recommend 6787 w/ De Sa for anyone familiar w/ ML who wants to get acquainted with how ML research is conducted on all sides---statistical to hardware. Took away a lot of messages and ended up thinking about/reading material outside of class. He lets students lead paper review lectures, and mainly moderated/clarified things.

De Sa was excellent in Principles of Large Scale Machine Learning. His lectures were clear, organized (notes on website), and very rigorous. I came out of the class feeling like I had strong skills in supervised learning, and good intuition for any related to ML or optimization. Material is used in practice in and is cutting edge for a ugrad course
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He's new to Cornell so, he was not well adjusted to teach CS 4780. Killian is much better and completely took over the course towards the end of the semester.
Chris de Sa is the Josh Peck of the CS department, beware you could get a newscaster incident. Also cares a lot about ML, and is invested in students learning the material.
This professor is angel.
By far the best professor I had my freshman year. I learned a lot about writing as well as broadly disability studies. Would and 100% will be taking again.
Amazing professor, incredibly engaging and very welcoming to students. Would 100% take another class with Dr. Green.

This was such a good FWS to take my first semester of Cornell. Dr. Green cares very much about both the content of the course and his students. He also takes feedback and makes changes to the course based on that. Grading was very clear and based on effort and improvement over the course. He also offered extra assignments for extra credit. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Green was such a nice and encouraging professor. Course demanded a decent amount of work, but grades are labor-based and not quality-based. Aka your grade is an actual reflection of how much effort you put in. Chose interesting books and he tried really hard to make the material interesting. Participation matters. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters
