I will say I did not like how he added Interpreters at the end since he has never taught that before and the TA's did not know it at all so you could barely get help on it. Otherwise, he explains what I thought would be a mid language really well.

His lectures were good but he was just a rude jerk sometimes for no reason. He would be nice to certain people and then randomly he would just choose someone to be completely rude and mean to for no reason. I remember a girl asking a normal question and he framed it like she asked a completely braindead question.

His lectures were pretty good, but outside of class he was rude. He held a review session and told everyone who asked a question to just look at his lecture slides, and refused to walk through problems. I think he would probably be better for higher level cs courses not for someone who has never coded before. lots of assignments and tough grader.

As someone that has never touched code in their life, I have learnt a lot from his lectures. His slides are really easy to understand and the way he explains everything is very concise and understandable. The assignments are pretty heavy in content but they are useful to your understanding.

Cannot teach at all and never knows what he's talking about. Tries to be funny but comes off as condescending. It's very clear he thinks he is smarter than everyone else when he actually knows nothing. Truly the worst person possible to teach CS and I would never recommend him or his classes to anyone else if they care about their mental health.

Clarkson was great in 3110. He wrote the textbook, and is so good at explaining things. He dresses up for Halloween and calls us his little class. Learnt a new language, learned so much about functional programming, and had a great time. Weekly programming assignments, one final group project, 90 minute in class exams. 10/10

Raw professor, Walker White if he was young and taught Ocaml. The workload is not the worst, only 1-2 of the assignments were actually a problem interms of time-commitment, the exams are some-what easier if not comparable to 2110 exams under mulburger, but unlike burger the median is higher, B+ > B, the lecture content is all available online, goat

I feel like a much better programmer after this class, but with an assignment/exam every week and the final project looming a class that should be enjoyable is not. I don't really like Clarkson's energy. The only classes I've experiences noise problems in are his. Attention should be earned, make the lectures invaluable and people will shut up.

Silly guy, but he cares a TON about the classes he teaches. It's clear a lot of effort goes into every assignment and making sure everything is fair.

That commitment to fairness can, in my opinion, go too far sometimes. He won't be lenient

I dont understand the hype around clarkson. He is not a great lecturer and I think he is trying to make CS 3110 more of a weed out class for the major. This semester there were 3 prelims all in an 8 week period lol. Course was very unforgiving with drops for assignments with required lecture attendance. Way too involved.

Professor Clarkson is an engaging lecturer. Discussions and lectures are both mandatory. Absurd workload for no reason 8-10 hours per week.

When students ask for help he is egotistical showing little care for them. His approach to assistance is him focusing on enforcing requirements rather than fostering a deeper understanding.

Professor Clarkson is a great lecturer. Each class was interesting and engaging. However, there was a lack of compassion for students. He wasn't very open to all kinds of questions, which was discouraging to many students. He has very high expectations, and was not understanding towards students who reached out for help.

Entitled, no idea why widely-liked. Boring lectures, useless language, repetitive concepts taught in previous core classes (that are also required!). What a waste of time, and we only live once. In the future I will surely reflect sadly upon all the time I spent on this class that I could have spent elsewhere pursuing knowledge and happiness.
Great professor, one of the best, if not the best, in the cs department. fair tests and homeworks, very knowledgable about the industry. His textbook is also great and easy to read.

Greatest CS professor I've ever had. Coming out of Muhlberger, who I liked in some ways and disliked in others, Clarkson was a breath of fresh air. IDK if I'll ever use functional programming in my job, but there's no denying how I've gone from memorizing code to actually understanding it. Take this class if you'll ever use any CS anywhere.
Michael Clarkson is a ball of glowing radiant sunshine.
Clarkson in cs == Messi in football
nn

Very clear, engaging, and informative lectures. Professor cares about students' long-term goals, pushes you to think like a high-level software engineer rather than just a programmer
Also a fun guy to be around
Really enjoyed his lectures although he didn't do too many along with the exam study guides which I believe he made. No complaints. Cares so much about the course and students.

It just simply does not get better than Prof. Clarkson. The man really cares about his students. Course is well-put together and grading is fair, especially on exams (no surprises). Take a class with him if you can.

Tests were hardest they have been for the past few years, the lectures didn't match the 'hard' questions, consultants CARRIED the class though. The co prof was just as mid. I believe Clarkson is just a mid prof, nothing special about him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Clarkson is a phenomenal CS lecturer who deeply cares about his students. His CS 3110 class will singlehandedly transform the way you look at programming fundamentally. Overall, an amazing class taught by a passionate, lovable, and unforgettable lecturer.
They were not joking when they said taking this class with Clarkson would change the way you think about programming.

His class is difficult for no reason. He makes his exams ridiculously hard this semester, with medians averaging in the 50s. He brags about how hard he makes his tests. Overall, I think he's an overrated lecturer, and that attending his lecture can be entertaining sometimes, but for the most part, you'll end up reading the textbook.
Clarkson is a legend who makes the class as approachable as possible, all in all, phenomenal.

Professor Clarkson is a great lecturer and easy to pay attention to. He explains concepts very well and is clearly very passionate. However the tests for CS 2110 cover a lot of content and are super obscure, so the average is very low in the 70-80s.

Amazing, personable lecturer. His exams are fair, projects are slightly on the difficult side. But he is very accommodating and cares for his students a lot. Also, is obsessed with camels and Taylor Swift.
Great professor
goat

Clarkson is the only professor I've ever rated a 5 and easily my favorite at Cornell by far. Not only is he so accommodating, but he also gives engaging lectures and ensures that help is always available. CS3110 has been my most difficult yet rewarding class.

Honestly, the best prof I've ever had. Prof. Clarkson truly and genuinely cares about his students, and he loves OCaml. I'd take 3110 over and over again if I could because it's such an incredible class.
Really great professor! Would love to take his class again (this semester 3110)

Awesome prof. Actually goated. Made online learning not only doable but also enjoyable. He's also genuinely passionate about functional programming and now I feel like I understand it's strengths and pitfalls exceptionally well. You can't skip this class anyway if you're a CS major but to allay your fears about him, he's a great prof

Phenomenal professor and phenomenal class. Clarkson made online learning so much fun. Every part of the course was so well done. The lectures, assignments, and projects were all extremely interesting and extremely educational. So much respect for Clarkson.

Very clear and easy to understand lectures. Funny and nerdy. Very understanding and sympathetic in COVID times. In my experience (and in the experience of a couple of friends), can come across curt in emails (not as much in Campuswire posts, but increasingly so as the semester goes on). Textbook used but necessity is arguable.
Professor Clarkson is very knowledgable, but his classes are pretty difficult.
Great professor and learned a lot from his lectures. Was also very accomodating when we transitioned online.

Attendance isn't exactly mandatory but I found going to lecture helpful. Class was medium difficulty for me because while assignments are easy, I consistently perform below the mean on exams (final is now mandatory btw). Clarkson is extremely clear, easy to understand, friendly, and nerdy (like D&D kind of nerdy).
He is so great!

Prof. Clarkson is very intelligent and humorous. The assignments are great and fun and are of acceptable difficulty. I learned so much in his class, although I have to admit that I sometimes felt sleepy during the lecture:) Also, it's extremely hard to get an A... even if you are above the median of A range.
I learned so much from his course, it blew my mind. I didn't appreciate the difference between just knowing how to code and actually understanding the principles of cs before taking this course.

Michael Clarkson is the best professor I've had at Cornell. He knows OCaml like the back of his hand, and unlike several other professors, he can explain the material in a very straightforward and interesting way. I highly recommend taking this class with Clarkson.
Simply not the best.
He's the best professor I've ever had. In my entire life. Like, seriously. You have /no/ idea.
Great lecturer.
HE IS THE BEST
The material is very well structured and very, very detailed. The workload is heavy, but this has been my favorite class so far in Cornell.

Great lecturer with a passion for functional programming and even more so for teaching.  Plays a different song related to the class topic each day, and then made a playlist available on spotify at the end of the year.  Some lectures he comes dressed in costumes and makes the lectures very fun and engaging, as well as very easy to follow.
It was alright. I didn't learn much. It's just that I lowkey was taking this ENGRI because it was easy.
Fantastic guy

One of the best profs ive had at Cornell. Was definitely my favorite class ive had this semester, and the content taught was super interesting. very reasonable grading, and he is also so nice and obviously cares about his students!! wish all of my professors were like him, take any class you can with him!!

This was by far one of my favorite classes that I have taken at Cornell. I took it my freshman year, spring 2022 and I learned so much from the class. There were no tests, two debates (which you just had to show up to and you got full credit for being there), weekly psets, and a final project. I learned a lot from this class with no stress.

Prof. Cowen is an amazing professor. I agree with the comment that PSETs could be confusing, but TAs are helpful at office hours. It's designed to be an "easy A" course as long as you do the proper work. NO exams, just a final project in which you design a net-zero carbon home. Spring 2023 median was an A.

Professor Cowen is incredibly knowledgeable on the topic and can explain things very well. Unfortunately, no one pays attention in class, and many people never even showed up until they had to do the final presentation. The homework can also be a little confusing since the professor writes the psets himself. Overall nice dude though.

Took 4350 (coastal engineering). Homeworks were tough to complete, but you learned a lot doing them -- he also gave good feedback and wasn't a harsh grader. Better be ready to pay attention all lecture, his content is fast paced and his notes can be tricky to decipher when they're posted after lecture.
He is a great guy. He will try his best to help you understand the concepts. His homework are hard but he usually doesn't have a hard limit on deadlines. He is also a lenient grader.

His lectures were fun, wish that I could've gone as an audience member only, not a student who needed to take notes and worry about how crazy hard this course was the whole time. Time consuming homework: yes. Tests were extraordinarily difficult: yes. Lab was good enough, I suppose. He needs better TAs too, but everything in this course needs work.

I took CEE fluids instead of BEE's (despite being a BEE major) because I'd heard good things about Cowen. In the end, I was not disappointed. When I was almost on track to fail, Cowen was very encouraging and helpful. He got me through the class. Lectures were sometimes boring, but could be pretty interesting at other times.

Class is pretty tough - the problem sets are long and involved and the exams are pretty difficult, even though they're open note/book.  Cowen is nice though, and the labs are kinda cool.  It seems boring at first, but the class gets more interesting as it goes along.  Textbook was very helpful.
good professor. the lecture notes are really helpful when it comes to test time. also, the best dressed professor in engineering.

He is a nice guy that wants you to do well. But, his tests are far from easy- open note, book and twice as much time as you need. If you work hard, you can do well. I'm still not sure how big the curve is.

Cool guy. makes class fun to go to. Homeworks and labs take time, but tests are easy. He hands out all the notes because his handwriting isnt great, and allthough i havn't gone to office hours, he seems friendly enough.

lectures are basically just reading off the slides (stutters a lot but it's okay we're all human). I assume she changed the way she grades from past years cuz no way people got a A+. Many instances where students corrected her during review, doesn't really know the content confidently herself. Great person but not the best prof. very harsh grader.

While I enjoyed the course content, I felt the delivery was bad. When students asked questions during lectures, the responses were her reading directly from the slides rather than providing clarification to address our confusion. She often got confused by what she was saying herself even though she has taught this class for a while.

This professor is very strict on grading & has been rude to myself and several others in dialogue and email discourse. Many colleagues have noted that what was an easy class now demands perfection of all students and is seemingly forcing the average grade down overnight through the enactment of unfair or potentially targeted strictness on grading.

She is so knowledgable and PUBPOL 3110 is an extremely interesting class and lectures were engaging even if not mandatory. There is a decent amount of homework for the drug project but it is graded very leniently and the tests are pretty fair. Also there are no readings so everything you need to know is on the slides.

PUBPOL 3110 is very similar to PUBPOL 2350 but a lot easier. The prelim and final make up half your grade and are super easy. The remaining half of your grade is a project (group or solo) that takes the entire semester and is also super duper easy. Overall, a great professor and a very passable class.

I took this class five years ago and it still haunts me. My friends and I still talk about it. The material is not communicated well by the professor. She does not seem to care about the students. Ironically a lack of cultural awareness in an intercultural comms class. Save yourself and choose something else.

I took Mindful Intercultural Communication with her for a few weeks before I dropped the course. We did not mention the topic of communication once, and largely focused on tangents and themes that were not described in the syllabus. The course description did a terrible job at describing what actually went on in the course.

Horrible class. Destroyed my GPA. Didn't learn a thing. Students asked her many times to change her approach. She'd reject all of them. This is a social science class, not a STEM class it shouldn't be impossible to succeed. Avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does not care. Unreasonable examination, too little time. Horrible lectures, boring, dense, goes off on irrelevant tangents. Grading is tough. Doesn't heed student feedback. You get tested on her verbal lecture rather than the actual course material. Worst professor and course I've taken. Tried to give her feedback once, and she rejected it.

By far the worst professor I have had at Cornell. Tons of busywork, inconsistent grading, and absolutely no feedback. Lectured directly from the textbook with powerpoints made by the textbook, not her. Also made many microaggressions during a class that is supposed to foster open communication. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Such a waste of time.

I think she is very responsible and trying to be nice to students, but she just has no idea what she is doing. The structure of the class and assignments is a mess. The prompts for the assignments are not clear. The lecture about the textbook is okay but the materials she found or explained just did not make any sense.

Probably the worst teacher I've had so far at Cornell. She is an incredibly boring lecturer, and most of the things she's saying either don't make sense or are just stupid. Makes us write a lot of pointless papers that have no clear prompt but are graded very harshly. Very poorly organized course. Mean professor. Overall just bad.
She knows the topic extremely well and the state of the current literature in the field. I have learnt a lot about social network analysis whilst taking this class.
She does not care about teaching at all.
No Comments
Awful teacher.  She seems uninterested in the topic and everyone sleeps through the class.
Tough accent, talks fast, sometimes isn't very clear, goes off on tangents.

Prof Connelly is a super passionate mathmatician and has a deep understanding of geometry. Unfortunately those things help very little when you're taking a calc 1 class with hundreds of other students and exams on the basics. He'll give interesting lectures that will be of no aid whatsoever to you on the homework and exams.
Sweet guy and has a deep passion for math, but lectures are incoherent, not on topic, and hard to understand.

My main source of suffering this semester, don't take this class unless you need to. Connelly is nice, but his lectures are useless so you'll have to self study everything. If you haven't taken Calc II before (like me), support sessions are where you actually learn. HW is hard but graded on completion, tests are easier but inconsistently graded.

Worst class Ive ever taken across all departments at Cornell. Instructor and TA are awful at teaching grading and communicating. 1) endless mistakes in lectures and in office hours and not releasing homework sols 2) pointlessly harsh rubrics, slow grading 3) neither Prof nor TA reply quickly to emails unless they need something from you

As people are saying, Connelly is very smart. But, his lectures are awful; he is unclear, makes tons of mistakes (AND BY TONS I MEAN TONS), and asks students for help constantly. Exams and hws are unfairly require a deep understanding of geometry. You will often never find out the answer to homework problems because there are no solutions posted.

Incredibly smart mathematician with many accolades. Will spend more time talking about his previous research and accomplishments than teaching material, especially that of the textbook assigned for the course. Interesting guy, miserable class

DO NOT and I repeat DO NOT take a class with this professor. The lectures are incoherent, no lecture notes are posted, no hw solutions are posted, hws are graded very harshly, and the course is overall a mess. This course has been a true bonding experience for the students... The professor is a nice and smart person but really not equipped to teach

DO NOT take a class with him!! Not only do we barely learn anything in lecture, but the textbook doesn't even help with the harshly graded HW. There is also no way to tell how you're doing in the class... the syllabus is "rough" and the prelim had a 66% max. score -meaning no one will pass this course (he didn't disclose any curve, or the median!)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Connelly is a certainly a phenomenal mathematician but just an alright lecturer. His lectures were often characterized by rambling about his field which was fine until it became unclear what we should know versus what he is simply rambling about. You'll definitely need the textbook to set straight what you need to know to pass.
Prelims were impossible as well as his lectures

MATH 1920 requires a type of visualization and thought that new students had not experienced yet. Connelly's lectures attempted to help with this visualization, but he was underprepared and often went on unrelated notes for far too long. He also loved strange application questions on quizzes and the head TA was rude. Nice guy though
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although Professor Connelly is undeniably smart, his lectures were very confusing and he went on long, unrelated tangents for about 30 minutes every class. On top of that, his quizzes and tests were extremely difficult. The head TA also wasn't great. She responded to ED posts three days late and was often rude/unhelpful. 1920 was just poorly run.

Professor Connelly is someone who deeply cares about his students. His prelim 1 and prelim 2 were quite challenging. The final was somewhat easy. Your grade in his multi class depends on how much effort you put into learning the material yourself. I made the mistake of not focusing early because of past multi experience. Don't make the same error.

Professor Connelly is a real gem. I was lucky to be in his MATH1920 class. He has a passion for teaching. He continues to teach, even though he could have retired a long time ago. I respect Professor Connelly a lot. He sometimes messed up in lecture, but he always caught himself. Boffa prelims were hella chedda, so you should be bing chilling.

Wow what a ride. A semester with Connelly felt like a roller coaster and I mean it in a bad way. Despite having prior knowledge coming into this class, I felt like Connelly's lectures actively untaught me MV. In short, he's a nice guy with a genius understanding of math, but he is god-awful at conveying the material. If possible, take Belk instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy but horrible teacher. Makes so many mistakes during lecture it's hard to know whether or not the notes you're taking are worth anything. Tests are extremely hard and aren't really related to the stuff he does in class. The textbook will help much more than going to lectures. If you can avoid it never take a class with this guy.

Connelly is passionate about his subject but he lacks ability to teach those who have never encountered multi. The textbook only helps if you're able to grasp concepts from reading but 1920 is a very visual course in order to understand. I watched prof. Leonard on YouTube who explains very well and I'm still failing. If never taken multi stay away
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tests are unnecessarily and ridiculously difficult. It seems as if already knowing multivariable calculus was a prerequisite for the class

Nice guy but horrible instructor. You basically 100% learn on your own + get a harder exam than usual. Don't expect good reviews on discussion either. No one is helpful besides the boring textbook. Took Multi in high school and still struggling with this class.

Mislead students with practice exams that werent relevant for the prelims at all, confusing lectures and the homework doesnt help practice the material at all. Lectures are confusing and not relevant to the subject material, and exams require a very deep understanding of the material that he simply doesnt provide. By far the worst math class

Math used to be my favorite subject before I took this course. I took Multivariable Calculus in high school, but taking Conelly's class makes me feel as if I am actively unlearning the material and studying a foreign language. His lecture style is confusing and disorganized. His way of explaining complicated subjects is highly unintuitive.
just simply can't learn anything from his lectures.... i guess im not alone

Professor Connelly is a really nice and kind professor, but not a great instructor. His lecture never highlights the concept we should grasp in the unit, and he always goes off track and starts to talk about some other theory or proofs. Half of the class study on their own or go to other lectures.

Brilliant guy, but absolute horrible teacher. Constantly makes mistakes during lecture and asks the students whether he did something wrong. Teaching style seems obsolete. He attempts to explain quadric surfaces using his fingers, whereas the better professor, James Belk, is reasonable and uses a projector to show the 3d plot. TEXTBOOK > CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Connelly is a real gem. I am lucky to be in his MATH 1920 class. He has a passion for teaching. He continues to teach even though he could have retired a long time ago. I respect professor Connelly a lot. He sometimes messes up in lectures, but he always catches himself. His exams are challenging, so you should know the material very well

Professor Robert Connelly has changed my outlook on how I perceive calculus and inspired me to change my major to mathematics. His office hours are amazing, and his way of teaching is extremely clever and simple. Please do take this class if you wish to build a stronger connection with the subject.
amazing prof!! do it you wont regret. GPA BOOSTER!!!

Though obviously an expert, Prof. Connelly had incredibly disorganized lectures that were extremely hard to follow. He made frequent mistakes and was often forgetful. The homework and quizzes are very difficult and ask you to go far beyond what's actually taught. I learned much more from Khan Academy and the textbook than lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Tough grader--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great person, I like him a lot. However, his lectures are so scattered and he teaches nothing relative to his quizzes/tests at all. I stopped going to lectures all together and just relied on the textbook. He makes lots of mistakes in lecture; he's funny and cares, though. If you have no prior experience with material: steer clear.

Professor Conelly dresses like a wizard, and is extremely well respected. His lectures were tad boring and were not well organised but, he is good during OH when you come with specific questions. The HW given was tough, but he offered OH 4 times a week. He is extremely caring, especially during the COVID crisis, he made stuff more lenient for us
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Robert Connelly is one of those rare instructors who really cares about his students. He cares about your success and the knowledge you take away from his class. I took ODE with him and although he doesn't make the class easy, he doesn't make it difficult either. Just show up, do the homework, and take the class seriously. 11/10 would recommend.

Really just a terrible professor. The only thing that saved this course was that another teacher for the course and the TAs in the course were trying to make the tests at least somewhat reasonable and allow students to pass. Were it not for the help of my TA's, I would have failed this course and learned nothing because Connelly is that bad.

Terrible lecturer.  He's obviously a brilliant mathematician, but he cannot for the life of him explain even simple concepts. Lectures are completely disorganized, and he makes tons of mistakes in examples. He probably makes sense to people to whom math comes intuitively, but for 90% of the class this isn't the case. Exams were ridiculously hard

Professor Connelly is the greatest teacher I have had, and takes a genuine interest in the success of his students in and beyond class. He is one of the most respected topologists in the country, and he uses his reputation to benefit his students. Plus, he looks dresses like a mystical wizard of math!
Makes several mistakes and is known as "Goth Moses" by among the students. Lectures are essentially useless... READ THE BOOK

To be fair I came into this class with prior experience in multivar. He does a great job conveying the eloquence behind the theorems being taught but he's not the best at teaching basics, which is tough if this is your first exposure to the material. Beyond 1920, hes incredibly accomplished (check wikipedia) and wears great outfits so thats cool.
Have to use the textbook to learn the material well.

Sometimes has a tough time communicating exactly what he is trying to say, but gets the job done at the end of the day. Very understanding and super generous with final grades. Bomb a prelim? It's okay if you do good on the final he'll bump you up at around a B
Connelly is one the few gems of the mathematics department. His wit and intellect is unmatched. And don't get me started on his fashion! So bold and progressive! A true academic!

Literally an atrocious professor.  Made absolutely no sense, frequently made mistakes in lecture, teaches straight out of the textbook which is also horrendous and he doesnt understand either, and is terrible at judging when the class is or is not following the lecture. Just watch the online lectures with Strang at MIT, start praying, and drop.

Going to Bob Connelly's office hours is a privilege that increased my understanding of mathematics by orders of magnitude. Doing proofs with him on the board is a humbling experience, because he is supremely gifted, but the benefit of the experience more than makes up for the blow to your ego.
Connelly frequently made mistakes on the board while lecturing.  He is not a clear lecturer.  Class would have been significantly easier if I knew what was going on.

Prove it was a small class and it's really a gentle introduction to higher level maths. Covers basic analysis, algebra, and geometry with a lot of emphasis on writing the proofs correctly and with good style. Office hours helpful, used an online textbook.

As others have said, Connelly is a boring lecturer. His examples were all theoretical and not what we would see on homework nor tests. He basically teaches right out of the textbook. He did seem to improve throughout the semester, however, which is good, because it implies that he does listen to student feedback, but by then, it was too late.

Connelly is a nice guy, but not the best teacher. I started going to the other professor's lectures after the first few weeks. The hardest part of 1920 is the volume of material they expect you to learn, so make sure you stay caught up and its much more manageable. Multi is actually pretty cool but unfortunately they don't present it the best way.

His lectures are littered with mistakes, and I genuinely think I learned less by going to them. I stopped going to them half way through the semester and my results were the same. Luckily, MATH1920 is a really easy class now since they got rid of prelims.
He tries... but that's not saying much. He will teach material incorrectly, and he constantly asks students if he made a mistake.
Literally and figuratively the worst math teacher I have ever had.

Terrible, inadequate teacher. He definitely does try, but he is always unable to convey anything without making tons of mistakes.  I used to love math in high school. Connelly singlehandedly killed my interest in mathematics.

Took this spring 2013, first 3000+ level math class. Really developed a lot of tools and perspective that helped me with other math classes later on. Lectures can be a little dry but still worth listening to and was helpful for office hours. Has a low rating for teaching boring classes like math 1920 to engineers.
Literally just the worst.

This class is hell.  Not only does he not teach anything relevant, it is completely incomprehensible.  After spending the entire class on a single problem riddled with mistakes, he simply says "well, this isn't right, but you get the point".  Avoid this class and this professor all together if possible.  HORRIBLE!!!!!!

He seems nice, but his lectures are riddled with enough mistakes to make even the most patient students want to bash their skulls against their desks.  He's very theoretical.  Also, he has a helix fetish.

His lectures are very unclear. He does not pick very good examples. He is not very good at answering questions.  My TA was terrible.  Way too theoretical.  Odds are, your book will become your professor.  There are 2 other profs for this class, I would recommend that you try them all the first week of class to see who is the best  for you.

Connelly is not very good at explaining anything.  Lectures lack any sense of flow, he chooses bad examples, and he is bad at helping people understand if they have questions.  Do not save homework for the last minutes, it always takes a while.  There are two other profs that teach the course, try them instead.

Connelly is a good guy, but an awful teacher. Makes many mistakes during lecture, often disorganized and unclear, rambles on topics completely irrelevent to course, and often pauses during lecture to try to fix his mistakes. His lectures are usually near-empty as everyone realizes its useless

I found the shear quantity of mistakes Connelly would make while teaching completely unacceptable. A professor should never have to ask his students if everything he put on the board is correct. By the end of the semester, most of my class was attending other lectures because Connelly's was completely useless.
His lecture was totally useless.  He generally spent half of each lecture attempting one example several times, letting students correct him all the way through.

Connelly is such a nice guy, but not a good teacher, especially for engineering math. He is very theoretical, spends way too much time proving things, and is very unclear. He'd probably be a fantastic theoretical math prof, but he's a terrible engineering math prof
single handedly ruined calculus for me. he's a nice man and he means well, but he's crazy. says the strangest things in class and hes very confusing. useless going to his lecture.

Connelly is a great guy, but I would not recommend taking his lecture. I'm currently in his 9:05 lecture, and I just sleep-in because I feel the extra hour of sleep will benefit me more than going to his class. Enroll in Matsumura's lecture.

He's OK - he is highly theoretical although the class is intended for engineers. He also makes frequent mistakes during lecture, and isn't really that clear. He's acceptable, but definitely try to get a better lecturer for 1920 if possible.

He loved to prove theorems and only devote a small amount of time to teaching what you need to know for the HW and tests. His explanations weren't very helpful but at least he brought in a few items to illustrate a few concepts in 3D. Best to take what he teaches and fill in the many conceptual gaps on your own.

If you know math VERY well and you just want to hear derivations of formulas and be challenged with complicated questions, this is the teacher for you. If you actually want to learn, especially if your learning from scratch, like me, find someone else.
Friendly and approachable... but too damn theoretical.
Pretty Unclear
No Comments
sometimes hard to understand since he's very theoretical but his lectures are still relatively enough with his dry humor
Hard to understand. Doesn't teach material well. Goes off on wild tangents.
Though I stopped attending lecture a month into the course, for the the ones I did attend he seemed simply alright...not terrible, but definitely not great.
Great prof
Despite being a challenging course, it is one of the best I have taken at Cornell. Fors was also awesome.
Good lecturer, and his tests are quite doable if you study. I never opened the textbook.

um everyone loved him but honestly i did not. his lecture tho was pretty straight forward. his handwriting is amazing and all. he gives cool uncle vibes - seems approachable but he really isnt. his tests people say it's easy but one MC is 10 points and no partial credit. I got 4 MCs wrong and that was like -27 points lolz. but happy i had him tho

Going in, I dreaded orgo, as do most. I left the course feeling this was a transformational experience. I am totally convinced Prof. Coates wanted everyone to excel in the course, and his love of science and teaching was inspirational. I wish the course were smaller so I felt like I could get to spend more individual time is my only regret.
Super fun and sweet professor who really wants to help students learn. Lectures are engaging and exams are fair
Hard class but Coates does a great job explaining complicated topics. I get the sense he deeply cares about his students. I am enjoying this class as one can enjoy Orgo!

Lectures were clear and very useful. Online help sessions were spectacular - highly recommend viewing them. Amazing professor and very caring and dedicated - I had no idea he is also one of the worlds best scientists!
Orgo itself is difficult. But his lecture is very clear and summarize textbook very well.

Its actually incredible to think that not only is he extremely distinguished, having won more awards than one can count and is one of the top 100 chemists in the world, but he is extremely caring and compassionate torwards his students. Coates really cares about his students and does the best job possible of doing his best to make sure we succeed.
Great guy - I like how he was always willing to help. Loves chemistry and teaching.

Professor Coates is one of the best lecturers at Cornell, and certainly does a great job teaching organic chemistry. He is extremely clear and organized, and is genuinely one of the nicest professors you will meet. His research focuses on polymer synthesis (and he's extremely good at it), so know those polymers and transition metal catalysts!

this prof views his role as an enabler, not a gatekeeper. no doubt this is a hard class, but the lectures are clear and organized. the Friday help sessions are amazingly helpful - relaxed informal setting. first exam was more than fair - if you attend lecture and do the homework you should do well. TAs are all very helpful.

One of the greatest lecturer who knows the material and knows how to explain them. Never fell asleep because his explanations were golden. And his my advisor and is a very down to earth person. I'm glad I had him for orgo.

Arguably one of the best professors I've had yet at Cornell. Coates is the man. He is very clear and organized in his lectures (and often funny), and he wants to see you do well. Difficult course in general due to the material, but much more bearable with Coates. Very down to earth guy. I highly recommend him.
Hes fun and nice. The class is hard.
Great course by a dedicated prof. Nuff said.

Prof Coates is my favorite teacher at Cornell so far.  He was a great guy and teacher.  He genuinely cared about teaching the students and has a great personality while lecturing. =)  Very much recommended for Orgo.
Absolutely great prof. ZVery challenging, but can be conquered if you attend classes and do the homework. Exam averages are ~60 - don't believe the "too easy" banter!

Not a bad orgo prof. His voice is kind of boring and it makes you want to go to sleep. The man does have a thing for polymers and by the end of the course, you're gonna need to know, like, 600 reactions.Regardless of the professor, orgo is still gonna be hard. So BEWARE of all all these high ratings! Good LUck!
Just Awesome!  Study hard and it should pay off.
Way easier than any other Chem course! Total "make it easy so they like me" guy.
Very amusing, friendly professor. His tests were fair, but still very difficult. His lectures were very clear and his demos were awesome. Ganem never had demos...

Probably about as good as orgo can be: clear lectures and fair tests. Both in terms of knowledge learned and grades achieved, you get what you put into this class; just study hard and pay attention to lecture. Also seems like a pretty nice person out of class.

I love his lectures, so easy to follow.  He's so willing to help the students, not bring them down like some premed courses do.  I don't know if he's a good person, though, after a certain incident in lecture.  But, that doesn't affect his teaching.  He's a great TEACH-er.

PROFESSOR COATES IS THE BEST SCIENCE PROFF I HAVE HAD EVER ! he makes the classss sooo much fun .. he is a kind guy with a lovely personality .. he is extremely helpful in any way and cornell is luck to have him ! i luv organic chem cause of him . his test are VERY FAIR .. and yes.. if u think they are hard,,, u need to be working harder!

ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS I HAVE COME ACROSS AT CORNELL...EVER PERIOD. HE IS FROM THE WEST COAST, AND HE IS VERY LAID BACK AND COOL ABOUT ORGO CHEM. HE MAKES A USUALLY STRESSFUL CLASS, FUN AND VERY INTERESTING. DEFINITELY TAKE HIS CLASS :)

very nice guy. almost like a dad. :).lectures are important cause he takes stuff directly offf off them for exams.problem seys are so much earsier then for 357. tests are VERY FAIR and if you think they are hard, then u need to be working harder. seems to be easier than 357. moves slower than 357 . lovely personality !

A good teacher. Not as good as Ruttlege, but his tests were easier (note: this doesn't mean the curve gets any easier!). Also, he follows the book more consistently than does Ruttlege, which could be good or bad depending on how you look at it. Overall, I really enjoyed him as a teacher, even if he's not as hilarious as Ruttlege.

Well, I wouldn't say this was easy, with exam scores in the single digits. However the tests were very fair, with questins ranging from easy mult choice to nearly impossible 'make the molecule'. Lookin back, I feel I learned alot about the stuff around us is made. Coates was very clear about the materialand his expectations. Great course. Nuff said
As good as orgo is going to get. Super nice guy as well.

Coates took all the challenge and excitement out of orgo.  His class consisted of memorizing reactions (mostly reagents and products) and spitting them back on the test in an easy, predictable manner.  You'll like him if you are a typical premed who hates orgo and loves to memorize things and spit them back without really understanding them.

Ok, so I didn't expect to be entertained by Coates as I was in 357, 358 was what I originally expected from an orgo class. dull sense of humor and all, he was extremely organized in presenting material and tests were VERY fair. of course it's hard... it's orgo! what do you expect?  Anyone saying his tests were unfair obviously didn't study enough.
Orgo sucks and I hate it but Coates is a good professor and makes it tolerable. He is very clear and is an all around nice guy. Much more organized than Ruttledge.

i hate him. all he cares about are his stupid polymers. he doesnt know what mechanisms are. his notes are straight from the book. he doesnt explain WHY things work like ruttledge bc he doesnt know, and just expects you to memorize things. like his polymer rxns. and hes NOT HOT. his mouth annoys me.

Coates is awesome! Orgo still sucks, but he is soo clear. He presents the material in an organized manner, he describes things well, plus he's a really great guy. His tests are very fair and not too hard. He really tests on the material he taught us. Best chem prof yet!!
Decent professor. not as crazy as rutledge but crazy enough. good guy though
I have to say that this class was one of the worst I've ever taken.

I suppose the rest of these pre-meds are rating him well just to be cut throat, but be warned!  He's an absolutely terrible professor with absolutely no remeeming qualities to him.  His lectures useless and his tests are extremely unfair.  This person should be kept away from teaching at all costs.
No Comments
Good teacher. Puts more emphasis on his teaching than on his research. Nice guy and always helpful.
My favorite quote from Geoff:  "Put the strap on, do the reaction."  :)

I took orgo last year, and I went to coates' last class on slope day to get ****. I gotta say, geoff's a pretty swell guy and a great teacher. I love how he had fun with the **** kids in class. Keep an eye on this man, he's a winner.
Coates is a great teacher. His lectures are clear, his tests are manageable, and he's overall a nice guy. Consider yourself lucky that he took over for meinwald.
Clear, concise, interesting lectures. He definitely wants us all to learn the material and do well.
I LOVE GEOFF COATES!
Coates is a great teacher, he really cares about the material and the well-being of his students. In Chem 301 he helped us develop interesting projects that were beyond the scope of any textbook.

Like oh my GOD!!! I thought I was going to hate organic lab. However, with the help of the like hottest teacher at Cornell, I loved it.  The smells were exotic and the research project that we did was phat.

Dr. Coates was probably the smartest professor I've had at Cornell so far.  His research is very impressive and if he keeps it up he is on track to win major awards.  Organic chem II lecture was very clear, with challenging but fair exams.
Best professor I've had at Cornell. Cares both about teaching and chemistry in general.  Very helpful at office hours, and responds quickly to e-mails.

What an amazing professor. He's funny and clearly passionate about Latin America and his passion is infectious. He has a great way of reframing events you may be familiar with but in a new light. The reading is heavy and a lot but definitely interesting. His slides were extremely helpful and he's very kind. Highly recommend!!

Craib is a great lecturer and teacher–even if you're not knowledgeable about or particularly interested in history. His lectures are thorough, incredibly informative, and organized in an appealing fashion. Try to participate–that does mean a lot (but I think with the atmosphere he creates, you'll want to). Computers are allowed.

Take this course! Craib did a great overview of US foreign policy in Latin America. I believe his slides, however, were overfilled. He's very passionate about the subject, but it was a little hard to retain information on places and people (there were so many!). Loved the information, but good thing there was no real exam. Great, but confusing.

For HIST 1951. Class isn't hard and I an easy A if you put in the work (which is a lot). However, there's a lot of reading so if you don't want to read a LOT, do not take this class. Attendance is mandatory for lecture and discussion sections. Lecture is incredibly annoying because the assigned readings tell you the same stuff in more detail.

Professor Craib was very informative and ensured that all lectures were interesting and pertained to the topic at hand. Professor Craib was very accessible outside of class and provided important feedback on written assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: amazing

pretty great lectures with a lot of information. you need to be quick about taking notes in it. you'll need them cause the readings aren't as helpful for the tests themselves. Attendance isnt mandatory by him but actually is. Though they help for the essays which are a lot. Nice guy and very helpful. Essays vary in length and get bigger later on.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is an amazing lecturer and gets to know each student. Lectures have a lot of material in not a lot of time, so get ready to write quickly. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you won't learn the material otherwise. Three papers, one midterm, and about 50 pages of reading a week. Highly recommend as an into history class.
Great professor and a really smart guy. Highly recommend any class taught by him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Ray Craib is a fantastic professor. He's a good lecturer and a really nice grader. I was really nervous about taking an essay-heavy class but he's so sweet and super helpful. You can always contact him after class and he's passionate about everything he teaches. I would totally recommend!
The absolute boy.

Very engaging, clear, direct, approachable and competent professor. Material was not my area of interest but he made it much better and had some great stories that he wove in. Very smart but not alienating.

Colonial Latin America isn't my cup of tea, but Craib made it well worth my time. Had trouble paying attention in lecture, but the discussions were fantastic. The reading was difficult, but it really made sense once he explained it and he exposed us to a wide range of sources. I came out of the class with a clear sense of an overall narrative.

Excellent professor. Lectures are interesting and flow nicely. He does go over the time limit sometimes. Only take 1960 if you are a confident writer; assignments are challenging but graded fairly. Be sure to check out a textbook primer when writing papers!
Really interesting guy.  Talks a little fast but is able to maintain your intrest.

Sharp as a knife and fun, too. He's the only prof I had who ever gave me reason to go into the Rare and Manuscript collection. He holds class outside sometimes (a def plus). He picks really good readings. And he knows how to lead a seminar better than anyone else I had at Cornell.

A great professor. He encourages questions & makes time for discussion. He doesn't use  PowerPoint but his lectures are clear & he provides outlines beforehand. He has a good personality & once in a while he will share a really funny personal story. If you do the readings & write your essays carefully, you'll do really well.
Lots of reading--but great class. Craib explains hard readings really well.

I think that Professor Craib is a pirate. He wears tiny tight pants, poofy shirts open far down his chest, and a gold hoop earring. Also, I borrowed his watch once. He's one of the few teachers I would take a 10:10 class with.

prof florea is so knowledgable, funny, and caring that it's impossible not to enjoy this class. that being said, this is a difficult course with lots of reading and tough/sometimes unclear grading. but imo it's worth the hard work, esp if you have any kind of interest in soviet history

You'll definitely learn a lot. But don't expect to do well. The grading is very strict. Reading assignments are a bit unbalanced, sometimes you'll be reading 3-5 pages for a lecture and other days you'll be reading an entire book. The material does have a unique character which sets it apart from boring textbooks and hard to read academic texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Florea was very passionate about what she taught, and I really enjoyed her class. The grade was made up of 3 papers (4 pages), a final paper (arond 15 pages), and short reading reflections before each class. The grading could be a bit tough, but just make sure you put effort and really think through before writing.

Florea was super caring (we got free treats!) and is one of the best history professors, imo. She may grade a little harshly, but the feedback is so good (a rarity!). Also, borders are awesome, so the class was very interesting. If you are passionate about debates on sovereignty and migration, take this course. But be prepared for one book a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Sweetest professor ever! Great lectures, great feedback on papers, etc. This is a class oriented towards non-history majors IMO, but if you're a humanities major getting an A isn't difficult considering the short length of the papers in this class. Professor/TA are also available and give great advice for papers.
Really good class and professor!

Professor Florea is a great lecturer. She approaches difficult topics through literature, primary sources, and a good dose of humour. The selected material is very interesting and contributes to your growth way beyond her class.

She genuinely cares about your progress and you as a person.

Florea was one of the most passionate and caring professors I've ever had. Her lectures are amazingly engaging, and she makes difficult topics easier to navigate. Very accessible outside of class, Professor Florea always helped spur discussions with insightful, leading questions that challenged us. Fantastic class and professor!

HIST2958 is very well structured. The materials are great + the lectures are super engaging and packed with fascinating content. You're also graded on a lot of small manageable assignments, which I found very convenient. Also, Prof. Florea is a top-notch instructor. She transmits her passion and genuinely cares about your progress. I'd enroll again

Professor Florea is fantastic. The lectures are super interesting, she does a good job of integrating student discussions into a relatively large class, and she and her TAs give great, clear feedback on the papers. It is not an easy course, though, so be prepared to do the readings carefully and revise your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cornell is lucky to have her. Prof. Florea puts her students first and is always full of advice and encouragement, even a semester after the class. If you're looking for a survey of Soviet history, take the class. There is a LOT of depth and work but the films and novellas she's picked really provide a human element forgotten in other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof Florea is so nice she genuinely cares about you doing well and understanding her class so is always available to chat. Tough grading (median grade B+) but if you pay attention and are interested in the material you'll have no problem getting that or higher. Not a class to take if you don't like the subject though because lectures are in depth
Unnecessarily difficult class. Would NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was for INFO4145: Professor Forestier is really nice and accommodating. He has some interesting insight to offer about privacy and the data economy and is humorous. Grading is not too difficult, especially if you just show up and do the work. I learned a lot in this class while also not being stressed out which was really pleasant.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Taking his Privacy and Security in the Data Economy and he is very knowledgeable and passionate.
Extremely rude and condescending. Don't bother asking questions on ed discussion if you aren't ready to be criticized and patronized
I loved Networks 2 as a class. The matter was very interesting and Professor Cristobal Cheyre Forestier is sweet and accommodating. Would recommend.

His lectures are boring (probably because the class started during the COVID Zoom class era) and the grading is incredibly harsh. Be prepared to show every single step of your work or lose three-quarter of your points.
his tests are awful. everyone fails them. i do not understand the point of making a test to fail

Oh, Crocker. Think of this class as the real estate minor weed-out course. We started the semester with 65 students and ended it with 16. You'll probably get a 25 on a test but don't worry... that'll be the median (heavy curve). Tedious psets & opaque grading. Rambling, nonsensical lectures. If you really want the minor, just get thru this class.

If you don't enjoy his class and work then you probably shouldn't consider a career in real estate. six credits with this professor and you'll have a far better understanding of the business compared to your counterparts also looking for entry level work. Im extremely grateful to have professors like him still at Cornell, as they are a dying breed.

Worst class I've ever taken. Prof tries to pass humor off as "dry" but just comes off rude and arrogant. Case studies are difficult and take days to complete; he doesn't lecture on the material needed until AFTER they are due. The midterm was ridiculously difficult and was NOT ON THE MATERIAL he covered in class. Makes you PAY for lecture notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You will learn a lot about RE. Unfortunately, Liu is conceited, sarcastic and frequently disdainful of students when they ask questions. Cases can be useful but too long & repetitive, as well as contain a lot of mistakes. Exams require you to remember arcane details from 1100 slides as opposed to whats actually important. Disappointing.

Very knowledgeable professor. Probably the most content-heavy class I have taken in my life but it was worth it! Employers would literally hire you after looking at the cases he will make you do. The people who have given sub-par reviews probably got Cs, which makes up for like 30% of his usual class.
If you want to learn real knowledge about real estate, take this course

Crocker Liu assigns a disrespectful amount of homework. It's content is not hard, but it's poorly written, unclear, and teaches you essentially nothing. Also, it takes more hours to complete than all other classes' work combined--hence, DISRESPECTFUL. Lectures are cursory and unnecessary. He makes you buy his slides instead of posting them online.

Professor Liu wants to give too much to the students. The AVERAGE score of the class of midterm is 32.4% of total score. And during the final exam, he started the exam 20min before the official time. Then during the test he announced the exam duration shortened from 3 hour to 2:30. But it doesn't change much of the result even with more time
The worst professor that I have ever had in the entirety of my Cornell career. So disorganized, I completely wasted an entire semester taking his course.

The poor reviews here are mainly for when he teaches things outside his area of research. For AEP 5510 Symmetry in Materials Physics / Applied Group & Representation Theory, his lectures are full of interesting content and delivered passionately. Notation can be a little confusing and the structure a little disorganized, but overall, pretty good.

Really insightful when it comes to teaching about his research field, perovskites; and gives you intuitive ways of thinking about concepts without doing too much math.  The course organization was great.
He cares about students' workload and does not want to cause stress. He genuinely loves solid state physics, but he gets a bit tongue-tied explaining things sometimes. :-)

2217 is a little easier than 1116, which is good. Fennie is strange. He brought cake to the final. He spells liek ths and loses track of time sometimes. Grading is also a little suspect. Fennie has gotten better, but he's still not great. He has a good grasp of the material and answers q's. If you take this class, Scott Hughes is a good reference.

Made a tough subject next to impossible through his hack-saw grading techniques and misguided, repeated and indistinguishable lectures. Made my semester pretty darn miserable. You may need to higher a professional to decipher his handwriting. Absolutely brilliant researcher, but should never set foot in a classroom.

Fennie is a good guy. As a prof he is mediocre at worst and decent at best. Gets confused sometimes during derivations. Lectures sometimes lack direction, sometimes easy to get bored. His lectures were based almost entirely on the "optional" textbook, Griffiths, while the only thing he used the "required" text (Purcell) for was homework.
Fennie is a nice professor. He does have a tendency to get kinda lost in some of his proofs, but he does generally know what he's doing.

Really not as bad as some of the other reviews on here make him seem. Overall, lectures are somewhat helpful, but make sure to read to book to reinforce the concepts. Fennie can be a bit unorganized, but he's still a decent prof

Professor Fennie is a good guy, but I think there's a lot he could do to make the class better. He knows the theory well, but his lectures sometimes lack focus and direction. He tries to answer every question, but sometimes his answers are too abstract. And his tests are ridiculous compared to the Problem Sets.

His lectures do not help with the psets at ALL. In fact my TAs were much more helpful in terms of problem solving. That being said, he does stress theory in his lectures...which he cannot do well. Makes annoying mistakes during derivations, cannot lucidly and confidently explain a concept...just plain confusing. E&M is a tough topic, but come on.

His lectures are only on the very basics and does not help at all when it comes to solving homework or test problems. The solutions to problem sets he provides are either incomprehensible or intangible. I don't want to sound like a hater, but he is really an awful teacher. And you don't have another choice for honors E&M in the spring.
super awesome way to quickly learn python for non CS majors!!! very sweet guy, brings his dog scooby to class

Frey was a solid professor! Organized, quick lectures followed by daily lab assignments was a great structure for the class that I really enjoyed. He gave good feedback on the two projects and was helpful in class when you're having trouble. Plus he brings his dog into lectures. Take his class if you want to learn Python quickly and efficiently!

Cares about student understanding of (in my case) C++, and other languages that pair well with it. The final project was in a group and allowed for very significant freedom. - also he brings his dog into class.

One of my favorite professors at Cornell; her classes were my reintroduction to American history after not doing much of it for a few years after high school (I'm a history major). Absolutely wonderful lecturer and has amazing personal historical anecdotes. I get the idea she wants to retire soon so take her classes while you can!
Highly knowledgeable, caring professor. I learned a lot in her class. Don't be afraid to approach for help or advice.

Professor Garcia is one of the best professors I've every had! She's very helpful and care about her students. All the readings are useful in case of understanding the main contents. She encourages me a lot and gives detailed instructions on my papers. She's super willing to help you when you reach out to her!!

Best professor ever!!! Cares so much about her students. She sets up her course brilliantly where the lectures are fascinating, the work load is not too intense, and participation matters so you are held accountable to engage with the material. Took this my first semester at Cornell, and the bar has been set so high. Sat in class jaw opened.
Decent lecturer but her real strength was in leading very engaging discussion sections.
She's a lenient essay grader. By far one of the best classes I've taken so far here, and she's the reason why I want to be a history major. I highly respect and look up to her.

This was a tough semester online because of covid but Professor Garcia was understanding, and she eliminated some assignments when she saw we were stressed. The lectures were interesting. Quizzes are easy if you do the readings. I hate writing papers but her feedback was helpful and I improved. The group project was fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My experience with this professor was not positive, but you can tell they want the best out of their students. If you are not a great writer I would not suggest taking this course unless you are willing to put in the extra work, but doing well is very possible. The material taught in the course is great!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Garcia has been my favorite professor at Cornell. She loves to have engaging conversations with her students, which is why I definitely recommend taking her seminars. She is also very accessible outside of class and constantly checks up on her students. Putting effort into your assignments and contributing in class is what matters.

The best professor at Cornell. She cares about her students. I had her during the COVID outbreak and she was so accommodating and constantly checked in to see if we were ok. She loves history and every one of her students. Take her class if you can, she is the best person you will ever meet.

While she is a good, interesting lecturer and is really sweet, she grades very harshly. She gives few guidelines and little feedback. Our class average on a paper was a C. In a humanities class full of students who generally want to learn about Latino History in the US, I found it ridiculous to grade so tough.
Knows so much about refugee and immigration history it's remarkable. Clear lecturer, but I think she really excels in a seminar. Incredibly approachable.
Great class, highly recommend Prof Garcia.

- Smart, engaging, approachable professor, one of my favorites - Moderate to heavy reading; however, as long as you understand what the general points of each piece are, you will be fine - Great discussion leader - Class requires a 25 pg research paper as only assignment FYI  - I would highly recommend MCG, she is an amazing person and teacher

Dr. Garcia is a fantastic professor. She is an awesome lecturer, very passionate and knows a ton about immigration, especially from Latin America. Class was interesting and eye opening. No tests, just a couple papers which were not too bad and fairly graded. There's also journals to write every week but only checked twice. HIGHLY recommend

Professor Garcia is an amazing lecturer, and I've never been very interested in history. She introduced a lot of real-life examples and cases that really made the material "stick." Try to keep up with the insane amount of readings, and attend class. She's flexible with grades if you simply show up! & she's very approachable. Love her.
One of the best professors at Cornell.  Tons of reading but the class is definitely worth it.

A really great professor and one of my favorites for this semester! She is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the border! A great class to take if you don't mind putting in the time and reading.

This is one of the most phenomenal professors at Cornell.  And she isn't famous just for being famous, she is so kind and helpful, fun and engaging; just an amazing teacher that everyone will remember.  Don't disrespect her though!  She does not take kindly to disrespect...but just be nice and work hard and she will be the most amazing teacher ever
Very friendly and great small sections leader and large class lecturer.  This is the second class I have taken with her; while she is not the easiest, she is a great Professor.

Great professor in a seminar and the nicest women you will ever meet. The latter point was especially important given that we were constantly discussing touchy issues of race, ethnicity, etc. Tolerant and supportive of those who disagree with her and extremely accessible.

AMAZING lecturer! -- Her passion for history is inspirational.  She is the BEST professor at Cornell.  Interest in class material is all relative depending on what one likes.  Personally, I love everything she teaches, thus I'm biased.  I highly recommend that students take a class with her before graduating, as again she is a wonderful lecturer.

She was by far the worst professor I have ever had, her lectures were straight her notes and not interesting at all and her choices for the readings were ridiculous, the class was a complete waste of time.  There were student raised questions she couldn't answer. Awful class I could never recommend.

an amazing and interesting lecturer.  she's obviously a very passionate historian and very dedicated professor.  she's also a fair grader and a very approachable professor, she goes out of her way to address student concerns.  i would gladly take more of her classes

during class discussions, there's a very obvious liberal bias. if you disagreed with her points, she basically ignored you and called on somebody else. class discussions were essentially garcia spewing her opinion, nobody else actually got to share their own thoughts.

an amazingly interesting lecturer - can never fall asleep in that class! her grading is pretty easy, and she's incredibly helpful and approachable.  I would recommend this class to anyone interested in American History or looking for a good professor.
If only Clarity were on a six point scale. She gets through a ton of material in class, and is very knowledgeable.
Best lecturer I've ever had. She's also really friendly.
She is a great lecturer, very well-informed.

I've taken 4240 and 4940 with Chris and both were good classes. 4240 can be a bit of a drag sometimes but you'll notice despite lots of complaints most people in the class get a grade in the A range. Chris is more enjoyable to take in 4940 because of the individualized attention you get so don't be afraid of other reviews.

Course had good message but grading/instruction methods made it horrid. TAs are so inconsistent and grading is harsh, you can easily get under 70s. While I tried to have a coachable attitude, it was impossible because every TA would say vastly different things I honestly got lost on how to even improve. I don't think many peers liked this class.

Overall, would not recommend taking this class. Assignments are tedious and require huge leaps to come up with a (usually) speculative design. Design methods were not taught well. Grading is subjective; difficult to improve/master. Lectures were the only positive of the course; they were often interesting and I appreciated Prof. C's sense of humor.

echoing what everyone else had said except for that one 5 rating. feedback is all over the place and they stop giving it at the end of the semester. one week a TA will praise you and another will degrade you the next week for the same quality of work, so there's no point in even applying feedback from previous assignments.

In addition to everything that's been said already professor Csikszenthmihayli continues to do what he does. Still hasn't put in grades 2 days past the deadline, with ungraded assignments from like months ago. Such a bad bad class recommenced everyone to STAY AWAY

The undergrad TAs don't know what they're doing. Insanely slow grading yet feels like a lottery. One week you'll get close to full points then the next you fail with the same quality of work. Feedback all over the place and professor is so snarky it's irritating. Even for INFO, choose another concentration course. DO NOT take for fun. I regret it.

Didn't learn anything in this class. Grading totally depends on the TA, but there are many opportunities for extra credit. Attendance is 100% mandatory, scarily so (checking attendance multiple times in a given lecture, counting number of students in the room, etc.). OK I guess for a major requirement but would not take for the pursuit of knowledge

Just terrible! Grading feels like roulette depending on what TA you get / how the professor is feeling. Class has 0 structure, readings / material is laughable — for those interested in design careers, this will not help you in the slightest 

Look at how many angry students there are this is pretty indicative how peers in the class feel

GRADING IS SO SUBJECTIVE. THEY GRADE SUBJECTIVELY AND LAZILY TO JUST TAKE POINTS OFF. CHRIS DOESN'T HAVE A CLEAR STRUCTURE IN LECTURE EITHER AND JUMPS BACK AND FORTH BETWEEN TOPICS. HE ALSO OFTEN UMMS/UHHS THROUGHOUT THE LECTURE WHICH IS DISTRACTING WHEN IT'S HARD TO UNHEAR.

my least fav class ever at cornell! prof is super rude + bashes students in class / assignments. beyond the prof the class itself is awful, its all over the place and lecture is him just stuttering / umm-ing through random topics with no flow
Amazing class, amazing prof. Really gets you thinking about how technology interacts with and impacts the world around us. Assignments encourage you to be very creative.

Wordy assignments make expectations unclear. Subjective grading and dependent on TAs — you might not always get the same TA so if one gives you positive feedback, another might not especially if the professor is grading it. The professor can be funny but snarky. You can do well with effort, though what counts as “effort” seems inconsistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Grading is subjective and harsh, by undergrad TAs who don't give clear feedback. Projects could be approved by one TA but criticized by another so confusing. Assignment instructions are scattered, which can cause large chunks of missed points. Prof can be snarky and passive aggressive. Choose another class. My least favorite INFO prof and course.

First time writing RMP because INFO4240 was a nightmare. Attendance is strict, class activities useless, 50 pages of dull readings every week, and workbooks are graded completely subjectively. 

Grading is biased and ridiculous. The instructor even calls graders who give too many 90 grade, completely unfair. Avoid this class—you'll learn nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
He assigns a lot of readings before each class, and they feel more like long research papers than enjoyable material. It's hard to focus during lectures because he says “umm” and “uh” 30 times in one sentence. The grading is very subjective, and getting over 90 seems nearly impossible. An 80 feels like a win.

I recommend you to not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Gave me a B+ even though I scored higher than my peers with As because I was a sophomore. Not saying he is biased but be careful when taking his courses.
I love this man

The material was presented very clearly and lectures were well organized. He's very good at explaining the concepts behind the material. The homework can be difficult, but the TAs are extremely helpful. Tests are fair.
Very nice person; can tell he likes teaching.

Csaba is the best! Very knowledgeable, is able to derive formulas without even consulting his notes. Highly recommend this course! Homeworks are a bit difficult at first, but once you become accustomed to them, you learn a lot.
No Comments
Very good professor. Lectures follow book but add material and are interesting. Homeworks are long, but doable. Prelims mostly cover the material taught and are fair. Overall, a very good course.

Class was really hard, and exams were overwhelming. The sheer amount of content you have to learn is insane. Also, professor is very by-the-book. Had an assignment where everything was correct, but had "cart" instead of "Cart" and because I did not follow assignment instructions, I was not permitted a regrade and lost a lot of points.

This class made me consider dropping the CS major. Lectures were ok but a little strangely paced and I lost focus frequently. Prelims had way too much content in a very short amount of time. Assignments were super long and wordy, but not too hard. 
Muhlberger is passionate but harsh, and unfairly blames low medians on students.

A needlessly brutal course. Of course during his last semester he makes assignments excessively tedious and time consuming, locking points behind difficult challenge extensions. Prelims and final were again excessively harsh grading-wise, with medians much lower than previous semesters. Thanks to him I have decided to no longer pursue a CS major.

Not an easy class. A bunch of work on top of an already busy schedule. TAs constantly mess up grading of exams. Of course he's not teaching this course next semester either. Had to leave the tedious stuff with us. Would not recommend.

Class is very well organized, I thought lectures were very interesting and assignments + quizzes definitely help with understanding of material. Definitely takes work to do well/above average but interesting class! Sometimes lectures are a little fast and very information dense but there are many provided resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Made this semester more difficult than the others (this was his last semester for 2110). Tests were long af for no reason and the averages were down from last time. Thinks students have more time than they actually have. He also has an attitude.

As a RAG Chatbot trained on the CS2110 syllabus, when you have extenuating family circumstances, he loves to give you NO lenience. 

While Curran is extremely knowledgeable about the CS2110 material, he tends to be inflexible when it comes to extensions or accommodations, even in cases involving extenuating personal circumstances.

Very average professor overall. Lectures are so monotone and made me want to fall asleep. And you can't even skip since there's participation. On the bright side, the course is organized very well and the content is presented somewhat clearly. If you can get past how boring the class is, you'll learn a lot of foundational skills.
Not amazing, but good at least.
Really great at lecturing, very fair exams.
Seriously one of the best taught classes at Cornell - what really pushed me to switch from Engineering

Some lectures may seem slow some too fast but the assignments helped me learn a lot! If you study for them, the prelims are doable. Responses on Ed were also generally helpful. Overall the course is very organized and the median was around a B+.
Lectures were sometimes fast-paced, but he was easily reachable via Ed and gave very clear instructions and guidelines to all assignments; I think it was a very doable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This guy definetely got bullied in high school
Great lecturer, sometimes could be a bit hard to follow. Assignments could get pretty long and tedious at times but instructions were very well put-together which made them doable
i love this guy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I struggled paying attention in class. In my opinion, he spoke a bit too fast. Most of the contents were interesting and useful. However, some of it really seemed unnecesary, as there was too much content, when you take into consideration lectures, discussions and assignments. The exams were very doable, and assignments were challenging.
