Not sure why everyone else on this forum is soo negative! Took 2110 in the fall and Muhlberger was great :)

He's okay. He covers a ton of things in lectures which makes it pretty difficult to retain all the information. Exams were basically memorization-based, and there wasn't a lot of generous partial credit. Assignments were half easy and half confusing. He didn't really have a personality, so he was just a middle-of-the-road professor.

Terrible programmer, terrible lecturer, terrible professor. For those of you who know the Java programming language, the dude once had us write an equals() method for an assignment. I also happened to rewrite the hashCode() method, as the JavaDoc contract, and lost points. Tf is this guy doing?

Explains CS concepts pretty poorly and made me wonder if I hated CS. Watching videos of other people explaining the concepts is infinitely more helpful and interesting than his lectures. Tests and Assignments were fair but the lectures truly make the class pretty hard to get through and uninteresting.
Like others have said, made me rethink my career path. A lot of the class feels like a trick that's out to get you, none of it feels like it's on your side.

Made me rethink majoring in CS. He needs to get his mic fixed or something because it's super hard to understand what he's saying in lecture. I don't really think he does a good job of explaining concepts either. The material is interesting on it's own, and the assignments aren't super hard, but for me, at least, the exams were bad.
Lectures not helpful enough to really be worth attending
Muhlberger is extremely difficult to keep up with during lecture, often taking the most difficult and unintuitive approach to explaining the simplest problems.

Honestly made me reconsider the CS major I'm not gonna lie. This class was pretty rough- assignments took forever and the TAs were so swamped during office hours. As the material got complex he got increasingly worse at explaining key concepts. Would take with another professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Excellent lecturer; he clearly cares deeply about the material. I highly recommend this class for anyone remotely interested in software engineering or just writing good code. He's worked in the industry (SpaceX!) for a long time, and it very much shows. While standards can be high at times, they are always built towards industry standards.

Took CS 2110 Freshmen fall, having learned Java already. Muhlberger is knowledgeable/nerdy in a good way, can speak fast at times but is very caring/genuine. Participation recorded using i-clicker, and assignments can be quite long. Final assignment was very fun and could compete against others. Overall, very enjoyable, you will learn a lot.

Very split on Muhlberger. He's such a sweetheart and is accessible outside of class when you need extra help or career advice, which I really appreciated. On the other hand, his lectures are very dense with examples, and he speaks very, very quickly. The class is curved to a B median :( Well organized class :) Study for the tests to do okay.

Taking this class made me seriously reconsider my career path. I only pray that those in industry do not code like Muhlberger wants us to. He explains concepts terribly and is unbelievably unhelpful with his Ed Discussion responses. Quizzes and prelims are full of gotcha questions. Do not take 2110 while Muhlberger is in charge.

Muhlberger lectures way too fast and uses bad analogies to explain coding concepts. The new projects he added to 2110 are excessively complex. He and his TAs, while responsive on Ed, sometimes give snarky, curt replies to questions that students post. Would not recommend at all.

Generally good, at times went too fast and glossed over things which demanded a review of textbook/lecture slides. All materials very accessible and he is very passionate about the subject. Assignments were manageable and tests had no trick questions, despite testing on difficult subjects.

Muhlberger is a very passionate and intelligent professor. However, his lecturing style is somewhat off-kilter: he talks too quickly and in a weird cadence. But he gives helpful responses on Ed Discussion and knows what he's talking about. Overall, course content is not difficult to understand and is very useful for software development.

The class is interesting enough, but Prof. Muhlberger is somewhat eccentric and certainly fast-paced. If you are a slow-learner, don't. If you write on paper, don't. Assignments are really hard but useful. Tests are fairly hard, but not unreasonable. Average grade in the class is a B - considered a mini-weeder
So bad

Muhlberger is truly an awful lecturer. He uses so many analogies that do not apply well to CS concepts. Furthermore, Muhlberger does not share the answers to the weekly quizzes. How are we supposed to learn in the end if we don't know what we did wrong?

Muhlberger is the driest lecturer I've ever had. He talks extremely fast and at a strange cadence. Muhlberger's  quizzes are full of gotcha-questions that don't teach you anything. He's also remaking the course and adding in a bunch of ludicrously complex projects. I learned more from W3 Schools than I did from Muhlberger. Would not recommend.
Decent

Lectures were informative and well-structured, course was very well organized. Assignments were challenging but I enjoyed working through them. Professor definitely cares about what he's teaching, he pushes you to think about software design rather than just programming
Only complaint is that some exam questions were wacky and very abstract

Lectures too fast and somewhat hard to understand as a lecturer covering too much too quick but definitely knew what he was doing and I enjoyed the class. He and Clarkson were great in 2110. Class was well done.

Muhlberger, unlike Myers, was extremely helpful outside of class in 2110. He gave very thorough and clear explanations on Ed Discussion. He only gave one lecture, but it was far more thorough than most of Myers's lectures. Overall a very friendly and caring professor.
Don't take if you wanna be happy.
The worst class I have taken at this school. I did well but only because I sunk more miserable hours into this class than most people.

Worst lecturer ever met. Classes and projects are disorganized. Limited help from TAs. Final grading is not followed by the posted criteria, which are not clarified until the midpoint of the semester.

Professor isn't bad tbf, he gives access to good resources, lectures are good for SWE, and he is very knowledgeable. The course sadly was a logistical nightmare as others have said already. Wait for a serious re-work of the course, take an external project, or try to get on an internal project with good docs and a knowledgeable + helpful TA/client

Pretty much what others have said about this course... VERY disorganized and the difficulty of the project varies . We worked on an internal project and the TAs and the prof barely knew anything about how the systems work. Avoid taking this class unless you have to.

The grading scale of the course was not disclosed until two-thirds of the way through the course. The difficulty of the projects varied greatly, and the TAs and professors are totally not helpful to the project. The course schedule is VERY bad, the exams are EXTREMELY unreasonable, and there is NO improvement in software development skills!

This class makes ZERO sense. We were doing a project called Gerrit but no professor, no TAs, no one knows how Gerrit work. The workload of different groups is completely different, we spent a almost 20 hours a week to finish our requirements. BUT, the group who have a little requirments got a good grade just because they have little things to do.
Awful

It is totally a joke to have him as the instructor for CS5150. Awful lectures and poor organization. Grades are given in a VERY unfair manner, TA and instructor did not keep the same standard. The grading policy was not determined even if it is near the end of the semester. He also refused to accommodate students with difficulties like covid.

Muhlberger was really detailed and prepared for lectures and answered questions clearly and in an understandable way. Also posted more helpful/descriptive answers to questions on EdStem than Gries. Overall good professor who knows his stuff!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Though he only taught for one semester of CS2110, he was my favorite of the pair. I went weekly to his OHs, not to ask about quizzes, but to talk and learn from this extremely well-read and knowledgeable person. Unlike Gries, he is less condescending and is always happy to talk about non-sequators. Highly recommend him as a professor and friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed all of professor Mulhberger's lectures. He's very smart and clearly knows what he's talking about. His best attribute is that he explains things very well in lecture which helped improve my understanding of CS.

I enjoyed this freshman academy class. I do believe that academy coaches (basically upperclassmen TA's) were the reason for my enjoyable time. However, although Prof Valero-Cuevas was not the most exciting person at times, you can tell he is a smart and nice guy with a good heart who really wants to see you succeed. Also an easy A.

(At USC now, not Cornell) ENGR102 is just an awful class in general. Valero Cuevas isn't the worst to take it with, as he doesn't really give any assignments, you just have to go every week to get an A. But it's SO BORING! His voice will put you to sleep, and he looks for phones like a hawk. It might not be worth it.
no clear concept of student understanding.  obviously has poor grasp of material he is lecturing on.

I didn't read the textbooks, just did my best to memorize the glossary terms from the assigned readings. I took extremely detailed notes of everything he SAYS. Memorize everything you can. His delivery of the lecture was most important. I learned a lot in this class and appreciate Prof Cutting's dedication and passion for these topics :D
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures and textbook cover different material with some overlap, and you have to study both for exams. In-class pop "essays" (really just a 2-3 sentence response to a basic question) count for 10%, top two exam scores (out of 2 prelims and the final) each count for 45%. Exams are short answer and require lots of memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His lecture slides by themselves are not too helpful. The real stuff happens in the professor's delivery in class. So attending lecture is key. If you make it, the lectures are fascinating and well-delivered; if you don't, well, good luck trying to infer the content from pictures and random terms. (When I tried that, it didn't go well.)
Knowledgable professor but he cannot communicate information clearly to students. Powerpoint slides are not very helpful. Prelims draw from pure memorization of random definitions.

At the very first lecture, Professor Cutting states that while he knows everyone here are at the top of their game in their respective high school classes, he is here to separate the very best from the best. And he does this by making his notes extremely disorganized and exams ridiculously hard. Knowledgeable professor but horrible teacher.

Yes the tests are really hard, but this class is very fair overall. Best formula to get an A: GO to lecture, write down about half of what he says, learn the bold terms in the book, and study hard for tests. Cutting is a masterful lecturer, very intelligent and knowledgeable. Boring every once in a while but usually fascinating, original material.

An incredibly thorough, clear, and well-organized teacher. Exams were detailed, but very fair. He also let the entire class know outright that lecture material and text readings would be distinct from one another, but that both would be covered on prelims. Hands-down one of the most competent people I've learned something from at Cornell.

The subject matter is interesting, but his exams are really hard - you need to know every little detail, even obscure book definitions that have never been discussed in class! But it's clear he's an expert in what he's talking about, and has many different interests. He's a true intellect, and extremely helpful during office hours. Great guy

Professor Cutting is an absolute genius and his lectures are fascinating. He talks a lot about art and is a very engaging lecturer overall. His exams are difficult, but if you attend lecture, read the book, and study a lot, you CAN get an A. Definitely recommend.
Examinations are a bomb, but if you study you can pass. Very good lecturer and very good prof. overall.Very profesional.

This class is hard. You have to be on top of everything and I mean every litte detail. I recommend taking this class if you have a easy course load. If not don't stress yourself out--Cornell is stressful already.
Very Hard

Prof. Cutting is my advisor. Class was decently hard. The tests were very hard because they involved very detailed memorization of truck-load of material. If you have a very good photographic memory of every page of text and lecture then you are garanteed to get an A or better in class. Last minute cramming will definitely not cut. Highly curved!

Never had a more competent and organized professor. He takes information from a wide range of disciplines and condenses it into these really impressive lectures. It's not easy to get an A, but it's worth it. I learned a lot. Not much reading. Show up, take good notes, and you'll do well. Don't take the optional final!!
HARDEST CLASS EVER!!! Don't subject yourself to it unless you like getting Cs.
Tests are very very hard but material is interesting.  Not good to take as a distribution but good but overall it was a decent course
very enthusiastic, knowledgeable, great use of powerpoint
very clear, knowledgable professor. Difficult exams, but absolutely possible to get good grades if you go to lectures and keep up with the stuff. PSYCH 205 was a really really fun class.
He shines with brilliance and his enthusiasm for the material. Tests are super hard. But I loved the lectures. Seldom have I looked forward so much to going to class.
Really enjoys the subject.  His presentations are very clear, although his tests are really difficult (the curves are generous though).  I would definitely reccommend taking a class with him.

Lectures are very good, but simplistic from my opinion. The course is easilly passable if you just go to lectures, and you can get a good grade if you do anything more. Its an interesting course, and it was great as a low-workload distribution course.
His 205 class was moderately interesting, but his exams were silly exercises in memorization. No real conclusions drawn from the course, but still some exposure to 'fun-to-know' type stuff.
No Comments
No Comments
get him alone if you want to talk about anything, but he's very helpful.

Professor Culler, though a genuine sweet-heart, is not a great teacher. I love poetry but his lectures made me (and many others) fall asleep. His voice drones and is way too quiet. Lecture information isn't helpful for graded material. Also, he doesn't give clear grade criteria so I never felt confident handing in any of my assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: It felt like I was taking a class with a legend - and I was. For someone as accomplished as he is, I never felt like he was judging me for being new to the major. Poetry recitation was a part of the grade, and he listened dutifully and with a smile. Remembers my name two semesters later. All-around great guy.

I took his class a few years ago, and just loved it.  Not only was he refreshingly clear and unpretentious, but when he walked in the room in his leather bomber jacket and raked his fingers through his silky silver hair, his uncanny resemblance to Indiana Jones was enough to make anyone go weak in the knees!

You will never look at the world the same way after this class.  The lecture format is the ideal way to digest dense theoretical texts.  Culler makes graspable the obtuse.  The work load was extremely manageable, and the grading was fair.  This class turned out to be one of the most useful classes I took, and I can't commend Culler highly enough.
take him before its too late
Took his lit. theory class a few years back. A bit uncomfortable at lecturing, but always clear and approachable. A really decent prof.
cornell's theory star, he is good at explaining things. he is very smart, but a little arrogant.
A little aloof, but makes very complex theory clear & understandable.

Verdie is great and loves to hear student feedback and participation. She can be a little tough at first but as long as you take her comments it will be just fine. Not the most approachable but definitely always willing to help. She is definitely passionate about her work in order to get students engaged
Verdie is passionate about the course material and excellent at engaging students. Her class taught me new ways of thinking and reading and provided a safe space to express my views.

Directionless, vague, poorly put-together. Verdie's True Stories is a disjointed mess of a class that bounces from book to book; books only related in the way that they serve to push her agenda. Not that I always disagreed with her agenda. For example, fighting racism and sexism are noble pursuits, but the class felt like well-trodden propaganda.

Sometimes the prompts for essays were confusing, but Verdie is generous with her time in office hours and her feedback is really thorough and helpful. The discussion and student-led sections were always great. She's tough at first but if you work hard and do all of the assignments it will pay off.

I had True Stories with her and it was a disjointed and disappointing haze of poorly-led discussions. She's very passive-aggressive so DO NOT get on her bad side; after I wrote something adverse to her agenda, papers were returned with vague criticisms and I couldn't do well. I ended up with a B-, while in my other FWS I got an A+. Don't take her!

Professor was very knowledgeable and flexible with deadlines. The class was manageable with steady effort. The class was a collection of guest lectures, so there are many lecture styles and materials within one class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cynthia is definitely a little goofy but in a good way. She makes the content interesting and keeps lectures fun. She does assign a lot of readings but if you just skim them you will be fine for lecture and section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The online format made the class 90% straight up lecture, 5% asking students to participate, and 5% about rabbits. Professor Robinson is definitely very knowledgeable about what she's teaching, especially since she is considered a leading scholar in the field. However, it can be quite abstract, and lectures are VERY important.

This class was really really boring (it was all online the semester I took it, so you may have a different experience in person). The teacher was nice, but you had to go to lecture or rewatch the lectures or you wouldn't pass. Super easy tests, but a lot of unnecessary papers. Not recommended unless you love love love art history.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: She provides clear guidelines for success, and although participation matters, there is plenty of extra credit. I ended up getting a 125% in the class, but the highest grade you can receive is an A. She has a very positive attitude and an infectious smile, and brings snacks to class, making the night class much more enjoyable. HW is long but easy.

The class was surprisingly easy for a 4000-level course. No outside materials were provided, and all the problem sets were based on lectures. Some policies were rigid. Sooooo much extra credit! Easy A, but no A+.

Summarized by nonsensical psets in both length and content, arbitrary grading policies, rambling lectures and content a middle schooler could learn in ten minutes being shoved into a 3 hour long lecture. I would have have been satisfied with this course if I actually learned something, instead I lose my weekends and my sanity to useless psets.

Looove Cynthia - she's super sweet, funny, and smart. The only thing about the way the course was set up was that the problem sets were really long. Lots of research on real-world examples, and she made the content super digestible .

It was the easiest Class I took at Cornell!
The professor is really nice and gives out free points from time to time. Even though the class is 3 hours long, she always finishes early. She also hands out handmade fortune cookies! She's a very caring professor. It was the best class I had! :)

very heavy workload class. Every class has a problem set and I have to spend a whole day every week on it, In the assignments, I would write almost 10 pages with one or two Excel sheets for linear programming and data analysis. TAs are nice but tough graders, and if you relax a little bit, you will get a lot of points deducted like 80 out of 100.

She is very knowledgeable and cares if you succeed. TA is also great and easily accessible. Class is taught very logically, and you are expected to follow her approaches on all assignments. Not hard to do well. The best part is the homemade baked goods she brings every class!

Awesome professor. Highly intelligent and Type A. No tests/final! But attendance is mandatory for grade (dw she brings her husband's delicious baking to each class for everyone). However, she's not that accessible outside of class as office hours are a bit weird (change weekly and are at odd/late times). Other than that, 10/10 course

I WOULD NOT PREFER. I RECEIVING A 50 ON THE FIRST ESSAY, I ASKED FOR GUIDANCE. WE EMAILED BACK AND FORWARDS ABOUT 3TIMES CONCERNING THE 2ND ESSAY. I MADE ALL CORRECTION AND TWEEKS SHE ASKED ME TO MAKE THREEEE TIMESSSS, AND I STILL RECEIVED A 'C' ON THE ESSAY. don't do it unless you want to drop your gpa!
Always willing to help and give you pointers. Very knowledgable.
She was a fun, and very clear teacher.  Sometimes the assignments can suck because the readings are so long, but overall it was a fun class.  If you improved your writing you generally did well.

Overall a very cool teacher. She is extremely helpful and understanding and will go out of her way to help you if you express any concern. Also, she is very well informed about the subject area. She is well-organized and clear about what she expects.
I was in Wind Symphony and loved every minute of it. Bet that dude didn't practice. Professor Turner is an amazing teacher and musician.

Professor Turner is a sweet heart, that is, if you are in Wind Ensemble. If you are put in Wind Symphony for CUWinds, you will surely understand that Prof Turner looks down on the Wind Symphony, in a condescending matter. While sure, we're not as good as the Wind Ensemble, we're still people.
Professor Turner is an expert in her field, and an amazing musician to work with. She cares deeply about her work and students. If you get the chance to work with her, take it!
Clear, effective and efficient rehearsals, great repertoire, challenging; believes in students and what we can do. Lucky to work with her. Excellent musician and teacher.
Extremely musical and knowledgeable. Great repertoire that challenged and stretched me as a musician. More fun and interesting than orchestra!
No Comments
Wow! Dr. Turner is a brilliant conductor and musician, truly a credit to any institution that retains her.  Highly recommended.
Professor Curtis can come across as tough, but engage with his teaching style and you'll find he's a caring instructor who knows his stuff. unstuck AI was a big help for exam prep.
Yikes, avoid this guy
Not good; very toxic. Do not take this class if you are interested in a career in finance

reviews.comment: Some people might be put off by his unfiltered lectures, but if you read the textbook, actually study a little bit, and attend office hours if you have questions, the class is very easy. Any other stuff is just people being annoyed because he doesn't allow phones in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He may come across as a tough at first but he's an incredibly caring man with a wealth of knowledge. Make the extra effort to get to know him and you're experience in the class will change drastically.
Very toxic class. Curtis keeps his students on edge for all the wrong reasons. Being in his lecture hall feels like a prison.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: In my 4 years at Cornell, I have never had an instructor that is as condescending, arrogant, rude, and obnoxious. In his initial email to the class, he stated that "Note the exam dates -- if you are not available on those dates, then you might consider taking AEM 2241 or AEM 5241 in the Spring or Fall of 2022", Says everything you need to know.

This was one of the best classes that I have taken at Cornell. Prof. Curtis catches a LOT of flack for having VERY strict phone and tardiness policies and will call you out if you don't follow his lecture rules. However, by the end of the semester you will learn that he is kindhearted, caring, and an EXCELLENT teacher of the subject matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly abrasive and condescending. When you reach out for help he has a way of making it worse and yelling at you. Resources he provides do not always help on the test. Made the class so much more stressful than it had to be and the amount of time you need to study for a 3 credit class is ridiculous just to pass.

Went from live to online. Curtis has an abrasive personality and lecture is not fun (no phones or laptops). Is decent at teaching. Tests were difficult in person and became somewhat easier online. Claims attendance is mandatory but he obviously doesn't check. You don't have to do any work except take the tests but study and practice hard for them.
super rude and agressive even though it was through an email.. after I told him I dropped, he suddenly became nice....

If u need to take this class for a requirement, do it now while it's online. He's super knowledgeable, genuinely caring, & is pretty engaging considering finance is dry af, but is VERY strict during in-person lectures. No phones/no coming a second late (which is difficult bc the class is @ the dairy bar). exams aren't bad, pay attention to lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Curtis is not a very pleasant guy and is very particular, but he puts a lot of effort into preparing his material and teaching finance. He says attendance is mandatory but it clearly is not. Whole grade based on 4 tests. His tests aren't easy, but seemed to become a lot easier once class went online. At least there's never any work besides studying

I took his class in 2012 and honestly, he made me pay attention and learn a lot. But... wow, what an unnecessarily unpleasant man. I've had plenty of other teachers that did not need to resort to oppressive tactics to make their students learn effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: TAKE HOTELIE FINANCE
Stay far away from this class if youre interested in learning anything useful about finance.
BAD CLASS BAD PROF

I learned everything from his 600 page "supplemental" course packet and that forsakenly dry textbook, but his pride will ensure you get no higher than a B- if you skip lecture bc of 5-6 questions on his exam that you could only have gotten if you epoxied your eyelids open during his vegetative-state inducing lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class is tough, but you can learn a lot from it. Professor has strict rules, but if you talk to him, his personality is very very nice! If you want to learn well in Finance, recommend this class. But if you're doing it just for fun or interest, consider the one in hotel school. Overall, I like this class very much. Almost cry in the last class lol

He is literally the worst professor I have had in four years. He doesn't know how to lecture and purely emphasizes memorization of all concepts. He picks random and unrelated topics from the textbook and tests you on it. His teaching style is incompatible with any student's learning. Take hotelie finance, it is significantly easier. ABORT
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was maddeningly tedious

Put in the work and you will do well. Curtis is a great professor when you get to know him and his teaching style. If youre willing to work hard and seek out help if youre struggling, Curtis will help you succeed; no other professor holds extra office hours late into the night (around midnight) the week before the exam. Highly recommend

reviews.comment: This course taught me that there is more to life than high finance.

reviews.comment: Terrible class, Curtis emphasizes memorization over concepts...
Professor Curtis is the only professor who refuses to take student questions during lectures. Let that sink in.
Strict professor and very disorganized lectures
This class was an absolute waste of time. Disorganized lectures, little guidance, and a moody professor. Take the finance course offered by the hotel school.
If you think the 40-paged syllabus is excessive, you're going to think this entire course is excessive.
Do not take this class if you have any interest in learning about finance.
Go to his review lectures, they will save you hours of cumbersome lectures throughout the semester. But if you really want to save some valuable time, take a different finance class.

His lectures are some of the most sleep inducing ordeals I have had to deal with at Cornell and he makes it worse by shaming you if you're not attentive. Considering that I only have this issue with this class, I wonder whose fault this really is.
He knows magic tricks. His most famous trip is making the class fall asleep.
He has a quick exam turn over, only good thing I can say about Prof. Curtis.
The ridiculous course packet, the ridiculous videos, ridiculous exams, the ridiculous lectures, and his ridiculous attitude make this a ridiculous class.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: An OK teacher that seems to care about his lectures, but it seems to be more about the way he displays himself rather actual care for students. Very unapproachable.
This was by far the worst course in the Dyson minor. Anyone interesting in learning about finance should avoid this class.
If you're shopping for finance classes to take for the business minor, I would not recommend this class. It's a lot of busy work and the professor is not very helpful or clear in lectures.
I cannot fathom why anyone would willingly subject themselves to this course willingly.
This class is awful. Avoid!

Unfair grading, exam, and lecture policies make this course extremely inconvenient. Lectures in a disorganized and unprepared fashion, worrying more about who he can get in trouble rather than the dissemination of knowledge. I probably learned more about course logistics from this class than I did finance. I would not recommend him or his class.
A terrible professor who is more interested in touting his ego than teaching finance.
Prof Curtis shows a disrespect towards students which makes this course a terrible experience. I recommend taking any other finance course available, he's really not helpful.
Dropped the class after the first two weeks because he yelled at a student who was taking notes for texting. The student was not texting.

Easily my favorite professor at Cornell. If you want to learn finance well, take this class - it was helpful for my interviews. He is very nice outside of class and passionate about the material. Tough but fair
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Terrible professor

I learned more from spending 2 hours skimming the textbook than I did from all of his lectures or the course packet. By the way, don't by the review manual, it is not helpful at all when studying for the exams.
This was the worst class I have ever taken.
He cares more about if you're paying attention to the color of his tie than if you're actually learning finance. Dumb questions like that are what come up on his exams.

Oh my god this class was so much busy work. If her presented the material in a more organized fashion, all the concepts would have come across better with less self teaching required. Exams super simple if you keep up with readings, which is essentially the entire class.

Definitely a tough class and professor has humor that not everyone loves... That being said, I LOVED the class. Great material and I feel 10000% more prepared for my internship in finance this summer. Hat off to you, Rich Curtis!!!!!!!!
It's impressive how this man managed to turn a course about finance into a course about him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His lectures and his course packet were useless and his attitude was disgusting. Worst professor ever.

reviews.comment: Rich Curtis is the definition of a power trip. So mean!

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes in AEM, if not at Cornell.

reviews.comment: If Professor Curtis wasn't so arrogant and condescending during lectures, I might have actually enjoyed this class.

This was one of the most disorganized courses I've ever been in. Professor Curtis acts as if his lectures are meticulously crafted, but he is clearly always winging it based on his complete inability to elaborate concepts to a lecture. Whenever he feels he is losing steam, he takes his frustration out on his students.

reviews.comment: My biggest regret as a business minor was choosing to take finance with Curtis. He was far and way the worst professor I have ever had. Whenever I walked into lecture, I was in fear that I would be one of the students roasted in every lecture. I barely made it out of this class in one piece.
Very disrespectful to student's and TA's. Avoid at all costs.

Professor Curtis makes you pay $35 for a bunch of sheets of paper required for his class that he refuses to distribute electronically because it would damage his ego to see students with laptops in his lectures. Save yourself some money and take finance with a more level-headed professor.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor's demeanor in lecture was very inappropriate for any healthy learning environment.

Disgusting attitude. Makes fun of kids who can't answer questions correctly, even when they make an honest effort. Doesn't remotely care about those who are struggling in class, blames it on you not making an effort
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I don't know what this course gave me that purchasing the textbook would not have given me.

This was by far the best and most comprehensive finance course at Cornell. What I learned in his course have helped me so much in getting a job at a very respected investment bank. Yes he is tough and sometimes not pleasant in class, but it is not personal. If you take the course seriously, Rich will go above and beyond. He is extremely caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: After 8 years of studying business at Cornell, Professor Curtis was undoubtably the worst professor I had to deal with.
"See me after class." The wise words of a professor of a graduate level class. Pathetic.

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and take Hotelie finance over this class. Lectures are useless and tests don't evaluate knowledge of the material well. On top of that, the professor is menacing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was really easy but filled with constant belaboring about its difficulty. The language spoken by the professor is reminiscent of a frustrated high school teacher.
Curtis made me scared to go to lecture with his discipline. A professor should never make his students feel that way.

I took this finance class in the summer of 2006.  In hindsight, it was a great learning experience: Mr. Curtis was meticulous in his lectures, and students truly immersed themselves in the interactive classroom experience.  That said, I believe the lecturer could have been less intimidating. One doesn't need to intimidate in order to inspire.
I found Professor Curtis' lectures to be rather uninspired, as if regurgitated from some textbook.

If you're an engineer, you can probably get away with just showing up to his 4+ hour review sessions. The lectures are very long winded and uninteresting; I just wish I went to fewer of them at the beginning. Really poorly organized course.
Finance with Professor Curtis was probably my most unpleasant experience taking a course at Cornell. He is unreasonably strict to the point of distraction.
I did not enjoy this class.

Would have been a better class if he wasn't so mean. Lectures always went overtime. Review sessions went on way longer than they should have. He said they shouldn't be substitution for lectures, but they essentially were lecture repeats. Stopped going to class after the first review session because I realized this and I missed nothing.

reviews.comment: Completely closed off from student feedback and arrogant. One of the worst professors I've ever had.
Cornell's most disresptful professor.

reviews.comment: By far Dyson's worst class...
Take this class if you feel like going back to high school. Take any other class if you feel like continuing your Ivy League education.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I put very little work in his class and got a good grade, but he was no help and incredibly rude to students in lecture.

Prof Curtis is challenging and expects a lot from his students.  however, his class is worthwhile especially if you are thinking about going into finance. the class is time consuming but Prof Curtis is very clear with how he assigns work and provides helpful review sessions before exams. would recommend this course to someone interested in finance

Professor Curtis is the best professor I've had over 8 years of academia. He inspired me to follow a career in Finance and now in teaching. There is no one like him. His classes were difficult but enjoyable. He set high expectations and helped you reach them. He knew all of his students by name because he cares for each student.

If you're doing the business minor, take this over Hotel finance - we covered the whole textbook but Hotel only goes up to around ch. 12. You will not believe this on the first day but he is an amazing professor. I think he acts unapproachable in the beginning so people take him seriously, but he cares a lot about teaching and you'll learn so much

Curtis is an OK teacher and goes all out in OH if he likes you. The problem is that he's extremely terrifying and vindictive in lectures, not hesitating to stop it to scream at somebody for having a water bottle in the auditorium. I got a good grade, but it felt like an abusive spouse - mean enough to scare, but nice enough that you won't leave.

took AEM 2241 and while definitely among the most difficult courses I've ever taken, Curtis is by far the BEST professor I've ever had. His lectures might be long and he might seem mean (esp if you have your phone out in lecture), but I learned so much. Curtis also gives candy during exams. Study the course packet and textbook.

Hard class. But Curtis is the most dedicated professor I've ever had. Take finance with him and it's guaranteed that you have a solid foundation in finance. He's strict - Don't skip class or use your phone during - but he instills a sense of discipline that is needed in college students. Very approachable outside of class. All around great guy.

Tough class, large amount of material and exams are challenging. Multiple choice but trickyreally have to know it wording. Curtis is very thorough and clear in lecture, but they are long (esp the 2hr "discussion") and his course packet is similarly comprehensive. Snippy and strict  discourages participation, but very nice when you approach him.
go to the review sessions, Curtis re-do all of it. the longest I've been to was 7 hrs, from 7pm to 2am. That's dedication

Honestly the best professor I've had at Cornell. I'm an engineer doing the business minor and this is the first class in which I have found lectures to be enjoyable. There is definitely a lot of material but if you put the effort in you will do great.

By far  one of the absolute best professors I've had. He is incredibly tough and demands a lot on the exams. However, his material is laid out in a very clear and straightforward format. You know exactly what is expected of you, most student simply dislike the fact that it is A LOT.  Grade is the class is directly proportional to effort put in
Covers an insane amount of material way too quickly. I found it impossible to keep up. Went in looking to major in finance, now I want nothing to do with it.

Curtis is by far and without any question the best professor I've had at Cornell so far. His class is far from easy, but his assessments are fair given his excellent pedagogical merit. Because of him, Finance is an extremely engaging course.

One of most adorable professors I haver had at Cornell. Really clear, caring, and sweet in a fairly unique way. Exams are fair and manageable. Just one thing. a 115-minute session is really too long and sometimes it gets really hard to stay awake no matter how interesting the lecture is.

Terrible professor. Would never take a class with him if had a choice. Take Finance somewhere else. Totally doesn't worth your time. I'm usually an A+ student, and got a B in his class. Not recommended at all.
Great professor, really care about the  students, lots of work

Great class! If you ever want to make it big in finance, take this class. He covers all the bases of finance in a intuitive way. This is one of the best classes I have taken. YOu might see comments saying class is hard. Honestly, no AEM class can ever be super-hard. Nevertheless, this is a class worth taking

I flunked his exam and had to drop, but he's an amazing professor whose super smart, but teaches at an extremely fast pace, so you better prepare cause he expects A LOT!! Great teacher + a much nicer person than I thought in general and definitely compared to people at Cornell. The textbook is excellent as well.

Best teacher and class I have ever had. You will become an expert in finance. You should definitely take this course. Go to class, pay attention and take good notes - don't read textbook - and its not hard since he teaches it so well. My grade was curved from an A- to an A and I skipped a prelim.
He's a very good teacher, but the workload is heavy and some of the concepts are tricky. His class is also definitely easier for people who like finance; and not so much to people who don't.

Easily the best class I've taken at Cornell. Pay attention, turn off your phone, and you will end up alright. Fantastic in office hours. Exams are very difficult, but that is the point. Get the supplemental review book, it is essential.

One of the hardest classes I have ever taken and also one of the best. If you put in the time, you will learn a ton. Tests are tough but with a lot of studying I was able to get good grades. YMMV. Curtis is excellent at explaining very abstract concepts. My only complaint is that I was often afraid to ask questions because he's pretty intimidating
Best teacher I've ever had.  Cares for students, and is willing to do whatever it takes to help students learn the material.

Great professor with an innate ability to translate complicated finance concepts into simple, easy-to-understand ideas. Can be very strict in giving instructions and very tough on students, but he does it because he cares so much about his students. He takes the time to get to know every student and truly wants to best for everyone.

He's a really good guy, honestly. He truly cares about the students. Truly gifted at explaining (I dislike math, but in class if I pay attention hard, I can almost predict what he's going to say). Do not fall behind on studying. Definitely take this class, even if you're not into finance, since everyone should know how to invest.

Curtis is the man. He tries to intimidate the class at first, and at times, it can be scary. However, he softens up to you. Be prepared for a lot of work in this class. HE TESTS ON EVERYTHING. Great teacher, He's really passionate about his class.
This guy knows how to teach, but don't expect anything else from him.  He's like a brick wall with a nice smile outside of the classroom.  He should have stuck with physics.

If Cornell ever wants a top notch program, they had better hire a Finance professor with real experience-- be it research or wall street.  I personally did not pay to hear a finance professor deprecate himself by telling his students how horrible he is at investing.  With that said, he is a strong teacher... but does not belong in a top program.
notes are useful but his lectures are verry fast-paced and he expects too much from his students
Great class! Material covered really helps with finance interviews. Some material is difficult but he provides enough study guides in order for students to do well on exams. Highly recommend.

The best professor I have had at Cornell. Tests are tough but if you study and read the text book no reason you cant do well. Always available to talk or answer questions (even though he gets back to you at 3 or 4 AM). Great class highly recommended to anyone who wants to go into finance.
Great professor/great class.
Quizzes everyday, but good class!

Rich is one of those teachers.  He's an absolute nut and you'll love every second that you're in his class.  I'm not going to lie, his 'cold calls' will keep you terrified and on your feet, but thats the best way I learn.  Don't fall asleep in his class and get to know him because he's a great teacher in his own specific way.

Very thorough teacher.  He makes all the notes, teaches the sections.  Very clear, and can sometimes seem scary, but great guy.  Course is tough, but he prepares you very well for exams.  In the end its a great course.  Dont talk in class, and don't think you'll ever get out of section early, even if the pink pages are finished.

I dont know what all this talk is about the class being easy it is by far the hardest class required in the AEM major, I guess say what you will about AEM. With that said, if you do enough work, this class is manageable for almost anyone. Curtis is a great professor, he is unbelievably passionate about finance, great guy too. One of my best classes

Very good teacher. Wants all his students to do well. He tries to intimidate you at first, but all you need to do is go to section and lecture. Read all the assignments and buy the course packet. Great guy once you get to know him and really knows his stuff.

A great professor,probably my favorite at Cornell.The class is a challenge, but he cares about every single one of his students and is really rooting for everyone to do well.At the beginning he tries to intimidate you but as long as you study you'll be fine.By the end you will love him and be happy you took the class. I will definetely miss him!

He is incredibly intelligent and an unbelievable lecturer. If you pay attention in class, then you will leave every lecture with a surprising comprehension of complex ideas. You definitely get the bang for your buck with this class. As a senior, he is the best professor I have had at Cornell yet! He may be scary, but you can't help not love him

He is definitely one of the few prof I will miss a lot.  His class is not terrible as long as you don't study at the last min.  Great Lecturer.  A nice and hardworking prof who cares about students a lot.  My friends say he replies students' e-mails AT 3:00AM.   Can't really ask for more from a teacher.  Highly recommended for all students.

Insanely smart lecturer. It was one of the best courses i've ever taken at cornell. Definitely up there with gov 181 with katzenstein. You can tell he really enjoys subject matter and communicates it effectively. Great prof overall!
Excellent teacher and you'll deffinitely learn finance well--the only catch is that he's an arrogant **** both in and outside of class.
He knows his stuff.  He is very helpful and up to date on the market.

he's a great guy, but finance is a miserable class.  he didn't make it any less interesting, but he tried hard to be funny.  very hard.  never fall asleep or let your phone ring in that class, and do well or he hunts you down with at least 2 ta's by his side to force you to get help.  but a nice guy
VERY impressive memory, knows every single student in a pool of hundreds. very clear lectures. a very good class to take
Best Prof. I have ever had. The most interesting course I have ever taken. It's a pretty tough course overall.
I hate Finance

If you tend to fall asleep in class don't take finance with him....there is no place in the whole auditorium he does not walk though. you can sneeze all the way across the room and he will say bless you..meaning..he is always watching you..but he is smart
Curtis is da man!  He is a magician!
best business class... he's a great teacher and makes the material really easy to understand
Best finance class ever!
Good class but he treats everyone there like high school students. Or maybe it's just the students
No Comments
This man is brilliant!  He memorizes every students name out of a 250 person lecture.
A great teacher, but God help you if you fall asleep in lecture or your cell phone goes off.  He will eat you alive.
I have never learned so much important information before!  It is a hard class, but if you want to consider yourself a smart person, take it with curtis.
Hard class, but he's a real good professor.  He's also helpful.
13 years ago, he was producing work that was truly futuristic and mind-blowing. (A phd well earned)  Nowadays, he just produces mediocre cardboard junk.  How has he regressed so much?
I'm glad he decided to start being a father to his kid. Lost all respect for this guy when he was out in Colorado.
I think its cute that he sounds like Arnold Schwarzenegger if he never got into steroids.  Class was ok.

His work you can find by Googling him is vastly different in quality & depth compared to what he teaches in classroom on the same subject matter. As such, Daniel Leithinger's class is profoundly underwhelming. He truly doesnt live up to his own reputation.
Miller was a wonderful professor! Very interesting lectures and material. Easy class - grade was primarily based on iClicker questions (readings required)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Miller is very nice, good lecturer, extremely knowledgeable. Always replied to e-mails really quickly & good at clearly explaining things.  This class was really interesting; one of the few I've taken that's actually useful in the real world!  Super easy--if willing to put in tiny bit of effort you will get an A. Take this class!

He's really nice, and his questions on tests are really straight forward. Easy to take notes during class.  The paper is easy points.  Dr. Gravani, who teaches the 2nd half of the class is very nitpicky though.  The class is worth taking for Miller's lectures though.
Tests are far too hard.  Class averages very low.  Avoid if possible.  Needs to be reminded that 2 credit courses shouldn't be more work than Orgo.

Davis was very nice and accessible, but I didn't feel like he taught well. I was much less prepared for his exam questions compared to the other lecturer. I didn't need the textbook until he started lecturing because I didn't feel he was explaining anything well. His homework was easy, though.
Davis seemed like he genuinely cared about students. The lectures were a little stale at times, but he made me enjoy 2070 more than the other lecturer.

Professor Davis seems like a nice guy but the lectures were very boring. He taught very slowly to the point where we were not able to cover enough material in each lecture. Problem sets were long but not hard. The textbook is the one thing that helped me do good.

Davis is slightly better than Hines (who taught the first half of 2070), an engaging lecturer who posts slides beforehand and is more open to questions. He teaches a bit slowly, though, and by the end we were struggling to cover everything before the final. The class is still held back by a diabolical grading system (iykyk) and borderline evil TAs.

2070 is a hard class regardless of professor, but Davis is a genuinely kind person and likes doing demonstrations and cracking jokes, which makes the lectures bearable. He uses slides and uploads them the night before lecture which is convenient. His examples can be slightly confusing sometimes so be sure to pay attention or else you'll be lost.

His lectures come straight from the textbook, but there are some engaging parts of lecture that add to understanding. Some homework questions appeared exactly on exams so understanding them is important. He's nice but the lectures are pretty boring. Read the textbook for anything you don't understand as he follows it exactly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He taught the second half of Chem2070. My biggest complaint is the homework. Hours upon hours of problem sets. The professor who taught the first half of the class gave problem sets, but Floyd gave so much more homework than she ever did.The lectures were pretty boring, but at least he made explosions to keep us engaged.

Very dependent on the textbook, everything he taught and all grading criteria came from the textbook. Often went on tangents in lectures to the point where you couldn't understand what was important and what was irrelevant. Rarely did any practice problems in class so most of us did not know how to actually apply the material.

His test questions could still be quite difficult (typical of CHEM 2070), but he seems like a very sweet and caring professor. His lectures were more slow-paced compared to Prof. Hines, and I enjoyed his in-class demonstrations.

Floyd is a lot better at teaching than M. Hines, in my opinion. He teaches at a slower pace and conducts experiments in class. He is also very caring, and he reminds me of the grandpa in UP. He's so cute and wholesome core.
They need to make the 50 min 2070 lecture  2x as long once he takes over. Half of class each time is spent watching him figure out his own computer. Painful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice professor. Take advantage of regrade requests; Professor Davis is very generous and understanding of circumstances that arise during prelim season. His lectures were fast paced, but all slides are posted and he listens to his students concerns and is very patient in answering questions. 100% take 2150 over 2070.

despite davis being a nice and caring guy, his lecture slides aren't helpful, examples and derivations don't correlate to hw or prelim q's. OH aren't helpful. he doesn't walk you through problems, he just talks (not great for visual learners). textbook isn't great either.

lab work for this class is hard. TAs often didn't show up to office hours.

Prof. Davis is a solid professor. Lectures can get quite dry and proof heavy with derivations (particularly with equations in thermo and quantum), but you won't be tested on 99% of it. He does post lecture slides, which is super helpful. For 2150 specifically, try to stay on top of the content and take advantage of old exams/psets.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
-willing to help (office hrs, etc)
-overestimates students knowledge
-doesn't explain overall concept/basics much: easy to get lost if you don't know content already
-posted online lecture slides aren't helpful: lack lots of explanations/content discussed in lecture
-very time consuming lab reports
-definitely caring, but not the clearest explainer

Tough class, but with the curve (average is B+) you should be okay (just try to stay around the mean for prelims. By looking at the textbook before lecture, you should be able to follow. Clearly a passionate and smart guy, just tends to gloss over the basics. If I had written this after my first prelim, which made me question taking the class, idk.

Lectures were very informative and held my attention. Did demos every class. Homework was reasonable and lecture slides are posted at least the day before lecture. Overall a great professor who is passionate about what he does.
Respectful professor. Really kind when answering questions.

Pretty great teacher all around! If you like Chemistry and you're gonna take a course with him, you're in good hands. Clearly shows he loves Chemistry and love to project that to his students. For 2150: Make sure to attend lectures and study from given HW, old PSETS and exams. Book not really necessary IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: lectures are somewhat hard to follow and heavy in proofs for equations (imo like a physics course); a little boring. fun demos at the end of lecs though. labs are time-consuming (learn to use excel) but easy to get full or almost full points every time. tests are difficult. study assigned psets + old tests A LOT. course curved to B average.
Unfair in his dealings with students. Only cares about himself and how he looks to his peers and the administration. Deceptive and dirty. Plays politics a lot.

A very helpful professor who is always open to questions from students. He responds to emails quickly. Lectures are also well-organized, (almost) each time ending with an interesting demo. Exams are not that difficult once you practice past prelims and problem sets. Be prepared for the time-consuming lab reports :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really nice prof. You don't really need to go to class because he posts lecture notes (I didn't go 95% of the time). Just skim the notes, do some problems, and you'll do fine

I had Professor Davis for CHEM 2080. While his lectures may seem a bit dull at first, they become interesting, and they are invaluable to passing this course. He always tries to keep things interesting, and always shows cool demos. His prelims are extremely fair. If you studied well, you will have no problem. Overall, Professor Davis is a good prof

The lectures are pretty heavy. Better go prepared e.g print the lecture slides maybe. Prof D used 90% of the lecture time going through some tough practice problems which turn out to be pretty helpful when studying for prelims. Labs started out tough and get a little better toward the end, so really work on those lab reports!

Delivers introductory chemistry material slowly but in an effective way. Attending lectures helps hugely, as he goes over practice problems that are similar to required weekly homework. (Also looks like the grandpa in Up!)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: He was fine but nothing special. Tests are tricky, because he only really covers the bare minimum in class

Prof. Davis did an OK job.  His explanations were very clear and simple.  Often he ran out of time at the end of lecture and scrambled to finish demos.  The first exam was way too easy and was compensated for by a much more difficult second exam.  Overall, he was fair and did an OK job.  I stopped going to class eventually and still did well.

Came into this class as a chem major, left as NOT a chem major. His lectures are mostly useless, and it's much easier to understand if you just read the textbook. TA's office hours are hit or miss. Prof's office hours were not really helpful. FYI, do NOT take this class if you aren't confident in your previous chemistry knowledge!
He's a great teacher with a lot of passion for what he does. The demos are all really cool. My favorite class in freshman year

As most people have said, the lectures are standard and the demos are cool. The P-sets really are a reflection of what he'll put on the tests, so do those (even though they aren't for a grade). He himself is pretty reasonable when it comes to grades and advice, though he may go over your head if you ask him about other chem topics.
Good teacher. Knows his stuff and communicates it pretty well. Tests are fair. Labs are difficult but there is a curve so it's all good. Funny guy, too, and demos are awesome.

Demos ever lecture, which kept it interesting-- he's really great at making the material clear if you listen, though I can't say he's particularly exciting or funny (you may fall asleep in class). Exams are doable, and the class has a pretty big curve. Lab starts out next to impossible but gets a lot better.

Very friendly teacher. He definitely loves the demos (as everyone else here has commented). His problem sets are a very good representation of the prelims, so if you understand the psets, you're set. Although I definitely didn't do well in the course, I'd definitely recommend people to take it (especially if you've had AP chem.) You'll enjoy it!

Great lecturer! Problem sets are a very good indication of exam-type problems. Exams can be a tad bit long, but nothing unmanageable. Helpful during office hours and very enthusiastic and knowledgeable regarding the material. Awesome demos as well.

His lectures were very interesting. He always has some demos for each of the lecture sessions. He communicates the materials very well to the students. He is also very organized and the exams are reasonable.

Great demos. He is really really into kinetics so if you don't understand rate laws well you are pretty much screwed. Tries to keep the class interesting, it sort of ran out of steam at the end of the semester, but it is very obvious that his genuinely interested in his students learning and chemistry overall.

I want to know where his cartoons went! Professor Davis loves chemistry and it shows, whether he's randomly firing cannons into the lecture hall or working out the steady state approximation for the tenth time. He explains concepts thoroughly and gives fair exams, not easy, not backbreaking. He's a really nice guy too!
Cool Demos, wakes me up when I am sleeping in class. It's very easy. I got A+.
Lectures are great; partly due to his clarity and partly to his demos. Understanding and helpful. The class was tough but problem sets and labs helped prepare you for exam.
Problem sets are clear indication of what's represented on exams-- lectures are interesting enough.

Lectures are really useful for understanding the topics and different types of problems.  Always does a cool demo, like exploding gummy bears or a hydrogen balloon.  The practice prelims are pretty much on par and really help you prepare.
demos!!!

Floyd's class is by far my favorite (first semester freshman year). He loves to do demonstrations in class; any day we dont blow something up is a day wasted in his eyes. He is obviously loves the material he is teaching and the feeling transfers to his students. It is a difficult class though.
I went to all lectures because there were awesome deomos. He is funny and friendly.

Throrough and clear presentations of material in class w/ fun demonstrations thrown in.  Definitely a good teacher for an intro. chem class.  A little more difficult than 207 in terms of problem sets, labs, and tests, but manageable.
It's an easy class as long you keep up with the material and do the problem sets by yourself or else you won't learn anything.

Davis teaches from the book a lot, but is helpful and easy to understand. He seems to try not to make exams too difficult. However, he often doesn't teach something needed for a problem set or lab until just before it's due. Loves demos. Overall, makes the class fairly enjoyable and bearable.

def. better than 207!  his tests are actually possible to pass, although the problem sets can be harder and take a longer time to complete. he seems really nice too...makes class bearable with his demonstrations
i love FLOYD
Complete waste of time if you took AP or honors chem in highschool.  Textbook is verbose, but contains little useful information.  Easy class though.

Lectures were a waste. He spent 50 minutes going over about 10 minutes worth of information and the rest was  spent with examples. Also, I went to meet with this professor one-on-one and he was not helpful at all. You can tell he wants to be a good professor, though.
Not the best lecturer, but he tries. His prelims are loooooooong. He could do a better job of using class time effectively (i.e. not so much math and more examples).
Waste of time.  I would have learned more by skipping class and reading the textbook.
Boring.

He's a pretty good teacher.  Lectures are strait forward and easy to follow, an appropriate level for chem 208.  He's a p-chemist and it shows.  if you don't like math, this class might not be for you, but as a physicist I love it.
He's an alright lecturer. Explains things but doesnt really show enough examples. He tries hard to keep people interested.
No Comments
He's a really good lecturer and explains things really well. tests are very similar to homework questions. it's definitely a good class, if you like chem and physics
This man is an actual psychpath
The guy lives in his own world
The professor's teaching style was so confusing... completely loses track of himself and hard to follow / keep up with homework which is totally out of sync with lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not well organized in in terms of the lecture, and difficult to get his email reply
Kinda bad honesty. Teacher was all over the place. Very poor organisation
one of the best lecturers at ECE

Overall a nice and knowledgeable lecturer. But he can be very unorganized at some points, which can create distractions (a typical phrase from him: "ok forget about this, let me explain it that way"). The problem is that he tries to teach the whole course from his memory. But somebody needs to tell him it is OK to use some notes while teaching.

Solid class. I'm lucky my roommate told me about it. Lectures were always interesting and the ‘no-tech' policy made a large class feel like a small school experience, which is what I wanted at Cornell. I learned a lot.

Took 1250&4021–totally different experiences bc big lecture vs small seminar w/a field trip to India + Sri Lanka. In both, prof Green gave her all! I am inspired by her dedication & learned so much about the industry. She has high expectations and you rise to them. Not easy but so worth it to find out what you're capable of learning and achieving.

I showed up with INTENSITY and it PAYED OFF big time dog. Be ready to dress up runway ready to compete with professor Green's fire ootds. Ngl her Lecture game is lowkey a little hard fr but defo a good time.

Professor Green's class was so awesome, I could really tell she is so passionate about the subjects she teaches! She can be a tough grader but if you follow along it's actually pretty easy to do well! I saw a few reviews saying she over explains- however I really felt that the more explanation the better. 10/10 would recommend

Took this w/ zero fashion background and now I see the whole designed world differently. Prof Green is so passionate, real, and actually meets students where they're at. Also tells it like it is. It's a tough crowd in the lecture hall but she still delivers. Honestly iconic.

Loved the lectures, assignments, and exams — so clear and actually fair. Super available outside class + always extra credit available to boost your grade. You can tell she's genuinely hyped about the subject, so lectures are never drag. grateful I got to take this class.

She overexplains way too much in lectures and her tests are interesting to say the least. She made a slideshow where we have one minute to answer each question and obviously that created problems. Everyone got messed up on that test but she's too stubborn to curve or do anything to fix that. Passive aggressive weird vibe.

Be prepared to be inspired and challenged. Approach this class with a growth mindset and you'll succeed and learn so much. The professor sincerely cares and holds students to high standards. Highly recommend!

I hated this class. In lectures, she just speaks and says so much and so little at the same time. She calls out people talking in class and does not even cover everything she says she will. I truly cannot believe this is the only required course for a fashion studies minor. I am so sorry for everyone who has to take this.
Professor Green's class itself wasn't bad. The tasks can be a little tedious but the material isn't hard to absorb. She's not nice tho. She'll never reply to your emails

She was okay...I think (and many other students have agreed with me) that her lectures, it is a lot of her just talking, but saying nothing at the same time. Nonetheless, the class wasn't bad. Although assignments were tedious and sometimes annoying, there were only a few. You can get away with not doing the readings, but must come to lecture!

FSAD 1250 was my favorite class! Prof Green is incredibly knowledgeable, passionate, and caring, and she makes every class interesting. Prof and TAs can be slightly harsh graders, but you can always go to office hours if you're afraid of that. I'm genuinely sad that Prof Green doesn't teach any other courses. I would 100% take this class again!

Prof Green has a flair for giving extremely interesting lectures. She covers so many different topics in just 1 semester and her homeworks are very do-able and exciting too! I would definitely recommend even non-FSAD majors take this intro course!

Insanely lecture heavy. He would just yap and yap, in lab too - often about something loosely related but unclear whether or not it was important. Problem set and exam questions were confusing and graded confusingly. No set office hours. Course jumped all over the place, which was annoying. Would not take again. he just yaps and is confusing.

This guy talks a lot but it's because he's interested in his work. Great lecturer, but if you don't show up to class good luck surviving. Despite this, very accessible and understanding outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Louis does talk a lot, but he's a great guy. If you make an effort to learn you will surely enjoy this class. Very unique professor at Cornell where he genuinely enjoys and understands his field, hard not to learn here.
If you get Lou going, he won't stop talking. The guy clearly loves his field, but can be monotonous after 2hrs of lecture in lab. Great guy though.
One of the best professors I've ever had. You can clearly see he has a love for the topic and enjoys talking to students after class. If you can, definitely take a class with him!
Super chill professor who also has interesting lectures. Big fan. Had him for 1141 and it was great.

Miloje is such an amazing professor! The concepts are difficult (especially in the syntax portion of the class) but he explains everything very clearly, and the homework and exams are straightforward. He is incredibly kind and wants everyone to do well. Plus his accent is awesome!

This class wasn't easy. The concepts are difficult and the application harder. Despic goes very fast, so I would often have to catch up outside of class. HOWEVER, I really admire the man. He makes you feel fantastic when you understand a concept, and he is engaged and present. He is committed to helping. I selected him specifically as my advisor.

Always kept lectures interesting and always willing to help with questions or re-explain things. Exams could be difficult but if you take the class seriously and do the homework you'll do well, and Prof. Despic does include (fairly easy) extra credit questions on each exam. Great professor & person, really made the class engaging even online.
Harsh grader, but justified since the material is covered in class thoroughly. But be prepared to do a lot of test preparation since the questions are specific and tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Made lecture interesting and was willing to answer questions and explain things. Had really good study guides for prelims.
I greatly enjoyed this class. Prof. Despic makes the course fun, engaging, and not difficult. Exams mirrored the weekly problem sets and even had bonus points.

Definitely expects you to take the class seriously. He provides handouts that have answers to questions he asks in class and the material that he goes through, which is really helpful when you're doing homework later in the weekstudying for exams. TA graded harshly, but Despic was considerate and mindful of the difficulty level of the work.

I've also taken 4423 and his lectures are formulaic: bring a handout and work through it. Admittedly gets a bit dull here and there but he's engaging enough (tends to pace the room while looking down at the handout). He asks a lot of obvious questions during lecture and nobody answers because they seem like trick questions. This can get awkward.

I used to be bored and not pay very much attention in my past math lectures, but Sanjay's engaging and clear lecturing style allowed me to pay close attention in lectures for the first time. This also deepened my interest in the course (differential equations) and made me enjoy it overall. However, the prelims were not too easy. Final was alright.

Pretty good lectures. Need to read the textbook to do the homework because sometimes the homework content wouldn't be covered in lecture until the day it was due. Grading was also fair. I think for the most part, the class isn't curved by very much and the average grade is like a B, but the tests were fair

Professor Dharmavaram is the best! I really enjoyed this class and we used the same textbook as my high school, so it wasn't too stressful. I really enjoyed the material and his presentation of it. The man really knows how to teach! It's really unfortunate that this is his last semester at Cornell. He'll be at UCLA for research soon! Godspeed. (A+)
Great Professor.
Very clear and willing to explain concepts in various ways with helpful examples.

First prelim was really hard. It got better after that though. Final was okay. Sanjay is good at teaching his stuff, but he was kinda boring sometimes. Also very helpful and always encouraged questions
good lecturer, test was really hard though
Really good instructor, I had him as a TA. His sections were probably more useful than the lectures. Also, very approachable and helpful person.
Really one of the best TAs (if not instructors) I have had at Cornell thus far. He's funny, engaging, approachable, and teaches the material incredibly well. Highly recommended

Dr. Cherney is a sweet woman, but she does not lecture well and her ppts were all over the place. I had zero experience with animal care, so the messy lectures paired with no textbook to supplement made it really difficult for me to really learn anything at all, so I personally struggled a lot on the prelims

Easiest class I've taken. All the assignments are easy and you can usually fight for points back. Don't take the 1 prelim lightly though, there aren't many grades in the class so make sure you do decent on that. There's a final project that's basically graded on completion. Lecture is very unorganized so you can skip and not miss anything.

She's a nice lady and easily one of the most caring you'll meet. However, she's not the best lecturer and lecture is a snooze fest. Just review the practice tests she provides and review the slides and you should be good. Lab assignments are tedious but it's really the only thing you have to worry about. Class is pretty easy just do the work.

Nothing against the professor, just how to course is organized. Half of the grade is just menial busywork that doesn't correlate to any real life application or to the course itself. Valuable feedback is never given with little clarity offered on questions, leaving students guessing as to how to get points. Labs and lecture are peak nap time hours.
So sweet and caring, but unorganized. Assignment grading criteria is often unclear. The practice exams are very helpful for the actual exams.

Very sweet woman, but so unorganized and unfocused in lectures it makes it so difficult to follow along with anything she is saying. She is a pretty easy grader on papers and assignments and tells you what you need to know for the one prelim in the class. Overall easy course, but hard to sit through her lectures.

While I think she can be a bit disorganized, she will only test on things she lectures on. I loved writing the papers for this class and enjoyed the freedom we were allowed. She's very caring and available to answer questions. I do think that you get out of this class what you put into it so if you don't care about it, you won't gain anything.

Dr. Cherney is such a nice lady and so helpful if you ever ask her anything. The class is interesting if you actually pay attention (the first couple of lectures were kind of boring and hard to follow but it gets better). She provides notes for all her lectures that are very helpful and prelims are fine. Noncumulative final

She is so unorganized in lectures and just rambles on and on. Extremely hard to follow. I only showed up for the first few lectures and then I couldn't take it anymore. Still have an A+ so very easy class, not a great professor. She is a nice person, just not good at her job

Cherney is a very nice professor and cares about her students, but the lectures are very disorganized, and grading criteria isn't very clear. It's not entirely clear what she's going to test her students on, and lab instructions are often poorly worded and difficult to follow the specifics for. Nice and relatively easy, but not the most organized.

A very nice woman, but her teaching style leaves me so discombobulated.
