She's a relatively easy grader, but does not usually provide her expectations for an assignment so if you get points off, it's usually because you didn't realize something had to be included in the first place. She's also pretty inaccessible. I didn't learn much in the class.

Cherney is very nice and is willing to help students who are worried about material. Lectures are often tangential and can be hard to follow, but she posts online notes and practice exams that practically spell out the answers to test questions. While she is approachable after class and during office hours, she doesn't often respond to emails.
Shes scatterbrained and unorganized. I couldnt follow a lecture to save my life.

She is honestly a very nice prof, who will take time to discuss any worries/issues you have. But although it is clear she cares about her students, her grasp of her own material is often spotty at best. She tries hard, but her lectures are disorganized and often rambling. She will frequently go off topic which can make lecture frustrating.

Cherney is super nice and cares a lot about her students.  Knows students have a life and other classes, and she is often willing to relax a deadline  for projects/assignments. For those who think she doesn't care: simply not true. She's extremely busy (just take a look at her office & desk) and does her best to make time to help students succeed!
horrible professor, does not pay attention at all in lecture and teaches us useless information just by reading off of the powerpoints she makes
Can be confusing at times, but generally a good professor. Cherney is very fair and gives you a good idea of what to expect on tests, etc. Genuinely cares about the success of her students.

Great discussion-based class, which is hard to find in most science departments.  Workload is not terrible- just participate in class and don't save the book review and final project for the last minute.  Dr. Cherney is so nice and willing to help students.  She's a sharp tack, but isn't condescending like some professors.

Dr. Cherney is a very sweet person.  She really cares about her students and how they do.  I think she is a fast paced lecturer who likes to get a lot of info in there, which is great.  Her lectures are interesting and highly informative.  She is a great advisor too- very kind and helpful.

Possibly one of the worst classes I've taken so far at Cornell. She doesn't really explain things well, and a lot of time it comes across as if she doesn't even know what she's talking about. Class is genuinely boring. If you aren't interested in farm animals, this might not be the class for you because we spend way too much time talking about cow.

She is one of the nicest professors I have ever had.  She genuinely cares about how her students are doing in the class and will do her best to clear things up if you dont understand them.Knowledgeable, straight forward, great all around. Im looking forward to having her as a professor again.

I've had Professor Cherney for 3 classes and she is always awesome. She explains things very well and is always available to her students. She makes her classes fun and is very fair when it comes to grading. A great Professor.
quite confused and seems at times to be way in over her head.
She's really nice and very smart.  Very down to earth and willing to help. Great teacher!
Very good teacher. Could be more confident, but she is very smart....
Dr. Dharia is easy as can be.  I learnt a ton in this class but didn't have to put much effort into it.  He works hard to try and make the material interesting is accent is hilarious.
Prof. Dharia is good.  He hardly use textbook.  I make A in him class and hardly homework.

Only once have I looked forward to class with such anticipation that I felt as though I was about to have a first kiss with a new love.  Dr. Dharia was the culprit.  And he was able to achieve that with a material as drab as economics.
Such a cutie. And so bright!  Not the easiest but you learn a lot.
No Comments
No Comments
Dr. Dharia is hilarious.  He tells great stories of his lady friends.  He should be the president.

Very organized class structure. Only thing a little strange was that assignments were due at 11:59 AM (noon), not PM. 

Do not underestimate the prelims.

Dr. Dietz was a gem. She was always willing to help and made sure rubrics were clear. Practice exams were given but only one for each. She went out of her way to make sure our questions were answered and showed patience even when me and others asked the silliest questions. It was always nice going to her office hours and chatting with her.

Nice to your face but not behind your back. Doesn't help or support students, and it doesn't understand whatsoever. If you take any classes with her, don't make mistakes, not even typos, and avoid interactions. The other professors in the courses are usually nice and understanding, so try to talk to them instead.

Took BIONB 2210 with Prof Dietz. While she doesn't give any of the lectures, she is the main organizer for this course. She's super kind and wonderful at explaining concepts. Discovered her office hours right before the final exam, and wish I had gone sooner!
Can be hard to understand, but genuinely cares about the material and gives helpful feedback
extremely confusing

do not take coml2723. i will say that the professor definitely cares about the subject and academic inquiry, however i do not recommend taking this class. there are better courses that value participation, effort, and discourse that are not stressful and punitive like this. grading is harsh and a lot is expected for only a 2000 level course.
simply a sigh

By far the best professor I have had in my (albeit short) time here. She is brilliant; she provides excellent explanation, and very clear guidelines for grading. The seminar can be a bit intense as an undergrad, but definitely worth it. I want to take as many of her classes as I can!

I loved taking her class my final semester. I wish I could have worked with her throughout my four years. She's simply amazing. I highly recommend going to office hours (but actually go!). In the beginning of the seminar, I struggled, but after office hours, I shared my voice and grew so much as a student and person, thank you for everything!

Enthusiastic, approachable, brilliant. For every point that a student makes about the readings, she has an entire day's worth of discussion questions. She structures her course in a way that you gain a strong foundation for later, more theoretical, topics. She expects her students to think critically about the texts, and is willing to help!

Good prof. His lectures follow the textbook very closely, and his test questions are interesting (though challenging). He is better at teaching some topics than others, but you always have the textbook. HW can be challenging, but never unfair (contrary to what others said).

One of the best and most engaging lecturers in the AEP department.  He provides insight where the book lacks and creates engaging, yet challenging problem sets.  Of course there were hiccups with course management, but students have 3 drops (for 14 assignments).  Exams ranged in difficulty (1st Avg: 86, 2nd Avg:50).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: A final HW with 11 questions to do over break. Long exams and no reference sheet to complete within 2 hours. Releasing full-length problem sets only 3 days before they're due and expecting students to complete it or take a 50% hit to that grade is unreasonable and does not facilitate learning. It facilitates rushed learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His teaching is fine, but he is a very unsympathetic professor. Many times he released a pset 3 days before it was due, then refused to give us extra time to do it. He gave hws over every single break.  For thanksgiving break, he gave us "2 weeks" to do the last problem set, except it was twice the length of a usual pset. TAs were alsoveryunhelpful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Assigned 11-problem homework set over Thanksgiving break, gave only Three days for another problem set, required students to know material one week in advance of the actual lecture on it, homework sets on material he hadn't taught yet
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: basically a self study class, why pay so much to go to university when you have to learn content on your own?

Prof. Savransky is an understanding and caring professor. He is lenient with grading at the end of the semester, allowing students to complete an extra credit problem set. With that said, it was difficult to retain much from lectures in the course, as a flipped-classroom approach was implemented. Homework assignments were also extremely long.

Horrible professor that makes a hard class harder. Tests are easier than hws but the homework's are excruciating. Extremely tough grader. ended with a 93.9 and that was an A-. Lectures were entirely unhelpful for hw or exams. primarily poll ev based. not understanding or nice

Most organized and clear class I have ever taken. Lectures are super interesting if you watch the videos ahead of time, like you are supposed to. He is a really funny guy who helps everyone make light of what is definitely a tough class. I think he lives on Ed and gives super great explanations to any questions. Had a really great experience
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really was great to learn from as someone who never did dynamics before - everything was super clear and if anyone had a question he usually responded in less than 20 minutes online. All lecture content was online in videos/handouts which made everything super easy to reference. Homework is hard, but lectures are super engaging and interesting

He is extremely passionate and it shines through with the effort he puts into his classes. He gives very detailed & rigorous notes for his lectures; with 4060 this was incredibly helpful since it is a complex topic, however it was definitely a lot harder. Only professor I've ever had that reminded/validated us how mechE is hard & we're doing great

Great professor - definitely loves the math side of dynamics but also very knowledgeable about the material and fielding questions. Makes you work for the class but at the end of the day is forgiving about grading.

Went incredibly fast through lectures at the beginning of the class, calmed down after a few weeks. Homeworks varied, some were easy but others were really long and tough. The material covered at the end was unnecessarily difficult for the course. Was sometimes condescending in lecture but usually helpful at office hours. Open note exams.

He speeds breathlessly through lectures so it's hard enough to write anything let alone understand what he's talking about. Even worse he makes a lot of mistakes in lecture which makes you feel even more lost. Treats dynamics as if we've all been studying it for the past ten years. The textbook is just as bad. Plenty of office hrs to help though.
super fast iclicker

Lectures were confusing and there was no textbook so if you did not understand them it was tough luck and you had to hope you could figure out the slides. Tons of homework that took a while to do. Grading was super easy though and there were tons of opportunities for extra credit and retakes for quizzes. She was nice when speaking one on one.

Really hard teacher but if you get to know her super funny and helpful. Lots of homework and strict grading for sure, but if you go to office hours you'll do great. Also generous with curving and extra credit. I'm not that strong of a math/cs student and I got a good grade in the class.

The professor is clearly very knowledgeable in OR. GO TO LECTURE, you will only learn the material in lecture. Lots of office hours and TAs are great. Quizzes almost every week, and attendance is based on you turning them in/picking up. Canvas is organized abysmally. Generous curve in the class, if you try a little you will be perfectly fine.

Brenda is sometimes condescending (fair enough, she was the VP of IBM so her huge ego is justifiable). Lots of tedious homework, but grading is fair and there is a lot of opportunity for extra credit. Tests are challenging & take a long time but not all questions need to be attempted, so it's manageable. An A-/A is the average grade of the class.

Prof. Brenda's lecture arent really gonna help you learning the material but her office hours will. The class is really nice and gives you a lot of opportunities to get your grades up even if you bomb homeworks or prelims.

Homeworks and exams often felt sloppy and were tedious. It was rather easy to get a good grade, however. Lectures were rather dense and were hard to follow, though certain slides were useful in studying.

homework is really heavy and varies a lot week to week, be prepared to spend a lot of time doing it. lectures are good, definitely teach useful skills for later classes even if you're not an ORIE major. tests are very fair to the content, and extra credit opportunities can boost your grade

Professor Dietrich makes an effort to know your name and care about you as a student. The homework's kinda suck and are graded harshly, but the professor and TA's are super accessible for office hours. The tests are very straightforward and she won't throw surprises at you. If you put in the effort, you can easily do very well in this class.

Prepare the course content in advance, including teaching materials, handouts, and demonstrations. She will ensure that the classroom content is organized and coherent.She pays attention to students' progress. She will pay attention to the learning progress of the class and provide necessary guidance and support.
her class is not hard if you put in effort and she is always available for office hours and stuff
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The other reviewers had a different professor than me. The only complaint about this class is frequent algebraic mistakes on slides. The workload is relatively steep for 3 credits, but it is made up for by light grading and quality office hours. Take this class if you have any interest in ORIE ever.

Professor Dietrich is awesome! She does go over lectures a bit quick but as long as you pay adequate attention lectures are not too hard to comprehend. She hosts a lot of office hours and is always accessible. Tests are easy as long as you review quizzes, homework, and practice prelim.

Her class has a heavy workload and can be fast-paced. However, she is very accessible outside of class and is always willing to help her students. One thing to note is that she tends to give low scores at the beginning of the semester, but she is generous with her curve. Overall, while the class may be challenging, it is also very rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lecture is very heavy and move through slides very fast. There are 11 homework through the semester. Each homework is a 20 pages & coding. I took four classes this semester, and the time I spent on her class is more than the sum of the time I spend on all other classes. I am regretful everyday for not dropping this class before the deadline.

Worst professor at Cornell. Lecture slides are extremely messy, some homework questions make no sense, homework takes forever to complete, a quiz at the end of the lecture that asks questions about the material that was just taught! Exams are long as hell. Don't take her class if you are a slow writer

She goes through the lecture slides way too fast, but records and posts them after class every day so you can go back and review them which is nice. Homework is an absurd amount of work and is harshly graded, but if you go to her office hours she is very helpful and will make sure you understand it. Attendance is important, since she gives quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lecture doesn't make any sense because of all the algebraic mistakes on the slides and she skim through the concept really quickly because she had been teaching the same topic for so many years. Lots of homework and harshly graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible. Literally the worst professor I had at Cornell ever. Will never take a class with her again.

Her lecture slides are very very messy. Full of small texts and no single picture included. What is worse, she basically reads all those text word by word during the lecture. Not informative at all. Avoid this class.

She is clearly brilliant, lectures on high level topics, and interesting, relevant content. First ORIE class in which I feel things are well applied to industry. However I don't think I would enjoy the course as much, if it weren't for the grading scale being lax (mostly participation and homework completion grades) as I was free to make mistakes.

She is actually the worst teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are uninformative, so you have to figure everything out yourself. She makes the homeworks impossible and super time consuming. The Prelims and Finals are copy and pasted from the practice exams, but there is no enough time to finish, ever. NEVER taking a class taught by Brenda, EVER.

You can probably get by without going to lecture, but be prepared to read the course packet because the uploaded lecture notes are vague--and even then, she doesn't follow the course packet that well. The homework assignments have contradictory, ambiguous directions, and sometimes unrelated to lecture content; they basically set you up for failure.

Have taken a few classes with Kriner, and they have all been amazing. The lectures are so interesting, and he loves engaging with students to hear their thoughts. If you have a decent understanding of politics, then this class will be so chill.

Great lecturer, passionate about the political system and the presidency in particular. Engaged the class in lecture and encouraged participation. Heavy on readings and grading could be a bit arbitrary but super approachable professor and really easy to work with.

Professor Kriner is a phenomenal lecturer. He's very engaging and obviously knowledgeable about his field of study.
Prelims are fairly easy if you go to lecture, participate in discussion, and review lecture notes. Important to actually do the assigned readings, as they are often recalled on prelims and the final.

Great guy, clear he loves what he does and is very passionate. Not reading off a script ever, very knowledgable. Just 3 essays throughout the semester with clear outlines. Final was online. Would take again!
Study up on readings and get on your TAs good side for papers

Really great professor! Definitely would recommend taking this class. Lectures basically repeat the textbook, but interesting information can be found in the lectures. Lecture notes can also be found online, and attendance not taken so you'll be fine missing a couple lectures. Discussions pretty important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is pretty easy and Kriner is a very good lecturer, often offering different perspectives on current government problems. Lectures aren't really important, but they are interesting. Make sure to do the readings and attend discussions, as a bulk of the tests are on the ideas from the readings... other topics are common sense US Govt principles
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: great professor seemed to be very knowledgeable and cares about the topics. lectures aren't that important but are pretty interesting. midterm and final are not bad at all if you go to the discussion sections.

I feel so lucky to have taken his class. He is such an intelligent person and engaging lecturer, and you will learn so much about the subject just from listening to him in class even if you already know a lot about politics. He is so chill that he made our final online since it was late in the semester and gives helpful extra credit opportunities.

Kriner is very passionate about what he teaches, and it shows. Great lectures. Wants the best for his students. Interesting material, little homework, several opportunities for extra credit. Grade is based on 3 writing assignments, 1 prelim, and 1 take home final. Would highly recommend this class for anyone who's interested in gov't/politics.

Solid class for understanding basics of U.S. government function. Assignments are time consuming but straightforward. Exams require basic memorization. It is a large class, so the lectures aren't always super engaging.
Incredibly intelligent and so open to talk with students. Really loved this class and would definitely take again.

Doug Kriner is by far one of the best Government professors at Cornell. It's clear he is passionate what he teaches and is always happen to listen what students have to say. Discussion sections matter! Make sure to do readings as they are vital for prelims and writing assignments. Overall, this was a fantastic course!
For GOVT3161: It's a fine class, but all of the writing assignments are heavily stats based (analysis and all that), so please be aware of that before signing up.

An amazing lecturer, so if you don't like the class, it probably means you don't want to study government. Participation in discussions are mandatory but graded somewhat arbitrarily. It can be tough to figure out what TAs want from writing assignments. Exams aren't bad.

Lectures weren't engaging. I just got by with my general knowledge of American politics and didn't do most of the reading. The data analyses he assigns should be super easy but take a lot longer because he wants you to use Microsoft Excel. It wasn't a bad class content-wise, but it was so complicated that I wouldn't put myself through it again

Although the content itself was interesting, it felt as though he was ranting during lecture, and not all the material that he talks about is on the slides, so if you miss a day, you will more than likely fall behind (as he doesn't even post them). Also, so much reading. There are only a few assignments, and if you don't do one, watch out!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I loved intro to American politics with Kriner. He is passionate about the subject matter and does a great job of incorporating data to make the themes have a poignant impact for the present day. He does focus heavily on the lecture slides, but he is a really good lecturer. 

The supplemental readings are SUPER important to do well in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kriner was really knowledgeable about American Government, and I learned a lot in his class. What I disliked about this class were the TAs. Mine graded extremely harshly without giving good feedback and barely covered the readings during discussion.

Great class! Prof. Kriner really shines when talking about his speciality of the American Presidency. Throughout the course he provided insight and fostered interesting discussion about the American Presidency. Grading was generous and the final project (a survey) was both interesting and relatively straightforward. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Skip this class if u can, I took it for fun and it made me change my whole major. I originally came in as a govt major and immediately changed it after this class. TAs graded unfairly (some didnt read any of the papers while others never gave above a B) his lectures are BORING, it was the longest 75 min of my life and I had to do it twice a week

Kriner is one of the best lecturers at Cornell. Other intro classes barely scrape half the class to show up to lectures, while most students showed up to Kriners lectures, despite them mostly repeating the textbook readings. Kriner was an engaging lecturer and I genuinely enjoyed showing up to class, but TA discretion largely determined grades...

I have Kriner now and he does not read from a script anymore. I can tell he is passionate about what he is lecturing on, and that he cares about the students. He is charismatic and funny and I would take another class of his.
Professor Kriner's lectures sure are scripted; however, the detailed descriptions of each topic are super useful.

Although you can tell hes reading from a script, I appreciated his effort to organize lectures in a way that helped students study for exams. I loved staying after lecture to listen to him answer students questions; I could tell that Kriner loved what he was teaching and was happy to see students engage.

Readings are dense sometimes, but are always analyzed in the discussion section so you can get the main ideas. In his lectures, it was clear that he puts a lot of time and effort into considering what to talk about - he does a lot of case studies/data analysis, and he is so accessible in office hours and invites student participation always!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures were incredibly boring. I swear he was reading off a script during class. His lecture slides were disorganized and all over the place. However, we had really good discussions during class. We also only had four assignments due throughout the semester, and they were super light.
Loved prof Kriner! He puts so much effort into his lectures, and the workload is totally manageable, all while learning a tremendous amount.

Alright what.. This class has an hour and 15 minute lectures along with a 50 minute snooze discussion section that requires participation or you get points deducted from your grade. There are pre-recorded 30 minute long lectures & as someone else pointed out he reads off a script, NOT ENGAGING. Theres also sm readings, 4 essays midterm and a final.

Kriner seems like a nice guy, but in lectures all he does in ramble on. You can literally see him reading off of his screen during live lectures AND pre-recorded lectures, so it's hard to engage with the material he's reciting. He also makes you read overly-long material before class. (BEWARE if you have no background in US gov / history)

Lectures are fascinating and always involve real-world applications/examples. Trump's impeachment inquiry began a month after class started, and Kriner adjusted on the fly and dedicated a bunch of class time to the impeachment proceedings. Somewhat easy A if you engage with the material.

Prof. Kriner gives lively lectures with opportunities for student input; theres a clear rationale throughout. Course went through insightful analysis on history of and contemporary debates on American government.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Toby is the goat. He makes you genuinely interested in the material and doesn't make his exams very difficult - they just test the main broad topics, nothing too specific. This class made me switch my concentration to microbio... everyone should take it!!
Microbiology is a hard course however Professor Doerr makes this class very engaging and interesting. He cares a lot about his students, and genuinely wants them to succeed.

Doerr was such a funny and sweet professor. His lectures were always engaging, and he really is passionate about microbiology which made me enjoy it too. His lecture slides can be a little overwhelming sometimes, and he does tend to go very in-depth about topics that aren't necessarily covered on the more straightforward exams. Still great prof!
Amazing guy. Smart, funny, knowledgable.
A professor that genuinely wants you to succeed. Rare to find within the bio major. Absolutely take him if you can. Also gives you skibidi toilet freebies.
He is so amazing!!!! I was ready to give up bio but he made me fall back in love. SO GOOD AT EXPLAINING CONCEPTS. He should teach more classes.
Honestly, one of the nicest profs I've met here. He makes the material digestible and is so accommodating to anyone's situation! A real lad
I really enjoyed his lectures and would show up even though attendance was not required. He was sometimes funny and the content was not too difficult.

Professor Doerschuk is a great guy--kind, funny, and approachable. However, his lectures were hard to follow and unorganized. I hardly ever looked back at my notes from lecture since they just weren't helpful when studying/doing homework and relied heavily on the textbook and youtube videos. Office hours are a must.
Teaches word for word from the textbook, so if you don't have a problem with that, he's great. Class overall isn't too hard and is like BC with some extra methods here and there.
He wasn't the best at explaining new material, so I would definitely read the textbook before class. Occasionally hilarious.
Lectures are not very useful if you haven't read the new material beforehand. But the office hours are amazing. He is an amazing and kind person always ready to help

absolute worst!Made ECE4670 a nightmare! Has no idea what's going on in labs,didn't cover the materials required for labs in lectures; HWs,labs left ungraded(has been 60 days), converted in-class prelim to take-home exam DURING the last 5 min of the exam! 9 min late to class on average, unresponsive on email/Piazza,Messed up commcloud several times

Not quite sure what class the previous student went to because his class is extremely disorganized. Piazza questions mainly left unanswered. The 3rd prelim was not graded till a week after the final. No regrades for either exam but they were "available for pickup in his office" days after the last day of finals when most students had already left.

Contrary to many reviews, Doerschuk's class was organized. A very caring professor who spent times outside of class to go over HW. His prelims are definitely fair when you study for them. He held review session, which I recommend.
HILARIOUS

I want to preface this by saying that Peter Doerschuk is not a bad guy. That being said, he is the most disorganized man I have met in my life. No syllabus on the first day, no exam stats when handing back tests, posting exam review after the exam, not showing up to his own review session. Come to lecture only if you want to make fun of his voice.

Super funny during lecture. Lectures are disorganized but the textbook and his typed notes make it pretty clear. He always gives out what will be on the exam so study those HW problems specifically or you'll fail. He also gives answers to the hw at the help sessions so go to them. Although I loved doerschuk, I don't think I learned much.

This mans is chaotic good. Super unorganized and sort of just unaware of what goes on outside his world, eg university policies and such, but really just trying to do good by his students. He's really explicit about what kinds of problems will be on exams, so just gotta know those and you're fine!

Very easy professor to learn from. He clearly writes down all the concepts during lectures as well as gives you very helpful hints for exam problems. Always has a review session before homework due dates and exams. Plus, he's really funny and likes to have fun while teaching.

Super funny lectures and pretty clear lectures, but there is a good amount of disorganization. Disorganization doesn't detract from the course too much.  Fair exams, with very specific hints to content on them. Really got me interested in signals in the first place.

Negative stigma about him is over hyped. I've had many professors who were harder to follow along during lecture. He really does care about students and wants everyone to succeed. He is also hilarious. However, the course's administration is disorganized. He gives extra help sessions every week. He drops one prelim grade.

Professor Doerschuk is extraordinarily enthusiastic and a nice guy. That being said, he has made an art form of disorganization. If you like things being on time and proceeding in a logical fashion, it will drive you insane. Tests: go to his review sessions if at all possible or talk to someone who was there; makes studying easier and more focused

Professor Doerschuk was... interesting. He's a really nice guy and seemed like he really wanted to help his students, answering any questions. Had review sessions before each exam and the night before each pset was due. He just was bad in lecture, where material was confusing, he went out of order from book. Final grades were lower than expected

This is definitely my worst teacher ever at Cornell. Makes such an easy course unnecessarily hard, assumes a lot when he explains, doesn't have a syllabus, jumps back and forth in the textbook, gives a lot of exam matching questions not related to the lecture and I can continue ranting on and on. But take signals with this man at your ow risk.
He tries to act cool but doesnt understand subject. Long winded explanations spends too much time on minor details and misses the point. Exams are same style.

Please don't take any class with this professor. He doesn't comes prepared for his lectures...makes the course a joke..his special ability is to present easy things in extremely difficult and incomplete way.His examz never focus on the true content of the class. His questions are full of ambiguity. I lost all my interest for the subject boz of him.

He explains concepts in an extremly clear way. Although some people mentioned that problem sets are long, there are only 6 in total and they are not very difficult. He also gives three practice exams before each prelim and the final, whch is super helpful.

McKee is honestly one of (if not the) best professors I have ever had at Cornell. He not only knows the material but can explain it in very simple terms, and actually cares about his students. I almost didn't take 3130 (not good at maths, never seen prob/stats before) but risked it since I'd heard he's an amazing prof, and best decision of my life!
The undisputed goat

This is probably the most useful class I've ever taken, and McKee is a chill guy. However, I didn't find the way he taught to be intuitive or helpful and I learned much more through self-studying. Problem sets do seem to be connected to the exams, but they were pretty long and repetitive which added a lot of work to an already difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To preface, he is an great person. However, lectures are unclear and hard to follow. Problem sets are long, but the bigger issue is that they are repetitive and include ideas meant to be "implied" (not mentioned) in lecture. The workload was certainly worth more than 4 credits yet the support systems did not align with what students needed help on.

[This rating is for Teaching and Learning Economics]. Amazing lecturer! Cares deeply about students and will know your name and offer to provide support if you need it. Be ready for a lot of group work.

McKee's teaching style is confusing: lectures are relaxed with frequent 10+ minute poll-EV breaks for asinine questions, but exams have medians of 70. If you've taken 3030 with him, 3120 will be much easier. Advice: when he sends out the form for what group you would like to be in, select you want the first row - it's going to help your grade.

Prof. McKee showed genuine interest in and enthusiasm for course content, and he was very accessible outside of class. He once spent over an hour in an appointment with just me to help me prep for the second prelim. The course content built up throughout the semester, so in my opinion, things got easier as you went, which helped too.
Great professor. Very charismatic and wants the best for his students.

Prof McKee is the best professor I have had at Cornell. I took ECON 3130 with him and even though it was a lot of homework, I enjoyed my time in this class. He truly cares for his students and is a nice, empathetic person. I'm a stats major, and he explains the content better than all stats profs at Cornell. Lots of hw but you can get help in OH!

This class was one of the hardest classes I've taken. But, Professor McKee was super kind and as helpful as he could have been. He also does a thing where instead of attending class you can watch the lectures and submit answers to the pollev questions which is lit.

Extremely fair grader. Very nice and funny teacher. Prof.McKee is very responsive to questions posted on Ed Discussion (he stayed up till 12am sometimes during the final week). Never curve down. Lectures cover some hard concepts and are sometimes confusing, but the exams are straightforward. Exams are curved generously if too hard.

Professor McKee is a great lecturer and professor. They always try to make the class interesting and applicable to the real world. The work can be a lot but he is always willing to help students when needed! I would absolutely take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the kindest professors I've encountered. He has great lectures, which are all recorded and posted, and is really good at explaining complex topics. Exams have a group portion at the end to boost your grade, and he is very fair overall with grading. Overall a great professor and human being.
Very accessible and understanding professor. He is willing to help in Econ3030 and is a professor economic majors should get to know.

Loved ECON 3030 with McKee though it was difficult at times to keep up paticularly as someone who took the class freshman fall. There's quite a bit of content in the course so it's important to keep up by going to office hours and to discussion sections. The TAs are really good so do take advantage of their help.

The exams were pretty tough and made sure you did all the homeworks legit and understood them. In person lectures aren't required in the sense you could make them up later. Quizzes were just tedious (but some of the questions showed up on the exams so make sure to do them). His lectures were very useful and him and a student were very active on ED.

Great professor with really great lectures. He is very active on Ed and quickly responds to emails. Very open to adapt to students' needs. Sometimes the homeworks were huge and also not the biggest fan of the PollEv's but you can do them after the class if you miss the lecture. Fair exams.

Exams aren't about how well you know the material, but about how much can he twist the material so that he can get the bell curve. 
Covers a lot of material in one class, make sure to study every week. He's a good prof, but exams just don't fairly reflect what we have studied or done in class/psets.
Best Econ professor for core classes by far. Teaches difficult material in an accessible way, but you will still have to put in the effort.

Bad comments are disappointing. He is an expert in economics education, truly the best Cornell prof. He can cover so many topics on time but also make you comprehend the important parts by giving you intuition without confusing you. GO TO THE LECTURES, they are well planned, you won't need to study much later. Very inspirational if you like econ!
Absolute goat.... this man makes a strong case for fav prof all time
Good guy

The class lacks a lot of substance relating to some very important concepts. Problem sets are nothing like the exams and are often long and repetitive, not really helping you improve much. Exams are pretty easy, but he tends to make them long for little substantive reason. Also, there is a really annoying group project that just super tedious.

Lots of econ majors love McKee. Very caring/accommodating but also fair. Teaches one of the most important core courses in econ and makes it worth your while. His "flipped classroom" technique wasn't my favorite, but it at least keeps people engaged during lecture. Class is even accessible to non-econ majors. He's just goated. Hope he sticks around

McKee is one of my favorite professors. I hadn't taken a math class in years, but he explained things clearly in class and was very accessible in office hours. The problem sets and the practice prelims were EXTREMELY helpful to learn and to study. I literally just did the practice prelims several times to study and got A's. Excellent teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Excellent professor! Long problem sets (I would definitely work with other people on these, which he encourages) but I learned a ton! I'm glad I took this class with professor mckee.

Amazing teacher! Professor McKee genuinely cares about his students & their learning. He's super helpful in office hours, especially for problem set and lecture questions. The textbook isn't necessary (I didn't even use it) but participation is VERY helpful. Also, the previous exams are a great way to study!!
Overall 10/10 great prof!
Incredible and passionate lecturer that truly stands out for his great ability at communicating the material. Would absolutely take any course with Professor McKee again!

One of the more overrated professors in the Econ department. He gives very superficial explanations for the concepts covered in the class and doesn't seem to care if students understand the underlying math and statistics. If you're looking for a class where you'll learn and be challenged, don't take this class.

McKee is a fantastic lecturer and really approachable outside of class. Go to his office hours, he's exceedingly helpful and always does his best to help the student understand. Prelims and final were very fair, problem sets were fine and he drops 1. Plenty of extra credit opportunities to boot. Definitely taking a class with him again if I can.

Prof. McKee is a real nice guy who is ready to help anytime. The positioning of the course was a bit weird as it is supposed to be a somewhat rigorous course but the target audience is a group of econ majors who have no training in higher math at all. The result is "learning" a bunch of formulae you never have to prove (or see the proof).

Nice and approachable, but class was structured badly. Required attendance at 8am lectures, where a lot of the time was spent in silent breakout rooms. Exams were all multiple choice, which is horrible for a math-heavy course!!! Problem sets were laborious, but really helpful to learn material. Overall good prof, bad class.

This man is easily the best professor I've had so far. He is a great lecturer, but more importantly he is super considerate and accommodating especially during a tough semester. Absolute goat, and this is coming from someone who took his 8am class.

Professor McKee is one of the best professors in the Econ department. He manages to make every class entertaining with games and challenges, even when course material is a bit dry. If you're someone who does better with active learning than lecture-style courses, I highly recommend ECON 3030 with McKee!
He's a really funny and interesting lecturer. Examples given in lecture are very good and help students understand the material

It took me time to get used to Professor McKee's interactive style of teaching, but once I did, I really enjoyed the class. Professor McKee truly cares about making sure students are thinking about the material in relation to the world they are living in. Go to office hours, they're really helpful.
Overall good teacher. Interesting lectures, relatively long homework (but nothing too bad), and pretty easy exams.
Prof McKee is amazing. He really cares for his students and rewards effort. Problem sets are quite challenging, prelims are less so. Highly recommend to take 3030 with him.

McKee is a stud- never seen a professor so intentioned in structuring their class. First day of class I was in awe at his grading criteria/expectations. He tries to reward hard work and understanding, not penalize you if you're struggling. He APPLIES the stuff we are learning to the real world. Don't expect an easy class, it's still a lot of work..
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: McKee is AMAZING. He knows his stuff, cares for students, class is not an easy A, but easy B if you study a lot. He is just a great guy in general, and as a prof he is ok. Online quizzes, HW, project, exams, and group exams. He does everything he can to make sure you get at least a B for 3120, not so sure about 3030. He is passionate about teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: Really approachable and nice professor. I put off taking this class on purpose because this class is one of the most rigorous classes one takes in the Economics major. I was fortunate enough to have this professor. Although problem sets are long, he is a great lecturer and as long as you pay attention in class he explains the material well.
The most amazing professor I've ever met. Professor McKee is super nice and a really good teacher. His office hours are valuable.

It's unfortunate that this is a required class for the Economics major at Cornell. This is a god awful class with a professor that doesn't teach clearly and gives extremely long and dumb problem sets. Be prepared to learn stata and try to work with people that may not want to work with you. WORST class I've taken so far.

Professor McKee is not only a fantastic teacher, but an awesome person. I had a bad first exam, but McKee was very easy to talk to and make sure my grade was not affected by one bad performance. When I had this meeting, I got to talk to Professor McKee as an equal and a counselor. He has been very successful; talk to him if you get the chance!

Professor Mckee is great! He is clearly passionate about the material and it really shows in his teaching. Its a hard course by its nature, but Doug does a good job of making it understandable. If you put in work, its definitely doable. Would highly recommend the class and the professor!
reviews.rating_tags: GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: This professor makes Intermediate microeconomics interesting and exciting! He also really cares about teaching and uses different perspectives to engage the class. Definitely one of my favorite teachers. He made me love the econ major again and have some hope. ECON 3030 was still just as hard as I had heard though.

I had put off taking this course because I was really scared but McKee is very sweet and patient. He actually cares about teaching-even has a whole podcast and blog about it. If you go to lecture and try your best to do the p-sets and actually are able to solve them before exams you can do really well. He's very helpful during office hours too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: WORST class I've taken at Cornell. Hands down. Purposely long and hard problem sets that no one could solve. Just resulted in students writing stuff down they didn't even understand.  Each problem set was painful, even after going to lectures and discussions. This class killed my major and cumulative GPA all on its own.

Most professors tell you how to improve essays. Not prof. Hill. Will instead ask what you think of your essay. Seeing a fortune teller about your essay may have the same results. Take a different class.

Every office hour consisted of me asking him for feedback and him saying "But what do *you* think should be changed?" while providing nothing from his side. EXTREMELY HARSH GRADER. In a required FWS class, only 2-3 people got 90+, even though the assignment topics were really hard. I communicated to him that English is my second language, no effect

Dr. Andrew Hill is easily the best professor I had at Cornell. Intelligent and well-spoken, even among his Ivy-League peer, yet lenient, caring, and clear. While he doesn't do much to make lectures exciting, the brilliant things he has to say about the material are enough to keep anyone sincerely interested in the subject matter thoroughly engaged.

At first I did not like his class at all. There were reading responses due before every class, and the texts he gives are quite challenging. The readings were a stepping stone to the final curatorial project Overall, Dr. Hill is very approachable and VERY lenient with deadlines. His grading criteria could be more clear. Helped me improve my writing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the most inspiring and fascinating minds you can find. I had Dr. Hill for my FWS, and was so motivated by his incredibly designed class format and assignments that I took his ENGL 2690 course. Any of his courses are essential if you are looking to evolve as a writer, artist, historian, or scholar. I can't recommend enough!
Great teaching style
very good professor

Heard good things about Professor Hill although I have not taken his class. Absolutely brilliant mind and is caring but forthright. Indubiably the most incredible human. 10/10 would take his class again.

When you think of the greats, who comes to mind? Albert Einstein, Isaac Newton, Nikola Tesla, perhaps. For me, it's Andrew Hill. Hill's mind may be the most brilliant I've ever had the honor of engaging with. Every thought was so well-formed, every conclusion so clear and decisive. I was in awe in every class.
Great professor with a great teaching style. Professor Hill is one of the most well spoken individuals I have ever met, and he makes his lectures and discussions enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy might genuinely be the most well versed person I know. Not only that but he let me borrow his lambo when my car was in the shops. I would die for this man
not responsive at all to emails
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: no just no
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: avoid at all costs

Overall, Professor Hill teaches a solid class, one that is highly conducive to creating unique perspectives on whatever reading is being covered. He cares a lot about students' progress and makes himself easily available, though he's not very engaging as a teacher and sometimes struggles to capture a class's attention.

Professor Hill is a little bit strange, definitely quirky but a funny guy once you get to know him. He shows no mercy when grading essays, and assigns several difficult readings every class. Like why was I reading a 50 page medieval bestiary and a culty version of the bible for homework. Overall, I would just switch.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Whitmore is pretty chill and straight to the point. Some content might be difficult but the TA's and the professor himself are very helpful. There's a fair amount of work but it never gets too difficult.
Really easy class, but significant amounts of work, and the TAs grade strictly but fairly. The professor is easily accessible through emails, office hours, or in person.

Professor Whitmore's class structure is odd, but pretty easy. 1740 is a super useful course and I genuinely learned a lot from it this semester. That being said, he doesn't really know how to answer questions. He doesn't really teach in class, only from video lectures, so I spent a lot of time working on materials outside of class. TAs are helpful.

Honeslty one of my favourite professors. He doesnt waste time and is a great teacher. He teaches exactly what you need to know for exams. Before the prelims and final, we have one full class for review where he will work through a similiar practice paper to the exam and makes the assignment as similar to exam as possible. very good guy. Lots of HW
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have taken two of his classes now and can say he is a really good professor. He is not as approachable for small talk as other professors but he does a really good job at teaching. He goes through content and explains everything in the best way possible. Everything is very easy to understand and his slides are also very concise.

I feel like Professor Whitmore is about as good a professor as you can get for biz comp. In class he's always willing to help you and his TAs are helpful as well (and hold lots of office hours). Regardless of who you get, the class has a ton of work, so just do it and you should be fine. The excel prelim and final are easy imo, only word was hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Practical class. Teacher was professional. Maybe too much coding in the lecture though.
Very useful class for internship and jobs. One of the harder core classes, but worth it at the end.

Now that we got our final grades I am much more satisfied with this class. It was a hard semester back on campus after over a year of remote learning. The situation with the final being postponed until the following semester didn't help either. That was the university, not him though. I did better than I expected and I think the grading was fair.

Pretty good. Was clear about expectations. Tough grader though. Good at explaining stuff in person, but the structure of the class didn't really facilitate much of that. I would suggest to hold more office hours and get to know students more. Other than that I learned a lot from him.
The single worst teacher I have ever had for a lectures. Disrespectful, entitled, arrogant, and self absorbed.

Professor Whitmore was 100% my worst professor this semester. His course is set up terribly so I will give him some credit for that, but he made it even worse. If someone was doing bad in the class, the other two prof. would try to help and give feedback but Whitmore did none. If you had an issue with grading or a question, he left you on your own

Andrew Whitmore is possibly the least caring professor I've ever had. He acts very passive aggressive towards students and is not accommodating towards individuals who ask questions. When students try to ask questions he usually gets angry rather than being helpful and asking a question.
Whitmore is the goat

Homework is 50% of the final grade and pretty easy, so if you do all the work you'll be fine. Be sure to format all things based on the rubric. It doesn't really matter which professor you have for this class because all content is the same (not sure if it's only because of online classes).
Simply the least understanding instructor at Cornell.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Whitmore is very professional and helpful. He will respond to your emails quickly and is responsive on discussion boards (if you have them). I highly suggest meeting with the TA's because they will be grading most of your assignments. I would definitely take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Whitmore is very talented and clear in his presentations and Business Computing comes highly recommended to any Cornellian. Though he can come off as arrogant and annoyed, he displays information in an easy to understand and comprehensive manner.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There are a few pop quizzes and a lot of reading, but the workload is manageable if you focus on key ideas. Professor Moisey is extremely funny and makes every lecture engaging with great jokes. I would recommend this course to anyone, even just for fun. He is super patient, answers questions clearly, and really encourages interest in learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lecturer that keeps you engaged and makes fun jokes. Took this class just for fun and out of interest, and I was able to learn so much more about photography. Exams are not hard and the TAs are super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Moisey is an incredible professor. I'm taking his class as a senior and wish I knew of him sooner. His lectures not only make me laugh out loud, but the way he roots the content in the broader scope of life makes every lecture incredible interesting and at times deeply moving. If you haven't had a class with him, you're missing out!
Genuinely good prof who cares about his students and their ability to learn. Entertaining in both content and presentation

Professor Moisey is an amazing lecturer, this is my favorite class at Cornell. He's genuinely interested in the material and explores it alongside you, plus is insanely entertaining which makes it easy to pay attention. The reading is a lot, but get the big ideas (skim+) and you'll be fine. Start the final paper early, and get your TA to proofread!

Lectures were always the highlight of my day. Moisey is a thoroughly interesting professor who encourages students to think outside the box and embrace somewhat abstract concepts. Very sad that I probably won't be able to take another one of his classes.

A professor that sincerely cares about what you learn and how it will impact your future life—whether that's academically or just day-to-day. He makes you think critically and creatively. He carefully curates lectures and guest speakers. Highly recommend his class and am grateful for all I learned.

Did not like Moisey. Not a difficult class but he was very full of himself and had minimal structure beyond his stream of conscience rambling. He was disrespectful to students on a few occasions as well and was not very approachable.
passionate but rude
Don't graduate without taking an Andrew Moisey class.

Moisey is an amazing lecturer. He is the funniest and most passionate professor you will ever meet. The topics for this class are very interesting and makes you think about the world in a deeper way. If you've taken Visual Studies, please take this class too. It's so worth it.
It was fine
Moisey is a great professor and he makes the course content interesting and engaging. The teaching team is very accommodating. Would definitely recommend to people even if they are non-majors.

Took this as a distribution requirement, and was definitely one of my more interesting ones. Classes at the beginning are definitely a little more boring, but second half was where I felt things got more interesting/relevant. Very easy class, Moisey also made attending lecture interesting even if the content was hit or miss for me. Funny guy

Moisey is such a funny and engaging lecturer. This class opens your eyes in ways few others do. ATTEND LECTURE, ALWAYS. Do the readings (they can be dense/long, but that's where lecture comes in). If you take diligent notes & review them before the exam so that you're familiar with the order of material, you'll do great (open-note exams).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: By far the best class I have ever taken at Cornell (and I think the best one I ever will take). He's the most engaging, enthusiastic, and humorous lecturer and he really makes you care about the material. You will leave every class with your mind blown.

Best class I have taken at Cornell. Goes beyond "Visual Studies" and explains everyday life. Moisey is an engaging lecturer and totally hilarious. Really cares about what he teaches. The first few readings are weed out but it gets more interesting after that. Definitely don't do the final paper at the last minute. Easy grading.
Fantastic professor. Fantastic class. You will never be bored in lecture, and you will leave with many things to think about.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really great class. Do the readings, participate in lecture discussions, attend the out of class events, and put effort into the major paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My favorite course I have taken. Highly interdisciplinary-- covers many potentially weighty theoretical and philosophical topics. The majority of the grade is a 15 page research paper, which he insists on being an intervention -- asking and answering a question that begs both. He is hilarious, and he wants you to care about the class. Approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Don't do it!

Pretty good professor! He is a nice guy and each time i went to office hour he really inspired me a lot. He truly wants all students to learn sth from his class. Comm1101 is chill and graded totally depends on ta.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Highly recommend this professor! Really enjoyed learning content in this class. Not a lot of assignments and lectures were interesting. Had many breakouts in class, so it was very engaging. Weekly discussions provided a helpful overview of what was learned in class that week. Extra credit offered through sona and final was very easy.
I actually took comm 1101 with him. He made pretty much every lecture engaging and fun to attend.

After coming to the first day of class, it was instantly clear that Prof Margolin was a bad professor. He's outdated and out of touch (he said that technology was not allowed in the classroom at all and that we had take handwritten notes). You could also sense was egotism... he talks as if what he's teaching is very important even though it's not.

He is pompous and thinks too highly of himself. The class is just him inflating his own ego and making the material harder than it is. I was bored throughout the semester. I would suggest taking a different professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture information was pretty straightforward. Class content feels like it could be summed up in a netflix docuseries tbh. Prof seemed cocky or snobby the entire semester - not sure what their deal was there. Overall could've made the class more interesting or thought provoking.
nice guy, annoying little class assignments, lectures get increasingly messy/ hard to follow. Still enjoyed the class and able to perform well.

Show up to class and submit your attendance. Lectures are easy and clear to follow. Test questions can be ambiguous. If I studied for more than a few hours before each prelim, I would've done better. Final is noncumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I liked INFO 2450 with Professor Margolin for the most part. The assignments gave you a lot of time to complete. He is a good lecturer at class when explaining concepts; however, some of his test questions are unnecessarily confusing. The exams could have been designed better to test the taught materials.

Engaging professor, does a good job explaining things. Tests aren't hard if you put in the effort, mostly just understanding vocabulary and coming up with your own examples. Writing assignments are easy A's if you clearly follow the guidelines. 1 video project, again easy A if you put in the effort. EC offered thru SONA.

Very clear grading criteria. There are three tests (15%) and 7 individual assignments (45%) plus attendance (10%). I thoroughly enjoyed going to Margolin's class twice a week. He's a passionate and assertive speaker. Just be careful of the third prelim.

He's a pretty engaging professor during lecture and gives a lot of relevant examples. Grading in the class is pretty harsh despite the material being pretty easy to understand. Annoying little things you have to do in the class like tweet twice a week and do short written assignments.

very very good lecturer, lots of interaction with students. class is feirly easy, but he keeps it interesting by relating everything to real world examples or concepts. the lectures are the key, and he does a very good job of explaining everything

He knows his stuff really well and cares that you learn but the class is insanely tedious. The workload is very heavy, feels like a 7 credit class with the group homework, random assignments, 2 hour calculation sessions, 3 prelims, and projects sprinkled in between. Plan wisely and make an effort to ask him questions and engage with the class.
He grades like he genuinely wants to fail you and makes the workload unbelievable undoable. Has a passive aggressive tone when speaking and you have to use the textbook he wrote.
A lot of work. Homeworks were so tedious and did not yield much. Overall a difficult class and a lot of your time commitment will be spent here. The professor gave good lectures.
Wasn't the best person but was a decent teacher. Learned a lot but he isn't the nicest.

This class was a nightmare. Insanely long homeworks with barely any course staff that could help. Exams were graded SO HARSHLY with almost close to 0 partial credit. Always rude whenever you spoke to him and lectures were always useless. Not sure what's gotten into him this semester.
Not sure if I had the same professor as other reviewers because he was always passive aggressive, declined to help you, and had a huge ego problem.

Prof Duncan cares a lot of about students learning, his lectures are very well organized and based off the textbook he wrote. TAs were cool and helpful with problem solving. Spreadsheet assignments were a pain but overall not that bad as far as ENGRD goes. I never went to the discussions but I'm pretty that's 10% grade for attendance.

Very good lecturer. Grading is spread evenly between homework, prelims and a final. Workload is fairly light. Lectures follow the textbook, but I would recommend reading the textbook before every lecture. Grading was lenient on exams and class was slightly curved. Would highly recommend this class for an engineering distribution as well.

Generally Duncan is a good professor. Can be blunt in lecture when receiving questions he thinks should be obvious. Group homeworks can be a drag. Tests require very solid conceptual understanding of the content, he will reapply concepts to completely new situations, so do lots of practice. Occasionally funny.

Prof. Duncan's lectures are AMAZING, and he provides every document on his website for easy access. We always knew what was expected of us, and office hours were well-timed throughout the week. Tests were difficult but fair, and homework was done in groups, which I personally loved. Sometimes he can be a bit sarcastic, but he is a great professor.
He was a passive-aggressive professor so it was not a welcoming environment when you wanted to talk to him. Plus, you have to buy his textbook he wrote.

A very respectable and respectful professor who genuinely cares about his students. His care takes the form of wanting the best for the student, which doesn't translate into lax standards in any way. Excellent explanations. Office hours are incredibly valuable.

While homework groups were annoying at times, they weren't terrible. All exams (3 prelims+final) were completely fair and if you took good notes in lecture and really understood homework and section problems, they were straight forward. Don't slack because it seems easier than PChem. Advice, do all problems yourself before exam so YOU actually know
Not the easiest intro course, but probably the most useful. Anyone with the slightest inclination toward pursuing ChemE should take the course.

TMD is the man! He lets you know from the start that it is not a normal intro class in the fact that you must work hard and you learn, but if you stick through it you gain a whole new perspective on your chosen major. It does stink that he wrote the textbook because lectures can seem repetitive, but he is very personable and helpful in office hours

He's an odd teacher - doesn't really teach to the style of the students, despite the fact that he says otherwise. Heavy emphasis on the textbook. Really smart guy though, but didn't seem connected to any of the students but his favorites.

He is best professor I have ever met. He always make everything clear and his class is well organized. Although it is not an easy class to get good grades, you can learn a lot in his class, not only engineering knowledge, but the attitude towards life, critical thinking and communication skills.
Professor Duncan changed my interest from "What is chemical engineering?" to "This is the coolest stuff ever!"
AMAZING

Fantastic course teacher.  Poor advisor.  Condescending if you are not confident or if you do not agree with him.  This is college; kids are supposed to find themselves, not be discouraged. His favorites get more confident while the shy ones get more shy.  This is an unfair and unstable method to students.

In a perfect situation Duncan would be a great teacher. He interacts with the class, seems friendly and is very intelligent.  But the reality is, he takes things personally, a very bad characteristic for someone in a position to educate.  Once he aligns himself against you, consider avoiding him at all costs and not depending on him for help.
He intimidates me ... oh TMD

I had him for multivariable calc and he was a great teacher. He was out of his subject matter and he did an excellent job of teaching the material. He was clear, comprehensive, and loved to interact with the class.
He's definitely someone who picks favorites. But watch out if he doesn't like you. He'll make your life miserable.

This is a very rigorous introduction to chemical engineering. It is not an easy class, but you will learn a lot if you put your earnest effort to it. A lot of skills are honed in this class. For instance, interpreting graphs, guessimating, etc. It is a critical thinking class, and this is how the professor wanted it to be.

Avoid this class at all means possible.  It requires much more work than an intro class and more time consuming than 3 credits should be. If you are thinking of being a chemical engineering, you will really rethink it after this class.

First time a teacher actually knew my name and cares how i was doing. Duncan is by far the best teacher I've had at Cornell (he was named teacher of the year in NY for 2007!) If you take this class, beware, he knows your name and whether or not you care to show up or try hard
Awesome teacher, very willing to help anyone out!!  Teaches great classes.
The best teacher that I have had so far.  He really knows what he is teaching and has a good sense of humor.  Excellent use of chalk and TAs.

He really knows his stuff, but taking notes in class is really hard because of the handouts.  Its impossible to study from the notes in class, and the text isnt much help. Best way to study is do the practice problems on the website. Office hours were overcrowded and the TA's didnt have enough time to be particularly helpful to anyone.
Great Professor in terms of knowing the material and getting it through to the students. Intro to cheme class will give you a good idea of wether chemical engineering is what you want.

The textbook is horrible and convoluted.  you basically buy it for the HW problems inside.  taking notes in class is nearly impossible and pointless since he passes out so many handouts. limited number of practice problems. studying for prelims and final are difficult because of this.
he looks like jack from lost

Helpful; tries to help us learn the material and understand different applications of topics. Lectures are disorganized and somewhat uninteresting, but he manages to teach fairly well anyway. Grades fairly and makes exams so that they really test our knowledge instead of trying to trick us. Helps you do well in the class.
No Comments

duncan is probably one of the worst teachers i have had at cornell. during pchem i had the impression that he didnt like me.  from the other posts,i can see im not the only one.  he does not act like a teacher.  by this i mean if you annoy or upset him, he takes it very personally and singles you out (ie not offering help, offering it arrogantly)

Lectures are quite disorganized.  Writes all over the board so it's hard to take organized notes without rewriting them after.  His book was the most poorly written book I've ever read (I stopped reading it).  Arrogant and moody.  Best to avoid interaction.
Awesome class and actually a lot of fun, but yes, prepare to work for your grade. I loved his lectures and the text was one of the few that I actually read.
very hard class. Duncan was an alright teacher. Need to get on his good side to do well. He was a bit patronizing.

Overall a bad professor.  His course was well-organized and clear.  But as a person he is: Arrogant, Rude, and Insulting.  If you get on his bad side - watch out; he's going to make your life difficult.  I found the best course to take with him was to avoid him.  In summary he's a decent teacher, but is a vindictive and mean-spirited person.

Quite possibly my favorite professor so far.  He goes far out of of his way to get to know his students really well - he often knows things that you never thought he would care about.  Lectures sound like you're reading from his textbook, which is clear as well.  Knows everything he teaches front and back.
No Comments
Great teacher!  One of the best at Cornell.
I love Prof. Duncan. He was really helpful during office hours. His lectures were clear, and he really cares about his students progress. He is one in a million.
i <3 T.M.D

Excellent class, very organized and straightforward. Takes time to learn the material well and to do the homework, but it's worth it. I never found him to be unpleasant or rude, nor do I know anyone that's felt that way.
Course is ok. Duncun is not. He can be is a cocky rude mood frequently. But deal-able when he's in non-hostile mode.
Designs very difficult exams, but is a very clear and straightforward teacher, if a bit impersonal.

Duncan was awful. He graded harshly (esp final), expected a lot of work, and was clearly discriminating among students. If you get on his good side, you're lucky. If he hates you, your life in ChemE is gonna be hell. I tried talking to him once, and he's really cocky and rude. God bless Mr. Duncan.

Great professor. He expects you to do a lot of work, but if you're willing to make the effort he really cares about helping you succeed. It was a relief to have a professor who treated teaching an intro class as an important job.
really gud prof...one of the best...xtremely helpful...
Very organized and clear, good professor.
Duncan proves that when you respect your students and treat them like adults, they will respect you back and give their utmost effort.
Professor Duncan is truly inspiring and I've learned more from him in the last few months than I have from any other professors!
The chalk!  the chalk!
Awesome teacher, went out of his way to give students tools for sucess
Wonderful teacher, also teaches math 192
The T. Michael Duncan was the best professor I had in the four years I took classes at Cornell.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Most organized person in the World!
No Comments
If he can't teach you graphical analysis, your just helpless

While lectures were interesting when he talked about the new tariffs, he basically just read off the slides. Easy problem sets, but hard prelim multiple choice Qs. His grading was unclear (besides the median and the “top 45% get an A” you don't know anything). Definitely not “bad”, just gave less effort than other Econ profs and uninspiring.

I don't like macro but this class was much better than expected. He spent some time explaining the new tariffs, which was interesting. Tests can be hard so make sure that you understand the slides well.
His accent made it difficult for me to take away much from his lectures, which consisted of reading off of slides. Not a very hard class conceptually, but be sure to study a lot outside of class!

As long as you study and understand lectures you can pass. he's generous with grading problem sets and has a good amount of office hours to help with any questions. The only bad thing is he doesn't post lecture slides after or a recording, so you have to go to class.
Mediocre lecturer but has easy tests and psets. mainly just reads off the slides

Nice dude, class was kinda forgettable though. Definitely did his best to explain the material clearly, but it could sometimes come off dry. Certainly not a hard class if you just stay on top of things and attend section, and considering it's a core course for ECON that's probably all you can ask for.

Buy the optional textbook! His lectures go extremely fast and are packed with so much information, but there are no lecture recordings. The lecture slides were often unclear/confusingly worded, so I highly recommend purchasing the optional textbook and reading the chapter summaries which do an amazing job of simplifying concepts.

Took his Intermediate Macro class this semester and I'm glad I did. Even over Zoom, he gives good lectures and his passion for the material comes through quite well. Grading is based entirely on problem sets and exams. The problem sets are simple enough but be sure to prepare well for the exams as they will probably be harder than you expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very interesting class and Professor. Good class to take if interested in law school. Pick 4 homeworks out of 16, final project, and participation. Light grader.

Dufresne is such a genuine professor who truly cares. There were no exams, 4 homeworks, and a final project. The class can get a little repetitive and boring because there are no lecture slides, and it is just her talking. She does tend to call on the same group of people over and over again (who are usually students in her advocacy clinic.

Professor Dufresne is amazing!! In my opinion, she gives the best lectures. If you're considering law school as a career choice, I'd highly recommend taking one of her classes. Her classes are very participation heavy, so you get out of it what you put into it.

Professor Dufresne has the amazing ability to take complex and difficult subjects like immigration and make them not only enjoyable to learn about but easy to digest. She goes out of her way to make sure both students who have a law background and those who do not are able to get the information they need.

Loved taking Professor Yang's Labor Relations class. As long as you go to class and pay attention you will do well. She and the TA want you to succeed, and the grading is pretty fair. She's an inspiring prof and had some guest lecturers in class.
