She's very nice and wholesome, and the course content is digestible and easily understood. Attendance counts, but exams are straightforward and generally graded leniently. Duanyi is super genuine and nice and helpful.
I love her class. She's nice, and I'm a pretty bad student so, I'd say that's a good way to judge a prof

Prof Yang is wonderful and I would recommend her to any student looking to take Labor Relations. The Collective Bargaining Simulation is one of the most fun group activities I have ever participated in. The class is super manageable and you learn a whole lot. Great class, even better professor!

Yang is great! I am currently in her class for Labor Relations and thoroughly enjoy it. You can tell that she wants her students to succeed and is passionate about the course. Will happily answer any questions you have about the material too. Recommend taking Labor Relations with her!

I enjoyed Labor Relations, and she made lectures as engaging as possible with guest lectures and class discussions. She provides study guides for quizzes and sets clear expectations for class assignments and quizzes. She wants everyone to succeed; take her if you can!

I would definitely recommend taking labor relations with Professor Yang!  She cares about students and gives good lectures.  The class was very straightforward with reasonable expectations.  Participation is important but there are many ways to earn credit.  She also provides study guides for all exams.  The group projects are not too difficult.
Nice professor, no outside assignments besides the final and some prep for a project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Yang is one of the best choices you can pick for 2050. She's extremely caring and knowledgeable. The class was pretty easy. Lectures are usually just what was in the textbook. My only complaint was the class was at 8am.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Ghosh is a wonder of a human being who is so considerate in the way she leads class discussions. Even if you don't do the readings, you will be able to contribute in class. The grading system is extremely generous if you put any effort into your essays. It is hard to get less than a B- if you are present and do the assignments.
Unbelievable professor. Easily the best lecturer at Cornell. She is a humble genius who steers the conversation in such a way as to be unimposing but also critical

Really great history class that pushes you to think of the big picture rather than just regurgitating events. Readings were all extremely interesting. A bit of a tough grader on the essays but she values improvements and gives a grade based off performance not numbers. Great class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Gives complete control of grades to TA probably with instructions to grade tough because you usually do not have the right to question. Material is interesting, but you are encouraged to follow her view on the subject matters even though her class is mentioned as open to debate. Would not recommend taking it unless absolutely necessary.

TA grades the papers, very unfairly. Prof Ghosh is good but readings are boring and hard to digest. She gives the control to TA completely. Discouraged to challenge your grade in class. Grossly unfair
One of the best lecturers I've had. As an engineering student I usually don't enjoy humanities courses but Ghosh was different. I can't imagine what someone who actually likes humanities would think!

Probably my best professor at cornell.  Her lectures were very organized and helped to explain the readings.  She is very helpful and open to questions (no matter how basic).  She grades very fairly and gives good comments.  I highly recommend Hist275 (it also fulfills a LOT of the A&S requirements).
Really good professor. Engaging lectures, extremely helpful and nice. Fair grading and good workload. Lots of academic readings. Recommended

Class consisted of 2 5-page essays, a midterm examination, and a final examination. Both examinations were in-class and a choice of essay topics. Reading assignments were moderate and interesting. The class is excellently organized and Prof. Ghosh is very articulate and interesting.

She is brilliant and articulate.  She's friendly, although she can seem a little brusque and not that personable.  I'm learning a LOT in her class, although there is a lot of very difficult reading.  She cares about teaching and wants her students to be engaged.

Hard to contact him should you find yourself needing to, but his hockey class is so much fun. He's such a genuinely nice guy, and I actually looked forward to this even though it was early. He's reasonable and takes everyone where they're at (experience-wise). 100% should take this class, Dusty is awesome.
Great guy, way more understanding than he had to be, considering certain people in the class could not ice skate whatsoever. I got much better at ice skating, and had a very fun time.

Great guy, actually so funny and understanding (really put up with a lot from some students). All you really need to do is show up to class and skate. I did get better at ice hockey even if I'm still bad. Highly recommend!

He is great. He lets you pace yourself so the class is what you make of it, but he's also happy to help with advice or stretches. His attendance policy is very fair(usually just make-up) and he's an overall relaxed guy that knows his stuff.

He's really chill and nice. If you're late, he won't be mad as long as you jump in to participate. As long as you don't go over your max limit of skips, you're cool. He will answer any questions you have about working out and building muscle.

Awesome professor. Really taught me how to become a better hockey player. Taught the class how to make Hockey Stops, and just simple maneuvers to better facilitate your flow of the game. But, you have to know how to skate on ice. Although the class is an intro, but most of the students are already good at hockey.

Note: the course I took is actually HIST 2931- Making an Empire in China. 
Prof. Du is very knowledgeable, caring, and hard-working. Her lectures are information-dense but well-structured. No need to do all readings, but read papers. Go to her office hours and you'll get great book recommendations, advice on writing, and even life lessons.
Super caring professor, grade based on weekly reflections and research paper at the end. Every class is a seminar, so come to class prepared and youll be fine.

If you attend all lectures you get half a grade up. I like her passion (although her accent might be a bit difficult to understand at first). Read the syllabus carefully. It's ok to not do the weekly readings. She is very accessible outside class and it's willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Duffy is a true gem. It looks like a lot of work, but she's flexible and caring. She recognizes when her students are struggling with school and life in general. She's also a great lecturer and gives many opportunities to earn points through different things (essays, tests, discussions).

Turned really interesting topics into dry discussions over common sense. Both lectures and overall class schedule are very disorganized. Would avoid class like this if you don't want to waste your time and tuition.

BEST communication professor. She is so genuine and caring. Really values students' opinions of the materials and course. Her classes are very lecture-heavy and likes to throw in a few readings that she likes to discuss in class. She's very approachable! Easy course with basic syllabus structure - highly recommend all of her courses

Prof. Duffy is one of the most incredible professors at Cornell. She genuinely cares about her student, makes class expectations clear and rather reasonable. The pace of this class was a bit slow, also lectures were heavily summaries of assigned readings making them kind of redundant. But great prof and easy course.
Beers with Dwayne is such a fun class! He clearly loves teaching about beer and you can learn a lot if you pay attention during lecture.
One of my favorite professors ever
Exams (multiple choice and online) were a bit challenging but there is a lot of extra credit

He's really chill and makes the class fun. Don't buy the textbook, you'll literally never need it. There's just a couple of assignments besides the midterm and final, and he grades really easy, so it's a grade GPA booster.

Class is eh. Professor is passionate big whoop! 2 credits and you need to memorize 600 slides worth of content for each prelim, for 5 prelims + a comprehensive final. No structure to exams, they ask random obscure details. If you want a good grade, don't come to this class unless you have photographic memory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took BIOMI 3310. He's a great lecturer and really cares about his students, but the course takes a ton of studying for only 2 credits. Exams are 100% of your grade and require you to memorize an insane amount of detail from the lecture slides. He does give bonus points though. Only take this course if you are really passionate about the material.
Overall, really easy class but requires time to rote memorize. Go to class. Memorize slides cold. Get the extra credit points. Get an A+ and pat yourself on the back.

Probably the best professor I've had here. He goes through a lot of material but he makes it wildly interesting. Additionally, he really cares about his students doing well and he goes out of his way to help. Definitely the most interested, interesting, and caring professor I've seen.

Probably the best class I've taken here. Dr. Bowman is extremely interested in what he is teaching and in doing whatever he can to help his students do well. The material isn't easy, but it's wildly interesting and Dr. Bowman makes it fun. I definitely recommend giving this class a try.

Too much information on slides. Slides are poorly organized with no structure to them. Talks too quickly, glosses over topics such that lectures becomes confusing. Exams are difficult and require LOTS of memorization of detail. Final is comprehensive, ridiculous given how many parasites are covered.

Tests are very hard. Have to remember many species and specific details about life cycles, length, location. It is way too much information and detail to remember for each exam.  Too much details on slides, and need to memorize huge amounts of info. Can't cram for exams. Hard exams.

Not an easy class. He is unclear and extremely vague on his tests. Very specific and a too much info needed. Almost impossible to learn it all unless you take other easy classes (which I did not). Easy based on no work but the tests are horrible

Bowman is awesome and makes lecture really interesting and applicable.  I learned so much in this class and am super glad I took it.  Tests are very fair, even though the memorization is kind of a pain.  Study back tests and review guides on blackboard, no need to read the textbook, and you will be fine.

Dr. Bowman is an awesome professor.  He is clearly enthralled with what he teaches, and even makes class interesting with witty descriptions and side stories that pop up every lecture.  Very approachable and makes fair tests.  Study the lectures and review sheets!

Clearly fascinated by what he teaches.  Very approachable and interested in answering questions.  Tests are very fair if you study the lecture material.  Lots of extra credit.  Wants students to do well -he's a good guy.

I love Dr. Bowman!  I work in his lab, and he is the nicest prof ever.  Def come to his dinners b/c he tells the best stories, but bring a friend with you (for potential awkwardness reduction).  I made flashcards for each parasite which seemed to really help me do well on tests.
He has a very good sense of humor that makes even the subject of deadly parasites entertaining to learn.

Engaging and entertaining lecturer, interesting subject material, fair tests. The material would probably be useful for anyone planning to be involved with tropical medicine in any way, though since the best way to do well on the tests is to memorize everything, the amount of information you'll actually retain beyond the course is questionable.
mother ****ing ****....i hated his class so damn much...

Dr. Bowman was awesome!  His classes are fun and informative.  The style was very loose, and you learned a lot but it was easy to get a good grade thanks to extra credit etc.  Definitely recommend him.
No Comments
loved him! loved the class!
Dr. Bowman was one of my favorite professors during my time at Cornell. His lectures were enjoyable and he's a fun person to work with.
he's an awesome professor and very cool.

I love Dr.Bowman.  He's so cool and friendly and personal (but not in an invasive way).  You can contact him 24/7 and he'll answer your e-mails and messages really fast!  I came in 4th place in Zoology wiht him.
Dr. Bowman is a very fair and fun professor usually, though lectures were sometimes a little disorganized.  Heavy use of visuals made it interesting.  Lots of extra credit.

One of the worst classes and professors Ive ever had in my life. I honestly dont think he is In teaching to actually teach. The entire class was just pushing out as many assignment as possible. And then when I got something wrong, he would not teach and let me know why, he just said this is not correct, like gee thanks TEACHER

You have to be a fast note taker b/c tons of information on slides that are fine print. No electronics allowed in class! Be on time to every lecture! Try to ask specific or detailed questions as much as you can b/c vague ones don't get accurate answers. Go to office hours frequently to understand structure of assignments as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Better communication skills needed and less words on the lecture slides, so information won't feel overwhelming when trying to take notes in a 50 min class. This class is fairly confusing when it comes to completing assignments. Overall, this class needs better structure and order to provide a more effective learning environment for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Story time with Corey was one of my favorite experiences at Cornell -- definitely one to take in your senior year then go to Luna's Monday night trivia afterward. Really helped me develop an appreciation and gratitude for my alma mater.
amazing class! corey gives great lectures and multiple fun opportunities for extra credit, definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Literally the easiest A+ you could possibly get at Cornell. Honestly, I felt a little bad throughout the course because since it was so beyond easy, nobody took the course seriously. A few extra mandatory assignments could make the course better in my opinion to keep students engaged. Lectures and professor were great otherwise.

Was an amazing professor. Took this class to lighten up my science heavy semester and boy am I glad that I did. His lectures are interesting and engaging and he gives so much opportunity for extra credit. I highly recommend this class to anyone and everyone.
Fantastic instructor. Never knew there was so much behind the history of the University!

Class is difficult and six hours of lab a week is brutal, but far and away best Professor I've had at Cornell. Knows the entire curriculum by heart, great person with a good sense of humor, and extremely helpful. Lectures can be a bit boring, but office hours and lab are incredibly useful. The most useful class you can take for research.

Prof. Kirkland is quiet which can make staying awake hard but he's a great teacher with a good sense of humor. He's always around during labs and is friendly/non-judgemental if you need extra help. The labs for this class are tedious and grindy, though, so make sure you don't fall behind. Weekly homeworks are short.
Awesome course

Incredibly smart and kind professor. Always has a keen eye for making even the most difficult or confusing concepts understandable; he never treats any question as trivial and always takes time to give a complete answer

Prof. Flanagan taught the advanced undergrad quantum class. 4443 is a mathematically sophisticated and theoretical course. He's a caring professor and 4443 is awesome. He covers topics in graduate quantum including density matrix, tensor products, path integrals and more . Lectures are important because the content isn't encapsulated by one book.

Flanagan turned PHYS4443 into basically GradQuantum1, covering about 80% of Sakurai through his very fast paced and extremely mathematically sophisticated lectures combined with challenging problem sets. Extremely caring professor with a gargantuan brain. Amazingly insightful and interesting class, but be mentally prepared for a baptism by fire.

Flanagan did two classes worth of material, and I am glad that he did: I learned a lot. His arguments are mathematical, offering a different perspective at problems compared to the "physical intuition method". Homeworks were the focus of class (50% of grade); they were tough, but you take a lot out of them.

I didn't really attend a lot of the lectures (cause they were optional) but I thought I'd nevertheless leave a review for the class. The class content was extremely interesting and insightful. Just download the textbook "Networks, Crowds and Markets" and read through some parts. You'll know whether you wanna take this class.

Difficulty of this class made a 180 compared to last year. Practice problems before the two exams were useless as not even 1/3 of the problems made it onto the exam. If you're looking for easy liberal studies and have a rough workload definitely think again. You have to read the textbook and camp office hours, not what I expected for 3 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i cant believe people thought this course was easy. midterms/finals are so advanced compared to psets and practice exams it was like whiplash. every time i felt like i understood something it got flipped upside down the next chapter or on the exam. i was an office hours warrior and barely passed. genuinely saw someone cry during the final today too

Easley and Kleinberg are the original authors for the textbook and them teaching the class is ABSOLUTELY GOATED. It was extremely eye-opening to hear him share his past experiences and it is obvious that he is extremely intelligent. Also very very kind during office hours. Best class I've ever taken at Cornell -- made me change my way of thinking.
Superb class, extremely applicable, and grading was both fair and unbiased. Anybody saying otherwise has cope levels off the charts, probably because they need to reevaluate their IQ score
AMAZING AND SO CLEAR -- HE MADE THE CLASS CONTENT SO EASY TO UNDERSTAND AND INTERESTING!

Networks gets a bad rap, as I never found it to be that bad. Lectures were clear (sometimes boring), but textbook a great resource if still confused. People got mad at the weekly HWs and they are kinda annoying but I never found them to be too difficult. Easley does his best to make lecture interesting, but the class was a bit forgettable overall

Amazing class and professor! It was a super interesting class, but there is a lot of work. weekly hw assignments that take a few hours to complete, but if you take time and do them well, the tests are easy and straight forward just like the hw.
The lectures are fantastic. The class is not easy but worth taking.

Dr. Easley makes PhD microeconomics clear and easy to understand. He knows the material inside and out and knows how to present it to the class. He is just as helpful outside of class, and is incredibly helpful in office hours. The class wasn't easy, but it was all fair.

Class: Networks. Very organized class. Most people wouldn't show up. It was pretty easy overall. Professor Easley did a great job at getting the content across. The average final grade was an A I think.
He's good at explaining hard to understand concepts in an easy-to-understand manner. Silky, butter-like, rich voice. He would have been a great sports commentator.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Networks is an easy class. Maybe it was made easy by Easley and Kleinberg's ability to teach, but truthfully I don't think teaching this material would be challenging for anyone. I would love to see what Easley could do in an intense economics course. He seems very smart and very personable.
Very good
Great lecturer and taught mostly from the textbook. The textbook is legally free to download digitally; print copies are $40.
Easley is easily one of the best profs I've had. Really nice guy and very happy to discuss material in office hours.
I prefer Kleinberg but Easley comes really close. Both great lecturers.
great + dedicated

Excellent class, highly recommended! Slow and steady coverage of material, easy, especially if you have prior experience in game theory (I did). Very good explanations of material. Better handwriting than Kleinberg. Easy tests and homework. Free electronic textbook is not necessary unless you don't understand the notes or want to go deeper.
Easley lectures to us as if we're two year olds. Networks is  boring but ridiculously easy. Class is optional because he recites what is in the textbook, verbatim.

there is not much work to do. the test is not very hard, but the grading system is kind of harsh. last year this class was a median A class, but this year I DONT THINK SO.i have pretty good GPA and i got the lowest grade on this class. the material is interesting though. if you are taking this class for GPA booster, think about it again

econ 204 / cs 285 Networks - great class, easy , interesting, little work and little reading to do . easley lectures very clearly, almost painstakingly slow over some material --- not hard to get an A.

This prof is pretty cool but his class is deceptive. It might seem easy at first but things just come like a torrent of information. Stay on top of your material you are almost guaranteed an B+/A-. His lectures are pretty interesting.

Easley is a very capable professor and definitely knows what he's talking about. His lectures were good, although I still slept through/missed a lot. But that's just me. Homeworks are doable and graded easily. Prelims are almost exactly like the example ones he gives you from the previous year.

easley is an amazing prof, one of the best at cornell.  he takes a drab subject and makes it approachable and bearable. the problem sets are hard but they are graded easily, and while the exams are tough, easley's teaching makes up for it.  i highly recommend this class.

Easley is an awesome professor. Period. He is fair. He grades without a curve so the smartasses don't hurt your grade. He tells you exactly how hard the class will be from the start. He has realistic expectations. Lecture is mandatory, but never boring. He's good at giving an intuition for econ.

Great lecturer.. you must attend class. Makes material much easier than it has to be. Willing to work with you, but is very busy (understandable with a 150 person class). Don't take Microecon with anyone other than him.

Easley is an excellent professor. His lectures are very clear and organized, and he uses interesting examples to supplement the sometimes dry material. Exams and problem sets are challening (somewhat) but you get used to it. Almost no understanding of calc is needed, he teaches it all.

This was my first econ class, and I can't praise Easley enough! He had great lectures and was always clear, organized, thoughtful, and provided many examples.  His weekly problem sets were very do-able, although it takes a little getting used to.  Same goes for the exams.  One of the best.

Teaches very well. Comes up with creative examples, and makes the dry material a bit better. As much as this is econ for engineers and calculus is expected, you barely need to understand a derivative.
Extremely helpful and clear, engaging, great professor. Very recommended.
Tough but fair, great instructor (for econ!)
Smooth lectures and fair exams.  A rarity for Cornell!!
great teacher.  great course
I admit that the course is well taught, but I suppose I just don't get economics.  Be aware that this course is DESIGNED FOR ENGINEERS!!!!
The class is deceptive. Everyone seemed to get a lower grade than their grades warranted. Only take the class if you have to, because it kinda blows.
Easley is a very good lecturer, using good examples and always making the material as interesting as it possibly can be. This is way better to take than ECON 313.  Plus, the TA's grade pretty easy.
Very dry. Methodical. Robotic, even.
He makes a difficult, boring subject somewhat easier to handle. The examples are well thought out and makes a topic simpler to grasp.
Seems like a nice guy.  The 75 minute lecture is a little long and gets boring towards the end.  However, he manages to come up with interesing/amusing examples to keep our attention.
clear and precise, great lecture.
Great Chest man!
Gotta love that open shirt!

I LOVED THIS CLASS!!! Made me really excited about Civil Engineering. The class was easy and interesting. Earls is really passionate about the material. Very helpful in office hours. No textbook, a few short homeworks, 1 paper, and a group project in the place of a final. The project was fun and a great way to apply the material. My favorite class.

Lectures were pretty interesting compared to some other classes, but lasted a long time. The homeworks are easy if you go to office hours. I loved this class because the final project was so much fun, and there's no final.

The professor is AMAZING!!There is no textbook so pay attention to the lecture. However, the lecture is so long(over an hour) and there is no light because of the ppt, so you can fall asleep easily even though the lecture is interesting. There're no tests, only easy homework with only 2 or 3 short questions, include one group project and one paper.

Made the class fun and applicable. While he didn't teach too much into the specifics of statics, mechanics, etc, the holistic approach was beneficial to the freshman class of engineers. The final project was superb and everyone had a good time with it

Prof Earls did a good job with steel design. Lectures were very clear and well organized. Earls was always willing to help students. Homeworks really taught me about steel design. Tests were similar to homeworks, not too difficult. I recommend this course for a CEE design requirement. PS he's hot!

Professor Earls did a good job with steel design. His lectures were put together very well and he was always willing to help students. Not too hard, not really easy either. I would recommend this course.
Professor Earls did a good job teaching Steel. I would recommmend this class.
Very kind and helpful professor, happy to meet outside of class, but very easy to understand in class.

FWS: Guts, Ghosts, & Glory was a pretty good writing seminar to take.  We had one or two less essays than most others.  Professor Eaton has her positives and negatives.  While she can provide good feedback and isn't a harsh grader, she tends to think that she's the only one that's right and that writing should only be in her particular style.
No Comments
Great guy
Amazing professor - very useful course due to its relevance to real world necessities.

Wow, Brian was probably the best professor I have ever had at Cornell. He is smart, funny, caring, and basically I could go on and on. The class is not that difficult, just make sure you read the book before the two tests, other than that, enjoy yourself and the lectures! Speeches are a breeze as well. Great job Brian, we love you!
Brian saved my bacon during my years at CU. A great teacher and better advisor and excellent friend. Far too few Brian Earless in higher ed. Highly recommended!
Prof. Earle genuinely cares about his students and his class was the most useful for post-college life!  He's wonderful!
Prof. Earle is awesome. He's funny and understanding, and you'll learn a lot in this class. A must-take before entering the business world! Per his request, I have labeled him as smokin' hot. Yowza!
Brian's the man

I was unexcited about the class at first, but it actually was very useful/valuable. A must for CALS Freshmen, taught by one of the most quality people I've ever met. He was always amazingly understanding, never giving up until he helped students to the best of his ability.

I just thought that this would be a continuation of COMM 201, but it's so much better than that.  His class is about REAL-WORLD stuff that I will never forget (i.e.: interviewing skills)  Really useful class and you enjoy talking to him just try not to mention that you like the Yankees.
the best prof i've ever had.

I was very unenthusiastic about the class at first, but it actually helped me develop study skills and learn a lot about Cornell's history. Very easy A to offset first semester Bio and Chem. Highly recommended.
Prof. Earle cares about his students and he obviously wants them to be able to take the skills and knowledge he imparts on life-long journeys.  He's a darling!
One of the best in the business. Most applicable course to the real world that Cornell offers.
I graduated in 1995, and even back then, Prof. Earle was one of the best at Cornell.  Take his class, it's easy and you'll learn a lot!!!

Not only a great teacher, but also important in the department. He's a large part of the reason I was able to transfer in, and he even eventually became my advisor. When I think about great teachers at Cornell, Brian is one of the first to come to mind.
Very reasonable guy, funny too.
unhelpful oldie
Everybody should take this class... He is very easy and will give you an A no matter what you do. Easy guy to ass kiss to get a good grade
No Comments
No Comments

Fantastic prof. Class can benefit anyone in any field where talking to groups or giving presentations is important. You even learn how to handle business dinners and lunches. Prof goes out of his way to help you if you show effort. A great asset to the Un
Great guy, interesting course.
Pretty easy class... funny guy

Readings were incredibly dense and lengthy. Lectures were genuinely unrelated to the readings. Baptist advertised his own merchandise and book repeatedly. Grading varied wildly across TAs. Grossly incompetent lecturer.

Worst class I've taken at Cornell. Horrible lectures. Boring, disorganized, filled with irrelevant information. Readings were lengthy but interesting. Tests are basically unrelated to much of the readings and lecture. Terrible class

Insane amounts of reading material. No consistency in lectures, and just when it seems he starts talking about something actually important to the core of the class he tangents off on something again losing the attention of his students. He seems like a nice guy who is passionate about what he does, but he is not meant to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Baptist came up with very interesting essay prompts that were virtually all of your grade. It was quite manageable if you paced yourself. Lots of readings but interesting, if you can't do them all it's not a big deal. I got better grades on essays than I expected- don't be afraid to ask him beforehand with questions, he's very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Baptist is very knowledgeable and kind to his students. Would definitely recommend, however be prepared for tough grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mean guy. Horrible lecturer that will put you to sleep every time. very unreasonable and gives off bad vibes. lecture is all over the place and class has no structure. Not too hard depending on your TA

Mean guy. Unreasonable. Probably unhappy with his life -- I've heard stories about him only justified by extreme unhappiness with his own life. After taking his class, he changed my entire perception of academia and confirmed the suspicion "those who cannot do, teach." Fears face-to-face confrontations.

Baptist is a nice guy and knows a ton but only an OK lecturer. Kind of rambles on and gets off topic easily. Lectures have nothing to do with what the tests are on. Assigned readings are very specific and pretty interesting. Discussion sections were pretty boring. Class was not as interesting as I thought it would be.

Prof. Baptist's Obama and Lincoln course was extremely informative. Some called the course premature but it was probably one of the best courses I've taken at Cornell. Baptist is very helpful during office hours and deeply cares about his students' opinions. Yes, he is a stickler for clear writing but what professor isn't? I highly recommend him!
A bit dry in lecture, but extremely knowledgeable about the subject. Chooses great books. As aren't impossible if you write clearly and ALWAYS check your work for errors.

Seminars w/ Baptist are a good way to get your AMSt diversity/pre-1900 requirements out of the way. Minimal work and Baptist is very knowledgable, passionate about the subject. A little dry, but there are much more boring professors here.

Great professor who is passionate about what he teaches.  Very hard to get A's on his essays...is a stickler for grammer and syntax...make sure to proofread your essays several times over before handing them in.  Good thing is you will be a better writer after taking his class...very nice and helpful too

nice man, but impossible and rather unreasonable grader.  also, in seminar, he can be disrespectful of students, ignoring they're input or in the least shooting them down as though they had no valid point.

Baptist is a fantastic professor.  Very personable and intellectually challenging at the same time. Thought-provoking seminar with interesting readings and discussion.  If you are interested in American history, you should definitely take one of his classes!

He is a great guy and truly loves to teach. Wants you to learn. However, at least in this class, it's really hard to get an A on a paper. He really pushes you to improve your writing. (btw, he's a stickler for grammer and syntax)
Prof Baptist is amazing...even if he tells me to drink more caffeine before class ;)

Baptist is the man. He took the time to review with me all of the essays I wrote for his class. Very intelligent, a great lecturer, and is passionate about both his courses and his students. Highly recommend.

Baptist is very helpful and a great lecturer, knows his material well and makes class interesting, a very fair grader who will go back and take a second look at your work if you ask and reconsider your grade...a great prof

Prof. Baptist is one of the best lecturers I've had, and the material he covers is very interesting. Also, the reading and writing requirements for the course weren't too demanding, and the grading was more than fair.
Prof Baptist is a terrific lecturer!
great teacher

He is a fantastic and interesting lecturer, but his tests present a problem as they often test irrelevant and minute details.  However, it's a fairly easy A if you are willing to pay attention in lectures and read the book thoroughly.  Median grade is like a B.

professor was completley inaccesible and unhelpful. In response to a question regarding the final exam he replied in an email "see class notes where this was discussed four weeks in a row" He could easily have answered my question. Tests are not too difficult but they dont test your knowledge of the subject. Steer clear if its not required
Test should reinforce what is learned - not to see if you can READ THE PROFESSORS MIND! Terrible professor.

STUDY FOR THE EXAMS.  I completely underestimated the difficulty of the prelims, but thankfully he let us drop a prelim so I still did really well (after some serious studying). Read the textbook, take really good notes, and pay attention to guest lectures and you'll do well.  Lectures are fun (movie clips and ads), but the book is boring as hell

This class is a MUST TAKE if u are interested in taking a business course at CU. The lectures are not only clear and easy-to-digest,they are also VERY FUN and INTERESTING!Yes,the exams are DIFFICULT as they require minute details from the textbook+lectures+guest lectures but if u take time to read the text book and attend lectures,all will be fine!

Ed McL is one of the few professors at Cornell who is active in research and talented at teaching.  His tests are tricky and require you to know the material cold, but if you focus in class, read the book, and do the extra credit, you're golden.  Lectures presented lots of information but were fun, thanks to inclusion of funny ads and movie scenes.

McLaughlin is a good guy. He really does make Marketing interesting and fun. The classes are based 50% on lecture and 50% on the text so you have to make sure you read. People only complain that there is a disconnect between his lectures and his tests because they are too lazy to go and actually read the required sections. Recommended Class!

Awful class... If his tests reflected his teaching method, it would be great.  But there's a huge disconnect between the two.  His lectures are easy & fun and span broad topics while his tests focus on details that often have NOTHING to do with the subject matter.  If you can avoid taking this class, do it.
This class sucks.  He teaches a very easy subject that only requires common sense, yet somehow his tests are impossible, requiring minute details.  This class is a waste of time

His lectures are decent and he does explain things in a easy-to-digest fashion. The tests, however, may be unexpected difficult and require you to recall tiny bits of useless information from text/guest lectures. If you want the bonus credits, make your response as cheesy as possible. Just imagine you are trying to entertain your grandfather.

This class is not an easy A. Maybe I was just too lazy but I didn't end up doing very well. You definitely need to do the readings for the tests, and really know them well.  Lecture was fun some times, esp. when he dressed up in a Campbell's soup costume.

Great , lively professor with awesome lectures. Only class where I actually wanted to go to class. :) I really enjoyed the guest speakers, the marketing derby, and the movie clips in class. :)  The exams are a little difficult though, so watch out for that...
Useless class, so-so professor, but very easy.

A good class if you're interested in marketing. Not too much work, just read the textbook and take good notes. Tricky exams but do the extra credits and especially the marketing derby if you want an A. McLaughlin a pretty nice guy, but be careful not to get on his bad side! I've seen this guy pissed off, and lets just say it's not pretty.

Prof. McLaughlin was not very helpful in general, not very insightful, and quite frankly I question his aptitude and the fact that he runs the AEM program. The class was not too hard, sure the prelims were tricky, but with all the extra credit ANYONE should be able to get an A. Read the book, especially the extra articles in the chapters.
my fav class
Take this class! One of the better AEM classes - fun and interesting. The prelims are very tricky, but they're curved up. Very little work.
Very interesting material and an amazing lecturer. But the tests, which make up 90% of your grade are very keen to details. They were much harder than I expected.
Wow...who knew marketing could be so hard.  The degree of difficulty of the lectures does not equal the difficulty of the exams.  Nice guy, but there is soo much to know for tests.
ed mclaughlin is my hero.  he knows his marketing, especially about the food industry.  a brilliant guy who should write more books.

Pretty easy, fun class. If you do the reading and study, and extra credit, you should end up in the A range. No outisde work other than studying for 3 prelims (don't have to take the final if you do well on them).

Interesting subject and pleasant professor but the tests are horrible. He tests on the most insignifacnt details instead of important concepts, discouraging actual learning in lieu of factual memorization. Be sure to go to class and, read several times, and pay attention at guest lectures.

One of the best classes I've ever taken. Great prof - interesting lectures, gotta love the movie clips and ads during lecture. Prelims are much easier than in past years. If you do extra credit and study for prelims, you should get in the A range.
Great guy, great class ... How funny was it when he fell off the stage? I loved it.
Really great lectures.  Tests are difficult, but overall the class is highly recommended.

Be sure to attend all his classes, he might cover some meterials outside the textbook.  Prior to Fall 2004, there are 3 out of 4 essay topic on each prilim.  At Fall 2004, only 1 out of 2 essay topic for each prelim. Pay more attention to the topic that he emphasizes in class repeatedly.
Interesting class, not a lot of work, but prelims are quite hard. Still, a good class that's worth taking

He's a great teacher! I loved the in-class commercials and guest lectures of very prominent business Cornell alum/people. Tests are hard, prepare for them! Out of the 4 exams you take, the lowest one gets dropped. AWESOME! Good amount of EC offered
Interesting lectures, but the prelims are a ****. He tests on the smallest most insignificant details in the text and lectures. If you don't read the text, the highest grade you will get is a C.
Very enjoyable class, but HARD tests.
the class is interesting, and the lectures are engaging, but the tests are horrendously hard. nothing you do will prepare you sufficiently for his nitpicky details....
very interesting class...nice guy, very interested in marketing...tough prelims though...I would reccommend the class

the pro of a good lecture does NOT outweigh the con of good grades..def NOT recommend this class for anyone wanting to do well in a course. appears to be a nice guy but NOT. "easy" lectures, hard prelims, and whats w/ completely random attendenc

great teacher, relaxing lecture class, but be sure to read, because many prelim questions are details in the text and prelims are somewhat difficult...i love how he uncorporates videos in his presentation, brings class to life=)
Nice professor, enjoyable class- many clips, guest speakers, class slides online, generally a fun and relaxing class.  Though, make sure you attend classes...
Not a bad teacher, but definitely an ass. He is the kind to punish you for skipping his class before a break. His tests are completely evil.
THE GOAT SWARTZ, I LOVE HIS MOANS

Very good professor who made content very interesting. Class got somewhat difficult after the 1st exam, but it is still a very good class to take if you are interested in higher-level math. Professor really pushes you to think about the concepts more deeply as opposed to simply applying algorithms to solve questions.
Swartz is a strong lecturer. He teaches math the right way. Would take a Math class taught by him any day of the week.
Ed Swartz is the best professor I have ever had. He was a very good lecturer, the lectures were challenging and thoughtful, although a bit scattered, they were always very engaging and interesting.

Swartz is a good professor in general. The class itself is quite easy; to do well in the class, all you have to do is read a couple textbook sections/do the homework once a week, and you can skip the lectures completely. The lectures themselves are a bit dry. The TA's for this class were fantastic - all knowledgeable grad students.
Great Proffesor!

The workload of this class is light. Prof. Swartz is rude and does not seem to care a for his students. His lectures followed a linear though process, but the writing on the board was small and disorganized. It seems, though, that he is one of the professors that I least interacted with since I would learn more the textbook than from his lectures.

Tests are 80% of grade (each prelim is 25%, final is 30%). Brilliant, funny guy, but writes small/messy on the board and talks quietly, so sometimes difficult to follow. Pretty boring too, hard to focus after 40 min. Exams are pretty difficult but doable with office hours and hw. TA's are really good and know what they're talking about.
Good professor with clear lectures and helpful Office Hours. If you didn't understand a concept he would always explain it multiple ways until you got it. I found his psets difficult though
An extremely knowledgeable and respected professor

a really incredible person. the tests are very fair and he is always willing to meet with any student. a truly good person to meet at cornell and a person guided by values and compassion for his students. take this class.

Amazing professor who really understands and knows the field. He is very passionate about the subject. Only graded by two exams and a analytical group research paper (usually combining economics and statistics). Read his book-its very helpful and the past exams are usually what he asks on the test.

Professor Ehrenberg was the best professor I have had at Cornell. I am so thankful that I took his class and wish I could take it again before I graduate! He is generally an amazing professor and I recommend that all students have the opportunity to take his class before graduating. He genuinely cares about his students. You're the best RGE!

RGE is a professor you won't appreciate until the very last day of classes. But he truly is an inspiration, a renown economist, and you will learn a ton from his class. He's also very fair - take his paper seriously, use the practice midterm/finals to study from, read Tuition Rising, pay attention in lecture and you'll be fine. He's genuinely nice.
Extremely caring and helpful. Really makes you think about controversial issues and encourages you to form your own opinion. Ehrenberg is the best!
willing to work with students who care

Wonderful professor. Clearly not trying to overburden students with work or destroy any GPAs, just wants us to understand the complexity of university decision making. Attend lecture, pay attention, read Tuition Rising, practice with last years' tests, and go see him in office hours.
Very interesting professor and class. I disagree with commenter who said he is full of himself; while he does boast it is very tongue in cheek.

Ehrenberg is awesome. You have to go well out of your way, more so than with other profs, to get him to notice you... but if you do it's well worth it. He's opinionated, and it's awesome, especially since ILR seems to only hire bleak, boring people who have nothing worth saying anymore. Ehrenberg is the best thing to happen to ILR
Good Class!
I dont know too much about the content, and that stuff... but two words...Stud Muffin.  Every day in this class was like a vacation of my senses.
Good class.

He's a great professor and lectures are very interesting. This class is perfect for economics students who want to listen to fun stories and write essays instead of solving math problems. Attendance is not mandatory, but you won't be bored if you go. Make sure you understand the practice prelim and you'll be fine for the real exam!

Great class. Great professor. He's so funny and amusing. Subject matter is definitely interesting, too. For the economics major, it is definitely a class to be taken if you want a break from all the math and tough grading.
Very interesting guy, good at telling stories, funny and nice but kind of full of himself (in an endearing way though...).  Good class.
No Comments

i had a great time and learned a lot. a very lighthearted but in-depth approach. was nervous about taking a course based on the prof's own book (those can be bad, when the prof just basically reads verbatim -- why go to class!??), but this was well worth it. had a good time with my end-of-term project too.
Very nice and helpful. Exams are a joke and he's very very easygoing. take 240 with him for an easy time

Ehrenberg cares SO MUCH about his students.  He is a very personable, endearing professor who has a passion for what he teaches.  His Econ of the University class is very interesting, great class, and good if you don't want too much work.
No Comments
really interesting, great and easy class (good excuse for a 300-level econ).
coolest prof at cornell... without a doubt
I have never met a man this intelligent or this skilled in his teaching abilities.  A few more like him and this university would be top five.
No Comments
No Comments
Simply politically incorrect, annoying in his comments to the last. Very clever but he jumps to conclussions very fast. Impatient and unclear. Self-centered, has personal and prejudice bias.
GET ME OUT OF HERE! is what I'm thinking everytime I'm in this class and he asks a question that no one cares about to the guest lecturer.
Actuallt cares about students, makes entertaining comments
No Comments
loud and ignant...his constant chiming in the middle of class is very annoying

This guy is a living legend.  He has over 500 published papers, and has been the pioneer for the field of chemical ecology.  His story-telling is fantastic, and all of the stuff he talks about is just so interesting.  One of my favorite professors that I have ever had, I stand in awe of his accomplishments as a researcher and a teacher.

FANTASTIC! Incredible storyteller, beautiful speaker; brought a sense of wonder, excitement, and commitment to nature to every lecture. Also, he's hilarious! I really loved this class and encourage everyone to take it; no grades, just for its own sake. you will relax, learn a lot, and enjoy.
There's a facebook group called "Tom Eisner Fan Club" because he is teh awesome.  His lectures were entertaining and informative.  And my chem HW this week used some of his research!
An amazing array of visiting and local speakers - whether you consider youself a naturalist or not, take this class.
An amazing class. He brought in a ton of great guest lecturers, but I thought his lectures were the best. He is so cool and a great biologist, but he talks very quietly.

SO OLD AND SO GOOD. Sometimes hard to understand because he moves around a lot and speaks softly, but if you pay attention to what he says, your mind will be blown. One of the most fascinating lecturers with the best slides. Funny, too.

Every undergrad's dream biology professor. I saw someone wearing a handmade "I Want to Be Tom Eisner" t-shirt around campus. That's how cool he is. There's like five different professors who teach this course and he's definitely the highlight.
Simply Amazing Professor.  One of the Best at Cornell, a man every undergrad should meet.

I heart Tom Eisner.  Catch him while you can.  (He's really old.) I took this class the first semester it was offered and there was no work, just a guaranteed S.  It's like getting credit for watching the discovery channel or national geographic.
Eisner is the greatest! He's so hillarious and cute and engaging-- I highly recommend taking his course!
Amazing prof. funniest and most interesting lecturer I've had here at Cornell.
this guy has a lot of interesting stories to tell.  have a conversation with him if you can.
grandpa!!! hes awesome. bugs blowing stuff out their butts at other bugs!
This guy is brilliant and he's a great teacher.  Very funny during lecture
No Comments

To be fair, I was really excited for this class before I took it. You just talk about paradoxes the entire course. It's great. Just show up to lecture, minimal readings that are basically optional. Very helpful lecture notes distributed in class. Class makes you think. Explains things clearly and thoroughly. Grading was kind of tough though.

Grades hard, provides lecture notes but has no talent in teaching, other than reading off the notes. Awkward silence for 75 minutes is the essence of the class. SO many students opt to not show up even if attendance matters bc of that. His thick accent and obvious rambling in English is often hard to listen to...

Prof. Eklund is a nice guy, and pretty knowledgeable, but the class wasn't that great or interesting.  However, he has a great Swiss (I believe) accent.  And he is very approachable.  I don't recommend the class though.  The grading really depends on the TA.

The course turned out to be easy for me, but I can see where it could cause trouble for some people. Best avoid this one if you aren't comfortable with math and philosophy. Course reading was relatively unimportant, lectures were everything. Tests were pretty easy, I got a 100 on a prelim. Oh, and Eklund is great--smart, nice, and approachable.

Her class was an absolute breeze work wise, and the content (I took No Spoilers!) was interesting. The workload never exceeds a fairly sized essay and she is genuinely one of the kindest people on earth. She's extremely lenient/understanding which was really helpful during tough times, & cares about her students. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER SHES AMAZING

Dr. Foster was excellent, and I would highly recommend taking any of her classes. All classwork and reading is super manageable and interesting. I feel as though my writing genuinely improved throughout the FWS. She gives great, specific feedback on all writing.

Great Prof for my FWS; super kind and understanding of people's other responsibilities outside of his class. Her feedback is really helpful, and the classwork is very light. Overall, great prof, and would definitely take her class again!

ENGL 3747 was a breath of fresh air! Grade is based on participation (attendance and speaking), 3 short book reports, mid-term, final essay, and a presentation. The assignments were manageable, fun, and included many options for us to choose from. Foster was charming and engaging, making the plethora of readings worthwhile! A must-take at Cornell.

Took ENGL3747. Dr. Foster is hands down the best professor at Cornell. This was my favorite class! It is not burdensome at all, but there is a lot of reading (super fun though) so don't fall behind. The class is pretty discussion heavy and you're technically graded on it. Highly recommend to anyone remotely interested in crime fiction in any form.
One of the most kind and caring profs at Cornell and very knowledgable too. Crime fiction class is insightful and gives you a lot of flexibility. Recommend to anyone.

One of the nicest professors. She taught the FWS Rom Coms course. She works with you to set up flexible deadlines around other exams and makes reading and analyzing Shakespeare fun. Just apply yourself and put real thought into your papers and you'll be fine. Only 3 complete papers and some other minor things. She also gives amazing feedback.

Professor Foster makes class really enjoyable and interesting. She gives great feedback and helped me take my research paper ideas to the next level. I would take any class with her regardless of the subject honestly.

She taught my FWS on Shakespeare and Rom Coms. She was engaging and the class was discussion based. We had really interesting conversation and she was great at encouraging ideas. Only homework was to read Shakespeare, write, and watch the occasional film. Fair grading with helpful feedback. She connects well with students. This was a great class!

This course was super fun and enjoyable. I loved how Professor Foster focused on content that was interesting to us. Professor foster brought a lot of energy to class, graded in a timely manner (a couple days), and made herself available with office hours and one-on-one meeting.

Em provided helpful and encouraging feedback on my essays and was always reachable outside of class. Attending office hours helped me grow a lot as a writer, and lectures were always engaging. Such an amazing and enjoyable FWS!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best FWS class ever. Clear grading, amazing feedback and fun classes.

GREAT FWS!!!!!!! Class material and essays (3) we had to do were engaging. All essays had good feedback provided. Very kind extention, revision, and attendence policies. Enjoyed going to this class and learning. 100% reccomend to anyone wanting to take an interesting FWS and grow as a writer without an overbearing workload.

Em's class was super engaging, and also allowed me to grow as a writer. There was only 3 essays to be written the whole semester and Em would give you detailed feedback on each one. Along with that, you were allowed to do essay revisions to get a higher grade. There were also lots of extra credit opportunities! Take fws with her!!
EM THE GOAT. Peak FWS, take it with them if you can.

Really great professor. Her lectures were engaging and she was very accessibly outside of class. It's clear that she cares for her students and as long as you study and complete the practice questions, you'll do well in the class.

she does not have a clear teaching style and lecture is very boring and unorganized. the homework is nothing like the exams. if you can avoid. she is very nice however the class could be improved significantly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
First time teaching the class and it showed 

Not competent, many mistakes were pointed in her lecture material multiple times in lecture/office hours 

Wrote an exam that averaged 61% in a class where historical averages were ~80%, blamed her students

Dramatic discrepancies in prelim grading, >30% of class received prelim regrades

Avoid.
Make sure to go to class and pay attention to the lecture. The class is manageable as long as you put in effort.

Dr. Teitelman is a great professor! She genuinely wants to see her students do well. Not a very demanding teacher, and if you go to her office hours, she will tell you exactly what she wants to see from you. Would 10000% take again
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't really have a strong opinion on her. She is a nice enough lady who cares about history. I think it was her first time teaching it because she gave take home essay, in class essay, quiz, and test. Grading was not very clear and half the class never showed up. She also does have favoritism towards girls. Overall, nice lady not bad, not best.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor is very helpful in office hours, is passionate about the subject she teaches, and provides good feedback. Get ready to read though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor was kind, passionate & grading criteria was clear. The course was discussion-based & work-heavy. The reading workload frequently exceeded the Knight Institute's 75-page guideline. Writing instruction was nonexistant, and earning an A required completing 8 additional essays. Take only if you are truly passionate or else it will be boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: 10/10 professor, cares deeply about the content despite it being an fws, really cares about her students, makes time to give extra feedback on essays, would definitely take again

Far and away the best professor I have ever had. There is no comparison to make. Professor Mora is inspirational, knowledgeable, eloquent, and extremely caring and passionate about his field and his students. There is nothing more to say; he is the best there is.
The best professor I've ever met. Interesting lecture and engaging class.
I love Prof. Mora. The kindest and most enthusiastic professor I've ever had. The course is super engaging and not perplexing at all. He even has a YouTube account, go watch it!
Very enthusiastic about the content he teaches. Do the extra credit for an easy A+

Highly recommend this class!! Prof Mora is extremely engaging, passionate, caring, and knowledgeable. Probably the best professor I've ever had! The class included weekly quizzes and three assignments (a group project, a paper, and a solo assignment). I genuinely enjoyed this class and learned so much!

Prof. Mora is AMAZING. He's always responsive to any questions raised by students. The course organization is excellent, is easy to follow, and helps to learn a lot. I am grateful to meet a teacher like him in my life.

What an amazing prof! Prof Mora has done some amazing research and taught all around the world. BEN is not an easy subject for me, but Prof Mora ensured I could understand the material. The extra credit helps you prepare for the prelims/quizzes. Prof is a guest lecturer, but I STRONGLY recommend his class!

Learning any new language is difficult and I think Emi does as well as any other professor would. The course itself is just content heavy. Nothing too easy or too extremely difficult, grammar is learning on your own so prepare for that, but she will help with vocab in class.

I enjoyed this class as it gave me more experiences with Spanish and especially using it in global and real-world contexts. Prof. Mahiques was great and conducted the class well. There was no cold calling in the class as well and allowed people to participate when they wanted to. She also was understanding, considerate, and responsive to emails.

Overall the semester wasn't too bad but she gave 5 cumulative assessments that she marked as not counting for much but we didn't have many other grades. The final paper was ridiculous. The instructions were extremely unclear she didn't tell us the due date until a week before it was due.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was an absolute disaster: incomprehensible notes, confusing homework, terrible teaching, struggling students, ridiculously hard tests, absurd participation, etc... Google became a better resource than her, 100%. It was an exhausting, disappointing, and frustrating experience that left everyone running out of her class. Fire her!

I had a great experience with Emi. Everyone in the class loved her as well. She genuinely wants us to succeed and become better language speakers, even if that means cold calling and pushing us to our limits to improve our language understanding, it pays off! Take her class if you want to learn Spanish.

Arguably one of the worst professors I have ever had at Cornell. She was discriminatory against students with learning disabilities and had near impossible expectations. Instead of supporting her students through feedback, she looks for ways to take off points. She does not care about teaching or her students well-being. Take another professor.

While the SPAN 1230 course curriculum mandates a lot of work, (very rare to not have homework or reading before class, usually both) Emi didn't make it any easier. On open ended grading assignments, she made it impossible to score well, and with an increase in my effort throughout the sem, my results stayed the same. Try to take w/ another prof.

Her class is so hard and I think her expectations are way too high and she is a mean grader. I think you should try to get on her good side and you need to study a lot because she does not explain grammar.
Very unfair grader at an intermediate level. She definitely chooses her favorites in her courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She expects perfection in class for intermediate to below non-native Spanish speakers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Emilia for SPAN 1230 and I thought she explained grammar well and was clear on grading. Her english wasn't the best, so it was difficult when she tried to explain things in english, but I think my Spanish definitely improved! The class is very textbook heavy which is frustrating since it was expensive though

FREN 1210*. Prof. Epperson is very effective at teaching a foreign language and I feel like I learned a lot in one semester. She is caring, accessible, and gives good feedback. Assignments are very manageable. Quizzes are easy as long as you actively participate/complete homework and do a little review.
Good teacher
Great teacher, kind and helpful

Professor Epperson is a fantastic teacher who really understands how to teach a foreign language to students so that they really understand the concepts. Took both 1210 and 1220 with her and the classes are not particularly hard but they are a lot of fun. Oral exams, short writing prompts and quizzes but that can be expected for any language class.

One of the best professors at Cornell! He has deep expertise and is a great presenter. It's clear that he has designed this class very thoughtfully, with content that is highly practical and relevant. I enjoy his lectures and his slides are well created too. His industry experience also effectively bridges AI theory with real-world application
Okayish...

Emaad doesn't encourage much interaction or participation from students. Overall just tiresome to attend class and feel motivated to do well.

You will most likely sleep as it's just one hour and fifteen minutes of straight lecturing. Its unfortunate that this professor is even at Cornell. All focus is on the engineering aspect, none on marketing.
far better courses to take at cornell, don't waste your time with this course
Manipulative, disrespectful, controlling, demanding, and downright abusive. She's regularly reported but protected by her tenure. Beware

Elizabeth Meyer clearly cares about printmaking - but her feedback is semi-helpful at best and downright demeaning at worst. I frequently was given better direction by the TA and technician. At least for introduction to Print, the workload was intense.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Loved this Intro to Printmaking! At the end of my semester I got to take my work to the Print Fair in NYC. Hard work - but worth it.

Passionate professor who is proactive with keeping the print media department contemporary. Expects you to engage fully in the class and you learn alot! She is critical with feedback/advise and pushes you to do well.

I don't think I have ever had a worse experience in my life. She constantly interrupts her co-teacher and other students while they talk, and she would talk non-stop for three hours about unrelated matter. She makes insensitive, rude and offensive comments, and she pries into your personal life. She expects you accommodate her mood and schedule.

Elisabeth is definitely a very passionate, worldly, and insightful professor. I think the conflict with students and her is her occasional mood-swings and judgmental spurts. She definitely chooses favorites. Her class is demanding, you learn a lot, she's tough, but students need that sometimes, especially students in Art School.
Personally One of the worst teachers I've ever had...
She's rude and insensitive.
She is bad at teaching.  She is inpatient.

I would never, ever, ever take a course with her again -- I recommend to all my friends the same.  Her comments are very misleading and often conflicting. She is moody and overly intense -- she refused to speak about one students work in crit bc they didn't look up the artist she suggested.
Don't expect her to be your best friend, but she will help your artmaking process so much. Yeah, she is tough, but students need that sometimes. She really does care about helping you.
Really Crazy.  Makes decisions based on her mood.  She gossips about students and teachers to students.

Likes students with good work ethic (try to work outside of class when she's there so she can see what a dedicated student you are).  Difficult teacher when things don't go her way in class.  Working through her assignments and class critiques were invaluable... take the class no matter how much you suffer.

By far the WORST professor I had in the department. Reminded me of Martha Stewart w/her cold compulsive demeanor. Favors men to an embarassing degree, and cares more about placing an ink can 30cm to the right than explaining why youre using it in the first place. A miserable perfectionist and miserable class, its like she tried to make you unhappy.
plain and simple, this woman is crazy.  like wacko crazy!
She is an intelligent woman who really cares about her students. As long as you can connect with her, you will love her. She is the consciousness of the art department.
No Comments
Random grading--will give a low grade on the final if she simply does not like its tone. An easy class, but don't try engaging with critical theory on the assignments as levity is always preferred.

While occasionally a lot of work (having to watch a movie along with reading the play for the next class), I found this class to be worthwhile. The grade depends on participation and two essays, and discussions were always interesting. Many Pulitzer-winning plays are on the curriculum, and thought was clearly put into structuring the curriculum.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly do not understand why this professor has lower reviews. The class has alot of readings & I haven't done half of them and still am able to participate. She only really cares about participation and is so sweet. The work looks overwhelming but it is easy and only 2 papers total. I only knew one of the plays and still found it interesting
don't take ENGL3370 if ur not an intense theatre kid. teacher can be straight up rude, you have hours and hours of homework for watching plays each week, and is just not an enjoyable class whatsoever

Not good, strict grader, quite rude actually. Has an lively exterior that masks this. Also drones on and on for things that could have been compactly said in a few words. Does not facilitate interesting discussion. Made what would have been an interesting class boring.
Classes are always entertaining and even include guest speakers at times. However, students are graded on very few things and the professor can be a harsh grader.
very accomodating and great class

The syllabus was a little confusing, but she grades lightly. Only a few essays which aren't that hard as long as you put in a bit of effort. She has a very bright personality and makes class fun at times. A couple of field trips make the class more enjoyable. Opportunities to redo essays are helpful and she gives good feedback.

Prof Gainor is the nicest prof ever. I took PMA 1161 (FWS) and it was really chill. Not many readings and easy essays. She is also very sweet and is extremely caring. I would definitely recommend this class to anyone looking for a FWS.
I loved Food and The Media with Professor Gainor! Such an interesting and engaging class. Gainor is also a very kind and understanding teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly was questioning the integrity of the university the entire time sitting in this class. He used AI Slop images every lecture, sometimes funny. No one learned anything useful in lectures but the sections with the TAs are nice though!
Parfait is a very knowledgeable and at times hilarious lecturer, but at times a little dry. I enjoyed the class, and thought it was structured well.

Given the other professors who were teaching this course (who are supposedly terrible), I thought Professor Eloundou was fantastic. He definitely has flaws (e.g. dry lectures), but I don't really understand the bad ratings. At least for this introductory course, he made the concepts really easy and was especially lenient with tests + extra credit

You get 4 pages of cheat sheet for the final 
I got a C on the final and passed with an A
Lectures were repetitive and not well organized, but easy class. The discussion section was helpful.
rants in lecture and doesnt have clear slides. must study by yourself since it is no help.

Parfait is a very enthusiastic and caring professor! He always made time for students and was always happy to answer questions or listen to students' thoughts on a variety of subjects. However, I felt that lectures only marginally aided my understanding of the course material. Overall, Parfait teaches a great and easy going course!

I think Parfait is one of the nicest and most enthusiastic professors at Cornell! He loves hearing from students and always wants us to take something home from the course. However, I do think that his lecture slides could have been organized more clearly and his lectures could be a little boring at times. Overall good course!

Professor was insightful and clearly knowledgeable on the content but was very very bland. Lectures were repetitive and the slides were confusing to look back on. Information was overall super disorganized. But the workload is light and content is interesting, so not all bad.

Seems like an incredibly knowledgeable professor, however, that does not shine through in lectures. Lectures (all the content for the final) are boring, repetitive, and hard to follow. Slides are cryptic and often times unintelligible. Lack of clear content and boring lectures do not bode well for a final which is all based on lectures.
Not a great professor. Was never accessible outside of class and mostly just read off the lecture slides.

Parfait is very smart and has an incredible amount of experience and knowledge. Regardless, listening to him lecture is mind-numbing. His lectures are boring and disengaging. I enjoyed the class content but lectures were so hard to follow because he just seemed so uninterested in teaching them.

One mid term and a final. If you go to lecture and understand basic ideas, the tests aren't too difficult. Go to lecture to get extra credit from iclickers. One group presentation in discussion section and weekly readings that you have to write on. Do the readings, they are on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Parfait really cares about the subject matter and his class stays interesting. I really enjoyed this class because it actually applies to our everyday lives. Not difficult, just have to read textbook for homework assignments.

His lectures are very disorganized, but you learn a lot from the readings alone that it's fine that the lectures are a bit messy. The discussion sections are the most beneficial time where you really learn the concepts. Overall a really good class that is easily doable and you actually learn a lot if you do the readings and attend section.

He is a kind professor, the grades mainly depend on the TAs though so try to find out which ones are good. The professor is a good lecturer and seems to care about students. At the end of one of the lectures (not the last lecture), everyone clapped because he was so inspirational. The tests are open note so they weren't too difficult.

An extremely intelligent man, but not a very good professor for introductory classes. Very disorganized but still managed to teach so that material stuck the first time hearing it. Attend discussionit helps. Go to office hours or email for help on essays and group projects.

This class is way too much for 3 credits, from 30 minute student presentations to very vague and unclear essay assignments with changing and unclear due dates. The lectures are unsimulating and I felt like I am not learning anything at all. This class needs more organization and clearness.

He's a nice person, but not the best professor. He didn't explain assignments clearly, so no one really ever knew what to do. Lectures were slow and somewhat disorganized, exams were all true/false and open book, the final project was pretty time-consuming, but not too hard.

Nice guy, like everyone else said, but USELESS professor. He can't stick to the syllabus, he doesn't give students enough time to do assignments (he sprang them on us all semester) and you don't learn ANYTHING in class. Attendance is mandatory but it doesn't help. Also, don't waste $$ on the textbook.

I really do like Parfait, he is nice, he makes cute jokes, and if you see him one on one, he is helpful.  However, this class was horrible.  We did not learn anything, and though Parfait is a great guy, he makes projects very vague and no one knows what is going on. I wish I could have learned to do more research, our project did not accomplish muc

He really does seem like a nice guy, but as a Prof, I didn't really like him.  His assignments and exams seem to be very arbitrary, and he wasn't really able to explain some logic behind arguments.  It was all analyzing models, not really addressing the issues, which was disappointing.

Prof. Parfait is really helpful and enthusiastic.Prelims are all true or false format, there're 3 main lab projects;they are ok, just a lot of excel!Participation is important.Prelims aren't hard, and he always does class reviews!Take it!
parfait is wonderful! his lectures are entertaining and informative. after taking two courses with him, i only wish the rest of my professors were as good.
Though he has a heavy accent, he really enjoys students and tries to make interesting projects.  A very nice person.
Very kind professor, feedback was good but most actual learning was done outside of class so prepare to learn grammatical rules and stuff in your own time and practice in class!
She really cares for her students and wants them to succeed. I would recommend taking her class!
Amazing prof. Make French enjoyable
Elise is very nice. She is an amazing professor and she does so much to help students succeed. Definitely recommend!
Had her for my FWS, I really enjoyed the content and the creative writing essays gave us a bunch of freedom. As long as you submit decent essays, youll be fine.

The course was actually great compared to CS 4700 when taught by Bart Selman. Yes, it used a class from Berkley, but that class is not too terrible. Would still recommend taking if you are cosidering.
This review is for CS 6172. Kevin is a really good lecturer and very caring. The class was chill and interesting. Definitely recommend taking it.

I could not stand lectures. Just read off Berkely CS188 slides all day. Much better to just save your time and watch youtube videos of Berkeley CS188 lectures. The day before the midterm only 14 people showed up including myself (I actually counted).

Absolutely the worst class at Cornell. The prof just read Berkeley CS188 slides with no passion, showing zero care for the subject or us. It was all over the place—lectures, homework, exams didn't match up. Exams had stuff we never covered, with a median of 50%. Felt pointless studying so much, and feeling like I wasted my time.
