Jack himself said that 2-3 students got an A last year. You'll stay up late and need to conform to his unorthodox grading style. It's doable, but you'll have to perform cartwheels and jump through hoops for that A. There's no canvas page; grades are put on the wall. My classmates and I still don't know exactly what we learned long after taking it.

Jack is an amazing professor for intro DEA course, he is passionate and easy going. It was a long semester, and everyone learned so much about design at the end of the year. Highly recommended if you want to look at the world from a designer's perspective.

very nice person. I think he told us that he became a looser grader for us this year but can be hard to reach during the limited office hours he offer cuz everyone wants to ask him about clarifications/feedback

The class was interesting and took me out of my comfort zone. Jack was also very accessible through office hours and would get back to you on any questions about the assignments. It did get difficult to sit for three hours and listen to lectures for an extended period of time.

Unclear expectations and always returned grades very very late. Has his own method of calculating grades and does not tell students how assignments are weighted. Has office hours and is usually accessible.

i enrolled in this class. I guess it was my fault for not understanding the times but this class is three hours long. You sit in the studio for three hours. the class seemed interesting, but it was boring and long. i switched out within the first week bc i just couldn't sit in a class for that long. the class also seems hard and confusing

Jack has been a great professor! I've really enjoyed taking his class and even though it's a lot of work, I feel like I learnt a lot. You'll get to know your classmates really well if you work on projects in the studio so you should do that. Also, presentations take a lot of time so be prepared for that! Jack's feedback is very helpful though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: At first, this class really stressed me out and I thought Jack was really intimidating but this class has been my favorite class at Cornell still. I got to know all of my classmates really well because we spent a lot of time in studio but we are all still good friends!

You might be intimidated by Jack at first but honestly he's awesome. He really gets to know his students and everything he does is for a reason. You will spend many, many hours in the studio, but it's worth it. I think i got a lot more out of this class than any other at cornell so far. So long as you commit, i definitely recommend this class =]

Very tough to get full points on the projects, but you get a lot of feedback so you always know why you get the grade you do. You will definitely invest a lot of time in this class, but Jack is always willing to help and is a really great guy and professor.
Gave out assignments that the class didn't understand, then made extra work for the class.
Very good with students and very involved, and cute and funny in a hippish way. Expects a lot from the students but is equally responsible in providing feedback.

You will spend HOURS (anywhere from 4-15) doing each [weekly] project, esp when you get into the second half of the semester. The content has nothing to do with interior design as much as just general ideas of color/light/form/etc. It's a tough course but you do learn a lot & Jack is really good. The reading summaries are tedious/time-consuming tho
Jack's class made me decide to transfer out of Arts and Sciences and into Human Ecology so that I could major in interior design... = ]
No Comments
I really liked Jack's DEA 101 class.  The projects were pretty interesting, esp the latter ones.  He gave useful comments and he's a funny guy.

First of all, Jack's classes are really interesting.  The guy knows a ton and his lectures cover a lot of ground.  On the other hand, there are too many projects and it is almost impossible to get questions answered in class or during office hours.

This guy is cool as long as you are liked by him.  Do your work and maintain his interest in you and your work and he will treat you well.  He likes good music and is overall a pretty fair teacher.  If you are at Cornell and on the Interior Design track in Hum Ec, you will most likely have him a few times so keeping a good rep with him will be pretty important.
He's a very helpful professor with a strong grasp of knowledge from various fields. He cares about his students. Serious, but funny. Difficult, but very fair.
No Comments
He's pretty cool and very helpful. The class is sometimes challenging but you will get through it!

Prof. Enns is a very down-to-earth guy who makes the effort to make lectures engaging for students with his humor and personality. His professional experience also makes the material that he's lecturing more interesting, since he's not just a pure academic.

Peter is by far the most helpful professor I have had at Cornell. He is always approachable after class and gives detailed comments on papers. Go to his office hours even if you don't have a specific question to ask. He is a nice person to talk to and he really likes getting to know students personally.
The nicest and most helpful government professor out there. I usually don't like government courses, but he sure made it fun. Highly recommended.
No Comments

Professor Musser really cares about his students. Pre-lims were tough but manageable if you are willing to put in effort. He offered extra review sessions and gave us a clear sense on what the final was going to be like. He is not the best, but he definitely deserves a higher rating.

Honestly, he seemed like a decent guy, but… Exams were way harder than anything he covered (just irrational). He did not prepare us enough for the midterms (not enough resources & did not go in enough depth). Labs were inconsistently graded & expectations were not made clear at any point in the course. Only did OK cause I knew most of it beforehand
Nice guy, difficult class. Lectures were not as in-depth as the prelims. Labs were long and TAs graded inconsistently.

Musser is a good guy and tries hard. Prelims were fair. Lectures were usually engaging. He can sometimes overcomplicate things. Ignore his overall rating; he was review-bombed. 

The class was annoying at times. Labs are really long and are graded arbitrarily. TAs often made mistakes grading prelims. Curve is nice though.

I honestly thought he was a really entertaining lecturer and really wanted us to do well; however, those prelims were so difficult. He would release practice problems that were supposed to be comparable to the difficulty of the prelims, but after getting pretty much every question right on the practice, I would get in the lower 50s on the prelims.

Evil class. So much material and he just goes at mach speed. The most memorable moment was when he asked who is feeling confused about the topic and when everyone raised their hands he laughed and went to the next topic not even thinking that he could maybe try explaining things better.

Dr. Musser is an excellent lecturer and very obviously cares about getting his students to understand the content. He is kind and funny, which made the difficult course more bearable. 2150 is hard and the exams are quite tough (~60% average usually). However, I think this is just due to the rigor of the course and not Musser's abilities as a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chill dude, but let me tell you the truth. He does not go into enough depth in his lectures and the exams are pretty unreasonable. I managed to do good since I already knew everything beforehand, but was surprised with the exam questions made. Also no rubrics for labs. People always spoke during class too, it was annoying. Nice guy though.

I thought Professor Musser was great! His lectures were clear and he covered the content to a depth that allowed for sufficient understanding yet wasn't overly complex. Every class was genuinely so engaging, and I would 100% recommended trying to take one of his classes at some point! His exams were also very fair.

Beware -- I'm 90% sure that Prof. Musser was review bombed on here (chemical engineer majors often complain about whoever teaches/taught Chem 2090). 2150 was difficult, but Musser explains the material well in lecture and in office hours.

Musser is a wonderful person with a great sense of humor and teaching style. 2150 is a lot of work, but totally worth it. I didn't have to open the textbook once to get a full understanding of the material we needed to learn. Every class was great, don't listen to the bots!
Genuinely a great guy. Ignore the bots, he cares about his students and his teaching. Far better than other chem profs
Terrible lecturer, doesn't care about students. Thank god he was denied tenure.
Chem2090 is a tough class to teach. Most of the engineering students never want to touch chemistry. He does a great job making the content approachable and meaningful. I enjoyed his class.
He's not as bad as people say he is... I think this is a valid class and the end grade for everyone isn't that bad. Everything will work out fine, trust
If you read the textbook carefully and stay on top of the homework it's not too bad, but this class does take a lot of time. Prof Musser is an ok lecturer and his review sessions were helpful.
Took CHEM2090 freshman year. Lectures got boring over time. He was helpful during office hours. If you put effort into the class you would be fine grade-wise. Pretty understanding guy.

The materials are there to succeed if you look for them. The practice prelims do not match the real prelims in difficulty (real prelims are harder). I was able to get an A by doing ~200 practice problems per prelim/final. Use MIT Opencourseware to find any extra problems he does not provide. Insanely challenging course but doable.
Nightmare.
Good luck and pray for that curve.
Was not truly able to teach.
His classes are very boring. He always makes amazing jokes that get the whole crowed laughing. He has a horrible grading critiria.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is really funny but I just don't like chemistry
impossible class. thinking of dropping out of Cornell

This class condenses all of gen chem into 1 semester, making it super hard to keep up. The content-load isn't Musser's fault, but his lectures are quite boring and confusing. Labs are super tedious and the exams are nothing like the practice prelims he uploads. Idek how I scored an A-, I can't tell u a single thing I actually learned in this class.
his exams r x100000000 harder than his lectures and his practice prelims. i genuinely think he wanted all of us to fail
Honestly, he's not a terrible professor, but the class itself is horrific. Even if you've taken AP chem before like I did, the class is too difficult.
Really hard
Not good...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: chem 2090 is a hard class, but not because of musser. he does his best to teach a lot of content in a limited time and is very available for additional help through office hours and after lecture. unsurprisingly, the lectures can get boring. overall, he's a good professor and the poor ratings are from people who blame the prof for their bad grade.
Best professor I've had at Cornell so far.
It is the best professor I've had at Cornell; I don't get the hate.
It is impossible to keep up with the pace of the class. Have fun!
I wanted to rate him a 0 but that's not possible here so I had to rate him a 1. Please try to take the CASE instead of taking this class.
Lectures are hard to follow, but reading the textbook, taking chem AEW, and going to office hours was enough to do decently in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst organized class you will ever take. Tests don't remotely cover content of lecture. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Way too much homework and chemistry labs are ridiculously vague. There is no instruction or help on how to complete the lab assignments. Lectures are long and you don't learn very much. The website used to complete the homework doesn't help anyone study either. Waste of time.

This class is a mixed bag. Musser's lectures can be a slog, but staying engaged and using outside resources helps a lot. If you put in the work, the high curve makes it manageable. Just be ready for a heavy workload and don't expect to learn everything from lectures alone.

This course is a bit of a mixed bag. The prof can be dry, but the material is manageable if you put in the effort. Just be sure to go to office hours and use outside resources to stay on top of things.

lectures are incredibly boring. i never paid attention in lecture and crammed in the last 24-48 hours and ended up pulling a B/B+ on every exam. there is a very heavy curve in the class (an 82% was an A-) which makes it okay, but can confidently say that i am not coming out of this class understanding even one small thing about gen chem.
He is a great Professor. You can't expect to learn everything in lecture. Just go to his OH.

Professor Musser exponentially helped make CHEM 2090 easy and understandable. His lectures were also entertaining. I would say that one needs to study and attend office hours to improve in this class, but the class curve is also good for the prelims and finals. There is no need to worry much about this class, as long as you put in the effort.

Very tough class and made the material much more difficult than it needed to be. Lectures went way too fast and the only way to follow was to write down all the slides before the lecture. Not a good professor. Avoid if possible.

A good professor, content was not as hard as expected and gave lots of prep material for the exams. Homework was good review so didn't have to do too much outside studying. Averages are super low, so there's a crazy high curve. The labs take forever though and the autograding is harsh.

Musser is nice, most of the problem are with CHEM 2090 itself. It has a heavy workload covering a lot of general chemistry, plus a lab for only 4 credits. Musser had to speed through every lecture, which is tough for anyone to do. Hw was quite a bit but helpful. Plus everyone is taking the class as a requirement, so general interest is low.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures were somewhat boring, so mostly utilize outside resources to learn the material which isn't the worst thing. Musser is a generally nice person though, just make sure to pay attention to the labs, homework etc for your grades sake.

Musser is a great professor teaching a hard class. This is a class for engineers, many of which will never take a chemistry class again, and for that reason It is extremely fast paced and lecture heavy. Practice Prelims and quizzes are a MUST TAKE. I went to review sessions and took an AEW which were extremely helpful. Use youtube to youradvantage
does not teach during lectures so you have to learn the course yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great person and even greater professor! He taught me everything I needed to know about chem in his fun and entertaining lectures (with a great sense of humor)! While it can seem difficult, as all chemistry is, Musser makes it fun and exciting, with the labs and class polls being my favorite parts of his class!

Dude, if you're looking for a chemistry professor who can turn a room full of compounds into a snoozefest, then Andrew Musser is your guy. His lectures are like watching paint dry, and his jokes about Avogadro's number could put a caffeine addict to sleep. Avoid at all costs if you want to actually enjoy learning chemistry.

Musser? More like Musser-able! This professor's teaching style is as dry as a lab experiment gone wrong. I felt like I needed a periodic table cheat sheet just to understand what he was saying. Seriously, if you're trying to understand chemistry, avoid Musser's class like the plague.
Don't need to attend lectures just read the textbook and do practice problems and you will be fine.
Kinda nice guy, just a bad lecturer

Dude, like, Prof Musser is the chemistry equivalent of a boring textbook. His lectures are about as exciting as watching paint dry, and his jokes are as funny as a chemistry lab explosion (which is actually pretty entertaining). Save yourself the trouble and find another prof who knows how to light up the periodic table with some actual enthusiasm.

Yo, so let me spill the tea on Musser, the "chemical comedian" of our college life. Dude's got a knack for turning basic chemistry into a snooze-fest, making even a nitrogen reaction more predictable than the Monday morning lecture. Seriously, if you're looking to feel drier than a test tube, take this guy's class. #ChemistryShouldn'tBeThisBoring.

Professor Musser might as well have been speaking Parseltongue because I couldn't understand a single word he said in class. I'd have a better chance decoding the Dead Sea Scrolls than deciphering his lectures on chemical equations. Save yourself the headache and enroll in an online tutorial hosted by a singing periodic table instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yo, let me tell you about Professor Musser's Chem class. It's like watching a chemistry magic show, but instead of pulling rabbits out of hats, he pulls confusion out of thin air. Dude somehow manages to make something as simple as balancing equations feel like advanced calculus.

This might be an unpopular opinion, but Professor Musser's teaching style leaves me more confused than a compound with an endless chain of carbons. I've never encountered anyone who can make chemistry equations sound as mysterious as alchemy. Good luck deciphering his lectures, folks!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Musser likes to mix things up in the classroom, but unfortunately, it's not with his teaching style. His lectures are as unpredictable as chemical reactions gone wrong, leaving students feeling more confused than when they started. If you enjoy deciphering hieroglyphics instead of understanding chemistry, then Musser's class is definitely for you.

Hey, so I took this chem class with Professor Musser and oh boy, it was like trying to decode the periodic table with blurry goggles on. His explanations were as clear as a mixture of hydrogen peroxide and sulfuric acid - explosive! Definitely avoid if you want to keep your brain cells intact.

Professor Andrew Musser? More like Professor Andrew MUDDER! His lectures are like trying to decipher a secret code written in hieroglyphics. I thought chemistry was already confusing, but Musser takes it to a whole new level. If you're a fan of mind-boggling equations and a professor who looks perpetually lost in the periodic table, he's your guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Musser's chemistry lectures were like a magic trick gone wrong. One minute we were talking about bonding, the next he vanished into thin air, leaving us as puzzled as an unsolved stoichiometry problem. Save yourself the headache, folks, and skip this chem class unless you enjoy feeling more lost than a rogue electron.

I gotta be honest, Musser's class felt more like a pop quiz than a chemistry lecture. The only reaction I had was confusion, and trust me, it wasn't an exothermic one. If you're looking for a professor who can make chemistry less mind-boggling, definitely look elsewhere!

Yo, so I had this professor Musser for chem and let me tell you, it was a chemical disaster. Dude was like mixing random elements in his teaching style, leaving us all confused AF. It was like trying to balance a crazy equation with no coefficients. Definitely avoid this dude unless you want your brain to undergo a spontaneous combustion.

Yo, so let's talk about Professor Musser's chem class. Honestly, it's like trying to decode a secret language. Dude throws around terms like "stoichiometry" and "quantum mechanics" without blinking an eye. I swear, I need a translator just to understand what he's saying. Ain't nobody got time for that, ya feel me?

Musser's chemistry lectures can be quite the puzzling experience. It's like trying to balance an equation with all the right elements, but he always manages to throw in a random reactant that leaves you scratching your head. You'll definitely need a strong bond with the textbook to survive his class!

Professor Andrew Musser is the "element" of excellence in teaching Chem2090. His classes are a true "chemical reaction" of enthusiasm and knowledge. His communication is crystal clear, and he's always willing to assist students, making the course feel like a "perfectly balanced equation."

Bro, let's just say Musser's lectures in CHEM2090 are like watching molasses drip in slow motion. I'm pretty sure the chemical reactions in his brain move faster than his explanations. Save yourself the headache and avoid this experiment gone wrong.

Musser's lectures are the kind of chemical formula you want to avoid in college - dry, confusing, and leaving you feeling like you're drowning in equations. His idea of humor seems to be a rare element, as it's nowhere to be found. Sadly, attending his classes is as enjoyable as trying to balance a redox reaction in your sleep.

Yo, so I took this Chem class with Prof. Musser and man, it was like watching paint dry! His lectures made stoichiometry seem more exciting than a Justin Bieber concert. Plus, his jokes about chemical reactions were as lame as trying to balance equations after an all-nighter. Time to pop a Celebrex for that headache!

Professor Musser may have a Ph.D. in Chemistry, but his lectures make me feel like I'm swimming in a beaker of confusion. His explanations are as clear as a solution with precipitated particles, and his enthusiasm for chemistry is about as visible as an invisible gas. Don't expect any sparks of knowledge to ignite in his class!

Yo, I gotta spill the chemistry beans about Prof Musser. This dude's teaching is literally drier than a 20-year-old beaker of sodium hydroxide. I swear, I've never seen someone make molecules sound more boring than him. Save yourself the headache and find another professor who can actually inject some excitement into this subject.

Whew, where do I even begin with Musser? This professor's lectures are like a bad acid trip filled with complicated reactions and zero explanations. It's like he's speaking in a language made entirely of gibberish and molecular structures.

Yo, so I took this chem class with Musser and man, it was like a never-ending, mind-numbing reaction. Dude would drone on about stoichiometry like it was the most captivating thing in the world, I nearly turned into a mole of boredom. His jokes were as dry as an overcooked lab report, and his exams felt like solving a Rubik's cube blindfolded.

Yo, so let me spill the tea on Professor Musser. Dude's got more chemicals in his syllabus than in his personality. I swear, his lectures are drier than a beaker-less lab experiment. Would've been easier understanding the mysteries of the periodic table from sipping on my morning coffee.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Yo, so I had this professor Musser for chem and let me just say, it was like watching a slow-motion chemical reaction gone wrong. Dude couldn't even explain the difference between an acid and a base without causing mass confusion. Avoid him like the plague if you actually want to understand anything about chemistry.

Yo, I gotta spill the tea about this Musser dude. His teaching style is as dry as a lab report on drying agents. I mean, he may know his chemistry stuff, but his lectures are more effective at putting you to sleep than a double replacement reaction.

Andrew Musser, more like Andrew Miserable! This chem professor must have brewed his own potion of confusion because understanding his lectures was like trying to decipher hieroglyphics without Rosetta Stone. I've never seen reactions go so wrong since my grandma tried to make a cake with salt instead of sugar.

Professor Musser? More like Professor Miserable! This guy sucked the joy out of chemistry faster than a reaction gone wrong. His lectures were as exciting as watching paint dry, and his explanations were about as clear as a jar of murky chemicals. Save yourself the headache and find a different chem professor pronto!

Yo, so I took this chem class with Prof Musser, and let me tell you, it was like watching paint dry in slow motion. This dude made the periodic table seem more exciting than a Taylor Swift concert. I'd rather calculate molar masses in my sleep than sit through another one of his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

Honestly, Musser's lectures suck. He just speeds through the slides and expects us to understand concepts like molecular structure and atomic orbitals. It's like he thinks we're all already chemistry whizzes.
Had to work extremely hard for this class. Musser is a great guy, but not a very clear lecturer. Make sure you do your readings and grind textbooks problems
Can't even proofread a prelim. Embarrassing.

The test average for the first prelim was a 30%, indicating a clear issue. Lectures were so confusing, about random topics, never connected, and somehow always stressed quantum mechanics even though it was an intro chem course. Spent hours doing problem sets every night. His dog Basil is cool though. This guy should stick to his research
british lullaby voice

Professor Musser gets such a bad rap for no reason because so many people just don't pay attention and don't read the textbook and think the subject of chemistry is hard and are blaming it on him. He's a really nice professor and students don't respect him enough! Doing the practice problems in the book help so much too

Musser gave hard exams (averaged 60%), but the low exam scores made it easier to do well without knowing all the material. I didn't take AP chem in high school and didn't really do Musser's assigned readings, but for me going to lecture and doing the assigned homework & the practice exam questions worked, especially for the multiple choice exams.

Chem 2090 is a hard class and the lectures do not help at all. My advice stick to the textbook and homework and make sure you do well outside of class work. My grades outside of the class carried me to a B. Lectures are hard to follow and get ready for a ton of homework. Musser did help by giving us extra assignments for more credit, but still hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Musser is a good professor. The problem isn't his teaching; it's the fact that there is TOO MUCH material to cover in Chem 2090. If the course was less dense, or if we had more than 1 semester to cover it alll, I'm sure there would be no issue. He has actually done more than most other professors to help out students. He puts in work!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Musser gets a very bad reputation because of the inherent difficulty of the course. As far as chemistry professors go, Musser made things very clear in lecture and there were no surprises on exams. His exams were tough, but fair, and he would drop homeworks/give extra credit to help students during tough times. Good guy, respect him a lot

Andrew Musser is one of the best professors I have had, and his exams are all super easy and straightforward. I could honestly do these exams in my sleep, and the grading is very fair. Professor Musser made me interested in pursuing a major in Chemistry and is an inspiring professor. I urge everyone to take his class and experience his teaching.
Nice guy, terrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Everything was taught out of order. Lectures were unclear and filled with scattered ideas that left everyone confused. You were expected to come in with loads of knowledge, if you didn't take ap chem, beware, you will not pass without destroying your mental health and sanity. He made me seriously debate leaving engineering.

His lectures were terrible. He would go through an entire slideshow of equations without linking them to the application, so nothing resonated with anyone. Especially in the quantum mechanics unit. ugh.

There were no lecture slides and he wrote everything very small. It was hard to follow lectures. Whatever you do, do not take this class unless you are confident in your chemistry abilities. Textbook is general chemistry by mcquarrie and you are better off reading it and doing the homework & extra practice problems rather than attending lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: SO MUCH HOMEWORK + TERRIBLY CONFUSING LECTURES = would not recommend

It's not his fault that he was given a class of > 400 students in an auditorium where he could barely be heard and the blackboard could be read. Still, his exams were difficult (around 50% median on both prelims and final).
Hard to hear or see in class

Like many people said, this guy is way too smart to be teaching a gen ed class. In the beginning half of the course, his lectures were not useful in teaching what was on the exam. Only the last few units did I feel like his lectures were relevant. Best way to do well is understand the problem sets and read the textbook. Mainly chemical calculations
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Musser was an uninspiring lecturer, to say the least. I advise teaching yourself the content via the homework, don't bother taking notes in class.

Prof. Musser is very kind and will answer any question you may have after class, but lectures are poorly organized and do not follow the homework schedule. Exams only test for speed of calculations, rather than actual content mastery. To succeed, prepare to rely heavily on Organic Chemistry Tutor, practice problems, and office hours for labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Andrew Musser is an insensitive and lazy professor. His answer keys are uninterpretable, his handwriting on the chalkboard is tiny, and he does not care about the wellbeing of his students. With a 3% Covid-19 positivity rate and 200 new active cases each day- -He refuses to modify the final exam to be online. This class has ruined my mental state.

If you want to teach yourself chemistry, take CHEM 2090 with Professor Musser. Professor Musser is a very nice, smart individual... who should never teach an Intro to Chemistry course. His lectures leave students with less understanding of the topics & don't align with the quiz & 50 weekly homework problems. Don't take his class. It's not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: While Musser probably has good intentions, he shouldn't be teaching gen chem to freshman while having a PHD in physics. Class is also badly organized (labs cover material not yet covered in class), making it difficult to succeed on worksheets. Only reason I'm not lost is because of AP Chem, but would be impossible without it.

Andrew Musser is too smart for his own good. Countless times throughout the semester he would spend entire lecture teaching to the board. Not only was the caliber of the lecturing atrocious but the majority of time spent teaching was spent on information irrelevant to the exam. I would not recommend taking this class if you have any other option.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unfortunately, the lecture and course organization is non-existent. The material is complicated and muddied by the heinously bad teaching. Professor Musser is a potato when it comes to teaching general chemistry.

There's a lot of complaints for Professor Musser, but I think those complaints should be directed towards CHEM2090 rather than him. If you put in the work in this class, you will be fine. I have an A in this course and haven't been to a lecture after the first few weeks of class. Just READ THE TEXTBOOK and MASTER the problem sets. That's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Most of the reviews on this page seem to have a negative view of him, but I would argue that the majority of these reviews are regarding the difficulty of the class, rather than Musser himself. I found his lectures to be insightful, and he has been very kind and understanding through difficult times (homework extensions, recorded lectures, etc.)

Professor Musser is a real gem. I am lucky to be in his CHEM 2090 class. He has a passion for teaching. I respect Professor Musser alot. He wrote a bit small in the beginning of the semester, but he has since started writing bigger. He cares about his students. His exams are challenging, so you should know the material very well.

Seems like a nice person, but is an absolutely awful professor. Way to smart to be teaching Gen Chem, and has no idea that his lectures are beyond the scope of the class. Goes to fast through super important topics and spends to much time on irrelevant info. If you take his class, read the textbook and listen in lecture, hints for tests

Although Professor Musser is intelligent and a nice guy, his skill set is not best suited to an intro course. The exams are long and difficult and there is a large amount of homework. The course is manageable if you work on problem sets in groups and read the textbook carefully.

This professor absolutely sucks. He writes insanely small on the board, doesnt speak loud enough and teaches content that doesnt pertain to the test. His lectures are a waste of time, but worth going to because he will throw the occasional grab on the test. The tests only test your speed of doing calculations, not your understanding of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't go to his lectures because it is a waste of time. He basically derives a formula that isn't even on the test. Just grind the homework and the PRACTICE SETS and your good
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Andrew really tries, which is why I am generous and giving two stars. He is new and inexperienced at teaching, so he is adjusting. His lectures are not engaging and are difficult to follow; I have fallen asleep multiple times during class. His exams are long and difficult, and he does not prepare us well for them. You are on your own in this class!

God awful professor. Nice dude, but he's too smart to be teaching an intro class, especially in chemistry. Mans a physics PHD yet teaching gen chem. Lectures are incredibly fast, sloppy, and of no help in exam prep. If you want to do well in this class (I have been so far), skip lectures, treat the textboook like a religious text, and do the psets

Andrew Musser is a nice guy, but should not be teaching gen chem. His lectures are incomprehensible. They don't line up with the textbook, the labs, or the expected curriculum of a gen chem class. I'm sure he would be a great quantum physics professor, but gen chem with him is incredibly difficult for no good reason. Ur better off not taking chem.

Musser is a really nice guy but the class is set up very poorly. He writes very small, talks quietly and doesnt teach in an engaging manner. Lecture never matches up with lab component and jumps into different topics far too quickly. He definitely tries his best and is considerate of the students but its he is very new to teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's definitely a very nice guy, but he's just an awful professor. Barely makes sense, the class is incredibly unstructured, his handwriting is nearly illegible on solutions. The experience has been really bad.

Musser is a smart man and a nice one, however his lectures are very difficult to understand as he is not articulate, his prelim exams are very difficult and the grading system is bogus, the homeworks are so much for so little time, the labs don't get graded till you're already done with them... its a mess.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: What you learn in lecture typically will not help you much on the (usually quite difficult) homework, and you are expected to read the textbook and learn most of it on your own. As a professor, he's totally fine. Problem is really just that it's a course that's meant to weed people out in a massive lecture hall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor taught gen chemistry even though he has a PHD in physics. The entire class focused on Quantum theory and the physics of electrons instead of chemistry. When going to lab periods no one knew how to do stoichiometry or basic chemistry which you would expect to learn.
